articles.title: Aerosmith Joined by Dave Grohl and Johnny Depp at Hollywood Bowl for First Show in Three Years, as GNR and Black Crowes Open With Tribute Sets: Concert Review
articles.full_text: × Oct 30, 2026 8:27am PT Aerosmith Joined by Dave Grohl and Johnny Depp at Hollywood Bowl for First Show in Three Years, as GNR and Black Crowes Open With Tribute Sets: Concert Review By Chris Willman Plus Icon Chris Willman Senior Music Writer and Chief Music Critic ChrisWillman Latest Noah Kahan Announces ‘The Last of the Bugs World Tour’ in Stadiums for Spring and Summer 2027 1 day ago Donnie Iris, Pittsburgh’s Favorite Rocker, Who Scored Hits With the Jaggerz and as a Solo Artist, Dies at 83 3 days ago Taylor Swift, Inducted Into Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame, Says ‘There Is No Music Community Like This Music Community. I Know, I Checked All the Communities’ 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Live Nation With Aerosmith , fans might not want to miss a thing, but they most especially did not want to miss — if at all possible — the band’s two all-star-guest-augmented shows at the Hollywood Bowl this week, the first of which was Thursday night. These two outings are the group’s first shows since they had to cut their farewell tour abruptly short a little over three years ago. Could they also be the last? No one has said anything official about this representing an actual finale for Aerosmith, and so many fans have figured that they may have further shows in them after this, perhaps going out at some point in the future with a hometown gig in Boston, in that line of prospective thinking. And yet, there was the show’s host, Bill Burr, at the very top of the evening, captured on video for all the world to hear declaring that these were “the final two shows in Aerosmith’s history.” The casual way in which he dropped that bombshell while introducing show-opener Warren Hayne made it clear he was speaking out of turn. But was Burr letting a real cat out of the bag? (Or, considering that he did a lengthy comic monologue about getting a DUI as a youth on his way home from an Aerosmith show, had he just dipped back into the sauce backstage for old time’s sake?) If these two shows should be the end of the line — rather than just being put together for the sake of filming for a TV special or documentary, as seemed to be happening — it would be a fairly proud way to go out, as the band sounded in completely top form during a short-ish but spectacular 45-minute set that rounded out the nearly four-hour evening. In particular, Steven Tyler gave no evidence of the vocal injury that halted the abortive 2023 tour. Not just back in the saddle — Tyler and Joe Perry, Tom Hamilton and Brad Whitford did not sound or act like cowpokes who had any immediate intention of re-vacating their seats upon the horse they rode in on. (L-R) Steven Tyler and Joey Kramer of Aerosmith perform onstage during California, Dream On: Aerosmith & Friends – Night 1 at the Hollywood Bowl on October 29, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Live Nation) Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Live Nation The asterisk on all that was the participation of original drummer Joey Kramer, who had had to take a break from the band due to health issues even prior to the ’23 interruption, but had made it clear he didn’t want to be done. For the first five numbers of Aerosmith’s six-song climactic set Thursday, the drummer on duty was Dave Grohl , slamming it home as if he were slugger Shohei Ohtani in his pre-midseason prime. So the question of “what about Joey?” was begged when, toward the end, Tyler said, “Before we say goodnight, I just want to say what a ride it’s been with my brothers — Joe, Tom, Brad and Joey,. Fifty-five fucking years, and we’re the same fucking band that started fifty-five and a half years ago.” (You’ve got to love a guy who’s so proud of his permanent record that he remembers to throw the “and a half” in there.) And there. suddenly, was Kramer, at center stage, sharing a hug with the frontman. He then retreated to the second drum kit that had been sitting out, promissorily, with the initials “JK” on it. Grohl gave up his position on the main kit and left the stage so that it could be taken over by John Douglas, the drum tech who had come to fill in previously for Kramer. As the two men drummed side-by-side on the final number, it seemed evident that Kramer was capable of laying down a good beat but probably not capable of doing the heavy lifting at this point in time. And so the way that it was handled seemed like a good, bittersweet compromise, in allowing the co-founder to come out and collect his flowers at the close as a still-working performer. No one from the general public who’d bought a ticket had too much idea what to expect out of Aerosmith for these two shows. So some might have thought the 45 minutes were too brief, although a look at the all-star lineup (some of whom will be repeating Sunday night, and some of whom will rotate out) made it clear to anyone attentive that this would not be a full career-summation kind of show. There were no sentimental musings, beyond Tyler’s aforementioned 55-and-a-half remarks. At the end of “Walk This Way,” without any farewells being offered, fireworks started going off over the Bowl’s shell, and it was unclear whether they’d be coming back for more after the sparklers went out or not. They did not, which made things feel a bit anticlimactic. Presumably, they’ll end night 2 with a slight bit more speechifying, whether or not they’re in the mood for clarifying future prospects or an end to all that. Anyway, aside from the odd finish, what the Bowl audience got in the broader sense was far from an anticlimax in the overall scheme of things. They wanted to see Aerosmith performing with the vigor of a mirage reassembling before their eyes, or as if there were four portraits of Dorian Gray being held in storage back in the green room. Against the odds of layoffs and advancing time, that’s exactly what they got. Long scarves tied to the mic stand and blowing in the wind? Check. Even longer hair on Tyler and Perry, also blowing in those hurricane-level breezes, with the singer festooned in a beautiful open blouse? Check. The band in crunchy precision, and the singer howling like he’d never taken a hiatus from dreaming on? Double-check. Whatever injury went down with Tyler’s larynx, it was apparently reversible, and he seems to have the kind of chops that naturally age well… which no one would take for granted after hearing some bumpy moments from some of the opening attractions. It was all you could have hoped for from the Aerosmith of 2026, and maybe even a little better than that. Related Stories ‘Young Sheldon’ Star Emily Osment Requested an Intimacy Coordinator Because of 'Uncomfortable' Age Gap With Montana Jordan: 'He Was a Baby!' ‘Young Sheldon’ Star Iain Armitage Says the Show Was a ‘Big Undertaking’ as Co-Star Acknowledges He Could Be ‘Difficult’ to Work With (L-R) Tom Hamilton, Steven Tyler and Joe Perry of Aerosmith perform onstage during California, Dream On: Aerosmith & Friends – Night 1 at the Hollywood Bowl on October 29, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Live Nation) Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Live Nation Grohl was not the only guest musician to sit in with Aerosmith, as Perry brought out his Hollywood Vampires bandmate, “Johnny fucking Depp,” to play on the penultimate number, “Train Kept A-Rollin’.” Lest any cynics imagine the actor did not have his instrument plugged in for his rhythm playing, Perry actually tossed Depp a spot to take half of his guitar solo, which he pulled off with fleeting aplomb. But the highlight might have occurred one song before that, with “Dream On,” which is a predictable choice for a standout, but when something that time-tested works, you don’t have to go looking for an underdog pick just for the sake of it. Tyler began the anthem accompanying himself on grand piano (while the audio from an interlude video was still playing) and eventually revealed that there was a small staircase behind the gleaming instrument, as there he was on top of it, preening and posing for the post-high-note outro like only someone of his greatest (?) generation can get away with. We love our Geese, and their modern-day modesty, but we may still love Tyler as a strutting, raunchy swan a little bit more. The two acts on the bill that got full mini-sets prior to Aerosmith’s appearance were the Black Crowes and Guns N’ Roses, each of whom devoted either most or all of their time on stage to covering the headliner. The BC guys were all about the Aerosmith, capably holding down the Joe Perry Project song “Let the Music Do the Talking” as their opener, followed by “Write Me a Letter,” “Combination,” “No More No More” and, finally, “Chip Away the Stone.” GNR did also did a five-song set, with three of those five being Aerosmith covers — “Nobody’s Fault,” “Seasons of Wither” and a delectable “Last Child” — before adding value for the audience with “Sweet Child of Mine” and “Welcome to the Jungle.” Slash was on form, and Axl Rose was game, though better in his lower range; in his upper, he sounded… well, different… sort of more like a choirboy falsetto, as heard here, than the raspier instrument we remember. Settling into and enjoying that difference may take more acclimation than we all had time for in such a quick appearance. Most everyone else on the bill got two numbers. With country superstar Eric Church, you’d have to count it as a split decision. “Rag Doll” was a lot of fun, given a very rootsy treatment. But “I Don’t Want to Miss a Thing” was, well, a miss, with the singer trying a little too strenuously to match Tyler’s intensity, while spending the entire number notably staring downward through his shades at the words on a monitor. It’s unclear whether he will also be on the bill for night 2, but he could use a do-over on that one; with a little more prep, it might yet be within his reach. Church was working with a house band that included Don Was, Kenny Aronoff, Andrew Watt and other famous names, as were those that preceded him — Heart’s Wilson sisters, Sammy Hagar, Billy Idol with Steve Stevens, Warren Haynes, and Sully of Godsmack. Chances are that most of those performers will not be returning for the second Bowl show, since a lot of the advertised acts have yet to appear, like Run-DMC, Tom Morello, Marcus King, Jerry Cantrell and Train’s Pat Monahan. Unless, that is, they are planning to move the start time for Sunday up even further than they did for Thursday; ticketholders for this first show got a warning through their apps in the afternoon that the very action-packed bill would be kicking off at 6:45 instead of 7. The two shows are being produced by by 724 Management and Blackbird Presents, with the involvement of the latter company being a sure sign that a doc or special is in store, pretty much confirmed by the presence of a flying camera on wires swooping back and forth above the venue’s box seats. The world will likely get a chance to see it, then, in some form. But only time — or maybe some additional remarks from the stage on Sunday? — will tell whether there might be still additional chances to see the band in the flesh down the road. articles.title: Russell Brand Rape Trial: Channel 4 Film Was Not “Magic Force” That Caused Accusers To “Recast” Memories, Court Hears In Closing Arguments
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake AI Dubbing Pioneer Flawless Sells Technology In Deal That Raises Questions About Its Future Russell Brand’s Wife Says Star Was “Caring” Lover At Time Of Rape Allegations BAFTA Launches Review Over Concerns About Trustees Accepting Free Awards Guest Tickets View All October 30, 2026 5:26am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand arrives in court this week Getty Editor’s note: T his story contains details of alleged sexual offenses that some readers may find distressing . Channel 4’s 2023 exposé on Russell Brand was not a “magic force” that caused six separate women to “recast” their memories and accuse the Despicable Me star of rape and sexual assault, a court has heard. Related Stories News Prosecution Rejects Russell Brand’s Claim He Has Been Abandoned: “You Have A Platform Of Millions” Legal Russell Brand’s Wife Says Star Was “Caring” Lover At Time Of Rape Allegations Riel Karmy-Jones, the prosecution barrister, presented her closing arguments to the jury at London’s Southwark Crown Court, where Brand is on trial over three charges of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one of attempted indecent assault. Deadline has been reporting daily on the trial from a live video feed of the courtroom. Karmy-Jones began her closing remarks by reminding the jury that the six women behind the seven charges are “wholly unconnected” insofar as they “do not know each other and have never met.” She continued: “Six women who have nothing to gain, who have not sought the limelight, who have not taken part in documentaries, who have not made claims for compensation … There is no benefit to them.” Watch on Deadline Karmy-Jones said Russell Brand: In Plain Sight , the 2023 Channel 4 documentary, and reporting by The Times of London , had caused the women — who have a lifelong right to anonymity — to come forward and tell stories about their encounters with Brand that had “haunted them for years.” Karmy-Jones rejected Brand’s defense that the documentary was “evil and untrue” and “caused them to recast what actually happened.” She asked: “Could a documentary or Times article have such sway over perfectly rational women? Could a documentary cause them to completely reinvent what happened?” Karmy-Jones argued there was no “magic force” and “woo-woo” in the film. Instead, she said the “women have realized they are not alone and have bravely come before you to tell the truth.” “They have vivid recollections of what took place,” the prosecution lawyer said, and “were not moved from their accounts” under cross-examination from defense barrister Ian Winter. In contrast, Karmy-Jones said Brand remembers very little of the women and manipulated his account after reading the prosecution’s case. In legal directions to the jury earlier on Friday, Mr Justice Bennathan, the judge presiding over the trial, told the jury to disregard the Channel 4 documentary when coming to their decision. “Do not think that a few women making anonymous complaints in a TV show adds any support at all to the prosecution,” he said. “The defendant denied the allegations [in the documentary] in robust, detailed terms. They were never tested in any court.” Bennathan said the jury must reach unanimous verdicts on each of the charges to convict Brand. He reminded jurors that the burden of proof is on the prosecution and that Brand is entitled to the benefit of the doubt. Bennathan expects the jury to begin verdict deliberations next Tuesday, November 3. The trial continues. articles.title: Female-Focused Circle Fiction Orbit Project Incubator Unveils 2026 Cohort
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Female-Focused Circle Fiction Orbit Project Incubator Unveils 2026 Cohort NewFilmmakers Los Angeles Sets Partnership With Mar Del Plata International Film Festival Cinema Guild Takes North America For Berlinale Title ‘My Wife Cries’ View All October 30, 2026 5:39am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Circle Fiction Orbit participants Circle EXCLUSIVE: The Circle Training Initiative, dedicated to women and gender-expansive filmmakers, has unveiled the five feature film projects selected for its third Circle Fiction Orbit incubator event taking place in Montenegro this week. They include Portuguese director and screenwriter Leonor Bettencourt Loureiro’s Por Este Arroios Acima , exploring the connection between the rapid transformation of the body, city and community building in the aftermath of a traumatic accident. It is the director’s second fiction feature after C’est Pas la Vie en Rose, which tapped into the zeitgeist of contemporary Lisbon as longtime residents grapple with implications of gentrification. Rita de Moura Santos at Grumpy Panda Productions is producing. Related Stories News Circle Kicks Off Inaugural Fiction Program With Nukâka Coster Waldau & Pipaluk Jørgensen Among Participants News Russell Brand Rape Trial: Channel 4 Film Was Not "Magic Force" That Caused Accusers To "Recast" Memories, Court Hears In Closing Arguments Georgian director and screenwriter Irine Jordania is participating with Tbilisi-set Nutsa.Love revolving around the unfolding relationship between an unlikely couple. It is her second feature after Air Blue Silk which premiered at the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival. She is joined by producer Elene Margvelashvili. Watch on Deadline The selection also features Dutch director Sabine Lubbe Bakker’s Premier Souffle , exploring whether a rebellious outsider can find her place in the world after years of isolation from her community. It is produced by Baldr Film. The director’s 2020 film Becoming Mona travelled the festival circuit. Montenegrin director and producer Katarina Bulajić is participating with first feature project Leech , about a woman returning to her hometown who is confronted by the magnitude of betrayal. Bulajić latest short film A Special Day is currently on the festival circuit and due to screen at Germany’s FilmFestival Cottbus next week. She is joined by screenwriter and producer Ana Vujadinovic at Montenegrin company Giggling Goat Production. The selection also includes Polish director and screenwriter Marta Prus’ drama Soloist , exploring the elite world of ballet and reinvention of the body and soul at the end of a career and beginning of something new. It follows Prus’ award-winning documentary Over The Limit about Russian gymnast and Olympic gold medalist Margarita Mamun. The new film is produced by Telemark. The lineup, focused on mid-career filmmakers and teams, was selected by a three-person committee consisting of writer and producer Suzy Gillet, film scholar Jelena Mišeljić and writer and director Ivana Mladenović. They were guided by Circle Head of Programme Biljana Tutorov – writer, director and producer of To Hold A Mountain , which is currently shortlisted for the European Film Award – and Circle Co-Head of Programme Brigid O’Shea. The seven-day residential project development retreat is currently underway in Herceg Novi, Montenegro and runs until November 1. It is led by award-winning producer and screenwriter Bianca Oana ( Touch Me Not , Collective , Anhell69 ). “This is a rare opportunity for filmmakers and producers to come together, to think and exchange experiences outside the norms and the excruciating pulse of the industry,” said Oana. “We make space to reflect not only on the films we want to make, but also on how we want to make them. Urgency and immediacy give way to listening and care. This slow time is the real time of cinema, where projects can grow into films.” She is joined by producers Myriam Sassine ( Costa Brava Lebanon) , Dana Bunescu ( The Death of Mr Lazarescu ) and Dominique Welinski, founder of the world cinema focused Next Steps Studio taking place within the framework of Cannes Critics’ Week. The programme also features a keynote session with Dea Kulumbegashvili and screening of her Venice Special Jury Prize-winning film April. “Circle Fiction Orbit is our cherished space for filmmakers working to reach the next level of their careers,” said Tutorov. “Dedicated to filmmakers, this mission informs every aspect of our methodology and framework: from the curation of mentors, experts and screenings to the location of Herceg Novi and led by Bianca Oana’s unique approach to activate their potential and find a new dynamic, all contributes to creating and environment conductive to holistic project development.” Three projects from the first two editions have come to fruition and are travelling the festival circuit: Lex Julia by director Laura Hyppönen which will compete for Best Baltic Film in Tallinn in November; IDDA , directed by Irene Dionisio, which world in Toronto and Perla by Alexandra Makarová (Austria and Slovakia) which played in Rotterdam. Founded in 2018, Circle was built to support women and gender-expansive filmmakers. It is co-funded by Creative Europe MEDIA and organised under the patronage of Eurimage by Wake Up Films. articles.title: Attorney For CNN, MS NOW & Politico Talks About Why It’s Urgent To Stop Latest Trump White House Ban: “The Chilling Effect Is Immense”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Paula Reid Joins MS NOW As Chief White House Reporter CNN, MS NOW And Politico Amend Lawsuit To Challenge Trump Ban On Access To Air Force One And The Oval Office Fox News Tops October Ratings, But Viewership Drops Vs. 2025; MS NOW And CNN Show Gains As Midterms Approach View All October 30, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Theodore J. Boutrous Jr. Photo by Randy Shropshire/Getty Images for PEN America This week, CNN , MS NOW and Politico challenged the Trump White House ‘s latest effort to punish the press: restricting the outlets from access to areas like Air Force One and the Oval Office . Already, a federal judge, Timothy Kelly, has ruled that the president’s wider ban on the three outlets, which barred access to the White House grounds, likely violated their due process and First Amendment rights. But the Trump administration has continued to prohibit CNN, MS NOW and Politico from such things as presidential travel or other pool assignments, the outlets say in the most recent legal filing. Related Stories News CNN, MS NOW And Politico Amend Lawsuit To Challenge Trump Ban On Access To Air Force One And The Oval Office Legal CNN’s Scott Jennings Hit With $72.5M Suit By Hasan Piker Over “Manipulated” Lynching Misquote The question of access to the smaller and more exclusive spaces of the presidency is a related but slightly different matter, but one that Theodore Boutrous Jr. , the lead attorney representing the news organizations, thinks is essential to challenge. He noted the administration’s other press restrictions, including access to the Pentagon, and expressed concerns that could spread to other areas of the federal government. Watch on Deadline The White House’s position is that access is a privilege and that no journalist has a First Amendment right to these areas. “No person and no journalist has a constitutional right” to the Oval Office, Air Force One or other areas, a White House official said.

articles.title: ‘Guria’ Wins Best Film At Asia Pacific Screen Awards; ‘9 Temples To Heaven’ Takes Best Director
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz ‘Guria’ Wins Best Film At Asia Pacific Screen Awards; ‘9 Temples To Heaven’ Takes Best Director Japan’s Animation Industry Grows 15.8% To Record $28BN, Driven By Both Domestic & Overseas Sales – TIFFCOM Justin H. Min Starrer ‘Journey There’ & Hong Sangsoo’s ‘Nowhere To Lay My Eyes’ Sell To Multiple Territories View All October 30, 2026 7:29am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Asia Pacific Screen Awards 2026 winners APSAs Guria , directed by Georgia’s Levan Koguashvili, won Best Film at the Asia Pacific Screen Awards on the Gold Coast, Australia, with the film’s producers Olena Yershova, Koguashvili and Boris Frumin recognized for the international co-production. Thai director Sompot Chidgasornpongse received Best Director for 9 Temples To Heaven , with a Special Mention going to Myanmar director Aung Phyoe for Fruit Gathering . The Jury Grand Prize was presented to Afghan filmmaker Shahrbanoo Sadat for No Good Men , acknowledging her “compelling approach to storytelling and her contribution to contemporary Afghan cinema”. Related Stories News Alternativa Distribution Takes 'No Good Men' & 'Four Daughters' To MIPCOM News Oscars: Thailand Selects Sompot Chidgasornpongse's '9 Temples To Heaven' For International Feature Film Race New Zealand filmmaker Paloma Schneideman and producers Vicky Pope and Thomas Coppell received Best Youth Film for Big Girls Don’t Cry , while Best Animated Film went to The Violinist , co-directed by Singapore’s Ervin Han and Spanish filmmaker Raúl García. Watch on Deadline Best Documentary Film award was presented to filmmakers Itab Azzam and Jack MacInness for One In A Million , a UK and U.S. co-production which was recognized for its documentary storytelling and exploration of a Syrian refugee’s lived experience. Best Screenplay went to Rakan Mayasi, Wahid Ajmi and Pôl Seif for Yesterday The Eye Didn’t Sleep , a collaboration involving Belgium, Lebanon, Palestine, Qatar and Saudi Arabia. Rising Korean talent Sim Su-bin received Best New Performer for The World Before , while Nepalese performer Pushpa Thing Lama was awarded Best Performance for Elephants In The Fog . Vietnamese cinematographer Nguyễn Vinh Phúc received Best Cinematography for Hearing . The Cultural Diversity Award was presented to Another Birth , directed and produced by Isabelle Kalandar, a collaboration between Tajikistan, U.S. and Qatar ( see full list of award winners below ). Also announced during this year’s APSAs ceremony were the five recipients of the 2026 MPA APSA Academy Film Fund, each receiving a grant of $10,000, supported by the Motion Picture Association (MPA). The five recipients include Indian director Payal Kapadia and producer Thomas Hakim for A Memory Of Being Here (India); Cambodian-French director Davy Chou and producer Charlotte Vincent for My Father’s Glory (France, Cambodia); Chinese director Taifeng Liu and producer Janet Wu for A Place In The Sun (China); and Singaporean director Nicole Midori Woodford and producer Anthony Chen for Incarnation (Singapore, Japan). The fifth project, documentary The Story Of My Shirt , from Zhanana Kurmasheva and producer Banu Ramazanova, is a a co-production involving Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, China and Chile. Tracey Vieira, chair of the Asia Pacific Screen Awards, said: “Tonight we celebrate an exceptional group of filmmakers whose work reflects the courage, creativity and cultural richness of the Asia Pacific. From Guria and No Good Men to Elephants In The Fog , this year’s winners remind us of the extraordinary stories emerging from our region and the importance of creating opportunities for these voices articles.title: Forest Whitaker Joins Rachid Bouchareb’s  ‘Boomerang Atomic’ As EP Ahead Of DOC NYC Screening
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Female-Focused Circle Fiction Orbit Project Incubator Unveils 2026 Cohort NewFilmmakers Los Angeles Sets Partnership With Mar Del Plata International Film Festival Cinema Guild Takes North America For Berlinale Title ‘My Wife Cries’ View All October 30, 2026 7:42am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Forest Whitaker Getty Images EXCLUSIVE : Academy Award-winning actor and producer Forest Whitaker has joined Rachid Bouchareb ’s Boomerang Atomic as an executive producer ahead of its screening at DOC NYC in November. The documentary revisits France’s first atomic bomb detonation on February 13, 1960 close to the remote town of Reggane in the heart of the Sahara Desert in Algeria , at a time when the country was still under French colonial rule. French Algerian director Bouchareb, whose 2006 drama Days of Glory was Oscar-nominated, examines the devastating consequences that continue to affect local populations and the environment more than six decades later. Related Stories Festivals 'Up Against It' Review: Antonio Banderas & Eva Birthisle In Trudie Styler's Witty Comedy About Divorced Couple Forced To Conceive Baby To Save Their Daughter - Toronto Film Festival News U.S. & Japanese Producers In Talks For Rachid Bouchareb's Algeria Majority-Backed French Nuclear Test Drama 'Reggane' Drawing exclusively on French state archives, the documentary presents the nuclear test through the images and commentary originally produced by French authorities, without contemporary narration, inviting audiences to confront both the history captured on film and the human realities left outside the frame. Watch on Deadline “I was impressed with the historical authenticity and powerful emotional impact. This important documentary made an indelible impact on me and needs to be seen,” said Whitaker. “After seeing Rachid Bouchareb’s documentary, I became aware of the human consequences of the atomic bomb testing in Algeria. Rachid has unveiled the misuse of the testing and its long-range consequences on the local populations and land. The film sheds a necessary light on the devastation and makes you think about what its usage would mean in warfare today.” Boomerang Atomic Boomerang Atomic is part of a larger body of work the filmmaker has been developing around France’s nuclear tests in the Algerian Sahara. The short documentary serves as the first chapter of this project, which will continue with Reggane, a feature film currently in development with American and Japanese co-producer s. Moving from archival documentary to fiction, the two films aim to illuminate a largely overlooked history, giving voice to the local populations, soldiers, and workers exposed to nuclear fallout and exploring the enduring consequences of the tests across generations and borders. “Through this documentary, I aim to revisit the French nuclear test in Reggane on 13 February 1960: France’s first atomic explosion on Algerian soil. This is not only about recounting a historical event, but about giving voice to the archival images of the time and their commentary, while shedding light on the health, environmental and human consequences that remain today,” said Bouchareb. The DOC NYC screening will continue a worldwide tour for Boomerang Atomic which premiered Out of Competition at the Venice Film Festival in 2025 and has played at numerous film festivals since, winning the Audience Award at the 2026 Seoul International Eco Film Festival. The film was also presented in Hiroshima by UNITAR, the United Nations Institute for Training and Research program, this summer as part of commemorations for the dropping of the world’s first deployed atomic bomb on the city on August 6, 1945. The bomb detonated close to Reggane was four times more powerful than that used on Hiroshima. Bouchareb’s exploration of the events around France’s Reggane nuclear tests intersects with his wider body of work exploring colonial memory, immigration, exile, identity, and Franco-Algerian history Aside from Days of Glory , his other award-winning films include Dust of Life (1995) and Outside the Law (2010). Bouchareb and Whitaker first connected through the former’s 2014 feature Berlinale competition film Two Men in Town. Whitaker starred as a recently released convict attempting to turnaround his life opposite Harvey Keitel as a vengeful sheriff determined to put him back inside. articles.title: Terry Sanders Wraps Documentary ‘On Rescuing Democracy And The Rule Of Law’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart ‘Talk To Me’ Backer Head Gear Opens U.S. Arm With Ambitious Indie Investment Plan Sphere Media & Paul Barbeau Team Up To Bring TV Drama To Quebec Maxine Peake Boards Short Film ‘The Secret Assistants’ Exploring Power Imbalances In The Movie Business View All October 30, 2026 8:17am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Terry Sanders doc ‘On Rescuing Democracy And The Rule Of Law’ American Film Foundation EXCLUSIVE: Terry Sanders has finished his latest project On Rescuing Democracy and the Rule of Law . Two-time Oscar winner Sanders writes and directs the documentary. It explores the challenges and threats that established democracies, including the U.S., are facing and tells the story of the people who became involved with the Central and East European Law Initiative (CEELI) after the fall of the Berlin Wall. The doc tells the story of how more than 5,000 American lawyers, judges and legal experts became involved with CEELI, which was a pro bono initiative that provided technical legal assistance to former Soviet Bloc countries. Its work included helping to rewrite the constitutions of these countries, reform court systems, and adopt democratic rule of law principles. Related Stories News HBO's Harry Potter Casts Its Ghosts, Sorting Hat & Fat Lady On Halloween Eve News Forest Whitaker Joins Rachid Bouchareb's 'Boomerang Atomic' As EP Ahead Of DOC NYC Screening Former U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright has said: “In my judgment, CEELI is the most effective voluntary legal assistance initiative in history.” Watch on Deadline Veteran filmmaker Sanders is co-head of the American Film Foundation, which produced On Rescuing Democracy and the Rule of Law . His earlier work includes producing Oscar-winning short A Time Out of War and co-producing Maya Lin: A Strong Clear Vision , which won the Best Documentary Feature Oscar. The team behind the new film said it will document how populist surges have softened some countries’ resolve to protect established democratic rule of law, and how the U.S. experienced a violent assault on the Capitol on January 6, 2021. Sanders explained to Deadline his the 33-minute doc is in three parts. It starts at the end of WWII and the Cold War, before taking in the fall of the Berlin Wall and rise of democracy in former Soviet Bloc countries. It goes on to take in events including January 6, before looking at the rise of authoritarianism and concluding with segments on the situation today and where we head next. On Rescuing Democracy and the Rule of Law has contributions from Homer Moyer, co-founder of CEELI, Mark Ellis, Executive Director of the International Bar Association, Betsy Andersen, former Executive Director of the World Justice Project as well as Supreme Court Justice Sandra Day O’Connor and historian Corey Brettschneider. articles.title: ‘The Sun Never Sets’ Sells Out For Capture As Focus Features Swoops On Multiple Territories
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Female-Focused Circle Fiction Orbit Project Incubator Unveils 2026 Cohort NewFilmmakers Los Angeles Sets Partnership With Mar Del Plata International Film Festival Cinema Guild Takes North America For Berlinale Title ‘My Wife Cries’ View All October 30, 2026 8:19am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Dakota Fanning and Cory Michael Smith in 'The Sun Never Sets' Independent Film Company/Sapan Studio EXCLUSIVE: London-based Capture has declared that Joe Swanberg ’s romantic drama The Sun Never Sets , starring Dakota Fanning , Jake Johnson and Cory Michael Smith, is sold-out as it unveils a raft of international deals. The picture the film has sold to Italy (Minerva), Scandinavia (NonStop) Portugal (NOS), Turkey (Chantier), former Yugoslavia (Jucer), Middle East (Phoenicia), worldwide airlines (Cinesky). Focus Features has acquired the rest of the world (excluding Italy, Scandinavia, Portugal, Eastern Europe, the Middle East, and Latin America) with Universal Pictures International set to handle international distribution for the studio. Related Stories News Prestige International Pictures Boards SXSW Mexican Teen Body Horror 'Fifteen' - AFM Acquisitions Focus Features & Blumhouse-Atomic Monster Snap Up Micro-Budget Horror Film 'Play House' From Nicolas Curcio Shot on 35mm against the backdrop of Anchorage, Alaska, the film had its world premiere at the 2026 SXSW Film Festival. It was released theatrically in the U.S. by IFC Films and in Canada by Mongrel Media. Watch on Deadline Written and directed by Swanberg ( Drinking Buddies, Happy Christmas ), The Sun Never Sets stars Fanning as a free-spirited woman whose seemingly happy relationship with an older, divorced father (Johnson) is thrown into question when he suggests they take a break. When she then unexpectedly reconnects with her former boyfriend Chuck), a complicated love triangle develops forcing her to confront what she really wants from life and love. The ensemble cast also includes Debby Ryan, Anna Konkle, Lamorne Morris and Karley Sciortino. “ The Sun Never Sets has been a joy to represent, and the response from international buyers has been fantastic. We’re thrilled to have secured such a strong roster of distribution partners, including Focus Features across multiple territories, bringing a hugely successful international sales campaign to a close,” said Ella Field, EVP of International Sales at Capture. The film is produced by Swanberg, Fanning, Johnson, Smith and Ashleigh Snead. articles.title: Russell Brand Trial: Prosecution Weaponizes “Amusement Park Of Orgasms” Quote Star Used In Wendy Williams Interview
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake AI Dubbing Pioneer Flawless Sells Technology In Deal That Raises Questions About Its Future Russell Brand’s Wife Says Star Was “Caring” Lover At Time Of Rape Allegations BAFTA Launches Review Over Concerns About Trustees Accepting Free Awards Guest Tickets View All October 30, 2026 8:35am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand Getty Russell Brand ‘s October 2017 appearance on The Wendy Williams Show has been used against him during his rape trial in London. The prosecution evoked the chat show in closing remarks on Friday at Southwark Crown Court, where Brand is on trial over three charges of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one of attempted indecent assault. Deadline has been reporting daily on the trial from a live video feed of the courtroom. Riel Karmy-Jones, the prosecution barrister, told the jury: “Women were disposable … they didn’t matter to him [Brand]. They were the amusements, in what he described in a Wendy Williams interview as his ‘playground of orgasms.'” Related Stories News Russell Brand Rape Trial: Channel 4 Film Was Not "Magic Force" That Caused Accusers To "Recast" Memories, Court Hears In Closing Arguments Legal Russell Brand's Wife Says Star Was "Caring" Lover At Time Of Rape Allegations Karmy-Jones slightly misquoted Brand’s original words on Wendy Williams — which were that he thought “the world was like an amusement park made out of orgasms” when he was young — but she used it to illustrate her argument that the Despicable Me star was “rampant in his desire to have sexual contact whenever he wished.” It is not the first time the prosecution has referenced the Wendy Williams comment. Watch on Deadline In her final argument to the jury, Karmy-Jones alleged that Brand saw junior women in the workplace as a “disposable commodity.” Four of the six complainants worked in the television and radio industry at the time of their encounter with Brand. All have a lifelong right to anonymity, despite being identified in court and giving evidence during the trial. Karmy-Jones invited the jury to put themselves in the shoes of Complainant 6, a former Channel 4 employee, who alleged that Brand demanded a massage and “plonked his head, mouth, and nose into the area of her genitals” during a workplace incident in 2009. “How would you feel if someone in a position of power in your workplace did that to you?” she asked. Karmy-Jones began her closing remarks by reminding the jury that the six women behind the seven charges are “wholly unconnected” insofar as they “do not know each other and have never met.” She continued: “Six women who have nothing to gain, who have not sought the limelight, who have not taken part in documentaries, who have not made claims for compensation … There is no benefit to them.” Karmy-Jones said Russell Brand: In Plain Sight , the 2023 Channel 4 documentary, and reporting by The Times of London , had caused the women to come forward and tell stories about their encounters with Brand that had “haunted them for years.” In legal directions to the jury earlier on Friday, Mr Justice Bennathan, the judge presiding over the trial, said they must reach unanimous verdicts on each of the charges to convict Brand. He reminded jurors that the burden of proof is on the prosecution and that Brand is entitled to the benefit of the doubt. Bennathan expects the jury to begin verdict deliberations next Tuesday, November 3. The trial continues. articles.title: Pauly Shore Bringing Newest Special ‘Road Comic: Live From Portland’ To PlayStation 5 In November
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Chase Sui Wonders In Talks to Join A24’s ‘Goblin’ ‘Widow’s Bay’ Breakout Kate O’Flynn Joins Olivia Wilde Comedy ‘Naughty’ At Universal; Jamie Demetriou & Dexter Sol Ansell Also Set Jay Roach Producing Female-Driven Ensemble Comedy For New Line From ‘Fockers’ Collaborator Larry Stuckey And Joanna Leeds View All October 30, 2026 8:41am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EXCLUSIVE: Comedian Pauly Shore is set to release a new half-hour stand-up special, Road Comic: Live from Portland , via PlayStation 5 on November 1. Shore’s special is one of the first ever made available for free on-demand viewing via Live TV streaming on the gaming console, joining recent specials from the likes of Jeremiah Watkins, Jack Jr. and Paul Virzi. Live TV marks a departure from earlier viewing options: Previously, the options for PlayStation users were either to purchase specials through the PlayStation Store — something Sony discontinued for all film/TV in 2021 — or stream through third-party apps such as YouTube. Related Stories News Comedy Central Returns To Full-Length Specials With Chloe Radcliffe's 'Eyes Down Here' News Janine Harouni Dates New YouTube Stand-Up Special 'Man'oushe' In his new special, Shore gets personal — messing with the audience, looking back on being raised by comedians at the legendary Comedy Store, reminiscing about his former co-stars, opening up about health scares and getting into his beef with Will Ferrell at Equinox. Check out a trailer above. Watch on Deadline Shore taped the special at the Portland Helium Comedy Club in Portland, OR and will release it on his YouTube page on November 17. He lists Ronald McDonald and Burger King as the producers of his special, with Taco Bell as its executive producer; probably take those credits with a grain of salt. He directed the half-hour himself, with Comedy Compound Productions and Robot Pirate Media as the production companies involved. Born into comedy — the son of comedian Sammy Shore and longtime Comedy Store owner Mitzi Shore — Pauly has now been performing stand-up for nearly four decades. He broke out via his MTV show Totally Pauly , which ran for six years, before going on to roles in iconic ’90s comedies like Bio Dome and Encino Man , and starring in and producing his own projects, like Pauly Shore Is Dead . Over the years, he’s released myriad specials and albums, and he continues to expand his creative work through both stand-up comedy and independent film projects. Most recently, he teamed with Nick Swardson and Doug Jones on Remain Calm , a horror-comedy short from writer-director Jake Lewis that is approaching 10M views on YouTube. Shore is repped by Curate and Vox. articles.title: Jamie Lee Curtis, Filmmaker Skip Chaisson and Disney’s Frank Chiocchi Tapped for Clio Entertainment Honors (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All October 29, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jamie Lee Curtis Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Disney Oscar-winning actor Jamie Lee Curtis , filmmaker and producer Skip Chaisson and Frank Chiocchi, executive vp marketing at Walt Disney Studios, will be honored at the 2026 Clio Entertainment Awards . The event, taking place Nov. 19 at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles, will be hosted by comedian Cat Cohen. Curtis will receive this year’s Honorary Clio Entertainment Award “in recognition of her versatile five-decade career across film and television, and her enduring impact on the arts. With her iconic performance in Halloween , Curtis established herself as a defining scream queen and helped transform horror’s cultural standing, influencing how the genre was positioned and marketed to audiences for decades to come and cementing her place as one of its most influential figures.” More recently, Curtis won an Oscar for her performance in Everything Everywhere All at Once and an Emmy for The Bear . Related Stories Movies 'The Invite' to Receive Vanguard Award at Palm Springs International Film Festival Movies John Carpenter to Receive ACE's Golden Eddie Filmmaker of the Year Award Chaisson has been tapped for the Trailblazer Award, which recognizes “visionaries whose signature style and bold creative choices redefine the art of entertainment marketing.” Chaisson, who was chosen for his “influence on cinematic trailer storytelling,” is the founder of Skip Film and a creative force at Wild Card Creative Group. Throughout his career, he’s shaped campaigns for films including Titanic, Gladiator, Gravity and F1. He also launched El Rey Network alongside Robert Rodriguez. Chiocchi will receive the Lifetime Achievement Award, “honoring his decades-long impact on entertainment marketing and his role in shaping some of the industry’s most iconic campaigns. From his early work on Toy Story at Craig Murray Productions to blockbuster campaigns at Universal Pictures and Disney, Chiocchi has helped bring some of Hollywood’s biggest blockbusters to audiences around the world,” Clio Entertainment organizers said. He also spearheaded the creation of The Hive, Disney’s in-house creative agency. Cohen won best newcomer at the 2019 Edinburgh Comedy Awards for her acclaimed show The Twist…? She’s Gorgeous , which later became her Netflix comedy special. Her screen credits include Only Murders in the Building, Girls5eva and What We Do in the Shadows. Most recently, Cohen starred in and wrote Broad Strokes, an Off-Broadway one-woman show. Clio Entertainment aims to celebrate creativity in the entertainment business. Originally established by The Hollywood Reporter in 1971, the program is one of five verticals developed by the Clios to honor boundary-pushing marketing, advertising and communications that shape popular culture across film, TV, streaming, live entertainment and gaming. Each cycle, leaders from across the entertainment industry around the world convene to determine which entries will earn the Grand, Gold, Silver and Bronze Clio Entertainment Awards. This year’s Grand Clio and Of the Year Award winners also will be revealed at the Nov. 19 awards ceremony. As previously announced, this year’s Clios Entertainment Award jury chairs are: Audio Visual Broadcast TV: Melissa King, Senior VP Creative Marketing, Disney Entertainment Television Audio Visual Craft: Alex Wong, Creative Director, TRANSIT Audio Visual Streaming: Jennie Wilkes, Executive VP Creative Marketing, Paramount+ and Pluto TV DTC Audio Visual Theatrical: Benedict Coulter, Owner, Rebel AV Broadcast TV & Streaming Executive: Sohini Sengupta, Creative Marketing Executive, Disney Branded Entertainment Content & Partnerships: Jill Brody, Executive VP, Global Partnership Marketing, Universal Pictures Design: Bianca Parkes, Head of Marketing, Black Bear Digital & Social: Scott Addison Clay, Founder & CEO, Addison Interactive Experiential, Fan Engagement & Innovation: Val Aveni, Senior Lead, Film Marketing, Prime Video & Amazon Studios Games: Monica Austin, Chief Marketing Officer, Blizzard Entertainment Key Art: Göktuğ Sarıöz, Founder/Chief Creative Officer, Grandson Theatrical Executive: Susie Shen, Executive VP, Global Creative Strategy, Warner Bros.
