articles.title: Cannibals, Dostoevsky in Nepal and a Dark Fairy Tale: Rotterdam Fest Sets First 10 World Premieres
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 29, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Ali and Ben's Spicy Meats' Courtesy of IFFR The International Film Festival Rotterdam ( IFFR ) has unveiled the first wave of world premieres for its 56th edition, taking place Jan. 28- Feb. 7. Screening in the fest’s Bright Future and Harbour sections, the 10 first titles revealed on Thursday underline IFFR’s “commitment to singular cinematic voices, from emerging filmmakers to established artists returning to Rotterdam,” organizers said. IFFR’s Bright Future program focuses on debut films. The first four movies selected are “characterized by original subjects, from claustrophobic fairy tales to tragic personal experiences and an adaptation of Dostoevsky’s Crime and Punishment , representing the breadth of cutting-edge contemporary filmmaking,” organizers said. Related Stories Movies Elke Sommer, Actress in 'A Shot in the Dark' and 'The Prize,' Dies at 85 Movies Darren Aronofsky to Receive Director's Award at Camerimage U.S.-born Ben Hicks will bring Kids Go Free , made over 15 years across three countries, to Rotterdam, while Parbat Chapagai’s stylized Dostoevsky adaptation Portrait of a Young Criminal has also been selected for the fest. Further debuting at IFFR will be Lucila Las Heras’ dark fairy tale The Muglur and Mohamed El Zayat’s Egyptian ensemble dramedy In the Name of Galeela . Given Rotterdam’s identity as a port city, IFFR’s Harbour program is designed to be “a safe haven to the full range of contemporary cinema.” Its first wave of selected titles digs into themes of surrealism, divided identities and personal resilience. The Harbour strand will welcome back to IFFR Kiluanji Kia Henda, who will bring Karl Marx, Luanda , “following the presentation of his work in a Short Profile at IFFR 2020 and his commissioned performance Resetting Birds’ Memories (2021), and Kyros Papavassiliou with Yiannis , following his 2015 IFFR Tiger Competition film Impressions of a Drowned Man. Rita Hui Nga Shu also returns to IFFR, following the premiere of Decameron in 2021, with The Lapse . In addition, Ali Bakhtiari brings his debut feature, the documentary Tehran the Obscure Atelier of Desire , to the Harbour program, while siblings Iskander and Feisal Azizuddin will premiere their comedic cannibal horror movie Ali and Ben’s Spicy Meats , and Omer Shamir will debut the intimate docu-portrait Waiting Room . “Cinema is at its most exciting when it challenges our expectations, when filmmakers find new ways to express experiences, contradictions and realities that resist easy answers,” said Vanja Kaludjercic , festival director at IFFR. “These first 10 films already offer a glimpse of that incredible range, from the playful and provocative to the intimate and politically urgent. The fest on Thursday also shared details on its 2027 campaign, developed in collaboration with Rotterdam design studio 75B, and echoing IFFR’s focus on shining a spotlight on “artists finding new forms to express the experience of the world around them.” Check out all the first titles selected across IFFR’s 2027 Bright Future and Harbour sections below. BRIGHT FUTURE The Muglur (World Premiere) Director: Lucila Las Heras Mexico, Argentina Struggling to write a fantasy novel under the thumb of her alcoholic father, Aurora makes a Faustian bargain with a strange creature: the Muglur. But what price will it ask of her? The answer will be found at the dark heart of this claustrophobic fairy tale. In the Name of Galeela (World Premiere) Director: Mohamed El Zayat Egypt When money for a pilgrimage to Mecca is stolen, a young man’s community comes together to convince his blind grandmother that she’s still going. Egyptian filmmaker Mohamed El Zayat asks us how far we’ll go for someone we love in his endlessly creative debut feature. Kids Go Free (World Premiere) Director: Ben Hicks United States, Taiwan, Japan A taste for worldly adventures can bring passionate love and the thrill of the unknown, as well as niggling questions about economic security and one’s future. Told through a kaleidoscopic structure and a humanist lens over 15 years, Ben Hicks’ debut feature tackles these concerns in a miraculous manner. Portrait of a Young Criminal (World Premiere) Director: Parbat Chapagai United States, Nepal David, a destitute tutor, develops an attachment to teenage sex worker Sonya. Wishing to save her from the spiritual squalor of their surroundings, David resolves to kill his rich employer. A stark, psychologically vivid adaptation of Dostoevsky’s Crime and Punishment set in small-town Nepal. HARBOUR Karl Marx, Luanda (World Premiere) Director: Kiluanji Kia Henda Angola, Portugal Kiluanji Kia Henda’s satirical future history of Angola imagines that the nation renews itself as a Marxist state. Via a time-traveling love story and bold Afro-sci-fi-spaghetti-Western, we are reminded of a rare basic truth: in the forest, political doctrines do not help the rain fall. Ali and Ben’s Spicy Meats (World Premiere) Director: Feisal Azizuddin, Iskander Azizuddin Malaysia Ali and Ben, broke buddies running a failing pickle business, stumble upon a magic recipe made from human meat. When their overnight success attracts the suspicion of a local politician, the friends must do what it takes to protect their nascent empire in this zany horror-comedy. Waiting Room (World Premiere) Director: Omer Shamir France Fleeing from Khan Younis, award-winning Palestinian photojournalist Mohammed Zaanoun moves his immediate family to safety in Egypt, unsure of what’s to come. Filmmaker and activist Omer Shamir paints a moving documentary portrait of this family, in their exile home, across one year. The Lapse (World Premiere) Director: Rita Hui Nga Shu Taiwan, United Kingdom Hong Kong filmmaker and artist Rita Hui Nga Shu layers life, declassified governmental documents and her AI-cloned voice to open a dialogue between the promises on paper and the reality of life for Hong Kongers. An uncompromising, impactful and radically human film-essay. Tehran the Obscure Atelier of Desire (World Premiere) Director: Ali Bakhtiari Iran A contemporary documentary portrait of artists in their studios across Tehran. They return to unfinished canvases, abandoned experiments and sketches of future projects. They scrape, paint, sculpt and listen intently to music, while outside, the threat of war looms. Yiannis (World Premiere) Director: Kyros Papavassiliou Cyprus, Greece When his father’s body vanishes from the morgue, a Cypriot teenager and his mother cross into the occupied north to find Yiannis, a bird psychologist from his father’s past. Kyros Papavassiliou turns a missing-body mystery into a dreamlike journey through grief on a divided island rarely seen on screen. THR

articles.title: Paula Reid Joins MS NOW as Chief White House Reporter
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 29, 2026 7:05am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Paula Reid Photo by Paul Morigi/Getty Images MS NOW is officially adding a big name from CNN to its White House team. The cable news channel says that Paula Reid is joining as its chief White House reporter, where she “will bring her deep experience to covering the administration, serve as a key reporting voice across MS NOW’s Washington Bureau, and help drive our newsroom’s investigative and enterprise journalism,” per a memo to MS NOW staff from D.C. bureau chief Sudeep Reddy. Reid was one of CNN’s most high-profile correspondents, covering the Justice Department, Supreme Court and other legal matters. She was also a substitute anchor on many programs. She previously worked at CBS News, where she covered the DOJ and the White House. At MS NOW Reid will joining a White House team that includes director Scott Foster, senior White House reporter Vaughn Hillyard, and White House reporters Laura Barrón-López, Akayla Gardner, and Jake Traylor. And she joins it as the White House is in the midst of a battle with MS NOW, CNN and Politico over its coverage, having previously barred them from the grounds before a judge ordered their passes returned. Reddy and the MS NOW executive team have been building out an entire news organization since the split from NBC News last year, and Reid hire underscores how that work is not done yet. “Paula joins our intrepid team of White House reporters and producers who have been covering the Trump administration day in and day out since we first established a Washington Bureau,” Reddy wrote. “They have continued that work without missing a beat, even while navigating attempts to limit their ability to report from the White House. Together, Paula and the team will work to deepen our coverage of the White House and Washington and deliver the kind of authoritative, news-breaking journalism that audiences increasingly turn to MS NOW for.” THR

articles.title: AMC’s Infamous ‘Dune’ Sandworm Popcorn Bucket Is Back for ‘Part Three’ With New Designs
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By James Hibberd Plus Icon James Hibberd Writer-at-Large JamesHibberd Follow Sign Up View All October 29, 2026 7:07am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy Logo text This time, you can get cozy with sandworm popcorn bucket as a couple. AMC Theatres has revealed follow ups to its most infamous movie tie-in merchandise for Dune: Part Three . The sandworm popcorn bucket for Part Two , which became an online and retail hit, as well the target of a Saturday Night Live sketch, is back. This time, there’s Sandworm Thumper Collectible along with a Double Sandworm Collectible (the latter a double-worm design for two people sharing). Such products can significantly boost theater revenue, with collectible buckets often selling for $25 to $50. The Dune: Part Two bucket was credited with setting off a popcorn bucket merchandising frenzy, with Regal selling a bucket last year for The Fantastic Four: First Steps for a whopping $80. Related Stories Business AMC Global Media Chief Communications Officer Georgia Juvelis Exiting Later This Year Movies 'Dune: Part Three' Smashes 'Odyssey' Presale Record at London's BFI IMAX “The AMC Sandworm popcorn bucket for Dune: Part Two became a viral phenomenon, and we knew that Dune fans would have high expectations for what came next,” said Hank Green, SVP, Food & Beverage, AMC Theatres. “From the moment we started planning the Dune: Part Three collectibles, our goal was to exceed those fan expectations. The Sandworm Thumper and Double Sandworm collectibles take the experience to the next level with designs straight from the movie.” Both buckets will come with a large popcorn and be available at AMC locations in the United States and at Odeon Cinemas throughout Europe. AMC will also offer other Dune: Part Three collectibles, including drinkware, “mystery keychains,” and a Sandworm plush. The price of the bucket will be announced closer to the film’s Dec. 18 release date. SNL mocked the previous popcorn bucket’s suggestive design with a musical sketch where a high school student played by Marcello Hernández excitedly tells his friends that he’s going to lose his virginity to the Dune popcorn bucket (at one point singing, “I’m not scared of the teeth in the middle”). The Dune: Part Two bucket’s creator, Marcus Gonzalez of the Zinc Group, told the Wall Street Journal that sexual innuendo “was definitely not the intent,” and explained, “The worm’s the worm’s the worm.” Dune: Part Three has strong advance sales, with London’s BFI IMAX ticket sales beating a previous record set by Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey . Here’s a closer look at the two new buckets: Courtesy THR

articles.title: Bryan Adams Releases New Trump Protest Song “Lake Ontario”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 29, 2026 7:58am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Bryan Adams Gary Miller/Getty Images Canadian rocker Bryan Adams has released another Donald Trump protest song, “Lake Ontario,” included as part of his upcoming album, How’s It Goin . The single, released to YouTube and other social media platforms by the legendary musician, takes aim at the U.S. president, while never naming Trump directly. A music video for the single has Adams standing on a giant rock alongside Lake Ontario, which Trump renamed as Lake America as part of an executive order amid a tariff and trade war with Canada. “The lake of shining waters is what the Iroquois called her/ It’s the First Nations name, not an executive order,” assert Adams’ lyrics. The star rocker then insists the lake name change was a diversion from a faltering presidency. Related Stories Music Neil Young Sues Trump for Using "Rockin' in the Free World" at Rally: "The Opposite of Everything Donald J. Trump Stands For" General News Nicki Minaj Lands Press Secretary Buzz After Mock Briefing on Air Force One “Things weren’t going his way in Iran/ So like a baby tossing the toys from the pram/ He may have thought it best to throw a low blow/ And create a real dog and pony show/ But it feels like another distraction,” Adams says in his song’s lyrics. “While the Epstein files are getting traction/ One day they’ll come out and we’ll say ‘There you go’ / And then we’ll all dive into Lake Ontario.” Earlier this year, Adams released another protest song, “51st State,” timed for Canada Day, the nation’s birthday on July 1. That single release followed Trump making repeated taunts about Canada becoming a 51st U.S. state and launching a cross-border tariff war. Known for timeless hits like ”Summer of ’69,” ”Heaven” and ”Everything I Do (I Do It for You)”, Vancouver-raised Adams has made a name in the global music scene with his love ballads and rock anthems. He wa s inducted into the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2011 alongside Canada’s Walk of Fame and the Canadian Broadcast Hall of Fame. His How’s It Goin’ album will be released Nov. 6 via BAD Records. On his website, Adams called the “Lake Ontario” song a response to those looking to rename a perennial cross-border body of water. “Empires and regimes, dictators and kings, they all come and go. Lake Ontario is forever. This is a song for all the sane people on both shores who know that the current madness will pass, and that Lake Ontario will always be Lake Ontario,” he wrote. THR

articles.title: How Bill Paxton’s Son Took Over His Father’s Role in a Western 35 Years in the Making
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Seth Abramovitch Plus Icon Seth Abramovitch Senior Writer SethAbramovitch Follow Sign Up View All October 29, 2026 8:04am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Last Train to Fortune TriCoast Worldwide Malcolm McDowell is not known for his cheerier side — at least not in the roles he plays on screen. The screen legend, 83, became a star in Stanley Kubrick’s pitch-black A Clockwork Orange (1971). He later got swept up in the sword-and-sandal sordidness of Caligula (1979). More recently, he played Dr. Loomis in Rob Zombie’s Halloween films. So audiences may be surprised about his latest turn, playing a cheerful educator in the Old West with an affinity for the literary classics. The film is Last Train to Fortune , and its journey to VOD on Nov. 6 marks the end of a 35-year effort to bring the Western comedy to the screen. Related Stories Movies 'Psycho Killer' Review: Georgina Campbell and Malcolm McDowell in Gavin Polone's Inane Slasher Pic Movies "Failure Is Not an Option": An Oral History of 'Apollo 13' He originally planned to make the film in 1991 opposite Bill Paxton , who would have played the outlaw who agrees to safely accompany McDowell’s character to his new post. At the time, Lindsay Anderson, who gave McDowell his breakthrough role in 1968’s if…. , was attached to direct. But Anderson died in 1994. In 2017, McDowell suffered another shocking loss when Paxton died following heart surgery. “I talked to him two days before he went in and he said, ‘Oh, it’s a routine thing,’” McDowell recalls of his last conversation with Paxton. “I mean, it was terrible. It was just terrible.” It was veteran producer Brad Wyman, the producer of the 2003 Charlize Theron film Monster , who suggested reviving the film. McDowell still thought the script, by Michele Rifkin, held promise — and pitched James Paxton, Bill’s son, for the part meant for his late father. The three sat around a kitchen table and took a crack at a read — and James proved to be an inspired choice. The screenwriter’s son, Adam Rifkin, directs. The film also serves as a happy re-pairing with Mary Steenburgen. Steenburgen and McDowell met on the set of the 1979 time-travel thriller Time After Time , fell in love and were married from 1980 to 1990. They had two children, including Charlie McDowell, a film and TV director who has helmed episodes of HBO’s Silicon Valley . (Steenburgen has been married to Ted Danson since 1995.) McDowell says he asked James to make the offer to Steenburgen to play the schoolteacher he encounters in the film’s final act. She accepted, but later confronted her ex-husband on set. “The first thing she said, ‘Why didn’t you call me?’” McDowell recalls. “I went, ‘Well, you’re here. Let’s just leave it at that.’” “I can’t think of doing it with anyone else,” he continues of their reunion. “It was so natural and so comfortable to work with her.” Last Train to Fortune has drawn positive notices — it holds an 86 percent positive score on Rotten Tomatoes — with critics saying the film “belongs to McDowell” and crediting its “easygoing charm.” It is available to rent or buy on Apple TV and other services beginning Nov. 6. THR

articles.title: Earl Barret, ‘Too Close for Comfort’ Writer and Producer, Dies at 94
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All October 29, 2026 8:06am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Earl Barret Courtesy J.K. Barret Earl Barret, the veteran comedy writer who co-developed the Ted Knight-starring Too Close for Comfort and worked on more than 30 other series, including Bewitched , Get Smart , Batman and The Andy Griffith Show , has died. He was 94. Barret died Oct. 22 of natural causes at his home in Sherman Oaks, his daughter, J.K. Barret, announced. He was a “lifelong learner with a keen, curious mind and a gift for impeccable comic timing,” she said. The Ohio native also wrote for My Favorite Martian , My Three Sons , My Mother the Car , I Spy , The Wild Wild West , Julia , The Bob Newhart Show , Sanford and Son and Welcome Back, Kotter . Related Stories Movies Elke Sommer, Actress in 'A Shot in the Dark' and 'The Prize,' Dies at 85 Movies Barbara Barrie, Actress in 'Breaking Away,' 'Company' and 'Barney Miller,' Dies at 95 He and longtime writing partner Arne Sultan developed, wrote and produced Too Close for Comfort , which was based on the British sitcom Keep It in the Family , created by Brian Cooke. The American adaptation, which ran for six seasons (1980-87) on ABC and in syndication, revolved around Knight’s Henry Rush, a cartoonist who works out of the San Francisco home he shares with his wife (Nancy Dussault) and adult daughters (Deborah Van Valkenburgh, Lydia Cornell). Barret and Sultan first worked together on the 1969-70 CBS comedy The Governor & J.J. , starring Dan Dailey and Julie Sommars. They continued with NBC’s The Partners (Don Adams’ first series after Get Smart ), CBS’ The Sandy Duncan Show , ABC’s Holmes and Yoyo and The New Odd Couple and the CTV’s Check It Out (Adams starred on that one, too). The pair also were among the credited writers on the 1989 feature See No Evil, Hear No Evil , directed by Arthur Hiller and starring Richard Pryor and Gene Wilder . An only child, Barret was born on Oct. 17, 1932, in Canton, Ohio. His parents, Aurel and Mary, who owned a confectionery store, got him tap dancing and violin lessons as a youngster before the family came west, and he graduated from Hollywood High School and Los Angeles City College. He originally pursued a career as an actor but changed direction after taking a free TV-writing class taught by Robert C. Dennis, a scribe on shows including Perry Mason and Alfred Hitchcock Presents . “No matter how busy he was, no matter what show he was working on, he gave a free class every Wednesday night,” Barret noted. Barret wrote on 1961 episodes of Sea Hunt , Hawaiian Eye and Ripcord , and he and Dennis would later partner on scripts for Get Smart , My Mother the Car , The Andy Griffith Show and The Wild Wild West . For Batman , he and Dennis came up with the character of King Tut (portrayed by Victor Buono) when producers wanted new villains for the series (the actors playing Joker, Riddler and Penguin apparently were demanding too much money). The duo then wrote the episodes “The Curse of Tut”/“The Pharaoh’s in a Rut” and “The Spell of Tut”/“Tut’s Case Is Shut.” Barret landed a gig as a story editor on The Governor and J.J. , created by Sultan and Get Smart writer Leonard Stern, and before long, he and Sultan were writing for the political comedy. (Barret also directed an episode of the show; later, he would helm 13 installments of Too Close for Comfort .) Barret and Sultan also wrote the comedy Wife Begins at 40 for the stage, later a 1988 BBC telefilm. In addition to daughter J.K., survivors include his wife, Barbara; his son, John; and five grandsons. He was preceded in death by another daughter, Lisa. Barret’s memoir, Eden Was on a Hollywood Hill , was published in 2010. It “tells how a Romanian chauffeur and Hungarian American waitress marry after a one-week courtship and spend the next 50 years pursuing the American Dream through the Great Depression, World War II and finally to the enchanted hills of Hollywood, where they hope their tap-dancing, violin-playing son will break into the movies. And why shouldn’t he? Wasn’t anything possible in America?” THR

articles.title: Hollywood’s Hottest New Event: the Airbnb.org Gala?
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All October 29, 2026 8:13am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Joshua Jackson, Cynthia Erivo and Charlize Theron attend the 2026 Airbnb.org Gala on Oct. 28 in Los Angeles. John Shearer/Getty Images for Airbnb A hot new gala has entered the Hollywood events scene, from a slightly unexpected source. Airbnb .org — the nonprofit arm of Airbnb that offers free, temporary housing to people in need — threw its first-ever gala on Wednesday night, featuring a top-tier guest list at Los Angeles’ Milk Studios. Jimmy Kimmel hosted the evening as A-listers including Charlize Theron , Matthew McConaughey, Zoe Saldaña, Cynthia Erivo, Charli xcx , Joaquin Phoenix and Rooney Mara, Sienna Miller, Greta Lee, Serena Williams, Elizabeth Banks, Jessica Alba, Tracee Ellis Ross, Paul Bettany, Joshua Jackson, Ava DuVernay and Demi Lovato were all in attendance. Related Stories Movies Elle Fanning, Mckenna Grace and Kieran Culkin Get Very Candid About Joining 'The Hunger Games' Universe Lifestyle Art of Elysium Gala to Celebrate Rock Photographer Henry Diltz The event was timed to Airbnb.org’s new initiative where Airbnb will donate a portion of its revenue from every stay to its nonprofit, which will help provide $500 million to Airbnb.org over the next five years. This is all towards the goal of providing 1 million nights of free housing annually and expanding its support beyond disaster response to families traveling for medical care, survivors fleeing domestic violence and more. Since its founding in 2020, Airbnb.org has provided 1.6 million nights of free emergency housing worldwide and responded to more than 200 disasters in 2026 alone. “We wanted to do a celebration, a gala to really get the word out and let people know that we’re here to help and we want to be able to keep housing more people,” Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky said of arranging the big night, teasing that with the star-studded group of guests, “we mostly do housing but we have a really good team that can get a good turnout together.” Rooney Mara and Joaquin Phoenix with Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky and wife Carly Helfrich Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images for Airbnb Levi Alves McConaughey, Matthew McConaughey and Camila Alves McConaughey Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images for Airbnb Kimmel got the evening going with some classic Airbnb humor, teasing that at the event “we have some ground rules. Quiet hours start at 10 p.m.; if you use dishes, please bring them to the sink. No pets are allowed unless they’re service animals, which we know none of them really are. And no sitting naked on the furniture or on Chef José Andrés,” who curated the gala’s dinner menu. The host also joked, “At the end of the show, you’ll have 14 days to post a review of your experience tonight. Please be generous, I hope it’s positive.” Theron made a brief appearance on stage to speak about the domestic violence element of the housing initiative, noting, “if you’ve ever sat down with a survivor of domestic violence, you’ll know that somewhere to stay isn’t just a small thing, it’s actually everything. Because one of the hardest parts of leaving is not just deciding to leave, it’s having somewhere to go,” adding, “the key to a door is not charity, it is the foundation that everything else is built on.” Many of the stars spent the evening mingling in between dinner courses, and the event closed out with a surprise performance from Charli xcx, with Greta Lee, will.i.am and Jaden Smith all spotted dancing in front of the stage. Among the gala’s additional guests: Kelly Rowland, Katie Couric, Charli D’Amelio, Chloe Grace Moretz, Madelyn Cline, La La Anthony, Adéla, Emily Bader and Megan Rapinoe. Demi Lovato and Charli xcx Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images for Airbnb Greta Lee and Tracee Ellis Ross Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images for Airbnb THR

articles.title: Naomi Ritz, Costume Designer and Widow of Harry Ritz of the Ritz Brothers, Dies at 87
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All October 29, 2026 8:38am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Naomi Ritz Courtesy Janna Ritz Taninbaum Naomi Ritz, an artist, costume designer and widow of comedian Harry Ritz of the Ritz Brothers, has died. She was 87. Good friends with Frank Sinatra , Ritz died Aug. 31 at her home in Pinyon Crest, California, her daughter Janna Ritz Taninbaum announced. Naomi and Harry married at their Beverly Hills home on Nov. 21, 1965 (she was his fourth wife), and she traveled with her husband, made costumes for him and humorously described herself as his valet. They spent lots of time during the early years of Caesars Palace in Las Vegas and were together until his death in March 1986 at age 78. Related Stories Movies Barbara Barrie, Actress in 'Breaking Away,' 'Company' and 'Barney Miller,' Dies at 95 General News Dolores Huerta, Influential Labor Leader, Feminist and Civil Rights Icon, Dies at 96 The youngest and last surviving member of the Ritz Brothers, Harry, with his brothers Al and Jimmy — their real last name was Joachim — made up a zany comedy team whose celebrated career stretched more than 50 years, from vaudeville and Broadway and Fox and Universal films to nightclubs, television and Vegas. Sid Caesar once called Harry “the funniest man of his time,” and in a 1985 interview, Mel Brooks said: “In my mind, the word ‘genius’ should be reserved for one person — Harry Ritz.” From left: Harry Ritz, Al Ritz and Jimmy Ritz — The Ritz Brothers — in 1939’s ‘The Gorilla.’ Courtesy Everett Collection Naomi Leon was born in Hollywood on May 31, 1939. Her father, Freddie, was a bandleader during World War II with roots in vaudeville, and her mother, Zare, was an independent businesswoman. Her folks eventually operated a prop warehouse that served the film industry. She grew up in Vegas in the early 1950s and came of age among the hotels, theaters, nightclubs, performers and musicians in town. She first met Harry through her dad, who knew him through their vaudeville-era circles. For about 30 years, she made her home in Pinyon Crest, a mountain retreat near Palm Desert that was built by Sinatra in 1970 as a private escape for family and friends. He dubbed her home “Villa Maggio” as a tribute to Pvt. Angelo Maggio, the character he portrayed in his Oscar-winning turn in From Here to Eternity (1953). Ritz studied art and art restoration in Santa Monica and was a designer, collector and animal lover who rescued, cared for or found homes for more than 60 dogs. “Naomi was funny, charming, strong-willed, wonderfully particular and, at times, challenging,” her daughter said. “Mention an old Hollywood movie, however, and everything could change. She knew the films, the actors and the stories and could play the game of ‘who was in what’ endlessly — and usually win. “She leaves behind an eye for beauty, a fascination with the past, a house full of stories and collections, an enduring love of animals and a wonderfully individual way of seeing the world.” Donations in her memory can be made to Bet Tzedek Legal Services or WISE & Healthy Aging, supporting their work to protect older, vulnerable adults from abuse, exploitation and injustice. THR

articles.title: Mekai Curtis Looks Ahead to ‘Power: Origins’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ronda Racha Penrice Plus Icon Ronda Racha Penrice View All October 29, 2026 8:45am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Mekai Curtis in 'Power Book III: Raising Kanan.' Starz Logo text At the start of the final season of Powerbook III: Raising Kanan , boss Sascha Penn told The Hollywood Reporter the “whole reason the series exists is to deconstruct Kanan as you met him in Power and explain how he became who he became.” Given Kanan’s big presence in Power , it’s only natural that Kanan plays a big role in Power: Origins , which is the next series in the franchise that Penn is also spearheading. So far, most of the reports about the show largely regard it as the genesis of Tommy Egan and James “Ghost” St. Patrick, conveniently ignoring that it’s also a continued look at Kanan and his evolution beyond Raising Kanan . So while young Ghost and Tommy, played by Spence Moore II and Charlie Mann, respectively, keep getting all the buzz for the highly anticipated prequel series, Mekai Curtis is far from done as Kanan Stark. Considering Kanan didn’t die until deep into the next-to-last season of Power , there’s a lot for him to do, especially since the original series hints at a much closer relationship between the three in the very beginning. Related Stories Music Skilla Baby Won't Be Stopped TV Patina Miller and 'Raising Kanan' Boss Sascha Penn on Closing Their Tragic Chapter in the 'Power' Universe: "This Ending Always Made Sense to Me" Kanan Stark is not the role a young actor previously known for voicing Zack Underwood in Disney’s Milo Murphy’s Law , and also playing Fish Fisher in Disney XD’s Kirby Buckets , typically lands. When Raising Kanan debuted July 21, 2021, Curtis was roughly three months shy of his 21st birthday. After five seasons, however, there’s no denying that Curtis has made it his own. Confirming Kanan’s strong presence in Power: Origins with THR , Penn praised Curtis’ work: “What Mekai has done on Kanan is spectacular. He’s taken this this guy from a wide-eyed kid to somewhat of a shaded, grizzled veteran. Working with Mekai is truly one of the joys of my career. You can throw anything at him. His performances are incredibly nuanced and layered. I think he’s one of the best young actors working today, hands down.” Tony winner Patina Miller, who starred as Kanan’s mother Raquel “Raq” Thomas, recalled the big impression Curtis made on her during their first chemistry read. “I saw the hunger. I saw his ability. I saw what he would do with this role,” she says. “I saw someone not afraid knowing he had big shoes to fill. He took it and welcomed it with open arms, and this shit is not easy. “I’m grateful that I was given the space to do the thing and be bold and scared and fearless, because you throw caution to the wind and do the thing and it turned out beautiful,” adds Curtis. “I’ve gotten to grow as an individual, as a person, and I’ve gotten to grow in my artistry. I’ve gotten to grow at my craft. I’ve gotten to grasp a deeper understanding of it, a deeper love for it. This has been the breeding ground for what will be a very long and fruitful career. I’m excited I was given the space for it.” Careful not to say too much more about Power: Origins , Penn delivered the sad news that Tony Danza’s Stefano would not appear, and teased that Breeze would also be with Kanan. “That’s part of the Power lore, right? Which is that there’s tension between them. And the dynamic between [Breeze] and Kanan is absolutely complicated.” THR spoke to Curtis, revisiting key moments from Raising Kanan ‘s series finale, along with pulling whatever we could from him about the upcoming Power: Origins, which wrapped filming months ago. *** Let’s reflect on the big endings in Power Book III: Raising Kanan . How do you view the beatdown Marvin gave Kanan? It was justified. I think that’s part of the reason Kanan doesn’t necessarily fight back. Aside from the intensity of the beatdown and how vicious every punch has been, he has no room to rest. I think Kanan again just realizes this has been coming. Everybody up to that point thinks Kanan has no remorse or regret for what happened, but in reality, I think he’s just so overwhelmed with everything he’s feeling [that] he doesn’t necessarily know how to go about it or what to say [or] how to say it. Kanan clearly kills Marvin, but was it fair for Kanan to be blamed for Lou’s death when it was accidental? I mean he pulled the trigger. He didn’t mean to, but when you look at the amalgamation of everything happening, there’s pressure on everybody. Everybody’s world is kind of crashing down. And then what happens with Lou-Lou — because he’s he mediator and the glue in the family. That’s what him and Juke connect[ed] on a lot. Why did Raq finally tell Marvin that Kanan killed Lou? She holds on to information and uses it when she needs to. And that was the time for that to come out. She didn’t know what else to do. She felt like her back was against the wall. She’s hearing that her son and his organization are climbing up the ranks and breathing down her neck. So now it’s time to get things back in control, and that’s what happened with that scene. Talk about your process of taking Kanan from likability to villain. For me it’s never been about likability, [but] more relatability. I think that’s why people “liked” Kanan at first, because you can see a lot of the innocence and naivete, things that we all go through, wanting to experience [life] for yourself and bumping your head a few times in X Y Z. Now the person you turn into after these hard lessons, that’s two different sides of the coin. It depends on how you want to play the deck. Kanan is just going the way that anybody who has been in this environment and experienced what he’s gone through would. In so many ways, you become a product of the things you’re seeing and are around. So that’s what’s happening with Kanan. For me as the actor, it’s not about making sure he’s likable; it’s making sure you understand why he is the way he is at this point. So, is Raq to blame for who Kanan becomes? I think she’s partially to blame, but again, Raq is doing what she can with what she has, as all parents do. And you don’t always get it right. You don’t always have all the answers. You may think you do. You may know what you want or what you think is the best for your child, but your child is a person themselves, and they’ll experience things and make their own choices and decisions based off that. You’re just seeing two people deal with that. You’re seeing a mother protect her son, and a son trying to protect his mother in the way he knows and has been shown. Do you think [Hailey Kilgore’s] Jukebox chose the right route to make Kanan really suffer by killing Raq? Kanan was already suffering. Juke has been so stoic throughout the entire show [that] it makes sense it happened that way. It’s justified, but not justified. When I was reading the script, as Mekai, I understood Juke saying, “Now you’re gonna be alone, like I’m alone.” Revenge feels good for the moment. I think she did accomplish that, but we all see how that turned both of them even worse. Patina Miller as Raq with Mekai Curtis as Kanan in Power Book III: Raising Kanan. Starz In the very last episode of Raising Kanan , a baby Jamie and baby Tommy were introduced; how excited are you to continue this character going into Power: Origins ? It’s been fun. I’m excited. What we got to do with the last season of Raising Kanan was to bridge the gap even more, because people got to see an entirely different Kanan at the very beginning of Raising Kanan . So from there to season five of Raising Kanan , you see a slight part of his life and what turns him into that. Then going into Origins , you’re going to see how he took everything he learned in Raising Kanan and applies it to life now, and the people who are now his community that he’s trying to protect and love in the same way that Raq did for everybody in Raising Kanan . Speaking of that, what did Shameik Moore coming on as Breeze mean to Kanan, and what does it mean to you Mekai? It was exciting. I had been a fan of his work for a while, so it was exciting that I was going to have somebody to actually spar with for a little while. So, yeah, it was a good time watching him come in and fall into the fold and figure out his footing and see how this shit goes. It was dope. I enjoy getting to watch dope artists do their thing, so I’m glad he had fun. From the last couple of episodes of Raising Kanan , it looks like there might be tension for Kanan and Breeze in Origins . I can’t give too much away just yet. But it’s been fun to continue to craft the brotherhood and love of all this in the middle of there being drugs and guns and everything else. And now you’re going to be No. 1 on the call sheet, right? Oh yeah, it’s a blessing. I think the reps and the 10,000 hours have prepared me for it. So yeah, it’s been cool to step into that spot and be trusted to helm a ship that way. *** All five seasons of Power Book III: Raising Kanan, as well as all six seasons of Power, are streaming on Starz. Currently there is no official release date for Power: Origins. THR

She was 85. She died just three months after her husband, Wolf Walther, died of cancer. “Now she can finally be with her beloved husband again,” Sebastian Walther told Bild. Her family fled the capital during World War II and relocated to the small town of Niederndorf. In 1957, Sommer moved to London and became an au pair for the family of actress Vicki Michelle. articles.title: ‘Christmas at the Kringles’ Review: Seasonal Caper Mixes Comedy and Horror, Missing the Mark on Both
articles.full_text: × Oct 29, 2026 7:34am PT ‘Christmas at the Kringles’ Review: Seasonal Caper Mixes Comedy and Horror, Missing the Mark on Both Despite a solid cast featuring Ron Livingston, Rachel Bilson and Thomas Lennon, Kevin Lewis' pre-Halloween Christmas movie is tired and unfunny. By Todd Gilchrist Plus Icon Todd Gilchrist Latest ‘Trust Me, I’m a Doctor’ Review: Kal Penn and Abbie Cornish Star in a Minor Sidebar to the Anna Nicole Smith Story 2 weeks ago ‘Clean Hands’ Review: Zach Braff Is a Cop on a Crusade to Save His Addict Daughter in an Uneasy Fact-Based Crime Drama 2 weeks ago ‘Forgotten Island’ Review: A Delightful Animated Celebration of Friendship and Filipino Culture 1 month ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy Everett Collection The only thing rarer in the horror canon than a good holiday film is a good comedy. “ Christmas at the Kringles ” manages to miss the overlap in that Venn diagram by being awful on both counts: deeply cynical about the Yuletide season but also just completely unfunny. This failure all the more baffling given a cast populated by stalwart joke-makers including Ron Livingston , Rachel Bilson , Thomas Lennon, Arden Myrin, Rob Riggle, Donald Faison and David Wain, while director Kevin Lewis (“Willy’s Wonderland”) pilfers from the playbooks of better filmmakers to deliver a movie as stale and tasteless as last year’s fruitcake. Related Stories Why Netflix Fired Dan Lin Fueled by ‘La Bola Negra,' Spain’s Indie Distribution Make Robust Gains, to Be Highlighted at Valladolid's Merci Market Livingston (“The Flash”) plays Mark Severson, a workaholic stock trader who moves with his wife Julie (Bilson) and son Bobby (Jack Jewkes) to a small town as a band-aid to keep the family from falling apart. Arriving a week before Christmas, Mark halfheartedly tries to pull together a celebration for Bobby, but fate intervenes when the Seversons meet the Kringles, a family that celebrates the holiday year-round. When Nick Kringle (Lennon) invites them over for dinner on Christmas Eve, Mark surrenders his big-city skepticism at Julie’s request — and much to his surprise, they actually have fun. Two months later, Mark is even more immersed in work than ever, much to the disappointment of Julie, who was hoping for a proper Valentine’s Day celebration. When Nick’s wife Carol (Myrin) invites Julie and Bobby over for dinner, Mark is initially thrilled, but when he receives a warning from their neighbor Daryl (Faison) that the Kringles aren’t all they seem to be, he rushes over to check on them. When he finds that he’s locked out, he and Daryl reach out to a mall Santa (Riggle) who’s part of a network of fellow mirth-bringers; together, they have identified the Kringles as dangerous maniacs. But when Santa fails to show up at their house to back them up, Mark and Daryl are forced to go in by themselves in the hopes of rescuing Julie and Bobby before the Kringles put the entire Severson family permanently on the naughty list. Written by Zack Imbrogno, “Christmas at the Kringles” feels like it’s been cobbled together from any number of other, much better movies, in the hope that seasoned improvisers like Lennon and Riggle can make the end result coherent. After a cold-open chase scene featuring a screaming woman and a murderer in a Santa Claus suit that seems entirely uninterested in either spatial geography or visual continuity, editor Ryan Leibert seems to embrace its disjointed pacing for the rest of the film. As the main story gets under way, there’s barely enough time for Livingston, Bilson and Jewkes to deliver their expository introductions before Mark almost plows into Santa, setting an ominous tone for their move to the suburbs. Julie’s desperate desire for small-town community is drawn one-dimensionally, but in comparison to Mark, Bilson’s character is a portrait in nuance. She reveals early that they’re looking to rekindle some of the magic in their relationship, but with Mark, it’s hard to understand why she even bothers. Livingston plays him like a jaded, unhappy dick who only barely begins to develop deeper humanity as the story progresses, and even after he decides to fight for his family he is alarmingly ineffectual. Ironically, his old “Swingers” costar Vince Vaughn would have been perfect for the role — he’s always been skilled at balancing a bitter edge with more sweetness — but for context, Livingston delivers a performance here about as likable as his notoriously awful “Sex and the City” boyfriend Berger. By comparison, Lennon and Myrin play the Kringles like they’re relatives of Adam Scott’s self-important helicopter leasing agent from “Step Brothers,” heckling the sour notes in their son’s recorder playing and championing their holiday life choice with a cult member’s zeal. Lennon’s always been a comedian who commits to a bit, for better or worse, but what he delivers in unhinged wholesomeness he lacks in true menace once the danger escalates for the Seversons. Riggle, meanwhile, has played a character like this (albeit not one with Saint Nick’s pedigree) a few dozen times already, so his comic contributions are reliable if not terribly fresh. On the other hand, “Scrubs” star Faison manages to inject effective (and funny) incredulity into the final siege by Mark and Daryl on the Kringles’ house. As the shepherd of Imbrogno’s uninspired script, Lewis tries to zhuzh up the material with quick-cut montages stolen from the likes of Edgar Wright, but none of it adds up to anything meaningful, or even entertaining. The “explanation” for the Kringles’ behavior is not only dumb, but it makes little sense: Are the three children living in their house their actual kids? Is there really no recourse for worried neighbors from the cops, despite what appears to be repeated disappearances connected to them? And why the hell is there a Christmas gimp living in their home? The movie prompts many questions, but it’s so badly done, you don’t really care what the answers are. Yet the thing about horror fans, even ones expecting filmmakers to hit the bullseye between a challenging tone (comedy) and topic (holidays), is that they are notoriously forgiving — if there’s something, anything there. But to ride out the metaphor that this film invites, “Christmas at the Kringles” is like a gift-wrapped box with nothing inside. Visually obnoxious but uninventive, featuring actors giving uninspired performances as characters you don’t care to see live or die, it lacks even an ounce of the joy that its eponymous family claims is their reason for living. Well, except for when it’s over. ‘Christmas at the Kringles’ Review: Seasonal Caper Mixes Comedy and Horror, Missing the Mark on Both Reviewed online, Oct. 28, 2026. MPA Rating: R. articles.title: NewsNation Plans Fast-Paced Election Night Focused on Hot Data, Not Hot Air
articles.full_text: × Oct 29, 2026 8:10am PT NewsNation Plans Fast-Paced Election Night Focused on Hot Data, Not Hot Air By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest NewsNation Plans Fast-Paced Election Night Focused on Hot Data, Not Hot Air 32 minutes ago TelevisaUnivision Q3 Buoyed by World Cup in Mexico, Streaming Revenue 5 hours ago Versant Expands Suite of FAST Channels With 4 New Selections From CNBC, E!, Oxygen 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of NewsNation NewsNation has a different kind of recipe for Election Night — heavy on stats, light on the gas. When the Nexstar cable-news outlet launches five hours of coverage of the nation’s 2026 midterm elections on November 3, it will do so with the intent of keeping viewers interested in key results and on-the-ground reporting, giving them so much of it they won’t be craving the usual analysis and roundtable chatter. Related Stories Sex, Love and War: How the Racy Gay Epic ‘La Bola Negra’ Could Win Netflix’s First Best Picture Oscar Netflix Lays Off 6% of Employees, Eliminating About 1,000 Jobs in Biggest Cutbacks to Date “I think what are aren’t going to have is a lot of noise,” says Page Lobdell, executive producer of special projects and events for NewsNation, during a recent interview. “All the opinion and the commentary and the talking heads sitting around a table giving their talking points, we are going to want to cut that out.” Executives at the network hope their coverage reminds some viewers of “NFL RedZone,” the “whip-around” format that takes viewers to important moments as they happen. The network is, as it has during recent coverage of elections, relying on Decision Desk HQ, a tabulator of voting data that enjoys a good record as an early caller of key races. That company’s data-miners will hold forth in a “war room” at Georgetown University and will offer behind-the-scenes looks at how the team analyzes incoming stats and makes its pronouncements. “More transparency is better,” says Chris Stirewalt, NewsNation’s political editor. “We live in an era of data. We live in an era of prediction markets. People have an expectation of what they are going to get and when they are going to get it. We can do that.” NewsNation will vie for attention Tuesday night with a growing host of media outlets that will also be covering elections. Some are bigger rivals like CNN or NBC News. Others are nimble start-ups led by digital “creators,” some of whom once worked in traditional media. Either way, says Stirewalt, NewsNation thinks it has an edge. Decision Desk HQ proved to be a pivotal ally. The company’s data helped NewsNation become the first network to call Donald Trump the winner of the presidential election in 2024. “I can’t promise you we are going to be first calling the House. I can’t promise you we are going to be first calling the Senate majority. I think we are going to be right before we are going to be first,” says Stirewalt. “I can tell you that the track record says if you are a betting person, you might put your wager on DDHQ and NewsNation.” The “whip-around” format has been making its way from sports to other genres. “RedZone” has become a popular offering for NFL die-hards on Sundays, but in recent years NBC Sports has unveiled a “GoldZone” that helps viewers dip in and out of sundry events during its many hours of Olympics coverage. CBS’ stations have played an instrumental role in a format that takes viewers to news events taking place in different parts of the country that are covered by CBS’ local newsrooms . Election Night can also be a good time to promote other parts of a network. The network’s regular evening hosts, Chris Cuomo, Elizabeth Vargas, Leland Vittert and Katie Pavlich, will co-anchor the evening’s proceedings from Washington, D.C, with Stirewalt and Connell McShane in New York ready to pore through data and stats. NewsNation can tap into resources from dozens of Nexstar stations around the country, and will have its own correspondents spread out around the nation. “We have a camera in a campaign headquarters at nearly every single race across the country,” says Lobdell. NewsNation’s on-air team will have a lot to study. Will results on the east coast serve as an indicator of how other states will vote? Stirewalt says he intends to keep a close eye on Ohio and North Carolina to see whether they eventually tilt red or blue. He also wants to see what the election says about the future of both Democrats and Republicans. Will the Democrats have to contend with left-wing insurgents like Republicans did the Tea Party? What will Republican voting say about the appeal of Vice President JD Vance? To deal with all these storylines, he says, the team needs to focus on numbers ,and not pontification. “We are not going to make you hear the same tired arguments again and again,” says Stirewalt. “What people want are results.” ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ VFX Boss Jerome Chen on Hulk’s Redesign, Finishing 445 Shots in a Week Loading comments...

Stock’s appointment at Hearst Magazines will be effective Jan. 1, 2027. Debi Chirichella, who has served as president of Hearst Magazines since 2020, will become chair of the group. Stock and Chirichella will report to both Steven R. Swartz, president and chief executive officer of Hearst, and Jordan Wertlieb, EVP and COO. For Stock, it’s a return to the magazine world: Prior to A+E, she worked for 11 years at Condé Nast, most recently as senior director of business and product development. Hearst’s hiring of Stock comes after it recently tapped another TV veteran for a key position: Chris Berend , previously chief digital officer of the NBCUniversal News Group, who joined Hearst Magazines this summer as chief content and experience officer. “We welcome Juliana back to the magazine business after more than a decade of leadership positions across digital video, marketing and general management at our A+E Networks,” Swartz said in a statement. “With Debi’s help, she will build on our great brands and great people to lead the next phase of growth in this business in which we have enjoyed a leadership position for more than 100 years.” Stock said in a statement provided by the company, “Hearst Magazines sets the standard for lifestyle journalism, and I’m honored to join a group with such powerful brands and such a talented team. Audiences are engaging with our content in more ways than ever, including digitally, and there’s a real opportunity to deepen those connections while continuing to deliver the trusted, high-quality print experiences our readers love. I’m grateful to Steve, Jordan and Debi for their confidence and excited to get to work.” In 2025, Stock was promoted to president of marketing and digital at A+E Global Media. In the role, she led the company’s trade and global consumer marketing, digital strategy and audience engagement initiatives across a portfolio that includes A&E, History, Lifetime, FYI and LMN. Stock is credited with reshaping the company’s marketing approach by realigning operations around “audience-first strategies.” On the digital side, Stock oversaw the A+E Global Media ecosystem. She led initiatives including the relaunch of History.com, the scaling of direct-to-consumer products (History Vault, Lifetime Movie Club, A&E Crime Central) and the growth of audiences across social platforms and YouTube. Since joining A+E Global Media in 2013, Stock held senior positions including chief marketing and brand officer. articles.title: Milwaukee Brewers Win First World Series In Franchise History
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Tom Tapp Tom Tapp Deputy Managing Editor More Stories By Tom Milwaukee Brewers Win First World Series In Franchise History Layoffs Hit Disney Experiences Ernie Johnson Leaving ‘Inside the NBA’ After This Season: “It’s Just Time” View All October 28, 2026 10:49pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Trevor Megill of the Milwaukee Brewers celebrates with teammates after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in the 2026 World Series Mike Stobe/Getty Images Somewhere up in heaven, Bob Uecker is cracking open a cold Miller Lite. The now-departed Uecker, more famous for his beer commercials than he ever was for his modest career as a MLB catcher, was the Milwaukee Brewers’ radio announcer until 2024. And tonight, as the team won its first-ever World Series , his 54 years in the booth were not forgotten. Related Stories News Fox World Series Hopes Revived By Tampa Rally, But A Wall Street Firm Sees Limited Hit From Shorter Series Trailers ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ World Series Sneak Peek Sees Mister Fantastic Throw Out First Pitch In his postgame locker room speech tonight, Brewers’ manager Pat Murphy carried on his schtick of delivering Uecker’s “messages” to the team from the great beyond. Here is the mesage, per The Athletic : Watch on Deadline “So, Ueck sent me a text today. He said, ‘Look, I helped you against the Padres. And I messed with the Dodgers a little bit. And then you came here, and you were on your own, because we had a doubleheader and they actually let me catch the last three innings of the game. But you did it for the city, you did it for the state, and you boys oughta be awfully proud to know that you’re the first-ever Milwaukee Brewer team to be world champions.'” Not that the Brewers needed any help. They were clearly the best team in Major League Baseball all season. They had the best record and stormed through the postseason, sweeping the two-time defending champion L.A. Dodgers to win the NLCS and beating the Tampa Bay Rays in a gentleman’s sweep, four games to one, in the World Series. In that’s quite a feat for the team from the league’s smallest market especially since, in its 57 years of existence, the club had never won the final game of the season. After taking each of the first two games in this year’s World Series by one run, the Brewers destroyed the Rays 10-0 in Game 3. Tampa Bay regained some dignity last night with a 4-3 win before being dominated again tonight. Milwaukee led from the second inning on. They went up 4-0 in the 6th when Brewers catcher William Contreras (later named series MVP) drove in Christian Yelich to score the team’s final run. Tampa Bay got some consolation in the bottom of the 9th when Chandler Simpson doubled to deep right field and brought Liam Hicks in to score. But it was Milwaukee’s night — and year. articles.title: Toho CEO Matsuoka Hiro On The Company’s Decision To Self-Distribute ‘Godzilla Minus One’ In The U.S. — Tokyo
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Toho CEO Matsuoka Hiro On The Company’s Decision To Self-Distribute ‘Godzilla Minus One’ In The U.S. — Tokyo How A Former Senior Netflix Staffer Launched One Of Japan’s Buzziest Indie Cinemas Yuriko Gamo Romer & Marc Smolowitz On The 12 Year Journey Behind Their Japanese-U.S. History Baseball Doc ‘Diamond Diplomacy’ — Tokyo View All October 29, 2026 12:10am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Toho International / Courtesy Everett Collection “It was all a coincidence,” Toho CEO Matsuoka Hiro said this afternoon during a Q&A at the Tokyo Film Festival when quizzed on his company’s decision to re-enter the U.S. market in 2023 to distribute Takashi Yamazaki’s box-office hit Godzilla Minus One. Godzilla Minus One opened Stateside in December 2023 and earned more than $11.4 million on opening weekend, becoming the biggest Stateside debut of a foreign film that year and the highest-grossing live-action Japanese film in North America. Matsuoka told an audience at this afternoon’s Q&A alongside AMPAS CEO Bill Kramer that until Godzilla Minus One, Toho had repeatedly failed to successfully distribute its films outside Japan, particularly in the United States. Related Stories News 'Merry Berry Love' Producers Nippon TV & CJ ENM Talk Korea-Japan Collaboration To Boost J-Drama - TIFFCOM News How A Former Senior Netflix Staffer Launched One Of Japan's Buzziest Indie Cinemas The veteran exec said he only refocused efforts on launching a film in the U.S. after he visited the exhibitors union during a Stateside trip and was told the U.S. studios weren’t making enough films to satisfy audience appetite. Watch on Deadline “When I became president of Toho, I went to the U.S. and the people from the box office union said the studios weren’t making enough films,” Matsuoka said. “They said to me, ‘Why don’t you think of making some anime,’ and that’s when I realized anime was popular in the US. We also already had Godzilla, so we decided to distribute it in the US.” Matsuoka said there was concern across Toho when he first suggested they distribute Godzilla Minus One across the U.S. themselves. But the film was ultimately a success, and most importantly, he said, “brought the profit to us.” “It wasn’t a strategy; we just tried,” Matsuoka added. Next week, the latest Godzilla film, Godzilla Minus Zero, will open in Japan and the U.S. following its bow at the Tokyo Film Festival . articles.title: Cannes Marché & TIFFCOM Commit To Holding Second Edition Of Japan IP Market In 2027
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz TBS Unpacks Collaborations With Legendary & Korea’s CJ ENM: “We Want To Create A New Global Genre Of J-Content” Cannes Marché & TIFFCOM Commit To Holding Second Edition Of Japan IP Market In 2027 ‘Merry Berry Love’ Producers Nippon TV & CJ ENM Talk Korea-Japan Collaboration To Boost J-Drama – TIFFCOM View All October 29, 2026 1:22am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Tao Okamoto and Virginie Efira accept Best Actress at Cannes Film Festival 2026 Stephane Cardinale - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images Cannes Marché du Film and Tokyo International Film Festival Content Market ( TIFFCOM ) have announced that they will co-organize the Japan IP Market in Cannes for a second consecutive year, from May 14-15. The announcement was made at TIFFCOM during the seminar ‘Beyond Country of Honour: Building the Next Global Partnerships with Japan’, featuring Alexandra Zakharchenko, Head of Industry Programs at the Marché du Film, among the speakers. Launched in May 2026 as part of Japan’s Country of Honour activities at the Marché du Film, the Japan IP Market brought leading Japanese rights holders together with international industry professionals through pitch sessions, targeted one-to-one meetings and industry discussions. Related Stories News Toho CEO Matsuoka Hiro On The Company's Decision To Self-Distribute 'Godzilla Minus One' In The U.S. -- Tokyo News 'Merry Berry Love' Producers Nippon TV & CJ ENM Talk Korea-Japan Collaboration To Boost J-Drama - TIFFCOM Participating companies included Kadokawa, Shochiku and Toei Company, while guest speakers included Filosophia Inc CEO Tetsu Fujimura, who was an executive producer on One Piece . Watch on Deadline Japan had a big presence at both the Cannes film festival and market this year. In addition to being selected as Country of Honor in the Marché, three Japanese films were selected for Cannes Competition and several others played in other sections of the festival. Japanese actress Tao Okamoto was a joint winner of the festival’s Best Actress award, along with Virginie Efira, for their roles in Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s All Of A Sudden . “The success of Japan, Country of Honour showed what can happen when a focused national presence creates lasting opportunities for the industry. The Japan IP Market is one of those outcomes: a collaboration that extends beyond a single edition and gives Japanese intellectual properties greater access to international partners,” said Guillaume Esmiol, Executive Director of the Marché du Film. “I’m delighted that we are continuing this work with TIFFCOM to create more opportunities for rights holders to connect with international producers and partners, develop new adaptations and bring their stories to global audiences.” Zakharchenko said: “The Japan IP Market is about creating the right conditions for business opportunities between Japanese rights holders and international companies,” says Alexandra, Head of Industry Programs at the Marché du Film. “By bringing them together in Cannes, we can help turn growing interest in Japanese content into concrete adaptation deals and acquisitions, while fostering new collaboration opportunities.” TIFFCOM CEO Yasushi Shiina said: “Our partnership with the Marché du Film, the world’s largest film festival market, plays a significant role for Japan’s audiovisual industry. Meeting the international professionals who gather there and creating together with them is the key to nurturing Japanese IP into global content. I am grateful to the Marché du Film for its focus on Japanese IP and for co-organizing the Japan IP Market with us once again next year.” Kaori Ikeda, TIFFCOM Managing Director, said: “At the inaugural Japan IP Market, we experienced the enthusiasm of producers and partners worldwide for Japanese IP,” adds “Through the continued partnership linking Cannes in May with the Tokyo IP Market in October, we are pleased to offer more professionals the opportunity to meet Japanese rights holders directly and discover the rich diversity of Japanese IP.” Further details on participating companies and the 2027 program will be announced in coming months. ‘The Diplomat’ Renewed For Season 5 At Netflix, Two Weeks After S4 Arrival Marcus Theatres Posts Record Q3 Led By ‘Spider-Man’, ‘The Odyssey’ Amid Boom Skydance Sets Leadership Team For Studios, Entertainment, News & Sports LaKeith Stanfield Exits ‘Molepeople’ As Ben Wheatley Replaces Rob Savage At Helm Read More About: Comments

articles.title: BAFTA Launches Review Over Concerns About Trustees Accepting Free Awards Guest Tickets
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake BAFTA Launches Review Over Concerns About Trustees Accepting Free Awards Guest Tickets BBC “Disappointed” As Staff Plan Industrial Action Vote Over Job Cuts Russell Brand Forcefully Denies Charges As He Gives Evidence During Rape Trial: “Consent Is More Important Than Sex Itself” View All October 29, 2026 1:52am Add us as a Google Preferred Source BAFTA Mask BAFTA BAFTA has launched a review after its trustees were accused of potentially breaching UK charity law by accepting free guest tickets to awards ceremonies. During BAFTA’s annual general meeting this week, Michael Pritchett, an independent film producer who serves as the elected chair of BAFTA’s membership council, raised concerns about whether trustees broke rules that prevent them from receiving remuneration or benefits. Pritchett alleged that trustees had received complimentary tickets for themselves and a guest at BAFTA’s film, television, and games awards, according to a transcription of his remarks seen by Deadline. He claimed that the custom had been ongoing for up to 20 years, with guests receiving top-table tickets potentially worth up to £2,000 ($2,665) for the film awards. Related Stories News BAFTA Names New Chair News BAFTA Makes Plans For 'I Swear's John Davidson To Attend Scotland Awards After N-Word Scandal Pritchett — who said he had been privately raising concerns with BAFTA officials for months — added that trustees approved accounts, which state that no trustees received any remuneration during the year for their services. Watch on Deadline Speaking at the AGM, Pritchett said he had paid for legal advice at his own expense, which concluded that “offenses under the Charities Act and the Companies Act are likely to have been committed by the trustees who approved those accounts.” Pritchett also raised questions over whether BAFTA had properly paid tax on the tickets. “Since 2016, a benefit like this is likely to have been taxable, with National Insurance payable by BAFTA. BAFTA has not told me that anything has ever been reported. So I can’t assure you whether it has or hasn’t,” he said. BAFTA stopped offering plus-one tickets to trustees last year following a recommendation from its governance committee. It has now launched a review of ticketing arrangements, which is being led by a group of three unnamed industry executives. A BAFTA spokesperson said: “Trustees of BAFTA are invited to attend events in a working capacity, representing the Academy in an ambassadorial role, and prior to 2025 they could also bring a ‘plus one’ guest to accompany them. “In 2025 BAFTA decided to review its guest tickets arrangements and discontinued the long-standing custom and practice of trustees inviting a plus one. The board has since established an independent review group to consider the historic guest ticket arrangement – the review is underway.” BAFTA stands by the practice of offering trustees themselves free tickets, believing it is part of their duties to attend events and act as ambassadors for the charity. BAFTA’s trustees, who provide their services voluntarily, include new chair, Hilary Rosen. Pritchett was also critical of BAFTA’s refusal to hand over records of who had received free awards tickets. He said his request was refused by a senior BAFTA executive, with “no policy cited.” During the annual general meeting, Sara Putt, BAFTA’s former chair, revealed that the Academy had obtained its own legal advice based on a fuller picture of the ticketing issue. articles.title: Pippa Harris & YouTube UK Boss Alison Lomax Join Board Of National Film & Television School
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max ‘Sweetpea’: Ella Purnell Is Back In Killer Role As Full Trailer Drops For Season 2 Of Sky And Starz Series ‘The Cube’ Creator Adam Adler Joins Channel 4’s Production Biz As Creative Director Pippa Harris & YouTube UK Boss Alison Lomax Join Board Of National Film & Television School View All October 29, 2026 2:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Pippa Harris (left) and Alison Lomax Taylor Hill EXCLUSIVE: Storied British producer Pippa Harris and YouTube UK boss Alison Lomax have joined the board of Britain’s National Film and Television School ( NFTS ). The pair join the likes of BBC content boss Kate Phillips and Sky Studios CEO Cécile Frot-Coutaz on the governors board. They bring together film and TV production expertise with digital as the school continues to evolve, according to the NFTS. Double Oscar nominee Harris is the founder of Neal Street and has been behind the likes of 1917, Call the Midwife and Hamnet. Upcoming she has Sam Mendes’ quartet of Beatles movies. As YouTube UK and Ireland boss for nearly four years, Lomax occupies a different lane. She has overseen serious growth for the Google-owned platform in the UK and has impressed traditional TV executives along the way. Related Stories News YouTube Ad Revenue Rises 9% But Parent Alphabet Misses Wall Street's Q3 Targets; Stock Drops News Entertainment Hits $332.5B To Become World's Second Most Valuable Sector As Netflix, YouTube & Spotify Fly - Interbrand Report Alongside Harris, Lomax, Phillips and Frot-Coutaz, the NFTS board is comprised of Roughcut TV founder Ash Atalla , Film4 Director Farhana Bhula, ITV Studios MD Julian Bellamy and ex-Warner Bros. Discovery VP Polly Cochrane. Watch on Deadline The appointments come at a significant moment for the NFTS as it prepares to open The Cubby Broccoli Building at its Beaconsfield HQ in January 2027. Supported by government and industry investment, the school’s expansion will provide 25,000 sq. ft. of additional teaching space, house new courses, expand apprenticeship opportunities and provide accessible student accommodation for the first time in its history. NFTS Chair Sophie Turner Laing said: “The way audiences discover, engage with and enjoy stories is changing at an extraordinary pace, and it’s vital the NFTS continues to reflect the full breadth of the industries our graduates are being trained to enter. Pippa and Alison bring hugely valuable and complementary perspectives, from the craft and ambition behind some of the world’s most successful film and television productions to the phenomenal growth of digital creators and new platforms. Both are exceptional leaders with a real commitment to creative talent, and I’m delighted they will be bringing their insight and experience to the Board at such an important moment for the School.” Harris added: “It is an honour to be joining the Board of Governors at the NFTS. The strength of our industry ultimately depends on the talent coming through and on ensuring that people from all backgrounds have the opportunity to develop their skills, find their voice and build lasting careers. The NFTS has an extraordinary track record of nurturing creative talent and I’m very much looking forward to playing a part in its next chapter.” Lomax said: “The National Film and Television School is globally renowned as a world-class training ground for craft, technical excellence, and storytelling. Its educational mission has never been more relevant as traditional production and creator-led entertainment increasingly converge. Through YouTube’s NFTS partnerships, including our Creator Incubator and Create x Connect, I’ve been deeply impressed with the School and am committed to opening access, building digital skills nationwide and championing the next generation of creative talent.” ‘The Diplomat’ Renewed For Season 5 At Netflix, Two Weeks After S4 Arrival Marcus Theatres Posts Record Q3 Led By ‘Spider-Man’, ‘The Odyssey’ Amid Boom Skydance Sets Leadership Team For Studios, Entertainment, News & Sports Gregory Nava Mourns Civil Rights Leader Delores Huerta, Updates On Biopic Plans Read More About: Comments

articles.title: TBS Unpacks Collaborations With Legendary & Korea’s CJ ENM: “We Want To Create A New Global Genre Of J-Content”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Cannes Marché & TIFFCOM Commit To Holding Second Edition Of Japan IP Market In 2027 ‘Merry Berry Love’ Producers Nippon TV & CJ ENM Talk Korea-Japan Collaboration To Boost J-Drama – TIFFCOM Amazon MGM Studios Japan To Double Investment In Original Content; ‘One Piece’ & ‘Kingdom’ Producers Talk IP Strategies – TIFFCOM View All October 29, 2026 2:23am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Alice In Borderland Season 3 The Seven, Netflix TBS Holdings executives outlined the strategy behind the Japanese broadcaster’s tie-ups with Legendary Entertainment and Korea’s CJ ENM in a TIFFCOM presentation today. In January 2026, TBS acquired a $150M minority stake in Legendary and entered into a non-exclusive agreement with the Dune and Godzilla franchise producer to source and develop Japanese IP. Katsuaki Setoguchi, TBS Holdings Executive Officer, Global Business Division, opened the presentation by explaining why the Japanese broadcaster made this move: “Why did we partner with Legendary? Our needs matched each other perfectly.” Related Stories News Cannes Marché & TIFFCOM Commit To Holding Second Edition Of Japan IP Market In 2027 News Toho CEO Matsuoka Hiro On The Company's Decision To Self-Distribute 'Godzilla Minus One' In The U.S. -- Tokyo He continued that Legendary has been “keeping a close eye on Japanese IP” and as the Godzilla franchise and other projects have proved, are willing to invest in big-budget live-action adaptations. In addition to Godzilla , the company is producing several theatrical and episodic projects based on Japanese IP, including Street Fighter, Gundam and Drops Of God Season 2 . Watch on Deadline “They needed upfront investment and to tie up with Japanese IP holders, but also had to understand the soul of the original work,” Setoguchi said. “Finding partners you can develop a deep relationship with is difficult. But TBS has long-standing relationships with many creators for live-action works, so working together with us, they could deliver Japanese IP to the rest of the world.” Setoguchi also said TBS has “neutral” relationships with all the major publishers in Japan, so isn’t limited to working with specific rights holders. He added that, starting this month, TBS employees will be setting up desks in the Legendary offices in Los Angeles to ensure a close working relationship. TBS already has its own offices in LA, and an outpost of its international production outfit The Seven, which has produced shows including three seasons of Alice In Borderland and Did Someone Happen To Mention Me , starring Koji Yakusho, both of which are streaming on Netflix, and Prime Original Rock Paper Landmine . Meanwhile, back in Asia, TBS has been forming similar tie-ups, launching a production joint venture Studio Monowa with Korea’s CJ ENM and Japanese streamer UNEXT, with announcements on the first projects expected soon. The aim for TBS is to propel Japanese drama to the same level of global recognition as Korean dramas. He observed that while K-drama is widely distributed to international markets, Japanese live-action content is not as well known, although anime and manga are hugely popular nearly everywhere in the world. Setoguchi recalled that one of the first shows co-produced by Japan and Korea was 2002 drama Friends – produced by TBS and Korea’s MBC – which was created to commemorate the 2002 FIFA World Cup co-hosted by South Korea and Japan. He described the show as “the first time Japanese was spoken on Korean TV since the war”. He added that, back then, Japan’s TV drama industry was much stronger than Korea’s and that Korean production staff were “enthusiastic to absorb every aspect of Japanese production expertise”. “We thought that since there’s a huge gap in production capabilities, it would be difficult for Korean teams to create global hits. More than 20 years have passed and we all know how that has turned out. Japan pursued domestic viewer ratings, while Korea looked at global markets, and those decisions have shaped today’s reality. We feel our mission now is to create a new global genre of J-Content.” On the unscripted side, TBS has built a global industry around the Ninja Warrior format, working with partners including Banijay, RTL and ITV Studio, who all appeared via video clips during the TIFFCOM presentation to talk about the strengths of the format. Banijay is selling the Israeli version of the show, which is returning after a three-year hiatus, while Australia is bringing it back after five years. Noting that sports-related programming is having a resurgence, Banijay Chief Content Officer James Townley said: “With the Olympics coming up, Ninja Warrior can capitalize on the strength of that and will be a major focus for us across Europe next year.” TIFFCOM is running for three days (October 28-30) at the Tokyo Metropolitan Industrial Trade Center in Hamamatsucho.
