articles.title: Mayur More & Ashlesha Thakur To Lead ‘Beta Builder’, Debut Hybrid AI Feature From Abundantia AiOn & InVideo
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse ‘Sweetpea’: Ella Purnell Is Back In Killer Role As Full Trailer Drops For Season 2 Of Sky And Starz Series European Production Association CEPI Welcomes Canadian Bodies As First International Members Disney+ & Netflix Hoover Up Non-English Acquisitions As Fervor For Japanese & Korean Content Continues – Ampere View All October 29, 2026 2:43am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Mayur More and Ashlesha Thakur Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: Mayur More and Ashlesha Thakur will star in the first AI-driven feature film from the pact between India ‘s Abundantia Entertainment and video tech firm InVideo . Beta Builder has InVideo’s Global Creative Lead, Hridaye A. Nagpal, attached to direct, with principal photography beginning today in Mumbai. The Indian city will, per the producers, serve “as both its home and creative starting point.” Abundantia is producing through its Abundantia AiOn division, which was formed last year as an AI production division framed as “human-first and AI-empowered.” Last year, it partnered with Sanket Shah’s San Francisco-headquartered InVideo on a slate of five AI-powered films launched over three years with a ₹100 crore ($10.5M) commitment behind it. Related Stories News Zee Studios Sets Release Date For Omung Kumar's 'Silaa' News Prime Video Adds Sony LIV To Indian Offer Beta Builder will tell the story of Jai, a self-taught, genius architect from Dharavi, a densely populated area of Mumbai, who “gets a chance to realize his dreams in the world of virtual reality), only to discover that winning means far more than proving himself. An underdog in every sense, Jai must fight the system that holds him back, win the love of his life, and give his community a voice in shaping its own future.” Watch on Deadline Producers say it is “rooted in one of India’s most iconic geographies and set against the limitless possibilities of a virtual world,” with the story exploring “ambition, belonging and what it truly means to build something that lasts.” The film is being positioned as a hybrid production, “pairing full-blown, live-action filming with AI-driven production,” and More ( Kotak Factory & Black , White & Gray: Love kills ) is starring alongside Thakur ( The Family Man ). “We are about to see a wave of fascinating films,” said director Nagpal. “With AI-assisted filmmaking, storytellers can dream much bigger, and backing a bold idea finally feels possible. The partnership between Abundantia and InVideo gives filmmakers the scale and creative support to take on ideas like this. Beta Builder is our bet on that future, with a live-action shoot and AI working side by side” Last month, Abundantia founder and CEO Vikram Malhotra outlined his vision for using AI in production in an interview with Deadline, while revealing Abundantia AiOn was morphing into a fully native standalone AI studio. He has sought to find the balance between the opportunity of AI and the “The capability needed to run AI at studio level will not be found solely within the conventional media and entertainment system,” he said at the time. “It is truly a confluence of technology and art.” Today, he said in a statement: “In our partnership with InVideo and Sanket, our focus is to leverage AI and tell stories that are unique, impactful and entertaining. I am delighted that the first film in our slate is one that tells a story set in a relatable, young world and explores aspirational possibilities beyond. “In Hridaye, we have a filmmaker who combines a strong creative vision with a deep command over technology, which makes him the ideal person to lead and bring Beta Builder to life. I am excited about how AiOn is enabling unique stories and storytellers to come to the fore and bring their best to fans all over the world.” “At InVideo, our mission has always been to put powerful tools in the hands of storytellers,” added Shah, CEO of InVideo. “ Beta Builder is where that mission takes the form of a full-length film, made with a partner of Abundantia’s calibre. It is a story about building something that lasts, which makes it the right film to begin this slate with.” Abundantia is known for the likes of Prime Video series Breathe and Daldal , Netflix crime-comedy Maa Behen , Baby , Toiler – Ek Prem Katha , Chhorii and Subedaar , the action thriller starring Anil Kapoor. InVideo, which is U.S.-based with offices in India, positions itself as a agnostic AI filmmaking platform with more than 50 million users. Its backers include Peak XV, Tiger Global, Greenoaks, RTP Global, Base Partners, and Hummingbird. articles.title: ‘The Cube’ Creator Adam Adler Joins Channel 4’s Production Biz As Creative Director
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max ‘Sweetpea’: Ella Purnell Is Back In Killer Role As Full Trailer Drops For Season 2 Of Sky And Starz Series ‘The Cube’ Creator Adam Adler Joins Channel 4’s Production Biz As Creative Director Pippa Harris & YouTube UK Boss Alison Lomax Join Board Of National Film & Television School View All October 29, 2026 4:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'The Cube' TBS EXCLUSIVE: Sarah Dillistone has made her first big hire at Channel 4 ’s in-house production biz. Dillistone has snapped up The Cube creator Adam Adler as Creative Director and he will lead on the creation of new shows for the nascent unit. Adler is a highly-regarded British formats executive who is best known as creator of ITV’s The Cube , which ran for 11 seasons and nearly 100 episodes beween 2009 and 2021. An American version aired for three seasons on TBS. Adler’s other creations include Bar Wars and The Games, while he has most recently been EPing Channel 4’s upcoming Derren Brown: Incognito. He is a former Channel 4 entertainment commissioner and also ran an indie, Gameface, before moving to ITV Studios-owned label Potato. Related Stories News Disney+ & Channel 4 Strike Landmark Deal In UK News Nicola Coughlan's 'I Am Helen' Trailer Shows Dark Side Of Modern Relationships As Toxic Masculinity Takes Its Toll Channel 4’s in-house production biz emerged from the UK government’s botched attempt to sell off the broadcaster and is one way in which the Gogglebox network can forge IP, which can then be sold around the world. The unit, which Channel 4 says is separated from its commissioning team by a “clear operational firewall,” unveiled ex- Made in Chelsea showrunner Dillistone as its lead at the start of 2026. She relocated to London from L.A., where she spent six years making shows like Perfect Match and The Ultimatum. Watch on Deadline More updates on the creative and development side of Channel 4 in-house are expected soon. Dillistone called Adler an “unrivalled creative force.” “He is one of the most prolific format creators around spanning gameshow, reality and entertainment,” she added. “Adam’s experience originating ambitious and unpredictable formats from The Cube to Channel 4’s brand new reality series Incognito , coupled with my own background originating and showrunning reality, social experiments and relationship shows, makes for an exciting mix.” Adler added: “I’m really excited to be joining Dilly at the start of this new venture. Channel 4 has always had attitude and originality, and I’d love us to bottle some of that up and take it out into the world. The ambition is to create exciting ideas with that same spirit, for TV and beyond.” In other Channel 4 news, highly-rated docs chief Alisa Pomeroy has taken on the top head of unscripted job amid the restructure that is seeing around half of commissioners laid off. Pomeroy’s fiefdom has expanded vastly and she is now looking after documentaries, factual entertainment, reality, entertainment and specialist factual. A day before Pomeroy’s promotion, Broadcast reported that comedy boss Charlie Perkins and entertainment chief Steve Handley are leaving. A scripted supremo looking after both drama and comedy is expected to be appointed in the coming months. articles.title: Russell Brand’s Wife Says Star Was “Caring” Lover At Time Of Rape Allegations
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Russell Brand’s Wife Says Star Was “Caring” Lover At Time Of Rape Allegations BAFTA Launches Review Over Concerns About Trustees Accepting Free Awards Guest Tickets BBC “Disappointed” As Staff Plan Industrial Action Vote Over Job Cuts View All October 29, 2026 4:06am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand and wife, Laura Brand, arrive at Southwark Crown Court Getty Russell Brand ‘s wife has told a court that the Despicable Me star was a caring and considerate lover during the period in which he has been accused of rape. Laura Brand took to the witness stand on Thursday at London’s Southwark Crown Court, giving evidence in support of her husband, who faces three charges of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one of attempted indecent assault. The charges span a 10-year period from 1999 to 2009. Laura Brand told the court that she first met Russell in August 2006 after a gig in Edinburgh, and they began a sexual relationship a month later. Asked what kind of lover Russell was, Laura said he was “very caring” and went at “my pace.” She added: “I felt entirely cared for and looked after by Russell.” Related Stories News Prosecution Rejects Russell Brand's Claim He Has Been Abandoned: "You Have A Platform Of Millions" Legal Russell Brand Forcefully Denies Charges As He Gives Evidence During Rape Trial: "Consent Is More Important Than Sex Itself" The pair broke up in February 2007 after Russell was unfaithful. “I was not interested in having a relationship with him if he was sleeping with other people — it was really difficult for him to be in a monogamous relationship,” Laura said. “I was a little heartbroken.” Watch on Deadline Riel Karmy-Jones, the prosecution barrister, pointed out that Laura was not in a relationship with Russell in 2009, when Complainant 5 alleged that she was anally raped by the Forgetting Sarah Marshall actor. Deadline has been reporting daily from a live video feed of the courtroom since the trial began. Russell and Laura reconnected a decade later, marrying in 2017 near Henley-on-Thames in Oxfordshire. They have three children together. Laura, who has been in court most days, described her husband as being “amazingly attentive” and “kind,” telling jurors: “I love him very much.” Two of Brand’s ex-girlfriends also gave evidence through witness statements that were read out in court by a defense lawyer. One woman, who dated Brand between 1996 and 1999, said he was “gentle and loving.” The second, who had an open relationship with Brand from 1999, added: “He never engaged in an intimate act without mutual consent.” Both said he was promiscuous, with the second noting that “women would circle like birds” around Brand as he became more famous. The prosecution and defense have now made their case to the jury. Closing arguments are expected tomorrow. The judge, Mr Justice Bennathan, expects the jury to begin verdict deliberations next Tuesday, November 3. articles.title: Disney+ & Netflix Hoover Up Non-English Acquisitions As Fervor For Japanese & Korean Content Continues – Ampere
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Bella Glanville Signs With Established Artists ‘Sweetpea’: Ella Purnell Is Back In Killer Role As Full Trailer Drops For Season 2 Of Sky And Starz Series European Production Association CEPI Welcomes Canadian Bodies As First International Members View All October 29, 2026 4:42am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Netflix drama 'Alice in Borderland' Netflix Disney+ and Netflix ‘s buying habits appear to be dispelling the notion that non-English-language acquisitions aren’t on their agendas. Research from Ampere Analysis shows that non-English content now accounts for at least half of acquisitions at both global streamers. As of September, non-English content accounted for 65% of Netflix acquisitions, with the figure at Disney+ hitting 50%. Japan and Korea were the leading source for Netflix acquisitions, with German and Japanese content topping Disney+’s list. Related Stories News Cannes Marché & TIFFCOM Commit To Holding Second Edition Of Japan IP Market In 2027 Books Everything We Know About Netflix's New 'Pride & Prejudice' Series So Far Ampere noted its research had identified Japanese, French, South Korean and Turkish as the biggest acquisition opportunities moving forwards if high demand and relatively low export volume was considered. Just 40% of Japanese streaming content is available worldwide, with the U.S. and South Korea the biggest buyers of what can be bought, though France and Germany also show relatively high interest. Watch on Deadline It’s a similar story for South Korean content – despite the global popularity of K-drama, only 45% of the country’s titles are available only on its own streaming services. The Middle East and Southeast Asia appear most likely to bite on its romantic-themed films and shows, Ampere claimed. “Non-English content remains underexploited despite growing global demand. In recent years, Amazon Prime Video, HBO Max and Disney+ have increasingly expanded non-English-language title licensing in multiple markets,” said Tingting Li, Research Manager at Ampere. “Japanese, South Korean, French and Turkish content present the top opportunities for international licensing, with strong audience appeal but still gaps in cross-border availability. For content owners and platforms, buying this content can bridge the gap between audience demand and international distribution.” ‘The Diplomat’ Renewed For Season 5 At Netflix, Two Weeks After S4 Arrival Marcus Theatres Posts Record Q3 Led By ‘Spider-Man’, ‘The Odyssey’ Amid Boom Skydance Sets Leadership Team For Studios, Entertainment, News & Sports Gregory Nava Mourns Civil Rights Leader Delores Huerta, Updates On Biopic Plans Read More About: Comments

articles.title: European Production Association CEPI Welcomes Canadian Bodies As First International Members
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Bella Glanville Signs With Established Artists ‘Sweetpea’: Ella Purnell Is Back In Killer Role As Full Trailer Drops For Season 2 Of Sky And Starz Series European Production Association CEPI Welcomes Canadian Bodies As First International Members View All October 29, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Canada and Europe have been moving closer politically Getty Canada and Europe have been moving closer together politically, and now their media production bodies are doing the same. CEPI , the European Audiovisual Production Association, has welcomed the Canadian Media Producers Association (CMPA) and the Association Québécoise de la Production Médiatique (AQPM) as its first international observer members. CEPI represents 3,000 independent production companies in 17 countries through 19 national associations and one European association, and now counts the two Canadian bodies among its ranks. Related Stories News Hudson Williams, Zach Galifianakis & Jay Baruchel Set For 'The Assembly' Season 2 At Canada's CBC News Raven Banner Boards Polish Folklore Horror 'Òpi' Ahead Of U.S. Festival Debut The European Union and Canada have moved closer politically together during the Trump Presidency, and their media bodies have followed suit, with CBC/Radio-Canada the first non-European network to become a full member of the European Broadcasting Union over the summer and Canada set to compete in the next Eurovision Song Contest. Watch on Deadline CEPI will work with the CMPA and AQPM to strengthen dialog and coordinate on shared advocacy issues such as regulation of streaming services, domestic production requirements, IP and rights, and co-productions. The news comes after the three bodes and other producer associations from Australia and across Europe signed a joint statement calling on governments to protect domestic production and local storytelling at the Toronto International Film Festival last month. “The arrival of CMPA and AQPM as CEPI’s first international observer members reflects the increasingly international nature of the audiovisual industry,” said Anthony Muldoon, President of CEPI. “While Europe and Canada may be an ocean apart, the challenges and opportunities facing our independent production sectors are remarkably similar. We share a commitment to supporting independent producers and creating original stories that reflect our respective cultural realities.” CMPA President and CEO Reynolds Mastin added: “Canadian and European independent producers face many of the same challenges, from modernizing regulations for the digital age to ensuring that local stories continue to be told, and to making sure domestic producers have a fair opportunity to own their work. We are stronger when we tackle these challenges together.” Hélène Messier, President and Executive Director at AQPM, called joining CEPI “a great privilege,” as she flagged challenges such as generative AI, diversity of cultural expression and preservation of cultural sovereignty. ‘The Diplomat’ Renewed For Season 5 At Netflix, Two Weeks After S4 Arrival Marcus Theatres Posts Record Q3 Led By ‘Spider-Man’, ‘The Odyssey’ Amid Boom Skydance Sets Leadership Team For Studios, Entertainment, News & Sports Gregory Nava Mourns Civil Rights Leader Delores Huerta, Updates On Biopic Plans Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Rotterdam Unveils First Titles Locked To World Premiere At 2027 Edition
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Rotterdam Unveils First Titles Locked To World Premiere At 2027 Edition Peter Farrelly’s ‘I Play Rocky’ To Open Cairo International Film Festival Israel Election: No Clear Winner But Opposition Parties Pull Ahead View All October 29, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: The Muglur, Tehran The Obscure Atelier of Desire. L-R: Kids Go Free, Karl Marx, Luanda IFFR The International Film Festival Rotterdam ( IFFR ) has unveiled a first selection of 10 feature titles locked to world premiere in the Bright Future and Harbour sidebars of its 56th edition in early 2027. The Harbour sidebar, inspired by Rotterdam ’s port city identity and “offering a safe haven” to contemporary filmmakers pushing cinematic boundaries, welcomes back a trio of directors with IFFR connections. Angolan director Kiluanji Kia Henda, who previously attended with Short Profile in 2020 and commissioned performance Resetting Birds’ Memories in 2021, returns with Karl Marx, Luanda (scroll down for synopses) Related Stories News Clare Stewart Steps Down As Rotterdam Managing Director Documentary SUPER7EVEN & MN Media Join Forces On Doc & Factual Storytelling Studio SuperIndie Cypriot filmmaker Kyros Papavassiliou returns with Yiannis, following his 2015 IFFR Tiger Competition selection for Impressions of a Drowned Man . Additionally, Hong Kong director Rita Hui Nga Shu is back, following the premiere of Decameron in 2021, with The Lapse . Watch on Deadline IFFR newcomers in the Harbour selection include Malaysian filmmaker siblings Iskander and Feisal Azizuddin with comedy cannibal horror Ali and Ben’s Spicy Meats , and Omer Shamir with intimate docu-portrait Waiting Room . First titles for Bright Future, focused on emerging talents, Ben Hicks’s Kids Go Free made over 15 years across three countries; director Parbat Chapagai’s stylised Dostoevsky adaptation Portrait of a Young Criminal , Lucila Las Heras’s dark fairy tale The Muglur , Mohamed El Zayat’s ensemble dramedy In The Name of Galeela and Ali Bakhtiari documentary Tehran The Obscure Atelier of Desire . “These first ten films already offer a glimpse of that incredible range, from the playful and provocative to the intimate and politically urgent,” said Vanja Kaludjercic, Festival Director at IFFR. “Cinema is at its most exciting when it challenges our expectations, when filmmakers find new ways to express experiences, contradictions and realities that resist easy answers.” IFFR 2027 Artwork Alongside the first film announcements, IFFR also unveiled its 2027 festival campaign, developed in collaboration with Rotterdam design studio 75B and echoing IFFR’s interest in artists finding new forms to express the experience of the world around them “We wanted our campaign for 2027 to reflect that same spirit of artistic freedom and curiosity. A reminder that there is no single way of looking at the world, and that there is always more to discover in how others see it,” said Kaludjercic. Previous titles in Bright Future from IFFR’s 2026 edition include: Ah Girl (IFFR’s Youth Jury Award and TIFF 2026), Let Them Be Seen (BFI London Film Festival 2026), while notable 2026 Harbourt titles include James J. Robinson’s debut First Light, Australia’s Academy Award Entry for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards in 2027. IFFR’s 56th edition will run from January 28 to February 7 2027. The complete lineup will be unveiled on 16 December 2026. Details of the first selections (synopses provided by IFFR) BRIGHT FUTURE THE MUGLUR Director: Lucila Las Heras Mexico, Argentina Struggling to write a fantasy novel under the thumb of her alcoholic father, Aurora makes a Faustian bargain with a strange creature: the Muglur. But what price will it ask of her? The answer will be found at the dark heart of this claustrophobic fairy tale. IN THE NAME OF GALEELA Director: Mohamed El Zayat Egypt When money for a pilgrimage to Mecca is stolen, a young man’s community comes together to convince his blind grandmother that she’s still going. Egyptian filmmaker Mohamed El Zayat asks us how far we’ll go for someone we love in his endlessly creative debut feature. KIDS GO FREE United States, Taiwan, Japan A taste for worldly adventures can bring passionate love and the thrill of the unknown, as well as niggling questions about economic security and one’s future. Told through a kaleidoscopic structure and a humanist lens over 15 years, Ben Hicks’ debut feature tackles these concerns in a miraculous manner. PORTRAIT OF A YOUNG CRIMINAL Director: Parbat Chapagai United States, Nepal David, a destitute tutor, develops an attachment to teenage sex worker Sonya. Wishing to save her from the spiritual squalor of their surroundings, David resolves to kill his rich employer. A stark, psychologically vivid adaptation of Dostoevsky’s Crime and Punishment set in small-town Nepal. HARBOUR KARL MARX, LUANDA Director: Kiluanji Kia Henda Angola, Portugal Kiluanji Kia Henda’s satirical future history of Angola imagines that the nation renews itself as a Marxist state. Via time-travelling love story and bold Afro-sci-fi-spaghetti-Western, we are reminded of a rare basic truth: in the forest, political doctrines do not help the rain fall. ALI AND BEN’S SPICY MEATS Director: Feisal Azizuddin, Iskander Azizuddin Malaysia Ali and Ben, broke buddies running a failing pickle business, stumble upon a magic recipe made from human meat. When their overnight success attracts the suspicion of a local politician, the friends must do what it takes to protect their nascent empire in this zany horror-comedy. WAITING ROOM (World Premiere) Director: Omer Shamir France Fleeing from Khan Younis, award-winning Palestinian photojournalist Mohammed Zaanoun moves his immediate family to safety in Egypt, unsure of what’s to come. Filmmaker and activist Omer Shamir paints a moving documentary portrait of this family, in their exile home, across one year. THE LAPSE (World Premiere) Director: Rita Hui Nga Shu Taiwan, United Kingdom Hong Kong filmmaker and artist Rita Hui Nga Shu layers life, declassified governmental documents and her AI-cloned voice to open a dialogue between the promises on paper and the reality of life for Hong Kongers. An uncompromising, impactful and radically human film-essay. TEHRAN THE OBSCURE ATELIER OF DESIRE (World Premiere) Director: Ali Bakhtiari Iran A contemporary documentary portrait of artists in their studios across Tehran. They return to unfinished canvases, abandoned experiments and sketches of future projects. They scrape, paint, sculpt and listen intently to music, while outside, the threat of war looms. YIANNIS (World Premiere) Director: Kyros Papavassiliou Cyprus, Greece When his father’s body vanishes from the morgue, a Cypriot teenager and his mother cross into the occupied north to find Yiannis, a bird psychologist from his father’s past. Kyros Papavassiliou turns a missing-body mystery into a dreamlike journey through grief on a divided island rarely seen on screen. ‘The Diplomat’ Renewed For Season 5 At Netflix, Two Weeks After S4 Arrival Marcus Theatres Posts Record Q3 Led By ‘Spider-Man’, ‘The Odyssey’ Amid Boom Skydance Sets Leadership Team For Studios, Entertainment, News & Sports Gregory Nava Mourns Civil Rights Leader Delores Huerta, Updates On Biopic Plans Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Paula Reid Joins MS NOW As Chief White House Reporter
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Paula Reid Joins MS NOW As Chief White House Reporter CNN, MS NOW And Politico Amend Lawsuit To Challenge Trump Ban On Access To Air Force One And The Oval Office Fox News Tops October Ratings, But Viewership Drops Vs. 2025; MS NOW And CNN Show Gains As Midterms Approach View All October 29, 2026 7:05am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Paula Reid MS NOW MS NOW confirmed on Thursday that Paula Reid has joined the network, nearly four months after her exit from CNN . Reid will serve as the news outlet’s chief White House reporter, the latest addition to MS NOW’s journalistic ranks since its split from Comcast nearly a year ago. Her first day is Thursday. Reid had been expected to join MS NOW following her departure from CNN in July after five years with the network, where she served as chief legal affairs correspondent. Before that, Reid was at CBS News, where she was on investigative and justice reporting teams before serving as White House correspondent. Reid’s exit preceded Paramount Skydance’s closing of its acquisition of CNN-parent Warner Bros. Discovery. Since the deal close earlier this month, chief international anchor Christiane Amanpour and Bianna Golodryga have announced their departures. articles.title: Camerimage: Hype Williams & Darren Aronofsky Set For Honorary Awards
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Camerimage: Hype Williams & Darren Aronofsky Set For Honorary Awards Toho CEO Matsuoka Hiro On The Company’s Decision To Self-Distribute ‘Godzilla Minus One’ In The U.S. — Tokyo How A Former Senior Netflix Staffer Launched One Of Japan’s Buzziest Indie Cinemas View All October 29, 2026 7:16am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Hype Williams & Darren Aronofsky Camerimage Film Festival. Veteran filmmakers Hype Williams and Darren Aronofsky , both best known for their experimental approach to filmmaking, will receive honorary awards at this year’s Camerimage Film Festival in Torún, Poland. Williams will be handed the ToruńCAMERIMAGE Award for Achievements in Music Video. Aronofsky will be honored with Camerimage’s honorary Award for Director. Williams is arguably the most influential filmmaker to work consistently in the music video format. His collaborators have included The Notorious B.I.G., Tupac Shakur, Missy Elliott, Busta Rhymes, Mary J. Blige, Jay-Z, Dr. Dre, Beyoncé, and Pharrell Williams. He is responsible for now-classic music videos such as Kanye West’s All of the Lights and Mase’s Feel So Good . In 1998, he directed the feature Belly , starring Nas and DMX, which is now considered one of the late masterworks of the 1990s. Williams will receive the award in person in Toruń. Watch on Deadline Aronofsky is one of the leading directors of his generation. He made his debut with Pi (1998), which earned him the directing award at Sundance and an Independent Spirit Award for Best First Screenplay. His other credits include Requiem for a Dream, The Wrestler, Black Swan , and The Whale . Aronofsky last directed Caught Stealing (2025). He won the Venice Golden Lion in 2008 with The Wrestler . articles.title: Chris Sullivan Joins Jeremy Holm On ‘Tessellation’ As Filming Gets Underway In Illinois
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Rotterdam Unveils First Titles Locked To World Premiere At 2027 Edition Peter Farrelly’s ‘I Play Rocky’ To Open Cairo International Film Festival Israel Election: No Clear Winner But Opposition Parties Pull Ahead View All October 29, 2026 7:26am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Chris Sullivan, Jeremy Holm, Winter Williams, Stephen Louis Grush Rob Holysz, Leslie Hassler, Winter Williams, Sarah King EXCLUSIVE: Emmy-nominated This is Us star Chris Sullivan has joined Jeremy Holm ( House of Cards , Mr. Robot ) on thriller Tessellation as production gets underway in Illinois. The feature directorial debut of screenwriter Michael Moreci follows disgraced puzzle champion and CIA codebreaker Anton (Holm) who is drawn into a conspiracy that forces him to confront the one code he could never crack: the reason his wife had to die. The cast also features Stephen Louis Grush ( The Righteous Gemstones ) and Winter Williams ( The Human Centipede ). Related Stories News Prestige International Pictures Boards SXSW Mexican Teen Body Horror 'Fifteen' - AFM News 'Mini War': First Look At Luke Wilson, Vanessa Hudgens, Nick Swardson & Rob Morgan In R-Rated Comedy “ Tessellation is very much a movie for our times,” said Moreci. “Nothing is real, fringe paranoia has become mainstream, and we’re losing our ability to even verify the truth. Watch on Deadline “We’re following in the footsteps of The Conversation , Blow Out , and The Parallax View , movies that also dealt with paranoia and distrust, and I’m proud to carry forward the tradition of these important films.” Moreci has won acclaim for his work spanning comics, film and television. His breakout comedic dark fantasy comic series Barbaric has sold more than one million copies and is currently in development as a series at Netflix. Other notable screenwriting credits include the Shudder horror film Revealer and Revival for Syfy/Peacock. Tessellation is produced by Robert Patrick Stern, Kevin Lau and Moreci, as well as Stephen Mastrocola, in association with Static Films. Damian Wassel, Jen Shelby, Rhett Bruno and Steven Beaulieu of Aethon Books serve as executive producers. Stephanie Slife is the line producer. “Static Films is built on the philosophy of supporting artists early in their careers, because Hollywood doesn’t always know what it wants until they see it. The low-budget debuts of Christopher Nolan ( Following ), Darren Aronofsky ( Pi ), and more recently, Jane Schoenbrun ( We’re All Going to the World’s Fair ) serve as both inspiration and reminders of where these filmmakers can go,” said Mastrocola. “When I first read Tessellation , I was immediately compelled by Michael’s vision, the script’s unique structure, and how relevant it is in these strange times. We’re looking forward to seeing if audiences can solve Anton’s puzzle when it comes to theaters next year,” added the producer who will be talking to buyers about the film at the upcoming AFM . Holm is represented by Formation Talent Agency and Prevail Artist Entertainment. Grush is represented by Stewart Talent, LTA and Robert Stein Management. Sullivan is represented by Gersh and Suskin/Karshan Management. Cameras are set to roll this week at Flyover Film Studios in Central Illinois. ‘The Diplomat’ Renewed For Season 5 At Netflix, Two Weeks After S4 Arrival Marcus Theatres Posts Record Q3 Led By ‘Spider-Man’, ‘The Odyssey’ Amid Boom Skydance Sets Leadership Team For Studios, Entertainment, News & Sports Gregory Nava Mourns Civil Rights Leader Delores Huerta, Updates On Biopic Plans Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Gerry Cardinale’s RedBird Capital, Guy Oseary’s Sound Ventures Set $1 Billion Investment Partnership
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill Marcus Theatres Posts Record Q3 Led By ‘Spider-Man’, ‘The Odyssey’ Amid Box Office Boom NYC Production Boom Sees Permits And Spending Surge, Sound Stages Max Out: “We Are Bursting At The Seams” Gotham Awards Film Nominations Led By ‘The Invite’, ‘Tender Loving Care’, ‘All Of A Sudden’ & More View All October 29, 2026 7:34am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Gerry Cardinale, Guy Oseary Courtesy/Getty Images Gerry Cardinale’s RedBird Capital Partners and Guy Oseary ’s venture capital firm Sound Ventures are partnering to invest $1 billion in emerging platforms at the convergence of tech, media and culture. The firms said the partnership “will capitalize on RedBird’s global reach and business-building expertise, alongside Sound’s access to founders and marketing acumen to pursue growth opportunities and support the world’s most consequential technology companies.” RedBird will also bring learnings from RedBird X, the firm’s AI investment and incubation platform headed by Hamid Biglari. Related Stories Executives Paramount-WBD Deal Architect Gerry Cardinale Says Most Of $6B In Expected Cost Savings Will Not Be From Layoffs News More Trump Vs. BBC: POTUS Vows To Sue UK Broadcaster For Up To $5B, Despite Getting Requested Apology “The next great technology companies and the entrepreneur founders behind them need versatile partners who understand the long-term trajectory of company building,” said RedBird founder and managing partner Cardinale. Watch on Deadline Sound Ventures was an early investor in Anthropic and OpenAI. “RedBird brings a different kind of outlook that complements what we have built at Sound, with the resources and scale to compound the impact of our investments,” said Oseary, the longtime music manager and entrepreneur who co-founded Sound Ventures in 2015. “Effie and I are excited to work closely with Gerry, Hamid and the RedBird team as we continue to back exceptional founders and companies, building out this differentiated investment platform together,” he said, referring to Effie Epstein, managing partner of Sound Ventures. RedBird, which focuses on the sports, media and entertainment space, and is a large investor in Skydance alongside the Ellison Family. It manages over $21 billion in assets. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘PAW Patrol 4’: Spin Master & Paramount Animation Pic In Works With Franchise Director Cal Brunker; Eyes 2029 Release Renée Zellweger, Dominic Sessa & Peter Dinklage Set For Sacha Gervasi’s High Concept Comedy Drama ‘Darlington’ – AFM Sundance 2027 In Boulder Unveils Legacy Lineup With ‘Better Luck Tomorrow’, ‘Memento’, ‘Y Tu Mamá También’ & More View All October 29, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Roman Coppola Film Independent Oscar nominated filmmaker Roman Coppola will serve in the newly created role of Creative Consultant for the 2027 Film Independent Spirit Awards . Coppola will work alongside Film Independent and President Juan Devis’ team to shape the tone, visual identity and experience for next year’s Spirit Awards. Coppola’s creative guidance will extend beyond the ceremony, helping connect the events surrounding the Awards through a shared artistic vision. Drawing on music, Los Angeles culture and the event’s Hollywood setting, he will explore new partnerships and unexpected collaborations to bring that vision to life throughout the season. Related Stories News Crazy Crypto Story Turned Into Comedy Series From Viv Ford & Roman Coppola's Decentralized Pictures News 'Train Dreams' Wins Best Feature; 'Sorry, Baby' Awarded Best Screenplay; 'Adolescence' Takes Home Four Trophies -- Spirit Awards Winners List “The Spirit Awards have always celebrated artists who challenge conventions and find new ways to tell stories. We believe the Spirits themselves should embrace that same creative freedom,” said Juan Devis, President of Film Independent. “Roman brings a unique sensibility, a sense of play, and a willingness to experiment. We’re excited to work with him to rethink not just the ceremony, but the entire experience of bringing our independent film community together.” Watch on Deadline “The endless inventiveness of cinema and the unique, diverse ways filmmakers find to express themselves are things I care deeply about,” said Coppola. “I’m looking forward to collaborating with the team to create a celebration that’s playful, adventurous, and full of surprises—one that will spotlight the remarkable voices that make independent cinema so vital.” Coppola was Oscar nominated in the Original Screenplay category for Wes Anderon’s Moonrise Kingdom. He’s a 2016 Emmy nominee for Netflix’s A Very Murray Christmas in Outstanding Television Movie in addition to being a Grammy nominee for Best Video Short Form for Green Day’s “Walking Contradiction”. He’s the co-creator, director, and writer of Prime Video’s Emmy winning series Mozart in the Jungle. He is know for his long running collaboration with Anderson as a producer and writer on such films, including, but not limited to, The Phoenician Scheme, Asteroid City, The French Dispatch, and The Darjeeling Limited. Coppola was also an EP on Sofia Coppola’s Priscilla, On The Rocks, Beguiled, and a producer on The Bling Ring and Somewhere . He made his feature directorial debut in 2001 with the 1960s sci-fi inspired movie CQ starring Jeremy Davies, Giancarlo Giannini, Jason Schwartzman and Gérard Depardieu. The Spirit Awards will take place on Saturday, March 6, 2027 at the Hollywood Palladium. The nominees will be announced on Wednesday, Dec. 2. articles.title: Elke Sommer Dies: ‘A Shot In The Dark’, ‘The Wrecking Crew’ Actor Was 85
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg ‘Paddington The Musical’ Extends London West End Run Through June 2028 Earl Barret Dies: Sitcom Writer Who Co-Created Ted Knight Vehicle ‘Too Close For Comfort’ Was 94 Barbara Barrie Dies: Star Of Broadway And ‘Barney Miller’ Was 95 View All October 29, 2026 8:09am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Elke Sommer in 1974 Daily Express/Hulton Archive/Getty Images Elke Sommer , the cool blond star whose distinctive German accent and regal bearing lent her a certain exotic quality that she brought to such 1960s films as the Pink Panther sequel A Shot in the Dark , Bob Hope’s comedy Boy, Did I Get a Wrong Number! , The Oscar starring Stephen Boyd and spy entry The Wrecking Crew , died Wednesday, October 28, of heart failure at her home in Bel-Air, California. She was 85. Her death was announced by her stepson Sebastian Walther, through a spokesperson, to the German newspaper Bild . The statement read: “Elke passed away peacefully around 10 p.m. Now she can finally be with her beloved husband again.” Sommers husband, German hotelier Wolf Walther, died three months ago, on July 22. Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries News Susan Saint James Dies: ‘McMillan & Wife’, ‘Kate & Allie’ Actor Was 80 Born Elke Schletz on November 5, 1940, in Berlin, to a family headed by her Lutheran minister father, Sommer moved briefly to London in 1957. While vacationing in Italy the following year, she was noticed by film director Vittorio De Sica, who began casting her in movies. She changed her surname to Sommer at that point. Watch on Deadline Her breakthrough came with 1963’s The Prize , a spy film and romantic comedy starring Paul Newman (Sommer was named Most Promising Newcomer Actress at the Golden Globes for her performance.) The following year brought A Shot in the Dark , the second in the durable Pink Panther franchise starring Peter Sellers. Peter Sellers and Elke Sommer in ‘A Shot In The Dark’ (1964) Everett Collection Sommers’ popularity continued through a string of 1960s films, many of them caper-style thrillers tinged with comedy and romance that paired Sommer with established leading men. There was The Art of Love in ’65 with James Garner; The Oscar with Boyd in 1966; and, that same year, Boy, Did I Get a Wrong Number! with Hope, and Deadlier Than the Male , a Bulldog Drummond spy movie with Richard Johnson. The Wrecking Crew (1968) was one of her more popular entries, starring Dean Martin as spy Matt Helm (the film also featured Sharon Tate and would be the last of Tate’s movies released before her murder in 1969). Through the mid-1970s, Sommer appeared in thriller Zeppelin , Agatha Christie’s Ten Little Indians , Italian horror films Baron Blood and Lisa and the Devil (the latter a 1972 film re-released in 1975 with additional scenes featuring Sommer and retitled House of Exorcism to piggyback on the popularity of The Exorcist ). Elke Sommer and Michael York in ‘Zeppelin’ (1971) Everett Collection Sommer, who several albums as a cabaret singer, increasingly worked in Europe though the ’70s, including the 1979 comedy The Prisoner of Zenda with her old Panther co-star Sellers. As her film career began to wane, Sommer shifted to television in the 1980s and ’90s, and she portrayed the wife of Joseph Goebbels in the 1982 ABC miniseries Inside the Third Reich. She frequently appeared on the NBC variety show hosted by her old Wrecking Crew co-star Dean Martin and guested on St. Elsewhere, The Love Boat and other shows. She even made a memorable appearance on The Muppet Show . In 1984, Sommer appeared on the CBS reality competition series Circus of the Stars, which led to a real-life feud and legal battle with Zsa Zsa Gabor. According to reports at the time, Gabor apparently heard Sommer crack a joke about Gabor’s weight. “Poor horse,” Sommer reportedly said when Gabor mounted the saddle, a quip overheard by Gabor, who then told a German news outlet that Sommer was destitute, hung out in sleazy bars, was balding and earned a living selling hand-knitted sweaters. Sommer sued Gabor and Gabor’s husband Frédéric Prinz von Anhalt for defamation and emotional distress, ultimately winning $3.3 million in general and punitive damages in Santa Monica Superior Court. Sommer married Hollywood newspaper columnist Joe Hyams in 1964 (they divorced in 1981). She was married to hotelier Walther from 1993 until his death from cancer three months ago. Complete information on survivors was not immediately available. ‘The Diplomat’ Renewed For Season 5 At Netflix, Two Weeks After S4 Arrival Marcus Theatres Posts Record Q3 Led By ‘Spider-Man’, ‘The Odyssey’ Amid Boom Skydance Sets Leadership Team For Studios, Entertainment, News & Sports Gregory Nava Mourns Civil Rights Leader Delores Huerta, Updates On Biopic Plans Read More About: Comments

Taking its cue from the Latin American tradition of quinceañera, a coming-of-age celebration when a girl turns 15, the film was directed by Mexican brothers Jack Zagha and Yossy Zagha from an original screenplay by Andrzej Rattinger and Ricardo Álvarez Canales ( (100 Days to Fall in Love) . Related Stories Culture Top 50 Classic Horror Movies News Top 50 Halloween Movies Photo Gallery: Creepy Classics From ‘Psycho,’ ‘The Shining’ To ‘Obsession’ & ‘Get Out’ Since its premiere at SXSW, it has played a raft of international genre and film festivals, including Seattle, Fantaspoa and Neuchâtel. The body horror follows a Mexican girl who has been planning the perfect quinceañera with her best friend until she begins to transform into something monstrous, causing a rift in their friendship as her birthday party spirals into chaos. Watch on Deadline Greta Martí stars alongside Macarena Oz (Nadie nos va a extrañar) , Aminta Ireta, Cloe Furlong and Mercedes Hernández, who recently appeared in Alejandro González Iñárritu’s Digger . articles.title: Russell Brand Takes the Stand in Rape Trial: “I Know What ‘No’ Means”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All October 28, 2026 4:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand outside Southwark Crown Court on Oct. 28. Courtesy of Getty Russell Brand took the stand for the first time in his ongoing rape and sexual assault trial on Wednesday and revealed that no one else has agreed to testify on his behalf. At London’s Southwark Crown Court, the prosecution has completed presenting its case and Brand’s defense team, led by Ian Winter, is now set to detail its arguments for the jury. The prosecution ran the court through all of the charges against the TV host and comedian, also star of St. Trinian’s and Forgetting Sarah Marshall . He is accused of three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one allegation of attempted indecent assault, with six women alleging offenses dating from 1999 to 2009. The final charge was reduced from indecent assault to attempted indecent assault by the judge, Justice Bennathan, on Tuesday afternoon. Related Stories Movies Jafar Panahi Facing Five Years' Imprisonment in Iran After Being Sentenced in Absentia Movies 'Men in Black' Director Barry Sonnenfeld Joins Short Film 'Serenity,' Set in Funeral Home, as Exec Producer (Exclusive) Among the claims is a woman who says Brand raped her in a Bournemouth hotel room in 1999 following one of his comedy gigs. Another says he grabbed her breasts and pushed her into a toilet in a bar in Soho, where he orally raped her in 2004. A separate woman alleges Brand anally raped her at his home in Hampstead in 2009, after consensual vaginal sex. Brand vehemently denies any criminal wrongdoing. According to Sky News coverage , there was a “significant shift” in the courtroom on Wednesday as Brand took the stand as the defense’s first witness. After taking his oath, his barrister began probing Brand on the “sea of change” brought about in his life after marrying U.S. pop superstar Katy Perry in 2010. “It did,” replied the defendant. “Staggering fame.” Brand was asked about the documentary that prompted the police to first investigate him in 2023 . Made by Channel 4’s Dispatches and followed by allegations in The Sunday Times , the program accused Brand of rape and assault . “It was devastating,” he told his barrister, who then asked: “Were you able to persuade a single person with relevant evidence to come to give evidence on your behalf?” Brand replied: “I have not.” When Winter asked if anyone “would touch him with a bargepole,” Brand said, “No.” He added: “My entire life has been consumed by these allegations. I have devoted myself to these matters.” Winter took Brand through various statements from the complainants, some of whom he remembers meeting and others whom he says he has no recollection of. Winter asked Brand, “Is that something that you normally do? Speak during sex?” His client replied, “Yes … I believe I would have been saying: ‘Am I doing this right, do you like this, is this OK?” Brand said when asked for his opinion on consent: “Consent is a fundamental, essential and necessary, and in many ways more important than sex itself.” He discussed the first complainant, saying he remembered meeting her at the Labour Party conference in Bournemouth in 1999. He told the court he found her “loquacious” and “interesting,” and when asked if there was any truth in her claim that Brand raped her that night in a hotel room, the defendant said: “No.” The prosecution, cross-examining Brand, then suggested he “just didn’t care whether she was interested in having sex with you or not.” Brand refuted that and told them he cared “very much.” He added: “I know what ‘no’ means.” The third complainant says Brand groped her breasts in a bar before pulling her to the toilets and forcing her to perform oral sex on him. He does remember meeting her, he told the court. He said a friend introduced him to the woman, telling him “something like, ‘There’s a bird here who really wants to meet you mate.'” Brand told the court that he would have said to this woman upon meeting her: “‘You’re really, really beautiful.'” “Is there any question you just grabbed her breasts?” Winter said to Brand. “Absolutely not,” he replied, saying the act does not turn him on because it’s “disgusting behavior.” He remembers speaking to the complainant for less than a minute before going to the bathroom to “fool around.” Winter said: “As far as you’re aware, is there any question that she did not consent to going into the cubicle with you?” Brand told him: “There’s absolutely no question.” Winter also asked: “Did your penis enter her mouth at all whilst in the cubicle?” His defendant said, “No.” On the allegation that he anally raped another woman at his North London home in 2009, Brand said after a “memorable” sexual encounter he was “excited and enthusiastic” to see her again. The woman said they had consensual vaginal sex in his bedroom, which Brand recalls. When asked if he had then anally raped her, Brand said: “No.” He was asked if she told him to stop, to which he replied: “No.” The trial could last up to six weeks. THR

articles.title: Peter Medak, Director of ‘The Ruling Class’ and ‘The Changeling,’ Dies at 88
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All October 28, 2026 5:39am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Peter Medak J. Quinton/WireImage Peter Medak, the Hungarian-born director who guided Peter O’Toole in The Ruling Class , George C. Scott in the classic ghost story The Changeling and Gary Oldman in the crime thriller Romeo Is Bleeding , died Tuesday in Los Angeles, his family announced. He was 88. Medak made his feature directorial debut on the erotic Negatives (1968), featuring Glenda Jackson in one of her first films, and followed that with the black comedy A Day in the Death of Joe Egg (1972), starring Alan Bates and Janet Suzman in an adaptation of Peter Nichols’ play. Related Stories TV Kevin Bleyer, Emmy-Winning 'Daily Show' Writer, Dies at 54 in Car Crash TV Susan Saint James, 'Name of the Game,' 'McMillan & Wife' and 'Kate & Allie' Star, Dies at 80 He also helmed the British gangster drama The Krays (1990), with Gary Kemp and brother Martin Kemp, both members of Spandau Ballet, as real-life British gangsters; Let Him Have It (1991), featuring Christopher Eccleston and Tom Courtenay in another true story, about a controversial hanging; and Zorro: The Gay Blade (1981), starring George Hamilton. For television, Medak worked on multiple episodes of Homicide: Life on the Street , Hart to Hart and Shelley Duvall ‘s Faerie Tale Theatre and on installments of Breaking Bad , The Wire , Space: 1999 , Magnum, P.I. , Law & Order: SVU , St. Elsewhere , Chicago Hope , House and Cold Case . With Medak calling the shots, O’Toole picked up the fifth of his eight career best actor Oscar nominations for his turn as a British nobleman who believes he’s Jesus Christ and then Jack the Ripper in the dark comedy The Ruling Class (1972). Based on a play by Peter Barnes, who also wrote the screenplay, the film played in competition at Cannes. Martin Scorsese, Steven Spielberg, Guillermo del Toro and Alejandro Amenábar are among those who admire his Changeling (1980), about a grieving composer (Scott) caught in a supernatural mystery involving his new home. Spielberg, in fact, screened the film several times for his crew on Poltergeist to help set the tone for that horror classic, Medak noted in a 2018 interview . “He said, ‘This is what it should be.’ It was a great compliment coming from him, and I know he even has his own 35mm copy of The Changeling , and so does Martin Scorsese,” he said. “It’s lovely to have that, to be on their lists of the greatest ghost stories of all time.” Oldman scored high marks for his performance as a corrupt New York homicide detective involved with a vicious hitwoman (Lena Olin) in Romeo Is Bleeding (1993). In his review for Rolling Stone , Peter Travers wrote that Medak “keeps the action stylish, sexy and fiendishly funny. The film rarely makes a lick of sense, but it’s compulsively watchable.” Alas, Medak also is famous for directing the lamentable Ghost in the Noonday Sun (1974), a comedy about bumbling 17th century pirates that starred the combustible Peter Sellers and Spike Milligan. “Oh, it was probably the biggest nightmare of my life,” he said in a 2007 interview for the DGA. Even though the film nearly torpedoed his career, he chose to revisit the experience by helming the 2018 documentary The Ghost of Peter Sellers . Peter Medak (center) with actors Janet Suzman and Alan Bates on the set of 1972’s ‘A Day in the Death of Joe Egg.’ Courtesy Everett Collection Medak was born on Dec. 23, 1937, in Budapest, Hungary. In 1956, he fled to England during his country’s uprising against the communists, and his aunt, an opera singer, helped him quickly land a job with the Associated British Picture Corp. He started out as an editor, cameraman and assistant director and helped out Fred Zinnemann on The Sundowners (1960). A stint as a second A.D. on The V.I.P.s (1963), starring Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton , led to him in 1963 to sign a seven-year contract at Universal Studios to direct for television in Hollywood and London. After many months of false starts, he made his helming debut with a 1965 episode of ITV/Universal’s Court Martial , starring Bradford Dillman and Peter Graves. He had quite the start to his film career. “My first three movies‚ Negatives , Joe Egg and Ruling Class , were just total perfection for me to make as a young director,” he said in a 2020 interview . In 1973, Medak was asked to direct Death Wish , but when he insisted that Henry Fonda be cast as the lead, Paramount turned to Michael Winner, who hired Charles Bronson for the role of vigilante Paul Kersey. On King’s Road in London that year, he ran into Sellers, who invited him to direct Ghost in the Noonday Sun. “Peter was a nightmare,” he recalled. “It was his project, which he developed for two years before me, and I realized about a month before shooting that he’s never read the script. If you can believe it.” The film was shot on location in Cypress, and its pirate ship broke down daily and had to be towed back to the harbor. Meanwhile, the mercurial Sellers fired the producers and faked a heart attack to get time off. (Days later, Medak was stunned to see a newspaper photo of his star dining with Princess Margaret.) The film was so bad, Columbia Pictures never released it; it finally made its way to VHS in the early ’80s. Medak didn’t direct another feature until The Odd Job (1978), starring Monty Python member Graham Chapman. “I was basically punishing myself unconsciously for not making the greatest success of a film with Peter Sellers and Spike Milligan,” he said. “But it wasn’t my fault. Peter’s terrible, insane, destructive behavior on that film [was the reason it failed].” Medak’s résumé also included the features The Men’s Club (1986), La voix humaine (1990), Pontiac Moon (1994) and Species II (1998) and the 1997 telefilm The Hunchback of Notre Dame , starring Mandy Patinkin as Quasimodo. And his love of music of all genres provided him with opportunities to direct early music videos for artists such as Peter Gabriel and Pink Floyd. Survivors include his children, Christopher, Joshua, Karen and Cornelia, and his grandchildren, Sacha, Marlowe, Ryden, Oliver and Anders. He was married to Catherine Marie La Kermance from 1963 until her death by suicide in 1972; to English actress Carolyn Seymour (she’s the wife of O’Toole’s character in The Ruling Class ) from 1973 until their 1984 divorce; and to opera singer Julia Migenes from 1988 until their 2003 divorce. “If it’s in your blood, directing, you never stop,” he said. “And it doesn’t matter that you’re alone in your mind, dreaming or imagining things, you’re always making a movie.” THR

articles.title: How “Toxically Optimistic” Zainab Johnson Found a Fan (and Hype Woman) in Michelle Obama
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Mikey O'Connell Plus Icon Mikey O'Connell Senior Entertainment Editor View All October 28, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Zainab Johnson Netflix “Washington, DC, make some noise for Zainab Johnson .” The intro itself isn’t an original way to start Johnson’s latest special, Netflix’s Toxically Optimistic , but the individual speaking as she takes the Howard Theatre stage marks a comedy first. That’s Michelle Obama riling up the audience. Johnson, the actress and stand-up who saw her comedy profile surge with 2023’s Hijabs Off , didn’t just get the former former First Lady to introduce her special. The Obamas’ Higher Ground produced the hour, out Oct. 27, a first for their ever-expanding company. So how did Johnson get into business with the Mrs. Obama? By accidentally kind of snubbing her a few years back. Related Stories TV Angry Golf Bros Tried to Ruin Heather McMahan. She Released a Hulu Special Instead Movies Harvey Keitel Threw 'Bad Lieutenant' in the Trash Before Giving One of His Greatest Performances Johnson was in Detroit for a show in late 2024, not far from where Kamala Harris was stumping for her presidential run. Obama was set to attend the rally, so when her team engaged Johnson about meeting her there, Johnson jumped in a car and headed that way. “But I didn’t know how political rallies work,” says Johnson. “I thought you just pull up, park and walk in. No, they shuttle you from a mall that’s ten miles away. I get there and realize I only have enough time to turn around if I’m going to make it to my show. I tell her people that I’m so sorry. And they’re like, ‘Are you sure? Because Michelle is really looking forward to meeting you.’ I know this sounds crazy, but I gotta go be a professional comedian.” Fortunately for Johnson, she’d get another chance a few weeks later —an encounter that’s since proven quite fruitful. Speaking during a recent episode of The Hollywood Reporter podcast I’m Having an Episode (listen to the complete interview on episode on Spotify , Amazon Music , Apple ), Johnson talked about finding a champion in Mrs. Obama, confusing U.K. audiences with a bit about her decision to buy a gun and the billboard she recently spotted that told her all she needed to know about TV’s backslide into defaulting to white actors. So how did you meet Mrs. Obama after this near-miss? In 2024, when Kamala Harris was campaigning, I was in Atlanta when Michelle was there for this bipartisan “Get out the vote” thing. A lot of powerful women in Hollywood were in this room — Kerry Washington, Shonda Rhimes — and I had just had this encounter with these celebrity girls. I was like, “Hey y’all, I’m a fan!” They looked at me like I was dirt. I will not say their names because I’m a huge fan of theirs. I don’t want the world to turn on them. So, I sat down, like, “I don’t know how I got in this room, but let me sit my ass down.” As soon as Michelle walks in the room, everybody flocks to her. She turns, sees me and she says, “Zainab Johnson!” She pulls me up to hug her. She turns me around to Shonda Rhimes, like, “Did you see this girl’s special? It’s fantastic!” She just starts raving about me. In my mind, I’m like, “My God, this is crazy.” Please tell me the women who blew you off were watching as all of this happened. Yes, they saw it. Right after they see Ms. Michelle fawning over me, they come back and apologize. It’s like a high school movie. Like a Mean Girls short starring Zainab Johnson, Michelle Obama and three beautiful, famous girls that will remain nameless. This is the first comedy special produced by the Obamas. I picture you walking into a general meeting, someone handing you a bottled water and Michelle and Barack just hanging out in a conference room. But I’m guessing that’s not how it happened. It’s so far off, not that I haven’t been to Higher Ground for some meetings been offered a wonderful bottle of water. So let’s fast forward to the top of 2026. My team and I decide I’m doing this special. I don’t care if I’m producing it or funding it myself. I’m not gonna wait on anybody to give me permission to put this out. But I had this idea as I was watching Sheng Wang’s special. I’ve always liked how Ali Wong sets the table for him. I thought, “Dang, if somebody were to introduce me, who would I want it to be? What if I got Michelle Obama to do it?” So I called my managers and said, “I’m gonna ask Michelle Obama to introduce my special.” Just voice of God. That’s all I need. I don’t need her to show her face. I don’t need her to produce it. I’m gonna do this thing all by myself. Which is not what happened. Maybe like a week or so later, I’m out to dinner with my friend, and, Michelle’s team, I get a text from them. “Hey, she’s recording the intro right now.” Simultaneously, I get a phone call from my managers. “Yes, she’s recording it. They want to produce the special. How do you feel about that?” I’m having all of the emotions. So they’re like, “Hello?” My friend who’s at dinner with me is asking what’s happening because she can see my face is stunned. And I’m like, “I would absolutely love that.” So then managers start screaming. And when I tell my friend, she says something so interesting to me. She asked how did this happen? “I just asked her to intro me.” She said, “You know what? That’s God, the universe, whatever you want to call it, telling you you can ask for more.” Something I learned about you in this special is that you bought a gun, at your friend’s suggestion, when you moved into a new house. How did the experience of buying a gun compare to how you thought it would be? When they were like, “Get a gun,” I’m thinking we gonna go get a gun with no serial number. I’m thinking we’re getting a back alley gun, right? No. When you go the legal route in California, you have to take classes, you have to get certified, then you have to go to the gun range with a with a certified person. I had to take a test. This used to be in my set, because this this set has come a long way. But I used to talk about how in California, you take a 20-question multiple choice test. I got two of the questions wrong, and they still gave me the gun. That you can get up to five questions wrong and they still give you a gun. That margin of error is crazy to me. And that bar is significantly lower in many other states. When I was touring this through the South, they were like, “Girl, just go to a Walmart! A gas station! Just make sure you have your driver’s license.” Then it was “Girl, you don’t even need that! Just make sure you got the money.” So this went through several incarnations, but you performed an early version at Edinburgh Fringe. This made me wonder how the U.K. audience responds to gun material versus a U.S. audience? The headline of one British paper’s review was “U.S. comic targets gun culture.” It was a bit different in Edinburgh, but I would not have described that show as “she takes on guns.” What’s interesting is that I didn’t just tour it in the U.K., I toured it in Paris. I brought it to Australia, a lot of places where civilians are unfamiliar with day-to-day gun ownership. I remember I would cold open the show with, “I got a gun.” A lot foreign audiences, they would feel confirmed about America with Donald Trump, like, “Yup! We knew it.” Slowly, they’d see some of the material that’s in the special now and they’d be like, “Well, if everybody who has a gun is like you, I guess it’s OK?” With a lot of people, I’m able to get them to see how I’m seeing things. The Edinburgh audience is an older audience. So when I would be like, “I got a gun,” they would be like “ha ha ha” and literally reach for their partner. Then I’d say, “I mean, I don’t have it on me. I don’t think they would have let me through customs.” Then they would understand, OK, this is gonna be a fun time. During a recent interview, you said that the only person that relates to Black women are other Black women. Knowing that, but also knowing that your audience is much broader, I’m curious how some material played. There’s one bit, during which you recount the potential outcomes of a scary encounter walking down a sidewalk. Predicting your possible death, you say, “I’m a Black woman in America. I’ve got to solve my own murder.” It’s a horrifying statement, because it’s very honest, but you play it for laughs. How did that one land on the road? Yeah, I gotta solve my own murder before I go. That’s painfully true, but that’s comedy, right? You bring levity. I’ve toured this hour in different places and when I drop that line, sometimes I would get a standing ovation. Sometimes I would liberate people in the room. Not just Black women. People who have that awareness and understand that truth. And sometimes, I would bring a really laughing crowd down to a sobering reality. It’d be like, “Wait, my God, that’s terrible.” I’m proud that I was able to convey that. It’s such a powerful thing, to convey that in between the absurdity. I’m happy that it landed and I’m happy that it made the final cut. You’re also an actress, and we’ve been talking a lot at work about how TV opportunities have been cratering for people of color. It’s like Hollywood has completely abandoned this push that, for a little while, actually seemed like it was gaining traction. So as you navigate that part of your career, what are the conversations you’re having about opportunities? What does your team say? The talks have been the same, which is, “There’s so little work.” I’m getting the same amount of enthusiasm and willingness to meet with me and pitch an idea. But that last part? The willingness to spend money, to invest, that’s the part. But entertainment is whatever the world is exhibiting at the moment. This might sound crazy, but I haven’t seen this in a very long time. I was driving up La Brea and I saw a billboard for a procedural show. All five of the cast were just cis white people. I I haven’t seen that in years. It’s very back. And I think I know the show you’re referring to. I couldn’t believe it. I almost had to avoid a traffic accident. Am I seeing what I think that I’m seeing? We’re back in the nineties with Friends . We’re back in those conversations. I think we’re in a time that we can call a regression. We are regressing. It’s scary and it’s sad. This is not specific to the show we’re talking that we will not name. But I think it’s all gonna prove to be very boring. THR

articles.title: Comedy Legend George Schlatter Sets Doc Release With Freestyle Digital Media (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 28, 2026 6:05am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Producer George Schlatter made an appearance at the Newport Beach Film Festival premiere of his doc 'Sock It to Me: The Legend of George Schlatter.' Tiffany Rose/Getty Images for Newport Beach Film Festival Freestyle Digital Media, the digital film distribution division of Byron Allen ’s Allen Media Group, has picked up the North American VOD rights to Sock It To Me: The Legend of George Schlatter . The feature documentary about Schlatter, the creator of Rowan & Martin’s Laugh-In , the groundbreaking comedy variety hour that launched on NBC in 1968, will debut on digital platforms from Dec. 8. Laugh In launched the careers of Goldie Hawn and Lily Tomlin and gave birth to late-night television, including Saturday Night Live. Schlatter also created and produced the NBC reality series Real People from 1979 that featured an 18 year-old Byron Allen in his first TV gig as a regular co-host. Recalling a seven-decade career as a prolific TV producer and director, Sock It To Me uses archival footage and interviews with stars like Hawn, Tom Hanks, Tomlin, Martin Short, Billy Crystal, Jay Leno, Jimmy Kimmel, Lionel Richie, Lisa Ann Walter, Berry Gordy and Byron Allen to explore how Schlatter, now 96, changed TV comedy. “People have been asking me to write an autobiography, and I’ve always said have somebody else write it. They then explained to me that it wouldn’t be an autobiography, so here we are,” Schlatter said in a statement. “It’s a full circle moment to work with Byron Allen’s company to get this documentary out into the world. You bet your sweet bippy I’m excited for audiences to see it and remind them of the power of laughter!” Written and directed by Chris Coronado, Sock It To Me was produced by Coronado, Greg Myers and Dayna Winston. Since 2016, Coronado has served as creative director at George Schlatter Productions, overseeing the creative development and production of documentary and entertainment projects. Freestyle Digital Media negotiated the deal to acquire Sock It To Me directly with the filmmakers and George Schlatter Productions. THR
