articles.title: ‘Transplant’ Creator Joseph Kay Sets Overall Deal at Netflix
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 28, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Joseph Kay Courtesy of Netflix Netflix has signed an exclusive overall deal with Joseph Kay, the creator and showrunner of the medical drama Transplant , which landed on NBC stateside. As part of the deal, Kay will develop and write new TV series for Netflix in Canada, starting with an untitled new family drama. He most recently worked with Netflix as a consulting producer on North of North season 2, the Arctic-set comedy also on the CBC and set to return on Nov. 5. Also for Netflix, he co-executive produced the upcoming adaptation of Carley Fortune’s bestselling novel, This Summer Will Be Different. Transplant, which ran for four seasons, was a medical procedural about a Syrian refugee working as a doctor in a Toronto trauma unit. The drama centered on Dr. Bashir “Bash” Hamed (Hamza Haq, Quantico ), a Syrian doctor with battle-tested skills in emergency medicine who fled his country with his younger sister, Amira (Sirena Gulamgaus). Together they struggled to build a new life in Canada while Bash strived to rebuild his career in medicine. Transplant was produced by Sphère Média Plus, in association with CTV and NBCUniversal International Studios. “I am beyond grateful and thrilled to partner with this incredible company. I have huge admiration for Netflix’s entire team, and for their unsurpassed drive to tell great stories and connect with audiences around the world,” Kay said in a statement on Wednesday. His TV writing credits include Ransom, This Life and Republic of Doyle. “Joe is a seasoned and gifted creator and showrunner, who is also adept at supporting other writers. We have loved working with him on our shows so far and we are thrilled to expand our relationship,” Danielle Woodrow and Tara Woodbury, directors of content at Netflix Canada, said in their own statement. Kay is represented by Dustin Alpern and Conrad Sun at Sundust Management. The overall deal was negotiated by Casey Chisick of Cassels Brock & Blackwell LLP. THR

articles.title: Sundance Sets Legacy Screenings Including Films by Christopher Nolan, Justin Lin and Alfonso Cuarón
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All October 28, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source A still from Justin Lin's 'Better Luck Tomorrow.' Courtesy of Sundance Institute As Sundance prepares to write a new legacy in Boulder, Colorado in 2027 and beyond, the film festival is bringing some hits from its past to the new home. Sundance Institute today revealed the lineup for the Legacy program for next year’s festival, and it includes works by filmmakers including Christopher Nolan, Alfonso Cuarón , Justin Lin , Stacy Peralta, Julie Taymor, Barbara Hammer, Patricia Cardoso and Tom Kalin. While old will be new again, there’s also something fresh for the lineup once known as From the Collection: Letterboxd joins as a co-presenter of the Legacy program with additional details for onsite activations to come. Related Stories Movies Alfonso Cuarón Reflects on Making 'Harry Potter': "Two of the Most Beautiful Years of My Life" 'Awards Chatter' Podcast John Leguizamo on 'The Odyssey,' Non-Traditional Casting and Being Uninvited From 'Spider-Man: Homecoming' Plucked for the Legacy program — curated as a home to showcase “groundbreaking independent cinema including archival and restoration screenings of fiction and nonfiction works as well as special events” — will feature brand-new restorations of the 2002 Sundance version of Lin’s Better Luck Tomorrow , a digital 4K restoration of Peralta’s Dogtown and Z-Boys , a 35th anniversary screening of Taymor’s Fool’s Fire , Hammer’s Nitrate Kisses , a 25th anniversary screening of Cardoso’s Real Women Have Curves, a star making turn for America Ferrera, a 35th anniversary screening of Kalin’s Swoon , and a 25th anniversary screening of a 4K restoration of Cuarón’s Y tu mamá también, a star making turn for Diego Luna and Gael Garcia Bernal. (Top left to right): Better Luck Tomorrow and Dogtown and Z-Boys ; (middle left to right): Fool’s Fire, Nitrate Kisses and Real Women Have Curves ; (bottom left to right): Swoon and Y tu mamá también . Legacy screenings will include director appearances and select cast members in attendance. Courtesy of Sundance Institute Sundance has also set a special two-part session on the final weekend of the festival dubbed “ Sundance Film Festival presents: Cinema Interruptus featuring Memento .” It will feature a 4K restoration and communal discussion for Nolan’s 2000 effort, Memento, starring Guy Pearce, Carrie-Anne Moss and Joe Pantoliano. “We’re excited to kick off the festival season in earnest with this first 2027 Sundance Film Festival announcement, revealing some of our Legacy programming,” explained Eugene Hernandez, who serves as director of the Sundance Film Festival and public programming. “Each year we honor the legacy of our founder Robert Redford and the history of the Sundance Film Festival by looking back at just a few of the films and filmmakers who have shaped our history. Our first festival in our new home in Boulder, Colorado will bring change, but as we evolve, we’ll keep at our core what we celebrate: our rich history.” Added Kim Yutani, director of programming: “Revisiting and becoming newly acquainted with films from our previous lineups in a theatrical setting, in community, and with some of the talent behind the films is a rare treat — even more so when these projects have been restored. We’re really looking forward to welcoming back these artists and know that audiences will enjoy the opportunity to complement the new films we will soon be announcing with these classics.” The Sundance Film Festival will take place in Boulder from Jan. 21–31. Additional Legacy programming will be announced in the coming weeks. THR

articles.title: Environmental Media Association and Its Awards Show to Become Part of Nonprofit United by Nature
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All October 28, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The 2025 Environmental Media Awards Gala. Amy Sussman/Getty Images for The Environmental Media Association It’s a new era for the Environmental Media Association, as the Hollywood sustainability group is becoming a part of nonprofit United by Nature. EMA has been active in the industry for nearly 40 years, creating conversation through educational initiatives, industry partnerships and events like the Impact Summit and its signature EMA Awards Gala. United by Nature — an organization focused on building the next generation of America’s conservation movement — plans to build upon these programs and relationships, as well as host the first United by Nature Awards in April 2027 to coincide with Earth Month. Related Stories News 'The Wild Robot,' 'The Daily Show' Among Winners at Environmental Media Awards News Stars Talk L.A Wildfires, Home Rebuilds and What to Do With Your Tesla at EMA Impact Summit “Environmental progress requires a bigger coalition that’s more reflective of communities across America,” Benji Backer, founder and CEO of United by Nature, said in a statement. “EMA proved how powerful storytelling can shape culture, unite people and drive meaningful outcomes for nature. Together, we’re building upon that impact by reaching new audiences and inviting people of all backgrounds to protect the outdoors they love.” Debbie Levin, the former CEO of EMA who will now serve as chief visionary officer of United by Nature, said, “EMA has always believed in the extraordinary power of entertainment and storytelling to inspire environmental action. For more than three decades, we’ve worked alongside the entertainment community to make sustainability part of the cultural conversation. We’re proud of the legacy we’ve built, and we’re excited to work with United by Nature to reach new audiences and continue making sustainability more accessible and engaging.” United by Nature’s inaugural takeover of the awards event will continue to celebrate the entertainment industry’s environmental leadership, while also expanding to recognize the individuals and organizations across music, sports, podcasts and universities that inspire positive change. Past EMA honorees include Billie Eilish, Michael Bloomberg, Jane Fonda, Ted Turner, Natalie Portman, Matt Damon and Laura Dern. The EMA Green Seal will also become the United by Nature Green Seal, which recognizes industries that take meaningful steps to reduce their environmental footprint. Wildwood , the animated fantasy film from Laika Studios, is the first movie to be awarded the United by Nature Green Seal; the movie joins nearly 3,000 other productions recognized for their sustainability efforts. THR

articles.title: TikTok Wants to Help Its Users Find Their Next Must Eat
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 28, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Photo Illustration by Justin Sullivan/Getty Images TikTok ‘s U.S. joint venture is leaning hard into the food creator community, launching a new product called Must Eat that is meant to boost food creators, as well as restaurants, all in service of helping its users find that next must visit place to grab a bite. The company officially rolled out Must Eat at a reception held at Undercote in New York City Tuesday evening, with Adam Presser, the CEO of TikTok’s U.S. business, hosting food creators in the lounge. “The first time that I came across FoodTok was actually before I joined the company, it was in the pandemic,” Presser told the attendees. “I came across the feta cheese pasta trend … So we were lucky enough to be able to get a block of feta cheese at that time, and we made the recipe, and it was incredible. And it was that first experience of being able to be watching videos, consuming content, and then translating that into real life experiences. And that journey has only continued on TikTok. “The ‘lunch in my city’ trend has really driven a lot of momentum,” he continued. “I know some of the creators here have made content around that trend. I have tried it out, it’s fantastic. And over the last several years, we’ve just seen more and more people have this experience of discovering something on the platform and driving their in-real-life experience. I saw a stat last year: More than 27 million Americans went to an independent restaurant, cafe, or store in the U.S. that they had discovered for the first time on TikTok.” So, Must Eat. The product is launching in New York, Los Angeles and the Bay Area, highlighting places in two categories: “Everyday Eats” and “Elevated Dining” featuring restaurants that have connected with TikTok food creators. TikTok also partnered with OpenTable to enable reservations at selected locations. The product, an expansion of “Must GO” (focused on travel), is an example of how TikTok U.S. is trying to carve its own path forward, now 10 months or so into its new ownership structure. For Presser, it is also a chance to bring his own imprint onto one of the biggest creator platforms in the country. “I am an L.A. native, and probably like most people that grew up in L.A., I had dreams of working in entertainment, but any hope of working in front of the camera were quickly dashed — I think it was around the eighth grade play. I was assigned the role of lighting director,” he quipped Tuesday, noting that he went on to work in the music industry and later as an executive at Warner Bros. Discovery before joining TikTok some four and a half years ago. “It was the first time that I really had the experience of realizing that you didn’t have to be at the top of the charts or on the big screen to be a star,” he said. “That it could be anybody with a voice, and a phone, and a vision, a creative perspective, and a platform like TikTok that could bring people’s voices to the world and have people discover the incredible, talented people that had something to say. So it is truly a dream come true.” THR

articles.title: Free IP and Fresh Eyes: How Hollywood Is Reinventing the Classics
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content East of Eden, A Tale of Two Cities, Sense and Sensibility photo illustration THR Staff/Nicholas Brawley Some stories refuse to stay on the page. The Hollywood Reporter’ s Beyond the Book column explores what happens when books make the leap to screen and beyond — unpacking what stayed, changed, how it was done and why it matters with the creatives who made it. *** East of Eden showrunner Zoe Kazan has had her eye on adapting John Steinbeck’s family saga since she first read it at 15. “Somebody has to put the thing on screen that I see in my head,” she told The Hollywood Reporter . And after “a good 20 years” of carrying that feeling, the opportunity to translate the story to screen finally came to fruition, with Kazan’s vision unfurling as an eight-episode Netflix limited series. Related Stories TV 'Transplant' Creator Joseph Kay Sets Overall Deal at Netflix TV 'Nobody Wants This' Star Condemns Adam Brody's Gaza "Genocide" Comments Hollywood has never been shy about mining the classics, with Pride and Prejudice , To Kill a Mockingbird and Little Women among the staples of film and TV’s page-to-screen catalog. This year, Kazan’s dip into the classic canon is joined by the likes of Christopher Nolan, who has taken on Homer’s The Odyssey , Emerald Fennell’s adaptation of Emily Brontë’s Wuthering Heights , and new versions of Jane Austen’s Sense and Sensibility and Charles Dickens’ A Tale of Two Cities . Steinbeck, Austen and Dickens come with name recognition, a built-in audience and, as Sense and Sensibility screenwriter Diana Reid puts it, “free IP.” But the prestige and name recognition only get a project so far with audiences desperate for something fresh. This year, the writers behind Netflix’s East of Eden , Focus Features ’ Sense and Sensibility and MGM+ ’s A Tale of Two Cities used that audience demand to do something different: leave the novels’ worlds intact and rebuild the people inside them. For Kazan, that meant re-reading Steinbeck’s Cathy. For Daniel West, it was giving Dickens’ Lucie a pulse. Reid let the Dashwood sisters Marianne and Elinor each grow into a bit of the other. And while a famous novel might spark initial curiosity, it offers no inherent road map once development begins. So rather than reimagining these books through a modern lens, each writer chose to lean into the ways the stories already transcend time. “You don’t need to spoon-feed the audience the modernity of it,” West says. Why a Classic Novel Already Has Appeal Esmé Creed-Miles stars as Marianne Dashwood and Daisy Edgar-Jones as Elinor Dashwood in Sense and Sensibility. Courtesy of Focus Features Reid is the first to admit the commercial logic of adapting a classic. “I think they are classic for a reason,” she says. But the appeal runs deeper. In an era of surface-level connection, she argues, audiences crave something that feels substantial. “There’s nothing more satisfying as an audience than encountering someone who’s superficially very different from you — they live in another time, they have different values and customs, they dress in a bizarre way — and then realizing that emotionally you have the same inner life.” She also knows she won’t be the last to take on Austen. “It’s nice to be part of such a big catalog. On one hand it’s an honor, and on the other it takes pressure off, because it’ll be one of many. It doesn’t need to be definitive.” West’s pitch for A Tale of Two Cities , a four-part series that premiered on MGM+ last month, started with what he calls a “unicorn”: a book with a huge cultural footprint that, by his account, hadn’t had a major screen adaptation in nearly 40 years. He and star and executive producer Kit Harington had been talking about adapting Dickens’ 1859 novel for roughly a decade, noting that there “hasn’t really been a seminal TV or film adaptation” of the story. “It was done quite a lot in the first half of the 20th century, but then it petered out. So a large part of the draw was the opportunity: There was this huge built-in audience that already knew the book, or at least knew of it,” he says. “The story itself is incredibly timely,” he adds. “It’s about a disenfranchised, broken society that is pushing back and reaching a crisis point. Within that, there’s a very personal, intimate love story.” Kazan has a personal tie to East of Eden — her grandfather, Elia Kazan, directed the 1955 film — but part of her motivation for making a series was to tell more of the novel than that film did. Though Steinbeck’s book was published in 1952, she says, “there’s this beautiful continuum between us and the past,” which is part of what makes revisiting a classic so appealing. Looking backward and forward at the same time, she adds, “is a profound part of what makes us human.” “It’s the opposite of AI. It’s not regurgitation, not spitting back up what we’ve already digested,” she says. “It’s why we should read these books. They’re like a bow shot across time from one human to another.” Rethinking the Novels’ Protagonists Mirren Mack as Lucie Manette in A Tale of Two Cities . Marcell Piti/Federation Studios/MGM+ Still, none of the three writers treated an established title as a safety net. Instead, their adaptations declined to modernize the novel’s setting and embraced finding new ways into the protagonists. While developing A Tale of Two Cities , West and his producers considered a contemporary reimagining early on before dropping it. “The issues these characters are dealing with, the injustice and the way it bleeds into vengeance and cruelty, already feel very 2026,” he says. What he changed instead was characterization. In Dickens’ novel, heroine Lucie Manette is “prone to a lot of weeping” and “quite a lot of fainting,” West says. “She’s not the most compelling heroine in large passages of it. So we made some fundamental changes. We made her much more intentional.” He wanted Lucie to be “the central pivot of the entire story” and “the investigative force” of the opening episodes, pushing against the walls of “buttoned-up Georgian London.” “That was a fairly big modernization from the book,” he says. Of Mirren Mack, who plays Lucie in the series, he adds: “Lucie is the central component of the whole thing, the sun at the center of the solar system, and then an actor arrives who delivers all of that and more and elevates it through her own interpretation.” He also replaced Jarvis Lorry and Miss Pross — who he felt were “serving a similar purpose” and were too “big and colorful” for the series’ taut, volatile tone — with a new character, Hester (Sharon Duncan-Brewster). “She isn’t a proxy father figure to Lucie. She’s an inherited family member, almost an inherited stepmother. … As the story goes on, they discover that they mean a lot to each other and are more than just inherited relations. They really are family, but they come to that on their own terms. That gives them a larger emotional distance to travel.” Thérèse Defarge (Roxane Duran) marks another departure. “We wanted to see somebody become, for want of a less anachronistic word, radicalized,” West says. “She starts as part of her community. She has a warmth and generosity. Because of what happens to her within the story, we see that crack begin to metastasize into something really sinister and ugly, and by the end, murderous. When we meet her in episode one, she’s a completely different person from what we see at the very end of the show.” From left: François Civil as Charles Darnay and Kit Harington as Sydney Carton in A Tale of Two Cities . Marcell Piti/Federation Studios/MGM+ Dickens’ book centers on a couple, but West wanted to “intensify that” and “twist it slightly into much more of a triangle and make it more live and more complex” between Sydney Carton (Harington), Lucie (Mack) and Charles Darnay (François Civil). “That way we don’t really know which way Lucie is going to go until she does, toward the back end of the story. I also wanted both men to be equally attractive, equally intriguing and volatile, each speaking to a different side of her, so we really feel the pull, the tension and the dilemma she’s wrestling with.” Kazan’s re-reading centered on Cathy Ames ( Florence Pugh ), the character who first hooked her in Steinbeck’s story. Writing the series, which released on Netflix on Oct. 1, she realized something she hadn’t anticipated: Cathy “is almost always telling the truth.” A fresh perspective also helped Kazan see the story as a love story between brothers Adam (Christopher Abbott) and Charles (Mike Faist), one that Cathy interrupts. “By watching Chris and Mike interact, I understood how much these characters loved each other,” she says. Respecting the Literary Blueprint — and Knowing When to Change It Creative liberties, the writers insist, aren’t changes for the sake of it. Reid describes her approach as “respect rather than reverence.” Her biggest liberty is a duel between Herbert Nordrum’s Colonel Brandon and Frank Dillane’s John Willoughby, which Austen mentions but keeps offstage. “Hearing about things secondhand in a novel is not so confusing, but on screen, hearing a character describe it isn’t very interesting,” she says. “You need to see it to reveal the drama.” Austen’s voice also served as a guide for balancing drama with wit. “When I read the book, I made a note of the lines that made me laugh, and a lot of those ended up verbatim in the film. Jane Austen’s just really funny,” Reid says. Cathy “is almost always telling the truth,“ Kazan says. Kirsty Griffin/Netflix Kazan’s challenge was the opposite: too much book. She was only interested in adapting it as a series because “the book is simply too big,” and even with seven episodes, “half is not in our series.” For A Tale of Two Cities , West’s key structural decision was genre. “I always wanted it to be a thriller: a very taut, limited story,” he explains. “Four episodes felt like the perfect length to keep the pace and stakes up, and to never let any of the characters settle. I really wanted to make sure that all the characters, whether they’re in London or Paris or moving between the two, are always in a state of agitation. Their feet are never quite on solid ground, so we feel the jeopardy and the volatility of their world.” Why We Keep Going Back Left to right: Mike Faist, Christopher Abbott and Florence Pugh in Netflix‘s East of Eden. Courtesy of Netflix Asked why classics keep returning, each offers their own perspective. West points to archetypes and longevity. A Tale of Two Cities , he says, “is the archetypal sacrificial story,” with “strong parallels in that act of sacrifice to the Bible and all the stories that form the basis of our narratives and our emotional map of the world.” Classics “still feel timeless, and they still feel as resonant today,” West adds. “The key thing for us as creatives is to find a new way of telling those classic stories, an angle and something new to say about them. That doesn’t mean reinventing the wheel. It just means giving yourself the license to look at them with fresh eyes.” Reid returns to the idea that classics are “classics for a reason.” She explains that “when an audience doesn’t feel patronized” and an adaptation allows “the classic to exist in its own time, that makes for incredibly powerful viewing.” Kazan sees adaptations as a way to lower the barrier for new readers. “One thing these adaptations can do is make a general audience feel they have access to East of Eden , The Odyssey , Wuthering Heights .” While they have differing ideas about what keeps the classics coming back, all three writers share the same hope: that viewers will pick up the book. Classics haven’t disappeared from school reading lists, but students are reportedly reading significantly fewer full-length books than in past decades. “As long as we don’t ban and burn these books, everybody will continue to have access to them,” Kazan says. “There are so many books I came to as an adult that changed my life, and if I’d read them in high school, I wouldn’t have cared or understood. The most important thing is to let kids feel they can have pleasure in reading.” There’s already evidence that these adaptations are sending people back to the page. Since the series’ Oct. 1 debut, sales of East of Eden have risen nearly 200 percent across all formats, according to publisher Penguin Classics. The novel also hit No. 1 on Amazon’s bestsellers list — 74 years after it was published. The Economist reports that U.S. sales of The Odyssey have quadrupled this year, while Wuthering Heights topped Britain’s bestseller list. “Anything that can nudge people back toward bookshops and toward discovering those works again can only be a good thing,” West says. “The reason the work of classic storytellers like Dickens, Shakespeare and Austen still resonates is that they’re saying something about the human condition, about what we’re all struggling with, yearning for and reaching for.” “It would be amazing if people went back to the book,” Reid says. If Sense and Sensibility “could make Austen and the classics feel less intimidating, and encourage people to see themselves in it and find emotional truth in a story they thought was too remote, that would be amazing!” “It would be amazing if people went back to the book,” Sense and Sensibility screenwriter Reid says. Courtesy of Focus Features THR

By Marc Malkin Plus Icon Marc Malkin Senior Editor, Culture and Events marcmalkin Latest Jennifer Lopez to Release New Single ‘Proof of Love’: ‘It’s a Happy Dance Song’ That Also Addresses ‘Pain and Grief When Someone’s Gone’ (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago Actors on the Verge of Losing SAG-AFTRA Health Insurance Find Support via ‘One Job Away’ Instagram Campaign: ‘The System Is Not Working’ 2 days ago Owen Thiele on His New Tinder Campaign, ‘Adults’ Season 3 and the ‘13 Going on 30’ Sequel (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Swan Gallet Jennifer Lopez is getting close to releasing new music. The multi-hyphenate tells me she was inspired to write and record again when her kids, twins Max and Emme Muniz with ex-husband Mark Anthony, left for college. “They take up such a big part of your brain for so long, and when they’re gone, which is devastating and sad and scary, you’re facing a life that’s totally different now, and you’re like, ‘What am I going to do with this space and this time?’ For me, I just went back in the studio. I’ve written some of the best songs that I’ve ever written, and I’m really excited,” Lopez tells me. “It’s a very happy era album. It’s some of the most joyous, beautiful songs that have just a tad of a tear in them.” Related Stories Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ The first new song, “Proof of Love,” will be included as a bonus track on the first-ever vinyl release of her 2011 album “Love?” in November. “It’s really a beautiful song about this kind of duality,” Lopez says. “It’s this happy dance song, and these are the things that are the proof of love. One of them is pain and grief when someone’s gone. You feel pain and grief. That’s really proof of love.” She continues, “I wanted to make that a happy thing. articles.full_text: Oct 28, 2026 5:00am PT Josh O’Connor Is a Reluctant Boxer in First-Look Clip of National Theatre Live’s ‘Golden Boy’ Ahead of Cinema Release (EXCLUSIVE) By Ellise Shafer Plus Icon Ellise Shafer Latest Josh O’Connor Is a Reluctant Boxer in First-Look Clip of National Theatre Live’s ‘Golden Boy’ Ahead of Cinema Release (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago Amelia Dimoldenberg’s Final ‘Chicken Shop Date’ Series to Screen in Theaters 1 day ago Meghan Markle to Co-Host ‘Junior MasterChef Australia’ 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Josh O’Connor may be in the James Bond conversation, but his next on-screen role is a filmed version of his most recent play, “Golden Boy.” After its sold-out run at London’s Almeida Theatre, National Theatre Live is bringing “Golden Boy” to the big screen starting Nov. 5. In Clifford Odets’ acclaimed play — directed by Sam Yates — O’Connor stars as Joe Bonaparte, “a gifted young violinist with a future in music, until a chance at fame and fortune lures him into the brutal world of professional boxing,” according to its synopsis. “He must confront what he’s willing to sacrifice, who he’s willing to become and how to find his place in a world that demands he choose a side.” Related Stories Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ In the exclusive first-look clip above, O’Connor artfully grapples with his longing to return to music, hugging a past version of himself playing the violin as his face bleeds from a boxing injury. Filmed during a performance at the Almeida Theatre, “Golden Boy” features a live string quartet alongside O’Connor and fellow cast members Hayley Squires and Daniel Mays. “Golden Boy” marked O’Connor’s return to the London stage after five years, in which he’s catapulted to worldwide fame. He’s an Emmy winner for his portrayal of King Charles in Netflix’s “The Crown,” and has earned acclaim for his film roles including “La Chimera,” Luca Guadagnino’s “Challengers,” “Knives Out: Wake Up Dead Man” and Steven Spielberg’s “Disclosure Day.” “Golden Boy” is coming to theaters worldwide starting Nov. 5. articles.full_text: × Oct 28, 2026 5:07am PT Latvian Oscar Submission ‘Ulya’ Sells Wide Ahead of Opening Tallinn: ‘This Film Is a Blockbuster’ (EXCLUSIVE) 'Ulya' has closed sales to a North America and France, while now the second most-watched film in Latvian history, notes director Viesturs Kairiš By Marta Balaga Plus Icon Marta Balaga Latest Latvian Oscar Submission ‘Ulya’ Sells Wide Ahead of Opening Tallinn: ‘This Film Is a Blockbuster’ (EXCLUSIVE) 3 hours ago ‘Barbara Forever’ Director Brydie O’Connor on Celebrating a Lesbian Icon Who Did It All – and Getting Support From Christine Vachon 1 day ago ‘Good Girls’ Director on Life in Girls’ Correctional Center in Poland: ‘It Damages You Even More’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Ulya,' Courtesy of Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival International distributors continue to fall for “ Ulya .” The Latvian Oscar submission for Best International Feature Film has closed North America (New Mountain Films), France (Destiny), Italy (Invisible Carpet), Slovakia (ASFK), former Yugoslavia (Five Star Distribution), Estonia (Hea Film), Lithuania (GPI), MENA (Teleview), Finland (Cinema Orion), Poland (1989) and Brazil (Belas Arte). Related Stories Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ The black-and-white film, directed by Viesturs Kairišs , will open the 30th edition of Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival . It premiered at Cannes’ Un Certain Regard section. Produced by Ego Media (LV), Allfilm (EE), Staroń Film (PL) and Tremora (LT), it’s sold by B-Rated International. Inspired by the life of legendary basketball player Ulyana Semjonova, born in 1952, “Ulya” is not a typical biopic. “I don’t think I could ever make a nice, typical biopic. My interest lies in arthouse films. I wasn’t really thinking about sports either. I wanted to tell a Werner Herzog-esque story about a giant girl living in the countryside,” Kairišs told Variety . Semjonova was known for her size; she stood at seven feet tall. But it also made her a bit of a recluse. “I’ve been wondering how to get into her head. I wanted it to be very, very subjective. To stick to her point of view, we used what we called ‘crazy cameras’ and slightly out-of-focus shots. Finding the landscape of her inner soul was a very concrete task.” It was not Kairišs who came up with the idea of making a film about Semjonova. It was the long-held dream of his lead, Kārlis Arnolds Avots . “When I became the artistic director of the Dailes Theatre, I was looking for actors and he was outstanding. During our first meeting, when I asked him to join our ensemble, he said: ‘You know, I would like to play Ulyana Semjonova.’ Then I forgot all about it,” recalled Kairišs. “In theatre, it’s not unusual for men to play women. It goes back to Shakespearean times. A few years later, he played in my film ‘January’. At one point, while I was resting, I heard Kārlis talking to our DP, explaining this idea to him again. That’s when I realized: It’s a film!” Other collaborators still needed convincing, though. “Everyone wanted us to make a standard biopic. I understand it. It could be a good film, but it wouldn’t be my film. We set out to make a film about a girl and we just had to believe in it.” As proved by a photograph of Semjonova with Kārlis Arnolds Avots, added at the end of the film, she actually gave them her blessing. She passed away in January, 2026. “She trusted us. It must have been strange to have us come over and say: ‘And a boy will be playing you.’ But it quickly became clear why it made sense,” said Kairišs. “I actually saw Kārlis yesterday. He’s been filming [the Viking series] ‘Bloodaxe,’ so he has a long beard and he’s really big right now. But he always felt close to her somehow. He knew how it felt to be treated as a ‘giant’.” Or simply as an outsider. To Kairišs’ surprise, “Ulya” has managed to connect with all kinds of viewers, regardless of their size. “Everyone is struggling with something they want to hide, but it’s probably the best part of who they are,” he said. “We had incredible reactions everywhere in Latvia. This film is a blockbuster – we’re already the second most-watched film in history. It was the same at Cannes, Rome and Los Angeles. None of my previous films have received this kind of response. Even my daughter said to me: ‘It’s about me, too.’ We touched upon something that’s very modern and very universal.” Kairišs added: “There’s so much pressure today to look the same and like the same things. We live in times that try to kill all the difference. Everyone struggles with their identity or feels like a ‘freak’. We just have to learn to trust this freak and embrace it as the best thing about us, rather than trying to get rid of it.” Viesturs Kairišs and actor Kārlis Arnolds Avots Courtesy of Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival Secuoya Studios Taps Carla Gómez to Lead Latin American Development as Regional Expansion Accelerates (EXCLUSIVE) HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ Music Will Be ‘As Far Away as Possible’ From the Movies; Hans Zimmer Says ‘I Can’t Write Like John Williams’ ‘Girls’ Shocker: Lena Dunham Sets Revival at HBO With Allison Williams, Zosia Mamet, Jemima Kirke Returning ‘Industry’ Season 5 Casts Ben Platt, Russell Tovey ‘Lanterns’ Episode 7 Hits 7 Million U.S. Viewers in Three Days as Season Reaches Average of Nearly 19 Million Globally ‘Harry Potter’ HBO Series Casts Its Arthur Weasley, Moaning Myrtle, Colin Creevey Loading comments...

articles.title: Jennifer Lawrence Says Playing Katniss Again After 11 Years in ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Was ‘Crazy,’ ‘Unbelievable’ and ‘So Beautiful’
articles.full_text: × Oct 28, 2026 6:38am PT Jennifer Lawrence Says Playing Katniss Again After 11 Years in ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Was ‘Crazy,’ ‘Unbelievable’ and ‘So Beautiful’ By Zack Sharf Plus Icon Zack Sharf Digital News Director ZSharf Latest Jennifer Lawrence Says Playing Katniss Again After 11 Years in ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Was ‘Crazy,’ ‘Unbelievable’ and ‘So Beautiful’ 2 hours ago Barry Keoghan Undergoes Skin-Tightening Cosmetic Treatment in Video Posted Months After He Called Out Online Abuse Over ‘How I Look’ 17 hours ago Jennifer Lawrence Did Not Start Her Beauty Brand Because of Hollywood Instability: ‘A Smarter Exit Plan Would Be Signing Up for a Big Franchise’ 22 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source ©Lions Gate/Courtesy Everett Collection Jennifer Lawrence appeared on the latest episode of the “Call Her Daddy” podcast and spoke out for the first time about what it was like to reprise Katniss Everdeen for the first time in 11 years. The Oscar winner is back as her iconic “Hunger Games” character in the upcoming prequel movie “Sunrise on the Reaping,” in theaters Nov. 20 from Lionsgate. “It was unbelievable,” Lawrence said about reprising Katniss. “It was so crazy. It was the same crew. It was the same AD, who I’ve worked with a million times because I love him. And with Josh [Hutcherson] and Woody [Harrelson] … it was so emotional. Josh and I didn’t walk to the bathroom without our arms around each other. It was so beautiful. And Woody, obviously, came through the window of my hotel room uninvited. It wouldn’t be the same if he listened to boundaries or used a door.” Related Stories Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ Variety reported last December that Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson were returning as Katniss and Peeta Mellark for a scene in “Sunrise on the Reaping.” Lawrence has now let it slip that Woody Harrelson will also be back as Haymitch. The new prequel movie centers on a young Haymitch (played by Joseph Zada) as he competes in the 50th Hunger Games. Book readers know that Suzanne Collins’ “Sunrise on the Reaping” novel ends with a flash-forward epilogue featuring Katniss, Peeta and Haymitch, so it appears the film adpatation is following suit. Lawrence told Variety during her “No Hard Feelings” press tour in 2023 that she was “totally” open to reprising her “Hunger Games” role of Katniss Everdeen should the right opportunity arise. She added at the time, “If Katniss ever could ever come back into my life, 100 percent.” As Katniss, Lawrence headlined four “Hunger Games” movies between 2012 and 2015. The franchise (which also includes the Rachel Zegler-led 2023 prequel “The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes”) has grossed $3.3 billion to date at the worldwide box office. “What made me nervous was how it could negatively affect my acting career and my personal life,” Lawrence said on the “Call Her Daddy” podcast about her biggest concern with joining the franchise when she was 20 years old. “The one thing I was always sure of when I was younger was that I wanted to be a mom, and this looked so different then doing some indies. ‘Twilight’ had just come out and everybody saw what that was. It was more like… how is this going to change my life and my acting career?” Watch Lawrence’s full interview on the “Call Her Daddy” podcast in the video below. articles.full_text: × Oct 28, 2026 7:00am PT Oscar Contender ‘Shame and Money’ Acquired in North America by Oscilloscope (EXCLUSIVE) By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest Oscar Contender ‘Shame and Money’ Acquired in North America by Oscilloscope (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago BAFTA Names Hilary Rosen as Chair 23 hours ago David Bowie Immersive Concert Experience ‘Stage’ From Brett Morgen to World Premiere at Berlin Film Festival 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Vicky Bane, Schuldenberg Films Oscilloscope Laboratories has acquired North American rights to Visar Morina ’s “ Shame and Money .” The film won the Grand Jury Prize in the World Cinema Dramatic Competition at the Sundance Film Festival, which qualifies it to compete for the Oscar for international feature film under new Academy rules . Oscilloscope is planning a theatrical release in early 2027. The film, which stars Astrit Kabashi, Flonja Kodheli, Kumrije Hoxa, Fiona Gllavica and Alban Ukaj, was co-written by Morina with Doruntina Basha. Related Stories Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ The film centers on a couple in their 40s who live with their extended family in rural Kosovo making a modest living on their farm. Following a familial dispute, their livelihood is lost. They are forced to move to Pristina where the pressure to provide for their family weighs heavily on the parents as they do their best to find work and a place to stay. Morina said: “In times when the majority of people worldwide are finding it increasingly difficult to make ends meet, I believe we need a kind of class consciousness, and I hope our film makes a small contribution toward that.” Oscilloscope president Dan Berger said, “Visar’s has drawn a portrait of a family that is subtle, searingly real and ultimately humane. We feel as one with the characters and their struggles, fully signed on for this indictment of an economic system constructed to keep too many people down.” The producers are Fabian Altenried, Sophie Ahrens and Kristof Gerega from Schuldenberg Films (“Objet a,” “Strange River,” “Life Is Not a Competition but I’m Winning”), along with Pia Hellenthal (“Searching Eva”) and Morina. articles.title: Peter Medak, Director of ‘The Changeling’ and ‘The Krays,’ Dies at 88
articles.full_text: × Oct 28, 2026 7:18am PT Peter Medak, Director of ‘The Changeling’ and ‘The Krays,’ Dies at 88 Medak also worked extensively in television, directing episodes of "Breaking Bad" and "The Wire." By Anna Tingley Plus Icon Anna Tingley Latest Peter Medak, Director of ‘The Changeling’ and ‘The Krays,’ Dies at 88 1 hour ago As NFL Expands Globally, Marriott Bonvoy Taps Cooper Kupp, Jerry Rice and More for City Travel Guides 20 hours ago Joy Behar Returns to ‘The View’ After Nearly a Month Away: ‘I Dislocated My Shoulder’ and the Pain Was ‘Worse Than Childbirth’ 24 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Peter Medak , the Hungarian-born director and actor best known for films including “ The Changeling ,” “ The Krays ” and “The Ruling Class” died Tuesday in Los Angeles. He was 88. Over a career spanning six decades, Medak directed 27 feature films, moving between psychological horror, black comedy and crime dramas. His 1980 supernatural thriller “The Changeling,” starring George C. Scott, won eight Genie Awards including best motion picture. He also directed the 1990 British gangster drama “The Krays,” for which he received the Evening Standard Award for best director. Related Stories Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ Born in Budapest in 1937, Medak spent part of World War II in hiding with his family. Under Hungary’s Communist regime, his father was imprisoned and Medak was barred from attending school. He fled to England during the Hungarian Revolution of 1956 and began working in the British film industry, eventually serving as assistant director before moving to Hollywood. He made his feature directorial debut with 1968’s “Negatives,” starring Glenda Jackson. His 1972 satire “The Ruling Class,” starring Peter O’ Toole, competed for the Palme d’Or at Cannes and earned an Oscar nomination for Toole. Other credits include “A Day in the Death of Joe Egg,” “Let Him Have It” and the Gary Oldman-led “Romeo Is Bleeding.” Medak also worked extensively in television, directing episodes of “Homocide: Life on the Street,” “The Wire,” “Breaking Bad” and “House.” His 2018 documentary “The Ghost of Peter Sellars” revisited his troubled production of the 1970s comedy “Ghost in the Noonday Sun.” He is survived by his four children, Christopher, Joshua, Karen and Cornela, and five grandchildren. articles.title: Fox News Ratings Sink a Staggering 27% in October, but It Still Has Much a Larger Audience Than CNN or MS NOW
articles.full_text: × Oct 28, 2026 8:10am PT Fox News Ratings Sink a Staggering 27% in October, but It Still Has Much a Larger Audience Than CNN or MS NOW By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Fox News Ratings Sink a Staggering 27% in October, but It Still Has Much a Larger Audience Than CNN or MS NOW 14 minutes ago Elmo Is Going as Meryl Streep’s Evil Fashion Editor Miranda Priestly for Halloween This Year 18 hours ago Trump Says ‘Artificial Intelligence’ Is ‘a Very Bad and Inaccurate Name,’ and That He Wants to Officially Ban the Term ‘AI’ 21 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Fox News In the lead-up to the 2026 midterm elections, Fox News lost more than a quarter of its overall viewing audience in the month of October, according to new data. That said, the network remains the most-watched news outlet on cable, well ahead of rivals CNN and MS NOW . For October 2026, Fox News is on track to post its lowest-rated month in total-day viewers since December 2023, according to preliminary figures from Nielsen, first reported by Status. FNC averaged 1.1 million total viewers for the month, down 27%, and 98,000 viewers in the key 25-54 demographic coveted by advertisers, a drop of 32%. Related Stories Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ The ratings decline comes amid a continuation of the drop-off in TV viewers overall — but Fox News has been losing viewers at a double-digit clip as CNN and MS NOW have been slightly up in recent months. As Variety has reported, Fox News on many nights draws a bigger live audience than one or more broadcast TV networks. But its viewership is steadily eroding: In the third quarter of 2026, Fox News saw total-day viewership decline 16%, and viewership in the 25-54 demo fall 24%. Both CNN and MS NOW saw small gains in overall audience for Q3. In primetime, Fox News averaged about 2 million total viewers (down 28% year over year) in October, with viewers in the 25-54 demo falling 36% to 183,000, according to the Nielsen data. “Fox & Friends” had its second consecutive month below 1 million total viewers and under 100,000 in the key demo, with October representing its lowest overall viewers since July 2015 (and its lowest in the 25-54 demographic since June 2001). Meanwhile, progressive rival MS NOW saw its daytime audience rise 16% to 588,000 total viewers in October, and CNN viewership was up 3% to 402,000 viewers over the same timeframe, according to the preliminary Nielsen figures. Variety has reached out to Fox News for comment. Some observers detect a worrisome sign in Fox News’ ratings decline that conservatives are tuning out at rates faster than CNN or MS NOW as the fight for control of the Senate and House of Representatives will be up for grabs on Election Day next week, Nov. 3. President Donald Trump — whose feelings about Fox News historically run hot and cold — recently complained that the network has not been backing Republicans strongly enough. “Fox spends more time defending Dumocrats, and putting on their views versus their Republican opponent, than at any time in the History of FoxNews,” Trump wrote in an Oct. 19 post on Truth Social. “It’s ridiculous! articles.title: ‘Talk To Me’ Backer Head Gear Opens U.S. Arm With Ambitious Indie Investment Plan
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart Sphere Media & Paul Barbeau Team Up To Bring TV Drama To Quebec Maxine Peake Boards Short Film ‘The Secret Assistants’ Exploring Power Imbalances In The Movie Business Riley Voelkel & Shiva Negar To Voice Adult Animated Comedy Project ‘Above Average’ View All October 28, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Phil Hunt, Samantha Allwinton Head Gear Films EXCLUSIVE: Head Gear Films is opening in the U.S. and company co-founder and CEO Phil Hunt has told Deadline Head Gear US will sink $120M into U.S. indie film and TV in year one. Head Gear exec Samantha Allwinton will run the new unit as Director of Operations. She will be based in Denver and spend time between there and LA. She was previously COO of Head Gear Films, based in London. Before joining Head Gear she was at Ingenious Media. Head Gear majors in independent film, TV and games finance, including government incentives, presales, gap and bridge funding, as well as executive production and packaging. It has recently helped finance The Apprentice , Talk to Me and How to Have Sex . Related Stories News New AFM Summit To Explore Federal Production Tax Incentive Politics Federal Film & TV Tax Credit Bill Adds Eight New Senate Co-Sponsors The Head Gear US office is opening its doors as a new proposed federal tax credit, part of the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, is moving through Congress. It would apply on top of new and existing state-level incentives. Watch on Deadline Hunt said he wants Head Gear to be in position as the aforementioned industry-boosting measures take effect, which he expects to happen by year-end. “Over 50% of our deal flow is American movies, so we’ve already laid that down. The reason to go to LA is to increase that flow because the federal tax credit’s coming in, which is nice timing. It’s about having more of a foothold in the U.S. and being on their time zone.” He added: “U.S. producers will have half their budget covered and still need the rest. We’ve closed that gap on close to 600 films. We want to be there before the rush.” Head Gear is using existing resources for its U.S. expansion and will provide various types of finance. “When we look at where the company is at right now, and all the other companies that we’re horizontally integrated into, they’re growing. We have got money that we can deploy,” Hunt said. The Head Gear team are regular visitors to the U.S. and Hunt made the point that having a full-fledged base there has been a long-held ambition. “I’ve been meaning to open up in the States for a very long time. I’ve never found the right person until now, who’s got exactly what Head Gear needs and understands Head Gear’s character and ethos, which is quite different from that of most people.” The newly-minted Head Gear US will be at AFM in November and then Sundance in January. “Independent producers need partners who understand their projects and know how to make the numbers work,” Allwinton said. “That’s what we’ve built Head Gear on and it’s what we’re bringing to the U.S. I’m looking forward to sitting across the table from American filmmakers and helping turn their most ambitious ideas into finished films and series.” Production Focus Hunt co-founded Head Gear in 2002 with Compton Ross, who as well as his film interests has been a CEO in the international oil and gas industry for 48 years. With the U.S. office opening, Hunt also spoke about his wider strategy for the business and plans to boost Head Gear’s production-side role. “We’ve been silently kind of working on the production side of Head Gear, and the next phase for us as a business is going back into production and really kind of being the producer’s producer. So, working for the producer in the background; they’ve developed projects, and then we help package them up, do the business affairs, get them off the ground, run finance plans, and then years down the line, we’re still helping collect the money.” Hunt said Head Gear is helping to fund about 30 movies a year and is a hands-on exec producer on a third of those. “Coming from a ‘failed’ producer background, I’m really fascinated with helping producers and guiding them through the marketplace better than ever using our data.” Hasan Piker Sues CNN’s Scott Jennings For $72.5M Over “Manipulated” Video ‘Star Trek’ Vets Reunite For Sci-Fi ‘Life 2.0′; Stephen Fry & Jane Horrocks Comedy Set Russell Brand Forcefully Denies Charges As He Gives Evidence In Rape Trial How ‘Klara And The Sun’ Got Blotted Out At the Box Office With Gloomy Opening Read More About: Comments

articles.title: BBC “Disappointed” As Staff Plan Industrial Action Vote Over Job Cuts
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Russell Brand Forcefully Denies Charges As He Gives Evidence During Rape Trial: “Consent Is More Important Than Sex Itself” Inside The BBC Cuts: Painful Service Closures Begin, But Worse Could Be To Come Meghan Markle “Deeply Distressed” Over Allegation Her Father Possessed Child Abuse Images View All October 28, 2026 6:23am Add us as a Google Preferred Source BBC News presenter Clive Myrie BBC EXCLUSIVE : The BBC ‘s plan to cut more than 100 journalism roles will be put to an industrial ballot amid unrest over the UK broadcaster’s £500 million ($664M) savings strategy. The National Union of Journalists (NUJ) will ballot members next month over newsroom redundancies, with members voting on whether to take strike action or other industrial measures, such as work to rule. BBC News announced last week that the division will close more than 100 roles over the coming months, saving £5.5M. BBC News still needs to find at least another £20M to hit its minimum goal of £51M in savings. Related Stories News BBC Pays $530,000 To 'Mr. Nobody Against Putin' Exec Over Antisemitism Claims News Disney+ Among Buyers For RTÉ & BBC Drama 'The Walsh Sisters' Rhodri Talfan Davies, the BBC’s deputy director general, emailed staff about the NUJ’s decision on Wednesday, saying the ballot was a “disappointing development.” Watch on Deadline “Over recent months, we have had extensive and constructive discussions with the NUJ and been clear that we will do everything possible to minimise compulsory redundancies. We’ve backed that up with action too – a large majority of the redundancies agreed to date have been achieved on a voluntary basis,” Talfan Davies said. “Faced with a £500 million financial savings challenge and significant operational pressures, we cannot offer a guarantee that there will be no compulsory redundancies. Whilst we will continue to do everything possible to minimise this, the reality is that no organisation of our scale and complexity could offer such an undertaking and it would inevitably compromise our service to audiences if we did.” The NUJ ballot will run from November 3 to 24. It is separate from a second ballot on pay, which closes on November 5. The BBC has increased its pay offer to a 1.5% rise or a minimum of £1,000, depending on which is higher. The corporation previously offered a 1% rise or a minimum of £500. The BBC has also ditched controversial changes to staff terms, including slashing usage for night shift workers . The NUJ and Bectu have a neutral position on the BBC pay offer, meaning they have neither endorsed nor denounced the deal. articles.title: Peter Medak Dies: ‘The Ruling Class’ & ‘Romeo Is Bleeding’ Director Was 88
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Peter Medak Dies: ‘The Ruling Class’ & ‘Romeo Is Bleeding’ Director Was 88 Kevin Bleyer Dies: Emmy Winning ‘Daily Show’ Writer & Barack Obama Speech Writer Dies In Car Crash At 54 Broadway’s ‘A Few Good Men’, ‘Other Desert Cities’, ‘860’ Fill Seats With Brisk Autumn Box Office View All October 28, 2026 6:24am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Peter Medak Courtesy Peter Medak , the award-winning Hungarian-British film and television director with a career spanning six decades and credits including The Changeling starring George C. Scott, Romeo Is Bleeding with Gary Oldman and The Krays starring Martin and Gary Kemp, died Tuesday, October 27 in Los Angeles. He was 88. His death was announced by family. Though a cause was not stated, the family noted that Medak died peacefully. Born in Budapest, Hungary in 1937, Medak showed interest in movie-making by the time he was eight years old when his aunt gave him a 35-millimeter hand-cranked projector and a piece of film. At 13, under the Communist regime, he was banned from going to school, later saying, “my father was a so-called capitalist…he was… put away to prison for years. … I spent an awful lot of time on my own, in our apartment, because my father was in prison, my mother was working in a plastics factory, I had a brother who died. …I became an observer… you know, looking through this incredible keyhole of our apartment.” Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries News Kevin Bleyer Dies: Emmy Winning ‘Daily Show’ Writer & Barack Obama Speech Writer Dies In Car Crash At 54 After fleeing to England in 1956 at 18, Medak started as a trainee at Associated British-Pathe, and worked on the sets of major British productions while soon getting promoted to assistant director on films such as The Great Armored Car Swindle (1961) and The Phantom of the Opera (1962). MCA Universal Pictures quickly noticed his work and in 1963, and he was brought to Los Angeles and signed to a television-directing contract, working on the series Court Martial. Watch on Deadline In 1967 Paramount signed him to direct his first feature, Negatives , with Glenda Jackson. His next two films were the highly acclaimed black comedies A Day in the Death of Joe Egg (1972), starring Alan Bates, and The Ruling Class (1972), with Peter O’ Toole, for which Medak was nominated for the Palme D’Or, and O’Toole was nominated for an Academy Award. Medak earned a reputation across his six-decade career as an “actors’ director,” resulting in 27 features with such acclaimed films as The Changeling (1980) with George C. Scott; The Krays (1990); Let Him Have It (1991), and Romeo is Bleeding (1993), with Gary Oldman. His 2018 documentary The Ghost of Peter Sellers received acclaim, winning Best Documentary at the Beverly Hills Film Festival. His prolific television directing work included of Homicide: Life on the Street, Chicago Hope, The Wire and Breaking Bad . With a deep interest in music, he directed some of the earliest music videos for artists such as Peter Gabriel and Pink Floyd, and, in the opera realm, directed La voix humaine with Julia Migenes. He staged a production of Salome in Minneapolis and Rigoletto with the Los Angeles Opera. In a career spanning 60 years, making both cult and critically acclaimed movies, Medak directed 27 features and 59 episodes of television. “If it’s in your blood, directing,” he said once. “You never stop directing and it doesn’t matter that you’re alone in your mind, dreaming or imagining things but you’re always making a movie.” Medak is survived by his children Christopher, Joshua, Karen and Cornelia Medak and grandchildren Sacha, Marlowe, Ryden, Oliver and Anders. He was previously married to Katherine La Kermance, Carolyn Seymour and Julia Migenes, and was in a relationship with Christine Wagner. articles.title: Tracee Ellis Ross, Lake Bell & Ken Leung Thriller ‘Blow The Horn’ Heads To AFM For Sales
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Four ‘Star Trek’ Vets Reunite For Sci-Fi ‘Life 2.0’, OneTwoThree Media Launches AFM Sales; Brit Comedy With Stephen Fry, Jane Horrocks Also On Slate Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell Set For Scout Taylor-Compton’s Horror Movie ‘Survive: The Game’; Filming Underway In Spain Tracee Ellis Ross, Lake Bell & Ken Leung Thriller ‘Blow The Horn’ Heads To AFM For Sales View All October 28, 2026 6:26am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Blow The Horn Concourse EXCLUSIVE : Concourse Media has acquired worldwide sales rights to the completed ensemble psychological thriller, Blow The Horn , starring Tracee Ellis Ross ( Black-ish ), Lake Bell ( In a World… ), Ken Leung (Industry ), Joshua Boone ( A Jazzman’s Blues ), Wrenn Schmidt ( For All Mankind ) and Dallas Roberts ( Monsters: The Lyle and Erik Menendez Story ). The company will introduce the film to domestic and international buyers at the upcoming American Film Market in Los Angeles. Written and directed by Nacho Arenas ( Momma ) as an adaptation of Del Federico’s play, the film recently made its world premiere at the Woodstock Film Festival before continuing its festival run at the Newport Beach Film Festival. The film was produced by Arenas alongside Jamin O’Brien ( Die My Love ). Related Stories News Annecy Title 'Cloud Girl' Flies To International Buyers For SC Films News Lilly Wachowski Boards Comedy 'Making A Bridesmaid' As Project Heads To AFM For Sales Based on Matías Del Federico’s Argentine stage play Bajo Terapia , the film “follows three couples who arrive at a Brooklyn artist’s studio expecting individual sessions with their psychologist. Instead, they discover their therapist left behind a letter and a series of sealed envelopes instructing them to conduct their own unconventional group therapy session, which quickly spirals into an increasingly volatile confrontation as long-buried secrets, betrayals and uncomfortable truths come to light. As the couples turn on one another and their relationships begin to unravel, the session builds toward a series of revelations that challenge everything they thought they knew about their partners.” Watch on Deadline “What’s exciting about Blow The Horn is that it takes a universally relatable subject and turns it into something wildly entertaining, unpredictable and genuinely provocative,” said Kristin Harris, head of acquisitions at Concourse Media. “Coming off its premieres at Woodstock and Newport Beach, we’re excited to bring it to buyers at AFM .” Concourse’s slate also includes Parish starring Nicolas Cage, Dane Dehaan and Alexandra Shipp, which wraps production this week in Minnesota, and Vision Board starring Lucy Hale, which is currently in pre-production. articles.title: Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell Set For Scout Taylor-Compton’s Horror Movie ‘Survive: The Game’; Filming Underway In Spain
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Four ‘Star Trek’ Vets Reunite For Sci-Fi ‘Life 2.0’, OneTwoThree Media Launches AFM Sales; Brit Comedy With Stephen Fry, Jane Horrocks Also On Slate Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell Set For Scout Taylor-Compton’s Horror Movie ‘Survive: The Game’; Filming Underway In Spain Tracee Ellis Ross, Lake Bell & Ken Leung Thriller ‘Blow The Horn’ Heads To AFM For Sales View All October 28, 2026 7:38am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell Jonny Marlow, Slaven Vlasic, Alim Sabir EXCLUSIVE : Olivia Holt ( Heart Eyes ), Jaimie Alexander ( Thor ) and Rohan Campbell ( Halloween Ends ) have been set to lead Scout Taylor-Compton’s Survive: The Game , a horror movie currently filming entirely in Gipuzkoa, Spain, at Zinealdea Studios, and on location in Irún, Spain. The synopsis reads: “When a group of friends unearth an ancient board game inside a secluded cabin with a violent past, each roll of the dice brings a deadly fate to life, and the only way to survive is to finish the game.” Holt, who recently starred in horror Heart Eyes , will appear opposite Alexander, best known for her five-season run as Jane Doe on Blindspot and her recurring role as Lady Sif in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Campbell, who broke out opposite Jamie Lee Curtis in Halloween Ends and currently stars in Netflix’s Below , rounds out the lead cast. Related Stories Agencies Independent Creative Management Signs Serhat Metin News Tracee Ellis Ross, Lake Bell & Ken Leung Thriller 'Blow The Horn' Heads To AFM For Sales Taylor-Compton is directing from a script she wrote with Michael Kennedy ( Heart Eyes ). An actress-turned-filmmaker known for the Halloween franchise, she previously wrote and directed Road to Recovery and co-directed Last Chance Motel . Watch on Deadline The film is being produced by Randy Wayne and Talia Bella under their Rebellium Films banner, Tom O’Connell and Scout Taylor-Compton of Building Blocks Productions, and Amy Covell of Red Phoenix Productions. Executive producers include Leire Apellaniz of Sr. y Sra., Mark Albela, Michael Kennedy, and Dauntless Productions. The production sees the film as having franchise potential. “I’ve played the final girl. I spent years learning what it takes to survive a horror movie: the running, the screaming, the moment you finally turn around and fight,” said Taylor-Compton. “With Survive: The Game , I wanted to ask a different question. What if the thing chasing you isn’t outside the door? What if surviving means confronting the worst version of yourself first?” “This is the fourth film we’ve worked on with Scout, and the second she’s directing for Rebellium,” said producer Randy Wayne. “She’s a powerhouse with an extreme attention to detail and an unmatched drive. Audiences are going to meet antagonists they’ve never seen before – creative, scary, and inventive. We’re honored to help bring Survive: The Game to life with her.” Holt is repped by WME, Entertainment 360, and Yorn, Levine. Alexander is repped by Gersh, Berwick & Kovacik and Ginsburg Daniels Kallis. Campbell is repped by CAA, Sol22 and Webster Talent Management. Taylor-Compton is repped by Innovative Artists. Dorn is joined in the film by fellow Star Trek franchise vets Marina Sirtis ( Star Trek: The Next Generation ), Michelle Hurd ( Star Trek: Picard ), and Dominic Keating ( Star Trek: Enterprise ). Dorn “plays an operative in deep-space isolation, with only an AI hologram for company, until an enigmatic new companion arrives. An accident uncovers the truth about their origins, forcing a fight for survival against motives engineered back on Earth.” Related Stories News Tracee Ellis Ross, Lake Bell & Ken Leung Thriller 'Blow The Horn' Heads To AFM For Sales News Annecy Title 'Cloud Girl' Flies To International Buyers For SC Films Produced by Emily Corcoran for Cork Films and Michael Dorn for Sabrejet, the film was shot entirely in the UK. The project marks Dorn’s feature directing debut and is the first science-fiction feature to reunite Dorn and Sirtis since 2002’s Star Trek: Nemesis . Watch on Deadline Alongside this title, the company has taken on international sales for two further features: the UK sci-fi comedy Time Travel Is Dangerous! and the US psychological thriller The Black Box . Also new to OneTwoThree Media’s slate is Time Travel Is Dangerous!, directed by Chris Reading. The London-set comedy feature is narrated by Stephen Fry and stars Johnny Vegas, Jane Horrocks, Sophie Thompson, and Mark Heap, with Brian Blessed voicing an octopus monster. It premiered at the Austin Film Festival. The third new addition is U.S. film The Black Box , described as a psychological thriller directed by Vitor Cardoso and Ricardo R. Marques. Set in the Hollywood Hills during a graduation farewell party, “a group of friends stumbles upon ‘The Black Box’ — an elusive internet sensation and twisted version of Truth or Dare said to choose its own players.” Deals across the slate were negotiated for OneTwoThree Media by Joey Dawson with Emily Corcoran of Cork Films on Life 2.0 , and Chris Reading of The Unreason Ltd on Time Travel Is Dangerous! , and Alan Green with Mark Silba on The Black Box . articles.title: TBD Post Hires Industry Veteran Matt Wallis As Head Of Post & Operations
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse TBD Post Hires Industry Veteran Matt Wallis As Head Of Post & Operations Independent Creative Management Signs Serhat Metin Kristen Brancaccio To Direct Microdrama & Feature Adaptations Of Claren Hammond’s Short Story ‘Summer Session’ View All October 28, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Matt Wallis TBD Post EXCLUSIVE: The co-creator of Showtime’s Emmy-nominated Disgraced has joined Austin’s TBD Post . Matthew Wallis was named Head of Post & Operations at the Texas -based post-production studio, which works on feature films, series, commercials and branded content for clients including Apple TV, Netflix, Disney and next-gen filmmakers like hugely popular YouTuber Markiplier. Wallis is known as co-creator and co-exec producer on 2017 feature doc Disgraced , which followed the 2003 case of the death of Baylor University basketball star Patrick Dennehy at the hands of teammate Carlton Dotson. He was also head of post on CNN’s High Profits . The 20-year industry veteran has served as producer and post-production supervisor on more than 100 hours of film and TV. Related Stories News James Talarico Leans Into Endorsement From Bill Nye To Launch New Teachers Group News New Goldenrod Platform Helps Productions Secure Texas Film Boost At TBD Post, Wallis will oversee staff, technology, strategy, and workflow across editorial, color, VFX, sound, and finishing, and lead projects from bid through delivery. His hire is part of an expansion of headcount at TBD, which is set to take advantage of the new Texas film incentive scheme, which will total $1.5B over ten years. Watch on Deadline TBD’s founders – Ted Griffis and Brandon Thomas – were among the group that last month launched Goldenrod, a technology-focused production business that consults on opportunities available from the expanded Texas Moving Image Industry Incentive Program . “I’ve worked with TBD since the company started, first as a client, then as a producer. I knew what this team could do long before I considered joining, and that’s most of why I did,” said Wallis. “After twenty years building the systems that let creative people do their best work, I’m bringing all of it here, starting the way I always do, by listening and asking a lot of questions. I’m excited for our future, and the future of post production in Texas.” TBD’s recent credits include Markiplier’s feature Iron Lung , Netflix sports pic The Long Game and Apple TV documentary Fathom , as well as film, television and commercial projects for brands such as Range Rover, EA, Bacardi and Dodge. “Matt has sat in our suites and theaters as a client for over a decade,” said Griffis. “He’s seen our work from the other side of the glass, and he knows exactly where we can go next.
