articles.title: Rolf de Heer & Fellow Tokyo Jury Members Talk Festival ‘A-List’ Ratings, Co-Production & How To Judge Films
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Rolf de Heer & Fellow Tokyo Jury Members Talk Festival ‘A-List’ Ratings, Co-Production & How To Judge Films Parallax Films Boards Sales On ‘Fuxi: Four Tales Of Feasting’ Ahead of Tokyo World Premiere Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi Pledges Support For Japanese Film At Tokyo Fest Opening View All October 26, 2026 9:40pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Yov Moor, Oh Jungwan, Rolf de Heer, Makiko Watanabe, Alex Lo Deadline Australian filmmaker Rolf de Heer , president of the competition jury at this year’s Tokyo International Film Festival, talked about the significance of ‘A-list’ ratings for film festivals at the jury press conference today. Tokyo has recently had its status as an A-list festival reaffirmed by the Fédération Internationale des Associations des Producteurs de Films (FIAPF), a Brussels-based global organization that rates film festivals. But the practice of rating festivals, and the process and criteria for rating them, has proved controversial over the years. Related Stories News Milcho Manchevski Talks 'Sister Brother Manhole Cover', His Second Feature Of 2026 & Exposing Corruption At Macedonia's Film Agency -- Tokyo News Parallax Films Boards Sales On 'Fuxi: Four Tales Of Feasting' Ahead of Tokyo World Premiere In March this year, FIAPF overhauled its festival accreditation system for the first time since 2007, with a new framework that classifies 17 festivals as “A-list” and expanding the overall number of accredited festivals around the world. Five of these festivals are based in the Asia Pacific region, including Tokyo, Busan, IFFI Goa, Cairo and Shanghai. When asked about the ratings system, De Heer said: “Tokyo has always been considered an A-list festival by most people who attend festivals, so in that sense I don’t think it makes a lot of difference. This sort of categorization seems to be becoming more important in terms of the quality of films that are available to a festival, so in that sense it may help that Tokyo now officially has that rating again, but I don’t think it changes the festival so much.” Watch on Deadline FIAPF’s old system classified festivals in four groups: competitive, specialized, non-competitive and documentary and short film festivals. The 2026 reform collapsed the four categories into one group of 49 accredited festivals across 29 countries on five continents. When pushed on the subject with another question, De Heer said: “It matters a great deal to some people and not at all to others, and that is at it should be.” De Heer is heading the main competition jury at this year’s Tokyo film festival , along with Korean producer Oh Jungwan, New York and Tokyo-based producer Alex C. Lo, French colorist Yov Moor and Japanese actress Makiko Watanabe. The jury also talked about international co-productions, as several films in this year’s line-up of 15 competition titles have been structured this way. Lo agreed with a question from the audience about the growing trend: “I didn’t notice there’s an increasing number of co-productions in the festival line-up, but it’s true that a lot of producers in Europe, US and the rest of the world are increasingly seeking co-production opportunities, mainly due to the link to their local government production support.” When asked about the potential for co-productions between Japan and Australia, De Heer noted that the Australian film industry does not approach co-production in the same way as European producers: “It makes no sense for a Japanese film to shoot in Australia, and it makes no sense for an Australian film to shoot in Japan. Europe is very good at doing co-productions only on a financial basis. Australia is not so good at that. “The sort of co-productions that work out of Australia have a natural story where some things need to be shot in Japan, some things in Australia. Those will always be possible if the scripts come and if they’re right.” The jury also talked about their criteria for judging the 15 films in competition, which includes titles from across Europe and the Asia Pacific region. Oh Jungwan said: “For me as a jury member, I’m looking at whether I’m convinced by the story the director is telling and the way he’s telling it.” She later said she’s also prepared to fight for the films she loves and once had a seven-hour discussion about a film when serving on another jury. Yov Moor said: “When watching each film, I’m looking at what is interesting and sincere in the film, but also really trying to imagine what the next film of this director could be.” Makiko Watanabe added: “I try to see films without any preconceived notions and don’t try to look for answers while watching. As jury, there are other things we need to look at, but mostly I’ll look for what touches me and later digest what I took from the film.” Tokyo International Film Festival opened last night and runs for ten days in the Hibiya-Ginza district of Tokyo. It closes on November 4 with the awards ceremony and a screening of Korean filmmaker Yeon Sang-ho’s Colony. articles.title: Bill Kramer Says AMPAS Plans To Expand List Of Festivals That Can Serve As Qualifiers For The International Oscar Category
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Bill Kramer Says AMPAS Plans To Expand List Of Festivals That Can Serve As Qualifiers For The International Oscar Category Milcho Manchevski Talks ‘Sister Brother Manhole Cover’, His Second Feature Of 2026 & Exposing Corruption At Macedonia’s Film Agency — Tokyo Janus Films Acquires Alfonso Cuarón’s ‘Y Tu Mamá También’ Ahead Of 25th Anniversary 4K Re-Release View All October 26, 2026 10:39pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Bill Kramer AMPS The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences will expand the list of festivals that can serve as standalone qualifiers for the International Film Oscar category, AMPAS CEO Bill Kramer confirmed this morning during an interview with Deadline at the Tokyo Film Festival. Related Stories News Oscars 2027 International Feature Film Submissions By Country: UK, Argentina, Iran, Rwanda Among Latest To Declare Below The Line 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More Kramer, who has become a frequent fixture on the international festival circuit in recent years, is at Tokyo alongside AMPAS President Lynette Howell Taylor and Chief Membership, Impact and Industry Officer Meredith Shea to take part in a series of public talks titled Academy in Tokyo. The sessions are one of the headline events this year at the Tokyo Film Festival . Kramer will also receive an honorary leadership award. Ahead of the festivities, Kramer sat down with Deadline in Tokyo. “Our plan is to expand the number of festivals,” Kramer told Deadline when asked about the list of festivals that can serve as feeders for the International Oscar category. Currently, under the rules introduced in May, films that win the top award at Berlin, Busan, Cannes, Sundance, Toronto, and Venice can be automatically submitted for the international category alongside films chosen by a country’s official submission committee. Watch on Deadline Kramer continued: “We started with six festivals because we wanted to make sure there were juried awards, which not every festival has.” Kramer added that the new rule is part of the Academy’s plan to globalize its efforts and approach the international category in a “more holistic way.” “A few years ago, the first thing we did was create a rule allowing refugee filmmakers who are no longer in their home country to have their films submitted by a host-country committee,” Kramer said. “That was the first step in creating a broader aperture for who can participate in the category. The next step was to consider how we could select films beyond committee-selected submissions and ensure greater global representation.” Kramer said AMPAS remains in constant conversation with film festivals across the globe. “We want to make sure there is proper global representation in the number of festivals we’re working with for this category,” he said. “It’s all about inviting more films into the conversation.” On the topic of international, Kramer said 25% of the Academy’s membership now resides outside the United States—a natural reflection, he believes, of global shifts in film production and consumption. “I think the lines between U.S. and non-U.S. cinema, first-run and classic films, animation, and documentaries have become much less distinct,” he said. “A lot of this has to do with the pandemic, when people at home watched films they normally wouldn’t have watched—young people especially. It changed the nature of our industry.” Kramer said the Academy’s increasing global makeup is one of the main factors that makes YouTube the most appropriate broadcast home for the Oscars moving forward. It was announced in December 2025 that YouTube won the rights to host the Academy Awards starting in 2029. The Google-owned service outbid other offers, including one from the Oscars’ longtime home ABC, which has been hosting the event since 1976. Disney’s deal runs through 2028. YouTube’s first show will be the 101st Oscars ceremony, and its deal will run through 2033. “The beauty of the YouTube deal is that everyone will see the same show,” he said. “We’ll have control over fan engagement and reach 2.5 billion people around the world at the same time, on the same night, in more than 30 languages. It also gives us more quality control over what our fans see and experience. That’s really important.” YouTube’s deal for the Oscars has been one of the biggest shifts as streaming platforms take on more live events. Netflix has the SAG Awards, now renamed The Actor Awards, and Prime Video will broadcast the Emmys from 2027. But the alliance between big tech and the film world hasn’t been without substantial friction; take Amazon’s mishandling of Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial . When asked whether the Academy has planned for similar scenarios, Kramer concluded: “There’s no censorship allowed at the Academy, at the Oscars, or on our broadcast. We’ve been very clear about that, and Google and YouTube completely understand.” The Tokyo Film Festival runs until November 4. articles.title: Brett Morgen’s David Bowie Immersive Concert Experience Set For Berlinale World Premiere
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Vantage Media Takes North American Rights To Pole-Dancing Drama ‘Exotic’ As Trailer Unveiled Brett Morgen’s David Bowie Immersive Concert Experience Set For Berlinale World Premiere Horror ‘The Block’ With Jack Falahee, Saphira Moran & Jackie Earle Haley Wraps; Unveils First Look View All October 27, 2026 4:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source David Bowie “Stage” Blackout The spirit of late pop and rock icon David Bowie is set to return to Berlin , the city he called home in the mid-1970s. The Berlin Film Festival has announced it will world premiere U.S. documentarian Brett Morgen ’s immersive concert experience David Bowie “Stage ” during its 77th edition in the city’s 17,000-capacity Uber Arena venue. Combining previously unseen Bowie concert footage and an immersive sound and light experience, the production is billed as “a new way of experiencing one of the most influential artists of the 20th century”. Related Stories News Berlinale 2027 Retrospective To Explore Visions Of The Future In Nod To Centenary Of Fritz Lang's 'Metropolis' News Quiver Distribution Takes U.S. For Jérémy Comte's Ghana & Canada-Set Drama 'Paradise' The work is designed around recently discovered and restored footage from the 1978 Isolar II World Tour, during which Bowie performed material from his landmark album ‘Heroes.’ Watch on Deadline Morgen first discovered the original camera negatives while working on his Grammy Award-winning, Oscar-nominated bio-doc Moonage Daydream, charting Bowie’s life and career. World premiering in Cannes in 2022, it was the first film to be officially authorized by Bowie’s estate. The new three-screen immersive experience combines large-scale projections and transparent LED screens with an elaborate lighting design by lighting designer Patrick Woodroffe, whose credits include collaborations with The Rolling Stones and Elton John. The production is further enhanced by a specially created sound mix from Academy Award winner Paul Massey ( Bohemian Rhapsody , Michael, Moonage Daydream ), and places audiences at the centre of a live concert experience using state-of-the-art 7.1 surround technology and spatial audio design. The production is a collaboration between Rob Hallett’s Wonderworld, the David Bowie Estate and Morgen. “David Bowie has bestowed upon us an extraordinary treasure, an unprecedented concert experience that has yet to be witnessed,” said live entertainment veteran and former AEG International President Hallet. “Working hand-in-hand with David Bowie’s Estate and Brett Morgen, we are ensuring this experience is 100% faithful to his legacy while making his genius accessible to global fans and a new generation.” Berlinale Director Tricia Tuttle added: “To have this world premiere in Berlin, a city so closely connected to David Bowie, makes the experience especially meaningful,” added Tricia Tuttle, Director of the Berlinale. “The Berlinale is a place where cinema, art, and new forms of storytelling intersect. It’s like a dream come true: Bowie, Brett Morgen, a world-class sound and light team all coming together in the city’s premiere music arena.” Morgen, whose credits also include Kurt Cobain bio-doc Cobain: Montage of Heck and Jane about Jane Goodall, will also be a headline speaker in the talks program of the Berlinale’s European Film Market (EFM). The 77th Berlinale will run from February 10 to 21, 2027, with the David Bowie “Stage ” world premiering on February 14. HBO ‘s Harry Potter series has cast the roles of the titular wizard’s parents, James and Lily Potter, with Jasper Talbot and Hannah Chinn, respectively. Additionally, Harry Gilby joins as Charlie Weasley, the second eldest son of Molly and Arthur Weasley after Bill, whose siblings also include Percy, Fred, George, Ron, and Ginny. Related Stories News ‘Harry Potter’ Production Accounts Reveal Clue About Budget For HBO Series News ‘Harry Potter’ TV Series Due To Hit HBO Christmas 2026: Everything We Know About The Cast, Who’s Creating It, What J.K. Rowling Says & More Harry’s parents did not appear much in the hit films based on the J.K. Rowling book series, and it is unknown how big a role they will play in the new HBO series. According to the first novel, James and Lily Potter were killed by the most evil dark wizard, Voldemort. Lily sacrificed her life on that day to protect wee Harry, just a baby at the time of her death, with a love shield. When Voldemort unleashed an evil curse on the Potters, it bounced off Harry and hit He-Who-Shall-Not-Be-Named, leaving his physical form nonexistent and his powers pretty useless. Harry was left with a lightning bolt scar on his forehead, a painful memento that marks the horrible night he lost his parents. In the upcoming Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone , viewers will be introduced to Harry (Dominic McLaughlin), who has nothing special about him- or so his Aunt Petunia (Bel Powley) tells him. But when a mysterious letter of admission to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry arrives, it opens the door to a hidden world of magic, friendship and adventure. Yet behind Hogwarts’ enchanted walls lie dark secrets. Harry must find the courage to prove himself against the darkest wizard of all. Chinn is represented by 42. Gilby is represented by Independent Talent Group and Untitled Entertainment. articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Vantage Media Takes North American Rights To Pole-Dancing Drama ‘Exotic’ As Trailer Unveiled Brett Morgen’s David Bowie Immersive Concert Experience Set For Berlinale World Premiere Horror ‘The Block’ With Jack Falahee, Saphira Moran & Jackie Earle Haley Wraps; Unveils First Look View All October 27, 2026 5:40am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EXCLUSIVE: Vantage Media has acquired North American rights to Polish feature Exotic , about a woman’s journey toward self-discovery through pole dancing, ahead of its premiere at the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival . The picture follows a writer whose quest to master pole dancing evolves into something far more profound when the process and community of dancers she encounters help her figure out her true self. It is the first feature of Sonja Orlewicz-Zakrzewska and grew out of her personal fascination with pole dancing. The deal was negotiated by Jessica Russo, COO of Productions and Acquisitions at VMI Worldwide and Vantage Media, and Daniel Vadocky, Head of Sales at Berlin-based Pluto Film, which has also unveiled a first international trailer to coincide with the announcement. Gutek is handling the Polish release. Related Stories News Raven Banner Boards Polish Folklore Horror 'Òpi' Ahead Of U.S. Festival Debut News Poland Selects Paweł Pawlikowski's 'Fatherland' To Compete In International Film Oscar Race “At a time when women’s rights and freedoms are increasingly being challenged in America, Exotic delivers a timely and empowering message about the importance of embracing who we truly are,” said Russo at Vantage/VMI. Watch on Deadline “Through the art of dance, the film celebrates female strength, confidence and self-expression, reminding us that empowerment often begins with the courage to step outside our comfort zones. Exotic is more than a story about pole dancing; it’s a celebration of sisterhood, self-discovery, and the freedom to unapologetically be yourself.” “We are very pleased to have secured a North American distribution deal ahead of the film’s world premiere,” added Vadocky at Pluto Film. “It is a strong sign to its international appeal and audience potential. We have full confidence that Vantage/VMI will successfully distribute the film across all platforms.” Exotic was shot during a recent real-life edition of a pole-dancing Exo Stars Camp featuring real participants and instructors, maintaining the authenticity of this vivid bubble. “As soon as I discovered exotic pole dance, I got so invested that I went straight to Exo Stars Camp,” explains the writer-director. “I was fascinated by the clash of the fragile, intimate universes we carried within us around the camp. It soon became clear that the camp itself was a perfect place to confront fears, leave one’s comfort zone and express oneself more than daily life ever allows. “ The film stars Jaśmina Polak, Magdalena Koleśnik and Monika Frajczyk. Director of Photography is Adam Suzin, with Tomasz Kajetan Naruszewicz as Editor and Tymek Papior as Composer.to here. It received support from the Polish Film Institute’s microbudget scheme aimed at first-time directors. Director, scriptwriter, visual artist and photographer Orlewicz-Zakrzewska holds a master’s degree in photography from the Cinematography Department of the Łódź Film School. Her first short, Cross’n’Carry (2019), screened at festivals including New Horizons, HollyShorts and BEAST Portugal. She also took part in the script training lab Atelier Scenariuszowe and the EAVE Producers Workshop (2021). As a cinematographer, she worked on Enthusiasts , a documentary series for Canal+. Her video art and photography have been shown in numerous exhibitions including the Leica Gallery Warsaw. Exotic will debut in the First Feature Competition of Estonia’s Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival running from November 6 to 22. articles.title: ‘Derek Vs Derek’: British Rewilding Doc About Warring Neighbors Tests Its “Unexpected” Protagonists In All The Right Ways
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max BAFTA Names New Chair Stephen & Simon Cornwell Take On Chairmen Roles At ‘Night Manager’ Producer The Ink Factory As Michele Wolkoff Upped To President Disney+ & Channel 4 Strike Landmark Deal In UK View All October 27, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Derek vs Derek' Joss Barratt Welcome to Global Breakouts , Deadline’s strand in which, each fortnight, we shine a spotlight on the TV shows and films killing it in their local territories. The industry is as globalized as it’s ever been, but breakout hits are appearing in pockets of the world all the time and it can be hard to keep track… So, we’re going to do the hard work for you. We’re in the UK this week spotlighting an environmental documentary about warring neighbors that is gaining big traction. With a U.S. premiere coming shortly, Derek vs Derek has taken years to get to the big screen. Its exec producer Adam Wishart sets out its journey below. Related Stories News The "Algorithm Breaking" 'Hunkkaar' Has Challenged Indian Audiences On The Limits Of Procedural TV - And Their Own Beliefs News International Insider: The Final Edinburgh... Or Is It?; Int'l Oscar Race Begins Name: Derek vs Derek Country: UK Producer: The Slate Works & Damer Films Distributor: CAT&Docs For fans of: Wilding Watch on Deadline Many years in the making, Derek vs Derek started life as a story of rewilding and arrived in cinemas as something quite different, a “universal” tale of warring neighbors who nevertheless never stop learning from each other, says the film’s exec producer, Adam Wishart. The low-budget British documentary is riding on a high and is about to screen in the U.S. for the first time, but its journey to the big screen has been long and winding. The movie follows two neighboring farmers in Devon, enjoyably both called Derek, one of whom, Derek Gow, is a rewilding conservationist, and the other, Derek Banbury, an intensive dairy farmer. Both have a natural distrust of their namesake, but are just about willing to hear them out. Wishart, a BAFTA nominee for the BBC and Apple TV’s fantastic 9/11: Inside the President’s War Room, lives in Devon, a short journey from Gow’s farm. He became aware of Gow and his work some time ago when he was advising on community regeneration. Derek Gow Joss Barratt Wishart was told a director, James Dawson, had been following Gow for some years in order to make a rewilding documentary similar to 2023 hit Wilding . He “tried to get the film commissioned and even used every piece of TV industry capital I had,” but Wishart kept running into brick walls. He felt something was missing. “I was supportive [of Dawson’s vision], but a little sceptical,” says Wishart. “Then he told me that, whenever he stayed with Derek Gow, Derek would point him towards the Banburys and tell him to go and have breakfast with them. Suddenly, it became apparent that there was a lovely film about their relationship and their two different visions.” Wishart knew this was more than a kernel of an idea and Dawson already had plenty footage, but funding was tricky to come by. In the end, money flowed in via a grant from the Redford Center foundation plus crowdfunding. “We’ve made it with a tiny budget, drawing favors from across the industry, with the whole endeavour held together by sticky back plastic and paperclips,” says Wishart, whose production house The Slate Works produced Derek vs Derek alongside Damer Films, with CAT&Docs handling international sales. While “getting documentaries off the ground has always been difficult,” Wishart notes that “it’s harder than ever to do something that doesn’t have an obvious hook – an anniversary, a major event or a famous celebrity.” Testing the protagonist Derek Banbury Joss Barratt The doc sees the Dereks execute their opposing visions while going about their day-to-day lives. Gow is a rewilder who is taking drastic measures like introducing wild boars to his farmland, and he wants to go even further by convincing locals to allow wolves to return to the UK. Banbury is a traditional farmer who is really about making ends meet. Slowly, and at times with great drama, their outlooks move closer towards each other, and Derek vs Derek by no means takes sides. Wishart feels the key to the doc’s success is really in the protagonists’ relationship and their individual characters, which he describes as “brilliant and rather archetypal, but also unexpected.” “There aren’t many documentaries about people like them,” he adds. “We live in such a polarized world that we assume two people with opposing views are going to fall out over every aspect of their lives and never speak again. But it’s perfectly possible to disagree about one aspect of your life and still call your neighbor if your tractor gets stuck.” Speaking a few weeks after the launch of Tom Cruise-starring satirical polemic Digger, Wishart feels docs and features about this subject matter have become overly preachy. “They make one group of people feel that their life choices are wonderful, while alienating another group,” he adds. “I thought [ Derek vs Derek ] was interesting because making a film that sits with only one protagonist can be problematic. It can feel like an ‘NGO film’ or piece of advocacy without much edge. The protagonist isn’t really being tested.” Gow and Banbury are now pals, and Wishart speaks to them frequently, with the pair appearing on Q&A panels around the country to support the movie. Wishart says the movie has made around £120,000 ($160,000) so far. According to the BFI, ticket sales for Derek vs Derek rose 114% week-on-week after launch. The movie has aired at festivals including in Thessaloniki and Zurich and will soon be given its U.S. premiere at New York’s Doc NY. While Wishart is “not betting my mortgage on it,” he says “if the film can find a wider audience” by perhaps picking up U.S. distribution, thereby “beginning conversations about how we relate to the natural world and the food system, then more power to it.” That, he thinks, is the beauty of Derek vs Derek, a “universal” story of grumpy neighbors that could maybe, whisper it, teach audiences a thing or two without them even realizing it. articles.title: Matthew Perry Netflix Docuseries: Five Takeaways From Flimsy Look At ‘Friends’ Star’s Life & Death
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Jay Z & Apple Make It Official! Hova’s Headlining The Super Bowl Halftime Show Neil Young Rocks Trump With $10M Suit Over Using That ‘Free World’ Tune Again ‘Smear’ Campaign: George Clooney, Betty Gilpin, Adam Scott & Laverne Cox Team To Read Clark Gregg-Penned Political Play As Midterms Fundraiser View All October 27, 2026 6:48am Add us as a Google Preferred Source (L-R) Roger Castillo, Matthew Perry, & David Pressman in The One About Matthew Perry Netflix SPOILER ALERT: The following article contains details about Netflix ‘s The One About Matthew Perry docuseries. Let’s be honest, Netflix’s just debuted The One About Matthew Perry is mainly for the hardcore Friends fans. Having said that even the devotees of Rachel, Ross, Monica, Joey, Phoebe and Chandler might be disappointed as there’s not much in this Mary Robertson directed three-part docuseries you haven’t heard before. Related Stories News Remembering Matthew Perry: A TV & Film Career In Photos Legal Matthew Perry Death: “Ketamine Queen” Sentenced For ‘Friends’ Star’s 2023 Overdose Over the approximately three-hour running time, The One About draws on tales of drunken nights, funny faces, and the rise, demands, and bends of fame. There’s interviews with old friends, family members (especially Perry’s younger half-sister and licensed therapist Mia Perry Bowick), NBC Entertainment boss Warren Littlefield, The Whole Nine Yards director and one now ex-U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California. Still, in a rush to get not really anywhere at all, the result is pretty much the officially authorized surface level stuff we all used to get in the 1990s from Behind the Music . Unlike VH1’s sometimes under appreciated Behind the Music, The One About Matthew Perry ‘s three-act play of the rise, the fall, and the resurrection never really gains much momentum. The comeback of sorts the third act should promise leaves you feeling at best deceived. The primary fuel here is the people who love the long time addiction-addled Perry, who drowned at the age of 54 in his West L.A. hot tub on October 28, 2023 after taking a ton of ketamine, clearly loved him a lot, and miss him a lot. Yet, The One About ( Friends fans get the nod to the successful sitcom) mainly leans on Perry’s best-selling 2022 Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing memoir and its subsequent press tour for its narrative. A decision that, as we know now in hindsight of the book itself, reveals little of the darkness-plagued man behind the Friend, if you know what I mean? Watch on Deadline Still, for better and worse, here are some of the highlights of The One About Matthew Perry : (L-R) Lisa Kudrow , Matt Leblanc , Courteney Cox , David Schwimmer , Jennifer Aniston , Matthew Perry, THERE ARE NO FRIENDS: if you are expecting to hear from Jennifer Aniston, Courteney Cox, Matt LeBlanc, Lisa Kudrow or David Schwimmer in The One About Matthew Perry, you are going to be very upset. While the Friends cast are seen thoughout The One About in behind the scenes footage, clips from the 10-season show, and on press junkets, none of them acquiesced to be interviewed by Robertson. In fact no one from Friends , not the cast, not guest stars, not co-creators Marta Kauffman and David Crane appear in the docuseries. The closest The One About ever gets to the mega-sitcom is one Jeff Strauss, who was a writer/producer on Season 1 of Friends. While Strauss appears to have been close to Perry initially as Friends came together, most of his subsequent observations and remarks about the actor becoming “challenging and problematic” are clearly second-hand at best. MATTHEW PERRY REALLY WANTED TO BE FAMOUS & THEN REALLY HATED BEING FAMOUS: The son of a journeyman actor and an ex-press secretary to a Canadian PM, Perry was also the stepson of a famous Canadian journalist and later Dateline NBC correspondent. From early days as the class clown to hanging around sets with his father figures and trying to catch a break in early 1990s L.A., Perry, as various pre-fame pals attest in docuseries, wanted to be famous. When he got there with Friends , on a level barely anyone achieves nowadays, it was overwhelming. To be precise as one can on such occasions, it seems to, from the docuseries and Perry’s own memoir, brought out crippling insecurities, as much as wealth and notoriety. Problem with The One About , unlike Robertson’s much better last Netflix docuseries Quiet on Set: The Dark Side of Kids TV, is that it is mostly examined though the lens of the spiraling booze, drug and emotional problems with little sense of context — which feels as hollow as canned studio audience laughter. Also, with that Little Richard attributed quote of “if you don’t want your picture taken, don’t become famous” in mind, the openly ambitious Perry himself is rarely held responsible for his own behavior, actions and addiction. It seems from The One About Matthew Perry that Matthew Perry was a ultimately a perpetual victim who, to quote one of his buddies from the series, “didn’t stand much of a chance” — and that’s just hard to buy. THERE WAS MORE THAN JUST FRIENDS : The stardom and sprawling legacy of Friends, even though it ended nearly 20 years before Perry’s death, seems to have haunted him in both a Hollywood cliche way and a very real disorienting way until the day he died. Spending decades outrunning Chandler Bing, Perry may have never given himself the ability to let go and find success elsewhere, The One About suggests While praised for short and Emmy-nominated stints on The West Wing, Ally McBeal, and The Good Wife , Perry may have floundered on the big screen but his TV leading roles from 2006 – 2013 displayed untapped talents that never got the time or space to thrive. Looking back from the streaming and revival standpoint of 2026, Perry’s leading roles on Aaron Sorkin’s flawed but prophetic Studio 60 on the Sunset Strip , Mr. Sunshine (which Perry co-created) and Go On all deserve much more attention, Robertson postulates in the second episode of The One About . There’s not a lot to argue with the Emmy winner’s POV on that — if only Robertson had done those later shows and roles justice. Getty THE ONE ABOUT DOESN’T HAVE A LOT ABOUT PERRY’S DEATH: I was at court hearings and sentencing hearing on Perry’s death right up until this year. Before that, I was on the story of Perry’s death within an hour or so of his body being discovered in late October 2023 by authorities in his Pacific Palisades home. As more details came out, the sad truth of Perry’s relapses and drug hustle emerged. What also emerged was the fast one the actor played on those around him — pronouncing himself clean and sober when he kept going back to using made his death look inevitable. Like the cast of Friends, you won’t find a lot of that in The One About Mathew Perry – it doesn’t fit the narrative they’ve constructed, true or not. One can debate the truth and consequence of Perry’s life and death for ages, I grant you as someone who saw a lot of it unfold close up. Yet, playing primarily on the slop side of the Netflix street, the docuseries doesn’t give you much more time than to take a breath before the epilogue begins. The One About gives Perry’s death, the investigation and convictions of the scummy doctors, personal assistant and the infamous “Ketamine Queen ” just around 15 minutes at the end of the third and final episode. In a summary, bad people did some bad things. While that is partially true, you never learn anything more nuanced about it than that — which makes the almost three hours up to that point feel like a psych-out of the viewer and the subjects in the docuseries. THIS IS WHY PEOPLE SPEND LESS TIME ON NETFLIX: Love it, hate or just eat it, few nowadays are going to tell you fast food is nutritious. Besides a few funny clips from old Friends episodes and some of Perry’s later work, there is nothing good for you or really even memorable about The One About Matthew Perry once you’ve watched all the episodes. In many ways, the whole series is a juiced up version of Netflix’s recently introduced InstaDocs series and their insta-take on a large event like the OpenAI Hugging Face cyberattack. In another sense, The One About Matthew Perry seems to exist in no small measure to get the streamer’s algorithm to pump you over to more easily digestible programming that you’ll lose interest in fairly quickly. As a passionate fan of Is It Cake? , don’t expect me to regal you with highbrow or die recommendations. Good escapism is a treat to me, and a tasty one at that the better it is cooked. However, at the same time, if you want to know, Ted and Greg, why Netflix subscribers are spending less time on the service, it is air-filled content like The One About Matthew Perry . Content that is truly much ado about nothing. As Perry himself is heard saying in The One About: “Reality is an acquired taste.” AMPAS To Expand Festival Qualifier List For International Oscar SAG-AFTRA Faces Reckoning As Few Members Qualify For Streaming Bonus Clooney & Others Set For Read Of Political Play ‘Smear’ As Midterms Fundraiser Keanu Reeves Takes Over From Alan Ritchson As Lead In Netflix Actioner ‘Maelstrom’ Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Susan Saint James Dies: ‘McMillan & Wife’, ‘Kate & Allie’ Actor Was 80
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Billy Crystal’s ‘860’ Extends Broadway Run To February Sylvester Stallone On Casting Daughter In ‘Tulsa King’: “Of Course It’s Nepotism, You Idiot” Ric Flair Latest Health Update: Ex-Wrestler Wears Eye Patch In Message Reassuring Fans “I Am Focused On My Healing And Recovery” View All October 27, 2026 6:56am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Susan Saint James in 1974 Albert Watson / TV Guide / Everett Collection Susan Saint James , the husky-voiced actress who starred in such popular TV series as McMillan & Wife and Kate & Allie, died Monday, October 26, of pancreatic cancer. She was 80. A rep for Saint James confirmed her death to People. Among her survivors are husband Dick Ebersol, the former President of NBC Sports and executive producer of NBC’s Saturday Night Live. Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries Obituaries Walter Koenig Dies: ‘Star Trek’s Original Ensign Chekov Was 90 In a statement, Saint James’ family described her as “generous with her time and energy, which she valued more than money, and instinctively drawn to whoever needed lifting up. She taught her children to pause, be kind and look out for other people.” “She never met a stranger,” the family statement continues. “Every person she met became the most important person in the room at that moment, from a fellow board member to the clerk at the shoe store, who usually walked away knowing her entire life story. Her defining act: weeks after losing her youngest son, Teddy, in the November 28, 2004 plane crash, she delivered his eulogy as a note to each of her other children and her husband, giving them words to heal. Even in the deepest grief of her life, she put everyone else first. Days after the crash she sat with Tim Russert to thank the people who had reached out and to tell them the family was okay.” The statement concluded, “She brought that same fire and positivity to everything that followed, and never lost it. She is survived by her husband, Dick Ebersol, her four children–Sunshine Lucas, Harmony Lucas, Charlie Ebersol and Willie Ebersol–her seven grandchildren; her sister, Mary Mercedes Dewey, as well as her beloved service dog, Lola.” Born Susan Jane Miller on August 14, 1946, in Los Angeles, Saint James was raised in Rockford, Illinois, where she began modeling as a teen. She launched her acting career in a 1966 TV movie called Fame Is the Name of the Game, then booked guest roles in the series Ironside and, when the TV movie became a series titled The Name of the Game , Saint James landed a series regular role. In 1968, she had a co-starring role in Where Angels Go, Trouble Follows , the sequel to the popular comedy The Trouble with Angels. Susan Saint James, Rock Hudson, ‘McMillan & Wife’ (1973) Albert Mackenzie Watson/ TV Guide /ABC/Everett Collection Other TV episodic work from the era included roles in It Takes a Thief and Alias Smith and Jones, but her early signature role arrived in 1971 when she was cast opposite Rock Hudson in the light crime drama series McMillan & Wife , a highly popular program that had Saint James portraying the younger wife and partner in crime-solving. The show lasted for six seasons, with its finale on April 24, 1977, but Saint James had departed early over a contract dispute. Her character was killed off in a plane crash and the “& Wife” part of the title was erased. The show didn’t survive another season; by the end of her run, Saint James had received four Emmy nominations for her performance. Saint James remained a prolific actor following her departure from the successful series, co-starring with Peter Fonda in the film Outlaw Blues (1977), George Hamilton in Love At First Bite (1979), and Jessica Lange and Jane Curtin in How To Beat The High Cost of Living (1980). Jane Curtin, Susan Saint James, ‘Kate & Allie’ (1984) Mario Casilli/TV Guide/CBS/Everett Collection Saint James and Curtin would reunite four years later in what would become high career points for both stars: The CBS sitcom Kate & Allie premiered on March 19, 1984, with the two stars portraying divorced mothers (and childhood friends) with children who decide to share a home in New York’s Greenwich Village. Saint James portrayed Kate, the more free-spirited of the two, with Curtin as the higher-strung conservative Allie. The combination proved a winner (and would be echoed decades later in the Jane Fonda-Lily Tomlin comedy Grace and Frankie ), and the series, created by Sherry Coben, was a hit with critics and audiences, appreciated for its intelligent humor and warm, groundbreaking, chosen-family approach. Saint James was nominated for two Emmys for her performance as Kate, with Curtin nominated for three and winning two. Following Kate & Allie, Saint James largely retired from show business – she’d appear in guest roles periodically – devoting her time to raising a family that included two children from her second marriage, to make-up artist Thomas Lucas, and the three sons she had with third husband, the Saturday Night Live executive producer Dick Ebersol. (She and Ebersol met when she guest-hosted the NBC comedy in 1981). Tragedy struck on November 28, 2004, when a private plane carrying Ebersol and sons Charles and Teddy crashed at the Montrose Regional Airport in Colorado. Dick and Charles Ebersol survived, but 14-year-old Teddy was killed (along with a pilot and flight attendant). After her son’s death, Saint James often devoted her time working with parents who had lost children. Saint James is survived by Ebersol, four children, seven grandchildren, and sister Mary Mercedes Dewey. articles.title: Omar Sharif Jr. & Sam Asghari Among Cast For Rom-Com ‘Crazy Rich Arabs’; Filming Kicks Off November In LA
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Indio Downey Books First Lead Movie Role With Addiction Drama ‘Love In Vein’; ‘American Psycho’ Producer Aboard Abramorama Dances To North American Rights For ‘Make Work’ About New York City Ballet’s Choreographic Institute Duplass Brothers Make Show ‘The Long Long Night’ Free On Spotify View All October 27, 2026 7:47am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Omar Sharif Jr., Sam Asghari, Maya Tonnous, Sophia Konat Getty & courtesy EXCLUSIVE : Indie rom-com movie Crazy Rich Arabs (no relation to WB’s Crazy Rich Asians franchise) kicks off in LA next week with cast led by Omar Sharif Jr . ( The Secret Scripture ), Sam Asghari ( Hacks ), Aron Kader ( Ramy ), and Walid Chaya ( The Blacklist: Redemption ). The ensemble also features Kourosh Parsapour ( In the Garden of Tulips ), Lara J Barry ( Where Murder Lies ), Sarah Siadat ( Veep ), George Khouri ( Funny or Die ), and newcomers Sophia Konat and Maya Tannous. Directed by Peter Takla and co-written by Chaya and Jimmy Monack, with Chaya and Sharif Jr. serving as executive producers, the story “follows Youssef (Walid Chaya), a sheltered musician from Beirut who travels to Los Angeles for an arranged marriage with Reema (Sophia Konat), whose protective brother (George Khouri) isn’t easily impressed. His plans take an unexpected turn when he discovers Omar (also played by Chaya), his long-lost identical twin and a wealthy Hollywood divorce attorney. When the brothers switch identities, romance, family secrets, and cultural clashes spiral into chaos, drawing in Omar’s best friend Layla (Maya Tannous), a Beverly Hills lounge owner, and charming Airbnb host Shay (Omar Sharif Jr.).” Related Stories News Evan Mirzai Preps Adaptation Of Sheeva Moshiri's Rom-Com 'The Cupid Index' With Shiva Negar, Alexander Uloom & Sam Asghari Casting 'Grand Death Lotto': Paul Feig's Amazon Action Comedy Adds Eight Original music and soundtrack will come from Rawan Chaya. Chaya’s Moonlit Wings Productions produces. Watch on Deadline According to Chaya, the production aims to challenge “Hollywood’s longstanding underrepresentation of Middle Eastern and North African (MENA) characters, particularly in leading roles”: “By placing Arab-American characters at the center of a glamorous, heartfelt comedy, the film offers a perspective rarely seen in mainstream romantic storytelling.” He continued: “Growing up, I rarely saw people who looked like me represented on screen, especially in stories that celebrated our culture rather than reinforced stereotypes. With Crazy Rich Arabs , we’re changing that—bringing Arab characters to the forefront through humor, heart, and a universal story about love, family, and what it really means to live a rich life.” AMPAS To Expand Festival Qualifier List For International Oscar SAG-AFTRA Faces Reckoning As Few Members Qualify For Streaming Bonus Clooney & Others Set For Read Of Political Play ‘Smear’ As Midterms Fundraiser Keanu Reeves Takes Over From Alan Ritchson As Lead In Netflix Actioner ‘Maelstrom’ Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Sosie Bacon Set As Co-Lead Alongside Nikolaj Coster-Waldau In MGM+ Series ‘The Black Tapes’
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘The Five Star Weekend’ Creator Bekah Brunstetter Inks Overall Deal With Universal Global Television Georgia Juvelis Leaving As Chief Communications Officer Of AMC Global Media After 19 Years With Company MGM+ Greenlights ‘The Black Tapes’ Horror Series Starring Nikolaj Coster-Waldau Based On Podcast View All October 27, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Sosie Bacon Martin Rusch Sosie Bacon ( Smile, Scarpetta ) has been tapped as the female lead opposite Nikolaj Coster-Waldau in The Black Tapes , MGM+ ‘s supernatural investigation drama series based on the 2015 horror podcast of the same name. In The Black Tapes , Dr. Richard Strand (Coster-Waldau), a brilliant psychiatrist with a mysterious past, teams with the obsessed, methodical physicist Alex Regan (Bacon) to debunk paranormal cases of hauntings, possessions, disappearances, and sinister legends – the infamous black tapes. articles.title: Jack Cressall Writing ‘Camp Justice’ Pilot Based On John Ryan Book ‘America’s Trial: Torture And The 9/11 Case’
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Ted Sarandos Shrugs Off U.S. Troubles To Mark Netflix’s 10 Years In Korea ‘Wentworth: Halfway Home’: Grace Chow & Nadine Garner Among 9 Joining Cast; Watch Trailer International Insider: Turmoil At Netflix; MIA Market Report; Patrick Brammall Interview View All October 27, 2026 8:07am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Naomi Harvey, Jack Cressall and John Ryan; 'America's Trial' (inset) Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: The TV adaptation of John Ryan ‘s non-fiction book America’s Trial: Torture and the 9/11 Case now has a writer. British screenwriter Jack Cressall is writing a pilot for Camp Justice , which will be based on Ryan’s non-fiction book from last year. Naomi Harvey from Golden Possum Productions has developed the book for TV and is attached to produce, with a U.S. co-producer being sought. It was previously with Clockwork Films, as we reported last year when Ryan’s book published. The series will explore the ongoing legal proceedings against the alleged architects of the 9/11 attacks at Guantánamo Bay, and per the synopsis will delve into “the complex legal and political landscape surrounding one of the most consequential cases in modern American history.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Daveigh Chase's Former Manager Vehemently Disputes GoFundMe Claims: "There Are No Medical Bills To Be Paid Or Funeral Expenses" Casting Sosie Bacon Set As Co-Lead Alongside Nikolaj Coster-Waldau In MGM+ Series 'The Black Tapes' Veteran legal affairs journalist Ryan wrote his book after spending a decade reporting from Guantánamo Bay in Cuba, exploring the post-9/11 interrogation program, the consequences of which are still playing out in court more than two decades after the events. The series will look into “justice and accountability and what happens when a nation’s pursuit of both becomes entangled with its own actions.” Ryan said: “Having Guantánamo Bay as my second home for a decade has been the reporting experience of a lifetime. The setting is surreal and the events are the literal definition of stranger than fiction. That’s why I got hooked, despite the costs to my personal life. I’m excited that more people will have a window into what goes on behind closed doors and can experience this bizarre place through Jack’s writing.” Scott Z. Burns’ film The Report , starring Adam Driver, covered similar ground, but was focused on the machinery of the interrogation program. Cressall’s debut short film, My Type , starred Sadie Stanley and Jacob Ward, with Daniel Ruah directing. It premiered at the Santa Barbara International Film Festival this year. He is developing a slate of feature films, including Destemido , a biographical drama about Brazilian big-wave surfer Marcelo Luna, and Dream Car Wash , a coming-of-age drama. For British producer Harvey and her Golden Possum operation, Camp Justice is the latest following an option for the life rights of Cuban baseball player Julio Estrada and development of a series based on John Romero, the godfather of first-person shooter whose titles including Doom , Wolfenstein 3D and Quake . “John’s book offers a rare window into life at Camp Justice,” said Harvey. “In a world where almost everything is captured on camera and shared instantly, one of the most consequential murder trials in modern history is unfolding largely out of public view. “John takes us inside a bizarre, almost surreal ecosystem where grieving families, defence lawyers, prosecutors and accused terrorists coexist on a tropical island where the makeshift court and camp x-ray co-exist with a crazy golf course, tiki bar and gitmo gift shop.” Cressall is managed by Eric Ziech at Untamed Artists LA. articles.title: Anthropic Warns in IPO Filing That Unfavorable Media Coverage of AI Could “Adversely Affect” Its Business
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 26, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Dario Amodei Photo by Alex Wong/Getty Images Anthropic, one of the two biggest artificial intelligence labs (alongside OpenAI) filed to go public Monday morning, and alongside platitudes about the wondrous potential of the technology (curing disease that has vexed humanity for centuries!) and the terrifying downside possibilities (“catastrophic or existential risks to humanity”), it warned of the looming threat of the media to its ongoing business. The company, founded by Dario Amodei, is one of the leading frontier labs developing AI tech, but as the company noted in its S-1 filing with the SEC Monday, the public perception of it may pose a serious threat to its ability to continue operating. The filing also noted the risks posed by copyright law, as well as the company’s priorities, including a section that calls out a divergence from OpenAI that may be relevant to Hollywood. But it is the threats of negative media coverage that comes up again and again in the filing, with the risk factors section spelling it out most clearly: “As our business has grown and as interest in us and the AI industry overall has increased, we have attracted, and may continue to attract, significant media coverage, public commentary, and scrutiny from time to time. This coverage and commentary have included, and we expect will continue to include, recurring narratives concerning the potential adverse societal impacts of AI, including that AI may displace or eliminate jobs, may be misused or otherwise cause harm, and may pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity,” the filing states. “Negative media coverage, including public figures making negative or threatening statements about our company, whether accurate or not, could also adversely affect our brand and reputation and may reduce market acceptance of our models, platform, and applications or impair our ability to attract and retain customers,” it adds. “As public awareness of our brand increases, any issues that draw media attention may have an amplified adverse effect on our reputation. If unfavorable media coverage or adverse public perceptions persist or intensify, the demand for our models, platform, and applications could decline and our brand, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.” As for Hollywood, the litigation threat around copyrighted works remains top of mind for the company, which listed all of the lawsuits and threat letters related to books, films, music and other copyright holders, with the company noting that it may require them to acquire a license to the material, which they may or may not be able to secure. The legal landscape around AI and IP remains deeply uncertain. “In each of the actions, we believe we have meritorious defenses and dispute any allegation of wrongdoing,” the company wrote. “Legal proceedings related to these matters can have an adverse effect on us because of defense and settlement costs individually and in the aggregate, diversion of management resources, and other factors.” And then there’s the video element. There are a swarm of startups looking to use the technology to transform entertainment, but Anthropic, unlike SpaceX and OpenAI, has never spent resources on video or image models. The company notes as much in its filing: “Every research project must ultimately advance our mission. This focus also guides what we choose not to pursue,” it says. “For example, we do not currently focus on developing video and image generation models, despite their commercial appeal. That compute instead goes to coding, agentic skills, and safety research—a research decision that has also aided the capital efficiency of our models.” Also unlike OpenAI or SpaceX, Anthropic does not have an advertising business, and while it does spend some on ads (like at the Super Bowl) it is hardly a major player. The company disclosed $147 million in advertising spend in 2025, with marketing and advertising expenses rising by $273 million in the first half of this year “reflecting higher media spend to support product launches.” THR

articles.title: Chris Brown Avoids Prison With Eight-Month Suspended Sentence for London Nightclub Attack
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 26, 2026 7:11am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Chris Brown arrives at London court on July 24, 2026. Courtesy of Getty Grammy-winning musician Chris Brown has avoided prison and received an eight-month suspended sentence in a London court after pleading guilty to affray following a confrontation at a London nightclub in 2023, the BBC News website reported on Monday. The incident took place in a nightclub in Mayfair, an upscale area of the British capital. Brown faced sentencing in the Southwark Crown Court along with a co-defendant, his vocal coach Omololu Akinlolu, who also performs under the name of Hoody Baby. Judge Tony Baumgartner told Brown and Akinlolu that their prison sentence was suspended for 12 months, which means they will be imprisoned if they commit another crime in the next year but otherwise stay free in the community. Related Stories Movies 'Ali G: Who Iz I?' Review: Sacha Baron Cohen Reprises Iconic Role, Yielding Equal Parts Belly Laughs and Boredom Movies Sacha Baron Cohen and 300 Ali G Look-Alikes Descend on London Ahead of New Movie 'Who Iz I?' “These sentences are the shortest custodial sentences which in my judgment are commensurate with the seriousness of your respective offenses … Each sentence is one of 12 months or less — by law I am required to suspend each custodial sentence unless you are an excluded offender or I am satisfied that exceptional circumstances relating to the offense or the offender justify an immediate custodial sentence,” Judge Baumgartner said during his sentencing. Brown and Akinlolu initially were set to face a trial over assault and grievous bodily harm charges, but the charges were later dropped. Brown also faced a charge of having an offensive weapon — a tequila bottle, according to reports — though that was dropped, too. He was told by the court judge the famous musician was not entitled to any special treatment, but Brown’s charitable activities and being a father of four were taken into consideration. Judge Baumgartner added Brown’s earlier convictions involving violence were “relevant,” but were now historic. The Grammy-winning artist has spent time in prison before — in Los Angeles — for a probation violation. It came after he pleaded guilty to felony assault of his then-girlfriend, Rihanna . THR

articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Tim Chan Plus Icon Tim Chan @mrtimchan Follow Sign Up View All October 26, 2026 7:51am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Amazon If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission. Fans of the hit animated children’s series Bluey now have a whole new way to experience the show with The Bluey Album Box Set , which brings the music of the show to vinyl for the very first time. The Amazon-exclusive set includes all four of the Bluey soundtrack albums: The Album, Dance Mode!, Rug Island and Up Here . Written and arranged by lead composer Joff Bush, the songs include the Bluey theme song, along with memorable tunes like “Keepy Uppy,” “Sleepytime” and “Cat Squad.” Amazon AMAZON EXCLUSIVE Bluey Album Box Set $109.99 Buy Now On Amazon The box set includes four LPs pressed on colored vinyl, with accompanying full color album sleeves and a pull-out panoramic poster. Everything is stored inside a slipcover box. There are more than 60 songs in total collected in this set. The Album is pressed on a white and blue vinyl disc inspired by the show logo, while Dance Mode! is pressed on pink and orange vinyl, inspired by Bluey’s favorite toy, Chattermax. Rug Island — named after a season two episode where the characters use their imagination to create an island from a rug, throw cushions and colored pens — comes on a green and orange LP. Up Here is pressed on a “blue space”-inspired vinyl. Related Stories BOOK ADVENT CALENDAR Bluey Advent Calendars Are Here for the Holidays, Swapping Bonbons for Books TV 'Stranger Things' and 'The Pitt' Were the Most Streamed Original Series in the First Half of 2026 This is an Amazon-exclusive release, meaning the retailer is the only place to find this Bluey music set online. You can also shop official Bluey merch on Amazon here . All of Bluey’s soundtrack albums have hit the Billboard Kids Album Chart, along with the Billboard Soundtrack Chart. The first release, The Album , debuted at number one on the ARIA Albums Chart in Australia in February 2021, becoming the first children’s album to reach the top of the charts Down Under. The music box set is a great gift idea for Bluey fans and vinyl collectors alike, and comes on the heels of a host of Bluey holiday releases, including an official advent calendar . articles.title: Instagram Tests 90-Minute Horizontal Videos In Major Play for Podcasters and Creators
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Caitlin Huston Plus Icon Caitlin Huston Business Writer hustonca Follow Sign Up View All October 26, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Instagram's new test of Features, which will play long-form videos on their TV app and phone. Meta Instagram is testing features aimed at capturing a bigger part of the entertainment landscape, including the ability to play long-form videos like podcasts and more on the platform. Starting Monday, Instagram will be launching a test of horizontal videos of up to 90 minutes with select creators in the U.S. The product, called Features, is aimed at podcasters, comedians and other long-form creators, with the ability to refer viewers to the full video from the short-form reels on the platform, which are typically around three minutes or less. “What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” said Tessa Lyons, vice president of product at Instagram. Instagram has already been testing the feature with creators in Brazil and has a plan of expanding to tens of thousands of creators in the U.S. The videos will also be recommended to users on Instagram’s Explore page and in other areas. Early creators involved in the test include podcast host and Skims co-founder Emma Grede, beauty and fashion creator Monet McMichael, Preston Rakovsky, who interviews New Yorkers about love and relationships and football content creator Donald De La Haye. This comes as Netflix, Disney and more have been adding podcasts and videos from creators to their platforms, in an effort to capture more consumer viewing hours, and compete with entertainment behemoth YouTube. One challenge for Instagram and others, in the battle against YouTube, has been competing against the platform’s lucrative revenue sharing deals, with YouTube offering qualified creators offered 55 percent of ad revenue and helping generate brand deals. Lyons said Instagram is currently working on “a few different deals” with the early creators for Features, but there’s currently no exclusivity around putting the videos on Instagram (unlike Netflix’s deals for podcasts). Additionally, existing ad deals will carry over into the videos, but Instagram will also work with creators without existing placements to find deals. “For established creators who already have those relationships, they can bring that content with those placements and that branded content. And we also think that there’s a big opportunity for us to help creators who don’t yet have that infrastructure and that business behind them,” Lyons said. Features will be available on mobile, but the goal is to carry the viewing experience over to Instagram for TV, which launched last year with Samsung, Fire TV, Google TV and is now expanding to Apple TV in the U.S. as part of Instagram’s move for more of the entertainment landscape. “We think the best viewing experience for long-form horizontal content is on a big horizontal screen, and so I think that that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said. Additionally, given the rise of microdramas, as well as a desire among creators for episodic videos, Instagram has been experimenting with Series, which provides a home for episodic Reels on a creator’s profile. In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to experiment with the feature, and has since been reaching out to individual creators, who have been experimenting with their own episodic content. In the coming months, Instagram plans to begin testing the feature in more countries and bring it to the U.S. by the end of year or early next year. The company has also begun testing how it will appear on the TV. These join other new features Instagram has been testing out, including integrating live video into the Reels tab and showing live videos to audience who don’t follow the users. This is launching in Indonesia and Brazil with plans to expand it to the U.S. next year. THR

articles.title: Ava DuVernay Defends Using AI in New Doc ’14th’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All October 26, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ava DuVernay attends the premiere of '14th' during AFI Fest at TCL Chinese Theatre on Oct. 25. Kevin Winter/Getty Images As Ava DuVernay continues to hit the festival circuit for her new documentary 14th , the director is opening up about her decision to use AI on elements of the film. The doc is a deep dive on the Constitution’s 14th Amendment and the fight over birthright citizenship, featuring archival photographs that are brought to life with the help of AI. This has sparked some criticism online, which DuVernay addressed to The Hollywood Reporter as the doc screened at AFI Fest on Sunday. “The tools that the artists used to do the parallax and the animation in the films have that technology in it, as does Pro Tools with sound, as does Avid with editorial, as does Resolve with color,” she said of industry post-production tools. “I think we’ve come to a place in filmmaking where we have to be really sober about the ways in which that technology is [used] across so much of the workflow.” Related Stories Business Anthropic Warns in IPO Filing That Unfavorable Media Coverage of AI Could "Adversely Affect" Its Business Music Anthropic Sued for Using Elvis Presley Music to Train AI Models She continued of the AI, “We didn’t use it to fabricate a person or make an avatar of a person or approximate someone’s voice that said something they didn’t say. We actually animated some photos that are in the public domain, and from what we’ve been hearing from people it does bring people closer to that time in history, which was our goal. So people have to see it and check it out for themselves and make their decisions about how they feel.” 14th comes a decade after DuVernay’s Oscar-nominated doc 13th , exploring the U.S. prison system and racial inequality in the light of the 13th Amendment. However, she doesn’t see the new film as a direct follow-up, and started considering a return to the Constitution after “hearing the current president talking about his desire to dismantle birthright citizenship while he was a candidate; he said he would do it in his first week in office. He actually did it in his first day in office, he attacked birthright citizenship.” “I don’t know much about the 14th Amendment at that point but I know birthright citizenship is in it. So we start thinking about the possibility of making this film at that point,” the filmmaker said, and “once we saw all of the tentacles of the current administration attacking this amendment, we knew that there was more there. So we investigated it and that’s what the film became.” 14th will get a limited theatrical run starting Nov. 27, and start streaming on Netflix on Dec. 4. THR

articles.title: Sofia Franklyn on the Phone Calls That Ended Her Relationship With Alex Cooper
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Hunter Moreno After months of negotiating with Barstool and Dave Portnoy over the IP for Call Her Daddy , it’s impossible for things not to be tense and charged between me and Alex, and our resentment toward each other for being stuck in this standstill becomes more and more blatant. I feel so worn down. We’re killing ourselves and our friendship by endlessly trying to prove ourselves on diametrically opposed points. I feel severed from the person I’m fighting both against and for. It’s too backward. And mics have been down for weeks. We need to come back alive. Related Stories Business Ethan Klein Says He's Working to "Urgently Remove My Ownership, Financial Stakes" From H3 Podcast After Wife Hila Klein Reveals His Affair Lifestyle 'Clueless' Inspired Kim Kardashian to Buy This Priceless Monet I ask Alex to FaceTime me and remind myself to be nice. I tell her we can stay: “I can’t do this anymore. I just don’t want to roll over on all the points.” She sounds relieved. “No, one hundred percent, totally, yeah. We’re going to make sure we get everything we need.” I get the call from my and Alex’s lawyer Bruce. “Alex is requesting separate representation,” Bruce says. “OK. … Like, you have to represent us as individuals and not as Call Her Daddy ?” “Well, I can still represent you if you want.” “Wait, I’m sorry, I’m so confused. Why would you all of a sudden not represent me? We’ve been doing this for months.” “So, when there’s joint representation and one person decides to seek separate counsel, sometimes people feel it’s … I don’t know, uncomfortable or unfair to use a person they once shared,” Bruce says. “So Alex got her own attorney — she’s not working with us or you anymore?” “That’s correct, but it’s up to you if you want to continue.” I can’t see straight. I feel a pit of fear opening inside me and try to think it away. Maybe separate counsel is smart. We let our lawyers handle it. They can have the tough conversations on our behalf. That’s actually better. We focus on the show, the partnership; we don’t have to live in the intensity anymore. Bruce’s calling again. “Hello?” “Hi, Sofia, one more thing and then I’ll send over that form for you to sign. I reviewed Alex’s contract. Remember you guys told me you had the same agreement, so I was just working off yours, but what was the basis for her higher compensation?” I feel like I’ve been told someone died. “As in, she’s making more money than me?” “Yeah, is that not something you’d talked about?” “No.” “Understood.” I’m silent. “Do you not think that’s weird she lied to you about it?” I press. “Well, it’s something to keep in mind …” Bruce trails off. His unwavering neutrality is off-putting now. His lack of bravado also. But I am putting it in a box for later. I’ll think about it then. I don’t know what else to do. Franklyn (left) and Alex Cooper in 2018. Says Franklyn in the book: “I live in her apartment. Our apartment. I take the train to work with her, then I sit next to her at work, and then I take the train home with her. Together. And then we go to Bubby’s and order pancakes.” Screenshot/YouTube All rationality is gone. The bitch. I feel pure hatred. I might combust. Who is this person? Alex, who is she? Am I stupid? Gullible? Dumb? Naive? Living something that wasn’t true? That’s not true? Was she ever my friend? She was! I saw it. I felt it. I live in her apartment. Our apartment. I take the train to work with her, and then I sit next to her at work, and then I take the train home with her. Together. And then we go to Bubby’s and order pancakes if we feel like it. I’ve seen her cry. She’s seen me. Really seen me. How long has she been carrying this secret? Am I so bad she was scared to tell me? And still is? But this secret is so …small. Who cares? She knows I wouldn’t, if she’d just told me. What was so bad about it that she’d lie to our attorney? Send him into meetings like the village idiot? I think about every contract conversation we’ve ever had. Jokes. How we share every single fucking thing with each other — space, time, emotions, work, pain, highs, shame, heartbreak, family. Alex wouldn’t do this. Lie about something so stupid. To me. When did she start making more money? Why wouldn’t she just tell me about it? Not just as a friend, but while we’re sitting in meetings and calls for six months fighting for fair pay. As CO-OWNERS. Why is she doing this? What is the truth? Muji, Alex’s best friend from high school, the Milfhunter. He’s the only person who can answer my questions, if he’ll even answer my call. We’re on bad terms right now. But are we , really? Alex is the one who fired him. Regardless, if I were him, I wouldn’t want to talk to me either. But who can I talk to? Alex is out of reach now, she’s literally not responding to me, but even if she was, can I trust her at all? Who is this person? I’m confused and angry and disturbed. What is real? Our walks to get pizza, adding red pepper flakes, her skinny wrists bobbing up and down; her legs sprawled out on our new couch, seeing her head cock back in the light of her computer, cackling for hours; doing every single load of laundry together in the 301 basement, half fucking around, half genuinely scared we were going to be murdered; dancing in the living room to Demi Lovato and Kelly Clarkson and Carrie Underwood and Hannah Montana. Was it all fake? Or is dumbass Bruce fake? I’m dropped into a panic attack, all my memories flashing violently in front of me, only to suddenly vanish while I sink into a sea of dread. I try not to drown by repeating things that still feel true, like that calling Muji would be a betrayal to Alex. Our trust is broken, but there must be a reason she lied. There will be an explanation, and I don’t want to commit treason in the process of finding it out. But I can’t live with this mindfuck for another minute without answers. Cooper in 2018. Screenshot/YouTube Muji sends me to voicemail twice, and then picks up. “Whaddup?” Why does he insist on always acting so unbothered? What is this tactic? “Oh, I don’t know, Muji, you used to work at the Barstool office, right? I’m sure you’ve heard a thing or two about what’s been going down.” “No, I haven’t.” Fucker. “I have no one else to talk to about this.” “About what?” “About what? You know exactly what. About ALEX.” “Sorry, but I can’t help you.” “Seriously, Muji?” “I mean, I feel bad, but at the end of the day, I really can’t.” “Did you know about her raise? Like 20K more than me?” I blurt out. Last-ditch effort. “Look, I really wish I could help you …” Click. Barstool Sports, founded by Dave Portnoy (center, in 2023), produced dozens of podcasts — hosted almost entirely by men — but Call Her Daddy was one of the company’s most popular and most lucrative when it ran from 2018 to 2021. Michael Hickey/Getty Images I inhale so hard from my Juul that the pod leaks onto my tongue. Buzz. Buzz. It’s Muji. Back for more. “What’s up?” He sounds chipper now. He might actually be insane. “Cooper doesn’t have friends. I’ve watched it happen since high school, you know what I mean?” I need him to stay on track. “Did you know she was making more money than me?” “I knew the whole time.” “Why wouldn’t she tell me? I wouldn’t even be mad if she had a bonus or something. I’ve said that to her face!!” “She didn’t tell you because she didn’t want you to know she tried to get you fired.” We stay on the phone for another hour, maybe more. I have no sense of reality, much less of the time. Muji tells me Alex has even reached out to him recently, asking him to come on as a producer. Hire him back?? Has she been anticipating a switch-up? He tells me this shit started years ago. I feel like I need to purge the last two years of my life. I want to wash myself from the inside out. All of my memories are violated. Do I need to get my sight checked? What did I miss? It’s not just the last few months. There were secrets even at the peak of our friendship. I thought Muji would give me an answer to today, to our battle with Dave and where to go next. But I know now it goes even further back. Is this who she is? I think about all the times I thought we were sisters, all the moments when it felt like the energy of the world could be generated from us ping-ponging off each other alone. Where did that girl go? Who am I without her? Muji ends the call by repeating that he saw it all coming and hangs up. I’m in shock. No moves left, besides throwing my phone at the wall as hard as I can.
