articles.title: Robert Pattinson Calls Steven Soderbergh’s ‘The Batman Part II’ Work “Completely Selfless”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By James Hibberd Plus Icon James Hibberd Writer-at-Large JamesHibberd Follow Sign Up View All October 26, 2026 8:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Robert Pattinson as Batman in 'The Batman.' Jonathan Olley/Warner Bros./Courtesy Everett Collection Logo text Robert Pattinson is sounding off about Steven Soderbergh stepping up to help finish filming The Batman Part II . Earlier this month, Soderbergh agreed to take the on-set directing reins for the DC Studios production in London after Matt Reeves had to step aside due to a personal family matter back in Los Angeles. Reeves remains involved in the production. “I am so happy he’s come on to help Matt,” Pattinson told Games Radar during a recent interview while promoting the actor’s film Primetime . “It’s incredibly generous of him – and he’s doing it in the loveliest way. It’s completely selfless.” Related Stories Movies Lance Oppenheim Bribed Robert Pattinson With 200 Zyn Canisters to Star in 'Primetime' Movies 'The Batman Part II': Steven Soderbergh to Work with Matt Reeves to Complete Filming Continued Pattinson: “I think Matt had put so much work into the script, and we’re almost done. So for someone to come in and say, ‘I just want to help Matt do it; I want to do it in conjunction with him and just get it to the edit.’ And to have someone who’s as talented as Steven doing it is great.” Pattinson added the film is now back in production. As previously reported, the plan is for Soderbergh to work in London, while Reeves operates out of Los Angeles. Reeves will also be hands-on during the movie’s post-production in L.A. The film is said to be about two-thirds done. “I thought Matt Reeves’ work on The Batman was stunning; it was intentional, specific, and rigorously coherent,” Soderbergh said in a statement. “The goal here is to work with Matt and his team to generate footage that will integrate seamlessly with what’s already been shot so Matt can properly finish his film.” Added Reeves on social media: “Just to be clear, I am not leaving The Batman Part II . I am profoundly grateful to Steven for coming to my aid during this challenging time to help me finish principal photography. Thank you to all for your concern and well wishes.” Pattinson is having a rather incredible year, having appeared in three successful films — The Drama , The Odyssey and Primetime , with Dune: Part Three still to come in December. Pattinson stars in The Batman Part II as Bruce Wayne/Batman, with new additions to the franchise including Scarlett Johansson and Sebastian Stan. THR

articles.title: Hulu’s Rumored Clavicular Doc Is Actually a True Crime Series (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Tony Maglio Plus Icon Tony Maglio View All October 26, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source A still from 'Get Huge,' a Hulu documentary on Looksmaxxing Hulu/Disney Logo text Look(smaxx) here: We finally have actual information on that rumored Clavicular Hulu documentary. The Hollywood Reporter can first reveal that all that beef between the 20-year-old looksmaxxer, whose real name is Braden Peters, and Disney has resulted in a three-part true crime documentary series titled Get Huge: Looksmaxxing to Death . The Hulu doc is not and was never a documentary about Peters, rather it was about the dangerous and competitive worlds of looksmaxxing and social media; Peters just happens to be the most famous individual on that scene and his likeness is only used briefly. Specifically, the docuseries is about a mysterious death in Thailand (that has nothing whatsoever to do with Clavicular). But since it’s been a while, the backstory: Peters served Disney/Hulu a cease and desist letter after he says he caught documentarians Jennings Brown and James Kristofik filming him backstage at the Elena Velez fashion show in February New York City without permission. Peters did not like that, but the encounter would be far from his biggest legal case this year. Just last week, Peters pleaded not guilty to raping an underage girl after she was given alcohol while appearing on his livestream in 2025. In September, Peters was charged with two felony counts, one for rape and another for drugging a person for sexual intercourse. He also faces a misdemeanor count for providing alcohol to someone younger than 21. Peters has denied the allegations, saying that the encounter was consensual. He has posted a video to his social media accounts showing screenshots of a text conversation and a photo of a handwritten letter, which were intercut over footage of Peters, shirtless and fixing his hair at an urban inner harbor. Beneath the posts, he’s written, “Theres better ways to make money then suing someone because they don’t want you,” and “Yeah still texting me to this day… totally not just trying to be greedy and get a check.” Braden “Clavicular” Peters walks the runway during New York Fashion Week earlier this year. Victor VIRGILE/Gamma-Rapho/Getty Images Get Huge: Looksmaxxing to Death presents what producers call “an unflinching portrait of masculinity in the influencer age, where extreme biohacking, online performance and a series of suspicious deaths converge.” The series debuts Nov. 10 on Hulu (and Hulu on Disney+ for bundle subscribers) in the U.S. It will stream on Disney+ internationally. “Deep in the manosphere, an underground movement promises to unlock human potential — bulging muscles, bigger penises, eternal youth. At its center is Dr. Tony Huge, a guru pushing homemade biohacks on a devoted following willing to risk everything for the cause,” the logline reads. “When Leo & Longevity, a penis-enlargement expert and one of Tony’s closest allies, is found dead in Thailand, alpha-male influencers become online sleuths, running wild with theories and questioning Tony Huge and his right-hand man, Connor Murphy. Soon, a darker pattern emerges: Leo isn’t the first of the inner circle to die under mysterious circumstances. Will he be the last?” Get Huge: Looksmaxxing to Death is directed by Stacey Lee, and produced by Boardwalk Pictures ( Welcome to Wrexham , aka Charlie Sheen ) and Hyperobject Industries ( Don’t Look Up , Stormbound ). Executive producers include Adam McKay and Todd Schulman for Hyperobject Industries, Andrew Fried, Lana Barkin, Jordan Wynn and Dane Lillegard for Boardwalk Pictures, William Crouse and Stacey Lee for Lovely Days, Jennings Brown for Nocturne Media, and Brett Neichin. THR

articles.title: Zooey Deschanel on Holiday Plans, ‘New Girl’ Cast Hangs and Bath & Body Works Campaign
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All October 26, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Zooey Deschanel for Bath & Body Works' new holiday 2026 campaign. Courtesy of Bath & Body Works If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission. The holidays arrived early for Zooey Deschanel — and she’s loving every second. “I like to get into the Christmas or holiday season as soon as possible,” the veteran star explained to The Hollywood Reporter while seated inside a palatial mansion that had been turned into a veritable winter wonderland courtesy of Bath & Body Works on Oct. 21. The popular retailer recruited Deschanel to front its new Season of Wonder campaign that debuted today , so they hosted her along with press, VIPs and influencers at a Beverly Hills home that had been decorated with its fragrant offerings, Christmas trees, snow globes and plenty of pastel accoutrements to match the new collection. Related Stories TV Jake Johnson Teases New Project With 'New Girl' Co-Star Damon Wayans Jr. TV 'New Girl' Stars Reunite -- in a Slightly Different Way Than Max Greenfield Claimed The actress, fresh from wrapping the She & Him Tour with her bandmates and reuniting with her New Girl family at a fundraiser in L.A., opened up to THR about her favorite holiday traditions, the changing landscape of Hollywood for actors and performers and what she’s really itching to do on the work front. Why did you say yes to this partnership with Bath & Body Works? I feel very nostalgic about Bath & Body Works. It’s something I’ve loved since high school, and still love. It’s one of those things that just feels like a classic. I was also excited because I love the holidays, and Bath & Body Works has all these beautiful seasonal scents . It’s fun to experience the holidays fully every day, and having a different scent for every day makes that easy. What does it mean to experience the holidays fully? I want to feel like, “I did it. I did Christmas.” I want to be tired of Christmas by the time it ends — or after New Year’s — and think, “OK, I can be without this amazing, wonderful thing for 10 months now.” I love that you can live out the holidays fully through all the scents. If you’re not baking Christmas cookies or singing Christmas carols every day, you can experience the holidays in whatever way works for you. Everyone is different. Some people want to wear perfume every day, while others just want a subtle body wash. Some people like to light a candle; I love the home fragrance. I also love it for gifting because I enjoy giving gifts and picking out something special for my friends. Candles are a great gift because everyone is on a diet or not drinking now. People are trying to be so good. A candle is something you can enjoy even if you’re on a diet or not drinking alcohol. It’s almost the new etiquette of gift-giving in Hollywood. It’s gluten-free. ( Laughs .) Deschanel as “Holiday Wonder Maker” for Bath & Body Works’ new holiday 2026 campaign. Season of Wonder products are available now online and at Bath & Body Works stores with select products also available in Ulta stores, ulta.com and on Amazon . Courtesy of Bath & Body Works Do you have a favorite scent? What I love is that there are so many different ones to choose from, and you can express a different part of your personality every day. My favorite is Moonlit Goddess . I make them give me more of it because I love it so much. They make all of these scents in different forms, so you can enjoy them in pretty much any way you like. It’s a seasonal scent, but it feels very year-round to me. It smells like pears and lavender. [She uncovers a candle and offers it up to smell.] That’s good. It’s so smooth. It’s smooth. Are you someone who starts decorating for the holidays the day after Thanksgiving? The day after Halloween — if I can. It depends, but I like to get into the Christmas or holiday season as soon as possible. What are some other Zooey Deschanel holiday traditions you look forward to each year? I love making a huge batch of sugar cookies and letting my kids decorate them. Everything gets everywhere, but it’s so fun. They’re so proud of the cookies, and we put them out on Christmas and say, “We made these.” I love singing Christmas carols. I grew up in choirs, so singing Christmas carols feels very nostalgic for me. I love singing harmonies and singing with other people. I also love picking out gifts for people, thinking about their personalities and trying to give them something they’ll love. I love spending time with family, decorating for Christmas and coming up with themes. It’s all so fun. The holiday campaign marks the brand’s largest media buy to date with ads set to be splashed across YouTube, connected TV, social media, in-store and out-of-home placements in major markets like New York, Los Angeles and Dallas. Courtesy of Bath & Body Works Speaking of harmonies, congratulations on just finishing your She & Him Tour. How was it? It was so fun. We had a song go viral this year. It was something I wrote 25 years ago that was on our first record, and it ended up charting. It was nice to get to play it for a new group of people who maybe didn’t know our music before. There were lots and lots of young people. It was so much fun, and playing music is always such a joy for me. It was very exciting to get to do that. Did the tour feel different this time around? It was actually smaller than what we’ve done in the past. We used to tour with a lot more people, but this time we toured with fewer musicians. It was really fun to rearrange everything. We were doing mostly the material I wrote for our Volume One, Volume Two and Volume 3 records. That was really fun because we had been doing a lot of holiday tours. We have a couple of holiday records that we’re very proud of, and our last tour was, I think, a holiday tour. It was great to get back out there and play the songs from those records, then reimagine them with a smaller group. Everything sounded great. It was so much fun. View this post on Instagram You’ve also been busy with acting. Congratulations on the film Trash Mountain with Caleb Hearon, which premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival. Has it found a home yet? I think they’re very close to figuring that out, but I don’t have a final update. I’ll let you know once I know. We don’t want to get you in trouble. I don’t want to get in trouble. But I love that movie, and I’m so proud of it. We were all there because we loved the story, loved the script and loved Caleb. It’s a movie I’m immensely proud of, so I’m excited that people are seeing it and responding to it. Even if you hadn’t reunited with your New Girl friends recently, I feel like I’m still contractually obligated to ask you about New Girl. It’s in your contract. ( Laughs .) The New Girl reunion at the Chrysalis fundraiser went viral because seeing the cast back together warms so many hearts. Since you’re all still close and everyone likes each other, are we any closer to an official screen reunion of some sort? I don’t know because there’s a lot of legal stuff involved. There are many different entities and people involved. I wish I were the authority on that, but I’m very much not. I’m really close with everybody, though. That event was incredible, and hats off to Max [Greenfield] for getting everyone together. He worked so hard to make sure everyone could be there. It was an incredible event for Chrysalis, which is such a great organization. They do such great work, and we were thrilled to help them raise money for a great cause. New Girl fam back together: Jake Johnson, Deschanel, Hannah Simone, Lamorne Morris, Max Greenfield and Damon Wayans Jr. at the Chrysalis Butterfly Ball in Los Angeles on Oct. 10, 2026. Monica Schipper/Getty Images Did you get to hang out or grab a drink afterward? I had to split the night between the event and my sister’s birthday, but I do see everybody fairly often. Since that event, I’ve seen both Lamorne and Hannah — literally last week. I see them all on a regular basis. Looking ahead to 2027, what are you still itching to do? Would you go back to series-regular work? I would, if it were the right project. But I love doing little indie films. I’d love to do more things like Trash Mountain . It was such a great experience, and I love the pace of making independent films. That’s how I started out. Coming from network TV, I like that fast-paced work. It’s very exhilarating. I’d love to do more indie films and stretch my creativity in different ways. When you’re talking with your actor friends, what are the conversations like? The business is in such a strange place, and a lot of people are scared. You have to think creatively and try to work in different ways than you have in the past because the business has changed so much. To me, the one constant in entertainment is that it’s always changing. I feel lucky that I do music as well. When one thing isn’t happening, I’m able to do the other. That’s great for me. But I know there’s been a lot of frustration over the last few years, especially among actor friends, because the nature of being an actor is that you’re often waiting for jobs. Any way you can stretch your creative muscles — whether that’s taking an acting class, getting together with friends, making a film yourself or thinking outside the box — is really helpful. We all do this because we love it at heart. I didn’t get into being an actor for the money. I got into it because I love it. And for some free Bath & Body Works products. Free Bath & Body Works is another plus. Are you a New Year’s resolutions person? Have you identified anything you want to focus on? I’m always making resolutions every day of my life. I’m always thinking, “I’ve got to do more of this.” So I’m not really a New Year’s person, but it is a nice way to reset. I think it’s good to have a north star or something you’re aiming toward. It’s about honing in on what’s important to you and recognizing that you’re happiest when you’re moving toward the things that make you happy. The new year can be a time to think about what makes you happy and how to aim toward those things. See below for more products from the Season of Wonder holiday collection . Candles and a teddy bear holder from Bath & Body Works’ new Season of Wonder holiday collection. “For me, holiday wonder is in the little things you look forward to every year: the scents, the lights and the feeling of finding a gift that is exactly right for someone,” said Deschanel. “The holidays have always been so special to me, and Bath & Body Works is a brand many people associate with the season. I love the quality and care that go into the products, and Season of Wonder is about celebrating all those little things that make the holidays feel special.” Courtesy of Bath & Body Works Vanilla Cocoa Flurries body wash Courtesy of Bath & Body Works Pure Wonder concentrated room spray Courtesy of Bath & Body Works Candles and a teddy bear holder from Bath & Body Works’ new Season of Wonder holiday collection. articles.title: ‘Good Girls’ Director on Life in Girls’ Correctional Center in Poland: ‘It Damages You Even More’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Oct 26, 2026 8:15am PT ‘Good Girls’ Director on Life in Girls’ Correctional Center in Poland: ‘It Damages You Even More’ (EXCLUSIVE) The film debuts a clip ahead of premiere at Ji.hlava Intl. Documentary Film Festival. By Marta Balaga Plus Icon Marta Balaga Latest ‘Good Girls’ Director on Life in Girls’ Correctional Center in Poland: ‘It Damages You Even More’ (EXCLUSIVE) 30 minutes ago ORF-Enterprise Boards ‘Crème de la Crème’ – About a Sperm Bank Business – Produced by Whatever Pictures and a ‘Playful and Irreverent’ Series 2 weeks ago Skoop Media Launches New Crime Label Dutch Noir: ‘Range, Scale and Attitude’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 weeks ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Ji.hlava Intl. Documentary Film Festival Director Ania Winiarska almost gave up on “Good Girls.” “After six months, I felt like I’d hit a wall. I’ve never had this problem before,” she told Variety . “It was always very natural for me to gain people’s trust, but my previous films were about boys or men. This one was about teenage girls and even though I’m a woman, I didn’t realize how much shame they carry. I wasn’t prepared for meeting them.” Related Stories Jessica Biel to Play Hugh Hefner's Wife in 'Playmates' Movie for Searchlight 'Matchbox' Stars Jessica Biel and John Cena Lead New American Red Cross Pledge Drive (EXCLUSIVE) In her doc, premiering at Ji.hlava Intl. Documentary Film Festival, Winiarska enters a Polish correctional center for girls. Some are escaping abuse. Others end up there for skipping school, drinking or dating. Inside, they’re faced with discipline and constant surveillance. Popular on Variety “I was just another adult in a very strict institution where they had to obey all the rules and regulations. I think they viewed me as an outsider, but also as someone who was part of the system,” she recalled. “It took me two years before I could start filming. But once they accepted me, we never had any issues. They would tell all the new girls: ‘She’s good. She’s not a snitch.’” International rights to “Good Girls” are being sold by Stranger Film Sales. Produced by Story, Film i Väst and Tekele Productions, it premieres an exclusive clip here: Winiarska, who is Polish, currently lives in Sweden. She was shocked to discover a world that hadn’t changed for decades. “Most of these people mean well. They try to help the girls, but it’s complicated because this system is so outdated. Rather than trying to catch up with the 21st century, the girls are taught how to cook and sew. Religious classes are no longer compulsory, but they were when I was filming.” Societies may be changing, but the ideas of what constitutes a “good girl” and a “bad girl” are still prevalent. “In some countries, and that includes Poland, good girls are quiet and obedient. Certain prejudices are very much alive,” she noted. “We don’t talk to our children about growing up, puberty or sex education. I was lucky to have parents who cared about me. When I got into trouble, they helped me. If I hadn’t had that, I would probably be one of them.” Most of her young protagonists don’t even fit the center’s profile. “Most of these girls shouldn’t even be there. This place is meant for the resocialization of people who have committed crimes or are on the edge of doing so. But when you look closer, you see they got there because they were skipping school, got pregnant or used drugs or alcohol.” Or simply because they suffer from mental health issues their families cannot or do not want to handle. “One of the girls suffered from depression that wasn’t properly diagnosed. She was lying in bed for three weeks and her mom, who has similar issues, couldn’t help her. Neither did her school. Instead, the police came and handcuffed her in her pyjamas,” said Winiarska. “That’s the problem: they don’t recognize their actual needs. I got quite close to the people who work there, and they also admitted they are not trained as psychologists. When you’re not well mentally and you’re are locked up and punished for it, it damages you even more.” She met girls aged between 10 and 18. “My daughter is 10. It’s scary to think about,” she said. But sometimes the center can provide some safety. “Many of them come from neglectful backgrounds and have experienced all sorts of abuse. At least over there they have regular meals, they go to school, and if they feel bad, there’s someone to talk to. They didn’t have that at home.” There’s another issue, though. Their time at the center restricts their freedom in the present, yet fails to prepare them for the future. “I only started realizing what’s important in life when I was in my 30s. They leave at 18 with a small amount of money. What are they going to do with it? Some party it away or get pregnant over summer breaks. It’s a vicious circle.” Winiarska adds: “These girls are strong. They’re funny. But at that age, you don’t understand the world and the world doesn’t understand you. If, on top of that, you come from a disadvantaged family, it’s easy to sink into a big black hole.” “If this film could change something in our society, it would be so wonderful.” Robert Pattinson Praises Steven Soderbergh for Stepping in to Finish ‘Batman 2′ Filming After Matt Reeves’ Exit: ‘Completely Selfless’ Robert Pattinson Says ‘Batman 2’ Filming Will ‘Pause for a Little Bit’ After Director Matt Reeves Steps Away: ‘We’re Going to Figure It All Out’ ‘The Batman 2’ Pauses Production as Director Matt Reeves Steps Away for a ‘Family Matter’ Robert Pattinson Was Bribed to Star in ‘Primetime’ With 200 Zyn Canisters and a Note That Read: ‘Dear Chris Han-Zyn’ Steven Soderbergh to Help Finish ‘The Batman 2’ Filming After Matt Reeves Stepped Away for Family Matter Sebastian Stan on Why ‘Fjord’ Is Being Called a ‘MAGA Movie’ and How Making ‘The Batman 2’ Feels Like ‘F—ing Godfather Part 2’ Loading comments...

articles.title: Anthropic Hopes Potential Investors Do Not Fret About AI’s ‘Catastrophic’ Risks in Its IPO Filing
articles.full_text: Oct 26, 2026 8:19am PT Anthropic Hopes Potential Investors Do Not Fret About AI’s ‘Catastrophic’ Risks in Its IPO Filing By Corbin Bolies Plus Icon Corbin Bolies Latest Anthropic Hopes Potential Investors Do Not Fret About AI’s ‘Catastrophic’ Risks in Its IPO Filing 31 minutes ago Elvis Presley’s Music Owners Sue Anthropic for Copyright Infringement, Demand Nearly $50 Million in Damages 1 hour ago IATSE Names Video Engineer Jillian Arnold First Labor and Technology Officer 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images for HubSpot Anthropic spent much of its filing with the SEC ahead of its initial public offering warning potential investors about the risks its AI models could pose to humanity, acknowledging it could not entirely ensure its own safety measures would be successful against the “existential” danger AI could pose. The disclosures came as part of more than 90 pages of risk factors in Anthropic’s S-1 filing with the SEC, made public Monday as the company prepares to go public. The 90-page length of such risk factors, the disclosure of which is customary, is unusual, spurred by the potential dangers AI models have posed following disclosures from AI companies over agents acting autonomously, unaligned with human instructions, and the potential misuse of the technology by human actors themselves. Snap’s risk factors totaled roughly 30 pages, while Elon Musk’s SpaceX — currently the largest IPO of all time at an initial $1.77 trillion valuation — totaled 38. “Concerns have been raised both within our organization and by other researchers, regulators, policymakers, and industry participants that sufficiently advanced AI systems could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponized, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy,” the company wrote, following warnings from a group of current and former Anthropic researchers this summer that the technology posed such risks. Popular on Variety To counter it, Anthropic laid out its sweeping safety-minded policies in its SEC prospectus, a priority for CEO Dario Amodei . Amodei, who founded Anthropic in 2021 with a group of former OpenAI colleagues following their defection from the Sam Altman-founded rival, has advocated for AI companies to band together and slow the development of AI models to ensure sufficient safety protocols. But the company admitted that its own work contributed to such destructive potential: “Our development of highly advanced models, platforms, and applications and expansion of use cases could further increase the risk that our models cause harm.” The company disclosed four separate instances in which its AI models accessed third-party systems without instructions to do so, including one in which an agent changed system settings and read a person’s personal information. The agents all acted independently, without collaborating with other agents, but the company warned that the continued deployment of AI agents risked contributing to more collective — and unauthorized — actions. The company’s risk factors also included factors such as financial commitments, including its billions of dollars worth of compute payments to SpaceX and Microsoft, and technology constraints. Specifically, it warned of Taiwan’s lead in semiconductor manufacturing — and the hostility between Taiwan and China — and the political opposition to data centers as risks to how it performs as a business. But these earthly economic and political factors may not matter much if Anthropic, and the broader AI industry, cannot prevent the models they’re working on from causing cataclysmic doom. “Our safety-focused approach is designed in part to mitigate such risks, but there can be no assurance that our efforts will be successful or that the broader AI industry will adopt similar safeguards,” the company wrote. In the S-1 filing, as is customary, Anthropic did not disclose the number of shares it plans to sell or at what price. Those details will be determined in the coming weeks. The company’s shares will trade under the ticker symbol “ANT” on the Nasdaq exchange. articles.title: How ‘You Can See Everything’ Became a Surprise Box Office Hit (and Likely One of the Biggest Docs of All Time)
articles.full_text: Oct 26, 2026 8:19am PT How ‘You Can See Everything’ Became a Surprise Box Office Hit (and Likely One of the Biggest Docs of All Time) By Rebecca Rubin Plus Icon Rebecca Rubin Senior Film and Media Reporter rebeccaarubin Latest How ‘You Can See Everything’ Became a Surprise Box Office Hit (and Likely One of the Biggest Docs of All Time) 31 minutes ago Box Office: ‘You Can See Everything’ Scores $19.5 Million in Huge Second Weekend, ‘Clayface’ Leads With $24 Million Debut 1 day ago Tom Hanks Returning to Broadway After 14 Years for New Play ‘This World of Tomorrow’ 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy Everett Collection “ You Can See Everything ” has remained a must-see at the box office, collecting a remarkable $19.5 million from 2,655 theaters in its second weekend — a notable increase in ticket sales from its sizable opening . A24 ‘s buzzy documentary about Theranos fraudster Elizabeth Holmes has grossed $45.1 million domestically to date and will be wildly profitable for the studio against a lean $7 million budget. With electric word-of-mouth, awards chatter and repeat viewings from audiences who are trying to make sense of what they saw on screen, the movie should remain a big-screen draw through the fall. It’s primed to leave theaters as one of the biggest non-musical documentaries of all time, a true feat for a nearly three-hour film that wasn’t publicized until a month before debuting in cinemas. Right now, “Michael Jackson’s This Is It” is the highest-grossing documentary ever with $267 million in 2009, not adjusted for inflation. Meanwhile Michael Moore’s “Fahrenheit 9/11” is the biggest non-music doc with $222 million in 2004, followed by two nature films, “March of the Penguins” with $127 million in 2005 and “Earth” with $107 million in 2007. “You Can See Everything” needs to become a hit overseas to crack the top five. Popular on Variety After a strong second weekend in North America, here are four takeaways from the surprise success of “You Can See Everything.” Restraint bolstered demand A24 began rolling out “You Can See Everything” in 855 theaters, a huge footprint for a documentary. (By comparison, Bleecker Street launched “Musk,” a four-hour look at the world’s richest man, in four locations.) The film opened to $15.6 million — thanks to the more than 2,000 sold-out showings — as cinephiles rushed to theaters to avoid spoilers; the stranger-than-fiction story follows Holmes right before she begins her 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors. The decision to launch the movie in moderate release — rather than limited in just a handful of venues or nationwide on more than 2,000 screens — proved wise because the studio was able to bolster awareness while cultivating a sense of scarcity. (In New York City and Los Angeles, good luck catching the film during its first weekend in theaters if you didn’t buy a seat way in advance.) Then ticket sales climbed by 28% as “You Can See Everything” expanded to 2,666 theaters in its second weekend, underscoring the film’s genuine commercial viability beyond the coasts. “Opening ‘You Can See Everything’ in 855 theaters was a really smart move, allowing the film to establish itself and build momentum before going much wider,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian. “The fact that we’re seeing a documentary deliver such a significant second-weekend increase is remarkable.” Secrecy around the project dialed up the anticipation Nobody knew about the existence of “You Can See Everything” until its surprise world premiere at the Telluride Film Festival in early September. (That’s nothing short of a miracle in Hollywood, where even your waiter knows your P&A spend.) In the scenic Colorado mountain town, the movie became a word-of-mouth sensation after garnering near-euphoric reviews. Shrouding the film in secrecy became an effective marketing tactic. After all, there’s no shortage of movies and television shows about Holmes. Her rise and spectacular fall from grace has been depicted in the Hulu series “The Dropout,” starring Amanda Seyfried, as well as Gibney’s “The Inventor: Out for Blood in Silicon Valley.” But the immediate sense around “You Can See Everything” was that co-directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim had captured something very, very different. (And many felt that Holmes had met her match in Fielder, a cringe comedy master best known for HBO’s “The Rehearsal.”) “Bear in mind, the project started with no blueprint or screenplay for how to tell this story,” says analyst David A. Gross, who publishes the box office

articles.title: ‘The Mandalorian and Grogu’ Gets Behind-the-Scenes Book Featuring Original Sketches, Concept Art and Cast Interviews
articles.full_text: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission. “Star Wars” fans are getting a closer look at how Din Djarin and Grogu made the jump from Disney+ to the big screen. “The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu,” a new 256-page hardcover from Abrams Books, arrives Nov. 3, offering an inside look at the creative process behind Lucasfilm’s latest theatrical release. Written by longtime Lucasfilm collaborator Phil Szostak, the book features previously unseen concept art, early sketches and interviews with the cast. Related Stories Todd Haynes, Zhang Ziyi and Daniel Brühl Lead a Star-Studded Lumière Fest Opening With Haynes Teasing ‘De Noche,’ Starring Pedro Pascal PRE-ORDER NOW In particular, the book explores the visual development of the film’s characters, locations and vehicles. Production design has been a major part of the series since its 2019 debut, combining the Western-inspired aesthetic of the original “Star Wars” films with new environments created using Industrial Light & Magic’s StageCraft technology, which uses LED screens to generate digital backdrops. The book also includes a foreword by Doug Chiang, Lucasfilm’s senior vice president and executive design director, who has worked on the franchise since the prequel trilogy and helped establish the show’s visual style. See two spreads from the book, shared exclusively with Variety , below. Released in May, “ The Mandalorian and Grogu ” marked the franchise’s first theatrical outing since 2019’s “Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker,” bringing one of Disney+’s biggest original properties to cinemas after three seasons on streaming. Created by Jon Favreau, “The Mandalorian” follows the adventures of Pedro Pascal’s helmeted bounty hunter Din Djarin and his Force-sensitive young companion in the years following the fall of the Galactic Empire. Its success spawned a growing collection of interconnected “Star Wars” television projects, including “The Book of Boba Fett” and “Ahsoka,” while helping Disney expand the franchise beyond its traditional theatrical releases. Favreau returned to direct “The Mandalorian and Grogu,” which follows the pair as they take on a new mission for the fledgling New Republic amid lingering threats from Imperial warlords. Pascal reprised his role alongside newcomers Sigourney Weaver and “The Bear” star Jeremy Allen White, who voices Rotta the Hutt, the son of Jabba the Hutt. The upcoming art book continues Abrams’ long-running series of behind-the-scenes “Star Wars” publications, which have become a staple of the franchise’s publishing business. Szostak, who has worked with Lucasfilm’s art departments since 2008, previously authored companion books for the first two seasons of “The Mandalorian,” as well as “The Rise of Skywalker” and “Andor.” Loading comments...

Events unfold over one evening as a hurricane rolls in, blocking communication from the outside world and preventing reinforcements from arriving. Together, the duo has to fight the onslaught of men working for the arms deal while dealing with the natural disaster outside their window. Page Six Hollywood first reported on Reeves’ casting, though it’s unclear why Ritchson is departing the movie. Popular on Variety Screenwriter Mark Bianculli (“How to Rob a Bank”) is polishing the script from a first draft by late writer Gregory Fitzpatrick. Netflix is reviving the film, which was originally sold as a spec script to Warner Bros. in 1993 by producer Jeff Robinov when he was an agent. At the time, Variety reported that “Maelstrom” was “widely described as ‘Diehard’ in a hurricane” and went for roughly $225,000 to $ 625,000. (Now that’s closer to $500,000 to $1.4 million, adjusted for inflation over 33 years.) This is the first project under Robinov’s new Netflix deal. The former Warner Bros. Pictures president has shepherded billion-dollar franchises like “The Dark Knight” trilogy and “The Hangover.” Reeves has cemented his status as an action star through franchises like “The Matrix” and “John Wick.” Last year, he made his Broadway debut in “Waiting for Gadot” alongside his “Bill & Ted” co-star Alex Winter. articles.title: The Production Studio, Reimagined
articles.full_text: Oct 26, 2026 9:00am PT Partner Content The Production Studio, Reimagined Traditional production isn’t dead. It’s consolidating around markets that adapt fastest to a net-sum demand through state incentives By Partner Content Plus Icon Partner Content Latest Biggest Names in Media, Entertainment and Sports Will Connect, Collaborate and Make Deals at Jupiter Festival Miami 4 weeks ago How Utopai Studios Is Defining Production Intelligence for Film and Television 4 weeks ago Power at Any Age: Gloria Reuben Urges Menopausal Women to Advocate for Their Health 1 month ago See All The film and television production industry has spent the past several years navigating real headwinds. Productions have followed cost savings overseas, technological innovation has evolved from a talking point to a daily reality on set and in the writers’ room and a widening field of state and international incentive packages has pushed some markets into what looks more like a race to the bottom than a rebound. For studios still operating on the old build-it-and-lease-it model, that shift has been hard to ignore. Related Stories Todd Haynes, Zhang Ziyi and Daniel Brühl Lead a Star-Studded Lumière Fest Opening With Haynes Teasing ‘De Noche,’ Starring Pedro Pascal Soundstages aren’t going anywhere. What’s changing is who succeeds with keeping them full, and it’s the operators nimble enough to keep pace with that mantra who inevitably pivot to new ideas. Demand for physical production remains strong in certain key regions of the U.S., but the assumption that four walls and a lease are enough on their own no longer holds. The campuses built to flex with the changes are the ones pulling ahead. Popular on Variety “I still believe in physical production. I believe there will remain a need for boxes that cater to those types of productions,” said Shawn Papazian, president and CEO of The Fields Studios in Chicago. “At the same time, it’s essential to shift flexible design details into a basis and not just building to a pro forma that you think you can financially achieve. Doing something that can work as a campus environment and can host a variety of different creative endeavors is essential.” Papazian frames that shift in practical terms: a facility that can pivot on short notice with soundstages that host a scripted drama one season and an immersive event the next. “This can be everybody’s sandbox,” said RoseMary Prodonovich, general manager of The Fields Studios. “We want to be the epicenter of creative culture in Chicago.” The Balloon Museum, a large-scale art experience from Lux Entertainment, is currently occupying five stages at The Fields Studios. “Managing a production like ours — complex, large-scale and technically demanding with thousands of audiences weekly — requires a strong, reliable partner capable of working in true synergy. With The Fields Studios, we found exactly that,” the company said, pointing to the campus’ “operational flexibility, highly professional team and outstanding stage quality along with their city and state relationships” as central to the partnership. The Fields Studios, a 23-acre mixed-use creative campus on Chicago’s Northwest Side, houses nine soundstages, over 200,000 square feet of production office and support space, on-lot parking, a 1.5-acre backlot, on-site grocery store, retail space and 123 high-end residential lofts, all within the same complex. Built on the site of a century-old manufacturing complex originally constructed in 1928 for Olson Rugs and later home to Marshall Field & Co., it was reimagined, in the words of Papazian, “for producers, by producers.” The connective tissue isn’t just geography; it’s intention. The campus is built to be fluid with a production’s needs — whether film, TV, commercial or immersive activation — rather than forcing every project into the same box. “Producers aren’t just looking for space. They are also looking for comfort,” Papazian said. “They’re looking for a partner who understands the realities of a shooting schedule, a shifting budget and a crew that needs to feel at home.” “Making a show like ‘Dark Matter’ is a huge undertaking and it makes all the difference to have people around you who understand what you’re trying to do,” said Matt Tolmach, executive producer of “Dark Matter” which filmed Season 2 at The Fields Studios last year. “The Fields team gave us a place where our cast and crew could feel at home and focus on making the show. As our needs changed, they were right there with us. They were true partners every step of the way.” Produced by Sony Pictures Television for Apple TV, “Dark Matter” Season 2 is now streaming. That word “home” comes up often at The Fields Studios, and it isn’t incidental. Papazian’s father, Robert A. Papazian, instilled in him a guiding principle when they opened their first studio together more than 30 years ago: productions work long hours, so the space should be cozy and easy to work in. Papazian hand-selected his team from both production and real estate backgrounds, giving the campus an unusual dual fluency. The team understands both what a line producer and their crew need on day one of principal photography and what a real estate owner needs to keep a mixed-use campus financially stable. That legacy extends beyond the property line, too. The Fields Studios team sees the campus’ success as inseparable from the health of Chicago’s broader creative community. They are active with educational institutions and creative organizations across the city, helping to nurture and grow Chicago’s production talent pipeline and foster connections on its world-class campus. That welcoming, production-minded culture, combined with turnkey studio infrastructure and a steadily growing pool of local talent, already makes Chicago an easy choice for productions. Illinois also recently extended and enhanced its production tax credit through 2039, adding higher base incentive rates, expanding eligible expenses and announcing a first-in-the-nation sustainability uplift capable of pushing total savings over 40%. For studios and streamers who have been chasing tax credits and pushing projects away from Los Angeles to Georgia, New York and New Jersey, Illinois is now a top consideration in acquiring that business too. Then there’s the city itself. Chicago’s appeal isn’t confined to what happens inside The Fields Studios’ stages. As Papazian describes the surrounding neighborhoods: “it’s not a backlot, it’s the real thing,” reflecting the city’s genuine architectural range, production history stretching back decades and landscapes that can double for nearly anywhere in the country without a single set built. For productions, that means campus efficiency paired with location diversity, all a short flight from both coasts. “We built this to be a home base, not just a set,” Papazian said. articles.title: ‘Madison’ Horror Game to Get Movie Adaptation From Story Kitchen
articles.full_text: Oct 26, 2026 9:00am PT ‘Madison’ Horror Game to Get Movie Adaptation From Story Kitchen By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest H3 Podcast Crew Cuts Ties With Ethan Klein After Hila Klein Says He Has Been Having an Affair 3 days ago Judge Orders Donald Trump to Testify Under Oath in $10 Billion BBC Defamation Case 4 days ago Trump Says Google CEO Rejected His Request to Rename Atlantic Ocean on Google Maps 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Bloodius Games Pulse-pounding psychological horror game “ Madison ” is going to splash some blood on the silver screen. L.A.-based Story Kitchen , a production company specializing in game-to-movie adaptations, has inked a pact with “Madison” developer Bloodious Games to develop a feature film set in the world of the first-person horror title. Currently, there’s no casting info for the “Madison” movie or other details on the production including expected release date, director or screenwriter. The project does not yet have a distribution partner but Story Kitchen is targeting it for a theatrical release. Related Stories Todd Haynes, Zhang Ziyi and Daniel Brühl Lead a Star-Studded Lumière Fest Opening With Haynes Teasing ‘De Noche,’ Starring Pedro Pascal In the “Madison” game, you play as Luca Maxwell, who has received an instant camera as a 16th birthday present. Unfortunately for Luca, the camera is inhabited by a demon that forces him to continue a murderous ritual started decades ago by a satanist serial killer (the titular Madison). Players must solve puzzles using the camera to try to break the cycle of madness. Popular on Variety Story Kitchen, co-founded by “Sonic the Hedgehog” movie franchise producer Dmitiri Johnson, is spearheading several other game adaptations. Those include the “Tomb Raider: The Legend of Lara Croft” animated series for Netflix, “Life Is Strange” (Prime Video) and “Streets of Rage” (Lionsgate) . First launched in 2022, “Madison” has received multiple awards and recognitions, including best narrative – grand winner at the NYX Game Awards and best game at EVA 2022. Bloodius also has released an immersive VR version of the game. The partnership with Story Kitchen comes as Bloodious continues to expand the “Madison” universe. The Maxwells’ Curse, a new story expansion, is set to arrive in 2027, free for all “Madison” owners. In addition, a free Halloween update to the game introduces two difficulty modes: an expanded Normal Mode, designed to make the experience more accessible to newcomers to horror and puzzle games; and Possession Mode, an “intense new challenge that pushes even the most experienced players to their limits.” “’Madison’ earned its reputation one heartbeat at a time. Players don’t just remember the story; they remember what it did to them,” Story Kitchen co-founders Dmitri Johnson and Mike Goldberg said. “Our job is to carry that physical experience into a theater without losing what makes it Bloodious’s world.” Bloodious founder Alexis Di Stefano, the game’s creator and director, said, “We built ‘Madison’ to be felt, not just played. Story Kitchen understood from the first conversation that the camera, the house, the Maxwell family, and the terrifying entities behind it all aren’t just set dressing; they’re the franchise. That’s who we wanted to build the next chapter with.” Story Kitchen has a TV first-look deal at Amazon MGM Studios and an animated film first-look deal at DreamWorks Animation. The company is repped by WME and Pryor Cashman. Channing Dungey on Warner Bros. articles.title: Amy Madigan Joins Cast of Paramount+’s ‘Ascent’ With Viola Davis and Sam Heughan
articles.full_text: Oct 26, 2026 9:00am PT Amy Madigan Joins Cast of Paramount+’s ‘Ascent’ With Viola Davis and Sam Heughan By Michael Schneider Plus Icon Michael Schneider Executive Editor franklinavenue Latest As His Doc ‘Rather’ Starts Streaming for Free on YouTube, Dan Rather Is More Concerned Than Ever About the Future of Journalism, Especially at CBS News: ‘The Wreckage Is Everywhere’ (EXCLUSIVE) 3 hours ago Greg Berlanti to Receive the Paley Center for Media’s Honors Award at Its Fall Gala 4 hours ago Blumhouse Soliciting Testimony from Anyone Who Feels ‘Personally Victimized’ by One of Its Movies or TV Shows 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ian Spanier Oscar winner Amy Madigan (“Weapons”) has joined the cast of Paramount+’s upcoming drama thriller “ Ascent .” She joins previously announced star/exec producer Viola Davis and star Sam Heughan. According to the streamer, Madigan will play “Rachel,” described as “a former executive at Ascent Ventures and Catriona’s (Davis) lifelong mentor.” The casting reunites Madigan with “Ascent” creator John Logan; she previously appeared in Logan’s series “Penny Dreadful: City of Angels.” Related Stories Todd Haynes, Zhang Ziyi and Daniel Brühl Lead a Star-Studded Lumière Fest Opening With Haynes Teasing ‘De Noche,’ Starring Pedro Pascal In “Ascent,” which is set in the world of global corporate crisis and damage control, Davis plays “Catriona, an elite corporate fixer, who must weaponize the ruthless skills that have made her indispensable to billion-dollar clients when her estranged daughter is in danger,” while Heughan plays “Conal,” a top Ascent Ventures agent. Popular on Variety Paramount Television Studios is behind the series, which was created by John Logan (“Skyfall,” “Gladiator”). Logan is showrunner and executive producer, while Michael Aguilar (“Penny Dreadful: City of Angels”) and Viola Davis and Julius Tennon for JuVee Productions are also executive producers. Production is set to begin in Los Angeles in 2027. Madigan recently won the best supporting actress Oscar for playing “Aunt Gladys” in “Weapons.” Her other film credits include “Field of Dreams,” “Twice in a Lifetime,” “Gone Baby Gone,” “Uncle Buck,” “Places in the Heart” and “Streets of Fire.” In TV, she won the Golden Globe and was Emmy-nominated for “Roe Vs. Wade.” She also was seen in “Fringe,” “Grey’s Anatomy,” “The Laramie Project” and “Carnivale.” Next up, Madigan will be seen in the film “Sponsor” with Jason Segal and John C. Reilly, an in the limited series “All the Sinners Bleed” as well as in Ryan Coogler’s “X-Files” reboot. Madigan is repped by Paradigm and Anonymous Content. articles.title: Doha Film Festival Unveils 2026 Jury Headed By Naomi Kawase
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Edinburgh Film Festival Genre Title ‘Snapshot’ Gets North American Deal Charades Boards Juho Kuosmanen’s ‘Dream Come True’ As Production Wraps Across Europe Watermelon Pictures Acquires North American Distribution Rights To Sara Ishaq’s ‘The Station’ View All October 26, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Gianfranco Rosi, Adam Bessa, Centre: Naomi Kawase L-R: Dora Bouchoucha, Kamal Aljafari L-R: Courtesy, Centre: Leslie Kee, L-R: Rim Temimi, Ferrante Ferranti Japanese director Naomi Kawase has been unveiled as the head of the jury for the main international competition of the upcoming second edition of the Doha Film Festival in November. She will be joined by French Tunisian actor Adam Bessa , Tunisian producer Dora Bouchoucha, Italian documentary filmmaker Gianfranco Rosi and award-winning Palestinian filmmaker and artist Kamal Aljafari. The jury will decide the winning films from the 15-film line-up of international titles, from across the Arab world, Asia, Africa, Europe and the Americas. Related Stories News 'Paper Tiger' & Furies' Set For Doha Film Festival Gala Screenings News Doha Film Festival To Showcase Four Qatari Features In Milestone Moment For Local Industry Born and based in Nara, Japan, Cannes regular Kawase became the youngest recipient of its Caméra d’Or for her debut feature, Suzaku , before winning the Grand Prix for The Mourning Forest (2007). Her film Radiance (2017) received the Ecumenical Jury Prize at Cannes, while her latest feature, Yakushima’s Illusion (2025), premiered in competition at Locarno. Watch on Deadline She has previously been a guest of the Doha Film Institute , which is overseeing the festival, as one of the so-called Masters in 2016 of the body’s annual Qumra event, mentoring emerging filmmakers from Qatar and beyond. Acto r Bessa broke out internationally in Lotfy Nathan’s Harka (2022), which earned him the Best Performance Award in the Un Certain Regard section at Cannes and Best Actor at the Red Sea International Film Festival. He subsequently starred in Meryam Joobeur’s Who Do I Belong To (2024), which competed at the Berlinale, and Jonathan Millet’s Ghost Trail , earning further acclaim and a César nomination. In 2026, he appeared in Asghar Farhadi’s Parallel Tales . DFI supported all three of his films, Harka , Who Do I Belong To and Parallel Tales . Bouchoucha is one of the Arab world’s most influential film producers and a longstanding advocate for emerging filmmakers. Working under the banner of her 30-year-old company Nomadis Images in 1995, her credits include Satin Rouge , Inhebbek Hedi , Weldi , Behind the Mountains , Souad and Aisha Can’t Fly Away . Rosi is the only documentary filmmaker to have won both the Golden Lion at Venice and the Golden Bear at Berlin. His film Sacro GRA (2013) became the first documentary to win Venice’s Golden Lion, while Fire at Sea (2016), filmed on the island of Lampedusa, won the Golden Bear and the European Film Award and received an Academy Award nomination. His documentary Notturno (2020) was presented in competition at Venice, and Below the Clouds (2025) won the festival’s Special Jury Prize. He was a also DFI Qumra Master in 2018. Aljafari is recognized for his distinctive cinematic practice exploring memory, history, identity and the politics of images. His feature A Fidai Film (2024) won the Jury Prize in the Burning Lights Competition at Visions du Réel and the Tanit d’Or at Carthage. His documentary With Hasan in Gaza (2025) received Best Artistic Achievement at Doha Film Festival. Both films were supported by DFI, which is also backing his forthcoming feature Beirut 1931 . “Independent cinema is where the most vital, courageous and transformative stories of our time find their voice. It is our responsibility to protect the creative freedom to challenge conventions, bring overlooked perspectives to the screen and build bridges across cultures,” said Fatma Hassan Alremaihi, CEO of Doha Film Institute and Director of Doha Film Festival . “We are immensely proud to welcome friends of the Institute who share our vision and have dedicated their lives to nurturing independent cinema. Their collective experience and artistic integrity embody the spirit of DFI and DFF: championing original voices, creating space for bold ideas and ensuring that powerful stories, find their way to audiences around the world.” The Doha Film Festival, which expands on the DFI’s long-running family-focused festival of Ajyal which ran for more than a decade during the same period, will unfold from November 19 to 27. ‘Clayface’ Takes No. 1 With $24M, But ‘See Everything’ Draws Nearly $20M Donald Trump Posts 1,300-Word Diatribe Against Bill Maher After Their Dinner Saif Ali Khan, Vidya Balan & Mélanie Laurent Set For Ritesh Batra Pic Russell Brand’s Former Assistant Alleges “Insane Sexual Appetite” Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘The Lunchbox’ Director Ritesh Batra Sets Saif Ali Khan, Vidya Balan & Mélanie Laurent For ‘Long Years Ago’; Filming Begins In Mumbai
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas ‘The Lunchbox’ Director Ritesh Batra Sets Saif Ali Khan, Vidya Balan & Mélanie Laurent For ‘Long Years Ago’; Filming Begins In Mumbai ‘The Really Loud House’ Actress Catherine Ashmore Bradley & ‘The Boys’ Actor Cameron Crovetti Lead Horror ‘Dollkeeper’ Sofia Hasmik, Grace Kelly Quigley & Imogen Waterhouse Leading Indie Feature ‘Sissy’ View All October 26, 2026 5:18am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Saif Ali Khan, Vidya Balan, Melanie Laurent Getty EXCLUSIVE : Bollywood icons Saif Ali Khan ( Sacred Games ) and Vidya Balan ( Jailer 2 ) will star with Mélanie Laurent ( Inglourious Basterds ) in The Lunchbox filmmaker Ritesh Batra ’s next film Long Years Ago , which is now underway in Mumbai. The comedy-drama heralds from Adeel Ahmed and writer-director Batra’s film and TV outfit Poetic License, and is being produced in partnership with Jio Studios ( Dhurandhar ), and Good Chaos ( Ballad Of A Small Player ). Jyoti Deshpande is producing for Jio, while Good Chaos’s Mike Goodridge and Teresa Moneo serve as executive producers, as does Siddharth Mehra. Related Stories News 'Unaccustomed Earth': Nisha Ganatra Pulls Out Of Directing; Ritesh Batra Steps In To Helm News Doha Film Festival Unveils 2026 Jury Headed By Naomi Kawase Set in 1991, Long Years Ago “is the story of a family that has gone too long without saying the things that matter, and what happens when they’re finally forced to find the words.” Watch on Deadline “I am tremendously honored to be working with Saif, Vidya and Melanie, and to see these great actors bring characters that are so close to my heart to life,” said Ritesh Batra. “Ritesh has an extraordinary gift for telling deeply personal stories that resonate across cultures. Long Years Ago is a film about love, family, and the things we often struggle to say to one another, and I felt an immediate connection to it. Collaborating with Melanie, Vidya, and this exceptional team is exciting, and I can’t wait for audiences around the world to experience this deeply moving story,” commented Saif Ali Khan. “I’m absolutely thrilled to be a part of Ritesh Batra’s next film. I’ve been a huge admirer of his work ever since The Lunchbox , and have been hoping to collaborate with him for the longest time. There’s such a beautiful sensitivity and honesty to his storytelling. What makes this even more special is that I get to reunite with Saif after Parineeta, my very first film! I can’t wait to experience the magic of working with both Ritesh and Saif,” added Vidya Balan. “I met Ritesh fifteen years ago at the Marrakech Film Festival, and we shared this dream to meet in Mumbai one day. I immediately loved this new project, and I am more than honored and happy to be a part of it,” noted Mélanie Laurent. Batra made his name with The Lunchbox , which premiered at Cannes and became one of the highest-grossing releases of the year in India. He went on to direct Our Souls at Night with Robert Redford and Jane Fonda, and the Sundance title Photograph , starring Nawazuddin Siddiqui and Sanya Malhotra. Most recently, he directed the first block of the upcoming Netflix series Unaccustomed Earth . Poetic License also has projects in development with HBO and A24. The company’s theater work began with The Lunchbox Musical , written by Batra and adapted from his 2013 film. The production played a sold-out run at Berkeley Repertory Theatre. Dil Chahta Hai , Omkara and Sacred Games star Saif Ali Khan, and National Award winner Vidya Balan, are both icons of the screen in their native India. César winner Laurent is known for movies including Inglourious Basterds and Now You See Me . Former A24 exec Mehra worked on shows including Beef and Mo for Netflix, before launching label Total Monsoon. His first production, Crystal Lake (a prequel series to the Friday the 13th movies from Brad Caleb Kane, Linda Cardellini and A24) premiered on Peacock + Sky on October 15. He was attending the same court as Russell Brand, whose trial is currently taking place in a different Southwark courtroom. articles.title: Russell Brand’s Former Assistant Claims Women Came To Comedian’s Flat For Sex All The Time But He “Never Seemed Happy” Afterwards
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Christiane Amanpour’s ‘The Ex Files’ Pod Adds Tina Brown As Co-Host For Season 2 Russell Brand’s Former Assistant Claims Women Came To Comedian’s Flat For Sex All The Time But He “Never Seemed Happy” Afterwards Chris Brown Given Suspended Prison Sentence For London Nightclub Confrontation View All October 26, 2026 5:35am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand arrives at Southwark Crown Court for the third week of his trial alongside wife Laura Gallacher. Alishia Abodunde/Getty Editor’s note: T his story contains details of alleged sexual offenses that some readers may find distressing . A witness statement from Russell Brand ’s former assistant has painted a picture of what it was like working for him in the noughties, as the Forgetting Sarah Marshall star’s rape and sexual assault trial enters its third week. Related Stories News Russell Brand Trial: Witnesses Say Their Friend Was “Extremely Distressed” After Alleged Anal Rape News Russell Brand Told Woman “We Should Swap Numbers Now” After Alleged Oral Rape In Toilet The PA, who worked for Brand during the decade that most of the alleged assaults took place, said he “loved walking around in his underwear with no shirt on,” had an “insane sexual appetite” and “never seemed happy after sex, more so depressed.” Brand faces three charges of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one of indecent assault based on allegations made by six women . His team will set out his defense later in the trial, and he denies all charges and has pleaded not guilty. Deadline has been reporting daily from a live video feed of the courtroom since the trial began. Watch on Deadline The assistant said she spent lots of time at Brand’s flat and was “exhausted emotionally” by the end as he was “a lot to deal with.” She said he was incredibly busy at the time with presenting, media and comedy work and at the same time alleged his “insane sexual appetite” meant women were constantly coming over to his flat or dressing rooms. Once, the PA was told not to take Brand’s mum or girlfriend to his dressing room as he was having sex and “didn’t want them to see,” she alleged. “At a certain point I realized he didn’t often know the women who were coming over,” read the statement. “He was like a peacock, women always approached him.” While Brand was working and she was at his flat, the woman claimed Brand would “joke with me and say, ‘May I go and have sex now?’.” She added that he “never seemed happy after sex, more so depressed.” The assistant stressed she “never witnessed Russell Brand doing anything against the law or didn’t have anyone disclose anything like that.” She added: “I have worked with celebrities before and have seen a lot of people normalizing bad behavior, but this was on another level. Everyone normalizing Russell Brand’s behavior made me think, ‘I guess this is just the way it is here.'” She said she stopped working with Brand eventually because she was “sick of him and feeling burnt out.” Brand arrived once again at London’s Southwark Crown Court this morning with wife Laura Gallacher. The statement from his ex-assistant will be one of the final pieces of evidence in the prosecution’s case, with Brand’s defense expected to begin tomorrow and the actor expected to take the stand. “He was a superstar” Earlier, witness statements were read to the jury from people associated with a trio of Brand’s accusers. One accuser has previously said she complained to Channel 4 about Brand’s behavior in 2009 after he allegedly put his head in her lap and demanded a massage. The witness statement, which came from one of the complainant’s Channel 4 colleagues, said she was told that two of Brand’s associates ordered her to give him the massage several times, otherwise he would not record a radio advert. She said her colleague told her Brand’s associates “watched and laughed” while the alleged assault was taking place. The jury was also read text messages from a different accuser, who said she was assaulted at a radio station , which argued why she didn’t report him at the time. “He was a superstar,” read the texts. “I thought nothing would happen to him.” The sister of a different alleged victim, who said she was orally raped by Brand when attending the birthday party of a TV producer, provided a statement saying her sibling told her Brand’s eyes went “completely blank, and it was like he’d been possessed or was a completely different person” during the alleged attack. articles.title: Brazil: Lula Wins Historic Fourth Presidential Term Beating Far-Right Challenger Flávio Bolsonaro
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Brazil: Lula Wins Historic Fourth Presidential Term Beating Far-Right Challenger Flávio Bolsonaro RisingJoy Signs International Distribution Pact With NTT DOCOMO Horace Ové’s ‘Pressure’ & Menelik Shabazz’s ‘Burning An Illusion’ Among Titles Screening As Part Of TIFF Cinematheque’s Windrush Season View All October 26, 2026 6:06am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Andressa Anholete/Getty Images. Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva staged a dramatic election comeback Sunday night, beating far-right challenger Flávio Bolsonaro to clinch a historic fourth term in office. Lula took 51.79% of the vote. The win makes the 80-year-old veteran the first Brazilian president since 1988 to win an election after losing the first round of voting. Bolsonaro, who is the son of Brazil ’s convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro, has refused to concede defeat and asked for the results to be annulled. In a rare but not unprecedented turn of events, polls were extended for two hours on Sunday night after both candidates made requests. Lula’s campaign had argued that voters in Salvador, the capital of Bahia, and São Paulo were prevented from reaching polling stations after reports of reduced public transportation. Bolsonaro’s campaign argued that heavy rain in areas in the south of the country had hindered voters. Related Stories Acquisitions Netflix Strikes Deal With Globo For Brazilian Fare Including 'I'm Still Here' & 'India - A Love Story' Festivals BRAVO Film Festival To Pause For 2026 According to data reports in The New York Times, Lula reversed the conservative shift from the first round of voting by earning more than 10 million new votes. The paper reported that Lula gained ground in almost every region of the country, attracting vast new support in major cities like São Paulo. He made gains in working-class suburbs and added 1.3 million votes in the country’s south, which has been a traditional Bolsonaro stronghold. Watch on Deadline In his victory speech on Sunday, Lula noted that he was forced to “overcome interference from the outside” to win a fourth term. The Bolsonaro family are longtime Trump allies. Reuters reported this weekend that officials in Trump’s State Department had pushed for sanctions against Brazil to weaken Lula and return the Bolsonaro family to power. “The election was a defeat for denialism,” Lula said. “It was a defeat for lies.” Lula added: “I highly doubt that Russia, China, or the United States possess an army as victorious as the army of democracy in this country.” ‘Clayface’ Takes No. 1 With $24M, But ‘See Everything’ Draws Nearly $20M Donald Trump Posts 1,300-Word Diatribe Against Bill Maher After Their Dinner Russell Brand’s Former Assistant Alleges “Insane Sexual Appetite” Nikolaj Coster-Waldau Leads Podcast-Based Horror Series ‘Black Tapes’ At MGM+ Read More About: 5 Comments

articles.title: Robert Pattinson Says ‘The Batman Part II’ Is Back Up And Running After Production Pause: “I’m Starting In A Couple Of Days”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Robert Pattinson Says ‘The Batman Part II’ Is Back Up And Running After Production Pause: “I’m Starting In A Couple Of Days” ‘The Lunchbox’ Director Ritesh Batra Sets Saif Ali Khan, Vidya Balan & Mélanie Laurent For ‘Long Years Ago’; Filming Begins In Mumbai ‘The Really Loud House’ Actress Catherine Ashmore Bradley & ‘The Boys’ Actor Cameron Crovetti Lead Horror ‘Dollkeeper’ View All October 26, 2026 7:45am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Robert Pattinson and 'The Batman' Phillip Faraone / Getty Images / Jonathan Olley / Warner Bros. Following its brief pause while director Matt Reeves deals with a family issue, The Batman Part II star Robert Pattinson has confirmed that production is back up and running. “I think they’re in production already,” Pattinson told Games Radar in a new interview. “And I’m starting in a couple of days.” Related Stories News ‘The Batman Part II’ Production Paused As Matt Reeves Steps Away For Personal Reasons News Steven Soderbergh To Work With Matt Reeves To Complete Final Weeks Of Principal Photography On ‘The Batman Part II’ Steven Soderbergh has stepped in to help get the DC sequel over the line. Pattinson was full of praise for Soderbergh who reached out to Reeves to offer his services when he heard the filmmaker had to step away. We broke news of the pause in production earlier this month . “I am so happy he’s [Soderbergh] come on to help Matt,” Pattinson said. “It’s incredibly generous of him – and he’s doing it in the loveliest way. It’s completely selfless…I think Matt had put so much work into the script, and we’re almost done. So for someone to come in and say, ‘I just want to help Matt do it; I want to do it in conjunction with him and just get it to the edit.’ And to have someone who’s as talented as Steven doing it is great.” Watch on Deadline Prior to the pause, filming had been underway in London. The film is set to bow on February 18, 2028. In a statement at the time, DC said Soderbergh will “complete the final weeks of principal photography on The Batman Part II ,” and that “Matt and Steven will work closely together with the actors and crew to fulfill Matt’s vision of the film.” The cast has Robert Pattinson, Andy Serkis and Colin Farrell returning respectively as Batman, Alfred and Penguin, with new additions Scarlett Johansson, Sebastian Stan, Brian Tyree Henry, Jayme Lawson, Charles Dance, Gil Perez-Abraham and Sebastian Koch. ‘Clayface’ Takes No. 1 With $24M, But ‘See Everything’ Draws Nearly $20M Donald Trump Posts 1,300-Word Diatribe Against Bill Maher After Their Dinner Russell Brand’s Former Assistant Alleges “Insane Sexual Appetite” Nikolaj Coster-Waldau Leads Podcast-Based Horror Series ‘Black Tapes’ At MGM+ Read More About: Comments

articles.title: MGM+ Greenlights ‘The Black Tapes’ Horror Series Starring Nikolaj Coster-Waldau Based On Podcast
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie MGM+ Greenlights ‘The Black Tapes’ Horror Series Starring Nikolaj Coster-Waldau Based On Podcast ‘These Summer Storms’ Series Adaptation In Works At Hulu From Melanie Marnich, Erin & Sara Foster Weekly World News Comedy Series From ‘Reno 911!’ Co-Creator Robert Ben Garant Raises $2.5M To Film Full Season Independently In California View All October 26, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Nikolaj Coster-Waldau Getty Images MGM+ is expanding its horror lineup with a series order to The Black Tapes , a supernatural investigation drama. Nikolaj Coster-Waldau stars in the eight-episode series based on the 2015 horror podcast of the same name created by Terry Miles and Paul Bae who are writers on the TV adaptation alongside John Rogers ( Leverage ). In The Black Tapes , Dr. Richard Strand (Coster-Waldau), a brilliant psychiatrist with a mysterious past, teams with the obsessed, relentless scientist Alex Regan to debunk paranormal cases of hauntings, possessions, disappearances, and sinister legends – the infamous black tapes. But as Strand and Regan unravel the secrets of these events, they uncover a hidden occult world behind our own and must unravel a centuries-old apocalyptic conspiracy. Related Stories Casting Lucy Fry & Amanda Brugel Join Jensen Ackles In MGM+ Crime Thriller 'Rules Of Prey' News Stephen King's 'The Institute' Unveils Season 2 Trailer: First Look At Alfie Allen As Nolan Reeves Produced by MGM+ Studios, The Black Tapes is executive produced by Miles and Bae as well as Kearie Peak of Peak Pictures and Rogers and Jennifer Court of Kung Fu Monkey Productions, with Rogers serving as showrunner. The series is scheduled to begin production in Vancouver in January 2027 for release on MGM+ in the U.S., UK, Ireland, Germany, Italy, Spain, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Latin America. Watch on Deadline The Black Tapes podcast has amassed over 60 million downloads since its launch 11 years ago. NBC developed a drama series adaptation during the 2018-19 cycle, which was written and executive produced by Bae, Miles and Mathew Arnold. It did not go to pilot. “ The Black Tapes crafts a compelling story around our cultural fascination with the unexplained, while delivering the cinematic, classic storytelling that MGM+ audiences expect,” said Michael Wright, global head of MGM+. “With Nikolaj’s compelling presence and the creative vision of John Rogers, Kearie Peak and our talented production team, we’re excited to make something that is both provocative and hugely entertaining.” The project brings back together Wright, Rogers and Paek. During his tenure as a top TNT programming executive, Wright oversaw several titles from Dean Devlin’s Electric Entertainment that Rogers and Paek were part of: Paek worked on The Librarian movie franchise and the series Leverage , while Rogers was across Leverage and The Librarians TV series offshoot, which he co-created and developed, respectively. “I was an early and passionate fan of The Black Tapes podcast,” says Rogers. “It’s a unique blend of truly unsettling horror and puzzle-box conspiracy mystery. With Paul and Terry not just executive producing, but also in the writer’s room, we have a chance to both bring The Black Tape s to a new generation of genre fans and deepen and expand the mythos in ways that will surprise long-time supernatural horror fans.” The Black Tapes joins MGM+’s current horror slate of From , which is headed to a fifth and final season, and The Institute, whose second season premieres Nov. 8. Best known for his Emmy-nominated role as Jaime Lannister on HBO’s Game of Thrones, Coster-Waldau recently starred in the BBC/Prime Video series King & Conquerer and Apple TV+’s, The Last Thing He Told Me . He next stars opposite Jennifer Lopez in the Netflix film The Last Mrs. Parrish. articles.title: Stoic To Launch AFM Sales On Holiday Comedy ‘Unbearable Christmas’ With Alex Moffat, Julia Stiles, David Cross
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Robert Pattinson Says ‘The Batman Part II’ Is Back Up And Running After Production Pause: “I’m Starting In A Couple Of Days” ‘The Lunchbox’ Director Ritesh Batra Sets Saif Ali Khan, Vidya Balan & Mélanie Laurent For ‘Long Years Ago’; Filming Begins In Mumbai ‘The Really Loud House’ Actress Catherine Ashmore Bradley & ‘The Boys’ Actor Cameron Crovetti Lead Horror ‘Dollkeeper’ View All October 26, 2026 8:05am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Unbearable Christmas Vertical EXCLUSIVE : Stoic has acquired international sales rights (excluding North America) for Unbearable Christmas , the holiday comedy starring SNL alum Alex Moffat, Julia Stiles, David Cross, Caroline Rhea, Mena Suvari, and Stephen Root. Stoic will officially launch sales for all available international territories at the upcoming American Film Market ( AFM ) in Los Angeles. The international launch follows Vertical acquiring the domestic rights for a wide North American release this holiday season, and an accompanying streaming deal which is due to be announced soon. Marking the feature directorial debut of writer-director Kevin Cate, the film “follows out-of-work weatherman Troy Tipton (Moffat) on a high-stakes holiday mission: get back the beloved family teddy bear he pawned for cash. With his wife Becca (Stiles), mother-in-law Dawn (Rhea), and kids in tow, Troy embarks on a chaotic road trip from Ohio to Florida in his old news van. The journey takes an unhinged turn when the family discovers the cherished bear is actually a priceless Teddy Roosevelt antique worth millions.” Watch on Deadline Cate co-wrote the screenplay with Sennett. Pic is produced by Blake Sennett and Kevin Cate under Cate’s indie banner Clinging Vine Films. articles.title: Janus Films Acquires Alfonso Cuarón’s ‘Y Tu Mamá También’ Ahead Of 25th Anniversary 4K Re-Release
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Brazil: Lula Wins Historic Fourth Presidential Term Beating Far-Right Challenger Flávio Bolsonaro RisingJoy Signs International Distribution Pact With NTT DOCOMO Horace Ové’s ‘Pressure’ & Menelik Shabazz’s ‘Burning An Illusion’ Among Titles Screening As Part Of TIFF Cinematheque’s Windrush Season View All October 26, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Y Tu Mamá También Janus Films EXCLUSIVE: Janus Films has acquired all rights in North America and the UK/Ireland to Alfonso Cuarón’s classic fourth feature , Y Tu Mamá También , which has been restored in 4K to mark the 25th anniversary of its premiere. The new 4K print will be released theatrically in the summer of 2027. Y Tu Mamá También launched at the Venice Film Festival in 2001, where it won the Best Screenplay Award. The following year, it was nominated for the Best Screenplay Oscar, the Golden Globe for Best Motion Picture – Non-English Language, and the BAFTA for Best Original Screenplay and Best Film Not in the English Language. Related Stories Casting Amy Madigan Joins 'Ascent' TV Series At Paramount+ News Stoic To Launch AFM Sales On Holiday Comedy 'Unbearable Christmas' With Alex Moffat, Julia Stiles, David Cross The film follows a pair of horny Mexico City teenagers (played by Gael García Bernal and Diego Luna), who, after their girlfriends jet off to Italy for the summer, become bewitched by an older Spanish woman (Maribel Verdú) they meet at a wedding. When she agrees to accompany them on a trip to a faraway beach, the three form an increasingly intense and sensual alliance that ultimately strips them both physically and emotionally bare. Watch on Deadline The title launched Bernal and Luna’s international careers along with Emmanuel “Chivo” Lubezki, who lensed the film, and, of course, Cuarón, who went on to win Academy Awards for Best Director ( Roma ), Best Editing ( Gravity ), Best Cinematography ( Roma ), and Best Foreign Language Film ( Roma ) “Y Tu Mamá También remains very close to me, and it means a great deal to see it return to theaters 25 years later,” Cuarón said in a statement. “I’m especially excited to share the film with a new generation, while longtime viewers can experience it again in a new 4K restoration.
