articles.title: TV Ratings: ‘Cupertino’ and ‘Line of Fire’ More than Double in Delayed Viewing
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All October 23, 2026 3:02pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Rachel Keller and Mike Colter in 'Cupertino' (left); Kat Cunning and Peter Krause in 'Line of Fire' Elizabeth Fisher/CBS; Ralph Bavaro/NBC Logo text Cupertino and Line of Fire are very different shows on screen, but their ratings profiles early in the season are very similar. Both shows draw about 3 million viewers for their initial airings (3.03 million for Cupertino’ s first two episodes on CBS, 2.98 million over three for Line of Fire on NBC). That’s not bad for a 10 p.m. network show — it tends to be the least watched hour of primetime — but a few other series that air in that hour are ahead of them. Cupertino and Line of Fire are also picking up a lot of viewing — most of their seven-day totals, in fact — after those initial airings. The 2026-27 TV season is just a month old, so these are necessarily small sample sizes. But if these early patterns hold up, Cupertino and Line of Fire are poised to draw audiences well above their same-day audiences. Related Stories TV Streaming Ratings: 'Carrie' Has a Bloody Good Opening Week TV NBC Extends 'Line of Fire' With Full-Season Pickup CBS’ two other rookies, NCIS: New York and Eternally Yours , also had good starts, with the former’s Oct. 6 series premiere ranking sixth among all network shows (excluding live sports) after a week of cross-platform viewing. The latest entry in the NCIS franchise grew to 10.25 million viewers over a week, according to Nielsen’s multi-platform ratings. That’s up from 5.62 million same-day viewers — a growth of 82 percent. Of the 4.63 million additional viewers for NCIS: New York , 2.45 million came via streaming (about 24 percent of the all-in, seven-day total) and 2.18 million via DVR. Cupertino’ s Oct. 8 premiere more than doubled after a week, going from 3.19 million on-air viewers to 7.17 million. The majority (2.18 million) of its after-air viewers came to the show via DVR, while an additional 1.8 million streamed the premiere in seven days. Through its first three episodes, Line of Fire is averaging 6.9 million cross-platform viewers over a week, also more than doubling its initial audience (2.98 million). Its delayed viewing also tilts a little toward DVR playback (2.08 million viewers) vs. streaming (1.84 million). In announcing a full-season order for the show on Thursday, NBC also noted that the Sept. 21 premiere has grown to 14 million viewers over a month’s time. Eternally Yours , a comedy about a family of vampires, also debuted Oct. 8. It had 4.12 million same-day viewers and 6.94 million after seven days, up 68 percent. About 1.58 million of those were streaming viewers, with 1.24 million coming from DVR playback. Here’s how the four new scripted shows that have premiered so far compare (a fifth, NBC’s comedy Newlyweds , debuts Friday). All figures are through Oct. 11. THR

articles.title: Chappell Roan Enlists PinkPantheress to Close Out Super Graphic Spectacular Fundraising Shows
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Nicole Fell Plus Icon Nicole Fell Associate Editor nicolemfell Follow Sign Up View All October 23, 2026 3:03pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Chappell Roan performs onstage at The Super Graphic Spectacular in Los Angeles. @IZZYNUZZOPHOTO Chappell Roan gathered together a slew of artists including Caroline Polachek, MUNA and surprise guest PinkPantheress in Los Angeles Thursday night for the second of two nights of The Super Graphic Spectacular. The two-day event, held at the Shrine Auditorium and Expo Hall, was billed as a fundraising event featuring live performances, volunteer opportunities, connection and a special headlining set from Roan herself. Roan was preceded by sets from Polachek, Muna, Alisa Mae, Fantasia Royale Gaga and Sweat Eddie. With a block party that kicked off in the afternoon, the event, which raised money for the pop star’s foundation The Midwest Princess Project, which supports trans youth and the LGBTQ+ community. All proceeds of the event were donated to the organization. Related Stories Movies Tanner Buchanan, Peyton Elizabeth Lee to Star in 'Gasoline' From 'SLC Punk!' Director James Merendino (Exclusive) Music Victoria Justice on Releasing a Remixed "Love Zombie," a Viral Hit 15 Years in the Making Comedian Caleb Hearon hosted the evening, and even joined MUNA during the band’s set. Roan delivered a high-energy performance to the just over 6,000 capacity room. It was a large underplay for the Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess singer, who is without-a-doubt a stadium act at this point, having drawn an estimated 40,000 per night at her Pasadena shows last year. The audience for Thursday’s show was just as high-energy back, and an argument could be made that they might be one of the most engaged crowd’s the venue’s ever seen. Roan used every inch of the gothic-themed stage during her roughly 70-minute set, kicking off with, unsurprisingly, “Super Graphic Ultra Modern Girl.” The setlist was consistent with other shows the singer’s done over the past year, leaning heavily on her breakout album The Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess, with some newer songs — “The Subway,” “Good Luck, Babe!” and “The Giver” — sprinkled in. Chappell Roan and PinkPantheress onstage during The Super Graphic Spectacular. @IZZYNUZZOPHOTO During night one, Christina Aguilera joined Roan, and she sang her her classic hit “Beautiful” before the two singers joined together for a duet of “Coffee.” For night two, Roan mixed things up, bringing out PinkPantheress, describing the British pop star as being “fantastic” and “just so cunt” as she introduced her. PinkPantheress performed “Tonight” for the crowd, while Roan danced around onstage with her band. Later in the show, Roan brought out Lola Young, who performed in one of the opening slots on night one, for a duet of Roan’s “Picture You.” The song, one of Roan’s more underrated offerings, was a highlight of the night. Naturally, Roan brought her signature candor and wit to the performance, joking around with fans in the audience. “There’s some straight people in the front row, I can tell,” she said at one point during the performance before later, during the song, rushing to tell the straight it was OK. It was all in good fun. Roan even dedicated “The Giver,” her lesbian country anthem, to “all the top lesbians out there.” The night ended with a performance of the singer’s remix of the Olivia Rodrigo song “Expectations,” which she performed as a solo, and smash hit “Pink Pony Club.” During the song — which features the lyrics “Won’t make my Mama proud / it’s gonna cause a scene / She sees her baby girl / I know she’s gonna scream” — the singer pointed to the mezzanine to inform the crowd her actual mother was in attendance. The moment got a big cheer from the crowd. “Pink Pony Club” is the type of concert anthem that will never get old, with every person in the room singing the lyrics as loud as they can. All net proceeds from both shows, sponsored by CashApp and Visa, will be donated to the The Midwest Princess Project to power “the next chapter” of the queer-centric organization’s work. THR

articles.title: Ethan Klein Says He’s Working to “Urgently Remove My Ownership, Financial Stakes” From H3 Podcast After Wife Hila Klein Reveals His Affair
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All October 23, 2026 3:05pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Hila Klein and Ethan Klein attend the 2023 Streamy Awards at Fairmont Century Plaza on August 27, 2023 in Los Angeles. Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images YouTuber Ethan Klein has been dropped from the popular H3 Podcast after his wife Hila Klein revealed that he has been having an affair for over six months, and he’s breaking his silence on the allegations. “We are all shocked, angry, and heartbroken to learn about Ethan’s ongoing affair. As soon as we found out, we all agreed: we would not continue working with Ethan involved or profiting in any way,” the H3 Podcast crew wrote on Instagram late Thursday. “We don’t yet know what that means for the future. There’s a lot to work through, and we wish we had more answers for you.” Related Stories Movies 'The Telepathy Tapes' Movie Based on Podcast Lands at Amazon MGM for Early 2027 Release (Exclusive) News Rupert Grint Sets Next Project: Noiser Audiobook Adaptation of 'Treasure Island' (Exclusive) The statement continued, “We stand with Hila and will support her every step of the way. We’re disgusted by Ethan’s actions and the hurt he has caused. We all deserved better: Hila, us, and you. “Please know that we’re safe, we’re sticking together, and we’re looking after each other. We’ve put so much of ourselves into this show, and it’s hard to find the words for what we’re feeling right now. Thank you for giving us some time to figure things out, and for all the love you’ve shown us. We love you, and we miss you already.” Ethan and Hila co-host H3 on their YouTube channel, which has amassed 2.5 million followers. Ethan previously co-hosted the Frenemies podcast (which aired on H3 ‘s YouTube) alongside Trisha Paytas, whom is married to Hila’s brother Moses Hacmon; they canceled that podcast after a fallout. Ethan shared an initial statement on his Instagram Story Friday asking fans to “please respect my family’s privacy and do not contact them looking for me or asking for their comments. They have nothing to do with this and share in your outrage and disappointment. Thank you.” He then shared a follow-up post when he confirmed he’s in the process of fully cutting ties with the H3 Podcast . “I am working with Hila to urgently remove my ownership and financial stakes in any podcasts, [Hila’s businesses] Teddy Fresh, Teddy Glow or any joint venture that I would profit from. All of your support will go directly to Hila and the crew,” Ethan wrote. “I do this in the hope that people can still support Hila and the Crew without the concern of enriching me. I know the crew will make an awesome show, they are packed to the brim with the most talented, creative, hilarious and all around great people.” Hila shared on Instagram late Thursday night that she learned her husband, Ethan, had been having an affair. She wrote, “I am living a nightmare I can’t wake up from. My husband has been having an affair. I have been fed lie after lie after lie for months. Here is the truth.” “I could sense something was wrong. I tried to ask him questions and share my concerns and hurt feelings. But I was met with dismissive answers and no action. Things that bothered me continued to bother me, and he did nothing about it. So I trusted him. Because I loved him. I stopped questioning him and began to question myself, my own instincts. My sanity,” she continued. “Eventually, he was caught in a lie, and I knew I was done. But the lies continued. ‘It was just a kiss’ became ‘it was emotional cheating.’ After I dragged these lies from him, he finally admitted he’d been in an affair for over 6 months, the extent of which I’m sure I still don’t know.” Hila wrote, “The betrayal I feel is immeasurable. The person I loved and trusted for 20 years evaporated overnight. He was my safe place, my partner in marriage, parenting, and business. My only family on this side of the world. How do I even begin to make sense of this?” “I don’t know what comes next; I’ve never been here before. I am in survival mode, trying to navigate separation, co-parenting, and unthinkable heartbreak. All I can do right now is focus on taking care of myself and my children, one day at a time. You’re not crazy. Trust your instincts. Trust yourself. If you’re not being treated right, get up and leave,” she concluded. The H3 Podcast launched in 2016 and has featured interviews with Post Malone, MrBeast and Jack Black. It’s been nominated for best podcast at the Streamy Awards five times. Ethan and Hila married in 2012, and share three children. THR

articles.title: Marysa Maslansky, Founder of the Renowned Visages Photo Agency, Dies at 82
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All October 23, 2026 3:44pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Marysa Maslansky Davis Factor Marysa Maslansky, whose influential Visages Photo Agency represented such A-list photographers as Herb Ritts, Mary Ellen Mark and George Hurrell in the 1980s and ’90s, has died. She was 82. Maslansky died Oct. 9 at her home in Los Angeles after a long illness, a family spokesperson announced. Born in Pas-de-Calais, France, on April 27, 1944, Maslansky settled in Los Angeles in 1969 and worked as a journalist for the Sygma Photo News agency before heading Gamma Liaison, the L.A. branch of Gamma, the prominent French photo agency. Related Stories TV Michael Gray, Former Teen Idol and Star of 'Shazam!,' Dies at 75 Movies Tom Skerritt, Star of 'Picket Fences' and 'Alien,' Dies at 93 In 1980, she founded Visages, and in addition to Ritts, Mark and Hurrell, the agency would become home to many other iconic celebrity and fashion photographers, among them William Claxton, Greg Gorman, Matthew Rolston, Paul Jasmin, Sofia Coppola, Brad Branson and Firooz Zahedi. When Ritts started with Maslansky at Visages, his fee was in the range of $750 a day, the Los Angeles Times wrote back then. But by 1990, he was earning about $20,000 a day as one of the highest-paid commercial photographers in the U.S. at the time. Visages closed its doors in 2000 amid the shift to digital, industry consolidation and competition from major syndicates including Getty Images and Corbis. Maslansky was married to Michael Maslansky — a founding partner (with Pat Kingsley and Neil Koenigsberg) of what would become PMK Public Relations — from 1975 until his death in 1993 of stroke complications at age 55. His clients included Goldie Hawn, Sylvester Stallone, Liza Minnelli and Katharine Hepburn . Survivors include her second husband, Christopher, son Max and daughter-in-law Nancy. Another son, Alex, died in 2023 at age 43. THR

articles.title: ‘Crawl 2’ Adds Sarah Niles, Ray Panthaki and 3 More Ahead of 2027 Paramount Release (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski Plus Icon Ryan Gajewski Senior Entertainment Reporter View All October 23, 2026 3:51pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Richard Brake (left), Sarah Niles, Ray Panthaki, Flula Borg and Charley Palmer Rothwell Courtesy of Subject Logo text Paramount Pictures ‘ forthcoming sequel to horror movie Crawl is snapping up more castmembers. Sarah Niles , Ray Panthaki , Richard Brake, Charley Palmer Rothwell and Flula Borg have joined the cast for filmmaker Alexandre Aja ‘s Crawl follow-up, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. Mason Gooding and Emily Rudd were previously announced to lead the untitled sequel feature that is set for theatrical release on July 16, 2027. The initial Crawl hit theaters in 2019 and centered on a woman (Kaya Scodelario) and her father (Barry Pepper) dealing with a swarm of massive alligators after a hurricane damages their Florida home. The film surpassed $91 million globally, with critic John DeFore writing in his THR review that “thrillseekers should appreciate the brisk pace with which scares, setbacks and possible escapes are delivered.” Related Stories Movies 'Cyberpunk 2077' Live Action Film in Development at Paramount Pictures Movies Tallinn Black Nights Fest Sets Competition and First Features Programs, Including Ray Panthaki Debut Aja helms the new movie from a script that he co-wrote with Jason Harry Pagan, Andrew Deutschman, and Gregory Levasseur. Producers include Craig Flores, Sam Raimi and Aja, while Levasseur, Kevan Van Thompson and Zainab Azizi executive produce. Niles has landed two Emmy Award nominations for her role on Apple TV’s Ted Lasso , and her feature work includes Fantastic Four: The First Steps , Heads of State and F1 . She is is represented by TFC Management, Denton Brierley and Shelby Weiser. Panthaki appeared alongside Samantha Morton and Charles Dance on the Starz series The Serpent Queen and had roles in such features as Boiling Point , Official Secrets and Colette . He is repped by CAA, TFC Management, CAM in London and Lucy Popkin. Brake is known for features like Barbarian , Mandy and Batman Begins and for such series as Mayor of Kingstown , Peaky Blinders and Game of Thrones . The actor is repped by Markham, Froggatt & Irwin in the U.K. and Untitled Entertainment in the U.S. Rothwell’s film credits include The Running Man , Midas Man and Dunkirk , along with series work in Industry and A Gentleman in Moscow . Rothwell is repped by Ollie Azis at Independent Talent Group. Borg has appeared in such features as Champagne Problems , My Spy: The Eternal City , The Suicide Squad and the Pitch Perfect franchise, in addition to his parts in series like Tulsa King and The Rookie . Borg is repped by Artists First, Artemis Entertainment, United Agents and Felker Toczek. THR

articles.title: Ken Atchity, Producer on ‘Joe Somebody’ and ‘The Meg,’ Dies at 82
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All October 23, 2026 4:12pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ken Atchity Courtesy of The Blaine Group Ken Atchity, an author and professor who became a literary manager and producer on such films as Joe Somebody , Hysteria and The Meg , has died. He was 82. Atchity died Monday of kidney failure at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles, his longtime business and producing partner, Chi-Li Wong, told The Hollywood Reporter . Atchity also was behind 16 romantic telefilms made under the banner of Shades of Love that were produced for cable and video. They ran in Canada and on HBO/Cinemax in the States and were released internationally by Warner Bros. Related Stories TV Michael Gray, Former Teen Idol and Star of 'Shazam!,' Dies at 75 Movies Tom Skerritt, Star of 'Picket Fences' and 'Alien,' Dies at 93 Atchity produced the shark thriller The Meg (2018) and its sequel, Meg 2: The Trench (2023), both starring Jason Statham. (Jon Turteltaub directed the first installment, Ben Wheatley the second.) In addition to Joe Somebody (2001), starring Tim Allen, and Hysteria (2011), starring Maggie Gyllenhaal, Atchity produced features including Life or Something Like It (2002), starring Angelina Jolie, and Gospel Hill (2008), directed by Giancarlo Esposito. Other producing credits included the 1989 telefilm The Amityville Horror: The Evil Escapes and the 2010 documentary The Kennedy Detail . An author of more than 20 books, Atchity headed Story Merchant Books, selling his clients’ work to publishers and to film and television outlets while publishing many other works himself. One of five kids, Kenneth John Atchity was born on Jan. 16, 1944, in Eunice, Louisiana. Raised in Kansas City, Missouri, he graduated from Rockhurst High School with an Ignatian Scholarship to study at Georgetown University (while in high school, he published his first book reviews for The Kansas City Star ). At Georgetown, Atchity majored in Classics and English, served as editor-in-chief of the student-run newspaper The Hoya and spent his junior summer at Cambridge University in England, studying literature and social institutions. While earning his master’s degree at Yale, he studied under A. Bartlett Giamatti and Erich Segal, then taught for more than a decade at Occidental College in L.A. before getting into show business in the 1980s. Survivors include his wife, Kayoko, whom he married in 2003; his children, Vincent and Rosemary; his grandchildren, Margaret, Edward, Oliver, Eliot and Louis; and his sisters, Mary and Laurie. Donations in his memory can be made Yoga Gives Back , which aims to empower women and children in India. THR

articles.title: Nick Reiner’s Push for Release of Trust Money to Be Decided by Mediator
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Winston Cho Plus Icon Winston Cho View All October 23, 2026 4:26pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Nick Reiner appears with Deputy Public Defender Kimberly Greene during his arraignment in Los Angeles County Superior Court on Feb. 23, 2026. Chris Torres-Pool/Getty Images A deal has been struck between lawyers for Nick Reiner and the trust allowing a mediator to decide whether he can access funds set aside for him by his parents. The mediation could open the door for him to rehire Alan Jackson, who has represented Harvey Weinstein and Karen Read, among others, and withdrew from the case because of Reiner’s financial constraints. “A criminal defendant has a constitutional right to use money that is lawfully his own to be defended by the lawyer he chooses,” Reiner’s lawyer, Anita Wu, said in a statement. “These issues need to get resolved as quickly as possible.” Related Stories General News Jamie Lee Curtis Leaning on "Love and Service" in Honoring the Late Rob and Michele Reiner: "Every Day With Them Was Activism" Lifestyle Jamie Lee Curtis to Receive Inaugural Award Inspired by Rob and Michele Reiner at Children's Institute Gala; John Mayer to Perform Reiner has been held in custody without bail since pleading not guilty to the murders in February. He was initially charged with two counts of first-degree murder with special circumstances relating to multiple homicides, meaning the maximum sentence he faces is life without parole. The Los Angeles County district attorney’s office has said it will not seek the death penalty after consulting Reiner’s siblings. The trust’s fiduciaries have maintained that Reiner is barred from accessing money in the trust, citing California’s so-called slayer statute. The law prohibits people from receiving an inheritance from those they kill. One issue in the case is whether the statute applies since Reiner hasn’t been convicted. Another is whether the money is already his since half of the funds should’ve been dispersed to him on his 30th birthday in 2023. Under the terms of the irrevocable trust, the other half is to be paid to him when he turns 35. Money from the trust is currently being used to pay for lawyers on both side of the litigation, including those trying to prevent Reiner from accessing the funds. So far, fiduciaries have paid lawyers more than $250,000, according to court filings. The figure is nearly half of the trust, $558,000, Reiner should’ve received when he turned 30. “None of that makes any sense, or serves anyone’s interests,” Wu said. The mediation will begin in December. In court filings, Reiner’s lawyers have also argued that a “substantial portion” of the disputed funds in the trust, at least $325,000, is money from his grandfather, Carl Reiner, who died in 2020. “Nick is not accused of causing his death,” the filing stated. “Money that was left to Nick by his grandfather is not money received by Nick from or through his parents. To the extent the funds Nick received from his grandfather are Nick’s personal assets, they remain Nick’s and should be segregated and released from this trust. Even if they were properly held by the trust, the ‘Slayer Statute’ does not supply a basis for withholding them.” THR

articles.title: ‘Street Fighter’ Breakout Callina Liang Talks Embracing Fan Skepticism and Reveals Two Key Scrapped Moments
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Brian Davids Plus Icon Brian Davids Writer PickYourBrian Follow Sign Up View All October 23, 2026 4:53pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Emma McIntyre/Getty Images for SiriusXM Logo text [This story contains spoilers for Street Fighter .] When Street Fighter star Callina Liang was cast as Chun-Li, one of her all-time favorite video game characters, she understood the fans’ skepticism. In fact, she shared their concerns that her physique didn’t yet match that of the beloved martial artist, whom many consider the most iconic female character in fighting games. She didn’t take the criticism personally, but she still used it as bulletin board material to hopefully win over her doubters. “A lot of the comments I read online motivated me even more to prove them wrong. But I agree that, physically, where I started wasn’t where I would ideally want Chun-Li to be,” Liang tells The Hollywood Reporter . Related Stories Movies 'Street Fighter' Director Kitao Sakurai Built a Career by Embracing the Ridiculous Movies 'You Can See Everything' Triumphs With $15M as 'Street Fighter' Wins Weekend From that moment on, Liang went all-in on becoming the beloved fighter, putting herself through an intense physical transformation to embody the undercover Interpol agent. She pumped iron multiple times a week, trained in stunts and martial arts daily and followed a rigorous diet that included 12 eggs per day. For a character whose martial arts style is defined by her powerful kicks, Liang added nearly three inches to her thighs. The physical overhaul was so dramatic that her stunt double had to wear “butt pads” to mirror Liang’s new figure whenever they swapped in and out of scenes. It’s a staggering metamorphosis, particularly for anyone familiar with the Canadian-Chinese actor’s previous roles as high school girls exploited by their classmates in Steven Soderbergh’s Presence and J.C. Lee’s Bad Genius . “Honestly, I wasn’t expecting [my legs to keep growing], but the amazing crafty table they had on set definitely helped,” Liang says. “I definitely felt the pressure. I just didn’t want to disappoint anyone.” Chun-Li infiltrates Lord M. Bison’s (David Dastmalchian) criminal and military organization to avenge her father’s murder at the hands of the Shadaloo leader. At the same time, Bison seeks to lure Ryu (Andrew Koji) into his second World Warrior tournament, where he plans to siphon the reigning champion’s psycho power for himself. Chun-Li helps track down Ken Masters’ (Noah Centineo) estranged adoptive brother, further ingratiating herself with Bison until he offers to formally welcome her into Shadaloo. In an earlier version of the script, Chun-Li was meant to sacrifice a finger as part of this initiation and show of loyalty to Bison’s syndicate, but Capcom, the creators of the Street Fighter video game franchise, appeared to take issue with the idea. The hesitation is understandable, especially when you consider the practical complications that could arise if sequels or spinoffs are to follow. It’s a similar predicament to the one filmmaker Chad Stahelski and Keanu Reeves encountered with John Wick’s own act of fealty in John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum . The assassin ultimately cut off his own finger, forcing the filmmakers to account for its absence in every subsequent shot of Chapter 3 , Chapter 4 and Ballerina , including the added VFX costs of digitally removing it. The compromise for Chun-Li was considerably less drastic. Instead of sacrificing a digit, she receives the mark of Shadaloo on her inner palm. “Chun-Li was originally supposed to chop off a finger, but Capcom … They went back and forth with the script, and eventually they decided that hand-branding was the better way to do it,” Liang shares. “If she had no pinky for the rest of the [potential series], it would be deforming the character in a way.” Getting into spoiler territory, Liang admits she was a little frustrated that Chun-Li didn’t get to fulfill her mission of taking down Bison. “Honestly, a little bit,” Liang says when asked if she was disappointed. “The whole film, especially Chun-Li’s storyline, builds toward Chun-Li’s final takedown of Bison. But there’s a reason for everything, and hopefully, if we get a sequel one day, we’ll get to explore that. I’m sure it’d be epic.” During a scene in which Chun-Li tries to wake Ken up to the fact that the tournament is merely a front for draining the power of his former best friend and training partner, Ryu, another creative choice wound up on the cutting-room floor. Dating back to her chemistry read with Centineo, Liang suggested slapping Ken, and her co-star encouraged her to truly go for the jugular. But despite filming the moment on set, the genuine slap ultimately fell by the wayside. “On the day, we actually tried multiple takes where I physically slapped him across the face,” Liang says. “There was no way to really fake it, so Noah just let me slap him in the face a couple of times. It didn’t end up making it into the final cut, but it was fun.” Below, in a conversation with THR , Liang also discusses the “Tuesday” homage to Raul Julia’s M. Bison in 1994’s Street Fighter , as well as turning Chun-Li’s infamous shower scene from Street Fighter II: The Animated Movie into an amusing gag. *** Callina Liang stars as Chloe in Steven Soderbergh’s Presence Courtesy of Sundance Institute I first saw you in Presence , and while it’s not easy to make single-location movies compelling, you guys pulled it off. Did you feel a career bump after that? Did it perhaps open the door to Street Fighter ? Presence definitely opened a lot of doors for me, but I don’t know if it directly connected to me getting Street Fighter . I started auditioning for Street Fighter two years after we finished Presence , so it had been a while. When I first connected with [Legendary Pictures producer] Cale [Boyter], I remember he was like, “No, I haven’t seen Presence .” Maybe he finally watched it after meeting me. But working with Steven Soderbergh was a huge honor, and I learned so much from being on set with him. Most of my scenes, as Chloe, were with the ghost, and the ghost was essentially the camera with Steven as the DoP. So a lot of it was mainly just me and Steven interacting with each other. It truly felt like a masterclass in cinematography. On the first day, Steven said to the cast, “I’m going to go all-in. It’s risky to make a movie like this. There’s only one way it’s going to go. It either works or it doesn’t, and we just all have to trust that it’s going to work.” And it ended up working. You got a call from your reps about auditioning for Chun-Li in Street Fighter , starting with a Zoom call with director Kitao Sakurai and producer Cale Boyter. Afterwards, they signaled to your agent that you were probably dead in the water, but you kept getting called back — to the point that you had to bail on your birthday plans with your friends to fly out for a chemistry read with Noah Centineo. Have your pals finally forgiven you for choosing career advancement over them? ( Laughs .) Oh, absolutely. If any of my friends were unwilling to forgive me, then they weren’t a real one to begin with. It was a crazy ride, and honestly, it was the best birthday present I could have ever asked for. A couple days after I got back from the chemistry read with Noah in L.A., Kitao called me personally to tell me that I got the role of Chun-Li. So it was a dream come true, and there was no better way I would’ve spent my birthday. Callina Liang’s Chun-Li and Noah Centineo’s Ken Masters in Street Fighter Courtesy of Paramount Pictures And Legendary Pictures Did you and Noah read the bathroom scene where she warns Ken that the tournament is a front to steal Ryu’s power? We did the scene where Chun-Li invites Ken to the tournament, and then we did the scene of us together in the bathroom. In the chemistry read, Cale sat in on some of it, but it was mostly me, Noah and Kitao working together. At some point, Kitao was like, “To get Ken to see that the tournament is not a real thing, I think Chun-Li would get physical. Do you think you can add some physicality to it?” And I was like, “Noah, are you comfortable with this?” And he was like, “Sure, go ahead.” And I was like, “Alright, if I have the green light.” So for one of the takes, I grabbed him by the collar and slapped him across the face, saying, “Wake up! This is not a real tournament.” It was so much fun. Then we brought Cale in to watch it, and he was like, “Oh my gosh, I wasn’t expecting that. That was great.” On the day, we actually tried multiple takes where I physically slapped him across the face. There was no way to really fake it, so Noah just let me slap him in the face a couple of times. It didn’t end up making it into the final cut, but it was fun. There’s a video of you guys promoting the movie somewhere, and Noah suddenly jumped on the game-inspired car that was there, giving you quite a jump-scare. What’s your version of that story? ComplexCon was a lot of fun, but hectic. We were up on this stage with an audience of people watching, and all I could think in my head was that I was wearing these six-inch heels with insane platforms. They looked amazing with my outfit. My stylists, Wayman and Micah, kill it every single time. But I was just trying my hardest to stay balanced and not fall over while we were taking pictures and filming content around that car in front of the crowd that gathered at our stand. Then Noah jumped on the car, but I’m honestly used to it. Working with Noah and [Andrew] Koji, they always pretend to fight each other or jump on things, on and off set. So I was mostly just like, Oh my gosh, I can’t fall over. Not right now. But other than that, I was like, Oh, it’s just Noah being Noah . I didn’t end up falling over, and all was good. But I was concerned about his shoulder. I actually asked him afterwards if he hurt it, and he said he didn’t. Callina Liang’s Chun-Li in Street Fighter Courtesy of Paramount Pictures And Legendary Pictures Back to pre-production, you had two months to get jacked, particularly your legs, since Chun-Li is known for her dangerous kicks. Was it a sprint to the finish line? Yeah, absolutely. I sprinted all the way. Even after filming had started, I kept going to weightlifting sessions whenever my schedule allowed it. Stunt training also kept going all throughout. I learned the first choreo I had to film, and then after we filmed that, I had to learn the second choreo I had to film. So I kept up with the eating, and that’s why my legs kept growing from the first day of filming to the last day of filming. Honestly, I wasn’t expecting it, but the amazing crafty table they had on set definitely helped. So I definitely felt the pressure of time, the expectations of longtime fans and the expectations I had of myself. I just didn’t want to disappoint anyone. So it’s true that you used the fan response to your casting as bulletin board material? Yeah, it really was motivation. A lot of the comments I read online just motivated me even more to prove them wrong, but nothing really got to me personally. I was like, Listen, I agree with you guys. As an outsider who’s also a fan of the games and the character, I agree that, physically, where I started wasn’t where I would ideally want Chun-Li to be. But there’s always room for growth. You can always be better, and that’s the way I looked at it. The Street Fighter cast is such an odd collection of people. You have wrestlers, a rapper, a real-life vampire, a few comedians, a country musician, a bodybuilder and several martial artists. Was the set basically a rambunctious carnival? Yes, absolutely. There’s really no better way to put it. There was never a dull moment on set. Every day was chaotic, but chaotic in a fun way. I was personally fangirling over 50 Cent whenever he was on set. Eric André and Schulz were always making jokes and filming prank videos. I was always confused by them, but I ended up laughing along with them. I was actually really intimidated by the wrestlers at first. Who wouldn’t be? You have Roman Reigns and Cody Rhodes, and what they do looks scary. But they ended up being the sweetest people. They’re such puppies in the best way, and they were super nice to hang around with on set. And Orville Peck has become one of my best friends after filming this whole thing together. David [Dastmalchian] is a real-life vampire, for sure, but in the best way. It was magnificent working with him and diving into the psychology of Bison and Chun-Li. We got to do some of the more serious stuff, which excited me a lot personally. But it was a crazy set. You had your crazy uncles and aunties and cousins, and it genuinely felt like one big, crazy family. Callina Liang’s Chun-Li in Street Fighter Paramount Pictures There’s an amazing sight gag in this film after Chun-Li does some drunken nunchucking. She goes to take a shower, and just as she’s about to be revealed, the movie match-cuts to E. Honda’s exposed upper body. Was this gag scripted carefully so that you knew what to expect? ( Laughs. ) It was scripted from day one. Kitao sent me a mock-up about a week before we filmed it, showing exactly how they were planning to shoot it, including the push-in and reveal of E. Honda’s big chest. I was made to feel very comfortable from the start, and I knew exactly what I was stepping into on the day. So I was very happy to do it because it’s such an iconic scene from Street Fighter II: The Animated Movie . As a fan myself, that’s probably my favorite movie in the franchise, so I was like, “We’ve got to add that Easter egg in there.” And now it’s gotten big laughs at all the screenings. Audiences have loved it. Even I laughed when I first saw it. Chun-Li is an undercover Interpol officer, and she infiltrates M. Bison’s organization as part of her long-running effort to avenge her father’s murder at his hand. She then brands herself with his Shadaloo symbol to prove her loyalty. Did they do anything on the day to give you some kind of sensation you could play off? No, actually. That scene used to be something else. I don’t know if I’m allowed to say this, but the movie is out now, so it should be fine. Chun-Li was originally supposed to chop off a finger, but Capcom … They went back and forth with the script, and eventually they decided that hand-branding was the better way to do it. I remember testing that scene during the camera test. I tried it, and I thought, It’s a lot. She’s about to physically hurt herself . But Kitao kept going, “More, more, more. I want to see it in her eyes. She’s almost shaking.” And I was like, “Alright, say less.” So, on the day, I mentally channeled whatever pain I could into what was happening physically. But I wish there had been something to help me feel that sensation. It was all just stone-cold acting. There was a lot of rigamarole with the studio over Keanu Reeves, as John Wick, cutting off a finger in the John Wick series, so that’s an interesting yet familiar story. I wonder if that’s where the inspiration came from. If she had no pinky for the rest of the [potential series], it would be deforming the character in a way. But regardless, I think the hand-branding worked, and it was very fun to play. Kitao told me that the reasoning came down to the source material being too substantial to cram it all into one movie, but were you disappointed at all that Chun-Li didn’t get to take out M. Bison in this film? Oh, man. Honestly, a little bit. The whole film, especially Chun-Li’s storyline, builds toward Chun-Li’s final takedown of Bison. But there’s a reason for everything, and hopefully, if we get a sequel one day, we’ll get to explore that. I’m sure it’d be epic. Callina Liang’s Chun-Li and David Dastmalchian’s Lord M. Bison in Street Fighter Courtesy of Paramount Pictures And Legendary Pictures You made a good point elsewhere that if she does kill him, who is she after that? She’s devoted her entire life toward this one mission. Exactly. That’s another part of her storyline and character arc I’d be interested to explore. Whenever I went into my scenes with Bison in this film, I had to tap into this weird mental state of hating him so much, but finding comfort in knowing exactly what Chun-Li needed to do, who she hated and what her mission was. Even in the moments before she brands herself, he says, “There’s a deep sadness in you and also a great potential.” I almost felt emotional as her during those moments. It’s almost the first time anyone has truly seen Chun-Li for who she is, so there’s a weird sense of emotional support in that moment. After she brands herself, he brings her up close to the painting of himself, which is hilarious. She could have easily chosen to attack him when he hands her the knife while standing that close to him, but she chose not to. So that’s really interesting to think about because she probably didn’t want her mission to end just yet. She was probably afraid to confront what would come for her, mentally, once it was all over. So I 100 percent don’t know how she’d feel after finally accomplishing Bison’s death. Maybe you weren’t there for David Dastmalchian’s coverage after Bison hits Chun-Li with the Psycho Crusher, but was there a lot of pomp and circumstance around his “Tuesday” homage to Raul Julia as he walks from her? Oh my gosh, absolutely. It’s the most iconic line ever. Even before filming started, we were all saying, “We’ve got to put that line in there somehow. We’ve got to find the right moment.” Then I saw the dailies where he delivered that line, and I was like, “Damn, that’s the one.” It was so satisfying to watch, and then it became a thing the rest of the shoot. He shot the line earlier on in the filming process, and every day afterwards, whenever we’d see each other, I’d be like, “Yeah, I’m going to kill you today.” I was just gearing up to fight him. But David was like, “Hey, it’s just a Tuesday for me.” So that iconic line became an ongoing joke between us. Callina Liang’s Chun-Li and Kyle Mooney’s Marvin in Street Fighter Courtesy of Paramount Pictures And Legendary Pictures Decades from now, when you look back on this experience, what day will you likely recall first? The one day that always stands out to me was when we filmed on that beautiful cliffside in Sydney. Chun-Li invites Dhalsim to the tournament, and it was just truly so beautiful. I could not believe we were filming at a location like that. After the part on the rocks, where Dhalism and his soldiers are doing their thing, we moved on to another oceanside cliff where the chopper is. Chun-Li has this crazy fight sequence with three of her Interpol bosses, and then kicking [Kyle Mooney’s] Marvin in the balls was the end of that day. So it was such a beautiful day. I got to fight three guys, kick another one in the balls and drive off in a van. It was a great day. I’ll never forget it. I wonder if it was a Tuesday. It might have been a Tuesday! *** Street Fighter is now playing in movie theaters . THR

articles.title: Hannah Einbinder Says Speaking Out for Palestine Is “the Bare Minimum”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All October 23, 2026 7:12pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Hannah Einbinder at The New Yorker Festival on Friday night in Manhattan. Craig Barritt/Getty Images for The New Yorker As she became increasingly well-known during her acclaimed five-season run alongside Jean Smart in HBO Max’s Hacks , Hannah Einbinder has used her time in the spotlight to speak out on various political and social issues she’s passionate about from climate change to AI to, most prominently in recent years, the fate of the Palestinian people amid the Israel -Gaza war. She famously called for a “free Palestine ” at the end of her 2025 Emmys acceptance speech and was arrested last month , along with other pro-Palestinian Hollywood activists like Susan Sarandon , as part of a protest ahead of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu‘s United Nations address. Related Stories Movies How Pat McAfee Landed His First Acting Role in 'The Mosquito Bowl' -- With Some Help From Bradley Cooper and Tom Cruise News Meghan Markle Says She's Kept Her Children From Her Father "to Protect Them" In Wake of Child Abuse Image Allegations While some celebs might choose to stay silent about their political views, for Einbinder, there’s no alternative. “I see it as the bare minimum,” Einbinder said at The New Yorker Festival on Friday of the “responsibility” she feels to speak out about her beliefs. “I think we are living in a time that is perhaps the worst point in human history. I think the threat of AI and climate [change] push us into that territory. And I know how many eyes I have on me. I know that difference that it can make. I know it from a financial perspective. I know that I can raise money. I have done it, and so I know that folks like myself and folks with even larger platforms can make tangible difference in the world. And for me, that’s been very specific to Palestine, and so knowing that, I don’t really see any other option.” Einbinder, who has previously spoken about how her views on Israel and Palestine have evolved since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attack on Israel, shared more about her recent education and perspective on the Israel-Gaza war at the New Yorker Festival event. “I started to attend IfNotNow vigils with my friends who were going, who were already anti-Zionists, and I found this amazing Jewish community and these Jewish spaces for me to go on a journey of unlearning the propaganda that we’re fed systemically,” Einbinder told The New Yorker ‘s Rachel Syme. “And once I unlearned all of that, I realized I had to arm myself with a lot of knowledge and really go through, yeah, sort of a relearning period, and when I felt equipped, you know, I started to speak because I think when you see this for what it is, you cannot help — well, some people can, I guess. But I think that it was just so intrinsically tied to my values and my sense of justice, and I felt like I have to make up for lost time because I was complicit and unconscious in this system for so long, and I have to change my mind and I have to learn and grow, and so that’s what I’ve tried to do.” And Einbinder praised the “amazing new voices” she’d been exposed to coming out of Palestine, specifically citing Al Jazeera journalist Anas al-Sharif, who was killed in an Israeli air strike in August of 2025. “There are these scenes that I think of that I saw happen when I think of him,” Einbinder recalled to a silent, sold-out audience at Manhattan’s Webster Hall who seemed to be listening intently as she spoke about her views on the conflict in the Middle East. “I feel like I watched this man’s life unfold, and Israel assassinated him. They knew that he and other journalists were sleeping in a tent, and they killed him because his voice was so powerful, and he had a beautiful daughter and a newborn son, and he risked his life to tell the truth about Israel’s crimes, and he was killed for that, and he was killed for being Palestinian.” In light of what happened to al-Sharif, Einbinder says any loss or “sacrifice” that she would experience for speaking out in support of Palestine pales in comparison. “When I speak about Palestine, when I say it’s the bare minimum, there is nothing on earth that I could ever lose or ever sacrifice. It would be a drop in the bucket to measure up to the most incredible human beings I have ever witnessed in my life and the sacrifices that they have made, so I want to draw attention to journalists like Anas and so many like him who were silenced. We are still here, and we have an obligation to tell their stories,” Einbinder said. “All of us have a responsibility, especially as Americans who are complicit as taxpayers whose money goes to fund the genocide. We have a responsibility to speak and not to stop until the genocide is ended.” Einbinder’s remarks were greeted with enthusiastic applause, including at least one person in the audience standing up after her “genocide” comment. Earlier in the event, Einbinder spoke about discovering comedy (and competitive cheerleading ) as she grew up in Los Angeles and her breakout role in Hacks , offering some constructive criticism as the festival audience watched her memorable Branzino meltdown during the fourth season of the comedy, when she served as head writer for Smart’s Deborah Vance-hosted Late Night . She also got emotional watching a more dramatic scene between Ava and Deborah near the end of the final season . Einbinder also spoke about her recent role opposite Gillian Anderson in Jane Schoenbrun’s Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma . THR

articles.title: Quentin Tarantino Shows Off First 17 Minutes of ‘Cliff Booth’ and Explains Decision to Revive Character
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All October 24, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Quentin Tarantino attends the AFI screening of 'Once Upon A Time In Hollywood' at TCL Chinese Theatre on Oct. 23. Michael Kovac/Getty Images for AFI Quentin Tarantino had quite a surprise in store on Friday night. The filmmaker made an appearance at AFI Fest in Los Angeles for a screening of Once Upon a Time in Hollywood , sitting down for a Q&A afterwards about his hit movie. But just as the night seemed to be wrapping up, Tarantino surprised the crowd at the TCL Chinese Theater with a first look at The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , showing off the first 17 minutes of the follow-up film . Tarantino wrote the script for Cliff Booth , with David Fincher stepping in to direct this time around. The new project sees Brad Pitt reprise his Oscar-winning role as stunt double Booth, and is set in 1977, eight years after the events of Once Upon a Time . Related Stories Movies 'Street Fighter' Director Kitao Sakurai Built a Career by Embracing the Ridiculous Movies Brad Pitt's 'Cliff Booth' Reveals Action-Packed Scenes in New Tease Ahead of Netflix Launch Before showing off the footage — which saw Booth working as a cinema projectionist while handling some more unsavory business on the side — Tarantino explained his decision to revisit the character in the first place. “I tend to not remember good reviews of mine in quotes; I kind of remember the bad reviews in quotes, but I don’t really remember good reviews of mine in quotes. But one quote that I do remember somebody writing about Once Upon a Time in Hollywood , it was like, ‘This seems like the first world Quentin Tarantino has ever created that he would like to live in,’ and there is that aspect,” he told the crowd. “I loved the Cliff Booth character, I loved the way that Brad played him, and there was this aspect of him as sort of like a paperback hero. I could see like a series of paperbacks with Cliff Booth getting involved with this adventure or that adventure or something like that.” Tarantino continued, “As time went on, I just thought about coming up with a different adventure, getting him in now a misadventure. I wanted to see what would happen with that.” He also noted how immersed he has become in the film’s world — having also written a Once Upon a Time novel — and explained, “I’ve got nothing to do but just invest in this mythology. I invested in it before I did the movie, and then I invested in it in the years since I’ve done the movie, just so I know the mythology. The audience doesn’t need to know everything, but it’s kind of nice that I know everything, and you can trust me that I know it.” During the conversation Tarantino also revealed that “if I’m going to watch any of my movies, it would be this one,” and it’s a film that he can watch again and again. He added, “Don’t get me wrong, I love my stories. I really, really love my stories, and I invest in my stories. But I kind of like that this doesn’t really have a story. I like that you’re just hanging out with them.” About to head into rehearsals for his upcoming play , Tarantino explained his current mindset is of being a writer first, as was put into action with opting not to direct Cliff Booth . “As I’m getting older, being a man of letters is more my thing,” he noted, “so screenplays and books and plays — everything except poetry.” The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is releasing in IMAX on Nov. 25 and streaming Dec. 23 on Netflix. THR

articles.title: Ken Atchity, ‘The Meg’ Producer and Literary Agent, Dies at 82
articles.full_text: Oct 23, 2026 5:59pm PT Ken Atchity, ‘The Meg’ Producer and Literary Agent, Dies at 82 By Tanya Fedak Plus Icon Tanya Fedak Latest Michael Gray, Star of ‘Shazam!’ TV Series, Dies at 75 2 days ago Chaka Khan to Be Honored at Soul Train Awards (TV News Roundup) 2 days ago ‘Paper Tiger’ Producer Rodrigo Teixeira Set for GLAFF’s First Visionary Award, Presented by Wagner Moura (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Kenneth Atchity, “ The Meg ” producer and literary agent, died on Monday. He was 82. Across his career as a literary manager, producer and writer, Atchity produced more than 30 films; wrote over 20 books; negotiated publishing and entertainment deals; and published hundreds of additional titles through his own imprint, Story Merchant Books. In addition to producing “The Meg” films with his business and producing partner Chi-Li Wong, he had credits on “Gambino,” “The Kennedy Detail,” “The Lost Valentine,” “The Amityville Horror: The Evil Escapes , ” “Joe Somebody” and “Life Or Something Like It.” Related Stories David Zaslav Bids Farewell to Warner Bros. Employees in Video on Eve of Skydance Merger Close: 'It's Been a Great Honor to Be Alongside All of You' Comcast Q3 Sees Continued Broadband Downturn, Despite Boosts From World Cup, Peacock Prior to working in Hollywood, Atchity served as an assistant professor of English and comparative literature at Occidental College before earning tenure and becoming a full-time professor. During his 17 years at the college, he became a Fulbright professor of American literature at the University of Bologna; founded and edited two magazines; and was awarded Occidental’s faculty achievement award and the UCLA Writers Program’s distinguished instructor award. Popular on Variety Atchity also worked as a communication engineer at AT&T Long Lines, where he designed and implemented the Green Network, which connects NASA’s 26 research centers. He decided to change careers to produce “Shades of Love,” a set of 16 films which were broadcast on HBO and Cinemax and were internationally distributed by Warner Bros.. Born in Eunice, La., in 1944, Atchity was raised in Kansas City, Mo., and attended Georgetown University before entering Yale as a Woodrow Wilson Fellow, where he earned a masters in philosophy and a PhD. While there, his doctoral dissertation won the John Addison Porter prize, the university’s highest academic award, and was published with an introduction by novelist John Gardner. Atchity is survived by his wife, Kayoko Mitsumatsu; his son, Vincent Atchity; his daughter, Rosemary Atchity; his five grandchildren, Margaret D. McKenna, Edward J. McKenna, Oliver D. Atchity, Eliot J. Atchity and Louis M. Atchity; and his sisters, Mary Calhoun and Laurie Dressman.. Donations may be made to Yoga Gives Back , an organization empowering women and children in India which Atchity served on the board for. articles.title: Bill Maher’s Embarrassing Karoline Leavitt Interview on ‘Real Time’
articles.full_text: Oct 23, 2026 7:27pm PT Bill Maher’s Embarrassing Karoline Leavitt Interview on ‘Real Time’ By Marlow Stern Plus Icon Marlow Stern Chief Correspondent Latest Shaquille O’Neal’s Advice for NBA Phenom Victor Wembanyama: ‘Be Meaner’ 4 days ago Inside ‘The New Stanford Prison Experiment,’ Netflix’s Controversial Reality Series: ‘People Are Going to Have Very Strong Feelings’ (EXCLUSIVE) 6 days ago 50 Cent Opens Up About Diddy’s Secret Smear Campaign Against Him, Why He Won’t Work With Courtney Kemp Again and Learning His Mom Was Gay: ‘I’m Not Ashamed of That in Any Way’ 7 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty/HBO Bill Maher appears to be on good terms with Trumpworld. The 70-year-old HBO host joined Kid Rock and Stephen A. Smith as President Trump’s White House dinner guests earlier this month, and, following the dinner, Trump intimated to reporters that Maher’s criticisms of him on his late-night program are mostly bluster, and he “likes me a lot more than people understand.” “Yeah, I did it again, bitches,” Maher said about his four-hour dinner with Trump during his opening monologue on “Real Time” Friday night , adding, “You know what? Fuck you. I like these dinners.” Related Stories David Zaslav Gets $606 Million Payout From Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Netflix Q3 Revenue Meets Wall Street Estimates, Forecasts Q4 Slowdown and Says It Will Miss Ad Sales Target for the Year Maher then managed to land Karoline Leavitt , Trump’s former press secretary who left the post in August, as an interview guest on his show “Real Time.” It’s a curious pairing given that Maher had previously attacked Leavitt on his program following the then-press secretary’s defense of Trump shouting, “Quiet, piggy!” to Bloomberg News reporter Catherine Lucey when she questioned him about Jeffrey Epstein aboard Air Force One. Leavitt spun the incident by claiming, “It’s actually admirable. It’s the president being frank, open, and honest. It’s actually good,’” prompting Maher to jokingly remark to Leavitt, “Well, in that case: Shut up, bitch .” Popular on Variety And so, Maher welcomed Leavitt to “Real Time” Friday night where he mostly treated her with kid gloves and poked fun at her successor, Katie Zacharia, for only lasting five days on the job. “The president sends his regards,” Leavitt told Maher. “I told him I was coming on the show and he said, ‘Tell him he loved that dinner and he knows it.’” “I do like it,” Maher admitted, before turning the talk back to Leavitt. “You were the youngest one to do this job… So what are you going to do now?” Leavitt said she left the job to take care of her two young children, who are 2 and six months, and then said she’ll be starting as a Fox News pundit on Nov. 1. No follow-up from Maher about the Trump-Fox News pipeline, but instead a silly rejoinder about how Trump wants to turn the White House press pool into an actual swimming pool. Cue Maher: “You know what? This is the one thing that people get mad at me [about]… I don’t give a shit about any of this. I like the ballroom! America does need a ballroom. It’s the United States of America.” The softball questions and flattery didn’t stop there, as Maher asked Leavitt about her penchant for being “sarcastic” and didn’t ask any follow-up questions when she touted Trump’s war with Iran. Maher delivered a litany of compliments about Trump, saying he “gets it” and, when Leavitt claimed Trump was “far more sane than the last [president]” who was “a mental patient,” Maher replied, “He’s far more energetic.” It’s another reminder that Maher isn’t a journalist and refuses to challenge the conservative guests on his show. He’s just happy for them to be there. articles.title: Vino G. Bastian, Pevita Pearce, Faradina Mufti, Indra Jegel Lead ‘Miracle in Cell No. 7’ Director Lee Hwan-kyung’s Indonesian Father-Son Drama ‘Gasigogi’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Oct 24, 2026 12:00am PT Vino G. Bastian, Pevita Pearce, Faradina Mufti, Indra Jegel Lead ‘Miracle in Cell No. 7’ Director Lee Hwan-kyung’s Indonesian Father-Son Drama ‘Gasigogi’ (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Kore-eda Hirokazu Explains Why He Never Films Children Crying – and What Ken Loach and Hou Hsiao-hsien Taught Him 4 hours ago Vino G. Bastian, Pevita Pearce, Faradina Mufti, Indra Jegel Lead ‘Miracle in Cell No. 7’ Director Lee Hwan-kyung’s Indonesian Father-Son Drama ‘Gasigogi’ (EXCLUSIVE) 6 hours ago Kartik Aaryan’s ‘Captain India’ Set Amid Houthi Conflict in Yemen (EXCLUSIVE) 11 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Fac Korean filmmaker Lee Hwan-kyung , director of “Miracle in Cell No. 7,” has assembled an Indonesian ensemble led by Vino G. Bastian , Pevita Pearce, Faradina Mufti and Indra Jegel for “ Gasigogi ,” a father-son drama now in production with Falcon Pictures. The film follows Jiwa, a father who sacrifices everything in a fight to save Juna, his son, who has blood cancer. Bastian plays the lead, with Pearce as co-lead and Mufti as Chitra. Falcon Pictures unveiled the cast together with Hwantasy Entertainment. Related Stories Comcast Q3 Sees Continued Broadband Downturn, Despite Boosts From World Cup, Peacock David Zaslav Bids Farewell to Warner Bros. Employees in Video on Eve of Skydance Merger Close: 'It's Been a Great Honor to Be Alongside All of You' Bastian starred in the Indonesian remake of “Miracle in Cell No. 7,” while Pearce is known for “5 cm” and Mufti for “Impetigore.” The supporting cast includes Altaaf Akavi (“Tunggu Aku Sukses Nanti”), Indro Warkop (“Miracle in Cell No. 7”), Dea Panendra (“Marlina the Murderer in Four Acts”), Sadana Agung (“Agak Laen”), Irma Novita Rihi (“Women From Rote Island”), Luisa Adreena (“Na Willa”), Pritt Timothy (“Ayah, Aku Mau Cerita”), Verdi Solaiman (“The Raid”) and Kiki Narendra (“Ghost in the Cell”). Popular on Variety The working title takes its inspiration from the stickleback fish. The male of the species remains alone with the eggs and fights off predators until his body gives out, at which point his flesh becomes the hatchlings’ first food. Lee uses the image as a metaphor for fatherhood and the sacrifices parents make for their children. The project marks Lee’s return to directing following the success of the Indonesian version of his earlier phenomenon, and he has called it the most emotionally taxing film he has taken on. He made “Miracle in Cell No. 7” as a gift for his daughter. “Gasigogi” is dedicated to his son. By shooting in Indonesia, Lee wants to draw on the country’s strong attachment to family, faith and community. He said the film is an original work rather than a transplant of Korean feeling, one that “breathes with Indonesian lungs.” “Just as a father gives everything to his child, I want to pour everything I have into creating a precious gift for this family,” Lee said. “The name of that gift is ‘Gasigogi.’ The goal is simple: I want to create a film so honest and resonant that when the credits roll, the first thing the audience wants to do is call their father.” “To be trusted with a story of this magnitude is both an incredible honor and a tremendous emotional challenge,” Bastian added. “Director Lee has crafted a raw, devastating, and beautiful narrative about what a father will endure for his child.” Mufti said she was grateful to Falcon and Lee for entrusting her with Chitra. “As a mother myself, this story feels very close to my heart,” she said. “It reminds me that love isn’t always expressed through words, but often through the things we do and the sacrifices we make for our children.” Falcon producer Frederica added, “The unparalleled dedication of our brilliant cast and crew, combined with Director Lee’s masterful storytelling, makes ‘Gasigogi’ a truly special project. articles.title: Impulso Morelia: Tatiana Huezo’s ‘Galerna’ Takes Top José María Riba Award, With ‘Homeboys’ Another Key Winner
articles.full_text: Oct 24, 2026 1:33am PT Impulso Morelia: Tatiana Huezo’s ‘Galerna’ Takes Top José María Riba Award, With ‘Homeboys’ Another Key Winner Winning Morelia's prestigious Works in Progress competition, 'Galerna,' from 'Roma' producer Pimienta Films and Spain's Elastica Films, presents its credentials for big fest selection in 2027 By Anna Marie de la Fuente Plus Icon Anna Marie de la Fuente @adelafuente1 Latest Morelia Film Festival Prizes: ‘Six Months in a Pink and Blue Building,’ an ‘Expression of Pure, Unbound Beauty,’ Wins Top ‘Ojo’ Award 11 minutes ago Impulso Morelia: Tatiana Huezo’s ‘Galerna’ Takes Top José María Riba Award, With ‘Homeboys’ Another Key Winner 4 hours ago Cinépolis Distribution Lands ‘5 More Minutes,’ a Time-Warping Thriller Starring ‘Talk to Her’ Lead Javier Cámara (EXCLUSIVE) 21 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Galerna' Courtesy of San Sebastian Festival “Galerna,” a fiction feature from Mexico’s Tatiana Huezo , has snagged the top prize at Impulso Morelia, the pix-in-post industry section of the 10-day Morelia Film Festival , which wraps Oct. 25. The José Maria Riba Award, presented by Cinépolis Distribution and Profest 2026, bestows $14,740. (250,000 pesos) toward outstanding post-production needs and/or promotional activities. Only her second fiction outing, following “Prayers for the Stolen,” Huezo first received critical acclaim for her documentaries, led by “Tempestad” and “The Tiniest Place,” both produced by Pimienta Films (“Roma”). “Galerna” recently won the coveted Egeda Platino Industria Award at the San Sebastian Festival where it participated in the festival’s WIP Latin America competition showcase. Popular on Variety Related Stories How David Ellison Won the Battle: Timeline of Paramount's Rocky Road to Acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery Warner Bros. Studios Leavesden Revenues Climb 11% to $390 Million Thanks to ‘Harry Potter’ Tour, Increased Production (EXCLUSIVE) The road movie follows two casting directors into the remote reaches of Mexico, where their search for natural actors for a sci-fi film becomes an unsettling journey into their own fears, biases and preconceptions. Following close behind with a Special Mention from the panel and a post-production award in kind from Caffeine was “Homeboys,” a documentary by Alonso Garibay and Alejandro Bernal which centers on Roberto Hernández, “Mr. Lucky,” who was deported to a country he barely knew and who later founded a shelter for those with similar experiences. “Homeboys” also took home the Eugenio Polgovsky award of $5,340.83 (100,000 pesos), created in memory of the beloved filmmaker. “Tatiana’s ‘Galerna’ represents a new exciting direction for one of the best filmmakers working today, and I’m certain it will be a watershed moment in Mexico cinema when it is finally released to the public. I couldn’t be more thrilled than it is being recognized with the top prize. This year’s selection was fantastic, and I’m sure we’ll see these films succeed with audiences and critics,” said Piano ’s Julio Chavezmontes, one of the jurors in the international panel. “On a personal note, it was deeply moving to see the inaugural Eugenio Polgovsky award go to “Homeboys”. This is a film that shares Eugenio’s fearless humanism, and I have no doubt he would have championed it, if he was still with us today,” said Chavezmontes. For fellow juror Mauricio Durán Ortega, president of National Film Industry Chamber, Canacine, “Impulso’s selection was outstanding, as always.” “All the projects deserved support and having a film reach that stage is already a major achievement. The award makes a real difference in helping filmmakers complete their work. Since most projects are already in post-production, our recommendations focus on what can still be refined. This year, the decision was unanimous – ‘Galerna’ stood out so clearly that no further debate was needed.” Post-production house Caffeine, selected “Galerna,” “All the Water in the World” and “Homeboys” to receive in-kind services valued at over $20,000 (387,000 pesos) in total. For Caffeine CEO Adrian Geyer, all three “show the range of Mexican cinema right now.” “Tatiana Huezo’s road movie takes us down paths that feel supernatural without ever becoming so, with images that tell so much they let us travel alongside the characters; Diego del Río and Diana Bracho’s ‘All the Water in the World’ dares to explore aging and family from a place Mexican cinema rarely goes, with an honesty that unsettles us because it confronts us, as viewers, with ourselves; and Alonso Garibay and Alejandro Bernal’s ‘Homeboys’ gives a voice, in their debut documentary, to people both countries have tried to forget.” Fernanda Garduño of Estudios Splendor Omnia chose documentaries “Raká,” and “Katechon” as winners of its in-kind services at the studios’ facilities in Tepoztlán, Morelos, which are valid for two years. “I chose Teresa Camou’s “Raká” for its sensitive direction, intimate storytelling and striking images. By letting its subjects speak for themselves without imposing judgments, the film offers a poetic view of alternative ways of life. Support for sound design will help bring its full potential to life.” For Garduño, Javier Toscano’s “Katechon” stands out for its “compelling portrayal of hope as a disciplined way of life rather than a cliché. Despite some familiar documentary tropes, its exceptional archival footage and creative storytelling make it visually distinctive and deserving of the award to support its color grading and finalization.” The 12 th Impulso Morelia unspooled Oct. 18-20 during the festival. Below are the prizewinners. INTERNATIONAL PANEL Jurors: Cara Cusumano, Carlos Rodríguez Ríos, Julio Chavezmontes, Mauricio Durán and Sandrine Dumas José Marià Riba Award “Galerna,” Tatiana Huezo (Pimienta Films, Elastica Films ) Special Mention “Homeboys,” Alonso Garibay and Alejandro Bernal (Norteña del Sur, Documotora) AMBULANTE–EUGENIO POLGOVSKY AWARD “Homeboys,” Alonso Garibay and Alejandro Bernal (Norteña del Sur, Documotora) CHURUBUSCO AWARD, image and post services in kind split evenly between two projects “Legit, Elisa Miller (Pimienta Films, UMI Films). “All the Water in the World (“Toda el agua del mundo,”Diego del Río) SPLENDOR OMNIA STUDIOS AWARD “Raká,”Teresa Camou (Fontana Films, Oriente Cine) “Katechon,”Javier Toscano (Didascalia Films) CAFFEINE POST-PRODUCTION AWARDS “Galerna,” Tatiana Huezo (Pimienta Films, Elastica Films) “Toda el agua del mundo,”Diego del Río “Homeboys,”Alonso Garibay and Alejandro Bernal (Norteña del Sur, Documotora) LATAM CINEMA AWARD “Galerna,” Tatiana Huezo (Pimienta Films, Elastica Films) A digital magazine ad and communications and press outreach consultancy valued at approximately $2,000.
