articles.title: Empire Founder Ghazi Launches Supply Chain, New Rights Management/ Distribution Company for Independent Music
articles.full_text: Oct 21, 2026 7:00am PT Empire Founder Ghazi Launches Supply Chain, New Rights Management/ Distribution Company for Independent Music By Jem Aswad Plus Icon Jem Aswad Executive Editor, Music jemaswad Latest Music Industry Moves: Barbara Cane, BMI’s VP of Worldwide Creative, to Retire After Five Decades 16 hours ago Cleo Sol Announces First-Ever North American Arena Tour Dates 24 hours ago Bob Buziak, Former President of RCA Records and Sony’s Tristar Music Group, Dies at 83 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ghazi , founder of the indie label and distribution giant Empire , has announced the launch of his newest company, Supply Chain, an independent B2B cloud-based distribution company for the global music industry, which encapsulates technology, distribution, operations, and commercial connectivity. Alongside the launch, the company announced two senior leadership appointments, with Craig May joining as SVP of marketing and Kristy May as SVP of business affairs. Supply Chain’s international headquarters are based in Amsterdam, one of Europe’s most-connected music and technology hubs. According to the announcement, the company’s goal is a huge one: to build the infrastructure that independent music runs on. “Its mission is to deliver the technology, expertise and commercial access needed to operate, grow and compete globally, in service of a broader vision of a world where independent music has the power to shape its own future,” the announcement reads. “The platform gives independent music businesses neutral, enterprise-grade infrastructure without requiring them to give up control of their catalog, data, client relationships or commercial choices.” Supply Chain launched in beta in 2025 and is now operational globally. Supply Chain is working with a variety of clients across the industry ecosystem, including a launch partnership with Beatport-owned Ampsuite, to power infrastructure expansion. Popular on Variety “There needs to be a fully fleshed-out rights management system that is also culturally nuanced,” Ghazi tells Variety. “The needs of an independent label in Brazil are not the same as an artist in India, which are not the same as a private equity company that’s invested $500 million in catalogs. Supply Chain can manage contracts, master royalties, publishing royalties, merch royalties, split payments and more. “It’s been a labor of love for five years,” he continues. “I wanted to build something as scale-able and as future-proof as possible. It introduces a lot of operational efficiencies and reduces tech friction, and when you do all that, you’re allowing creativity to flourish. Our software is built for independents and it’s designed to connect and serve the independent community.” Beatport CEO Matt Gralen says, “Ampsuite offers the most complete set of tools for the labels that power Beatport, but we are always looking to provide more and respond to evolution in the industry. articles.title: Kari Skogland To Direct Vigilante Crime Thriller ‘Vigilant’ From ‘Severance’ Star Ólafur Darri Ólafsson
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart Kari Skogland To Direct Vigilante Crime Thriller ‘Vigilant’ From ‘Severance’ Star Ólafur Darri Ólafsson Christie Brinkley Opens Personal Archive With Never-Before-Seen Home Movies For ‘Uptown Girl’ Docuseries Lance Armstrong On Schwinn Bicycles Documentary ‘No Hands’: “It’s An Incredible American Story” View All October 21, 2026 2:03am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Kari Skogland & Ólafur Darri Ólafsson David Leyes, Jonatan Gretarsson EXCLUSIVE: Kari Skogland will direct Vigilant , a vigilante crime thriller based on a Skúli Sigurðsson novel and adapted for TV by Severance star Ólafur Darri Ólafsson . The project is a big-ticket European co-production and has been greenlit by Icelandic production company ACT4 alongside German broadcaster ZDF and its distribution division ZDF Studios . Iceland’s Siminn is also on board. ZDF Studios will sell the English-language show internationally. Zero Gravity is handling U.S. sales. Vigilant follows a female journalist who is approached by a self-styled vigilante who is waging a violent campaign against sexual predators. The reporter initially sees him as a voice for the voiceless, but soon begins to suspect a darker truth. As her reporting fuels a nationwide debate, the series explores whether violence can ever be justified when the justice system fails. Related Stories News Buyers Move For German Crime Drama 'SOKO' As ZDF Studios Brings Classic & YA Series To Cannes News Icelandic Drama 'Elma' Set For Siminn Bow As Glassriver Debuts 'NCU' At MIPCOM Ólafur is a partner in ACT4 and starred in Severance . He has adapted Sigurðsson’s novel ‘Stóri bróðir’ (‘Big Brother’ in English) for TV. Víkingur Kristjánsson, Anita Briem, Teitur Magnússon and Anna Gunndís Guðmundsdóttir are co-writers, meaning a powerhouse Icelandic creative team. Watch on Deadline “Skúli’s novel had a profound impact on me when I first read it,” Ólafur said. “Beneath the thriller, I found a story asking difficult questions about justice, anger and what happens when people lose faith in the systems meant to protect them. “I’m incredibly proud of the scripts we’ve created, and I can’t wait to see Kari bring this world and these characters to life with her extraordinary vision, alongside the incredible cast and creative team we’ve assembled.” Skogland’s many directing credits include The Handmaid’s Tale , The Walking Dead and Vikings . She will also executive produce the six-part series. “ Vigilant captivated me from the first page,” she said. “The characters walk their own lines of morality that continually makes the audience question their own moral position. Everyone’s damage is exposed at some point, their fragility and strength are tested in this fantastic landscape for thought-provoking performance opportunities, all while wrapped in a nail-biting thriller.” “ Vigilant is exactly the kind of premium international drama that resonates across borders: a compelling thriller rooted in a highly relevant societal dilemma,” said Rodrigo Herrera Ibarguengoytia, Director Drama, ZDF Studios. “The series combines Iceland’s distinctive storytelling tradition with universal themes that will connect with audiences worldwide.” Production kicks off on October 29 in Iceland, where the drama is set. ZDF will have the show for Germany and Iceland’s Siminn, which has an IPTV and streaming service, has local rights. Katharina Kremling, Commissioning Editor at ZDF, said: “As an international co-production partner, we are proud to collaborate with ACT4, ZDF Studios and Síminn in bringing this ambitious and distinctive project to the screen and to our German audience.” Ryan Murphy’s ‘Glee’ Reboot Lands Series Order At Disney+ & Hulu Bayona & Bardem Team On Doc About Spanish Cinematographer Q3 Earnings Ding Stock; Sarandos Praises Bajaria, Talks Up Rice; More Takeaways Denzel Washington And Christopher McQuarrie Teaming On New Thriller At UA, Amazon Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Hiam Abbass To Receive Honorary European Film Academy Award
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Watermelon Pictures Acquires North American Distribution Rights To Sara Ishaq’s ‘The Station’ Hiam Abbass To Receive Honorary European Film Academy Award J. A. Bayona, Javier Bardem & Laurent Bouzereau Partner On Movistar Plus Doc About Life Of Legendary Spanish Cinematographer Néstor Almendros View All October 21, 2026 2:24am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Hiam Abbass Deadline Hiam Abbass is set to receive the European Film Academy ’s honorary award for European Achievement in World Cinema. Abbass will be handed the award at the 39th European Film Awards on 16 January 2027 in Athens. She will be the ceremony’s honorary guest. Abbass was born in Nazareth, the child of a Palestinian family that was forced into exile in 1948. She began her acting career at the Palestinian National Theatre El-Hakawati in East Jerusalem, which was often closed by the Israeli authorities. During a theatre tour through Europe, she decided to leave Palestine for London and has been living in Paris since the late 1980s. Related Stories News 'La Bola Negra', 'Woman Unknown', 'NAZA' & 'Fjord' Among 68 Films On Shortlist For 39th European Film Awards Festivals 'Succession' Star Hiam Abbass On How She Had "Real" Connections Working With Kenneth Branagh & Boyd Holbrook On 'Atonement' - TIFF Abbass played her first lead role in 1989 in La nuit miraculeuse directed by Ariane Mnouchkine. She has since acted in over 100 films, including Satin Rouge by Raja Amari, Paradise Now by Hany Abu-Assad, The Visitor by Tom McCarthy, and Denis Villeneuve’s Blade Runner 2049 . Watch on Deadline Abbass has been nominated twice for European Film Awards, in both cases for her performance in films directed by Eran Riklis: She was nominated for the People’s Choice Award 2005 for Syrian Bride and for European Actress 2008 for Lemon Tree , which won her an Asia Pacific Screen Award. Her daughter Lina Soualem’s documentary Bye Bye Tiberias , which returns to her home village Deir Hanna and explores her bold choices and her bond to her family, was also nominated for the European Film Awards 2024. Alongside her work as an actress, Hiam Abbass also directs. Her film Inheritance was screened at Gijón, São Paulo, and Venice Days (2012). articles.title: Jane Tranter Calls For “Stories That Change The Lack Of Empathy In Our World” & Reveals How James Gandolfini Influenced Bad Wolf
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Jane Tranter Calls For “Stories That Change The Lack Of Empathy In Our World” & Reveals How James Gandolfini Influenced Bad Wolf Prime Video Adds Sony LIV To Indian Offer Ex-Disney, NBCU & Bloomberg TV Execs Among New Advisory Board At Storyboarding Platform Pzaz View All October 21, 2026 3:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jane Tranter on stage at the MIA Market in Rome MIA The Other Bennet Sister producer Jane Tranter has launched an impassioned plea for TV makers to search out stories that “that will make our world a more empathetic place.” In a keynote talk at MIA Market this week, the Bad Wolf Production CEO and co-founder used the example of a “farmer in his 70s” who had identified with Mary, the outcast protagonist of BBC period drama The Other Bennet Sister played by the 30-year-old Ella Bruccoleri. “Being able to make a drama in 2026 that features a woman who some people in society doesn’t think should be an acceptable face of a woman,” said Tranter. Related Stories News 'Industry' Star Myha'la Claims "Unconscious Racial Bias" Is Baked Into 'The Traitors' News International Insider: 'Doctor Who' Regeneration Underway; MIPCOM Preview; Busan Takeaways “She doesn’t look like what people want her to look like, she doesn’t sound like what people want her to sound like and she doesn’t behave like society wants a woman to behave like and yet she is her own woman. Watch on Deadline “In 2026, stories about people being accepted for who they choose to be are the kind of stories I will keep making until someone carries me out in a wooden box. I really urge you to look for those stories. We have to tell stories that change the lack of empathy in our world. Look into yourselves and go and tell your own stories that will make our world a more empathetic place.” The Other Bennet Sister is an adaptation of former BBC executive Janice Hadlow’s novel of the same name. The BBC series, which plays on BritBox in the U.S., tells the story of Jane Austen’s Pride and Prejudice from the viewpoint of Mary, the overlooked sister from the Bennet family, before telling the tale of her journeys to London and the Lake District. A three-part Christmas special has been ordered. As one of the most experienced execs working in scripted having led the BBC’s drama before launching Bad Wolf, Tranter has made shows such as Doctor Who and Industry . While she acknowledged funding high-end dramas is challenged, she said demand for major series remains strong. “If someone says to you, ‘You can’t make period dramas, no one’s buying them… You can’t make fantasy, no one is buying it.’ You can’t make a drama set in finance. Make it. Just find a way to make it,” she said. As such, Tranter’s Sony-owned Bad Wolf is also known for productions such as Industry , His Dark Materials and Doctor Who , making it one of the UK’s most prolific drama producers across genres of the past decade. James Gandolfini’s influence Earlier in her talk at the Excelsior Westin Hotel in Rome, Tranter played the audience an extended clip of The Night Of , the HBO drama starring Riz Ahmed about a man who is accused of murdering a woman after a one-night stand. Based on a BBC series, Criminal Justice , the series was big hit in 2016 and earned five Emmy wins. She recalled how the HBO production became challenged when James Gandolfini, who had championed the project, unexpectedly passed away while away on holiday in Italy in 2013. He had played Ahmed’s defense lawyer in a pilot and was an exec producer on the show, and his passing left Tranter, then new to the U.S. system having only recently moved from the UK, and series creator Steven Zaillian at a crossroads. “I got really lucky that Steven took on the show, and then I got even luckier that James Gandolfini came in to play the role of John Stone,” she said. “And then James unexpectedly died and the whole project got put on hold for a while. Then, as in life sometimes happens, one door closes and another opens. John Turturro, who is the most brilliant actor and the nicest of men, came in, and so we continued making The Night Of .” Tranter revealed that her experience producing The Night Of also influenced her decision to launch a major production studio in Wales, where the Bad Wolf era of Doctor Who was filmed. “After Jim’s death, I continued to work with a lot of his crew,” she explained. “He was very, very loyal, and his crew were very loyal to him. so a lot of his Sopranos [crew] worked on The Night Of , and I got to know and understand a lot of them from New Jersey. I understood what it was like to work within the community, and I began to think of Wales and the passion of the crews that I had worked with in my time.” Earlier this month, Deadline revealed the production companies vying to become the next producer on Doctor Who when it returns in 2028. Bad Wolf and showrunner Russell T. Davies both dramatically exited in June. Tranter was not quizzed on the current Doctor Who situation on stage. articles.title: Tokyo Film Festival Chiefs Talk Balancing Blockbusters & Arthouse; Launching International Films In Japan
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz How TIFFCOM Is Building On Cannes Recognition To Strengthen Global Networks, Co-Production & Japanese IP Tokyo Film Festival Chiefs Talk Balancing Blockbusters & Arthouse; Launching International Films In Japan Disney Appoints Carol Choi As Asia Pacific President Following Luke Kang’s Retirement View All October 21, 2026 3:24am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Godzilla Minus Zero Toho It’s an exciting time for Japanese cinema, with franchise hits from Demon Slayer to Godzilla stomping around the world, and Japanese arthouse titles taking the spotlight at major film festivals including Venice, Toronto and Cannes. This year’s Tokyo International Film Festival, taking place in the Hibiya-Ginza district of the city from October 26 to November 4, aims to take full advantage of the momentum and help expand the international profile of Japanese films. Under incoming Festival Director Takeo Hisamatsu, and Programming Director Shozo Ichiyama, the festival is also positioning itself as a launchpad for international films in Japan. Related Stories Commentary We Can See Oscar Possibilities For A24's Hit Documentary 'You Can See Everything' - And That Includes An Acting Category News 'La Bola Negra' Directing Duo Los Javis Reveal How Spanish Sensation Became "The Journey Of Our Lives" Hisamatsu, who previously held senior posts at Warner Bros Japan and local studio Shochiku, headed the festival from 2017-2021 and returned earlier this year when Hiroyasu Ando stepped down after seven years at the helm. While Ichiyama has been strengthening the festival’s competitions, Gala and World Focus line-ups, Hisamatsu says he wants to bolster the glamour quotient at the festival, especially as it gears up for its 40th edition next year. Watch on Deadline “We want to combine art and entertainment and make the festival as multifaceted as possible,” says Hisamatsu, sitting down with Deadline at the festival’s office in the historic Togeki Building in Ginza. “This should be a festival for cinephiles, for general film fans, and also for people who maybe only visit a cinema once or twice in a year. Everyone should be able to find something they want to see.” While describing this year’s pre-anniversary edition as a time for evaluation, he envisages a line-up that includes Japanese films, Hollywood and other international titles, awards contenders, and every genre and format from live action and animation to documentary and short films. The U.S. studios have not been promoting heavily at Asian film festivals in recent years, but Hisamatsu hopes to lure them back: “Japan is still a big market – last year our box office hit a record and surpassed pre-pandemic revenues. Now is a good time to reboot the popularity of Hollywood films in Japan.” Hisamatsu is also engaging with international organisations, including the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences ( AMPAS ), which is bringing a delegation of executives, including Academy CEO Bill Kramer, to participate in a busy schedule of panels and networking events at the festival. Several awards season contenders, including Wild Horse Nine , La Bola Negra , animated feature Wildwood , and Christian Mungiu’s Cannes Palme d’Or winner Fjord , are screening across the festival’s Gala, World Focus and Special Screenings sections. ‘Wild Horse Nine’ Searchlight Pictures However, the festival toppers stress that this doesn’t mean any attention will be taken away from Japanese titles. “One of our major goals is to introduce Japanese films to international markets,” says Hisamatsu. The festival will open with a Japanese film – Zeze Takahisa’s Sukiyaki , about the historic song that topped the Billboard charts and remains one of the world’s best-selling tunes – while Takashi Yamazaki’s Godzilla Minus Zero , the highly-anticipated sequel to Oscar-winning Godzilla Minus One , will play as the Centerpiece Film. Korean filmmaker Yang Sang-ho’s zombie thriller Colony will close the festival. Three Japanese films have been selected for the festival’s main Competition section: The Canary’s Lullaby , directed by Akira Ikeda; Yukiko Mishima’s Two Cigarettes, Three Nights ; and Akira Yamamoto’s The Intertwining . Ichiyama, the festival’s Programming Director, explains that The Canary’s Lullaby is a Japan-Taiwan co-production, partly filmed on Taiwan’s Kinmen Island, and The Intertwining is based on a Japanese novel but has Korean elements, demonstrating the more international outlook of Japan’s new generation of directors. With major festivals including Cannes, Venice and Toronto, all of which take place before Tokyo, hoovering up Japanese titles over the past few years, Ichiyama says his focus has been on discoveries, as the festival requires world premieres for the Japanese films in competition. “These three filmmakers are not so well known internationally, but they’re all extremely promising, and have the potential to go to European film festivals in the future,” he says. Takeo Hisamatsu [L] & Shozo Ichiyama [R] Other world premieres in the Competition line-up include Indonesian filmmaker Garin Nugroho’s Red Before Dawn , set in a newly independent Indonesia in the 1940s, which Ichiyama describes as “a big-budget epic drama”; Macedonian filmmaker Milcho Manchevski’s social satire Sister Brother Manhole Cover ; and two Chinese-language titles Fuxi: Four Tales Of Feasting , from Qiu Jiongjiong, and Wang Jianyong’s The Night That Binds Us . Also in the line-up of 15 competition titles is Rubaiyat Hussain’s The Difficult Bride , which world premiered in the Horizons section of this year’s Venice film festival and marks the first ever Bangladeshi film selected for Tokyo main competition. “We saw it in Venice and sent the the invitation very quickly,” says Ichiyama. “We usually see two or three interesting films from Bangladesh in one year, and this one is outstanding.” Rounding out the competition are Heysel 85 , from Romanian filmmaker Teodora Ana Mihai, joining Tokyo Competition for the third time following Traffic and La Civil ; Until The Day Ends , from Serbian filmmaker Jelena Maksimović; Double Freedom , from Argentina’s Lisandro Alonso; Even If Hell Came , from Italy’s Samuele Rossi; Portuguese filmmaker Sérgio Graciano’s Memories Of Prison ; Singaporean animation Magic Atlas from Sun Xun, and Trees Are Watching from Iranian-Kurdish filmmaker Bahman Ghobadi. ‘Heysel 85’ Australian filmmaker Rolf de Heer is heading the main competition jury, which also includes Tokyo and New York-based producer Alex Lo, Korean producer Oh Jungwan, French colorist Yov Moor and Japanese actress Makiko Watanabe. An Australia Spotlight will screen De Heer’s 2022 The Survival Of Kindness ; Natalie Erika James’ body horror Saccharine , and Vee Shi’s hybrid documentary Time And Tide . Other talent attending the festival include Cate Blanchett , in town to celebrate the Japan premieres of five short films supported by the Displacement Film Fund (and who is also a producer on Alpha Gang , recently added to Special Screenings); as well as Iranian director Mohammad Rasoulof and Japanese filmmaker Mipo O, both recipients of this year’s Kurosawa Akira Award. Filmmakers including Ilya Khrzhanovsky ( DAU ), Teodora Ana Mihai ( Heysel 85 ), Zeze Takahisa ( Sukiyaki ), Shahrbanoo Sadat ( No Good Men ) and Yukiko Sode ( All The Lovers In The Night ) will deliver talk sessions and masterclasses. Tokyo has two other competition sections – Asian Future, focused on emerging Asian directors, and Nippon Cinema Now, which aims to present an overview of the current state of contemporary Japanese film. Nippon Cinema Now will screen eight titles, from both new and established directors, and has introduced two new awards for Best Film and a Special Jury Prize. Asian Future, programmed by Kenji Ishizaka, will screen 10 world premieres from Japan, Korea, Philippines, India, Turkey, Kazakhstan, Indonesia and Iran. This year also sees the return of the festival’s non-competitive section dedicated to Southeast Asian cinema, Crosscut Asia, held in partnership with the Japan Foundation, which stopped running during the pandemic period. Now titled Crosscut Asia+, the section will screen three recent festival hits, Four Seasons In Java , Filipiñana and Becoming Human , along with a selection of retrospective titles. ‘ Iron Boy ‘ Other major sections include Animation, which will screen Cannes Un Certain Regard special jury prize winner Iron Boy , among other titles; Women’s Empowerment, including recent festival breakouts Lovers In The Blue Night , from India’s Anupama Roy, and A Girl Unknown , from China’s Zou Jing; Japanese Classics, including a Kenji Mizoguchi retrospective; and the Youth and Asian Students Film Conference sections. Taking place towards the end of the year, Tokyo Film Festival has always been in a good position to present a “best of fests” round-up for local audiences, and this year aims to double down on efforts to connect international films with Japanese buyers, both directly at the festival and through the TIFFCOM contents market taking place a few metro stops away. “Especially in World Focus, we’re showing many films that played in Berlin, Venice and Cannes, several of which have still not found a Japanese distributor,” Ichiyama says. “Japan has many strong, independent buyers, but with the current weakness of the Japanese yen, they’ve not been so eager to travel to Venice and Toronto or acquire new films. We can present those titles here in theatres with local audiences and Japanese subtitles.” With many screenings already sold out, filmmakers and industry can expect packed houses and attentive audiences for these films. As Hisamatsu observes, Japan continues to be one of the world’s top theatrical markets, and while anime and Godzilla may be pulling the biggest crowds, Tokyo Film Festival is one time of year at least when movies of all genres, languages and budget levels will be reaching audiences on a big screen. The festival kicks off on Monday, October 26, with an opening ceremony and screening of Sukiyaki, and runs until Wednesday, November 4, while TIFFCOM is taking place October 28-30 at the Tokyo Metropolitan Industrial Trade Center in Hamamatsucho. articles.title: How TIFFCOM Is Building On Cannes Recognition To Strengthen Global Networks, Co-Production & Japanese IP
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz How TIFFCOM Is Building On Cannes Recognition To Strengthen Global Networks, Co-Production & Japanese IP Tokyo Film Festival Chiefs Talk Balancing Blockbusters & Arthouse; Launching International Films In Japan Disney Appoints Carol Choi As Asia Pacific President Following Luke Kang’s Retirement View All October 21, 2026 3:27am Add us as a Google Preferred Source TIFFCOM 2025 TIFFCOM At this year’s Marché du Film at the Cannes film festival, it would be no exaggeration to say that Japanese content and creators were everywhere you turned. Designated ‘Country of Honour’ at the market, Japan was involved in a slew of panels, workshops and labs; played a prominent role in Cannes flagship programs, including Cannes Animation, Co-Production Day, and Producers Network; and also launched the Japan IP Market, a three-day initiative co-hosted by the Marché and Japan’s leading contents market TIFFCOM . The Marché decided to shine a spotlight on Japan in recognition of the strength of its content and intellectual property (IP), as well as recent efforts – by the Japanese government, local studios, and independent filmmakers and producers – to engage with the rest of the world. As Deadline noted at TIFFCOM two years ago, Japan was once reliant on its huge domestic market, but is now actively seeking co-production, collaboration and exports, focusing its efforts on North and South America, Europe, and the rest of Asia. Related Stories Executives Amazon MGM Studios Elevates Julie Rapaport & Alana Mayo In Film Division Reorg News 'Lizard Music' Starring Dwayne Johnson And Directed By Benny Safdie To Tune Up Christmas Day 2027 Via Amazon MGM All these efforts are being supported by the Japanese government, which last year launched the ‘Content Industry Growth Investment Support Program’, branded as IP360, which aims to expand overseas sales of Japanese content (across film, anime, games and music) to $126BN (JPY20 trillion) by 2033. Watch on Deadline “Historically, sectors including Japanese anime and live-action content have been optimized for the domestic market, lacking an industrial structure designed to expand into global markets,” explains TIFFCOM CEO Yasushi Shiina. “At Cannes this year, as the Country of Honour, the public and private sectors joined forces to showcase Japan’s key strengths, including anime and manga. In doing so, we built networks with international producers, distributors, and other industry professionals, driving strong momentum toward transforming the sector into an IP-driven industry that generates global revenue. “Following this, TIFFCOM will leverage the home-ground advantage of being hosted in Japan to promote Japanese IP alongside a diverse array of participants. For international attendees as well, we aim to make TIFFCOM a platform where they can connect directly with Japanese partners and unlock new business opportunities.” Yasushi Shiina [L] & Kaori Ikeda [R] A key program within TIFFCOM is the Tokyo IP Market: Adaptation & Remake (TIPM), an initiative that the Cannes IP event was also based on, which brings together publishers and production companies holding rights to Japanese manga, audiovisual works, novels and games. This year, the number of participating IP holders has expanded from six to ten companies, including content giants such as Amuse Creative Studio, Kadokawa, Nippon Animation, Shochiku and Toei . TIPM organizes a series of one-on-one meetings between the rights holders and international producers, mostly from North America, Europe and the rest of Asia. In addition, eight of these companies will hold an open pitch event, with audiovisual support from Imagica Group, to present their flagship IP. “We co-organized the Japan IP Market in Cannes – the Cannes edition of TIPM – with the Marché du Film, and the event generated an exceptionally strong response,” explains TIFFCOM managing director Kaori Ikeda. “Thanks to this success, the Tokyo edition is seeing an increasing number of leading producers attending from Europe and Hollywood. We’re excited to offer everyone in Tokyo this premier opportunity to connect with high-quality Japanese IP.” Another key TIFFCOM track is the Tokyo Gap Financing Market (TGFM), which presents projects with Asian elements and at least 60% of their funding in place, that are seeking to complete their budgets through co-production, sales, distribution and other forms of investment. This year, the event has selected 24 projects including Vincci Cheuk’s Hong Kong-Japan co-production 38.83 ; Boo Junfeng’s multi-territory co-production Trinity ; François-Marc Baillet’s animated feature Back To Tomioka ; five projects selected through a partnership with Canada’s Frontières genre market, and three in partnership with Italy’s Cinecitta ( see here for the full list of selected projects ). In addition, TGFM talk sessions will introduce Japan’s various support schemes – including grants for international co-productions from Japan’s Agency for Cultural Affairs (Bunka-cho) – alongside funding from Canada and Brazil. Japanese producers have been co-producing with their East Asian neighbors in Taiwan and South Korea for quite some time but have recently been venturing further afield into Southeast Asia and Europe. “Two factors are driving this,” says Ikeda. “First, production volume is increasing across Asia as a whole, including Southeast Asia, and production capabilities are also rising. “Second, opportunities to build networks with one another at film festivals and markets across Asia are expanding. Platforms such as TGFM are facilitating mutual introductions, leading to an increasing number of co-production projects with Southeast Asia. Japan also recently joined the new Asian Producers Alliance with the Agency for Cultural Affairs as the representative member.” In Europe, co-productions between Japan and France have been the most common, but Ikeda observes that projects with Italy have also increased following the signing of an official Japan-Italy co-production treaty in 2024. Recent co-productions involving Japan include Sleep No More , from Indonesian filmmaker Edwin, which premiered at this year’s Berlinale; Ria , from the Philippines’ Arvin Belarmino, which won the Heart of Eurasia Award at Busan film festival, and Boo’s upcoming Trinity , which has around ten co-producers across Europe and Asia. Trinity , Ria and Janus Victoria’s Japan-Philippines co-production Diamonds In The Sand were all selected for various editions of TGFM. ‘Ria’ Meanwhile, TIFFCOM’s conference program will present around 20 sessions organized along thematic lines: intellectual property (IP), artificial intelligence (AI), Japanese TV, Asian Series & Films, market trends and co-production. Key sessions include an ‘Unlocking the Global Potential of Japanese IP’, with speakers from Credeus ( Kokuho ), Amazon MGM Studios and Netflix’s One Piece ; an AI-themed keynote with AGBO ’s Chris Brearton and Dominic Hughes; and the annual session by the Association of Japanese Animations, presenting data on the anime industry. Leading Japanese broadcasters Nippon TV and TBS will host sessions on their international activities; an Anime Co-Production Conference will feature speakers including Ervin Han ( The Violinist ), and a “Beyond Country of Honour” session has speakers from Toho and K2 Pictures, along with TIFFCOM’s Shiina and Cannes Marché Head of Industry Programs Alexandra Zakharchenko. Last year’s TIFFCOM had more than 4,600 attendees from 46 countries and regions, an increase of 13% from the previous year, while international participation rose by 10%. As of two weeks before this year’s edition, Ikeda says that visitor registrations – mostly buyers and producers – were up about 10% on the same point last year. “East Asia continues to drive strong participation, led by Taiwan and South Korea, as well as a dedicated pavilion from Thailand,” Ikeda says. “Some companies from China, including streaming platforms, will also take part. And in a notable new trend, we are also seeing increasing participation from companies offering AI and data analytics solutions.” TIFFCOM is taking place October 28 to 30 at the Tokyo Metropolitan Industrial Trade Center in Hamamatsucho district, which is just a few train stops away from Tokyo International Film Festival’s main venues in Hibiya-Ginza. The festival is running from October 26 to November 4. The BBC has canned The Catch Up as part of the planned closure of BBC Three , the youth network that will be switched off for a second time in spring 2027. BBC Three ‘s brand will be retained on iPlayer. The Catch Up was launched in 2022 and was pitched as an attempt to “bring back” 16- to 24-year-old viewers to traditional news bulletins. Its debut coincided with BBC Three being restored to linear TV, a decision that was reversed on Tuesday. Related Stories Acquisitions The BBC & MHz Choice Board Sweden's Latest 'Wallander' Series News BBC Three To Be Switched Off For Second Time, As BBC Confirms TV & Radio Network Closures The two- to four-minute news bulletin was designed to provide young viewers with a roundup of the day’s headlines in an accessible format, complete with graphics and a conversational tone. Watch on Deadline Tuesday’s bulletin was hosted by BBC journalist Ben Henley-Washford and featured a report on BBC Three’s demise as a linear television network. “The BBC has announced it is closing BBC Three,” Henley-Washford said. “Not just yet, though. They said the TV channel, along with BBC Scotland’s channel, will close in the spring as the corporation continues to make £500 million pounds worth of savings by 2028.” He did not mention that The Catch Up would be discontinued. When The Catch Up launched, then editor Amanda Goodman told Press Gazette : “We want to create relatable news for young people that doesn’t necessarily sound like the BBC, or the BBC they think exists at present.” BBC News was not on TikTok in 2022, but this has changed. The BBC News account now has 16.5 million followers and more than 1 billion likes. A BBC News spokesperson said: “The BBC is the UK’s leading news publisher for 16-34 year olds in the UK – reaching around half of 16–34-year-olds each week across its BBC News platforms, including youth-focused offerings such as Newsbeat , as well as Newsround for a younger audience. “Further to this, there are significant and growing numbers of young people accessing BBC News across our social channels – including TikTok, Instagram and YouTube. articles.title: Russell Brand Told Fan To “Clean Up Mess” After Alleged Rape As Accuser Tells Court She “Carried Feeling Of Guilt & Shame” For Years
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Amelia Dimoldenberg’s Manager Spearheading Entertainment & New Media Biz At Three Six Zero Russell Brand Accuser Says She Reported Comedian To Channel 4 In 2009 After He Allegedly Lay His Head On Her Lap & Demanded Massage Russell Brand Accuser Alleges Witnesses Were Present When He “Grabbed My Face” & “Pushed His Body Against Mine” At Radio Station View All October 21, 2026 5:33am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand arrives at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday Getty Editor’s note: T his story contains details of alleged sexual offenses that readers may find distressing Russell Brand told one of his fans to “clean up the mess” after allegedly anally raping her at his home in north London, a court has been told. On a busy day at London’s Southwark Crown Court, the jury heard from three of Brand’s six accusers. The court was played a 2024 video recording of a police interview with one woman, whom we are calling Complainant 5 (C5) as she has a lifelong right to anonymity . During the two-hour-long interview, C5 was frequently in tears and distressed as she relived her alleged encounter with Brand. Related Stories News Russell Brand Accuser Says She Reported Comedian To Channel 4 In 2009 After He Allegedly Lay His Head On Her Lap & Demanded Massage Legal Russell Brand Accuser Alleges Witnesses Were Present When He "Grabbed My Face" & "Pushed His Body Against Mine" At Radio Station The Despicable Me star faces three charges of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one of indecent assault based on allegations made by six women . He will set out his defense later in the trial, denies all charges, and has pleaded not guilty. Watch on Deadline C5, who thought Brand was “interesting, articulate and intelligent about things that others would shy away from,” said she met Brand at one of his comedy gigs in 2009 at the Hammersmith Apollo. She was “invited upstairs for drinks,” after which she consensually performed oral sex on him but told him she didn’t want to have penetrative sex. She said he took her number, “thought I’d never hear from him again,” but Brand kept messaging her and soon after she agreed to go to his house in Hampstead, north London. She was driven to his home by a driver, let in by an associate of Brand’s and was told, “Russell’s on the phone to America.” Brand then came downstairs and told her, “This is the best decision you’ve ever made,” she said during the police interview, which was played to the jury to avoid C5 having to retell her story in the courtroom. Deadline has been following the trial live via a closed video stream from the courtroom. C5 alleged that Brand’s demeanor changed when they were kissing on his bed and he suddenly said, “You need to have a shower because your hair smells funny,” which “didn’t sound kind” but made her “feel like I was dirty.” At first, C5 alleged she and Brand had consensual penetrative sex and Brand was using a condom. “I didn’t enjoy the experience because I felt like somebody was just f**king a hole,” she added. “I could have been anyone. It didn’t matter who I was.” After having consensual sex for some time, C5 alleged Brand “turned me onto my front,” and she assumed he wanted to continue vaginal sex. Instead, she said he inserted his fingers into her anus before anally raping her, which she said was extremely painful. C5 alleged Brand said to her, “I want you to feel my cum,” at which point he ejaculated inside her anus and she realized he had removed his condom. After he was finished, she alleged Brand “looked absolutely horrified” and told her, “You need to clean up the mess that you’ve made.” He then left the room and his associate told her that Brand was performing another gig shortly and “whenever you are ready you can leave.” C5 was in tears during the police interview when she said: “I went there knowing I would have sex with him and what I mean is vaginal penetrative sex. I went knowing that would happen. I want to make that clear because I’ve struggled to accept what happened to me because I went there knowingly and willingly.” “He did not act like he’d done anything wrong” That evening, she said she told her flatmate what had happened and was in so much pain she had to “sit on an ice cube tray.” She was later told she had an anal tear and became convinced she had contracted HIV, for which she tested negative. “I wanted to just leave it all behind,” she told police. “I thought maybe he does that all the time. He did not act like he’d done anything wrong.” Since the incident, C5 said she has struggled with alcohol addiction and went to rehab in 2023, during which time she opened up about the incident. Around that time, Channel 4 aired its Russell Brand: In Plain Sight documentary, which was a catalyst for her going to police. “I’ve tried not thinking about it and it hasn’t worked, so whatever happens after this [police interview], I know I’ve sat in a room and said what happened to me,” she explained. “I just don’t want to die knowing that what he did to me I have not said to the right people.” “I carried the feeling of guilt and shame” C5 is the final Brand accuser to give evidence and took to the stand for questioning on Wednesday. All of the accusers came forward after watching the Channel 4 documentary, but none of them know each other, the prosecution has said. Under questioning from Brand’s lawyer Ian Winter, C5, who gave evidence to the court from behind a screen, said she had “carried the burden” and “carried the feeling of guilt and shame” for years after the alleged attack. She was repeatedly pressed by Winter on whether she had in fact consented to anal sex as well as vaginal sex with Brand, but continued to deny that this was the case. “Just because you go somewhere willingly, that does not mean the outcome at the end is [necessarily] consensual,” she said. “I did not make the decision to have anal sex with Mr. Brand. I did not make that decision. We never had a conversation about anal sex.” The summer after the alleged rape took place, the court heard that C5 saw Brand from a distance at an event she was working at during the Edinburgh Festival. She said he texted her and she replied asking why he was messaging her, and Brand responded, “Because you’re dirty and I wanna push you further.” C5 said she then responded by saying, “I think you pushed me far enough, you treated me like an animal,” to which Brand then quickly apologized and the text conversation ended. Pushed by Winter on why she didn’t tell Brand he had raped her, C5 said: “To give you that answer is really difficult.” She was also pressed by Winter on how much she “adored” Brand, with Winter putting forward the idea several times that she was “obsessed” with Brand before she first met him at the Hammersmith Apollo. “You knew he was extremely sexually active with multiple women?,” asked Winter, to which C5 replied: “Correct.” “You knew he had won The Sun newspaper’s ‘Shagger of the Year’ award three years running,” Winter then asked. “I don’t think I was aware of that,” replied C5. The evidence from Brand’s accusers is now over and the court will return tomorrow with witnesses. The court has been told repeatedly that Brand declined to answer questions when interviewed by police. He instead relied on a prepared statement, in which he claimed that he did not recall meeting the women and did not remember their names. He said any sexual contact was consensual. The trial continues. articles.title: Snap Enlists Robert Downey Jr. to Push Specs
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Robert Downey Jr. for Specs Snap Inc. Robert Downey Jr. plans to bring a little bit of Iron Man technology to pop culture, linking up with Specs to become its chief customer experience officer. The position is mostly a marketing one, with the Marvel actor working with the Specs team on original content, lens experiences, hardware collaborations and other features. Specs, of course, is the augmented reality glasses concept from Snap Inc. The company was early to the game with the original Snap Spectacles in 2016, which were available in limited quantities. The new version is much more advanced, using technology to overlay images on the real world through a glasses-like form factor, much smaller and lighter than VR headsets. The Downey partnership will launch on TV with a video campaign set to debut during tonight’s New York Knicks vs. Philadelphia 76ers NBA Tip-Off game, with another spot set to launch during game one of the MLB World Series later this week. The first pieces of content are available now on the Specs website and on YouTube. Downey, in a statement, said that the technology reminds him of what Tony Stark himself used in the Marvel movies. “Trying is believing. Having tested practically every wearable tech that’s come to market in the last 20 years, and been largely unimpressed, I was absolutely sold on Specs within 40 seconds,” said Downey Jr. “The applications are endless. Families can share experiences instead of hunching over devices, skills can be honed, big business can streamline development. In short, it delivers on the promise of AR glasses made by a certain techno optimist superhero I portrayed. Life imitates art-imitates life! I’ve never experienced the confident, warm and creatively inviting atmosphere that Evan has cultivated at Specs anywhere else in the tech sector. Wait’ll you see what we create for you to enjoy.” “We’re incredibly excited to welcome Robert Downey Jr. to Specs to help shape the future of augmented reality,” added Evan Spiegel, co-founder and CEO of Snap Inc. “Robert has been imagining what this technology could become for nearly twenty years, and it’s an honor to work with him to bring that vision to life.” THR

articles.title: Christina Applegate Reveals She Was Misdiagnosed and Does Not Have MS: “I Haven’t Gotten Better … I’m Back at Square One”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Jackie Strause Plus Icon Jackie Strause Managing Editor, East Coast jackiedstrause Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 6:04am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Christina Applegate in 2024. Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images for Critics Choice Association Christina Applegate returned to her podcast after some time away to reveal that she was misdiagnosed and does not, in fact, have MS. Applegate revealed in a two-part episode of her MeSsY podcast that she co-hosts with Jamie-Lynn Sigler, who has multiple sclerosis (MS), that, in 2021, she was being tested for “everything under the sun,” but not MS right away. She had brain and spinal MRIs, and a spinal tap, which determined that she had RMS, which was, at the time, “on the low scale.” However, Applegate said she was getting progressively worse. The doctor then showed her the lesions on her brain, almost 40, she said, and “that was it. That was my answer to everything that was going on” at the time. Related Stories General News Christina Applegate Breaks Silence Amid Hospitalization Reports to Give Health Update Movies Christina Applegate: Will Ferrell and Adam McKay Gave Me Parts of Their 'Anchorman' Salaries After "Offensive" Studio Offer Applegate revealed her diagnosis in August 2021, at age 49, sharing publicly that she had been diagnosed a few months prior. On her podcast episode released on Tuesday, she said that after her diagnosis, she then leaned on the MS community, which includes her co-host, and started infusions that went on for years, wreaking “havoc” on her body. A “couple of years ago,” however, Applegate said, her doctor wanted to take her off of the infusion and monitor her B cells. When her B cells didn’t change, that’s when they began a study into her diagnosis. Thanks to new technology around brain MRIs, Applegate recently learned she was misdiagnosed. “She came into my room and she said, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS. Congratulations.’,” she recalled, fighting back tears. Applegate said everyone else was so happy but, “I’m not happy at all.” “You don’t get misdiagnosed, and then all of a sudden, I’m better,” she added. “I haven’t gotten better, Jamie. If anything, I’ve gotten worse in some ways. So I’m back at square one where I don’t know what’s going on with me, and that’s going to be an online investigation that my doctors are going to get into to find out what has been happening since 2021. Why did this happen? I have every symptom of someone with MS — every single one.” Applegate said there is a high number of misdiagnoses with MS, even after years of infusions like she had. She began crying while saying, “I feel like I let everybody down. I became, you and I, the poster children for MS. I had a reason — I had a fucking reason — as to why my day sucked every day. And now I don’t have a reason, and it’s very unnerving and very confusing for me.” Applegate continued to say she’s currently in a state of shock. “It’s a mind fuck, for sure,” she told Sigler. The investigation into her health is so new, she said, that next week she begins a process that will involve her being her own advocate and finding the right specialists. “I needed some time to process that, but I also needed me time, after the book and some health stuff that was going on,” she said. “I just needed time to find the love in life again.” She said it “hurts to get out of bed; it hurts to stand up. I’m still sleeping all the time. I’ve still got a lot of health issues. But I’m finding ways to make my room joyous and make sure that my doors are open and that I can hear the birds and the fountain outside.” Applegate and Sigler said they will have experts on to respond to the news but that their podcast will also still be an entertaining space for the two of them to discuss the things that bring them joy (like Bravo shows and Andy Cohen). Ultimately, she said she’s not relieved, but Sigler pushed her to be curious. “Your reaction is very human and real, and I think one that anyone would share,” said Sigler, then insisting that Applegate look forward to doing a little dance, “a little shuffle,” over not having MS. “I’ve been talking about that damn jumping for so long!” Applegate said, with a laugh. THR

articles.title: David Ellison, Dina Powell McCormick, Chris Winfrey and Roger Lynch Join Paley Center Board
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 6:17am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The Paley Center for Media in New York Photo by Noam Galai/Getty Images for CBS The Paley Center for Media is adding some boldface names to its board of trustees. The nonprofit says that Skydance CEO David Ellison, Mattel CEO Roger Lynch, Meta president and vice chair Dina Powell McCormick and Charter CEO Chris Winfrey are joining its board, and that Recording Academy CEO Harvey Mason Jr. is joining its Los Angeles board of governors. The Paley Center operates two facilities, one in New York and the other in L.A., which provide a year-round museum focused on media, entertainment culture, as well as public-facing and invitation-only events like Paleyfest. In fact, the new trustees were announced at the kickoff of the 2026 Paley International Council Summit, which will include sessions with people like Strauss Zelnick, John Malone, David Solomon, Gary Bettman and others. The board is already comprised of media and entertainment heavy hitters that include Lachlan Murdoch, Ynon Kreiz, Eddy Cue, Neal Mohan, Roger Goodell, Tyler Perry and Josh D’Amaro. “We are privileged to welcome this renowned group of exceptional and distinguished leaders to Paley’s Board of Trustees and Los Angeles Board of Governors,” said Maureen J. Reidy, president & CEO of The Paley Center for Media. “Their visionary leadership, innovative insights, and extraordinary expertise will further strengthen Paley’s standing as the media industry’s preeminent nonprofit cultural institution.” “I am honored to join The Paley Center for Media’s Board of Trustees,” added David Ellison. “For decades, Paley has been home to the conversation about how media shapes our culture, preserving the stories that have captivated audiences around the world while championing the creators and innovators who will define what comes next. At Skydance, we believe deeply in the power of media to entertain, inform and bring people together, whether through film, television, streaming or the news. I look forward to working alongside this distinguished group of leaders to support the Paley Center’s vital work and its mission to celebrate and advance the media landscape for future generations.” “The Paley Center has been an enduring force in both preserving media’s history and helping shape its future,” said Roger Lynch. “It is an honor to join the Board of Trustees, and I look forward to contributing to Paley’s important work for years to come.” “Music and media have the power to make us feel seen, open our minds, and connect us like nothing else can,” added Harvey Mason Jr. “That power comes from people with a story to tell and the courage to create. I’m honored to join the Paley Center’s Los Angeles Board of Governors and help champion those voices, celebrate the work that has shaped our lives, and inspire the next generation to leave their own mark.” THR

articles.title: Tilda Swinton to Star Off-Broadway In Solo Show ‘Man to Man’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Caitlin Huston Plus Icon Caitlin Huston Business Writer hustonca Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 6:56am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Tilda Swinton in 'Man to Man.' Ruediger Glatz Tilda Swinton will make her New York stage debut this winter in Manfred Karge’s Man to Man . The solo show will play the Lucille Lortel Theatre starting Feb. 21, 2027, with an opening night Feb. 28 for a strictly limited eight-week run. Swinton returns to the role after originating the role in 1987. The Academy Award winner is currently performing in the role at London’s Royal Court Theatre, marking her first return to the stage for the first time since the original production. This production will also have limited runs in Scotland at the Traverse Theatre and in Germany with the Berliner Ensemble before coming to New York. Set in 1930s Germany, the play follows a woman who assumes her dead husband’s identity and lives as Ella/Max as the country changes, including through war and dictatorship. The production originated at the Traverse Theatre, which first commissioned the original production in 1987 before it transferred in 1988 to the Royal Court. This revival brings back the original creative team with direction by Stephen Unwin, design by Bunny Christie and translation by Anthoyn Vivis, with revisions by Unwin. Lighting Design is by Ben Ormerod, sound design by Elena Peña and projection design by Matt Powell. Swinton won the Academy Award in 2007 for her role in Michael Clayton . Other film credits include The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, Burn After Reading, Orlando and her frequent collaborations with director Wes Anderson , which include roles in Moonrise Kingdom, The Grand Budapest Hotel , The French Dispatch and Asteroid City . Brian and Dayna Lee, The Royal Court Theatre, Berliner Ensemble, and Madison Wells Live are producing. THR

articles.title: Hannah Berner and Paige DeSorbo’s ‘Giggly Squad’ to Play Madison Square Garden (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Caitlin Huston Plus Icon Caitlin Huston Business Writer hustonca Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Paige DeSorbo and Hannah Berner of 'Giggly Squad.' Lucio Andreozzi Foto Hannah Berner and Paige DeSorbo’s Giggly Squad is coming to Madison Square Garden. The popular podcast will stop at the Garden for a live recording of the show on Feb. 18, 2027, as part of a broader U.S. and European tour. This will be the first female hosted podcast to perform at Madison Square Garden. Berner and DeSorbo launched the show on Instagram Live in 2020, as the two rose to fame on Bravo’s reality show Summer House . It has since grown into a top 10 comedy podcast. The show, which streams twice weekly, sees the two friends chat about their lives, dating, pop culture, fashion and more. The podcast has previously held live tours across 70 cities, including two shows at Radio City Music Hall, and sparked a New York Times bestselling book, How to Giggle . Giggly Squad was named podcast of the year at the 2026 iHeartPodcast Awards. Giggly Squad recently moved to SiriusXM in a multiyear deal valued at $160 million, according to sources familiar with the matter. As part of the deal, SiriusXM has exclusive global sales for the audio and video episodes of the podcast. New programming from Giggly Squad is expected to roll out in 2027. Previous podcasts to record a show at Madison Square Garden include Kill Tony Live , with Tony Hinchcliffe and Brian Redban, and The Basement Yard , hosted by Joe Santagato and Frank Alvarez. New York Knicks players Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart, and Matt Hillman, hosted a live edition of their Roommates Show from Madison Square Garden’s Infosy’s Theater this past summer. THR

articles.title: Two-Thirds of Microdramas Released in Latest Quarter Outside China Were AI Generated, Says Report
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Katie Kilkenny Plus Icon Katie Kilkenny Enterprise Reporter, TV & Labor katiekilkenny7 Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source An image of My Muse, Holywater’s AI-generated verticals app. Courtesy of Holywater Microdramas released on major platforms are increasingly being generated by AI, according to a new report from Owl & Co. Two-thirds of vertical drama releases outside China in the third quarter of 2026 from 20 top platforms were AI generated, according to the consulting firm’s latest “What We Watched on Vertical” report, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. Compare that with the the percentage of AI-generated stories released in the first quarter of the year (3 percent) and the second quarter (28 percent), and it’s clear that AI storytelling is increasingly dominating the sapce. The development echoes the format’s evolution in China, where microdramas were first popularized and where AI-generated titles have flooded the platforms in recent months. More than 95 percent of titles released in the first three months of 2026 in the country were reportedly made using AI. And it follows U.S. workers in the microdrama industry recently speaking out about the ways that the technology has reshaped the business. In September, workers in the industry told THR that they were observing fewer job opportunities as well as unscrupulous use of the technology on their work. The prevalence of AI in microdramas is reflected in the top-performing titles that Owl & Co. found for the latest quarter on apps that require viewers to pay for their stories. Only one live-action title — ReelShort’s My X-Ray Vision Sees Right Through You — broke the list of the top five highest-performing verticals in terms of minutes watched. And just two live-action titles ( My X-Ray Vision Sees Right Through You and ReelShort’s You’ve Been Replaced, First Love ) made the top 20. Top AI-generated titles, meanwhile, included the number-one best performer, ReelShort’s The Great and Powerful Genie , about a hot genie required by a wish to marry a woman for five years. It was followed by the popular DramaBox fantasy title Deny Me, Dragon King and another DramaBox dragon yarn, Married to the Hidden Dragon King . Overall, Owl & Co. found its tracked apps yielded 63 billion microdrama views in the third quarter and two billion viewing hours. TikTok‘s free PineDrama app was on the ascent, accounting for more than half of all views in the quarter. That’s notable, considering that PineDrama has been live for less than a year. The app is aggressively building its library, adding 15,501 new titles in the quarter, accounting for a more than 300 percent increase compared with the previous quarter. As for paid apps, DramaBox came out on top with 36 percent of views, followed by ReelShort with 29 percent, NetShort with 20 percent and DramaWave with 11 percent. All is not lost for human performance, however. Despite the prevalence of AI dramas in viewers’ feeds at the moment, the Owl & Co. report noted that China is already showing “a pullback towards live action.” The report’s dataset additionally found the number of stories featuring human performers growing alongside the increase of AI titles. And at ReelShort, “we observed live-action titles have a higher chance of remaining in the top 10 percent by views 30 days after release than AI titles,” the report stated. In other words, there is some early evidence that, long term, viewers may express more sustained interest in dramas portrayed by human actors rather than AI-generated performers. THR

articles.title: ‘Yaga’ Review: Carrie-Anne Moss and Hudson Williams in AMC+’s Intriguing but Undercooked Brew of Modern Crime and Ancient Folklore
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Angie Han Plus Icon Angie Han Television Critic ajhan Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Carrie-Anne Moss in ‘Yaga.’ Christopher Lawrence/Crave Perhaps it is only appropriate that Yaga , the new genre-bending thriller from AMC+ and Crave , should feel so devilishly difficult to pin down. After all, it’s only doing what myths have always done, which is transform — to reflect a new context, introduce a fresh perspective, impart an updated moral. And while it takes some time to see what shape this version of the Baba Yaga tale (as in Slavic folklore, not, as is explained by a couple different characters, the movie John Wick ) might take, it’s easy enough to fall under its spell at first. The atmosphere is deliciously chilly, the cast stuffed with actors you’ve loved in other things. But the longer it runs, the thinner its charms grow — leaving behind a show that’s enjoyable enough to binge, but not quite sharp enough to treasure. Related Stories TV 'Yaga' Cast Teases Timely Take on Female Rage, Double Hudson Williams and "A Lot of Chicken Stuff" TV AMC's 'Mayfair Witches: Salem Coven' Gets December Debut as Catherine Zeta-Jones, Carrie-Anne Moss Tease 'Kill Jackie' and 'Yaga' at NYCC Yaga The Bottom Line Plays hard to get. Airdate: Friday, Oct. 23 (AMC+) Cast: Carrie-Anne Moss, Clark Backo, Noah Reid, Hudson Williams, Sheila McCarthy Creator: Kat Sandler Adapted by Kat Sandler from her own play, Yaga opens at a point of uncertainty about whether there even is a mystery to be solved at all, though one presumes we would not all be gathered here if there were not. At some point in the last few days, Henry ( Hudson Williams ), the spoiled 22-year-old scion of a fish processing magnate, has disappeared from his giant mansion perched at the edge of a Canadian island. Well, maybe. Carson ( Clark Backo ), the no-nonsense Whittock PD detective assigned to the case, assumes he’s just out partying; even his dorkier doppelgänger of a roommate, Logan (also Williams), admits Henry’s prone to doing things like jet off to Paris on a last-minute romantic getaway. But there’s reason to suspect his absence has something to do with Katherine ( Carrie-Anne Moss ), a biology professor nicknamed the “Boner Beast” for rumors she sleeps with her students. Henry’s family are concerned enough to have sent in their own smarmy private investigator, Rapp ( Noah Reid ), though not quite concerned enough to cut short their own business trip to Japan. In any case, the kid must be found. As Carson and Rapp’s search for Henry deepens, Yaga cuts a jagged (though, at this point, well-trod by shows like Hulu’s Furious or even Netflix’s East of Eden ) path through themes of wealth, male entitlement, female rage and the purpose of myth. All of it flows toward a reconsideration of the legend of Baba Yaga herself, who bemoans her own malignment in raspy voiceovers that open and close each chapter. “I wonder why you tell stories of the wicked old witch when no one will stay and get to know me,” she complains. “I’m very funny, you know.” And she can be. One of Yaga ’s most potent assets is its tone: equal parts eerie and sexy and mischievous, with occasional flashes of lurid violence. You know a crime drama’s not going to take itself overly seriously when its version of a slick private dick is introduced tripping over his own feet immediately after an onlooker comments on how cool he looks. You know you’re in for something spookier than a run-of-the-mill kidnapping when dead birds, hallucinogenic concoctions and strange ancient symbols quickly become recurring motifs. And you know you’re in for something uneasily horny when our relatable point of entry into this seductive world, Carson, is first shown devouring “fairy smut” (i.e., a romantasy novel) on the job. In Yaga , even an explanation of something as dry as how ears work can sound suspiciously like dirty talk. “A whisper, a moan, a groan,” Katherine purrs, her voice as smooth as the whiskey in her glass. “Your bones listen. Before your brain understands, your bones say yes.” Armed with that unexpectedly playful tone and loaded with enough bizarre clues and creepy discoveries to keep up a brisk pace, Yaga ’s half-hour episodes (seven of eight were sent to critics) practically fly by; it’s the kind of show you can devour in a sitting without even meaning to do so. But it’s also one that starts to feel less substantive as its early promise gives way to uneven execution. While Sandler’s lack of preciousness about her own source material — she’s freely rearranged plot points and added characters, such that even those familiar with the original might be thrown for a few loops — saves Yaga from the airlessness so common to stage adaptations, her handling of the expanded scope isn’t quite so deft. Her cast help make up for some of the script’s thinness. Moss is the icy attention-grabber, turning the very quality Yaga points out should make her invisible — her maturity — into a nigh-irresistible source of sexual power; if there’s a single star turn that makes this whole experience worthwhile, it’s hers. In a more restrained role, Backo also acquits herself quite nicely, mapping out Carson’s interiority through the private, silent reactions she allows herself when she thinks no one’s looking. But while Williams demonstrates admirable range with his dual role as obnoxiously cocky Henry and uncomfortably withdrawn Logan, the characters get less screen time, and thus less depth, than one might hope. And though Reid does his best with the brazenly flirtatious, casually chauvinistic Rapp, Yaga badly overplays its hand with his womanizing. Unless there’s a last-minute reveal that the whole town has been dosed with a love potion, not even Reid’s considerable magnetism can justify the immediacy and intensity with which every single gal Rapp encounters practically throws her underwear at him. The coyness that initially seemed so enticing turns underwhelming as it becomes apparent that Yaga is better at suggesting hidden depths than excavating them, and gesturing at grand ideas than shining new light on them. Even the central question of what’s happened to Henry becomes less urgent the more time we spend in Whittock, among an insular cast of citizens who barely seem to notice the guy is missing, let alone care why. Yaga concocts one entertainingly heady brew, thanks to its beguiling mood and fearless cast. It’s just not, in the end, a fully satisfying one. THR

articles.title: Instagram Lines Up Donatella Versace, A$AP Rocky, Finneas, Chloé Zhao as This Year’s Creator Awards Judges (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Instagram Instagram is bringing its in-house creator awards program back for a second year: Instagram Rings. Rings will once again see an all-star panel of judges nominate and select winning creators from across the platform, spanning all types of genres and content, with the winners receiving a physical gold ring designed by Emily Adams Bode Aujla (who is also a judge) as well as special digital creative tools that they can use to distinguish their Instagram profiles. The Hollywood Reporter has learned that the 2026 Rings judges panel will include fashion icon Donatella Versace, A$AP Rocky, designer Emily Adams Bode Aujla, Finneas, director Chloé Zhao, professional skier Mikaela Shiffrin, artists OSGEMEOS, head of Instagram Adam Mosseri, dancer and choreographer Charm La’Donna, Instagram head of fashion partnerships Eva Chen, GQ editor-in-chief Will Welch, makeup artist Isamaya Ffrench, chef Vikas Khanna, and creator Jack Edwards. “We really wanted to have this like global mix of people who are moving culture forward in their respective fields and beyond,” Chen tells THR . “It’s people we think that are doing interesting things in the world as well as on Instagram, and who’ve charted their own course.” Chen says that the judges will be both nominating and selecting the winners, “I love watching the conversations where it’s like actors on actors, icons on icons, and that’s kind of the approach we took,” Chen says. “[The winners are] artists who are on their way to becoming iconic in their fields, chosen by like fellow icons, and so it’s not chosen by an algorithm, it is chosen by people in the fields and who are out there in the world who are discovering and inspired by like what their peers are doing on Instagram, and so the thing that we are not centering this around is follower count.” As for what changes the Rings program will in its second year, Chen says that they wanted to complement the physical ring with more of a digital presence, expanding beyonf the gold ring around their profile to include other things. And longer-term, Instagram wants to build an entire community around Rings, seeing as the honorees will be different year after year. Chen notes that the pool of winners will rise from 25 last year to 50 this year. “One of our goals for this program, is year-over-year for you to feel like you are part of this like community of people, and so to me, this program will be a success if a year one winner like strikes up a conversation with a year two winner, and they exchange numbers or they start DMing and they collab on something together,” Chen says. “That sense of connection and community is one of I think the goals for this program. Every year the pool is going to increase, and so hopefully with this year we’re able to start forging those connections and creating that sense of feeling of like you’re part of this group of people who have been recognized.” Instagram will announce this year’s Rings honorees later this month. THR

articles.title: Lin-Manuel Miranda’s ‘Warriors’ Sets Broadway Cast
articles.full_text: Oct 20, 2026 5:30am PT Lin-Manuel Miranda’s ‘Warriors’ Sets Broadway Cast By Rebecca Rubin Plus Icon Rebecca Rubin Senior Film and Media Reporter rebeccaarubin Latest Lin-Manuel Miranda’s ‘Warriors’ Sets Broadway Cast 2 hours ago Box Office: ‘La Bola Negra’ Scores $277,500 From Four Theaters as Netflix Reports Grosses for First Time Ever 2 days ago Box Office: ‘You Can See Everything’ Stuns With $15 Million Debut, ‘Street Fighter’ Leads With $31 Million 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Alyssa Greenberg/WWD Lin-Manuel Miranda has announced the cast for his next Broadway venture, “ Warriors ,” which comes a decade after “Hamilton” became a pop culture sensation. The upcoming production, which opens in the spring, will star Jaci Calderon, Aneesa Folds, Amber Gray, Julia Harriman, Sasha Hutchings, Gizel Jiménez, Jasmine Cephas Jones, Kenita R. Miller, Sasha Allen, Casey Likes, and Donald Webber Jr. — several of whom have either worked on prior iterations of “Warriors” or appeared in Miranda’s other shows, “Hamilton” and “In the Heights. Additional cast members will be announced at a later date. Related Stories '14th,' 'You Can See Everything' and 'Once Upon a Time in Harlem' Lead Critics Choice Documentary Awards Nominations Nathan Fielder and Elizabeth Holmes Are This Year’s Ultimate Deep-Cut Halloween Costume Duo “Warriors” will begin previews at the Lunt-Fontanne Theatre on March 9 ahead of opening night on April 8. Popular on Variety “Warriors” features a book, music and lyrics by co-writers Miranda and Eisa Davis. Based on Sol Yurick’s 1965 novel and Paramount’s 1979 action film, “Warriors” follows a fictional New York gang from the Bronx to their home turf in Coney Island after they’re framed for the murder of a respected gang leader. The movie version of “Warriors” isn’t a musical, but it does feature songs by Barry De Vorzon, Joe Walsh and Arnold McCuller. The stage show originated as a 2024 concept album, executive produced by Nas and produced by musician Mike Elizondo. It featured the voices of Ms. Lauryn Hill, Busta Rhymes, Marc Anthony, Billy Porter, Ghostface Killah, RZA, Colman Domingo, Cam’ron, and Kim Dracula. “We’re having the time of our lives making ‘Warriors.’ It’s a rollercoaster like the Coney Island Cyclone, with all the action of Walter Hill’s classic film,” Miranda and Davis said in a statement. “It’s a New York story to the bone, with music steeped in all the genres that were born and revolutionized here, from hip-hop to salsa to ska and metal and everything in between. It’s an edge-of-your-seat journey from Brooklyn to the Bronx and back again. It’s a dream of a more peaceful city where we all come home alive. This is the sound of something being born.” “Warriors” will be directed by Jenny Koons and co-directed and choreographed by Andy Blankenbuehler, a Tony winner who worked with Miranda on “In the Heights” and “Hamilton.” Producers include Thomas Kail (“Hamilton”), Miranda and his father, Luis A. Miranda, Jr., and Jeffrey Seller. “Warriors” features scenic design by David Korins, costume design by Dede Ayite, lighting design by Natasha Katz, sound design by Jason Crystal, projection design by Hana S. Kim, fight direction by Drew Leary, music supervision by Kurt Crowley, and orchestrations by Kurt Crowley, Mike Elizondo and Scott Wasserman. articles.title: Prince Harry Opens Up About Move Back to England and Wanting to ‘Work It Out’ With King Charles and Prince William: ‘The Most Important Thing Is to Reconcile’
articles.full_text: Oct 20, 2026 5:37am PT Prince Harry Opens Up About Move Back to England and Wanting to ‘Work It Out’ With King Charles and Prince William: ‘The Most Important Thing Is to Reconcile’ By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest LuckyChap International Hires Experienced Searchlight Exec Katie Goodson-Thomas as President of Film 1 hour ago Prince Harry Opens Up About Move Back to England and Wanting to ‘Work It Out’ With King Charles and Prince William: ‘The Most Important Thing Is to Reconcile’ 2 hours ago Emily Watson Joins ‘The Drive,’ Inspired by JFK Assassination, as Exec Producer (EXCLUSIVE) 3 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images Prince Harry says he wants to make peace with both his father and brother. Speaking in his first major interview since returning to the U.K. with his family earlier in the summer, the Duke of Sussex discussed his complicated and fractured relationship with King Charles and Prince William, claiming that he wanted to fix the much-publicized family rift. “Some people don’t want it to work out. I want it to work out. With everything else that’s going on in the world, the most important thing is to reconcile — that’s the key point,” he told GQ . “Scars stick around forever. But what your perception is, and what your mindset is to those things that have happened, letting go of the past. That’s something that I would encourage everybody to do: If there’s certain things from the past that are still affecting you every day, that’s harder to let go of. But, for me, there’s enough drama in the world and enough drama in people’s lives to continue with issues with family.” Related Stories Oscars: Rwanda Selects 'Ben'Imana' as First-Ever Entry to International Feature Race Amanda Seyfried Rejects Sex Scenes and Turned Down a TV Series Where 'I'd Have to Have Sex All the Time': I Don't Want to Be 'Naked With a Stranger' Harry raised eyebrows in August when it was revealed that he was moving back to the U.K. alongside his wife Meghan Markle and their two children after six years living in California. Unsurprisingly, numerous rumors spread as to why they were ditching life in the U.S. and returning home after their famed “Megxit” in 2020. Popular on Variety Speaking of his return to England and his relationship with the country after several tumultuous years spent dealing with the press (with whom he’s had several legal battles), Harry said his “attitude” had changed. “I think once you’ve been through it, once you’ve been able to talk about it, and raise awareness to it, then people see it for what it is, it makes the environment slightly easier. It’s not going to necessarily stop the behavior, but I think the behavior might — my hope that it will — change,” he said. “What happened back then was then. What’s happened over that over the last six years has been a continuation of that. Some battles that had been fought—and necessarily so. With everything else that’s going on in the world, there’s aspects of the past that I’m sure all of us — me, my family, and some of the British press—that we’d all like to leave behind us and work for the greater good.” Harry, who in the last few years has released a bestselling memoir that detailed his difficult family relationships, and front a Netflix docuseries that did the same, also told GQ that he’s been “really criticized” for telling his story. “I find it fascinating because everybody else is allowed to tell their version of my story, but God forbid I should be able to tell the other side of it.” Charlize Theron on ‘The Odyssey’ Becoming Universal’s Highest-Grossing Movie and Raising Millions to Fight Femicide in Africa With CTAOP Loading comments...
