articles.title: U2 Set For Halftime Performance During Netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve NFL Broadcast
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Katie Goodson-Thomas Joins LuckyChap International As President Of Film British Council’s Film Lab Africa Previews ‘TABOO’ Anthology Series At London Screening Indonesian Star & ‘Reacher’ Actress Agnez Mo Joins Nicolas Cage & Michael Sheen In Cyber-Thriller ‘C.L.A.Y.’ View All October 20, 2026 6:04am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Win McNamee/Getty Images U2 will perform at halftime during Netflix ’s Thanksgiving Eve coverage of the Green Bay Packers vs. the Los Angeles Rams. The performance marks the band’s first return to an NFL field since 2002, when they performed at Super Bowl XXXVI, which, coincidentally, also featured the Rams, then the St. Louis Rams. The team lost to Bill Belichick’s Patriots in a tight championship game. The Packers/Rams game will be the first time the NFL is holding a Thanksgiving Eve game. The pre-Turkey slot has traditionally been dominated by the NBA, which last year held its first Thanksgiving Eve tripleheader. But the NFL continues to encroach on the NBA’s space on the broadcasting calendar. In recent years, the NFL has scheduled multiple games on Christmas Day, which had traditionally been known as an NBA holiday. Last year, the NFL trounced the NBA in the Christmas Day ratings, even with many of the league’s high-profile talents such as Patrick Mahomes not featuring due to injury. Related Stories Sports 'Star Wars' Headed To Super Bowl LXI For Animated Altcast On Disney+, Disney Channel and Disney XD Politics 'Friday Night Lights' Stars Hit The Field To Aid James Talarico's Smashmouth Attempt To Score A Texas Senate Race Win Netflix also carried last year’s Christmas Day NFL games. Snoop Dogg performed at halftime during the streamer’s broadcast of the Detroit Lions vs. Minnesota Vikings. Beyoncé led the halftime performance during Netflix’s first Christmas Day broadcast in 2024. Watch on Deadline Discussing U2’s performance, Ted Sarandos, co-CEO of Netflix, said: “There’s a reason U2 has headlined stadiums for decades: they don’t just perform, they deliver iconic moments audiences remember forever. We’re thrilled that they’ll bring that same magic to the NFL stage on Netflix. articles.title: Katie Goodson-Thomas Joins LuckyChap International As President Of Film
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac British Council’s Film Lab Africa Previews ‘TABOO’ Anthology Series At London Screening Indonesian Star & ‘Reacher’ Actress Agnez Mo Joins Nicolas Cage & Michael Sheen In Cyber-Thriller ‘C.L.A.Y.’ Thessaloniki: Walter Thompson-Hernández’s ‘If I Go Will They Miss Me’ Among Titles Set For International Competition View All October 20, 2026 6:41am Add us as a Google Preferred Source LuckyChap International Katie Goodson-Thomas has joined LuckyChap International as President of Film. The veteran UK exec was most recently Executive Vice President and Co-Head of Production and Development at Searchlight Pictures. The company has said Goodson-Thomas will officially take up her position in the new year and will lead LuckyChap International’s film slate in close partnership with Co-Managing Directors Mona Qureshi and Tanya Qureshi. Goodson-Thomas was at Searchlight for more than a decade. She oversaw several high-profile titles such as Yorgos Lanthimos’ The Favourite and Poor Things , Martin McDonagh’s Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri, The Banshees of Inisherin and the upcoming Wild Horse Nine, as well as All of Us Strangers, The Roses and Alice Birch’s forthcoming directorial debut Sweetsick , starring Cate Blanchett. Related Stories News LuckyChap Launches International Venture With Mediawan; Outfit Will Be Led By Managing Directors Mona Qureshi & Tanya Qureshi News U2 Set For Haltime Performance During Netflix's Thanksgiving Eve NFL Broadcast LuckyChap’s U.S. partners, Margot Robbie, Tom Ackerley, Josey McNamara and Milan Popelka, said Goodson-Thomas brings “undeniable creative talents, vision and depth of experience to LuckyChap International.” Watch on Deadline “She’s such a kindred spirit culturally, and we’ve long admired her ability to spot exceptional filmmaking talent and champion their projects from the very beginning all the way through,” they continued. “We genuinely couldn’t be more excited to have her join us on this adventure, and to forge a killer slate together that we can all be incredibly proud of.” Goodson-Thomas added: “The LuckyChap team has exceptional taste, fearlessness and a creative identity entirely its own, as well as an infectious sense of possibility about what the company can achieve. Searchlight has been such an incredible creative home for me that I always knew it would take somewhere truly special to tempt me away. The opportunity to join that alongside Mona, Tanya and such a brilliant team was simply too exciting to resist. The UK and Europe are full of remarkable talent, and I’m hugely ambitious about what we can find, back and get made together.” BBC Closing ‘Fleabag’ Network BBC Three Once Again Banijay’s Bassetti On Europe Vs Studios Battle; Edward Berger On Netflix Axed As Netflix Film Boss, Latest In Streamer Purge Of Top Execs Gwyneth Paltrow To Star In ‘The Apology’ Series At Netflix; 2-Season Order Set Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Netflix’s ‘The Hunting Wives’ Season 2 Trailer Promises “Someone Is Going Down”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Lin-Manuel Miranda’s ‘Warriors’ Broadway Cast To Include Casey Likes, Amber Gray & Jasmine Cephas Jones; Opening Date, Venue Announced Controversial ‘Downstate’ Again Delays Broadway Previews Due To Illness ‘Other Desert Cities’ Review: Julia Louis-Dreyfus Gets Seriously Funny For Broadway Debut View All October 20, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The second season of Netflix ‘s The Hunting Wives promises yet more mystery and risqué goings-on when the series returns next month, with a new trailer – set to the tune of the old, aptly titled Nancy Sinatra hit “Bang Bang” – promising plenty of action on both fronts. With talk of “evil-doers,” “Texas justice” and the pledge that “someone is going down” – and the clip makes clear that Hunting Wives chooses that phrase carefully – the new trailer offers a few hints as to what fans can expect from the new eight-episode season, which launches November 26. The logline: “At the start of Season 2, Sophie and Margo are on the outs. But soon enough, old secrets and new foes force them back together. As they play their dangerous games, the question arises. Are they the hunters or the hunted?” Related Stories News U2 Set For Haltime Performance During Netflix's Thanksgiving Eve NFL Broadcast News Netflix Faces Anxious Wall Street As Earnings Season Kicks Off Watch the trailer above. articles.title: Russell Brand Accuser Says She Reported Comedian To Channel 4 In 2009 After He Allegedly Lay His Head On Her Lap & Demanded Massage
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Russell Brand Accuser Alleges Witnesses Were Present When He “Grabbed My Face” & “Pushed His Body Against Mine” At Radio Station Former A24 Docs Chief Joins ‘Oasis: Don’t Look Back In Anger’ Outfit Magna Studios Soccer YouTuber Eman SV2 Launches Creator Company View All October 20, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand Getty Editor’s note: T his story contains details of alleged sexual offenses that some readers may find distressing . A woman has revealed that she complained to Channel 4 about Russell Brand’s behavior in 2009 after he allegedly put his head in her lap and demanded a massage, a court has heard. The woman, whom we are calling Complainant 6 (C6) as she has a lifelong right to anonymity , was working for Channel 4 at the time of the alleged attack. Giving evidence as part of Brand’s rape trial, C6 claimed she reported her experience to her line manager and was assured the matter had been escalated. Related Stories Legal Russell Brand Accuser Alleges Witnesses Were Present When He "Grabbed My Face" & "Pushed His Body Against Mine" At Radio Station News Ex-MTV Worker Didn't Report Alleged Russell Brand Rape Because "Media Industry Protects Its Own" Brand faces three charges of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one of indecent assault based on allegations made by six women . He will set out his defense later in the trial, denies all charges and has pleaded not guilty. Deadline has been reporting from a live video feed of the courtroom since the trial began, but a tech outage meant remote access was down this morning. Watch on Deadline In evidence to London’s Southwark Crown Court, C6 alleged that the comedian and actor had forced her to give him a massage. Speaking from behind a screen, she said she was working for Channel 4 at the time and had “briefly” met Brand once before. According to Sky News, C6 alleged Brand briefly left the room they were both in, returned and lay his head on her lap, before saying, “Come on then.” C6 alleged she could feel his breath on her vagina. “I just thought I need to get him off me, so my hands went down at a diagonal [during the massage]. I was so repulsed by the situation I just thought, ‘Oh, you’re so bony. Ugh,” she was quoted by Sky News as telling the courtroom. The court has been told repeatedly that Brand declined to answer questions when interviewed by police. He instead relied on a prepared statement, in which he claimed that he did not recall meeting the women and did not remember their names. He said any sexual contact was consensual. Yesterday at the trial, a former MTV employee said she didn’t initially report her allegation of rape against Brand because she feared being “seen as trouble.” The trial continues. articles.title: Netflix’s Jinny Howe Restructures UCAN Scripted Operation By Genre, Ups Cole Galvin To VP
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Netflix’s Jinny Howe Restructures U.S.-Canada Scripted Operation By Genre, Ups Cole Galvin To VP Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘The Gilded Age’: 2 Supporting Characters Not Returning For Season 4 Jeff Daniels To Star In ‘Bannerman’ TV Series For AMC & Netflix Gwyneth Paltrow To Star In ‘The Apology’ A24 Series Which Lands 2-Season Order At Netflix With Thomas Vinterberg Directing View All October 20, 2026 7:05am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jinny Howe Netflix EXCLUSIVE : Jinny Howe , Netflix ‘s Head of UCAN (U.S.-Canada) Scripted Series, is introducing a new structure to the division she has overseen for almost 14 months. The changes include breaking the teams into genre-specific pods, Cole Galvin being elevated from Director to VP and Neil Thomas to Director, with former Media Res President of Scripted Lindsey Springer joining as Director. The reorg had been in the works for awhile, way before the layoffs last Wednesday that impacted 1,000 across Netflix, including several director and manager-level executives in the scripted series operation, and the major Netflix executive shakeup the following day, which saw Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria exiting , replaced by Peter Rice . Related Stories News Netflix's 'The Hunting Wives' Season 2 Trailer Promises "Someone Is Going Down" News U2 Set For Halftime Performance During Netflix's Thanksgiving Eve NFL Broadcast Changes of that caliber often have a ripple effect, with the attention quickly focusing on two of Bajaria’s direct reports, Howe and Netflix Head of Film Dan Lin. As Deadline reported on the day of the Bajaria-Rice switch , a Lin exit was likely, one by Howe was not. Watch on Deadline Lin was ousted over the weekend , while Howe’s move to restructure her division is further confirmation that she is staying on, along with her stepping up over the weekend to nab The Apology , a hot series project starring Gwyneth Paltrow, with a two-season order . Rice is said to have spoken with Howe about working together. A rising executive at Netflix where she has had four promotions since joining the company in 2018 as VP, Drama Series, Howe has shepherded seven series that have landed on Netflix’s Most Popular English series list. She manages the largest market in Netflix’s global business, driving roughly 35% of overall revenue and about 50 greenlights this year. Howe had not reorganized the UCAN Scripted Series operations since she took over at the end of August 2025 following the departure of Peter Friedlander. The goal for the new structure is to provide more depth and curation in specific lanes instead of spreading attention across every lane at once, better match of material to executives with expertise in a space and strong relationships with those creators, and better specialization. Drama Development The team overseeing all drama (except prestige fare), which has been overseen by VP, Drama Development Michael Azzolino since January 2025, will be divided into two areas led by Azzolino and Cole Galvin , who both will report to Howe. Drama, Thriller, & YA , run by Galvin, is targeting co-viewing adult audience with a female skew. It will focus on sophisticated relationship dramas (family, friendship, workplace), propulsive mystery/thrillers ( The Apology, God of the Woods, His & Hers ), YA/early adult and romance ( Lovesick, Calabasas, Poser ). Joining his team as Director, Drama Development is Lindsay Springer will report to Cole. Genre, Action, & Crime , run by Azzolino, is targeting co-viewing adult audience with a female skew. It will focus on action, adventure, sci-fi, world-building, horror, westerns, spy dramas, and crime. Continuing to report to Azzolino and part of his pod are the tentpole/IP team led by Teddy Biaselli, who was promoted to VP last November, and Carrie Gillogly (Director, Drama Development) who will be shepherding muscular programming that does not fall into Biaselli’s purview. Comedy Development The lanes under Netflix’s VP, Comedy Tracey Pakosta, who continues as head of the department will be led by her existing team members: Brooke Kessler (Director, Comedy), in charge of the Commercial Comedy strategy, creating big, entertainment-forward, broadly appealing content for large audiences (Nobody Wants This, Running Point, Tires); and Andrea Alvarado (Director, Comedy), overseeing the Auteur-Driven strategy, curating comedy IP and creating more risk-forward, unique, award-focused content. Continuing in their existing roles on Paskosta’s team are Robbie Praw (VP, Stand-up Comedy), who lead Stand-up Comedy and the newly formed Netflix Is a Joke Studio, a mini studio/incubator working across formats with comedian talent in-house, and Billy Wee (Director, Comedy), who continues to lead Adult Animation. Studio The team led by Nne Ebong (VP, Studio Scripted Series), which manages talent deals and titles, will continue to focus on self-generating, ground-up, early stage development on shows that are not actively coming in through the open marketplace (The Decorator, The Understudy). Neil Thomas, who joined Netflix in 2023, has been promoted to Director, Studio Scripted Series. Current Programming & Specialty Renate Radford (VP, Current Scripted Series) will continue to lead current programming, and Nora Skinner (VP, Specialty Scripted Series) will continue to be in charge of Specialty, which is elevated, prestige series. The seven titles Howe has steered onto Netflix’s Most Popular list are I Will Find You, His & Hers, The Night Agent, Bridgerton S1, Inventing Anna, Maid, and Queen Charlotte: A Bridgerton Story. Out of Netflix’s 111 Emmy nominations this year, 83 of them came from the scripted series and variety specials on Howe’s slate. Howe also has been aggressive in securring competitive packages, winning the bvidding for such projects as The Corrections (Meryl Streep) and Hancock Park (Regé-Jean Page). Galvin has been at Netflix since late 2017 when he joined as Manager. He was promoted to Director of Original Series in June 2019. During his tenure, Galvin developed one of Netflix’s biggest YA series Ginny & Georgia . He also has been involved in the English-language adaptations of Harlan Coben’s novels, from the 2020 The Stranger to this year’s I Will Find You, which made Netflix’s Most Popular English Series list at No.5. Other recent series he worked on include East of Eden and The Beast In Me. After starting his career in the mailroom of WME, Galvin became an assistant to then-President of Universal Television Bela Bajaria before getting promoted to coordinator and then Director, Drama Development. In November 2017, he followed Bajaria to Netflix where she was most recently Chief Content Officer until her exit last week. ‘Fleabag’ Network BBC Three Closing Again; 100 Layoffs Coming In News Division Tilda Swinton Sets New York Stage Debut In ‘Man To Man’ This Winter U2 Set For Halftime Performance During Netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve NFL Show Banijay’s Bassetti On Europe Vs Studios Battle; Edward Berger On Netflix Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Angry Golf Bros Tried to Ruin Heather McMahon. She Released a Hulu Special Instead
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Netflix Film Head Dan Lin Out close By Mikey O'Connell Plus Icon Mikey O'Connell Senior Entertainment Editor View All October 19, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Heather McMahon Courtesy of For a brief moment in 2025, it seemed like Heather McMahon was about to be canceled — and over a sequence of events so preposterous that the comedian couldn’t have scripted it herself. Hired to emcee the first tee of the Ryder Cup, the annual tournament that’s meant to be a friendly battle between American and European golfers, she was struggling to win over her crowd: a rowdy, largely drunk, overwhelmingly male and decidedly American horde at the Long Island course. When they started chanting “fuck you, Rory,” a dig at Northern Irish golf star Rory McIlroy, McMahon saw an opportunity to ingratiate herself with her new audience. What she got was a minor international incident . Related Stories TV Everybody Needs to Calm Down -- Comedian Laura Ramoso Says She Can Help With That Business Bowen Yang and Matt Rogers' 'Las Culturistas' to Stream On Disney+, Hulu The tournament fired McMahon. Tensions between the two teams escalated. She issued a public apology to McIlroy, but it was too late. For 72 hours, she was the recipient of the golf subsection of the manosphere’s vitriol and threats. She says she fielded challenges to meet up for physical fights. When she returned from a brief social media blackout, she was relieved to see her feed had been cleansed. “Taylor Swift really saved my ass,” recalls McMahon. “It was so bad for three days, and then she dropped Life of a Showgirl. The entire news cycle had changed.” But the impact of her brief cancellation stuck with McMahon, most auspiciously in her new special. By a Thread , which dropped on Hulu over the weekend, opens with McMahon’s vivid retelling of the event and the ensuing fallout. She also tackles myriad other subjects, but it’s a hell of a way to open the show. Speaking during a recent of The Hollywood Reporter podcast I’m Having an Episode (listen tot he full episode on Spotify , Amazon Music , Apple ), she talked about the similarities between sexism in sports and comedy — and how her enthusiasm for Pitbull landed her a Guinness World Record. With all respect to the emotional toll this cost you … as reasons for being “canceled” go, this one is pretty cartoonish. It’s hilarious. It’s insane. For the first three days, a full 72 hours, it was very scary. I had grown men sending me personal messages, messaging my managers, my publicists, everybody. “Have Heather meet me outside of XYZ steakhouse in Atlanta. We’re ready to brawl.” It is insane what people will send from their personal accounts. Like, this is from Bill. He’s an accountant. I can see what firm he works at. What was scary was that I had never been in that sort of situation, specifically in a man’s world. My audience is strongly females and fab gays. They get me. Afterwards, of course, every single one of my buddies in comedy messaged me like, “This is gold. This is the best thing that could happen to you.” Once I had apologized, once we got over the hump, I was like, there’s so much here. Having been raised in a very golf-centric family myself, what struck me about your experience is how rowdy the tournament crowds have gotten. It’s like the dark side of Happy Gilmore . How do you see it? Golf is in a really weird space. I grew up playing golf. I was a golfer in high school. It’s in my blood. My husband and I go to The Masters every year. The Ryder Cup has always been known to be heavily competitive between Europe and America. But it’s always been in good fun? I think [having it in Long Island], the already the weird animosity that America was having to outsiders, I don’t think they were set up for success that year. And, I’ll fall on the sword. I did not help the cause. It’s just really wild. What does golf want to be? Is it all buttoned up like The Masters? Is it trying to be Happy Gilmore? I do think golf needed like shake off the cobwebs, quit being as stuffy, but it doesn’t know where it wants to go. Has this has this experience changed your relationship golf? Yes and no. Golf has had some real moments recently. The Calloway situation! Who the fuck signed off on this shit? [ Calloway partnered with Good Good Golf on a commercial that depicted a man assaulting a woman .] You watch that and realize that this is the problem. I learned that men don’t want women in their spaces. You learn that a little bit in comedy, too. We’re already having to like elbow our way into rooms and to get the respect that we deserve. But the sports world? I had so many sports reporters and women in the business reach out to me say, “This happens across every sport. We all deal with the craziness.” I’m not even shitting on golf, because I’m still a huge fan, but I did just learn like I don’t need to be put in those spaces. I can enjoy it and do my thing. I’m only going to LPGA events now. Like that’s what I want to focus on and and root for the girls. It put a bad taste in my mouth for the the manosphere in general. So you’re watching the LPGA. Did you watch Rory win the Masters this year? I went to the Masters and got to see him win again. I’m still a huge fan. It’s not the players. They’re doing their thing. It’s just this kind of weird environment with some of the the male fans these days. And again, I apologized, but I do think, had a male comedian been in my shoes, we would have never had this conversation. They wouldn’t have given a shit. Dudes being dudes. Set it on fire, man. In a much lighter arena, I would like to address your Pitbull affinity. I started dressing in drag as Pitbull like 10 years ago, on a whim one Halloween. I went around trick-or-treating with a bunch of my friends’ kids and they had no idea it was me for like the first hour and a half. They just thought some creepy guy was following them. Then I started doing impressions as him. By my first tour, people just knew that was my shtick. I love Pitbull. But how did you come play such a prominent role at this past summer’s largest recorded gathering of Baldies — the people who wear bald caps to Pitbull shows? This past summer I get a text from a Miami number, and it’s Armando [Pérez], the real Pitbull. He’s like, “Heather, I’ve seen all your stuff. I adore you. We have to have you be a part of this Guinness Book of World Records party in Hyde Park.” So I end up going to London, I’m in drag. I host this full countdown to the concert with two other guys. I think like 75,000 people came out, but the people actually there in time to be counted for the Guinness Record was around like 22,000. It was just incredible. Guinness sent me a plaque that’s like, “You were a part of it.” It was unreal. And I got to hang out with Armando. They say, “Don’t meet your heroes,” in this business. But meet Pitbull. THR

articles.title: Entertainment 360, Griffin Gaming Launch HITpoint to Bring Characters, Stories to Film, TV
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Netflix Film Head Dan Lin Out close By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 19, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Walton Goggins in 'Fallout.' Prime Video Game on! Talent management and production company Entertainment 360 ( Game of Thrones, Ripley , Stick ), based in Century City, and Santa Monica-based gaming-centric venture capital firm Griffin Gaming Partners have teamed up to launch HITpoint Entertainment, a new company “dedicated to bringing the characters, worlds, and stories of video games to film and television.” HITpoint brings together the talent and production expertise of Entertainment 360 with Griffin Gaming ‘s relationships in the sector. Griffin has more than $1.6 billion in assets under management with its investments across the video game industry and adjacent spaces. Earlier this year , Griffin launched a fund for independent gaming titles with Hollywood potential. Both companies have experience at the intersection of gaming and Hollywood. Entertainment 360 clients are writing and starring in the upcoming The Legend of Zelda film, and the firm is also producing a recently unveiled an adaptation deal with Universal for an Atari property that wasn’t immediately disclosed. And Peter Levin , co-founder and managing director of Griffin Gaming, played a key role in bringing Fallout to the screen. “HITpoint will source, develop, package, and produce adaptations across the full range of genres represented in gaming – from action, horror, and high-concept spectacle to comedy, romance, and coming-of-age stories,” the partners said. The new company recognizes how core gaming has become in the entertainment landscape, with more than 3.7 billion people worldwide estimated to be actively playing video games. “Gen Z, which accounted for nearly 40 percent of North American moviegoers last year, ranks gaming as its favorite form of entertainment,” the partners also highlighted. Recent hit screen adaptations of games include A Minecraft Movie , Amazon’s Fallout series and HBO’s The Last of Us . They have “demonstrated the enormous potential of gaming IP across both theaters and streaming,” Griffin and Entertainment 360 said. “HITpoint will combine Griffin’s relationships with game developers and publishers with Entertainment 360’s producing track record on IP-driven franchises, including Game of Thrones. In addition to providing opportunities for the firm’s clients, the new venture will mine relationships across the broader creative community, pairing each property with the filmmakers, talent, and studio partners best suited to bring it to the screen.” The new company wants to pursue both established hit franchises and fast-growing independent games, drawing in part on Griffin’s new indie game fund to identify breakout titles and creators. “Video games represent one of the most exciting sources of stories and characters for film and television, but adapting them successfully requires a real understanding of the creativity and passion developers bring to their work,” said Levin. “Griffin has spent many years building trusted relationships across the gaming community, from major publishers to the independent studios we support. We see this vehicle as a differentiating resource for our 100+ portfolio companies, our strategic partners as well as the gaming ecosystem writ large. I couldn’t be more excited to partner with the team at Entertainment 360 and give fans new ways to experience the stories they already love.” “For younger audiences, games aren’t a side interest. They are where many of their favorite characters, stories, and worlds live,” said Entertainment 360, which was founded in 2002 and received a strategic minority investment from private equity firm Carlyle in 2025, allowing it to invest in its business. “There has long been an infrastructure in Hollywood for discovering books and other underlying material early. HITpoint brings that same focus to gaming. Together with Griffin, we can identify compelling IP at an early stage, bring it into a development environment, and pair it with filmmakers who genuinely understand the material and what makes it special.” Dedicated hires to manage HITpoint will be unveiled at a later stage. Respect for the source material will be central to HITpoint’s culture and business approach. “The company will keep game creators closely involved from initial development through production, aligning incentives while giving them direct access to leading writers, filmmakers, actors, and producing partners,” the partners highlighted. THR

articles.title: Russell Brand Trial: Police Asked Accuser What She Was Wearing During Alleged Oral Rape in Bar Toilet
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Netflix Film Head Dan Lin Out close By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All October 19, 2026 7:02am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand and his wife, Laura Gallacher, arrive at Southwark Crown Court on Oct. 19, 2026. Leon Neal/Getty Images Russell Brand ‘s rape and sexual assault trial is in its second week at London’s Southwark Crown Court. As a reminder, the ex-presenter, actor and comedian is accused of three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one allegation of indecent assault, with six women alleging crimes dating from 1999 to 2009. He denies all of the claims, which were presented in depth by lead prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones last week. The first complainant gave evidence on Thursday , telling the court about her and Brand’s 1999 encounter in a Bournemouth hotel room: “He did rape me, he did push me on the bed. … He did pull my clothes off.” She said the experience left her feeling “dirty” and in fear that she was pregnant. Brand maintains the interaction was consensual. Related Stories Movies Edward Berger Talks Filmmaking in a Streaming Age: "The Movie Industry Needed Netflix to Wake Up" Business Netflix Earnings Preview: Not the Time to Chill On Monday, another complainant’s police interview played as Brand watched on and his wife, Laura Gallacher, sat in the public gallery. The accuser went into detail about meeting Brand at a bar in Soho, London, in 2004. He went on to star in the likes of St. Trinian’s and Forgetting Sarah Marshall but was best known at this time for presenting Big Brother ‘s spinoff show. According to Sky News , the complainant said Brand grabbed at her breasts after talking “for a minute max.” She said Brand took her arm and dragged her into the toilets close to where they were standing. Here, the court was shown a floor plan of the bar. She said Brand stood on the toilet seat. “It happened so fast,” said the complainant in the police interview. “He pulled me over and put his penis in my mouth.” The woman explained that she tried to resist but Brand said, “‘Don’t be a spoilsport,’ or something along those lines.” She became emotional as she spoke, according to Sky, imagining others asking her: “‘Why didn’t you bite him?’ I just froze. I didn’t know what to do.” She alleged Brand then “ejaculated into my mouth.” The accuser recalled banging on the locked toilet door to escape and says a man outside may have shouted to ask if everything was okay. Brand acted as if “nothing had happened” and said to her: “I guess we should swap numbers now,” according to the woman. She says she was steered into a car with Brand, still in “disbelief and shock.” While in the car, she realized Brand had his penis out, the complainant claimed. She alleges he said, “Come on and suck it.” She says she told him no, and that Brand “took no for an answer.” On what was going through her mind at the time of the alleged oral rape, the accuser reportedly said: “If I do this maybe he won’t try to rape me further. … He won’t try to invade my body. … I felt it was the lesser of two evils.” She described it as a “survival thing,” and remembered thinking: “Just do what he wants and get out of here, and then it’s done. … I closed my eyes and tried to not be there.” She didn’t come forward to the police because, said the woman, she “felt shame that someone could do that to me.” It was only in 2023, after seeing reports in the press around other allegations against Brand, that she decided to come forward. Sky News added that the police interview showed the officer probing the woman on what she was wearing during the attack. She told them: “It wouldn’t have been boobs hanging out. I don’t dress like that.” The complainant says she was “absolutely appalled” when her employer, MTV, later hired him to be a presenter. “Any time he was in the building, I just refused to go over or to any parties. If I knew where he was, I would just avoid,” she said. “I did see him in the distance a couple of times. He probably wouldn’t even recognize me. I’m just a face.” The woman was then cross-examined by Brand’s defense lawyer, Ian Winter, who asked her on Monday: “Can you explain why you didn’t tell a single human being until you rang the police in September 2023?” She maintains she did tell people that Brand had grabbed her breasts while standing at the bar. Winter responded: “I suggest you didn’t tell anyone.” The woman answers: “I don’t agree with your summation.” Sky says the defense then asked: “Why didn’t you slap his face?” She said: “I was completely shocked someone I’d be talking to for around 30 seconds would do that to me.” Winter suggested it would have been “perfectly easy” for her to “struggle” or “kick off” about the interaction. She disagreed, telling the courtroom that the bar had “cleared out” a little. “I was dragged [into the toilet] against my will,” she added. Brand has pleaded not guilty to all the charges. The trial could last up to six weeks. THR

articles.title: Banijay CEO: We Need Scale to Compete With Big Tech
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Netflix Film Head Dan Lin Out close By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 19, 2026 7:26am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Marco Bassetti, CEO, Banijay Entertainment Tyler Miller Banijay Entertainment CEO Marco Bassetti fittingly discussed creating an even bigger indie production and distribution colossus in once-imperial Rome on Monday. “We want to define ourselves as an entertainment company,” after adding distribution and sports assets to an established production powerhouse, UK-based Bassetti said on stage at the Westin Excelsior Hotel as he addressed a global business upended by consolidation and technological disruption. But while describing the super indie as “big,” Bassetti added that, against Silicon Valley competitors like Alphabet and Meta as they grow exponentially, Banijay has had to get bigger still. The move by Banijay to scale up follows earlier acquisitions, like Zodiak Media in 2015 and Endemol Shine in 2019 . Banijay, while enabling All3Media producers a bigger international footprint, has also extended and expanded its own reach into live events, sports and across social media with Little Dot Studios. “We are producers on a global scale, we have to be big. But if we want to define the market everywhere, we’re small,” Bassetti said of the paradox of a growing European entertainment giant still being dwarfed in a fast-changing global entertainment and media business driven by Silicon Valley innovations. His comments follow the international production giant completing mega-merger with fellow indie giant All3Media to create a new $8.5 billion super indie. Not surprisingly, Bassetti during his informal conversation discussed the benefits of scale in today’s international TV business. “Every time we have a tranformational deal, it’s much better to buy a company with proven success, instead of starting from scratch. Getting to market as short as possible is crucial to our strategy,” he argued. The new London-based production and distribution group brings together nearly 200 production companies and labels across 25 territories, including the companies that make and sell such shows as The Traitors , Big Brother , Survivor , MasterChef , Peaky Blinders and Black Mirror , some hundreds of thousands of hours of programming, and combined revenues of $8.5 billion. The enlarged giant amid continuing industry consolidation is seen as beneficial as broadcasters and streamers need hit TV content and original IP as production budgets shrink after the end fo the Peak TV era. Speaking of scale, Bassetti talked about the recent Paramount takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery and as a combined company is set to produce 30 feature films each year and 80 series of all types on some 20 different networks and streamers. “The latest one is the biggest one of all — $111 million billion dollars,” he said of the combined studio led by CEO David Ellison, who he considers a friend. “You have to look at how much you invest, and the return on investment,” Bassetti said of his mergers and acquisitions strategy. “if you’re good, it’s an advantage.” THR

articles.title: ‘Slow Horses’ Season 7 Casts Varada Sethu, Tuppence Middleton, Joshua McGuire
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Breaking News Netflix Film Head Dan Lin Out close By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All October 19, 2026 7:31am Add us as a Google Preferred Source From left: Varada Sethu, Tuppence Middleton, Joshua McGuire Danny Kasirye/Michael Shelford/Apple TV Logo text Varada Sethu ( Doctor Who , Andor ), Ethan Moorhouse ( Ludwig , MobLand ), Tuppence Middleton ( Downton Abbey: A New Era ), Merab Ninidze ( Homeland , The Courier ) and Joshua McGuire ( The Gold , Anatomy of a Scandal ) have all joined the seventh season of Apple TV ‘s Slow Horses . The upcoming installment is adapted from the Bad Actors novel in Mick Herron’s popular Slough House book series and is set to see Gary Oldman ‘s Jackson Lamb attempt to hunt and neutralize a mole at the heart of the British government before they can bring down the state. Related Stories News Russell Brand Trial: Police Asked Accuser What She Was Wearing During Alleged Oral Rape in Bar Toilet Movies Edward Berger Talks Filmmaking in a Streaming Age: "The Movie Industry Needed Netflix to Wake Up" His co-star, Jack Lowden , recently made headlines when Oldman suggested he’s on the shortlist for the next James Bond . (Though Oldman later clarified his comments .) Monday’s casting news comes shortly after the confirmation of Slow Horses ‘ season eight renewal , which will depict Herron’s ninth novel in the series, Clown Town . That installment will follow Lamb and Diana Taverner ( Kristin Scott Thomas ) as they face off in their most explosive confrontation yet. Current castmembers also include Saskia Reeves as Catherine Standish, Christopher Cho as tech expert Roddy, Rosalind Eleazar as Louisa, Aimee-Ffion Edwards as Shirley, Tom Brooke as JK Coe and Jonathan Pryce as David Cartwright. Season six has also seen the return of Hugo Weaving as Frank Harkness, River’s birth father, and Olivia Cooke as Sid, an agent who was believed dead. The series is produced for Apple TV by See-Saw Films, with Jamie Laurenson, Hakan Kousetta, Iain Canning, Emile Sherman, Dan Hassid, Helen Gregory, Mick Herron, Gail Mutrux, Douglas Urbanski and Oldman serving as executive producers. Season seven is adapted for television and executive produced by Ben Vanstone, with Robert McKillop set to direct. See-Saw Films is part of the Mediawan group. THR

articles.title: Fox Sports Soccer Announcer John Strong Is the New Voice of the Westminster Dog Show (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Breaking News Netflix Film Head Dan Lin Out close By Tony Maglio Plus Icon Tony Maglio View All October 19, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source John Strong and his doggies Courtesy John Strong Logo text Fox Sports ‘ lead soccer play-by-play announcer John Strong is now sitting — and presumably staying — in the big chair. Strong has been named the new in-venue show announcer for the Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show , The Hollywood Reporter has learned, which returns to New York City in early 2027 with its 151st installment. Strong, who has called the FIFA World Cup and Major League Soccer (MLS), succeeds Michael J. LaFave as the “Voice of Westminster.” LaFave put 25 years into the role. As announced in May, the Westminster dog show will stream on Netflix . The Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show is the second-longest continuously held sporting event, behind only the Kentucky Derby. Related Stories Movies Edward Berger Talks Filmmaking in a Streaming Age: "The Movie Industry Needed Netflix to Wake Up" Business Netflix Earnings Preview: Not the Time to Chill Strong is no new pup here — he’s called the play-by-play for the Masters Agility Championship and hosted the Best of Breed competition the past seven years for Fox. “As the legacy of Westminster continues, we are overjoyed to welcome John back to the show in this exciting new role,” said Dr. Donald Sturz, president of The Westminster Kennel Club. “John has called some of the world’s most historic sporting moments, including some of Westminster’s very own. We know he will bring his signature flair, expert commentary and genuine love of dogs to every moment leading up to Best in Show.” “I am humbled and honored to step into this prestigious role for The Westminster Kennel Club,” added Strong. “I look forward to honoring the legacy of Westminster and celebrating the future of this beloved sporting event while lending my passion for dogs and live sports experience to the world’s top canine competitors.” “Bark! Bark!” said the dogs, probably. (But actually, they probably didn’t — these pooches are very well-behaved.) For the first time, the Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show’s evening group judging and Best in Show competition will stream live on Netflix from Madison Square Garden on Feb. 1-2. The daytime breed competitions at the Jacob K. Javits Convention Center will stream live on The Westminster Kennel Club’s website and YouTube channel. The Javits competitions begin on Jan. 30; the 14th annual Masters Agility Championship will be taped and streamed on Netflix at a later date. THR

articles.title: CNN Shocker: Christiane Amanpour to Exit News Channel Next Year
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Netflix Film Head Dan Lin Out close By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 19, 2026 8:26am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Christiane Amanpour Photo by Sean Gallup/Getty Images CNN is losing one of its highest-profile anchors and correspondents next year. Christiane Amanpour will scale back her work at CNN over the next few months, and leave the channel entirely next June. CNN CEO Mark Thompson shared the news in a note to staff Monday morning. “Christiane has thought carefully about this decision, and she and I have been discussing it for some months,” he wrote. “Like so many CNNers who will hear the news today, I’m very sorry to see her go, but I’ve come to accept that this is the right time for her, both personally and professionally.” Amanpour has been with CNN for 43 years, becoming perhaps its most famous foreign correspondent, and a staple of its lineup. Why Amanpour is leaving is not clear, but the announcement comes just weeks after Skydance completed its acquisition of Warner bros. Discovery, bringing CNN into its fold. Thompson will continue to lead CNN for the time being, though longer-term anything could happen. “After many months of thought and a few sleepless nights, I have decided to separate from CNN, my partner of 43 fantastic years!” she said in a statement. “I will end my daily shows across CNN and PBS at the end of this year, while continuing to maintain a weekly show on CNN through May and working on a smooth transition through June. Amanpour had publicly expressed concern with the takeover, saying at an event in May that “Clearly I’m concerned, and I’m not sure how much I’m allowed to say about a corporate thing that’s under way, but I am obviously, as a person, as a journalist with a record, concerned, and I’m concerned based on what’s happened to the other things that [Ellison has] taken over already, like CBS News.” For now, she will gradually pull back on her CNN International show this year bfore it ends next May. She will continue to host her podcast The Ex Filed, which she co-hosts with her ex-husband and former U.S. diplomat and Assistant Secretary of State Jamie Rubin. The podcast is not produced by CNN. “I want to thank all the amazingly talented people I’ve worked with throughout this incredible journey. Especially my beloved show teams and field crews,” she continued. “From my very first big exciting assignment covering the First Gulf War, to the horrors of the Bosnian War, Rwanda, Afghanistan, Ukrain and Iran and all the points in between, it’s the teams and the camaraderie that counted so much, as we together battled to seek the facts, the evidence and the humanity, so that CNN could always broadcast the truth about the world and to the world, without fear nor favor.” You can read Thompson’s note to staff below. Dear all, I’m writing today with news about a CNN icon – and our dear friend and colleague – Christiane Amanpour. After more than 43 years at CNN, Christiane has decided that the time is right to begin a new chapter. Early in 2027, she will scale back her CNN International show, Amanpour, to once a week. The program will conclude in May, and she will leave CNN at the end of June. Christiane has thought carefully about this decision, and she and I have been discussing it for some months. Like so many CNNers who will hear the news today, I’m very sorry to see her go, but I’ve come to accept that this is the right time for her, both personally and professionally. Christiane has been a household name around the world for decades. Yet she began more than 40 years ago not as one of the biggest stars in CNN’s history, but as a news desk assistant in our Atlanta newsroom. Famously, one of her bosses told her back then that she didn’t have what it took to become a foreign correspondent – or to hold any on-air role at all. Boy, did she prove him wrong! It would be impossible to list all of her reporting triumphs, exclusive interviews, awards and broadcasting firsts, or the many other accomplishments that have made her one of the most trusted and beloved journalists anywhere. We will make sure to share and celebrate them all before she departs next year. In the meantime, on behalf of the entire CNN leadership team, I want to thank Christiane for 43 extraordinary years of remarkable journalism, loyalty and friendship. Mark THR

articles.title: Netflix Film Head Dan Lin Out
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Netflix Film Head Dan Lin Out close By Mia Galuppo Plus Icon Mia Galuppo Senior Entertainment Reporter miagaluppo Follow Sign Up View All October 19, 2026 8:38am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Dan Lin Jon Kopaloff/Getty Images for American Cinematheque Dan Lin is out as Netflix ‘s film chief, sources tell The Hollywood Reporter . The news comes as the streamer cuts from its uppermost ranks and implements layoffs that will affect roughly 1,000 people, the company’s biggest cut since 2022. Prior to Lin, chief content officer Bela Bajaria was exited, along with VP of film Doug Belgrad and a series of high-ranking television executives. It is unclear who will assume Lin’s role, but the understanding is that Peter Rice, who took over the chief content officer post, will be in charge of finding new leadership. Netflix did not immediately reply for comment. Lin joined Netflix in 2024, taking over from then film chief Scott Stuber. Under Stuber, Netflix became known as the place where name filmmakers could land big budgets and paydays as the traditional studios implemented more cost-conscious spending practices. During this time, the streamer consistently ended up with best picture nominations, but top awards have notoriously evaded Netflix films. Lin, who was hired by Bajaria, was brought in to curb spending while (ideally) increasing the quality of the entire film slate, not just the titles from big-name directors. Under Lin, the streamer‘s movies division was reorganized by genre , with deputies like Kira Goldberg and Niija Kuykendall handling films that fell under categories like sci-fi, rom-com and family film. Netflix began offering more mid-size films that have been ignored by theatrical players, including big book adaptations like Remarkably Bright Creatures and People We Meet on Vacation , as well as mid-budget action films like Apex and The RIP. (This is not to say that Netflix’s Lin tenure was without big swings — see: Greta Gerwig‘s Narnia movie due out next year or David Fincher’s The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth — but the offerings no doubt slowed.) Lin came from his production company Rideback, which minted the $1 billion grossing Aladdin and was involved in the hit It movies as well as The Lego Movies . He departed the company when he joined Netflix, leaving partners at the helm who found another $1 billion hit with last summer’s live-action Lilo & Stitch . Presumably, he could return to Rideback now that his Netflix tenure is up. As of late, the streamer hasn’t been able to capture audience interest, at least at the rate co-CEO Ted Sarandos would like, with viewership and subscriber growth stagnant. Under Rice‘s leadership, Netflix will focus on “creating big, buzzy hits,“ as Sarandos wrote in his memo to staff. THR

articles.title: ‘Carrie’ Star Alison Thornton Knows Exactly How You Feel About Her Polarizing Character
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Breaking News Netflix Film Head Dan Lin Out close Alison Thornton Jenna Berman Logo text Alison Thornton is fully embracing the divided online discourse provoked by her polarizing character in Prime Video ‘s Carrie . The Vancouver native actress, who is in the midst of continued press for Mike Flanagan ‘s series adaptation of Stephen King’s classic, which was released on Prime Video on Oct. 7, knows her Chris Hargensen villain role has given viewers moral whiplash. “Some people hate Chris, some people forgive Chris, some people want to give her a hug, and some people cheer when she dies,” Thornton tells The Hollywood Reporter, laughing. Related Stories Beyond the Book Inside Tubi's Plan to Build an R.L. Stine Cinematic Universe TV Amazon Orders Tennis Drama 'Rally' From Julie Plec and Andre Agassi The 27-year-old actress has an array of onscreen credits already, including Girlfriends’ Guide to Divorce , Dare Me and School Spirits . However, her portrayal of the tragic villain in Flanagan’s adaptation of King’s Carrie felt like a stroke of destiny. Thornton revealed that the iconic author was a “huge deal” in her household while growing up. “My mom is the biggest Stephen King fan, and I grew up reading a lot of his books . … I had actually read Carrie twice before even auditioning,” she shares. Despite being familiar with the story of the bullied teen with telekinetic powers, reading the script for Flanagan’s take on the horror caught the actress off guard, realizing how his expanded version added new layers of depth to the ensemble of characters originally introduced in the 1974 novel and its previous film adaptations. Flanagan’s Carrie marks the first time the novel has been reimagined for the small screen with the cast also including Summer H. Howell and Samantha Sloyan. The role of Chris Hargensen has been portrayed by Nancy Allen, Emilie de Ravin and Portia Doubleday in previous screen versions of the book, but in Flanagan’s Carrie , viewers see a more developed Chris, and chronicling how her internal conflicts leads her to a path of tragic disaster. Thornton has been navigating the whirlwind of attention surrounding her role at the heart of the show’s intense discourse. “The response has been incredible. I love seeing people argue about the characters, about who’s morally wrong and who’s morally right. All the conversations around redemption and kindness versus cruelty are exactly what we wanted,” she says. Throughout Flanagan’s eight-episode series, each of the characters are placed at the center of a complex moral debate, continually forced to choose between kindness and cruelty. As their interpersonal dynamics fray, a constant tug-of-war between power and vulnerability not only shapes the characters’ individual choices, but also profoundly impacts their ultimate journeys and tragic fates. Thornton’s Chris journey is one that reflects a tragic spiral and fate. But the series’ choice to humanize the villain without excusing her actions was intentional, Thornton explains. “Reasons are not excuses,” she says. Though she even admits, “If I knew her, I’d want to give her a hug and also yell at her.” In a chat with THR , Thornton reflects on the divisiveness over her character, the parallel journey of Chris and Carrie and responds to those Christine theories. It’s been a little while since the show came out. What have you made of the response, and how are you feeling now that it’s out there for audiences to watch? It’s so wild that the show is finally out, because we shot it over a year ago. The response has been incredible. I love seeing people argue about the characters, about who’s morally wrong and who’s morally right. All the conversations around redemption and kindness versus cruelty are exactly what we wanted. Some people hate Chris, some people forgive Chris, some people want to give her a hug, and some people cheer when she dies. (Laughs.) I love the debate around her. The conversation is really meaningful to me. Take me back to the start. Were you familiar with the Carrie book and the other adaptations? What did you think of the story overall? I was very familiar with Carrie going into this. Stephen King is a huge deal in my household. My mom is the biggest Stephen King fan, and I grew up reading a lot of his books. I’d seen the Brian De Palma movie and the 2013 movie, and I had actually read Carrie twice before even auditioning, so I went in thinking I knew exactly what it was going to be. Then I read Mike [Flanagan]’s scripts, and seeing how much time we had with the characters and how three-dimensional everyone was, I was blown away. I was also a fan of Mike Flanagan, so I was over the moon to be in the Flanniverse and the Stephen King universe. The characters aren’t necessarily what I was expecting from the book, which was such a treat to play. Everyone is so layered. In the show we get to learn Chris’s home dynamic. Her mother is no longer in the picture, and her father is there but not a loving, present figure. Can you talk about the Chris we first meet and how this family dynamic has impacted her? The family dynamic is a huge reason for the choices Chris makes. Working with Michael Trucco and Heather Graham was a dream. One thing I thought was so important is that Chris has truly been shielded from facing any consequences her whole life. Her dad has always covered everything up for her, so I don’t think she understands what adult repercussions look like, and I don’t think she understands how much damage she can actually cause, to other people and to herself. Working on the family dynamic and seeing Michael’s portrayal of John Hargensen, I saw just how ruthless he was. They have a winner mentality, and they view cruelty and being mean as power. There were so many moments in the scripts, and in things we found on the day, where the only time Chris feels affection from her dad is when she’s making fun of Brooklyn or being cruel to someone else. That was so interesting to me: her lack of good role models and her lack of emotional support at home. In the very first scene where we meet Chris and John, Chris doesn’t get breakfast from her dad. She ends up getting a burrito from Sue (Siena Agudong). She really doesn’t have any parental figures at home, which is tragic for her. “She’s such a product of how she was raised, which of course doesn’t justify anything she does, because she does really unforgivable things,“ Thornton says of her villain character. Jenna Berman At school, Chris projects a strong, unfazed persona. She has popularity, power and a following, while Carrie is the complete opposite, someone who can easily become a target. The saying is hurt people hurt people. Do you think Carrie is just a bystander Chris chooses to project her hurt and anger onto, and that it could easily have been someone else? Why Carrie and why not Brooklyn? I love that question, because I really don’t think it has anything to do with Carrie herself. As you said, it’s just bad timing for Carrie. I love that Carrie and Brooklyn look kind of similar, and that Brooklyn is off limits. I think a lot of Chris’s reason for targeting Carrie is how vulnerable she is and also the threat of losing Sue. Carrie enters the picture, and Sue gravitates toward her and shows her all this warmth. I think Chris is really envious of that, especially since she’s losing her support system at home, and Sue has been the only parent and healthy role model Chris has ever had. When that gets threatened, Chris thinks, “I need to push this girl as far away from our friend group as possible and hopefully get Sue back.” There’s also something interesting in Summer’s beautiful portrayal of Carrie and how optimistic she is. She’s so wholesome and genuinely kind, and people start gravitating toward her. Carrie gets more and more popular throughout the show, and I think that’s really threatening to Chris because of how she was raised. She’s been taught that you get power from making people afraid of you and being cruel. Chris has such a sinister view of the world, so seeing this girl come in and truly embody kindness, and that being enough to give her power, is so threatening to Chris’ identity. She can’t handle it. So there are a lot of reasons Chris is unaware of for why she chooses to bully Carrie, but none of them have to do with Carrie herself. Despite being different, Carrie and Chris have more in common than they may think. Both of their parents project their own faults onto their kids, yet Carrie and Chris turn out differently. Carrie wants to escape and be free from her mom, whereas Chris internalizes that cruelty and uses it against others. Do you think Chris could ever see that similarity, that they’re two sides of the same coin? I don’t think Chris has the perspective to see that. She’s so caught up in her own pain and her own world. But I love the parallel between them. One thing I thought was so cool in the scripts is that, as you said, they both lose their emotional support at home in the first episode. They both discover power early on: for Carrie it’s telekinesis, and for Chris it’s social media and bullying. They’re both then influenced by outside forces to do the wrong thing: for Carrie it’s Emaline (Thalia Dudek), and for Chris it’s Billy (Arthur Conti). They’re on a parallel track the whole time. I think one of the most interesting conversations around the show is: once you discover you have that power, whatever it may be, do you use it for good or for bad? I don’t think Chris is old enough or has the maturity to see the tragedy that they could actually have been friends, that they’re quite similar and could have helped each other out. That’s such a shame. The characters all have a choice between kindness and cruelty, yet they all seem to take the more destructive path. Chris takes the cruel path, but it doesn’t always seem solid. There are moments, like with Billy holding the rock over the freeway or wanting to hit Carrie with his car, where she shows hesitance and that there’s still a moral compass there. What did you make of her internal conflict? I think there are many moments in the show where Chris hesitates. One of my favorites is the trench sequence at the construction site. I really don’t think Chris knows how far she’s going to take it. She’s discovering this power as she goes, and she’s being influenced by Billy, who at that point is the only person validating her and giving her any kind of attention. He likes it when she’s cruel, so she plays that up around him, especially once Sue has exited Chris’ life. Chris really needs someone to say, “Hey, you’re OK, you’re enough. All of these dark thoughts, acting on them is the wrong choice.” Billy (portrayed by Arthur Conti) “is the only person validating her and giving her any kind of attention,“ Thornton says of their dynamic. Prime Video I also love how many moments there are where I think Chris is about to apologize. I think she’s about to apologize in the principal’s office. I think she wants so badly to apologize when she’s alone with Carrie in the bathroom. The internal conflict she’s facing is that she wants everything to go away and go back to normal, but she’s also hearing her dad’s voice in her head, the idea that the Hargensens don’t lose, and that if she apologizes, she’s admitting defeat. Combine that with her never actually being held responsible for any of her actions, and it’s a perfect storm. She’s so stubborn that she can’t make things right, which is also very sad to me. There’s something really scary about being at that age, where you don’t really understand the consequences yet, or how much damage you can do through cruelty. She’s facing all of that at the same time, which is unfortunate for her. It does not end well. You mentioned how she wants to go back to normal, but there’s a new normal that she’s unwilling to accept. She has one identity crisis, which will probably be one of many she’d have in life, but it’s so tragic to her that she thinks, “Everything’s over. I can’t handle it.” I think she really needed the promise of going to Duke and getting out of Chamberlain, getting away from her mom and her dad. She needed that so much, especially with Sue. When that falls apart, she’s just like, “Well, I don’t know what to do now. It’s done.” “I saw just how ruthless he was. They have a winner mentality, and they view cruelty and being mean as power,“ Thornton says of Chris‘ father (portrayed by Michael Trucco). Prime Video You brought up the bathroom scene with Carrie. In that moment, Carrie genuinely wants to understand and seems to give Chris the chance to explain so they can move on. It could have been the moment everything changed for the better. Can you talk more about that scene? I love that scene so much. Episode six was the last episode we shot, so we’d been building toward it the whole time. Summer and I kept calling it the real mediation, because the parents hijack the actual mediation. The scene felt so complicated and layered to me. Carrie’s question, “Why me?” is such a fair question, and no one has really asked Chris that. It’s the only scene where Chris and Carrie are alone together, and I think it catches Chris off guard. I don’t think she’s thought about it: why, genuinely, did you do this? At that point she’s dug herself into such a deep hole that I don’t think she can process anything clearly. Carrie does get through to her for a second. Chris is actually reflecting for the first time and almost apologizes, and then at the last minute she pulls back. I remember reading it and wanting to shake her and say, “Come on, you’re so close! You could have fixed everything.” It’s my favorite scene in the show, I think, because it’s when Chris doubles down. After that, it’s the point of no return for her. There’s a scene where it alternates between Chris and Carrie in the car. Carrie is happy and free, allowing herself to be a normal teenager for the first time, lifting the car without even knowing it. In contrast, we see Chris completely breaking down, hiding it from Sue while Sue drives. If she could just show that part of herself, I’d imagine people would be there for her more than she thinks. I totally agree. Chris has unfortunately been taught that vulnerability is weakness. If she could open up to the people around her and lean on Sue. … I think she could benefit from some therapy and just talking about her feelings. She’s such a product of how she was raised, which of course doesn’t justify anything she does, because she does really unforgivable things. That scene is so interesting to me, too, because from Chris’ perspective, that was supposed to be her night, her at her most powerful, running this party. It wasn’t supposed to end with Carrie on top. Chris doesn’t really witness that, but once again it’s the parallel between them. They’re on very similar tracks. They’re two sides of the same coin, essentially. “Working with Michael Trucco and Heather Graham was a dream.“ (Pictured from left: Trucco, Thornton and Heather Graham.) Prime Video With all the characters in the show, there’s an exploration of losing control, taking control and relinquishing control, and Chris experiences all of those. What was Chris’ relationship with control like to you, and how did it shape the path she’s on? She’s seemingly losing control and trying to take it back, but in the wrong way. Chris has always been someone who has had control and power, just because of her family circumstances, and she loses it really quickly in the first episode. I think that’s a big reason she makes the “Carrie Red” account. It’s the only power she has. Bullying Carrie is a new kind of power she finds, essentially the only control in her life. The more followers she gets and the more people send posts to “Carrie Red,” the more she realizes she’s having a pretty large impact, and that feels good, especially since she doesn’t have power in any other part of her life at that moment. As you said, she’s grasping for these morsels of power and control, and she finds them in really destructive places. Do you think her friendship with Sue would have been repairable? We see the moment on the “Carrie Red” social media account where Chris reveals Sue‘s big secret yet we also see Chris learn Sue is the one to betrayed her by recording her admission of being behind the social media account. I would hope so, but I feel like the scars would have been so deep that it would have taken so much work. I think they could use years apart. They have a really co-dependent, really toxic friendship. I do think Chris addresses Sue’s betrayal by posting the photo of Sue’s pregnancy test. It’s a little bit of revenge and a cry for help at the same time. But the damage is so deep in that friendship that I think they should probably separate for a while and see who they are without each other. Chris needed support and love from other people, and she was very dependent on Sue for that. She needed other healthy friendships and role models in her life, too. “They have a really co-dependent, really toxic friendship,“ Thornton says of Chris and Sue (portrayed by Siena Agudong). Prime Video The final scene between Chris and Carrie where Chris is about to die, she attempts to apologize to Carrie. Do you think she was genuinely saying sorry in that moment, or was it an act of desperation to save herself? I think Chris is genuinely sorry. I think of the conversation she has with Billy right before the car flips, when she looks at him and says, “What did we do?” She’s facing so much guilt and remorse, and she’s being forced to see the impact of her actions. In those final moments, she knows what’s going to happen. She knows there’s nothing she can do, and there’s no point in fighting. She just wants to make things as right as possible before she dies. So I think it’s genuine remorse. The show ends on a cliffhanger, and there’s been a lot of online discussion and conspiracy theories about the story’s connections and where it could lead. One is that Chris’ soul possesses Billy’s car at her death and turns it into Stephen King’s famous killer car, Christine. Have you heard that? Do you have thoughts? I’ve heard that one, and I really like it. It’s so exciting. The evil car, of course. I trust Mike Flanagan. Whatever he thinks for season two is in his hands. But I do love the conspiracy theories. I love seeing people say, “They’re wearing the same necklace! What does that mean?” People keep sending me screenshots of conspiracy theories asking, “What is this?” And I’m like, “I don’t know. I didn’t notice that either.” (Laughs.) I do think the Christine connection makes the most sense. I could play a car for a few hours in hair and makeup, easy! I’m so here for it! This show’s version of Chris is one where we can humanize her and understand how she became this deeply broken person, but we can also still not excuse a single thing she does. After playing her, do you feel protective of her? What do you make of playing a character that people can be conflicted over? She’s polarizing.I have very complicated feelings. What I was really holding on to is that reasons are not excuses. We see her reasoning, and I understand her decision-making, and she’s also making the wrong choices. When I was playing her, the only way to play her was to have so much empathy for her. If I knew her, I’d want to give her a hug and also yell at her. I feel so bad for her. I really think her death is a tragedy, and it’s a tragedy also because she’ll never be able to make things right. My interpretation is that I would have loved to see her go to juvie, get some therapy, do community service and then actually get on a better path. I was never cheering for her to die. There are moments in the show where I’m like, “What are you doing? Please stop. This is cruel.” But, again, reasons are not excuses. And I love that she’s polarizing. It’s so fun. I imagine things are still very Carrie -focused right now, but what are you working on, and what roles and stories are you hoping to tell? I imagine this feels like a big chapter in your career, and hopefully one of many. I can’t say too much. I do have a movie coming out soon called And Love Knocked , but there are a few things on the horizon that I can’t share yet. Carrie was a dream project with dream collaborators: the cast, Mike Flanagan, Stephen King. It was such a dream role and such a pivotal chapter in my life, and it was a masterclass to work with everyone. Right now I’m just in Carrie world and reveling in that. We shall see! Mike Flanagan is known for having his staple ensembles and teaming with the same actors in different projects. Is there another story he could take on that you’d love to be part of? I would love to work with him on anything! He’s such an incredible director and a great guy, and I’d love to keep working with him. The cast of actors he works with are all so phenomenal. I keep saying I would love a Pet Sematary remake, because it’s my favorite Stephen King book, so I’m putting it out there! About those Christine rumors: “I could play a car for a few hours in hair and makeup, easy! I’m so here for it!“ Jenna Berman THR

articles.title: Foo Fighters, Weezer, Sublime Join KROQ’s 2026 Almost Acoustic Christmas Lineup
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Netflix Film Head Dan Lin Out close By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All October 19, 2026 8:55am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Dave Grohl of Foo Fighters. Daniel Boczarski/Getty Images for Harley-Davidson Foo Fighters , Weezer and Sublime are among the recording acts that will be on the lineup for this year’s KROQ Almost Acoustic Christmas. Interpol, Joyce Manor, Julia Wolf, Almost Monday and The Linda Lindas also will be headliners at this year’s event, which will take place Dec. 12 at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles. KROQ, the legendary alternative rock station in Los Angeles that’s owned by Audacy, is bringing the event back to Southern California for its 35th year. The annual event also gives back to the local community, with proceeds benefiting Para Los Niños and Al Wooten Jr. Youth Center. Related Stories Music Young Miko Gets Flirty With L.A. During Her Late Checkout Tour Music Miley Cyrus Returns to the Stage With Emotional and Cathartic Hollywood Bowl Show Founded in 1980 in Skid Row, Los Angeles, Para Los Niños partners with children, youth, and their families through integrated education, wellness, support and advocacy to address individual and systemic barriers and create pathways to success. The Al Wooten Jr. Youth Center in Los Angeles hosts free after-school and low-cost summer programs, through which it revitalizes and empowers communities in crisis by providing a safe, nurturing environment committed to good citizenship and academic excellence. “Almost Acoustic Christmas has always been about the bands and their connection with our listeners,” said Kevin Weatherly, senior vp programming at KROQ. “That’s what makes this show so special, and we’re incredibly grateful to the artists who take the time to be part of it. Celebrating 35 years of this together is pretty amazing. And to be able to give back to two great organizations supporting local youth makes it that much more meaningful.” Tickets go on sale at noon Oct. 30. THR

articles.title: Locarno Golden Leopard Winner Sho Miyake Gets First North American Retrospective, 14-City Tour (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Oct 19, 2026 7:00am PT Locarno Golden Leopard Winner Sho Miyake Gets First North American Retrospective, 14-City Tour (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Locarno Golden Leopard Winner Sho Miyake Gets First North American Retrospective, 14-City Tour (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Ju Ji-hoon, Choo Young-woo Return for Netflix’s ‘The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call’ Seasons 2 and 3 6 hours ago Selena Gomez Reveals Vaping Nicotine Changed Her Voice: ‘It’s Not Worth It’ 6 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Bitters End Japanese director Sho Miyake , whose “Two Seasons, Two Strangers” won the Golden Leopard at Locarno in 2025, will get his first North American retrospective at New York’s Metrograph from Nov. 7–17. It is one stop on a Japan Foundation tour of 14 cities in eight countries. The Metrograph program, titled “Unspoken Gestures: The Films of Sho Miyake,” is co-organized and presented by the Japan Foundation. Miyake will attend in person over the opening weekend, and select encore screenings will follow the main run. Related Stories Olivia vs. Olivia: Predicting the Grammys' Album of the Year Contenders... and Why Rodrigo and Dean Are at the Front of the Race Taylor Swift Spends Her 100th Week at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, as 'Life of a Showgirl' Stays on Top in Week 2 of 'Encore' Rebound The series brings together eight of Miyake’s own titles. They include his 2012 debut feature “Playback,” which premiered at Locarno, and “The Cockpit” (2014), a 64-minute film that watches producer-rapper OMSB and his collaborator Bim make a track in a small suburban Tokyo apartment. “And Your Bird Can Sing” (2018) screens with the 2016 short “August 8th,” and “Two Seasons, Two Strangers” is paired with the 2016 short “Nagahama.” Boxing drama “Small, Slow but Steady” (2022) and “All the Long Nights” (2024) round out the lineup. Popular on Variety Miyake has also picked two films that influenced his work as carte blanche selections: David Elfick’s 1973 surf film “Crystal Voyager” and Aoyama Shinji’s 2007 drama “Sad Vacation,” the final part of Aoyama’s “Kitakyushu Saga,” starring Asano Tadanobu. He will introduce both on Nov. 8, after Q&As following “Small, Slow but Steady” and “Two Seasons, Two Strangers” the day before. “For a long time now, Sho Miyake has been one of international cinema’s best-kept secrets, each of his films landing quietly but forcefully amid the cacophony of contemporary film culture. With this retrospective, we’re giving the man a microphone and calling on New York audiences to attend the voice of an essential Japanese film artist,” said Metrograph programmer Edo Choi. The tour opens on Nov. 3 in Washington, D.C., where the Japan Information & Culture Center at the Embassy of Japan will screen “Two Seasons, Two Strangers” and Miyake will join the Q&A remotely. Oklahoma follows from Nov. 9–11, with screenings at the University of Oklahoma’s Meacham Auditorium in Norman and the Oklahoma City Museum of Art. Miyake will also teach a masterclass for a university screenwriting class that is closed to the public. Los Angeles hosts the program Nov. 13–15 at the Japan Foundation, Los Angeles, UCR Arts at the University of California, Riverside, and the American Cinematheque’s Los Feliz Theatre. The lineup there adds King Vidor’s “The Patsy” (1928) and Tony Scott’s “Deja Vu” (2006). Toronto runs Nov. 17–19 at TIFF Bell Lightbox, the Fox Theatre and Paradise Cinema, with Miyake’s 2010 film “Good for Nothing” and Jacques Demy’s “Bay of Angels” (1962) on the bill. In the new year, the tour heads to Paris, Toulouse, Rome, Turin, Madrid, Zurich, Cologne, London and Derby, and wraps in February 2027. Miyake will travel to every city except Washington. In a joint statement, Inoue Ryo and Rokkaku Akinaru of the Japan Foundation pointed to Miyake’s own description of a director’s job as “taking on the responsibility of creating images of humanity.” “We, too, are among the audience members who were once struck and moved by his gaze. We sincerely hope to bring that sense of wonder and emotion to as many viewers as possible in theaters around the world,” they said. Miyake made “Playback” while still in his mid-twenties. Murakami Jun plays an actor nearing 40 who wakes up on the way to a hometown wedding wearing his old school uniform. His friend Hamaguchi Ryusuke compared the film to “a modern-day reincarnation of [John Cassavetes’s] ‘Opening Night.’” “Small, Slow but Steady” stars Kishii Yukino and is drawn from the life of deaf boxer Ogasawara Keiko. “All the Long Nights,” adapted from Seo Maiko’s novel, pairs Matsumura Hokuto and Kamishiraishi Mone as co-workers who form a bond. “Two Seasons, Two Strangers” adapts two manga by Tsuge Yoshiharu and stars Kawai Yuumi, Takada Mansaku, Shim Eun-kyung and Tsutsumi Shinichi.
