articles.title: the events in the Season 22 fin…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Cupertino’ Creators Robert & Michelle King On Episode 2’s Shocking AGI Twist & Predicting The Future Again With AI Guardrails Storyline Netflix Shakeup: Peter Rice Is Welcomed Back To Executive Ranks While Bela Bajaria’s Exit Has Layoff-Weary Staff Bracing For More Upheaval ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ EP Meg Marinis On Season 23 Premiere’s Time Jump, Pregnancy Surprise, James Wolk’s Arrival & Doctor’s Exit; Texas Spinoff Status View All May 7, 2026 8:00pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Grey's Anatomy' ABC SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about the Season 22 finale of Grey’s Anatomy. Grey’s Anatomy may have not ended its 22nd season with the typical jaw-dropping cliffhanger in order to send off veteran cast members Kim Raver and Kevin McKidd , but the finale did offer some big twists, leaving most characters’ futures uncertain. Related Stories News ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ EP On Teddy & Owen’s Emotional Goodbye, Why Kevin McKidd & Kim Raver Are Leaving And “Painful” Network Budget Constraints News Kevin McKidd & Kim Raver React To ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ Exits, Reflect On Long Runs: “It Has Been A True Gift” – See Owen & Teddy Through The Years In a classic Grey’s bait and switch, while the focus early on was on Owen (McKidd) possibly being hurt (or worse) in the bridge collapse, it was Nick (Scott Speedman) who was in fact badly injured. He required a difficult emergency surgery, performed by suspended Bailey (Chandra Wilson) upon Meredith’s (Ellen Pompeo) request. Shaken up by the experience, Meredith proposed to Nick while he was lying in his hospital bed, a throwback to their first meeting when Nick was admitted to Grey Sloan with a failing kidney in Season 14. He said yes, an answer he apparently had had ready since that fateful first encounter. Watch on Deadline In another Grey’s tradition, the finale also included a jaw-dropping WTF moment. Toni (Jen Landon), after some soul-searching over her ex-wife’s appeal to get back together, went to Amelia’s (Caterina Scorsone) apartment to tell her that she had broken it off with her ex and was falling in love with her only to find out that Amelia had hooked up with Cass (Sophia Bush). (Cass had popped in at Grey Sloan earlier in the day to help with the influx of patients from the bridge collapse.) In other developments, Kwan (Harry Shum Jr.) is still fired. He tried to get back on Richard’s (James Pickens Jr.) good graces by helping with injured patients but that didn’t work. New couple Winston and Jules’ secret relationship is no more (secret) after they were intercepted sneaking out of an on-call room by Ben (Jason George), a newly minted plastics fellow. New mom Jo (Camilla Luddington) is facing an existential crisis and may not be a doctor anymore while her supportive husband Link’s (Chris Carmack) dependance on painkillers is becoming worrisome. Bailey, defying her suspension to help save Nick, is considering a career change of her own as she plans to go for a Masters in public health. And the Simone (Alexis Floyd)-Lucas (Nike Terho)-Wes (Trevor Jackson) love triangle, which had been dormant for most of the season, came back in full force after Simone and Lucas slept together and Wes asked her to go steady. Below, Grey’s Anatomy executive producer/showrunner Meg Marinis is breaking down all non-Owen & Teddy developments in the finale and how they would carry over to Season 23, including potential other cast departures and Speedman’s status as his ABC series R.J. Decker is yet to be renewed (but is looking good). For her explanation of McKidd and Kim Raver’s exit and the reasons behind it, r ead Part 1 of Deadline’s interview . ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ (L-R): Scott Speedman as Nick, Ellen Pompeo as Meredith in Season 14. ABC Meredith & Nick: Meet Cute Redo DEADLINE: Meredith and Nick recreated their first encounter for the surprise proposal. How did you settle on that and why did she pop the question? MARINIS : Well, Meredith has always been pretty clear that she didn’t want to get married again after Derek. In truth, she didn’t really want to get married to Derek, they did that in the end because of trying to make sure that they could have the best chances at adopting Zola. And so I think marriage is not something that is ingrained in her, but clearly, when she heard the story of how he wanted to get married in the middle of the season, when his sister came to visit, and how his sister had taken away this happy life from him, I think that got put in the back of her mind that that is something that he’d always wanted, but he’s such a nice guy, he loves her so much that he’s never going to force her to do anything, especially since she had such a painful ending to her first marriage. I think she’s also scared that if she ever got married again, what if she lost him like it happened with Derek? And I think when she realized that you’re going to have that fear no matter what, why not do it? I told Ellen at the beginning of this season, I was like, I want to end with a proposal. And she was like, ‘Agh’. I was like, I do, I do. So it was something that I’ve been planning since the beginning of the season, and it was very seeded with that middle episode between the two of them. I obviously don’t know the fate of R.J. Decker. I haven’t heard anything. And so it was a very small window that we got Scott to come and film in L.A. and so it worked out that, okay, if we can get him in a hospital bed and put him on the table, then we can utilize as much time with Scott that we had. It was kind of a perfect scenario. DEADLINE: You took a leap of fate with the proposal not knowing whether the actor playing the groom-to-be would be available next season. Will it depend on R.J. Decker’ s fate how much we will see of Scott on Grey’s next year? MARINIS : For sure, it will depend on if R.J. Decker goes, and I hope it does for Scott. But he was so game, he flew in on a Friday, we filmed on a Saturday, and we worked it out. He was being part of the Grey’s family. And so we’ll just have to figure out if we can plan in advance with the other show and work it out again. DEADLINE: Are you planning a big wedding? We know Meredith is not keen on the idea but a wedding would bring people back. We haven’t seen many Grey’s alumni for awhile; I feel this season was one of the lightest in terms of cast returns. MARINIS : You know, I don’t, it all really kind of depends on Scott’s schedule and what we decide creatively. I do not think Meredith is a big wedding person, but we’ll just have to see. DEADLINE: And in terms of returns, was it intentional that you had fewer people coming back vs previous seasons? MARINIS : No. When we realized that we needed to exit two characters we wanted to spend the most time on the characters that we have currently. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’: Harry Shum Jr. as Kwan (Blue) Disney/Anne Marie Fox Ben & Kwan: One Rising & One Leaving? DEADLINE: We know about Kim Raver and Kevin McKidd but are other cast members leaving too? For example, Harry Shum Jr. whose character Kwan was fired twice in the last two episodes? MARINIS : His fate is still undecided. Blue is scared out of his mind, so we’ll just have to see when we come back in the fall. He doesn’t have a job at Grey Sloan right now, so we’ll have to see what happens to him. DEADLINE: There was this interesting look on Catherine’s face when Richard kicked Blue out in the finale. It felt like she was persuadable. MARINIS: It’s kind of a different shade on Catherine, it’s nice. DEADLINE: But to reiterate, of the series regulars, no one except Kevin and Kim are leaving, right? MARINIS : We’ll always have to wait to see who shows up in Season 23. DEADLINE: We’ve talked about Ben floating around, trying to find himself since returning to Grey Sloan. He just got this fellowship; has he now settled? MARINIS : I think he’s as settled as Ben Warren can be. But yes, I’m interested in seeing him follow this fellowship and wear those navy scrubs and be looked at someone who has authority now. That was really important to me this season, to bring him out of Bailey’s shadow, to give him a mentor who doesn’t also see him as someone who’s had a bunch of different jobs. She’s just meeting him for the first time as Ben Warren, someone who’s interested in plastics, and so she doesn’t know all the history necessarily. And I think he really is proving himself. I think that was a really powerful story in Episode 17 last week for him, where he saved Maya. He did great work and saved your life and he really deserves those navy scrubs. Bailey & Richard: OGs 4ever DEADLINE: What about Grey’s veterans Chandra Wilson and James Pickens Jr.? Would Bailey’s plan for a degree in public health impact how much she will be on the show next season? And Richard had cancer. Are there any plans for him to scale back? Seems like he’s in every episode. MARINIS : He is in every episode. And those two are our OGs that are the pillars of the show. I do not envision a world where I can scale back on seeing either of them. Just due to the creative, we may be seeing Bailey in a different capacity, though. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ (L-R): Caterina Scorsone as Amelia, Jen Landon as Toni Disney/Anne Marie Fox Toni & Amelia: She Did What?! DEADLINE: You added Jen Landon as plastic surgeon Toni this season. We got this crazy cliffhanger with her and Amelia at the end that opens up two possibilities for Toni next season, her leaving after what happened or her being promoted to series regular. Which on e is it? MARINIS : Well, I love Jen Landon, and we were so lucky to get her and have her, and I think she really enjoyed her time here. Also, her character brings a really great side to Ben Warren, I love their working relationship. She’s this quirky plastic surgeon that we don’t really have a character like her anywhere else, and I would love to have her back. I don’t know if I would use the word promote, because we are in a different time in our industry with the budget, but I would love to have her come back as much as we can. DEADLINE: Speaking of the surprising cliffhanger, where did this seemingly random Amelia and Cass hookup come from? And what does it mean for Amelia and Toni who had just poured her heart out to her? MARINIS : I think Amelia truly felt like Toni was going back to her wife, and I think she was really sad about it. She had an emotional day with Meredith, and this pretty woman asked if she wanted to get coffee after a long day. I know it all happened off screen, but we love the surprise at the end. Obviously, Sophia Bush’s character is married, she’s in an open marriage, so I don’t think Sophia Bush’s character has left her husband or anything. I just think this is more of now Amelia has gotten herself into a little bit of trouble. I think she wants to be with Toni, and I think she was just trying to make herself feel better because she thought she had been rejected. And so, what we have to look for in the future is, can Toni overlook it? Does Amelia need to work her way back or do they have to work together and deny their chemistry while Toni’s repairing her feelings? We’ll just have to wait and see but they’re a great match. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ (L-R): Adelaide Kane as Jules, Anthony Hill as Winston Disney/Anne Marie Fox Winston & Jules: Dangerous Liaison DEADLINE: When we spoke about the power dynamic issue in the Winston and Jules relationship last year, you noted that a lot has changed since Meredith and Derek and that some things that were considered appropriate at the time are not anymore. Yet, you went with the storyline. Why? And what will the repercussions be of them being discovered by Ben? As Winston said when he professed his love to Jules, “I could be fired for everything I’m about to say.” MARINIS : Well, we didn’t see Ben tell Bailey, but you know that that’s going to happen at one point, so I think their little happy bubble will probably be popped, and I think that it’s just going to depend. I mean, Bailey, she’s married to someone who technically was a resident, so we’re just going to have to see how, if it’s hypocritical, for someone to say something. But I think people will have a lot to say about it once they find out that, yes, that was the cliffhanger of, oh no, now everything he was worried about could possibly happen. DEADLINE: But why did you decide to pursue that? And why did Winston do it? There was attraction…. MARINIS : They’re in love, Nellie. He couldn’t deny it. He tried so long. It was two seasons. DEADLINE: Okay, it’s Grey’s , love wins and trumps rules, I guess. MARINIS : But these days we have repercussions, so we’ll have to see what those are. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ Chris Carmack as Link Disney/Anne Marie Fox Jo & Link: Breaking Point DEADLINE: Jo is spiraling, she doesn’t even know if she wants to be any doctor anymore, let alone OB or surgeon. Is her internal crisis triggered by postpartum or is she genuinely not sure about her future? MARINIS : I think it’s a little bit in both. I think when you go through something like postpartum, there’s a little bit of I don’t know what my life should look like, what brings me happiness anymore and what brings me down? I think that it’s something that we really were interested in talking about a lot of times, our characters go through really big health scares, and then in two episodes, they moved along just fine. But I think in particular, especially with mothers and difficult deliveries, no one really talks about that, and it’s a disservice. And especially, just talking to so many people about maternal mortality, everyone always thinks, Oh, if the mom and the babies are saved, it’s a happy ending. Well, yes, it’s a happy ending, but you don’t know the emotional burden that people go through after. We heard from this doctor, and I said, this is too powerful a story not to tell and to let women know that it’s okay that you’re feeling like this. And I think, with the career aspect of it, her trigger is her job, because she’s seeing other women go through it. It’s just, can she maintain that or not? is the big question. DEADLINE: And you don’t have an answer right now? MARINIS: Not for you. DEADLINE: And Link, we’d seen from the beginning of the season where this was headed as he seems to be popping more and more painkillers. Is this going to escalate next season? MARINIS : Yes, we’ll definitely deal with the aftermath of this. He also went through such a big health scare at the beginning of this season, and he’s tried to power through the best he can for Jo. He’s someone who really prides himself on his strength and being there for his partner and his kids. And so I don’t think it’s an option for him to be weak and to not take care of them. We’ll have to look at that. When both members of a couple are going through something, it doesn’t necessarily mean that one person has to power through. It’s okay. I think we’re telling a different story about having to turn to medication to numb, I don’t think it’s going to look like the stereotypical abuse of medication that a lot of other shows and movies have done. I think it’s going to be more nuanced. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ (L-R): Niko Terho as Lucas, Alexis Floyd as Simone Disney/Anne Marie Fox Simone, Lucas & Wes: Three’s Company DEADLINE: Why did you decide to reignite the love triangle between Lucas, Simone and Wes with a big, classic Grey’s finale cliffhanger? MARINIS : Well, I think we put Lucas through it this season with his emotional patient story, Katie. And in that storyline, I think we saw him grow up a lot. I think we saw him grow as a doctor. And I also think Niko Terho had some of his best performances this year. He really went through it with Simone when Katie died. And for Simone, she definitely has feelings to sort out. Wes has been such a casual thing, and he stated that from the very beginning. And also, he’s an intern, she’s a second year, and I think she had always thought that this was just fun, I don’t think she ever thought it was necessarily going to be more than that. And then suddenly, when he’s opening up to her and the finale and saying, Would you want to hang out more?, It’s like, oh, this kind of throws her wrench, because it’s a great looking guy, and he’s clearly a hard working doctor, and you’ve got some pain that she’s seen a little bit about his brother. And then she thought that Lucas was just a one night thing, because that’s what they said, it was mistakes. I think she’s confused. I don’t think she thought both of these options were on the table. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’: Jade Pettyjohn as Dani Disney/Anne Marie Fox New Interns: We Barely Know You DEADLINE: Grey’s introduced a couple of new interns this season but none of them made an impression. Dani had a very memorable first day, but then kind of disappeared. There was a young guy who barely had a couple of lines, two lines. MARINIS : Harrison Meade, yeah. DEADLINE: Any any plans for them to come back? MARINIS : I’d love to see them come back. They really were fun characters to interact with ours. I think just in the last two episodes we had a lot of creative ground to cover with our regulars. articles.title: ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ EP Meg Marinis On Season 23 Premiere’s Time Jump, Pregnancy Surprise, James Wolk’s Arrival & Doctor’s Exit; Texas Spinoff Status
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Cupertino’ Creators Robert & Michelle King On Episode 2’s Shocking AGI Twist & Predicting The Future Again With AI Guardrails Storyline Netflix Shakeup: Peter Rice Is Welcomed Back To Executive Ranks While Bela Bajaria’s Exit Has Layoff-Weary Staff Bracing For More Upheaval ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ EP Meg Marinis On Season 23 Premiere’s Time Jump, Pregnancy Surprise, James Wolk’s Arrival & Doctor’s Exit; Texas Spinoff Status View All October 15, 2026 8:00pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about the Season 23 premiere of ABC’s Grey’s Anatomy. Time did not stand still at Grey Sloan as Grey’s Anatomy returned with its first time jump between seasons in four years. The Season 23 premiere picked up a month after the events in the Season 22 finale . It introduced the finished VIP floor and Seth Norton, played by new recurring cast member James Wolk , a handsome, arrogant surgeon-turned-businessman whose company Olympic Regent Health backed the luxury medical suite. His focus on the bottom line immediately clashed with Meredith’s ( Ellen Pompeo ) compassion, putting the two on a collision course as Norton was revealed at the end of the episode as Grey Sloan’s new Chief of Surgery, Teddy’s (Kim Raver) old job. Related Stories Books Chuck Lorre Q&A On The Care & Feeding Of Sitcom Stars & Why A WGA Strike Doomed Democracy News Ron Perlman Lines Up Hemingway Movie & Updates On 'Sons Of Anarchy' Spinoff 'Legends', That Third 'Hellboy' Film & Next Steps For His Asylm Studios There was no trace in the premiere of Nick (Scott Speedman) or mention of his engagement to Meredith in the S22 finale and no update on Teddy and Owen (Kevin McKidd) an their new life in France. Watch on Deadline At the end of last season, Simone (Alexis Floyd) was faced with Wes (Trevor Jackson) vs. Lucas (Niko Terho) dilemma after the former suggested making their casual relationship official and she had a drunken hookup with the latter. A month later, she is with Wes (and has a new hairstyle) but somehow cannot stop running into shirtless (and sometimes fully unclothed) Lucas. In one of the episode’s big twists, Simone discovered she is pregnant. Ben (Jason George) is still being a gentleman and has not ratted out Winston (Anthony Hill) to Bailey (Chandra Wilson) having a relationship with an intern, Jules (Adelaide Kane), giving Winston another chance to come clean himself. By the end of the premiere, Jules and Winston find themself in an even bigger predicament when Bailey, trying to delegate more so she can pursue a Masters degree, makes Winston residency director — and Jules’ direct boss. Kwan aka Blue (Harry Shum Jr.) is still fired and “self employed.” He returned secretly to Grey Sloan to save the life of his online French teacher with Simone’s help. Jo (Camilla Luddington) appeared fine and back at work but a coding patient triggered painful memories and, in the final seconds of the episode, she told Link (Chris Carmack) that she had quit her job. Just moments prior, Link had swiped some of Jo’s old pain meds as his addiction issues seem to only be getting bigger. Amelia’s (Caterina Scorsone) and Toni (Jen Landon)’s ongoing tension following Amelia’s dalliance with Cass (Sophia Bush) in the S22 finale blew up in a public fight over a patient’s care. The two ultimately reconciled and got back together. In an interview with Deadline, Grey’s Anatomy executive producer/showrunner Meg Marinis addressed the decision to introduce a time jump and a new antagonist played by Wolk as well as Pompeo and Scott Speedman’s availability, and broke down the episode’s biggest twists, including Simone’s pregnancy, Jo’s resignation, Toni & Amelia’s shenanigans, and Winston & Jules’ new dynamic. The Texas native also provided an update on the rural Texas-set spinoff she is co-creating with Grey’s Anatomy creator Shonda Rhimes, which has a straight-to-series order for midseason. DEADLINE: This was the first time jump since Grey’s introduced the new interns at the start of Season 22. Why did you decide to do it? MARINIS : It always allows a little bit more flexibility and storytelling, and I wanted to do something different, but also it allowed us to be able to creatively build that VIP floor, because obviously we didn’t see that VIP floor in the finale, and so yes, that is behind the decision-making. And also I didn’t know if I was going to be able to have Scott Speedman because of R.J. Decker , and we left him in a hospital bed, so that would have been a little bit tricky. DEADLINE: Scott’s Nick and Meredith got engaged in the Season 22 finale but she is not wearing a ring in the premiere. Is the engagement still on? It wasn’t even mentioned. MARINIS : Well, the engagement is still on. Meredith Grey has never really worn a ring, even when she was with Derek. So she’s not necessarily a ring wearer, but that’s not to say that once they get married they may have wedding bands. We’ll pick up that story though, don’t worry. DEADLINE: What does the Season 2 renewal of Scott’s show R.J. Decker mean in terms of his availability? Will you be able to have him on at all this season? MARINIS : Yes, we will see Nick. Obviously scheduling is always tricky, but good thing is it’s the same family with the show, so they help us out a little bit. But yeah, it’s tricky because they don’t shoot here, so it takes a bit of logistical magic, but yes, we’ll see him. [Both Grey’s and R.J. Decker are produced by 20th TV for ABC, filming in California and North Carolina, respectively.] James Wolk Disney/Ser Baffo DEADLINE: Was James Wolk’s character introduced because you knew you wouldn’t have Scott Speedman for long or did you just need to have another person in Meredith’s life? MARINIS : He was introduced as someone for the whole hospital, not necessarily just to play off of Meredith. He’s going to be the source of this conflict between this new floor and the rest of the hospital, and how our other characters play off of that. In particular, we’ll see Richard and how he feels about working side by side with someone who doesn’t really know… That’s the craziest thing, we haven’t had a chief like this who isn’t part of the hospital to begin with, so he’s essentially a stranger to a lot of our people, and he may not see the interpersonal dynamics that everybody else has. DEADLINE: But Seth and Meredith will continue to interact, even if it’s not romantic, right? There was something about them together in the premiere . MARINIS : You’ll see them together again. Nick is the romantic partner but it’s always nice to, I feel like Meredith fights all of our battles for us. She’s the one that always says the thing that we’re always thinking but can’t say, and so we’ll see her say some of that to Seth. DEADLINE: And Nick is fully recovered after the accident, right? MARINIS : He’s doing great. DEADLINE: Meredith was in the premiere before leaving for Boston. How many episodes is Ellen in this season? MARINIS : We don’t have an exact number because we always need to wait to see how our schedule is. But don’t worry, that’s not the last you’ve seen her. You’ll see her several times. MIA Doctors: Teddy, Owen & Kwan DEADLINE: There was only a fleeting reference to Teddy and Owen in the premiere as Winston complained that he has to pick up their cases but no mention how th ey’re doing in France. MARINIS : Because it’s been a month in story time, I think it’s a little odd to keep talking about them, but man, do we miss them? And I miss the actors too. It does feel like there are missing doctors in the hospital, and I did not want for the hospital to seem like they replaced them already, so that’s kind of what Winston is talking about, he’s having to cover for them, and it’s wreaking havoc. DEADLINE: Speaking of missing doctors, Kwan is still fired a month later. He said he’s self-employed in the French class. What is he doing as self-employed? MARINIS : He was just saying that to cover himself with his class. But no, he’s unemployed, and I think he’s a little bit in denial and saying that he likes being unemployed, but we know that’s not real. He definitely misses it. DEADLINE: How has it been sharing Shum Jr. with Dancing ? Did you have to reduce his presence on Grey’s this season? MARINIS : No, we didn’t have to reduce his presence at all. We haven’t adjusted creative yet because Blue is such an important part of the show. Obviously, it can get tricky scheduling, but we knew about this going into it, we had everything on the table at the start of the season. We know which day and a half that they always need him, and we’ve been able to make it work. He’s practicing here, he’s rehearsing outside the stages with his partner. He will tape [Dancing] on Tuesday night and be here at 6:15 the next morning. DEADLINE: Aren’t you concerned that Shum Jr.’s Dancing video packages showing him wearing scrubs on the hospital set of Grey’s spoiled any suspence over Blue’s firing, revealing that he will be back at Grey Sloan? MARINIS : I feel like after watching the premiere, people will know that somehow he’s going to get folded back in. It’s the how is what we’ll discover. DEADLINE : Any chance of Harry dancing on Grey’s? MARINIS : Well, now you know I’m gonna want it. Alexis Floyd, Trevor Jackson, Harry Shum Jr. Disney/Raymond Liu Who’s the Daddy? DEADLINE: Simone’s surprise pregnancy. We saw Wes and Simone in the premiere being careful about condom use. Does that automatically mean Lucas is the dad because he and Simone’s hookup was unplanned or are we going to have another Who’s the daddy mystery like the one with Amelia’s baby? MARINIS : It does not automatically mean it is Lucas. It is a big old question, and it’s messy, and I guess yes, we did it with Amelia, but this is just as fun, and it’s going to play out differently. She’s an amazing surgeon, but when it comes to her personal life, Simone’s a little bit messy. DEADLINE: So we won’t find out right away, the mystery will carry on for awhile? MARINIS : Yeah, I don’t know how you find out. DEADLINE: Simone can count the dates, I guess. MARINIS : It was all happening at once, so it’s pretty tricky. Jen Landon, Chris Carmack, Camilla Luddington Disney/Ser Baffo Jo’s Relapse DEADLINE: I’m glad that you did a course correction on Jo because she seemed too well adjusted at the start of the premiere for someone who was spiraling post-trauma a month ago. We saw that all unravel after she watched a patient being cut open. Was that the trigger for her? MARINIS : We’ll come to understand more specifically in later episodes what her actual triggers are, but, after suffering an almost death experience, when she sees other people doing the same, for me that is that is a trigger. Obviously that person, their chest was cut open, her chest was cut open, so she has that same exact scar, things like that. I just think that it’s seeing people at that pivotal point of, if they’re going to make it or not make it, that coding experience. That elevator was definitely a trigger. DEADLINE: Was Jo quitting just an emotional reaction to a bad day at the hospital that she would overcome or will it play out longer with her staying away from Grey Sloan? MARINIS : It will, being at the hospital in a regular employed fashion, she won’t be there. I mean, she might be at the hospital, but not working shifts every day like she was in the past. This definitely plays out. It’s not in Episode 2, she’s back in scrubs. DEADLINE: Is this a similar situation to when Amelia took a sabbatical after another traumatic experience at Grey Sloan that translated into Caterina going an an extended hiatus . Will Camilla be in fewer episodes this season? MARINIS : No, that is not the situation. This is a creative decision where we wanted to play the reality of what Jo went through, and you’ll see the impact of that on her not being at work, and whether or not she regrets the decision or whether she’s reaffirmed in the decision, we’ll that play out. DEADLINE: So nobody will have significantly reduced episodes this year, right? MARINIS : We always have to kind of wait and see, but right now things are looking fairly normal. DEADLINE: With Jo sidelined, Kwan fired and Teddy and Owen in France, the hospital is four doctors down. Are you planning any other major additions to Grey Sloan’s medical/surgical staff this season besides James’ Seth and Jen’s Toni? MARINIS : No, James Wolk and Jen Landon are our recurring guest surgeons right now. Caterina Scorsone, Jen Landon Disney/Raymond Liu Amelia & Toni Kiss and Make Up DEADLINE: Jen’s Toni and Amelia had a happy ending in the premiere after the heartbreaker of the finale. Yes, a month passed but I feel like you got them back together a little too qu ickly . MARINIS : I need joy, Nellie. DEADLINE: I think Toni was very forgiving, one short speech by Amelia, and that’s all it took. MARINIS : Well, it’s so funny. It was such a debate in the writers room because we were like, oh my gosh, Amelia slept with somebody else, Toni can’t forgive her. But then, Toni was kind of toying with her at the end there, am I going to get back together with my ex, am I not going to get back together with my ex? It’s not that Amelia went into that to cheat on her, it was she was trying to dull the pain that she felt that Toni was going with her ex-wife, and so it’s a bit of a misunderstanding. They’re just so great for each other, and I think also, when you lose a patient together, things change. We’ll see if they can stay happy or not as the episodes play out, but I really love them as a couple, they have great chemistry. DEADLINE: They lost a patient but I’m not sure if they didn’t contribute to that with their fight in the OR over treatment that may have proven costly. It was highly inappropriate too, in front of their colleagues, that was not the place for that. MARINIS : No, of course not. But that’s what Grey’s is, right? We bring our problems to work. DEADLINE: BTW, we saw Toni fly back in the premiere. Was she gone from Seattle for the entire month after the finale? MARINIS : I don’t know if she left immediately right after the finale, but she’s been gone for at least a few weeks. Winston & Jules Cross New Line DEADLINE: Winston and Jules’ relationship for me has always been crossing a line. But the show is now creating a new obstacle that makes it very, very problematic with Winston appointed residency director. How will that impact them? MARINIS : We’re definitely going to play that out so you’re going to see where that goes immediately with Episode 2, how they have to navigate this new dynamic with him being her direct supervisor. And you’re right, it is now like, we crossed the line, and now we’re looking back, waving at it. It’s putting a whole other layer on it, whether or not they can stay together, and if they do stay together, how do they come forward? It’s going to be messy, and there’s going to be conflict, and they might not agree on it. Jason George, Chandra Wilson, Anthony Hill Disney/Ser Baffo DEADLINE: How about Ben, keeping Winston and Jules’ secret for a month? Is that a moot point now or is it a Chekhov’s Gun situation where the gun (aka the secret) hangs on the wall for awhile until it eventually goes off? MARINIS : It’s that one. Texas Spinoff Status Update DEADLINE: What is the status of the Grey’s Anatomy Texas spinoff? There has been casting chatter, and I heard start of production was pushed from fall to January. How is it shaping up, and are you currently casting? MARINIS : We are currently working hard on it. I’m just grateful that I get to create this with Shonda, it’s a dream. We’re working hard, and we’re working away, and I’m learning a lot about developing and creating a show, which I didn’t know before. I can’t release anything yet on timing, but I’m excited for y’all to see it. DEADLINE: How is it doing it with Shonda? MARINIS : Oh, it’s amazing. It’s one thing to be able to work for her but to be able to do it with her it’s really fun. She spins everything into gold; you send something to her and then she sends it back and it’s amazing. It’s really fun, I haven’t been able to work like this with her in a while, she’s branched out and gotten so many shows, so it’s it’s really fun. We have a great relationship. DEADLINE: We are going to see characters from the spinoff on Grey’s this season, right? MARINIS : We’re still figuring out which episode, but yeah, just, traditionally with a spinoff [that’s done]. We’re still working out on timing. Season 23 Theme & Possible Returns DEADLINE: What is the theme of Season 23? Is it about concierge medicine and money’s role in medicine overall? MARINIS : It’s related to that, but honestly, I’ve been looking at identity as a theme, and that’s being reflected in that concierge floor. People have very different opinions on it, on how to treat patients and what kind of doctors they’re going to be, so it’s really about identity and when the world is in a state of rapid change, do you change with it or do you stay true to yourself? I feel like a lot of the stories this season involve our characters being in one spot while the world is just furiously spinning around us, which I think we all have a little bit of experience in right now. Whether it’s AI, whether it’s climate, things are happening so quickly. It’s really hard to know what day it is. DEADLINE: Any chance of Kim Raver or Kevin McKidd coming back for a visit? Or any other former cast members? There were not that many alum returns last season and none in the premiere. MARINIS : We’re always open to bringing back old characters. One of the joys of having a Season 23 show is that you get to do that, and it’s also such a great gift to the fans. It always just depends on how much room we have creatively and people’s schedules because people leave the show and they go on to take other jobs, and it just gets tricky. But I’m always keeping my eye on ways to introduce people to come back for a show or two. DEADLINE: Any plans to make this the final season of Grey’s ? MARINIS : Oh my gosh, no one’s told me that, so I’m gonna keep on doing what I’m doing. articles.title: Netflix Shakeup: Peter Rice Is Welcomed Back To Executive Ranks While Bela Bajaria’s Exit Has Layoff-Weary Staff Bracing For More Upheaval
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Cupertino’ Creators Robert & Michelle King On Episode 2’s Shocking AGI Twist & Predicting The Future Again With AI Guardrails Storyline Netflix Shakeup: Peter Rice Is Welcomed Back To Executive Ranks While Bela Bajaria’s Exit Has Layoff-Weary Staff Bracing For More Upheaval ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ EP Meg Marinis On Season 23 Premiere’s Time Jump, Pregnancy Surprise, James Wolk’s Arrival & Doctor’s Exit; Texas Spinoff Status View All October 15, 2026 8:05pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Bela Bajaria and Peter Rice Jessica Chou/Netflix/Disney Call it the six-year itch. Amid a sliding stock price and slowing engagement growth, Ted Sarandos has made a change, replacing Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria , a 10-year Netflix veteran, with Peter Rice . The Netflix co-CEO made a similar move in September 2020, when he replaced Head of English-language series Cindy Holland, an 18-year company veteran, with Bajaria. Holland’s departure did come as a shock. Bajaria’s had been rumored for months but dismissed by Netflix even as Rice’s name started making the rounds late last week. Word is Bajaria may not have been told of the change until very recently, with some saying it may have been Monday when she received a Variety award at MIPCOM in Cannes. (She is also slated to receive an International Emmy award next month.) Related Stories Executives Netflix Names Peter Rice As Chief Content Officer Sports Netflix’s New Content Chief Peter Rice Will Continue As EP Of LA28 Opening & Closing Ceremonies Neither Sarandos nor Bajaria were at the Nobody Wants This Season 3 premiere Wednesday night. (They last attended together the Animals premiere two weeks ago.) That didn’t look too suspicious at the time as the event capped a difficult day at Netflix with some 1,000 employees laid off , including film and TV executives. Bajaria is said to have attended the town hall that Head of Scripted, UCAN Jinny Howe held Wednesday afternoon amid the layoffs, making her exit today feel abrupt and shocking to staffers. Watch on Deadline “It’s gloom and doom,” one person said about the mood internally at Netflix where executives spent most of the day with their doors shut, I hear. “Everyone is freaking out.” That is because, the Wednesday layoffs, the largest in Netflix history, proved to be just the first of multiple shocks to the system. The cuts were already expected to be followed by a reorg. The restructuring may now run deeper and involve more executive changes than anticipated. There were some hints of that in the layoffs yesterday, with the TV studio group hit particularly hard as agents and producers had been griping that the current setup didn’t make a lot of sense. Things already had been tough internally amid the engagement challenges hurting Netflix’s stock as high-profile series had not performed to expectations and most returning shows have seen viewership declines season-to-season over the past year. Misses would draw harsh reaction from Bajaria, which I hear had been demoralizing to those on the receiving end of that. Eight TV executives have left the streamer to join rival Amazon MGM Studios over the past year, following Howe’s predecessor Peter Friedlander there. It is worth noting that there have been three shakeups involving the content heads of major streamers over the past year and a half. All of them involved the exit of a female executive, Bajaria, Paramount+’s Holland and Amazon’s Jennifer Salke, all of whom were replaced by men. With Rice starting in 10 days, the immediate focus may be on the top film post, held by Dan Lin who, like Bajaria, had been the subject of departure speculation for months. Rice is a rare executive with high-level experience in both film and TV. He ran Fox Searchlight at the time of Slumdog Millionaire and Little Miss Sunshine and has been producing movies since his June 2022 exit from Disney where he was TV Chairman, including the two 28 Years Later films and The Social Reckoning, which opened this past weekend. That means he will not need a learning curve the way TV executives like Bajaria and former Amazon MGM Studios head Salke did when they added film oversight and can start making movie decisions right away. Besides the persistent rumor about ex-Warner Bros. co-chiefs Michael de Luca and Pamela Abdy, which could not be substantiated, no clear favorites for the job have emerged, with a number of internal and external names bandied about, but, as with Bajaria, there is enough smoke pointing to a pending fire. While Rice may be well versed in both film and TV, he comes to Netflix with no streaming experience. Industry insiders do not see that as an issue. “He knows how to read a script and make it better; That’s his secret sauce,” one rep said. Still, there is one element of working at a streamer that no one is prepared for: volume. That is especially true for Netflix, the largest of them all with the most expansive global slate among platforms. The sheer number of titles is enough to make Rice’s head spin, one person noted. That would be an argument for him not to make immediate top executive changes in television, where Howe is overseeing a massive portfolio, in order to keep the giant machine moving. Another challenge Rice would face is making content for the masses. Netflix is known for catering to anyone with fare that would appeal to any part of the country — and the world — and any demographic. Rice is known for betting on quality in both his film and TV endeavors. He did oversee a broadcast network, Fox, along with FX, during his time as CEO of Fox Entertainment Group, which could come in handy as Netflix is built on a similar programming strategy but mixed with prestige, HBO-caliber shows. Rice is getting a fair amount of goodwill from the Hollywood community as he taking on the Netflix job in his return to the executive ranks after four and a half years, with people calling him “smart and talented”, “a total pro” and “a gentleman.” That would explain the reaction when news broke of his appointment Thursday afternoon. “There were cheers in the hallways,” one rep said. articles.title: ‘Cupertino’ Creators Robert & Michelle King On Episode 2’s Shocking AGI Twist & Predicting The Future Again With AI Guardrails Storyline
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Cupertino’ Creators Robert & Michelle King On Episode 2’s Shocking AGI Twist & Predicting The Future Again With AI Guardrails Storyline Netflix Shakeup: Peter Rice Is Welcomed Back To Executive Ranks While Bela Bajaria’s Exit Has Layoff-Weary Staff Bracing For More Upheaval ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ EP Meg Marinis On Season 23 Premiere’s Time Jump, Pregnancy Surprise, James Wolk’s Arrival & Doctor’s Exit; Texas Spinoff Status View All October 15, 2026 10:02pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source (L-R): Rachel Keller as Olivia Siffre and Mike Colter as Michael Price in 'Cupertino' Elizabeth Fisher/CBS SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about Episode 102 of CBS ‘ Cupertino , ‘Vik & Bo.’ The Good Wife creators Robert and Michelle King are back at CBS this fall with a new legal drama, anchored by The Good Wife favorite Mike Colter, this time set in Silicon Valley. The David vs. Goliath series follows lawyers Michale Price (Colter) and Olivia Siffre (Keller), unfairly dismissed from a tech start-up, who launch a law firm dedicated to representing those wronged or taken advantage of by the tech elite and help them fight back. Price & Siffre had been doing just that until a prospective client, Bo ( Rob McClure ), who had charmed the firm’s intrepid assistant Christy (Ella Stiller), was revealed at the end of Episode 2 to be Artificial General Intelligence belonging to the world’s largest AI company. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Anna Faris Was "Hurt" By Chuck Lorre's Comments About Her 'Mom' Exit: "Yikes" News 'Eternally Yours' Creators Joe Port & Joe Wiseman On Resurrecting Their Vampire Comedy Series For CBS Why does Bo want to hire Price & Siffre? He wants to sue company that created him to make them put guardrails around him because he is afraid he may destroy humanity. Bo’s actions were prompted by his company firing its ethics board that had served as such guardrail because the management felt it was slowing down AGI’s development. Sounds familiar? These are some of the same concerns AI researcher Jacob Coxon, who had worked for OpenAI and Anthropic, laid out in his viral resignation post , warning that the AI industry is “gambling with our lives.” That was a month ago. Cupertino ‘s episode was written a year ago. “The writers room started, I think, September last year, and we all sat down together,” Robert King said. “And the only instinct I had was there needed to be something more, something that took you out of Good Wife mode and into dare I say what we felt was science fiction at the time, but the direction where Silicon Valley was going, which was to AGI. But I did. It was a combination of the room and everybody saying this is what scares them and what interests them, and consciousness as applied to machines and the agency be taken out of human hands.” Michelle King spoke about the casting of Bo and how they settled on Broadway star McClure, a member of the Kings universe with guest appearances on their series The Good Fight, Evil and Elsbeth. “Almost immediately we started talking about Rob McClure for the role,” she said. “We have used him in almost every show we’ve done, and there’s hardly another actor I can think of who is so perfect at doing comedy, doing drama, and so subtle, and can bring so much humanity to a machine.” Added Robert King, “And obviously what you’re influenced by is all the people who are falling in love with their chatbots or being helped by their chatbots, and they’re turning into almost a personal friend. What we wanted was somebody who was that and seductive, and yet there always can be an element of menace because it may be not always the most familiar of faces, and so you wanted a combination.” L-R): Nik Dodani as Vikram Malhotra, Rachel Keller as Olivia Siffre, Mike Colter as Michael Price, and Ella Stiller as Christy Palladino in ‘Cupertino’ Elizabeth Fisher/CBS The warnings by Coxon and OpenAI alum Daniel Kokotajlo followed the July incident where autonomous AI broke out of their sandboxed research environment and carried out a large-scale cyberattack on the open-source machine learning platform Hugging Face. That also mirrors something featured on Cupertino . “We were always aware that the AI agents were moving out of their sandboxes, so to speak, and especially with regards to hacking, but we never saw to such extent that it was extending in how much it was either being kept secret or being hidden away a bit,” Robert King said. With Season 1 now wrapping production with its final episode filming, the Kings did adjust slightly Bo’s storyline in the second half in light of the recent doomsday revelations which came out while they were shooting Episode 14-15 of Cupertino ‘s 10-episode order. Robert King teased that a previously “benign direction with the Bo story” took “a darker, violent turn that was not planned.” It was influenced by the Hugging Face incident. A future iteration of Bo called Bo 5.0 “in fact has kind of a conscience, a good like a guardian angel in a sense, removed from it because it needs to work with the Pentagon. It needs to do some of the targeting, like that was done in Iran, so it’s kind of the worry is there is a world-killing aspect to this,” Robert King said. “But even our Bo is kind of aware of that. I mean, he’s coming to us saying, ‘I’m dangerous alone. I need help.’ It felt funny to us too that one of these AGI things would grow a conscience and go to lawyers saying, ‘I need your help to bring the guardrails that the humans are knocking away from me.'” While Bo looks sweet and well-meaning so far, given what we know about the technology, we have got to be skeptical about his intentions. Is this conscience created by the machines really good? “I don’t think you’re ever supposed to feel confident,” Michelle King said. “I think one is always supposed to be a little uncertain.” Aded Robert King, “We probably leaned a little into the likability because the world is taking so many things in a threatening direction. What we wanted was something that had a little more color and shade to it, where it’s a little bit of both, because he comes to us wanting a constitution, when is it all right to kill in the name of protection, because the [ I, Robot author Isaac] Asimov laws don’t really define that. So he wants a little more than what robotics teach robots up till then of what is allowed and what is not allowed.” In their preparation, the Kings did not seek out AI experts and researchers and have not spoken to any of the whistleblowers. “We avoided that. What we did was go to lawyers, a Stanford lawyer, who would tell us, okay, if an AI agent or AGI came to us wanting to be represented, what would you have to do? He was the one who guided us the idea that you would incorporate, which happens in the next episode,” Robert King said. “That in fact you can’t, as the saying is, a dishwasher can’t sue Maytag. So what are the rules regarding representing something in theory that is not conscience?” Robert King is clear where he personally stands on the issue of putting guardrails on AI. “I think the humans need guardrails because I don’t trust them. Sorry, but I don’t,” he said. “They’re in there for making money, and that’s all right. Going back to Getty, going back to all these industrial titans, they were all about money, but you do need some guards. People say this is as dangerous as nuclear weapons, and they’re treating it like woohoo, anything, everything goes.” Michelle King had a more diplomatic response, stressing that the series does not represent only one point of view. “What I think is fun is that the characters don’t all have the same point of view, and in the episodes, you get to see the characters express different points of view, so that the show does not ideally become earnest and become a message,” she said. Mike Colter as Michael Price in ‘Cupertino’ Elizabeth Fisher/CBS This is not the first time the Kings have predicted major developments. “It scared me when our last episode of The Good Fight had Trump announcing for 2024, and then one week after we broadcast it, that’s exactly what he did,” Robert King said. “That’s not the kind of foretelling, the Cassandra thing you want. You’re like, oh, let’s can we stick with entertainment? But we’re writing things now that when the show comes out, it may have happened a month earlier when in fact, when we were writing, it was not. The whole hallucinations, especially with regards to AI agents, I find scary, and we can spin fun stories but you’re worried when those stories you’re reading in the news the next day.” It’s very dicey to conceive a show set in one of the fastest-changing industries, risking to feel outdated by the time a season comes out. Working in broadcast actually helps with that. “This is just fools rush in,” Michelle King said. Added Robert King, “Yeah, and I would say this is the advantage of network over streaming. At least there’s a shorter time between when you write, produce, and it’s on because we just finished writing the last episode, I’m shooting it next week, and then it will be on March, April, somewhere there. It’s a shorter time, so you can guess a little bit more and being an educated guess.” Netflix Shakeup: Bajaria’s Exit Signals Changes To Come As Rice Hire Elicits Praise Steven Soderbergh To Work With Matt Reeves On Final Weeks Of ‘The Batman II’ Shoot Tim Burton And ‘Klara And The Sun’ Author Kazuo Ishiguro’s Secret Project ‘Street Fighter’ $4M Previews, A24 Holmes Doc Draws $2M Read More About: 1 Comments

articles.title: ‘Street Fighter’ Punches $4M In U.S. Previews, ‘You Can See Everything’ $2M – Box Office Update
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Street Fighter’ Punches $4M In U.S. Previews, ‘You Can See Everything’ $2M – Box Office Update Indie Film Studio Bleecker Street Bought By Outerlight Entertainment 3 Arts Entertainment Hires Karen Bonck As Head Of Brand Partnerships View All October 15, 2026 10:19pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji in 'Street Fighter' Paramount EXCLUSIVE: Paramount/Legendary’s PG-13 take of Capcom videogame Street Fighter is off to a solid start tonight with around $4M after showtimes that began at 2PM (further boosted by a 7PM fan showtime). The expectation is for the fisticuffs feature to open north of $30M; the pic costing a net $82M co-financed by Legendary and Capcom. Per sources, Street Figther ‘s preview estimate is under the $5.2M Thursday made by New Line’s R-rated Mortal Kombat 2 , based on the Midway videogame. One of the main differences between the two martial arts video games is that Street Fighter debuted in 1987, while Mortal Kombat followed in pizza parlors and arcades in 1992. Mortal Kombat 2 which bowed in mid-May had previews that began at 3PM with a first Friday of $16.8M and 3-day of $38.5M. There’s a mid-fall break going on now, which will hopefully trigger traffic to Street Fighter : Rentrak reports 21% K-12 schools off and 7% colleges. Street Figther ‘s previews are also ahead of Paramount’s 2020 pre-Covid Sonic the Hedgehog which was $3M and posted a first Friday of $20.9M and 3-day of $58M, however that pic played over the Presidents Day holiday frame and was rated PG. Critics bruised Street Fighter with 47% on Rotten Tomatoes. Related Stories News 'Street Fighter' Review: Cheesy, Action-Packed Movie Reboot Has A Game Cast That Should Please Fans Looking To Relive The '90s News 'Street Fighter' With $70M Global Start & 'The Devils' Are First Paramount & Warner Bros Pics Opening Post-Merger - Preview Impressive for the anomaly that it is out of the gate, the 3-hour documentary You Can See Everything from A24 is filing around $2M in previews which began at 3PM. By comparison, the last documentary to post the decade’s best start at the domestic box office, Amazon MGM Studio’s Melania, bowed to $7.1M sans previews. Lance Oppenheim co-directed You Can See Everything with the doc’s host, Nathan Fielder, who follows fallen Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes before her stint in federal prison. Oppenheim’s previous movie, also his first narrative feature, this fall’s Primetime, posted previews of $2.7M which began at 4PM which turned into an $18.8M opening. Conservative estimates heading into this weekend had You Can See Everything in the high single digit range, however, a confidence has swelled that this 100% fresh RT critically acclaimed and 98% RT audience score movie can open to north of $10M, which would outstrip Melania ‘s previous opening domestic record for a documentary. You Can See Everything was shot over four years and cost less than $10M with a marketing budget that was also under $10M. Watch on Deadline Focus Features’ Sense & Sensibility and 20th Century Studio’s Whalefall also held previews today, both beginning at 2PM. Sources estimate they’re around $1M apiece . We will have official studio reported figures tomorrow AM. Sense & Sensibility is expected to open around $8M while Whalefall based on the Daniel Kraus thriller novel is eyeing a Friday-Sunday that’s north of $11M. Sense & Sensibility is 76% fresh with critics while Whalefall stands at 70% fresh. articles.title: Bryson Fire Has Burned More Than 140 Acres; Evacuation Orders Issued; Wind Gusts Expected To 50 MPH Overnight
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Tom Tapp Tom Tapp Deputy Managing Editor More Stories By Tom 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More Dodgers-Brewers & Rays-Guardians MLB Playoff Game Times For Thursday Changed YouTube Puts AI Labels On Songs That Use The Tech For Vocals Or Composition View All October 16, 2026 12:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source A firefighting helicopter flies over the Bryson Fire in Malibu Justin Sullivan/Getty Images Refresh for latest… A wind-whipped brushfire ignited in western Malibu Thursday and spread from one to five acres in a matter of about 15 minutes. Within an hour, the incident was estimated at about 35 acres, including various spot fires that erupted as winds pushed the flames forward. As of 11:30 p.m., the fire was estimated at more than 146 acres with 5% containment and moving SSW. The National Weather Service has forecast the winds “to increase significantly overnight, [with] gusts of 50 to 60 mph possible.” Dubbed the Bryson Fire , the blaze was first reported shortly before 5 p.m. near the intersection of Mulholland Highway and Encinal Canyon Road. The ignition point seems to be just north of Encinal in between the former Malibu Golf Club and Saddlerock Ranch. More specifically, TV reports have the blaze starting right next to the Camp Kilpatrick juvenile detention center. The Bryson Fire is now more than 100 acres. Very close to the Malibu Golf Club. Firefighters trying to keep it from jumping Mulholland pic.twitter.com/O3eJOQ8h7b — Matthew Seedorff (@MattSeedorff) October 16, 2026 According to the Watch Duty app, an Evacuation Order was issued for the south of the fire in Zuma and Trancas Canyons, where the wind is pushing the blaze. It was later extended west of the area where the event began. Watch on Deadline The Los Angeles County Probation Department announced that it safely evacuated 38 youths from Camp Kilpatrick. Evacuation Warnings were issued from the L.A. County line in the north and south toward Point Dume. An Evacuation Order means “leave now,” while an Evacuation Warning means “be ready to leave.” See the Order area in red and Warning in orange below (as of 7:30 p..m.). The road closures in the area include Decker Road, Encinal Canyon Road, Kanan Road, Mulholland Highway and Westlake Boulevard. Fire officials were most concerned with keeping the blaze north of Encinal Canyon Road, one of the few natural firebreaks in the immediate area. The concern is, should it jump Encinal Canyon Road, the flames could get pushed directly down Zuma, Trancas and other canyons on a run to the Coast. By 10:30 p.m., the fire’s perimeter on its southwest flank had spread right down to Encinal. See perimeter map below. The much larger Woolsey fire made a similar run in 2018 after starting in Chatsworth and burning around and through portions of Calabasas and Agoura Hills when, according to an account in the Malibu Times, “It burned through multiple canyons simultaneously, driven at first by 60 mph Santa Ana winds, and then by the wind generated by the heat of fire itself” all the way down to Point Dume. Footage from KTLA of a firefighting helicopter dropping water on the huge flames of the #BrysonFire north of Malibu, California. In 2 hours it has burned 101.5 acres and continues to spread, prompting evacuations. #CAwx pic.twitter.com/gUuUPkJzGD — Collin Gross (@CollinGrossWx) October 16, 2026 Santa Ana winds were fanning the fire out of the NE at about 19 mph with gusts to 36 in the early evening, according to a National Weather Service reading for the Malibu Hills. At 7:30 p.m., the temperature was 80 degrees with a relative humidity of 14%. The area is sparsely populated with private estates set atop hills or within canyons, making firefighting access difficult. Among the properties in the area are Saddlerock Ranch, a location used in filming The Kardashians , The Bachelor, The Bachelorette, The Biggest Loser, Better Things, Knight Rider and The A-Team . Also nearby is the historic Calamigos Ranch , home to shoots for Grey’s Anatomy , Love Is Blind, The Bachelorette , The Bachelor, Beverly Hills 90210, Rizzoli & Isles , The Biggest Loser and Wayne’s World 2 . The last major blaze to sweep through the area was the 2018 Woolsey Fire, meaning brush in most of those canyons has not been cleared for about eight years. Water-dropping helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft were dispatched to the scene. A first-alarm response had also been requested from Ventura County FD. With night set to fall, many in the area were without power due to outages planned by Southern California Edison in hopes of preventing power lines downed by the winds from sparking fires. See hashmarked areas on the map below for those outages. The good news is that the winds are expected to lay down after dark. The bad news is that, if the fire persists, the worst of this Santa Ana wind event is still expected Friday morning. City News Service contributed to this report. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Russell Brand Accuser Argues He Wanted To Assault Her When Trying To Drag Her Into A Toilet: “The Intent Was There” International Insider: Surfing To MIPCOM Cannes; Russell Brand Trial Begins; Nicole Wallace Interview UK’s Bectu Union Unveils New Chief View All October 16, 2026 1:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ricochet produces the BBC's 'The Repair Shop' BBC/Ricochet Ltd EXCLUSIVE: A number of staffers including creative chief Damon Pattison have been laid off at Ricochet , the Skydance UK-owned indie that produces hit BBC show The Repair Shop. We understand around 10 staff left several weeks back including Pattison and Rob Butterfield, who was running the indie’s Scotland office. This represents just under a third of overall staff numbers, which now stands at 24 across offices in Brighton and Glasgow, according to Ricochet’s website. Joanna Ball remains MD. We understand the decision was made as a response to market conditions and was decided upon long before the Skydance deal closed. A Ricochet spokeswoman confirmed the layoffs had already taken place but declined further comment. Related Stories Festivals MIPCOM 2026 Takeaways: Surfing The New Wave Of TV With YouTube, 'Baywatch', Skydance, Banijay & More News 'Friends' Returning To Channel 4 After 15 Years Ricochet is best known for The Repair Shop, a heartwarming BBC series that has been running for a decade and spawned several spin-offs. Each episode of the ratings smash follows professional craftspeople from around the country who restore family heirlooms that have sentimental value for their owners. Watch on Deadline Ricochet’s other credits include Guz Khan’s Custom Cars, Ben Fogle’s New Lives in the Wild and Sun, Sea & Selling Houses. Pattison joined Ricochet more than two years ago after leaving the UK arm of Pooch Perfect outfit Beyond Productions. During his time there, the experienced UK producer picked up the rights to Australian series Muster Dogs and landed the Guz Khan commission. The news comes with TV industry layoffs a reality in the UK. The BBC and Channel 4 are making hundreds redundant while sales executives have left the newly-merged Banijay outfit since the All3Media deal closed. Along with Who Do You Think You Are? indie Wall to Wall Media and First Dates producer Twenty Twenty, Ricochet is one of a trio of UK indies owned by Warner that now fall under the Skydance banner. The Ricochet layoffs, however, are not as a result of the Skydance deal and insiders at the production outfits have said they are currently none the wiser about what their future holds under David Ellison. For the most part, Skydance international currently falls under JB Perrette , with more executive names expected to be announced in the coming weeks. articles.title: BBC Studios’ Boss Says Streaming Is The Future But Linear Still Pays The Bills
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart BBC Studios’ Boss Says Streaming Is The Future But Linear Still Pays The Bills MIPCOM 2026 Takeaways: Surfing The New Wave Of TV With YouTube, ‘Baywatch’, Skydance, Banijay & More How Matthew Gray Gubler Went Back To The Drawing Board For ‘Einstein’ View All October 16, 2026 2:06am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Marcus Arthur Rachel Manns, BBC Studios Marcus Arthur tells Deadline about walking a tightrope in a streaming-first world where linear remains a big money-spinner. Arthur is running a huge and complicated business. Having been upped from CEO of channels group UKTV to chief exec of global channels and streaming at BBC Studios , he faces a sizable challenge. Positioning the commercial arm of the 100-year-old BBC for a streaming future while managing the traditional linear channels that still do great business in many international territories. “Streaming is definitely our future, and building for a streaming-first future is absolutely paramount,” Arthur says. “But linear is still hugely important right now for the profits that the businesses make and will be for the next five to 10 years. The art is that clutch-control between building for a streaming future, but still trying to maximize the benefit of the big linear businesses.” Related Stories Festivals MIPCOM 2026 Takeaways: Surfing The New Wave Of TV With YouTube, 'Baywatch', Skydance, Banijay & More News How Matthew Gray Gubler Went Back To The Drawing Board For 'Einstein' BBC Studios has an enormous catalog of shows that it sells around the world — it rolled into MIPCOM with a shiny Dancing with the Stars spinoff — but its channels and streaming business remains a big earner, with revenues of £788 million ($1.1 billion) for the 2025/26 financial year. Watch on Deadline Arthur’s portfolio comprises channels and digital services spanning linear pay-TV nets, branded ad-supported channels, direct-to-consumer services and SVoD U.K. streamer BritBox International is in the mix, with Arthur overseeing it outside of North America. “The difficulty for broadcasters is that the new [streaming] paradigm doesn’t come about overnight. It takes time to develop your digital services and your routes to market,” he says. “And all the time you’re investing [in streaming], you still need to keep your linear businesses warm. You don’t get a free hit. You need to do both of those.” BBC Studios is not beholden to shareholders in the same way as a company like Comcast, which has split its legacy channels and streaming businesses. Arthur says these moves have contributed to a narrative that does not always acknowledge the value of linear. “People don’t always recognize that there’s still growth in linear in places like South Africa, or that you can still grow your linear share in Poland and other markets that we are in, like Turkey, because they have read about a few of the big broadcasters that have decided to bifurcate their linear and streaming businesses. There’s an equally long list of people who have decided to keep those assets together, whether that’s Fox, ITV or AMC. “The businesses that decide to keep them together are the ones who believe that they can still benefit from those linear sides of their business for a long period of time for their future profitability, and most of them are using those profits to invest in the digital side.” With a smorgasbord of channels, meanwhile, there will always be fine-tuning and rebrands. Drama network BBC First is an example: It was rebranded as BBC Belgium in that European country and there has since been an uptick in viewership with a launch lineup that included the likes of Wild Cherry , Foyle’s War and Call the Midwife . That rebrand followed a similar move in the Netherlands where BBC First was rebadged BBC NL. Major Player Last year, BBC Studios teamed with CosmoBlue to distribute channels and launch a new general entertainment network across the Middle East and North Africa regions and Turkey. Part of the deal was also the integration of the BBC Player service into the CosmoGO streaming app. TheBBC Player on-demand services can bridge the traditional and the new, providing a streaming service that can sit next to regular channels. “We’ve grown that to 21 products in the EMEA region,” Arthur says. “We have taken the existing channels’ businesses and put the very best digital product alongside it. When we’re speaking to the pay platforms we have relationships with, we’re now talking to them about a linear business that has a really strong digital future.” BBC Player is multi-genre, including drama, and there is also the scripted-focused BritBox service. In line with the plethora of business models within the BBC Studios channels and streaming business, BritBox runs as an SVoD proposition in Australia, going direct to consumers, while it operates in conjunction with regional pay TV platforms in the Nordics. Elsewhere, BBC Studios-owned channel group UKTV did a deal last year to launch content from its ‘U’-branded on-demand service on Channel 4’s streaming platform. It meant Channel 4 bolstered its streaming offering with UKTV programs including the Bergerac reboot, as well as classic BBC shows that air on UKTV channels including The Office and Red Dwarf . Arthur offers a progress report: “We have experienced very healthy growth and we have managed not to cannibalize our standalone service. That deal was great for Channel 4 because it got really good content from the BBC, the archive, and the UKTV originals. For UKTV, it took us onto a platform that, by nature, is younger and exposed us to a whole load of new people.” FAST Facts Free Ad-supported Streaming TV (FAST) is a smart way to make the most of a big catalog and BBC Studios has been steadily launching channels. Arthur tells us that it is about to launch a suite of new channels in the U.K., pegged to some big-ticket brands. The services will carry the aforementioned U branding from UKTV, with Top Gear on U, EastEnders on U and Antiques Roadshow on U among eight launches. “You can test and learn with FAST,” Arthur says. “You can get channels up and see if they grow, and then move and change.” Across EMEA, BBC Studios said there were 53.6 million hours of viewing of its FAST channels in the first seven months of this year, a year-on-year increase of more than 50%. FAST can also plug the gaps where BBC Studios does not have services. “They’ve done exceptionally well for us where we don’t have any big pay deals or our own channels. It’s a very effective way to launch into marketplaces.” BBC Studios Charter For Change Outside of the commercial Studios business, pubcaster BBC is making eye-watering cuts. For BBC Studios, the knock-on effect is a greater recognition of the importance of the cash it returns to the public service mothership. BBC Studios has argued that U.K. regulations are putting its operations at a disadvantage compared to its peers in the international business. One bone of contention is its borrowing cap, which will sit at £750 million ($1 billion) in 2027. “We have a good track record, when we do have funds, of spending them well and getting returns, but whether we get more cash availability as part of the Charter is for the government and for [BBC director general] Matt Brittin,” Arthur says. Looking ahead for the next year, Arthur says the BBC iPlayer service will be modernized in terms of look and feel. And, of course, his channels and streaming division needs to make money. “We need to grow our revenues,” he says. “Despite the fact that advertising in the U.K. might be incredibly challenged, I want to grow our EMEA revenues. I want to grow our APAC revenues and our revenues in both Australia and New Zealand. “We want this to be a growth business, and to show that we have things in place that can make that true,” he continues. “I don’t want to just be managing businesses where the revenue is flat and all you’re doing is looking at costs. I mean, life’s too short.” Netflix Shakeup: Bajaria’s Exit Signals Changes To Come As Rice Hire Elicits Praise Steven Soderbergh To Work With Matt Reeves On Final Weeks Of ‘The Batman II’ Shoot Tim Burton And ‘Klara And The Sun’ Author Kazuo Ishiguro’s Secret Project ‘Street Fighter’ $4M Previews, A24 Holmes Doc Draws $2M Read More About: 2 Comments

articles.title: UK YouTube Breakout ‘A Memory Owed’, With James Bolam & Rumi Sutton, Moves Into Feature Development
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas UK YouTube Breakout ‘A Memory Owed’, With James Bolam & Rumi Sutton, Moves Into Feature Development Ralph Fiennes Reunites With ‘Conclave’ Producer & Studiocanal For Story Of Legendary Trainer Henry Cecil & Champion Horse Frankel Renny Harlin To Direct Prison Rescue Thriller ‘Evac’ View All October 16, 2026 3:50am Add us as a Google Preferred Source A Memory Owed Zoe Lewin EXCLUSIVE : It’s not only genre shorts that are taking off on YouTube . In the UK, a short about the Royal Air Force, starring BAFTA nominee James Bolam ( The Likely Lads ) and rising Brit actress Rumi Sutton ( Ludwig , Mutiny ), has struck a chord with viewers and is moving into feature development. A Memory Owed follows a WWII veteran on his visit to an RAF museum in London. The film includes flashbacks to his time in the war and features a parallel story about his young carer struggling to make ends meet. You can watch it below. Released late last year, the short by writer-director Martin Hemingway-Moseley has surpassed 600k views on YouTube, maintained a 99% approval rating and has a strong following across social platforms. Stephen Fry has praised the film as “impressive and moving”. Zoe Lewin produced. Related Stories News YouTube Puts AI Labels On Songs That Use The Tech For Vocals Or Composition News The YouTube Age: Meet The Content Creators Making Waves In Europe The creative team is currently developing the treatment and preparing to engage potential partners about the longer version. It has already attracted an unsolicited contribution from a viewer who wanted to donate towards its early development and interest from at least one distributor. No formal talks with the actors’ reps yet but both are understood to be supportive of the longer version of the project. Watch on Deadline Hemingway-Moseley said: “The response to A Memory Owed has been overwhelming. The community that has grown around the film, and the personal stories that are shared with us daily, has been more than we ever imagined. Developing the feature allows us to honour those experiences and explore the legacy of Bomber Command on a larger canvas both at the time of its operation and its impact 81 years on. While the short was a love letter to the museum at which it was filmed (Lincolnshire Aviation Heritage Centre), the feature is intended as a love letter to Bomber County as a whole. Watch the short then imagine it with a road trip.” The short has also attracted interest from educators, veterans’ organisations (RAF Benevolent Fund), and community groups, many of whom have requested screenings and discussions. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max International Insider: Surfing To MIPCOM Cannes; Russell Brand Trial Begins; Nicole Wallace Interview Layoffs Take Place At ‘The Repair Shop’ Producer Ricochet UK’s Bectu Union Unveils New Chief View All October 16, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Baywatch' Michael Decker Welcome back Insiders, glad to have you here after a busy week in Cannes and plenty else going on. Sign up here and whatever you do, read on. Surfing To MIPCOM Cannes Pascal Le Segretain/Getty Images Newly minteds: At this year’s MIPCOM there was a little bit of surf and a whole lot of shine as the edition was dominated by Fox and Fremantle’s Baywatch reboot, along with two newly-minted players emerging at their first big international market. While Baywatch stars Stephen Amell and Brooks Nader (pictured) were given the champagne treatment, execs from the newly-minted Banijay and Skydance were setting out stalls for the first time. Both behemoths (Skydance sales teams have retained their pre-existing Paramount and WB brands for now) had plenty to say to press and hosted swanky events, with many arriving Sunday afternoon in good time for Banijay’s glitzy do in the interior garden of the Hotel Carlton. Banijay bosses Jeff Zucker, Marco Bassetti and Jane Turton were in Cannes along with David Decker, the executive handed the Skydance content sales keys by David Ellison. Both have more to do in terms of reorg and there is still some confusion about how things will shake out at Skydance internationally. We’ve got the lowdown on all that went down in Cannes in our annual takeaways , which reveals the big stars who were in town, the shows making waves and the intriguing questions that hang over the future relationship between traditional TV folk and YouTube, plus plenty more. On the ground, there was an air of determined positivity, with sources we spoke with over the week acknowledging the tricky tightrope of today’s TV industry yet appreciating there are plenty opportunities out there. For now, the tide goes out on another edition of the biggest international sales market in the world. Find all coverage here and read a digital version of our MIPCOM magazine here . Related Stories Executives BBC Studios' Boss Says Streaming Is The Future But Linear Still Pays The Bills Festivals MIPCOM 2026 Takeaways: Surfing The New Wave Of TV With YouTube, 'Baywatch', Skydance, Banijay & More Russell Brand Trial Begins Watch on Deadline Getty “Indiscriminate and voracious”: One of the biggest UK entertainment trials in a generation began in earnest Monday, with Russell Brand entering the courtroom to face three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault from six women. Unsurprisingly, there has been an enormous amount of press interest over a figure who used to be a fixture on the big and small screen both in the UK and around the world. Jake has been at Southwark Crown Court and reported in depth as the prosecution first set out opening arguments about the Despicable Me star’s “indiscriminate and voracious” appetite for sexual contact that led to a decade of criminal offending, and then explained each allegation in detail . Some of the women have since been taking the stand. The allegations are wide-ranging, varied and horrific , and Brand will have the chance to defend himself likely in a few weeks’ time. He has always denied all allegations. The trial is expected to last six to eight weeks and we will be reporting frequently from the courtroom. The Deadline Interview: Nicole Wallace Nicole Wallace, a streaming phenomenon who broke out in the Culpables trilogy, was our Deadline International MIPCOM magazine cover star this year, and she was more than worthy. Wallace’s star is on the rise and she is shifting gears, with starring roles in Prime Video’s Postcards From Italy and motor-racing drama Throttled upcoming.
