You’ll soon be able to unleash your inner “ KPop Demon Hunters ” idol on the Toca Boca World storytelling gaming app for kids, through an exclusive in-game collab with Netflix for the animated hit movie. The Toca Boca World x “KPop Demon Hunters” collaboration launches Oct. 27, featuring stylized depictions of the movie’s characters with looks inspired by Huntr/x, the Saja Boys and more. The experience will highlight fashion and music from the award-winning film, which has become Netflix’s most-watched movie ever. The app is developed by Toca Boca, the digital studio arm of toy and entertainment company Spin Master. Related Stories FlyDubai Hijacking Incident Set for Development as an Inspirational Movie by Dori Media Group and India's Sphereorigin Zach Bryan Announces 2027 Stadium Tour Dates, John Fogerty, Ryan Bingham, More to Support The new content in Toca Boca World brings together two distinctive dimensions of the world of “KPop Demon Hunters”: the characters’ everyday style and the energy of the K-pop stage. Players can mix and match both to create characters and stories to personalize their storytelling. Popular on Variety As you would expect, music from the movie will be a key feature of the experience. Toca Boca World is launching a new music player including four chart-topping songs from the film — “Golden,” “How It’s Done,” “Soda Pop” and “Your Idol.” For a limited time, players will be able to use these songs as soundtracks for their own stories within Toca Boca World. “Netflix’s ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ is a global cultural phenomenon, bringing together music, fashion and beloved characters in a way that has clearly resonated with our players,” said Marc De Vellis, Spin Master’s president and digital games. “We were already seeing the Toca Boca community draw inspiration from the film in their stories within Toca Boca World, so this collaboration felt incredibly natural. It gives our players access to authentic and exclusive ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ content, with even more ways to create, play, tell stories and express themselves in a world they love.” The Toca Boca World app, geared toward younger children, has nearly 60 million players. Previous collaborations in Toca Boca World have included activations with Adidas, Conan Gray, Katseye and “Wicked: For Good” as well as in-game music from popular recording artists Olivia Rodrigo, Sienna Spiro and TWICE. In addition to the Toca Boca World x “Kpop Demon Hunters” collaboration, Netflix is adding a new experience for gamers on Netflix Playground. “Toca Boca Jr Kitchen” has teamed with Netflix to introduce a stylized “KPop Demon Hunters” update. While keeping the core mechanics intact, the collaboration transforms the gameplay into a mukbang-themed culinary experience. The game is currently available to download on iOS and Android devices, and it’s available for no additional cost with a Netflix subscription. “KPop Demon Hunters,” produced by Sony Pictures Animation and directed by Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans, became a global phenomenon following its release on June 20, 2025. The movie has generated more 670 million views on Netflix and spent 63 consecutive weeks on the streamer’s Global Top 10. A “KPop Demon Hunters” sequel is in the works , reportedly eyeing a 2029 release. “Kpop Demon Hunters” won the 2026 Oscar for animated feature and picked up other laurels, including Critics’ Choice Awards, Golden Globes and 10 Annie Awards. articles.full_text: Oct 15, 2026 7:00am PT ‘POV Shorts’ Moves From PBS to Time Studios’ YouTube Channel (EXCLUSIVE) By Michael Schneider Plus Icon Michael Schneider Executive Editor franklinavenue Latest ‘The Lowdown’ Creator Sterlin Harjo on the Films That Inspired Season 2, and What Convinced Tommy Lee Jones to Join the Show 13 hours ago Mark Duplass Joins Cast of Hulu’s Erotic Thriller Limited Series ‘Victoria’ 20 hours ago Netflix TV Layoffs Include Director of Original Series Carolina Garcia, Who Exits After 10 Years 20 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source POV Shorts “ POV Shorts ,” the PBS series focused on independent short-form documentaries, is moving homes. For Season 9, “POV Shorts” will run its films on Time Studios ‘ YouTube page. The season, which launches Nov. 17, will kick off with “Bloodlines, Mississippi” from director Crystal Kayiza and “The Boys and the Bees” from director Arielle Knight. Those two films will also air on PBS, but after that, this season of “POV Shorts” will be exclusive to Time Studios. That includes Aurora Brachman and LaTajh Simmons-Weaver’s “Hold Me Close,” Brit Fryer and Lydia Cornett’s “Tessitura,” Serville Poblete’s “In the Morning Sun,” Arjun Fischer’s “Artificial Love,” Mars Verrone’s “Buckskin,” Victor Tadashi Suárez and Livia Albeck-Ripka’s “Still Standing,” Arshia Shakiba’s “Who Loves the Sun” and Nathan Truesdell’s “A Derailment.” Related Stories Spike Lee and Mick Jagger’s Favorite Eyewear Brand Unveils First Collection From New Creative Directors John Juniper and Jeff Solorio Mubi Sets Theatrical Release for Sundance Prize Winning Doc 'Nuisance Bear' - Film News in Brief Six of the season’s films have qualified for Oscars consideration in the documentary short film category: “Bloodlines, Mississippi,” “The Boys and the Bees,” “A Derailment,” “Buckskin,” “In the Morning Sun” and “Still Standing.” Popular on Variety “POV Shorts” and Time Studios previously collaborated on the Season 6 film “Sol in the Garden,” from Débora Souza Silva and Emily Cohen Ibañez. “Nine seasons in, POV Shorts has shown that a twenty-minute film can change how someone sees a problem they thought they understood,” said Opal H. Bennett, executive producer, POV Shorts and senior producer, POV, in a statement. “Partnering with Time Studios means these stories reach people who might never seek out an independent documentary — which has always been the point. “Season 9 asks ‘what holds people together when the systems around them fail,’ added Bennett. “A doctor in the Delta fighting to keep patients whole, two brothers learning their homestead, a town living inside the aftermath of a toxic derailment — these films offer answers to that question from completely different perspectives, which is exactly what short form does best.” “POV Shorts” films have won three IDA Documentary Awards for Best Short Form Series, and landed several Academy Award nominations since launch in 2018. Time Studios also recently joined as distribution partner for the Co-Production Fund from American Documentary/POV Shorts and Chicken & Egg Films. “For more than a century, Time has been dedicated to powerful real-world reporting and extraordinary storytelling,” said Justine Simons, executive producer, video, Time, in a statement. “Our partnership with POV Shorts builds on that mission, bringing our audience some of the finest short documentaries being made today. We’re thrilled to collaborate on Season 9 and share these remarkable films across our platforms.” Here’s a first look at “Bloodlines, Mississippi,” produced by Harri Grace, Paul King and created in collaboration with Nobel Prize Outreach, which “follows Dr. Foluso Fakorede and his team at Cardiovascular Solutions of Central Mississippi as they work to prevent avoidable amputations. Set in the Mississippi Delta, Kayiza’s film looks at community-centered healthcare as a response to racial disparities and the barriers patients face in accessing treatment within a system shaped by historic inequality.” And here’s a first look at “The Boys and the Bees,” produced by Knight and Sean Weiner. “The film follows two brothers as they tend hives and restore their family’s Georgia homestead, deepening their bond along the way.”: ‘Angel and the Badman’ Review: Zachary Levi Leads Angel Studios’ Fitfully Engaging Remake of a John Wayne Vehicle ‘The Social Reckoning’ Review: Aaron Sorkin’s ‘Social Network’ Follow-Up Is Missing More Than Just David Fincher Is ‘Rubber Soul’ the Beatles’ Best Album? He is a true master of cinematic suspense and grand-scale action. Sidney has crafted a brilliant pressure-cooker world that balances prison politics with raw survival prowess. We are confident EVAC will become an unforgettable theatrical experience for action fans worldwide.” Harlin is repped by M3 Global Strategy. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Midjourney: Report Claims AI Model Is Worst Offender For Flouting Hollywood Copyright Russell Brand’s Accusers: Prosecutors Claim ‘Despicable Me’ Star Preyed On Women In TV Industry During “Frenzied” & “Wild-Eyed” Incidents Ben Frow To Leave Skydance’s UK Network 5 After 14 Years View All October 15, 2026 4:44am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand Getty Editor’s note: This story contains details of alleged sexual offenses that some readers may find distressing. Russell Brand allegedly raped a woman in her hotel room after he asked her to take photographs of him in his underwear, a court has heard. On day four of Brand’s rape trial at London’s Southwark Crown Court, the jury was shown a video of a 2023 police interview with an alleged victim. The woman has a lifelong right to anonymity — Deadline refers to her as Complainant 1 (C1) — though she is being named in the court proceedings. Related Stories News Russell Brand's Accusers: Prosecutors Claim 'Despicable Me' Star Preyed On Women In TV Industry During "Frenzied" & "Wild-Eyed" Incidents Legal Russell Brand Rape Trial: 'Forgetting Sarah Marshall' Star Allegedly Had "Indiscriminate & Voracious" Sexual Appetite During the video interview, C1 alleged that she was raped by Brand, now 51, after meeting him on the fringes of the Labour Party Conference in Bournemouth in 1999. The woman was in her twenties at the time of the alleged incident. Watch on Deadline The pair struck up a conversation after he was “playful” and tugged her ponytail. The woman recalled Brand being “polite, courteous, attentive,” and “child”-like during their interaction. She assumed he was gay and said she was not physically attracted to him. She went on to watch a cabaret event in which Brand was performing, and after the show, she suggested he come back to her hotel room as she did not wish to go to a bar or club. “He was very gentlemanly… I didn’t think he was trying it on with me,” she said. Once back at the hotel, the woman said she remembered going to the toilet and returning to find Brand in a pair of briefs, “prancing around being silly.” The woman alleged that Brand asked her to take photos of him, during which she claimed he became visibly aroused. “I could see he was getting hard,” she said during the police interview played in court. C1 claimed Brand pushed her on the bed, pulled down her trousers and underwear, and proceeded to rape her. The woman repeatedly told police that she remembered his weight on her and that he attempted to put his fingers in her mouth. C1, who became visibly emotional during her 2023 interview, alleged that he was “pushing and pushing” until he ejaculated. “I know I said, ‘No,'” she told police. “I drifted out of my head.” She continued: “I wanted him to finish quickly… and get off me. He was making a lot of noises of enjoyment and saying how pretty I was.” After the alleged incident, C1 alleged that Brand told her that he gets “tested regularly” for sexually transmitted diseases. She recalled him saying he had to leave to “get back to his Mum” and that he wrote down his email address before exiting her hotel room. “He tried to kiss me as he went,” C1 said. “He made me feel so dirty. [I felt like] it was my fault,” she told detectives. “I know I was crying; I felt stupid.” C1 said she did not report the alleged incident at the time, saying she worried that she would be told by authorities, “What did you expect?,” after inviting him back to the hotel room. C1 came forward to the police after watching the 2023 Channel 4 documentary, Russell Brand: In Plain Sight . “I feel guilty coming forward now and not before,” she told detectives. Brand, a comedian and MAGA-sphere influencer, faces three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault based on allegations made by six women . Brand has pleaded not guilty to all charges. During evidence on Wednesday, Riel Karmy-Jones, the prosecution barrister, described Brand as “charming,” “ruthless,” and “calculating” in his efforts to satisfy his hunger for sexual activity. Karmy-Jones has stressed that none of the women who came forward know each other. Brand will set out his defense later in the trial. The court was told repeatedly that Brand declined to answer questions when interviewed by police. He instead relied on a prepared statement, in which he claimed that he did not recall meeting the women and did not remember their names. He said any sexual contact was consensual. The trial continues. articles.title: Sky-ITV: UK Culture Secretary “Minded To Intervene” Over $2.1B Merger
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Sky-ITV: UK Culture Secretary “Minded To Intervene” Over $2.1B Merger London TV Screenings Unveils 2027 Schedule Featuring Newly-Merged Banijay Multitude Media Restructures Leader Team & Prepares Live Entertainment Push View All October 15, 2026 5:09am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Lisa Nandy Jerod Harris/Getty for Greater Together Los Angeles The UK culture secretary is “minded to intervene” over the £1.6B ($2.1B) Sky – ITV deal. Lisa Nandy issued her notice over “public interest considerations” including “the need for free expression of opinion in news media,” “the need for a sufficient plurality of views in news media in each market” and “the need for the availability throughout the United Kingdom of a wide range of broadcasting, on-demand programmes or both.” Notably, Nandy is also considering bringing forward legislation that would update the latter to include streaming. She said this legislation “was drafted at a time where viewing was largely via broadcast linear channels.” This reared its head during the Paramount-Warner-Skydance deal stage, for which Nandy similarly said she was “minded to intervene” and the deal was subsequently waved through. It completed in the U.S. last week. Related Stories News ITV Buys 'The Galway Bay Murders' Thriller Starring Kate Mulgrew & Colm Meaney News Luke Evans Says His New ITV Thriller 'The Party' Reveals How The British Class System Still Dominates: "The Idea Of Being Born With A Silver Spoon Is Alive And Well" Nandy stressed that she has not made a final decision and both Sky and ITV have five days to respond to her notice. Watch on Deadline Her next step would be to potentially issue an intervention notice, which would mean Ofcom assessing and reporting on public interest considerations, and the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) assessing and report on whether a relevant merger situation has been created that would damage competition. Nandy could then refer Sky-ITV for a more detailed investigation by the CMA. Nandy said she will update parliament shortly. The Sky-ITV merger shocked the world of broadcasting when it was announced late last year, bringing together the UK’s pay-TV giant and oldest commercial broadcaster. Sky was previously owned by Comcast but was spun out earlier this year under the NBCUniversal umbrella. Thoughts have already turned to the newly-merged entity, which won’t include producer-distributor ITV Studios. Sky Studios boss Cécile Frot-Coutaz said last month she would like to experiment by putting Sky hits like The Day of the Jackal and Brassic free-to-air on ITV. articles.title: London’s Prince Charles Cinema Secures Future With New Long-Term Lease
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac London’s Prince Charles Cinema Secures Future With New Long-Term Lease SXSW London Sets 2027 Festival Theme Thessaloniki: Adaptation Of Ioanna Karystiani’s ‘Swell’ Among 2026 Agora Works In Progress Titles View All October 15, 2026 5:34am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Prince Charles Cinema Tim Whitby/Getty Images for Universal Pictures. The Prince Charles Cinema (PCC) in London’s West End has signed a new long-term lease with its landlord, securing the popular venue’s future and ending an almost two-year public campaign to save the cinema. The cinema’s management team have signed a new 25-year lease with landlord Zedwell LSQ Ltd. The lease includes a no-break clause. This means both the landlord and tenant (The PCC) are locked in for the duration of the lease. Inclusion of the clause is a win for The PCC management, which had voiced concerns that Zedwell might have ambitions to shut the cinema and redevelop the site to open a more profitable business. Related Stories News Sky-ITV: UK Culture Secretary "Minded To Intervene" Over $2.1B Merger Legal Russell Brand Trial: Woman Alleges She Was Raped By Star In Hotel Room After He Posed For Semi-Nude Photos “After 21 months of uncertainty, we’re delighted to have secured the future of the cinema, and we couldn’t have done it without the support, commitment and belief of many, many people,” The PCC management said in a statement. Watch on Deadline “To every one of the 168,645 people (and counting) who signed the petition and ensured we never felt outnumbered. To the Soho Society, who recommended that Westminster Council officially designate us an Asset of Community Value, and the Council, who did so… We are so incredibly thankful to each and every one of you.” Read The PCC’s full statement below. The campaign to save The PCC began in early 2025, when the cinema’s management released a public statement stating the cinema was under “serious threat” of closure. The cinema’s long-standing lease with Zedwell had been set to expire in September 2025. Under UK law, the cinema’s management team was legally entitled to a new lease. They applied for a new lease of a minimum of 15 years at the going market rent and on similar terms to their existing lease. Zedwell responded by asking to include a redevelopment break clause in the new lease that would entitle them to terminate the lease at 6 months’ notice at any time once the new lease has commenced. The PCC is the only independent cinema in the West End. The venue is popular with hipsters and young film fans. It is best known for its all-night screening events and rep seasons, which have frequently highlighted filmmakers like Paul Thomas Anderson and Stanley Kubrick. articles.title: CBS Bringing ‘Pillsbury Bake-Off Classic’ To Primetime With Drew Barrymore As Host
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Campione Katie Campione Senior TV & Labor Reporter @katie_campione More Stories By Katherine Inevitable Foundation Reveals 2026 Accelerate Fellows ‘Abbott Elementary’ Welcomes Miranda Cosgrove, Edi Patterson & Ali Wong As Season 6 Guest Stars ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Recap: Super Bowl Night Sends Home A Fan Favorite View All October 15, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EXCLUSIVE: CBS is bringing the Pillsbury Bake-Off Classic back to television with the help of Drew Barrymore . Barrymore will host this year’s competition, which will air live on CBS and Paramount+ on November 23, marking the first time the program has been televised on a broadcast network since 2014, Deadline has confirmed. Set to air at 8 p.m. ET/PT, not only is the American tradition back on the airwaves, it is getting a spot in primetime. The news was also revealed by Barrymore at the top of her titular talk show on Thursday morning. Watch the announcement above. Related Stories News Chuck Lorre Says CBS "Hated" Melissa McCarthy Casting In 'Mike & Molly': "They Wanted A Hot Young Woman" News Mark Harmon & Michael Weatherly To Reunite On 'NCIS: Origins' The special is being produced by is produced by Studio Large Eyes, Pantheon Media Group and Juma Entertainment in association with General Mills . The Pillsbury Bake-Off Classic has been around since 1949, originally called the “Grand National Recipe and Baking Contest.” Over the years, it’s brought together talented contestants from across the country for five rounds of baking challenges that put their technical skills and imagination to the test. The group of home bakers will be challenged to put their signature twist on everything from cookies to Thanksgiving pies. For more than five decades, CBS aired the special on daytime television before it transitioned periodically across cable and digital platforms. It has not had a consistent home since CBS had it from 1949 to 2002. Barrymore also joins a long list of television personalities to lend their hosting chops to the competition. Past hosts have included Bob Barker, Alex Trebek, Phylicia Rashad, Martha Stewart and Oprah Winfrey. This year, Christina Tosi and Dook Chase will serve as the celebrity chef judges to evaluate the competitors’ creations. The top baker from each round will earn a coveted spot in the ultimate “Best in Bake” finale, where finalists will be tasked with crafting edible wreaths. Whoever is crowned the champ will take home a $25,000 cash prize and a Kitchen Aid equipment package. “Bringing the Pillsbury Bake-Off back to primetime television after more than 20 years is an exciting way to celebrate the creativity and joy home bakers have shared with us for generations,” Maria Carolina Comings, vice president and business unit director for Pillsbury at General Mills, said in a statement to Deadline. “We’re thrilled to kick off the holiday baking season on such a large stage and inspire both longtime fans and a new generation of viewers.” Executive producers for this year’s Pillsbury Bake-Off Classic include Scott Weintrob for Studio Large Eyes, Jennifer O’Connell, Ariel Brozell, Eden Sutley and Martha Chaput for Pantheon, Robert Horowitz for Juma Entertainment and Brielle Cohen is showrunner. Lisa Balzo, Kenzie Caron and Eleanor Harkness serve as executive producers for General Mills. articles.title: Easterseals Disability Arts & Culture Awards Honor ‘The Pitt’, PBS Docuseries ‘Renegades’, ‘Facts of Life’ Trailblazer Geri Jewell & More
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Destiny Jackson Destiny Jackson Crafts Editor, Awards @DestinyDreadful More Stories By Destiny CAPE’s 35th Anniversary Gala Raises $350K As Randall Park, Manny Jacinto, The Women Of ‘The Pitt’ & More Celebrate BTS’ RM Explores Fame, Identity & Curiosity In Debut Art Exhibition ‘Between You And Me’ At SFMOMA Noah Hawley On His Sentimental ‘Amazing Spider-Man #1000’ Comic Book Debut: “He’s The New York Mets Of Superheroes” View All October 15, 2026 6:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Easterseals Disability Arts & Culture Awards Easterseals Southern California The inaugural Easterseals Disability Arts & Culture Awards ( DARCYS ) celebrated its first competitive class of winners Saturday, marking a new chapter for an awards program formerly known as the Media Access Awards, established in 1979. Co-produced by Easterseals Southern California and Film Independent, the ceremony recognized achievements in authentic disability representation across film, television and media, honoring the performers, filmmakers and storytellers working to reshape narratives in entertainment. Hosted by comedian and cerebral palsy advocate Tina Friml, the ceremony took place at The Barker Hangar in Santa Monica, combining humor with pointed calls for the film and television industry to invest more in recruiting disabled talent. Among the evening’s winners were PBS docuseries Renegades and HBO’s The Pitt , while Facts of Life star Geri Jewell received the inaugural DARCYS Legacy Award and Vincent Rutley took home the Christopher Reeve Emerging Talent Award. Related Stories Casting Casting Society Reveals Artios Awards Non-Film Nominees List: 'The Pitt', 'Heated Rivalry,' 'Pluribus' & More News CAPE's 35th Anniversary Gala Raises $350K As Randall Park, Manny Jacinto, The Women Of 'The Pitt' & More Celebrate Film Independent President Juan Devis, who took over in April this year, replacing acting president Brenda Robinson, who took over the role after the passing of Josh Welsh in January 2025, said that he was happy to continue the organization’s relationship with Easterseals, which has spanned more than a decade. “What we have been fighting for, for 42 years, is access and representation and pushing for the entire ecosystem to understand the value of what we bring,” Devis told Deadline. “Each year I think it becomes more evident that these types of events are just part of who we are.” Watch on Deadline Friml established the afternoon’s tone with an opening monologue that humorously described the gathering as a “truly mass disabling event.” Explaining the DARCYS acronym, she offered her own interpretation of the Y: “Yeah, you’re a good person for watching this.” The comedian also aimed at the healthcare industry, referencing The Pitt , one of the ceremony’s nominees. “The only way to get healthcare [these days] is by going to a fake hospital,” she said, before adding, “I’m still on a payment plan with Doc McStuffins, and that ended six years ago.” Among the biggest laughs of the ceremony came during Friml’s take on an awards-show in memoriam. Instead of honoring industry figures who had died, she eulogized disability tropes onscreen, including “Characters That Would Rather Die Than Be Disabled,” “The Miracle Cure,” “Cripping Up”—the practice of casting non-disabled actors in disabled roles—and “Teary Eyes.” On the first trope, Friml joked, “Sure, your career as a boxer may be over, but have you tried telemarketing?” For “Teary Eyes,” she delivered another punchline: “I don’t want Michael B. Jordan crying because a puppy is dead. I want him crying because a hot woman is still alive.” The humor gave way to a more urgent industry appeal when Amanda Upson, series producer of Renegades , accepted the award for Best Unscripted Series. The five-episode PBS short-film docuseries, hosted by award-winning musician and disability rights advocate Lachi, highlights the lives and cultural contributions of lesser-known historical figures with disabilities. Upson said the project grew into a vision shared by more than 50 disabled filmmakers, emphasizing the value of employing disabled talent both behind and in front of the camera.“We prove that empowering disabled talent behind the camera yields nuanced storytelling that outperforms traditional programming. Please check out their work and hire them,” she said. Upson also called on studios, streamers and foundations to provide more funding for disabled creators, citing approximately $45 million in funding cuts under the current administration and warning of the consequences for disabled artists and their ability to tell their stories. “In the face of near-invisible onscreen representation in this onslaught of systematic erasure, we need allies,” she said. “Studios and foundations, it is your turn to show up and invest mightily in us.” The Pitt won Best Scripted Series and Best Achievement in a Casting Ensemble, with cast members and casting director Cathy Sandrich using their acceptance speeches to highlight the importance of authentic representation. Tal Anderson, who appeared alongside fellow cast members Taylor Dearden, Jessica “Limer” Flores, Christopher Thornton and Diana Elizabeth Jordan, thanked Easterseals, HBO Max and Warner Bros. before recognizing the work of the series’ cast and crew. “Authentic representation is very, very important,” Anderson said. “And The Pitt has done such an amazing, spectacular job when it comes to authentic stories and representation.” Sandrich, accepting on behalf of the casting team, credited creators John Wells, R. Scott Gemmill and Noah Wyle with a commitment to telling stories that reflect the world and communities that have too often been underrepresented on television. “It was an enormous thrill for all of us to cast a disabled actor in a role that had not originally been conceived or written as a character with a disability,” she said. Sandrich also spoke about the importance of audiences seeing themselves reflected on screen, saying that the series’ commitment to authentic casting extended to changing a character’s gender to get the casting right. She praised the performances of Anderson, Thornton and Flores, and noted that the writers had also created roles specifically for disabled actors.“Their talents are undeniable,” Sandrich said. “We feel incredibly lucky to be given such extraordinary material, and we know that our writers, producers, and directors will continue their commitment to reflecting the truth and complexity of our world.” Rutley, recipient of the Christopher Reeve Emerging Talent Award, noted that the ceremony fell on his 41st birthday and offered encouragement to actors still waiting for their breakthrough. “I want to say today is my 41st birthday and I want to give a shout-out to all of the actors whose career didn’t blow up until after 40. I’ll see you on set,” he said. “It’s not a matter of if. It’s a matter of when. Your number will be called. Your name will be called. Today is my day. Tomorrow may be yours. Let’s ride. Love you.” Jewell, meanwhile, reflected on her career and the support of Norman Lear, who cast her in The Facts of Life after seeing her stand-up comedy routine. Jewell recalled meeting Lear in 1980 at the second annual Media Access Awards, where her friend, producer Fern Field, introduced them. “He said, ‘You’re real funny, kid, but you’re way before your time.’ I said, ‘So wait a couple months.’ He waited two months, and then he cast me on The Facts of Life ,” Jewell said. Accepting the Legacy Award at age 70, the comedian reflected on the significance of the recognition and encouraged others to believe in themselves. “I just want to say believe in yourself always, no matter what anybody else believes about you, because anybody who has believed negative confidence or what they think you can’t do, that’s not going to carry you in life. What’s going to kill you is what you believe about yourself, and never underestimate the power of the human spirit. Thank you, and God bless you.” Among those in attendance were Marlee Matlin, Wendi McLendon-Covey, Lisa Whelchel, John Ortiz, Marissa Bode, Cesily Collette Taylor, Scoot McNairy, Abby Elliott, Karen Pittman, Jamie Brewer, Victoria Mack, Daniel Monks, Jessy Yates, Matthew Reeve, Devis and Lynell Davis of Easterseals Southern California. The Inaugural Winners Are: Best Feature Horsegirls Director/Writer: Lauren Meyering Writer/Producer: Mackenzie Breeden Producers: Alix Madigan-Yorkin, Michael Sherman Featured Talent: Lillian Carrier, Matthew Schwab Best Performance in a Feature Anna Sargent, Take Me Home Best Documentary The Haunting of Pennhurst Directors/Producers: Mike Attie, Katarina Poljak, Nathan R. Stenberg Producer: Daniel J. Chalfen Best Scripted Series The Pitt Creator/Executive Producer: R. Scott Gemmill Executive Producers: Simran Baidwan, Michael Hissrich, Erin Jontow, Joe Sachs, John Wells, Noah Wyle Featured Talent: Tal Anderson, Jessica “Limer” Flores, Victoria Mack, Christopher Thornton Best Performance in a Scripted Series Daniel Monks, All Her Fault Best Unscripted Series Renegades Creator: Day Al-Mohamed Series Producer: Amanda Upson Executive Producers: Michael Kantor, Carrie Lozano, Charlotte Mangin Best Achievement in Casting Ensemble The Pitt Creator/Executive Producer: R. articles.title: Rita Coburn & Jeffrey Wright To Bring Their Feature Doc ‘W.E.B. Du Bois: Rebel With A Cause’ To London
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac London’s Prince Charles Cinema Secures Future With New Long-Term Lease SXSW London Sets 2027 Festival Theme Thessaloniki: Adaptation Of Ioanna Karystiani’s ‘Swell’ Among 2026 Agora Works In Progress Titles View All October 15, 2026 6:55am Add us as a Google Preferred Source After its U.S. broadcast debut and theatrical roadshow tour, W .E.B. Du Bois: Rebel With A Cause , the new feature documentary by filmmaker Rita Coburn ( Marian Anderson: The Whole World in Her Hands ) on the life and legacy of the legendary writer W.E.B. Du Bois, is heading to the UK. Check out a trailer for the film above. The film will screen on Sunday, October 18, 2026, at the Charlotte Street Hotel in London. The screening will be followed by a conversation with Coburn and actor Jeffrey Wright , who narrates Du Bois’ work in the film. Directed, written, and produced by Coburn, W.E .B. Du Bois: Rebel With A Cause chronicles the extraordinary life and enduring legacy of Dr. William Edward Burghardt Du Bois, the scholar, historian, sociologist, author, activist, and Pan-Africanist whose work helped shape modern civil rights thought. Related Stories News Jeffrey Wright Taps His College Lacrosse Roots In Promo For PLL Championship Game On ABC News Dustin Hoffman, Juliette Binoche, Jeffrey Wright & Cinematographer Robert Richardson To Be Honored At Karlovy Vary Narrated by Viola Davis, the two-hour documentary explores Du Bois’ writing through dramatic readings by Common, Courtney B. Vance, and Wright. The readings are stitched together with rare archival footage, photographs, and historical documents. “I’m not prouder of any other piece that I’ve been a part of than I am to be a part of this,” Wright said of the film. Born in 1868, just five years after the Emancipation Proclamation, Du Bois lived through Reconstruction, Jim Crow, two World Wars, and the dawn of the modern Civil Rights Movement. The documentary follows his journey from groundbreaking academic achievement (Du Bois was the first African American to earn a Ph.D. from Harvard) to the founding of the NAACP, his international Pan-African work, and his death in Ghana in 1963, on the eve of the March on Washington. The documentary features commentary from leading historians, scholars, and cultural voices, including Raymond Arsenault, Karida Brown, Eric Foner, Henry Louis Gates Jr., Eddie S. Glaude Jr., Nikole Hannah-Jones, David Levering Lewis, and Imani Perry. Coburn’s previous documentaries include Maya Angelou: And Still I Rise and Marian Anderson: The Whole World in Her Hands . W.E .B. Du Bois: Rebel With A Cause screened on PBS in the U.S. in May and has since toured North America. articles.title: Fandango And Plex Team To Integrate Movie Ticket Sales Into Streaming
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Skydance Shares Tumble In Technical Adjustment As Inflation, Interest Rate Jitters Roil Markets; Apple Regains $5 Trillion Market Cap Candle In The Wind: 5-Year-Old Media Firm Faces New Questions After Hello Sunshine Exit ‘Elsinore’ And ‘La Bola Negra’ Continue Awards Momentum With Wins At Hamptons Film Festival View All October 15, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source An example of the Fandango movie ticket buying feature on Plex's streaming platform Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: Established streaming platform Plex has teamed up with Fandango to allow U.S. users to find showtimes and buy movie tickets as they browse and watch films. Founded in 2011, Plex offers a suite of streaming options from free, ad-supported live and on-demand programming to transactional VOD. Its discovery and community efforts have enabled the company to hold its own in a streaming world dominated by Roku, Amazon and other large-scale players. It operates in more than 180 countries and has more than 42 million monthly active users. Fandango has branched out from its origins under current owner Versant, adding general-entertainment streaming and other offerings, but it remains the leading online movie ticket seller. Related Stories News Discovery+ Raises Prices In One Of Skydance's First Streaming Moves After Merger Close Sports Disney+ To Stream Super Bowl For First Time & Carry Two 'Monday Night Football' Games This Season Especially as moviegoing has rebounded after Covid, a number of streamers have looked to unite the small and big screens in various ways. Roku in 2025 added a “coming soon to theaters” feature to its user experience, but it stopped short of enabling ticket purchases. Watch on Deadline Under the partnership, which lit up this week, Plex users in the U.S. will see a Fandango ticketing option on title pages for movies that are currently playing in theaters. The feature lets them click through to Fandango to find showtimes and buy tickets. The integration also includes direct attribution through measurement firm Kochava, which promises to give studios and advertisers greater visibility into how campaigns and audience engagement translate into ticket sales. As more of streaming has shifted toward advertising over the past few years, with all major streamers except Apple TV making it a major strategic focus, there has also been an increased emphasis on outcomes. In other words, knowing how ads prompt purchase decisions is even more of a brass ring than ever. The Letterboxd-like community aspect of Plex is a key element in the partnership. More than 45 million users create watchlists, the company says, giving it an advantage in terms of content discovery in a marketplace where average viewers struggle to find films and series of interest. “Our vision is to make Plex the place where people can discover what to watch, regardless of where that content lives. Fandango lets us extend that experience to all theatrical releases in the U.S., giving fans an easy way to act once they find a movie they want to see,” Scott Olechowski, co-founder and chief product officer of Plex, said in a statement. “Plex has a unique view into what movie fans are actively considering, from what they’re searching for to what they’re watching across services,” said Jerramy Hainline, EVP of Fandango. “By connecting those discovery signals with Fandango ticketing, we’re making it easier for fans to turn that interest into a trip to the theater, while giving studios and advertisers a more direct, measurable path to ticket sales.” Zendaya Set For Alex Garland’s Untitled Science Fiction Movie At A24 Key Takeaways Including ‘Baywatch’, YouTube, Skydance & Banijay UK Gov’t “Minded To Intervene” Over $2.1B Sky-ITV Merger Netflix Cuts About 1,000 Jobs; VP Film, Directors & Managers Among Affected Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Disney+ And Hulu To Stream Pave Studios True-Crime Podcasts ‘Clues’ And ‘Mother Knows Murder’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Skydance Shares Tumble In Technical Adjustment As Inflation, Interest Rate Jitters Roil Markets; Apple Regains $5 Trillion Market Cap Candle In The Wind: 5-Year-Old Media Firm Faces New Questions After Hello Sunshine Exit ‘Elsinore’ And ‘La Bola Negra’ Continue Awards Momentum With Wins At Hamptons Film Festival View All October 15, 2026 7:01am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EXCLUSIVE: Disney+ and Hulu will stream Pave Studios true-crime video podcasts Clues and Mother Knows Murder in exclusive windows before they go into wide release. The two titles, which are part of Pave’s Crime House sub-brand, are the company’s first to be picked up by a major streaming platform. Seeing the growth of YouTube in the living room, Netflix, HBO Max, Peacock and lately Disney+ have been looking to add podcast programming, which is seen as a budget-friendly way to boost view time and engagement. Pave Studios was founded by Max Cutler, who previously founded Parcast and went on to become an executive at Spotify after the streaming giant acquired his company. Related Stories News British True Crime Producer Association Welcomes Non-UK Producers For First Time Including America's Gennie Studios, My Entertainment and Texas Crew Legal FBI Adds Ex-Bellum Entertainment CEO To Most Wanted Fraudsters List; Offering $150K Reward For Info On Fugitive Mary Carole McDonnell Clues , hosted by Kaelyn Moore, will premiere next Tuesday. Mother Knows Murder , hosted by The Rookie: Feds and Claws star Niecy Nash and her daughter, actress Dia Nash, will debut on November 9. Watch on Deadline New episodes of both series will premiere on Disney+ and Hulu one day before they become available on other podcast platforms. Clues , which won a Webby earlier this year, promises to take viewers and listeners “deep into the world of notorious crimes and forensic breakthroughs.” New podcast Mother Knows Murder sees the Nashes breaking down an actual case as they recline in bed. Moore, known as the host of Heart Starts Pounding and the newly premiered Last Trace with Kaelyn Moore said Clues “was developed with a streaming audience in mind from day one. Our goal was to create a show with the production quality and storytelling that would stand naturally alongside other premium content on a streamer like Disney+ and Hulu.” Cutler said the Disney streaming deal is “proof” of the audience-friendly, creator-led approach of Crime House. Disney is “the first of many places we expect these stories to go,” he added. “As streaming platforms increasingly look to add premium content from talented creators, Pave is well-positioned to be a content collaborator to these companies, and we are excited to be working with Disney to bring our shows to their streaming viewers.” Zendaya Set For Alex Garland’s Untitled Science Fiction Movie At A24 Key Takeaways Including ‘Baywatch’, YouTube, Skydance & Banijay UK Gov’t “Minded To Intervene” Over $2.1B Sky-ITV Merger Netflix Cuts About 1,000 Jobs; VP Film, Directors & Managers Among Affected Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Ralph Fiennes Reunites With ‘Conclave’ Producer Tessa Ross & Studiocanal For Story Of Legendary Trainer Henry Cecil & Champion Horse Frankel
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Renny Harlin To Direct Prison Rescue Thriller ‘Evac’ ‘Red Sonja’ Producer Christa Campbell Launches Film & TV Company XTA Media Ron Perlman Lines Up Hemingway Movie & Updates On ‘Sons Of Anarchy’ Spinoff ‘Legends’, That Third ‘Hellboy’ Film & Next Steps For His Asylm Studios View All October 15, 2026 7:02am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ralph Fiennes, Henry Cecil, Frankel Lea Meienberg/Getty EXCLUSIVE : Three-time Oscar nominee Ralph Fiennes is reuniting with Conclave producer Tessa Ross and A Bigger Splash backer Studiocanal on Unbeaten , a biopic of legendary British horse racing trainer Henry Cecil and his most famous charge, Frankel. Fiennes will star as Cecil and serve as executive producer on the film, which is being lined up to shoot next year. The screenplay from Boardwalk Empire WGA nominee Bash Doran, the consulting producer on Beef , will be directed by BAFTA winner Nora Fingscheidt ( System Crasher ) with Tessa Ross producing for House Productions and Rory Aitken producing for Escapade Pictures. 42 will also produce. Pic has been developed with support from BBC Film and Conclave and The Zone Of Interest backer Access Entertainment. Related Stories News Ralph Fiennes, Colin Farrell & Wagner Moura Set For Comedy 'Art' From Director Fernando Meirelles & Screenwriter Christopher Hampton; 193 Launches For Cannes Market News Ralph Fiennes, Viggo Mortensen, Charlotte Rampling, Katherine Langford & More Set For István Szabó's 'Embers'; Filming Underway & First Looks Revealed With Embankment Aboard For Cannes Market Studiocanal is fully financing the film and will release theatrically in their territories of the UK, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Benelux, Australia and New Zealand. Executive producers include Anna Marsh, Ron Halpern and Joe Naftalin for Studiocanal, as well as Fiennes and Doran. Studiocanal is handling worldwide sales. Watch on Deadline Cecil, knighted by the Queen in 2011, was one of horse racing’s most recognizable and celebrated global figures. A ten-time champion trainer in the UK, the undefeated Frankel was his most famous horse, winning ten Group 1 races. Many consider the horse to be the greatest European thoroughbred ever and a rival to U.S. champ Secretariat. The film will follow the late Cecil’s bittersweet final years as he triumphantly rebuilds his career and life after suffering personal heartbreak, tabloid scandal, health crises and falling out with the industry’s most powerful owner. The relationship with Frankel and rekindling with his third wife Jane McKeown were key to his return to the top of his sport. Tony Rushmer, author of The Triumph of Henry Cecil: The Authorised Biography , is a consultant on the film. Ralph Fiennes commented: “I knew nothing about the legendary Henry Cecil until I read Bash Doran’s screenplay. I was compelled and moved by it and by Henry’s story with the great horse Frankel. Henry was – and still is – a unique figure, complex and competitive in the very specific world of horse racing. I’m delighted to be reunited with Tessa Ross (producer) and to be working alongside Rory Aitken (producer) and Studiocanal. I’m particularly excited to be collaborating with Nora Fingscheidt. Her intensely immersive approach and desire for authenticity is inspiring. I was blown away by her film The Outrun .” The project marks the second collaboration between Berlin Silver Bear winner Fingscheidt and Euro studio Studiocanal following the UK release of BAFTA nominated The Outrun , starring Saoirse Ronan. Fiennes is repped by 42 Management and Production, CAA, and SOWDLLP. Fingscheidt is with Casarotto Ramsay & Associates, Ilene Feldman Management and Homebase. Doran is repped by UTA, Untitled and Schreck Rose. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past. And if they don’t, it’s GAME OVER!” Related Stories Movies DC Studios' 'Clayface': First Reactions Movies Austin Abrams' 'Whalefall': First Reactions The full cast includes Joe “ Roman Reigns ” Anoa’i (Akuma), David Dastmalchian (M. articles.title: Stephen Chow’s ‘Shaolin Soccer’ Spinoff ‘Kung Fu Soccer’ Sets U.S. Release After Dominating China’s Summer Box Office
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All October 14, 2026 4:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Kung Fu Soccer' Encore Films Stephen Chow ’s Kung Fu Soccer is heading to North American and British cinemas after finishing the summer as China’s biggest box office hit. Singapore-based distributor Encore Films said Wednesday that the comedy legend’s long-awaited Shaolin Soccer spinoff will open Oct. 23 in the U.S., Canada, U.K. and Ireland. The rollout will include the original-language version and a newly produced English dub featuring voice performances by Chow, Jimmy O. Yang and MC Jin. The release arrives in the 25th anniversary year of Shaolin Soccer , which became Hong Kong’s highest-grossing local film upon its 2001 release before developing a global cult following. Chow followed it with Kung Fu Hustle (2004), another genre-blending smash that earned more than $100 million worldwide and cemented his reputation as one of Hong Kong’s greatest comedy-action hitmakers. Related Stories Movies Tallinn Black Nights Fest Unveils Baltic Film Competition TV Mikael Marcimain's 'The Cold Song' Marks a Rare Return to Big Swing European TV Drama (Exclusive First Look) Timed at home to tap into this summer’s World Cup fever, Kung Fu Soccer earned approximately $344.4 million (RMB 2.315 billion) during China’s June 1-Aug. 31 summer moviegoing season, becoming the season’s biggest earner. Chow’s return helped lift the country’s summer theatrical revenue to $1.86 billion (RMB 12.498 billion), up 4.45 percent from a year earlier, according to figures from the China Film Administration and Maoyan Research Institute. Written and directed by Chow, Kung Fu Soccer marks his first feature behind the camera since 2019’s The New King of Comedy. Previously announced under the title Shaolin Women’s Soccer , the Hong Kong-China co-production reworks the original film’s martial-arts-meets-scrappy-sports-team premise around an all-female squad of underdogs. ‘Kung Fu Soccer’ Encore Films Zhang Xiaofei, the star of Chinese blockbuster Hi, Mom , plays the captain of the Emei Women’s Football Team, which enters the Supreme Invincible Cup determined to prove its doubters wrong. Dilraba Dilmurat plays the team’s star striker, while Lay Zhang serves as its kung fu mentor, helping the players combine martial arts mastery with soccer skills to overcome formidable opponents and setbacks on and off the field. The ensemble also includes Hong Kong screen icon Carina Lau, Japanese star Takeru Satoh, Sisley Choi, Louis Cheung, Yang and Jin. Encore acquired worldwide distribution rights outside mainland China from Chow’s production banner, The Star Overseas , in June. The October openings in the West follow the film’s earlier theatrical rollout across the Asia -Pacific region. “Following the tremendous response to Kung Fu Soccer across Asia and Oceania, we’re excited to bring the film to cinema audiences in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom and Ireland,” said Encore Films managing director Joyce Lee. “Stephen Chow’s films have always transcended language and cultural boundaries, bringing audiences together through his unique blend of action, comedy and heart,” she added. Encore has also completed a Cantonese dub. “Through a special English-dubbed version that makes the film more accessible to wider audiences, alongside a newly completed Cantonese-dubbed version whose voice cast will be announced soon, we hope to introduce Stephen Chow’s signature style of comedy to new audiences while reconnecting with longtime fans,” Lee said. articles.title: ‘Pop Pop,’ ‘Kidney’ and ‘Sounds of the Desert’: Tallinn Sets Rebels With a Cause, Critics’ Picks Programs
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 14, 2026 5:25am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Sounds of the Desert' Courtesy of PÖFF The Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF) has revealed the Rebels With a Cause and Critics’ Pics Competition programs for its 30th edition , taking place Nov. 6-22, including its Baltic Film Competition. The 2026 Rebels With a Cause Competition will screen nine world premieres that explore “unconventional approaches to filmmaking,” organizers of the Estonian fest said on Wednesday. Curated by Javier Garcia Puerto, the program has been celebrating filmmakers who challenge cinematic conventions, bringing together emerging voices and established directors. Related Stories TV Mikael Marcimain's 'The Cold Song' Marks a Rare Return to Big Swing European TV Drama (Exclusive First Look) Movies 'Behemoth!' Wouldn't Have Been Possible Without 'Andor' Success, Says Tony Gilroy Among this year’s lineup is Lithuanian filmmaker Emilija Škarnulytė’s Sounds of the Desert , a Lithuanian-Norwegian co-production, which extends the presence of Baltic cinema beyond PÖFF’s regional competition , and Dylan Stephen Levers’ debut feature Pop Pop from the U.S. The latter is described by the festival as “a mash-up of viral meme culture and social media references, set in a makeup digital environment with a retrofuturistic aesthetic, [that] makes us dive into the complex layers of toxic masculinity, cancel culture, and radical positioning, going beyond the standards of black comedy.” Meanwhile, curated by Nikolaj Nikitin, the Critics’ Picks Competition will present 10 world premieres from emerging and established filmmakers. The section is designed to highlight “films with a clear artistic vision that explore genre conventions while engaging in dialogue with film history.” This year’s selection features productions and co-productions from Japan, China, Morocco, Mexico and Uruguay, alongside European titles. Estonia is represented by Eeva Mägi’s Mo Amor . Check out the full lineups for the PÖFF Rebels With a Cause and Critics’ Picks Competition below. articles.title: Snoop Dogg’s Daughter Cori Broadus Debuts Character in Animated Series ‘Doggyland’ — Fulfilling a Childhood Dream (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All October 14, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Cori Broadus Mason Sexton Snoop Dogg ‘s daughter Cori Broadus has landed a role in Doggyland , the 3D animated children’s series co-created by her father, fulfilling a childhood dream. This marks the animated debut for Broadus, who plays Maxine, a confident, sassy labradoodle, in the series, which was co-created by Snoop Dogg, Emmy-nominated producer and creator Claude Brooks and Grammy-winning artist and producer October London. Doggyland also marks the beginning of a dream come true for the actress, who has harbored ambitions of becoming part of the world of children’s animation for two decades. As a youngster, she auditioned for the animated series The Backyardigans , but didn’t land the part. Now, she now only is voicing a character but also helped create her. Related Stories Music Tupac Murder Trial: Duane "Keffe D" Davis Sentenced 40 Years to Life in Prison TV Lucian Piane, Former 'RuPaul's Drag Race' Music Producer, Dies at 46 Broadus was hands-on throughout the character development process alongside Brooks, helping shape Maxine’s personality, look and spirit. The 27-year-old describes the character as “an extension of her inner child” — bold, playful, expressive and unapologetically herself. Maxine makes her first appearance in the music video for “You’re Enough,” the title track from Doggyland ’s latest full-length album. “I’m so excited to be part of Doggyland and bring Maxine to life,” Broadus said. “I love that she’s confident, a little sassy, and encourages kids to be themselves. ‘You’re Enough’ is such a special message because I want every kid to know they’re already perfect just being who they are.” Doggyland features a cast of dogs who sing, rap and dance to fun and educational songs that promote social-emotional and cognitive development in young children. Since its inception in 2022, Doggyland has produced a variety of educational songs about affirmations, letters, numbers, colors, animals, good habits and accepting others. The series focuses on delivering positive messages through music and storytelling, making learning an enjoyable experience for young viewers. The show focuses on a group of puppies led by Bow Wizzle (voiced by Snoop Dogg), who serves as the adult mentor to the rest of the cast, including Woofee (voiced by London), a smooth singer who is always cheering on his friends; Yap Yap, a high-spirited character who is known for her positive and cheery personality; Chow Wow, an empathic team player, and Barks-A-Locks, the curious one of the group who is always discovering new adventures. The show, which has been honored with an NAACP Image Award, Telly Award and Mom’s Choice Award, has amassed 1.3 million subscribers to the Doggyland YouTube channel. Said Snoop Dogg (whose real name is Calvin Broadus Jr.): “Looking back at where we are now with Doggyland and everything, it’s wild. When Cori was just an itty-bitty pup, she was always saying how she wanted to be part of a cartoon, and now here we are. Not only is she a cartoon character, but it’s one she helped create herself. What we’ve got here is a beautiful, full-circle moment, and I’m just so proud to be a part of it as her father. Maxine’s got Cori’s confidence, her personality and a little bit of that secret ingredient. I’m talking about sass. What’s even better is that Maxine is coming in hot with that patented Doggyland positive message. She’s here to let the kids know they should love themselves because you’re already enough just the way you are. Life lesson!” From left: October London, Snoop Dogg and Claude Brooks Chris Enriquez Broadus also is a professional DJ, performing under the moniker of Princess Broadus, and an entrepreneur, working in the worlds of beauty, fashion and music, with a growing focus on building brands and experiences that challenge traditional ideas of identity and culture. The message behind Maxine’s debut in “You’re Enough” is said be at the heart of Doggyland’s mission. Maxine encourages young viewers to embrace their individuality and reminds them that there is nothing they need to change about themselves in order to be worthy, lovable or enough. Maxine’s debut follows on the heels of the introduction of Banjo Bucky, voiced by country music singer Jake Tankersley. Watch the “You’re Enough” music video below. THR

articles.title: TikTok Inks Second Major Microdrama Deal, Partners With Made By Us Studios
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Katie Kilkenny Plus Icon Katie Kilkenny Enterprise Reporter, TV & Labor katiekilkenny7 Follow Sign Up View All October 14, 2026 6:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Hannah Stocking, who will appear in the TikTok-Made By Us Studios coproduction ‘Player,’ attends the 97th Annual Oscars at Dolby Theatre in 2025. Photo by Monica Schipper/Getty Images TikTok is deepening its commitment to the microdrama format with a new deal aimed at producing vertical stories starring creators. The company has inked an agreement with Made By Us Studios, the production arm of major creator management company Made By All, to co-produce creator-led vertical series for TikTok and its microdrama app PineDrama. It’s the social media company’s second major microdrama deal after it announced a partnership with Issa Rae’s Hoorae Media to co-develop microseries in April. Mady By All, the management company behind Made By Us Studios, represents creators including Dhar Mann (who is already making his own microdramas with Fox and Holywater), One Battle After Another actor Teyana Taylor and YouTuber Adam Waheed. Made By Us Studios is led by former Range Partner Tanya Cohen as well as Made By All founder Leanne Perice and Made By Us president of production Nic Stanich. The deal was announced at MIPCOM, where TikTok unveiled the first two projects in the slate. Player is a romantic revenge thriller starring and co-executive produced by creator Hannah Stocking and additionally produced by Jonas Barnes. The series was written by Arun Blair-Mangat and Chela Reyna and directed by Louiza Zouzias. The Knock is described as a “genre microseries” (no word yet as to the precise genre) starring actor and content creator Adam Rose and actor Zaria Simone ( Pretty Little Liars: Original Sin ). It was created and directed by R.H. Stavis and is executive produced by Spooky Pictures (Watcher) alongside the musician Moby’s Little Walnut Productions. Moby also composed the series’ music. “Micro-series are pioneering a new language of storytelling,” TikTok’s global head of entertainment and micro-series Dawn Yang said in a statement about the deal. “We’re thrilled to partner with Made By Us on a slate that puts creators at the center, alongside established producers and industry talent, to tell stories designed for the feed from the start. This is an exciting step forward in our continued investment in the next generation of premium vertical storytelling on TikTok and PineDrama.” Made By Us Studios co-CEO Tanya Cohen said in a statement that vertical series are “the next evolution” for creators. “The opportunity isn’t to make smaller versions of television — it’s to build an entirely new premium storytelling language around the way audiences actually consume entertainment today,” Cohen added. “TikTok understands that behavior at a global scale, and together we have the opportunity to build franchises with creators who arrive with audience, community and cultural relevance already built in.” TikTok’s deal with Hoorae Media started big earlier in the year with Screen Time , a hit microdrama about a terrible double date. The series, starring Xavier Avila, Jasmine Luv, Eric C. Lynch and Brittney Jefferson, has earned nearly 580 million views globally since it premiered in April. THR

articles.title: Netflix Lays Off Around 1,000 Employees In Largest Cuts Since 2022
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 14, 2026 6:31am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images Netflix staff were informed that the company will undergo significant layoffs Wednesday, a source confirms to The Hollywood Reporter , as the streaming giant seeks a reset amid efforts to keep its global business growing. The company is expected to cut about 6 percent of its workforce, or about 1,000 people, making it the largest staff reduction at the company since 2022. Netflix co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters announced the cuts in a memo to staff Wednesday morning. The company’s product, tech, legal and HR teams are said to have been particularly impacted. “Our mission – to entertain the world – is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” the co-CEOs wrote in the memo, which was obtained by THR . “Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full- year forecast. We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high- impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors.” Ted Sarandos lamented at the Bloomberg Screentime summit on Sept. 30 that “overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to, and we’re working on making that move faster.” While the company continues to post robust profits, and remains the biggest player in subscription streaming, its viewing time has stagnated in recent months. With advertising one of the company’s growth areas, it needs to keep boosting that viewership engagement. Netflix has mostly avoided large-scale layoffs in recent years (the last major round of cuts was 2022 ), though the company has made adjustments on specific teams over time. The streaming giant is set to report its Q3 earnings next week, and the company is expected to share more information at that time. You can read the memo from Sarandos and Peters below. Team – We wanted to share that we are making a number of organizational changes and, as a result, we’ll be letting go of roughly 6% of our colleagues, with the greatest impact to our product, tech, legal, and HR teams. Decisions like these are never easy, and we don’t take them lightly. Our top priority today is to support those who are leaving Netflix. The process will vary somewhat by country, but leaders will be connecting with impacted employees soon. If you are leaving, please know that we will support you throughout this transition and make sure you have as much clarity and context as possible. We also want to say thank you. What you’ve built, and the care you brought to Netflix, have made a lasting difference and we will always be grateful. For the rest of the team, we know you have questions, too. Our mission – to entertain the world – is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources. Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full- year forecast. We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high- impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors. We know changes like this are tough, but let’s stay focused. This is one of the most dynamic times in the history of entertainment – and it’s a moment perfectly suited to a company like ours that’s built at the intersection of technology and entertainment. Now it’s on us to step up and meet the moment, together, like we always do. Ted and Greg More to come. THR

articles.title: “Ruthless, Sexual Predator”: Russell Brand Rape Allegations Detailed as Prosecution Opens Case
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All October 14, 2026 6:56am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand arriving at Southwark Crown Court on Oct. 14, 2026. Courtesy of Getty Russell Brand ‘s rape trial is officially underway at London’s Southwark Crown Court, with the prosecution describing the disgraced actor and comedian as a “ruthless” and “calculated” sexual predator. Eight men and four women are serving on the jury, the selection of which took place on Monday and Tuesday this week . On Wednesday, Brand was photographed arriving at the court with his wife, Laura, who was reported to have warmly smiled at him throughout the proceedings in court. Brand, best known for his roles on Big Brother’s Big Mouth and in Forgetting Sarah Marshall , is accused of three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one allegation of indecent assault, with six women alleging crimes dating from 1999 to 2009. He denies all of them, telling a swarm of journalists on Wednesday morning: “I feel blessed. I feel, of course, concerned, but hopeful that this process will lead to good outcomes for everybody — that is my prayer.” (Since the allegations have come to light, Brand has turned to Christianity and been baptized.) Related Stories Movies 'Pop Pop,' 'Kidney' and 'Sounds of the Desert': Tallinn Sets Rebels With a Cause, Critics' Picks Programs Movies Stephen Chow's 'Shaolin Soccer' Spinoff 'Kung Fu Soccer' Sets U.S. Release After Dominating China's Summer Box Office Such was the heavy media presence at Southwark Crown Court that officials were forced to put journalists in an “overflow room” watching through video link, according to BBC News coverage . The BBC described Brand as remaining “very still” throughout Wednesday’s session, rubbing what looked like a pebble. Details of the claims against Brand were revealed by the prosecution, led by lawyer Riel Karmy-Jones. She kicked off by telling the jury that Brand was “ruthless and calculated” in his attacks against the six women, who “have never met each other, and who came forward independently of each other.” “His desire, strong desire for some form of sexual contact was indiscriminate and voracious,” continued Karmy-Jones in her opening remarks. She called Brand a “sexual predator,” and cited the testimony of a former friend of his, who said Brand bragged to him that he was “a ladies man, a womaniser, and an expert pick-up artist.” According to this ex-acquaintance, Brand said he wanted to “bed 5,000 women” in his lifetime and had set himself “rules” to achieve this. The first complainant, whose claims Brand says are untrue, was said by the prosecution to have been raped by Brand. In her 20s at the time, Karmy-Jones said she was told “exactly what she needed to hear” and that he manipulated the situation to have sex with her “against her will.” This woman reportedly assumed Brand was gay and left the room to use the bathroom, telling him to make a cup of tea. When she emerged from the toilet, the prosecution said, Brand was partially undressed. “She was taken aback, she was shocked and didn’t really know what to do, and in her words, she froze a bit,” said Karmy-Jones. After the alleged rape, the prosecution says Brand was questioned by police. He said if it happened, he didn’t remember the incident. He said he did not remember the complainant’s name but “had never engaged in non-consensual activity.” The first complainant said she was “too scared to say anything” because of his celebrity status. The second complainant’s allegation of indecent assault dates back to 2001, when she was in her 30s and working at MTV. After admiring Brand’s T-shirt, the prosecution said that he offered to give the woman the item of clothing. “Make sure you give it a good wash first,” she says she told him, and offered to show Brand where the toilets were. Here, prosecutors say, he asked her to “come in” and grabbed her forearm. She began struggling and pulling back and described a “desperate, wide-eyed look on his face,” according to the BBC. Brand eventually relented and went into the toilet. A third complainant says she met Brand at a party in Soho, London in 2004. In the middle of a conversation, he lurched forward and grabbed her breasts and squeezed them with both hands, the prosecution told the jury. The woman was “shocked” and Brand had a “big, weird grin” on his face, she said. He grabbed her arm and pulled her toward the toilets. As they drove to another venue later in the evening, the prosecution says Brand pulled out his penis and told the complainant to “suck it.” Karmy-Jones said: “He simply laughed but appeared to accept her refusal.” The fourth complainant relates to an incident in 2004/2005 at Capital Radio, where Brand “grabbed” the woman’s face with both hands and pushed her up against a wall, the prosecution said. “He also grabbed her body, at her breasts, sides and buttocks — aggressively,” according to Karmy-Jones’ counsel. The complainant tried to push him off, but “he was too strong. […] He continued to kiss her on her face, and down her neck and onto her chest area, grabbing her bum and moving his mouth towards her cleavage, and grabbing her breast so hard that it was painful.” She was then able to push him away. A reminder: Brand denies all of these claims. The fifth complainant is reportedly the youngest of the women involved. She is said to have met Brand when he was performing at the Hammersmith Apollo in London in 2009. The incident began with consensual vaginal sex. “She said she did not really enjoy the experience. It felt very awkward and said it could have been anyone,” according to Karmy-Jones. Brand then raped her anally, while the woman asked him to stop, the jury was told. “She spent months and years blaming herself for what had happened, and became extremely anxious and continued to be unwell as a result,” said Karmy-Jones. Prosecutors say after this interaction that the woman received a text from Brand, to which she replied something along the lines of: “Why are you even messaging me?” He is said to have responded: “Because you’re dirty, and I wanna push you further.” The fifth complainant says told him: “I think you pushed me far enough — you treated me like an animal.” His response was immediate — “I’m sorry” — and she did not see or hear from Brand again, the jury heard. The prosecution said Brand was interviewed in relation to this offence, and provided a statement to police. “In that statement he set out that he has never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity, and that any accounts had been reinvented or imagined after a defamatory documentary and subsequent press reporting,” the counsel informed the court. The sixth complainant accused Brand of sexual assault. She says he demanded a massage when she was working with him in 2009. When she refused, Brand was described as becoming “unhappy” and said he would not complete the task otherwise. He is alleged to have fallen to his knees “and placed his head directly into her groin area.” The woman did complain at the time in 2009 and it “went higher up the ladder,” but she felt it wasn’t taken seriously. Brand denies every single allegation from these six women. Toward the end of Wednesday’s proceedings, the jury was again told that he “provided a prepared statement setting out that he has never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity, and that any accounts had been reinvented or imagined after a defamatory documentary and subsequent press reporting.” The trial could last up to 10 weeks. THR

articles.title: NBC’s ‘Dateline’ Headed to Canada
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 14, 2026 7:08am Add us as a Google Preferred Source From left: Longtime 'Dateline' correspondents Keith Morrison, Josh Mankiewicz and Andrea Canning, and the team’s senior executive producer, Liz Cole, photographed July 26 at PMC Studios in Los Angeles. Photographed by Joelle Grace Taylor NBC’s Dateline , the top-rated true crime series, is getting a Canadian spin-off series north of the border from Nov. 26. Keith Morrison, who got his start in journalism in his native Canada, will be in Toronto on Wednesday to tout the first international expansion of the Dateline franchise as part of a licensing deal with Rogers Studios. Dateline Canada on Citytv and Citytv+ will be hosted by Diana Swain, a former senior investigative correspondent for CBC News and host of The Investigators on the CBC News Network in Canada. She left Canada’s public broadcaster in 2024 after 33 years with the CBC, where Morrison in part perfected his iconic Dateline voice. After starting out in Canadian radio in the 1960s, Morrison joined the CTV Network in 1973 as a correspondent, producer and eventually a news anchor. In the early 1980s, Morrison became a co-host of the CBC Network’s The Journal flagship news and current affairs program. He joined NBC in January 1986 as co-anchor of the 5 p.m. and 11 p.m. news on KNBC-TV in Los Angeles. Dateline Canada will premiere with a two-hour special revisiting the wrongful conviction of Robert Baltovich, who was jailed for the murder of then-girlfriend Elizabeth Bain after her disappearance in 1990. Baltovich spent nine years in prison until 2000, before an eventual acquittal in 2008 after prosecutors dropped all charges. The Dateline Canada t eam, having reviewed police files on the case, claims to have uncovered an unreported police investigation. The long form true crime special will feature Baltovich, a retired Toronto Police officer who worked on the case and experts as it kicks off a Citytv series about sensational Canadian crimes and their victims and suspects.
