articles.title: Banana Republic Debuts First Scripted Microseries, an Office Comedy Starring Jack Innanen (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Katie Kilkenny Plus Icon Katie Kilkenny Enterprise Reporter, TV & Labor katiekilkenny7 Follow Sign Up View All October 14, 2026 7:09am Add us as a Google Preferred Source In ’The Agency,’ Jack Innanen plays four different employees of a fictional travel agency. Courtesy of Banana Republic Maybelline. Crocs. Marc Jacobs. These are just a few of the brands that have recently turned to the microdramas format to spin a yarn while, naturally, advertising their goods. And now, Banana Republic can be added to that list. The Gap-owned brand debuted the initial episode of its first scripted microdrama on Wednesday, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. The Agency stars Adults and Big Mistakes actor Jack Innanen as four different employees at an old-school, full-service travel agency called Travel & Tours that is rocked when a corporate suit (played by Innanen’s Big Mistakes costar Taylor Ortega) arrives to modernize it. Milo Tucker-Meyer plays the agency’s intern. Soapy, salacious and steamy romance stories might have popularized the microdrama format globally, but the first episode of The Agency positions the series as an office comedy with quick cuts and wink-wink lines and visuals. Innanen‘s characters in the five-episode series include a manager lacking confidence, a cocky cruise specialist, an adventure expert who deeply fears adventure and a Francophile who hasn‘t left American soil since the late ’90s. As one might expect, each of his characters are impeccably dressed in Banana Republic fits. Banana Republic chief marketing officer Meena Anvary said the brand decided to try the format in order to honor its “storytelling heritage.” Banana Republic Travel & Safari Clothing Company, as the company was initially titled, was the 1978 brainchild of a journalist and newspaper illustrator (founders Mel and Patricia Ziegler) whose early catalogs paired travel stories with apparel for sale. “We viewed this as a really interesting opportunity and way for us to hit on the nostalgia of the brand that people know and love and introduce the brand to new audiences via this TikTok series, bringing in some humor and storytelling to it as well,” Anvary said. Anvary was tightlipped about whether the brand will continue to invest in microseries or more entertainment moving forward, saying executives want to see how the audience engages with this first attempt first. But The Agency , at least, is part of a larger trend as Banana Republic’s parent company, Gap, Inc., has recently invested in building up an entertainment infrastructure amid a “fashiontainment” push. Earlier this year the company hired former Paramount exec Pam Kaufman as its chief entertainment officer and fellow Paramount alum Lourdes Arocho as head of licensing . The production company behind The Agency , Banana Republic Productions, dates back to earlier this year when the label collaborated with New York’s Explorers Club on a shortform docuseries about notable figures in science and exploration. “When we look at Gap Inc.‘s fashiontainment platform, it’s been a huge area of focus at the total company,” Anvary said. “For Banana in particular, it’s about us going back to our DNA and heritage and storytelling roots.” Entertainment is particularly valuable for marketing, Anvary added, because it helps keep a brand top of mind for consumers and encourages them to consider it when making purchasing decisions. The Agency , which has been produced especially for the TikTok audience but will be available on multiple social channels, will release episodes (and some behind-the-scenes material) weekly. Watch the series debut below. @bananarepublic Meet Travel & Tours. The last travel agency in New York City, where things have been done a certain way for a very long time. Until now. New faces, big ideas, and a staff that doesn’t exactly see eye to eye. The Agency, Episode 1 is here. ♬ original sound – Banana Republic – THR

articles.title: France’s Luxbox, Spain’s Amore Cine Join Melina León’s Ventana Sur Proyecta Title ‘Portrait Huaco’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Oct 14, 2026 5:16am PT France’s Luxbox, Spain’s Amore Cine Join Melina León’s Ventana Sur Proyecta Title ‘Portrait Huaco’ (EXCLUSIVE) Director Melina León was the first female Peruvian filmmaker to screen at Cannes' Directors' Fortnight with her debut feature 'Song Without a Name,' also handled by Luxbox By Anna Marie de la Fuente Plus Icon Anna Marie de la Fuente @adelafuente1 Latest France’s Luxbox, Spain’s Amore Cine Join Melina León’s Ventana Sur Proyecta Title ‘Portrait Huaco’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago ‘I’m Still Here’ Star Maeve Jinkings Set for Women’s Convent-Prison Daring Escape Drama ‘Cabildo 71’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Cannes Festival Winning Producer Quijote Films Launches In-House Scripted Series Division (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Portrait Huaco' Credit: Natalia Grande France’s Luxbox and Spain’s Amore Cine have boarded the Peruvian drama “Portrait Huaco” (“Huaco retrato”) by Melina León, best known for her debut feature “Song Without a Name” (“Canción sin nombre”), which world premiered at the 2019 Cannes Directors’ Fortnight. “ After the incredible journey we shared with ‘Song Without a Name,’ I’m thrilled to continue collaborating with Melina, now as both international sales agent and co-producer,” said Luxbox’s Fiorella Moretti. Related Stories Skydance to Fully Reorganize International; Kevin MacLellan Will Not Lead Key Group 'Cyberpunk 2077' Movie in the Works at Paramount She added: “As a Peruvian, it is especially meaningful to help bring Gabriela Wiener’s bold and contemporary work to the screen through Melina’s singular vision. ‘Portrait Huaco’ explores questions at the heart of today’s conversations in a truly original way, and I have no doubt it will resonate with audiences around the world.” Popular on Variety For Paz Lázaro, who co-founded Amore Cine alongside Edson Sidonie (“Karnawal”) and Juan Pablo Felix (“Mil pedazos”), “Adapting Gabriela Wiener’s ‘Portrait Huaco’ means bringing to the screen a work that bridges Latin America and Spain, weaving colonialism, racism, identity and desire with a voice both ancient and radically contemporary.” “For Amore Cine, alongside our fellow producing partners, this is an opportunity to champion a film with international reach that challenges perspectives and reexamines our shared history.” Based on the autobiographical novel of the Peruvian author, the project participates in the 8th Proyecta Co-Production Forum at Ventana Sur , which takes place in Montevideo, Uruguay this year from Nov. 30 – Dec. 4. Amore Cine and Luxbox join Peru’s Mano de Obra Cine, led by Melissa Cordero, and La Vida Misma Films, which produced “Song Without a Name.” The story follows Gabriela who returns to Lima after her father dies. Back home, she discovers a book by her great-great-grandfather, Austrian explorer Charles Wiener. Her search into the family past becomes a reckoning with the lingering legacies of colonialism, internalized racism and abandonment. “’Portrait Huaco’ combines a distinctly Peruvian perspective with universal themes of identity, memory and colonial heritage. Under the direction of Melina León, the film seeks to preserve its cultural roots and Peruvian creative leadership while embracing an international scope through strategic co-production partnerships,” said Cordero. This is the second time for Mano de Obra to co-produce with Amore Cine. Late coming-of-age drama, “Ofelia,” currently in post,’ is a European-Latin American co-production that includes Amore, Argentina’s Bikini Films, Quijote Films of Chile, Brazil’s África Filmes and CUP Filmes, Spain’s Potenza Producciones and France’s Reality Films. Said Cordero: “I’m interested in producing auteur-driven films with a distinctive cinematic voice and strong cultural identity, as well as genre films that can connect with wider audiences. I’m particularly drawn to stories rooted in Peru and Latin America that explore universal themes, bringing local perspectives to an international audience.” “My near-term strategy is to strengthen Mano de Obra Cine’s position as a production company focused on feature films, building strategic co-production partnerships across Latin America and Europe. I aim to combine public and private financing with international partnerships and distribution opportunities to develop a sustainable slate of films with strong creative identities and international reach.” Director Melina León Fox News Expands Podcasts With All-Female ‘the Girls’ ‘48 Hours’ Expands Use of Video Podcasting With ‘Woman in the Woods’ Erin Andrews and Charissa Thompson Bring Their ‘Calm Down’ Podcast to Colin Cowherd’s The Volume Netflix Doubles Down on Podcasts: Streamer Orders New Shows From Katt Williams and Harlan Coben, Renews Full Slate of Originals Kerry Washington Expands ‘Street You Grew Up On’ Interview Series Into Weekly Ongoing Podcast From Her Simpson Street Production Company and Daylight Nile Rodgers to Host iHeartMedia’s ‘Before the Moment’ Podcast With Sienna Spiro, John Legend and More Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘Forensic Files’ to Resume Original Production Amid the Streaming Boom for Vintage True Crime Series
articles.full_text: Oct 14, 2026 5:30am PT ‘Forensic Files’ to Resume Original Production Amid the Streaming Boom for Vintage True Crime Series By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest ‘Forensic Files’ to Resume Original Production Amid the Streaming Boom for Vintage True Crime Series 2 hours ago Gary Cosay, Co-Founder of United Talent Agency, Dies at 92 2 hours ago ITV Studios Revs Up Scripted Dramas and Format Deals Amid Media Arm Sale Process 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Radial Entertainment “ Forensic Files ” is headed back to the lab. Radial Entertainment has teamed with Content Partners and ITV Studios to produce new episodes of the series that examines true crime tales from the perspective of scientific evidence and data analysis. The partners plan to deliver 20 fresh episodes that are expected to spark renewed interest and viewership of the “Forensic Files” library of 400 episodes. The series originated in the mid-1990s on Discovery’s TLC channel as “Medical Detectives.” It’s had numerous incarnations since then and is available on YouTube and other ad-supported streaming platforms. With the new batch of episodes, Radial and Content Partners will give the show a big SEO push across multiple digital platforms. Radial is in the midst of executing the same model on the unrelated unscripted series “The FBI Files.” Related Stories Bradley Cooper to Star as Duke in 'G.I. Joe' Reboot From Danny McBride A24 British Shows ‘It Gets Worse,’ ‘Major Players’ and ‘The Ministry of Time’ to Stream on Paramount+ in U.S. “ ‘Forensic Files’ helped define true crime television, and its focus on science and evidence continues to resonate with one of the most loyal audiences in the genre,” said David Buoymaster, Radial Entertainment’s chief investment officer. “Working with Content Partners to create new episodes is a natural next step in our relationship and an opportunity to build on the series’ legacy.” Popular on Variety Content Partners, the Los Angeles-based rights management firm and holding company, has owned “Forensic Files” since 2024. “From the outset, we saw an opportunity to build on the extraordinary history of ‘Forensic Files,’” said Scott Hemming, Content Partners’ executive VP. “Radial shares our commitment to the series, and with ITV America’s production expertise, we’re excited to bring audiences new investigations with the scientific detail and clarity that have made ‘Forensic Files’ a tentpole of unscripted television.” Buoymaster, Cristina Guggino and Katie Carroll are executive producers for Radial Entertainment, with Steve Kram, Hemming and John Mass serving as executive producers for Content Partners. articles.title: DataFuelX Launches Video Ad Marketplace That Taps 13 Different Publishers
articles.full_text: Oct 14, 2026 6:00am PT DataFuelX Launches Video Ad Marketplace That Taps 13 Different Publishers By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest DataFuelX Launches Video Ad Marketplace That Taps 13 Different Publishers 1 hour ago Rachel Nichols Will Lead ‘The Story,’ a Daily Show From Sports Illustrated 2 hours ago Disney Broadens Super Bowl LXI Plans With Pat McAfee, Next-Gen Stats 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Cheyne Gateley/VIP As media audiences fall apart, one analytics company hopes to knit some of them back together. DataFuelX , a company led by former TV-sales executives is launching DFX Marketplace, a new way for advertisers to connect to commercial inventory across multiple publishers with a single point of entry. The company, co-founded by Dan Aversano and Michael Strober, two sales veterans who have between them logged stints in senior roles at places like WarnerMedia, TelevisaUnivision, and Nexstar Media, among other companies, launches its offer at a moment when advertisers find themselves hard-pressed to reach large groups of consumers across linear or digital. Related Stories 'Cyberpunk 2077' Movie in the Works at Paramount Bradley Cooper to Star as Duke in 'G.I. Joe' Reboot From Danny McBride “We’re launching a cross-publisher marketplace for linear and CTV, supporting both demographic and audience-based buying. Agencies will have multiple ways to participate –through the platform, APIs or their own AI agents. Our platform will also support direct transaction across linear and digital as well as programmatic execution. This is a very unique model,” says Aversano during a recent email conversation. “Most solutions we have come across are primarily focused on digital-only programmatic transactions.” Popular on Variety The company says DFX Marketplace is supported by 13 premium video publishers representing nearly 40% of linear impressions across more than 50 networks, reaching 70% of U.S. TV households. Aversano declined to name the companies involved, but a Wednesday event unveiling the marketplace is slated to include executives from Fox Corp. and TelevisaUnivison, as well as Sean Cunningham, president and CEO of the VAB, a trade organization that represents most U.S. TV networks to the broader advertising market. The rise of such a marketplace comes as more commercial inventory, particularly that associated with streaming, is purchased in programmatic fashion, or via algorithms and software designed to seek out ad time that is seen by a particular audience niche, such as someone in a particular geographic region, for example, or someone who is likely to be in need of a car or baby products. DataFuelX said its new marketplace will support buying and selling done via agentic AI and will enable AI assistants and customer agents to work across all participating publishers through a single connection. The marketplace is being built to support agentic buying and selling, enabling DFX AI assistants and approved customer agents to work across participating publishers through a single connection while preserving human control over strategy and final decisions. Participants in the new marketplace will be able to keep tabs on planning, activation, optimization and other tasks all under one system. “Premium video remains one of the most powerful ways for advertisers to build reach, but the complexity of differentiating true premium video across an increasingly expanding, but diluted ad inventory infrastructure has limited the growth and its share of overall video ad dollars,” says Cunningham, in a statement. “DFX Marketplace represents an important step toward modernizing that infrastructure for cross-publisher and cross-platform, using intelligence, automation and AI to make premium video easier to access, transact and optimize at scale.” The company says its platform is already used by major publishers and has supported more than $300 million in media transactions. Clayface is Matt Hagen, an actor whose face is disfigured by a local mob boss. Desperate, he volunteers as a test subject for scientist Dr. Caitlyn Corr (Naomi Ackie), who transforms his body into clay and causes him to lose his sanity. articles.title: Ventana Sur Proyecta 2026: A Powerhouse New Generation Lineup Backed by Some of Latin America’s Finest Producers
articles.full_text: Oct 14, 2026 6:09am PT Ventana Sur Proyecta 2026: A Powerhouse New Generation Lineup Backed by Some of Latin America’s Finest Producers Natalia Oreiro, Maeve Jinkings are attached to star in projects; producers include Rei Pictures, Piano, Tarea Fina, Luxbox and Cannes Un Certain Regard winner Simón Mesa Soto By John Hopewell , Emiliano de Pablos Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Rabbits' Courtesy of Ocúltimo Packed to its entirety by first and second-time directors, the 12 projects at this year’s Ventana Sur Proyecta co-production forum delivers a new generation snapshot backed by some of Latin America’s finest producers which delivers a searing portrait of the contemporary realities. In key casting Brazil’s Maeve Jinkings, renowned for her pivotal role in Walter Salles’ Oscar-winning “I’m Still Here,” is set to star in “Cabildo 71.” Natalia Oreiro (“Yosi, the Regretful Spy”) in “The Other Mountain.” Related Stories David Ellison's 'Day One’ Skydance Press Conference: Studio Lot Dibs, Trump Ties and Everything Else We Learned A24 British Shows ‘It Gets Worse,’ ‘Major Players’ and ‘The Ministry of Time’ to Stream on Paramount+ in U.S. Of project confirmed Tuesday by the San Sebastián Oil. Festival, which partners on Proyecta with Cannes Festival’s Marché du Film and Ventana Sur, “Give Me Shelter” marks one of the latest projects from Rei Pictures . Based in Argentina, Mexico and Spain, it is behind Lucrecia Martel’s Venice Selected “Our Land,” Argentine Oscar submission “Kill the Jockey” and Cannes Un Certain Regard winner “The Settlers” of just recent films. Popular on Variety “Give Me Shelter” will mark Nicolás Pérez Veiga’s feature debut after an prize-laden adversing career, including seven Cannes Lions, an International Emmy nomination for “Out There” and directing “Ringo, Glory and Death.” Set up at Cannes Critics’ Week Next Step workshop, “The Absence” is produced by Julio Chavezmontes’ famed Piano, a Mexico City-based producer and co-producer on movies from Apichatpong Weerasethakul, Ruben Östlund, Lucrecia Martel and Leos Carax. “Rabbits” marks the first new Colombian director title from Colombia-based Ocúltimo, co-founded by Simón Mesa Soto , director of acclaimed “A Poet,” a Cannes Un Certain Regard Jury Prize. Ocúltimo aims “to become a platform for new generations of Colombian filmmakers with bold, director-driven films,” Mesa Soto told Variety . “Los Mejores Días” is set up at Juan Pablo Miller’s Tarea Fina , a bastion of Argentine arthouse cinema, behind such standouts as Cannes Camera d’Or winner Las acacias,” “Incident Light” and “Sleepwalkers.” Boarded by France’s Luxbox Spain’s Amore Cine, Ventana Sur Proyecta Co-Production Forum Title “Portrait Huaco” weighs as the second feature from Melina León, whose “Song Without a Name” (“Canción sin nombre”) world premiered at the 2019 Cannes Directors’ Fortnight. A closer look at the 12 film projects at this year’s Proyecta lineup: “ The Absence,” (“La Ausencia,” Jorge Sistos Moreno, Mexico) The feature debut of Sistos Moreno, whose “The Darkness was selected for Cannes Critics’ Week in 2022. In 18th century Morelia, a mestizo woman, the lady of an estate, invokes an ancestral deity in search for a for her husband’s syphilis, passed on to her. “This film speaks to a wound that remains open even today: racism, and the inability to accept ourselves and our heritage because of the forces and paradigms imposed upon us,” says Sistos Moreno. “ Cabildo 71,” (Victoria “Pitoka” Pena, Uruguay, Brazil, Argentina, Spain) A sophomore outing for Victoria “Pitoka” Pena, whose debut feature, “Delia”, won the Silver Biznaga for Best Director at the Málaga Film Festival, “Cabildo 71” is based on real-life events about the women imprisoned in Cabildo — a prison-convent run by the nuns of the Good Shepherd. An intimate take on the biggest women’s jail break in history. Boarded by Una Presencia (Argentina) and Vitrine Filmes (Brazil/Spain), lead produced by Monarca Films of Uruguay and co-producer Boulevard Filmes, Brazil. “ Dirty Face” (“Cara sucia,” Ignacio Acconcia, Spain) Acconcia draws on a decade working with people with intellectual disabilities for his fiction feature debut. Led by Ayhe Productions alongside Kabiria Films and Barcelona-based Contraria Media, the drama follows a Black teenager with vitiligo who finds acceptance while performing community service at a disability care home. The producers are also behind the upcoming “March 14th,” winner of the Berlinale Co-Production Market’s VFF Talent Highlight Award. Ayhe’s David Aymerich says the film aims to bring underrepresented communities to the screen. ‘Dirty Face’ Courtesy of Ayhe Productions “ Give Me Shelter,” (“Un Lugar Seguro,” Nicolás Pérez Veiga, Argentina, Mexico) “A true facts-based thriller, set just days before Argentina’s 1976 military coup, “a story of resilience and courage that almost nobody knows,” says Pérez Veiga. When his father is kidnapped by a paramilitary task force days before the coup, doctor Gustavo Vaca Narvaja returns to his family and decides to risk everything on a desperate escape. “There’s only one problem: they are twenty six, and none can be left behind.” ‘Give Me Shelter’ Courtesy of Rei Pictures “ Isabel Hernández” (Giorgio Giampà, Italy-Mexico) Italy’s Zoe Films, behind Venice competition entry “A Bit of Light,” leads Giampà’s feature debut alongside LaDoc and Mexico’s Fiasco and Madrefoca. Set in Guatemala, the drama follows a young agronomist investigating her long-absent father amid the migration crisis. With established Italian arthouse distributor Teodora Film on board, the project participated in TorinoFilmLab’s FeatureLab 2026. “I was immediately drawn to the depth and complexity of its characters and its careful exploration of how trauma translates across generations,” says Fiasco’s Elena Fortes. ‘Isabel Hernández’ Courtesy of Zoe Films “ Los Mejores Días,” (Maria Zanetti, Argentina) The second feature from María Zanetti, a 2025 Argentina AMPAS best first feature for debut “Alemania.” Set over three timelines and straddling Argentina and Spain, a potentially powerful portrait of young love and an enduring passion, despite a darker side, an “exploration of love with no adornment nor emphases,” says Zanetti. “ The Other Mountain” (“La otra montaña,” Horacio Reyes Páez, Uruguay-Argentina) Natalia Oreiro (“Wakolda”) is attached to star in a new take on the 1972 Andes plane crash, told from the perspective of a mother awaiting news of her missing son. Reyes Páez, her real-life grandson, calls it “the intimate, invisible battle of a mother, far from the snow and the wreckage.” Uruguay’s U Films and Sueño Cine produce alongside Argentina’s FAM Contenidos. ‘The Other Mountain’ Courtesy of U Films “ The Place and the Hope,” (“El lugar y la esperanza,” Ariagna Fajardo Nuviola, Cuba-France) Nuviola revisits the impact of a community filmmaking initiative launched 30 years ago in her native Sierra Maestra. Produced by Julio Raúl Vega Garcés’ Torrente Films, the feature documentary draws on family archives to explore cinema’s power to preserve collective memory. Backed by Cuba’s Film Promotion Fund, it won a Eurodoc special mention at Montreal’s RIDM Forum. ‘The Place and the Hope’ Courtesy of Torrente Films “ Portrait Huaco,” (“Huaco Retrato,” Melina León, Peru, France, Spain) An awaited adaptation of Peruvian author Gabriela Wiener’s autobiographical novel “Portrait Huaco.” Gabriela returns to Lima after her father dies. Back home, she discovers a book by her great-great-grandfather, Austrian explorer Charles Wiener. Her search into the family past becomes a reckoning with the lingering legacies of colonialism, internalized racism and abandonment. Produced by Peru’s Mano de Obra Cine, led by Melissa Cordero, and La Vida Misma Films, both behind “Song Without a Name.” “ Rabbits,” (“Conejos,” Sara Nanclares, Colombia, Chile, Germany, France) A powerful high-caliber Latin-America-Europe co-production that revisits a social experiment in birth control carried out in Colombia for over 30 years. “With a sharp script and a witty, outspoken protagonist who refuses to be defined by her circumstances, the film challenges conventional views of teenage pregnancy, bringing to light the desires and contradictions that lie beneath it,” says Nanclares. “ Salamanca,” (Juan Sebastian Torales, Argentina, France) The second feature from Torales whose “Almamula,” a coming-of-age drama , rooted in the legends and folklore of the Argentine countryside, played Berlín’s 2023 Generation 14Plus. Set up at Lorena Quevedo Argentina’s Twin Latin Films (“Venezia”), who co-produced Torales’ debut. “ Unfit Mother,” (“Mala madre,” Manuela Espiñeira, Chile) Chilean outfit Pinda Producciones, behind Berlinale players “Skin in Spring” and “The Nature of Invisible Things,” teams with Espiñeira’s MoveShot on her feature debut. Actress and co-scribe Nicole Rubio stars as a progressive politician whose baby dies after she accidentally leaves him in her car, triggering a devastating personal and public reckoning. “The Movie Teller” actress Sara Becker co-stars. It explores how a woman is judged “not only for what happened, but for the way she has worked, loved and mothered,” Espiñeira says. ‘Unfit Mother’ Courtesy of Pinda Producciones HBO Max to Revamp Harry Potter Film Rewatch Podcast Into Companion Series for New TV Show (EXCLUSIVE) Tom Hanks, Ta-Nehisi Coates and More Join Barack Obama’s ‘A Great Book’ Podcast at Audible Fox News Expands Podcasts With All-Female ‘the Girls’ Ethan Hawke Stars in Supernatural Horror Podcast ‘Midnight Radio’: ‘There’s an Intimacy to the Audio-Only Medium’ Marvel Launches ‘Countdown to Avengers: Doomsday Official Podcast’ Ahead of Movie’s December Debut ‘48 Hours’ Expands Use of Video Podcasting With ‘Woman in the Woods’ Loading comments...

articles.title: Netflix Lays Off 6% of Employees, Elimination About 1,000 Jobs in Biggest Cutbacks to Date
articles.full_text: Oct 14, 2026 6:18am PT Netflix Lays Off 6% of Employees, Elimination About 1,000 Jobs in Biggest Cutbacks to Date By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Netflix Lays Off 6% of Employees, Elimination About 1,000 Jobs in Biggest Cutbacks to Date 56 minutes ago Ari Emanuel and Ben Persky’s Podcast ‘Rushmore’ Returns for Season 2 With Guests Including Larry David and Jerry Seinfeld 19 hours ago Peacock App Launches ‘Your Bravoverse,’ Featuring a Personalized TikTok-Style Video Feed Hosted by AI-Generated Andy Cohen 22 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images Netflix is swinging the axe — laying off around 1,000 employees, representing 6% of its workforce, in what is its biggest layoff to date. Most of the layoffs will affect workers in Netflix’s product, technology, legal and HR teams, co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters wrote in an email to employees Wednesday morning about the layoffs. “Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” the co-CEOs said in the memo, a copy of which was obtained by Variety (read it in full below). Related Stories A24 British Shows ‘It Gets Worse,’ ‘Major Players’ and ‘The Ministry of Time’ to Stream on Paramount+ in U.S. Skydance to Fully Reorganize International; Kevin MacLellan Will Not Lead Key Group A Netflix spokesperson said the company did not have any comment beyond the memo from Sarandos and Peters. Popular on Variety Netflix, the industry’s biggest premium streaming provider with more than 325 million customers globally, has posted double-digit growth in both revenue and profits in recent years. In 2025, the company had $45.2 billion in revenue (up 16%) and net income of $11 billion (up 26%). But investors have been concerned that Netflix’s engagement on a per-user basis slowed in the first half of 2026. “Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full-year forecast,” Sarandos and Peters said in the memo. For 2026, Netflix projects revenue of $51.0 billion-$51.4 billion (up 13%-14%) and operating margin of 31.5% (versus 29.5% in 2024). The co-CEOs continued, “We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation.” However, they said, “Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors.” As of the end of 2025, Netflix had about 16,000 full-time employees. The last major Netflix layoffs came in 2022, when it axed about 450 staffers following the streamer’s net decline of 200,000 subscribers in the first quarter of that year, its first such drop in more than a decade. The company has made additional smaller cutbacks since then, including letting go several dozen members of its global product team earlier in 2026. Netflix is scheduled to report third quarter 2026 earnings on Tuesday, Oct. 20, after market close. For the second quarter, the streamer posted earnings in line with Wall Street forecasts , with revenue up 13.4% year-over-year to $12.6 billion and operating margin of 33.4% (down from 34.1% in the year-earlier period). But Netflix issued Q3 revenue guidance below analyst expectations, driving the stock price down. Shares of Netflix were down 0.3% in trading as of 10:10 a.m. ET Wednesday, to $70.26/share, amid a decline in the broader market. Read the memo from Sarandos and Peters to Netflix staffers: Team — We wanted to share that we are making a number of organizational changes and, as a result, we’ll be letting go of roughly 6% of our colleagues, with the greatest impact to our product, tech, legal, and HR teams. Decisions like these are never easy, and we don’t take them lightly. Our top priority today is to support those who are leaving Netflix. The process will vary somewhat by country, but leaders will be connecting with impacted employees soon. If you are leaving, please know that we will support you throughout this transition and make sure you have as much clarity and context as possible. We also want to say thank you. What you’ve built, and the care you brought to Netflix, have made a lasting difference and we will always be grateful. For the rest of the team, we know you have questions, too. Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources. Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full year forecast. We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors. We know changes like this are tough, but let’s stay focused. This is one of the most dynamic times in the history of entertainment — and it’s a moment perfectly suited to a company like ours that’s built at the intersection of technology and entertainment. Now it’s on us to step up and meet the moment, together, like we always do. articles.title: Apple TV’s Hit German Series ‘Where’s Wanda?’ Returns for Season 2, Again Asking: ‘How Far Would You Go to Save Your Child?’
articles.full_text: Oct 14, 2026 6:41am PT Apple TV’s Hit German Series ‘Where’s Wanda?’ Returns for Season 2, Again Asking: ‘How Far Would You Go to Save Your Child?’ UFA Fiction managing director and executive producer Nataly Kudiabor discusses the dark comedy's popularity, maintaining momentum and the elements that set it apart, including its star-studded ensemble cast By Ed Meza Plus Icon Ed Meza @edmezavar Latest Apple TV’s Hit German Series ‘Where’s Wanda?’ Returns for Season 2, Again Asking: ‘How Far Would You Go to Save Your Child?’ 34 minutes ago Going Big in Japan: International French Hit ‘Bright Minds’ Season 7 Heads to Tokyo (EXCLUSIVE) 6 hours ago Louis Malle’s ‘Elevator to the Gallows’ Set for 70th Anniversary 4K Release as Jean-Jacques Beineix’s ‘Betty Blue’ Hits Big Screen After 35 Years 22 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Where's Wanda? Courtesy of Apple TV “Where’s Wanda?” Apple TV ’s first German series, proved a major hit for the streamer. The show’s creative team at UFA Fiction have now raised the stakes with Season 2. Set in the town of Sundersheim, the series’ first season followed parents Carlotta (Heike Makatsch) and Dedo (Axel Stein) Klatt on their desperate search for their missing daughter (Lea Drinda), with the help of tech-savvy son Ole (Leo Simon). Obtaining gear from the darknet, they spy on their neighbors and local residents, uncovering in the process many of the town’s hidden secrets. Related Stories A24 British Shows ‘It Gets Worse,’ ‘Major Players’ and ‘The Ministry of Time’ to Stream on Paramount+ in U.S. Bradley Cooper to Star as Duke in 'G.I. Joe' Reboot From Danny McBride Wanda was finally found at the end of Season 1. But, found standing over a dead body, Wanda ends up behind bars in Season 2. Popular on Variety “Where’s Wanda?” Season 2 was created, written and executive produced by Oliver Lansley, whose credits include the Anna Paquin drama “ Flack ,” alongside award-winning executive producer and UFA Fiction managing director Nataly Kudiabor (“Arthur’s Law”) and Oliver Ossege (“Helgoland 513”). The series was co-created and based on a story by Zoltan Spirandelli (“Vaya con Dios”) and is directed by Tobi Baumann (“Faking Hitler”) and Christian Ditter (“How To Be Single”). Speaking to Variety about the success of “Where’s Wanda?” Kudiabor discusses the hit show’s popularity, the challenges of maintaining momentum and an ensemble cast that boasts some of Germany’s top acting talent. Season 2 picks up at “a fantastic starting point,” Kudiabor notes. Without revealing spoilers, it’s suffice to say a major plot twist at the end of Season 1 “opened up a whole new set of possibilities.” “Wanda’s parents Carlotta and Dedo are once again desperately trying to protect their daughter, this time by proving her innocence and finding the real killer. Meanwhile, Wanda finds herself in prison, where she encounters some familiar enemies and faces threats of her own. “So, while we’re telling an entirely new story, we’re staying true to the emotional heart of the series: just how far would you go to save your child?” It was that concept that propelled Season 1 and made Apple TV’s first German-language series a solid hit. “For us, the priority was always to tell a compelling story that would connect with audiences, regardless of where they live,” Kudiabor stresses. The question of how far parents would go to save their child is a universal one, she adds. “We were delighted that Apple TV shared our belief that this was a theme with strong international appeal. “At the same time,” she adds, “it was very important to us that the show retain its distinctly German identity. This was also something our co-creators Zoltan Spirandelli and Oliver Lansley felt strongly about. Even though Sundersheim is a heightened, somewhat absurd version of a German small town, we wanted audiences to feel that this story is genuinely rooted in Germany. “I believe that authenticity is actually what helps a story travel internationally. You don’t have to make something less local to make it more universal.” Identifying the key elements that have contributed to the show’s success, Kudiabor says: “I think our secret ingredient is dark comedy. Alongside a genuinely gripping and emotionally grounded crime story, humor has always been an essential part of the DNA of the show: particularly for our writer and creator, Oliver Lansley. “Oliver has an extraordinary ability to balance real emotions and very human problems with increasingly absurd and sometimes outrageous situations. You find yourself laughing at moments when you probably shouldn’t, while still being completely invested in the characters and their struggles.” It’s precisely that balance that gives the show “its distinctive tone and sets it apart from other crime and mystery shows,” she adds. Another element that has made the show so appealing is its star-studded cast. This season Sam Riley (“Mint”), Alexandra Maria Lara (“ All Those Things We Never Said ”) and David Schütter (“ Barbarians ”) join the series. Returning cast members include Nikeata Thompson (“Späti”); Harriet Herbig-Matten (“ Maxton Hall: The World Between Us ”); Gisa Flake (“Berlin Station”); Palina Rojinski (“Welcome to Germany”); Suzanne von Borsody (“Run Lola Run”); Kostja Ullmann (“A Most Wanted Man”); Devid Striesow (“All Quiet on the Western Front”); Frederic Balonier (“Maxton Hall: The World Between Us”); Sascha Geršak (“Murder Mindfully”); Torben Liebrecht (“Altered Carbon”); Aaron Maldonado-Morales (“Sun and Concrete”); and Anton Dreger (“Two Sides of the Abyss”). “We’re incredibly fortunate to have such a brilliant ensemble from Season 1, and we’re thrilled to welcome some fantastic new actors for the second season,” Kudiabor says. “For us, it’s a huge compliment when actors of this caliber tell us they loved the first season, really connect with the scripts and are excited to become part of the show.” “Having Alexandra Maria Lara and Sam Riley — who are married in real life — playing the mysterious new neighbors of Carlotta and Dedo, portrayed so wonderfully by Heike Makatsch and Axel Stein, is a real gift. Their characters arrive in Sundersheim with a big secret of their own, adding another intriguing layer to the story. Kudiabor stresses that “bringing together such an exceptional cast, including familiar faces in unexpected roles, creates a real sense of excitement and curiosity for the audience.” Looking beyond Season 2, Kudiabor teases the possibility of future adventures. “Let’s just say that Oliver Lansley and all of us still have a few tricks up our sleeves when it comes to the future of the Klatt family. But for now, we’re very much looking forward to sharing Season 2 with audiences when it premieres on Apple TV on Oct. 21.” Pablo Torre Sounds Off on the NBA’s Historic Ruling Against the Clippers, Kawhi Leonard and ESPN — and Teases His Next Big Sports Investigation Marvel Launches ‘Countdown to Avengers: Doomsday Official Podcast’ Ahead of Movie’s December Debut Tom Hanks, Ta-Nehisi Coates and More Join Barack Obama’s ‘A Great Book’ Podcast at Audible Nile Rodgers to Host iHeartMedia’s ‘Before the Moment’ Podcast With Sienna Spiro, John Legend and More Erin Andrews and Charissa Thompson Bring Their ‘Calm Down’ Podcast to Colin Cowherd’s The Volume Ethan Hawke Stars in Supernatural Horror Podcast ‘Midnight Radio’: ‘There’s an Intimacy to the Audio-Only Medium’ Loading comments...

articles.title: Paul McCartney Calls Out Beatles Movies Because Paul Mescal Is Shorter Than John Lennon Actor; He Texted Director Sam Mendes: ‘Don’t Do This!’
articles.full_text: Oct 14, 2026 7:24am PT Paul McCartney Calls Out Beatles Movies Because Paul Mescal Is Shorter Than John Lennon Actor; He Texted Director Sam Mendes: ‘Don’t Do This!’ By Zack Sharf Plus Icon Zack Sharf Digital News Director ZSharf Latest Jessica Lange Says FX Was ‘Too F—ing Cheap’ to Pay for Cars Home From ‘American Horror Story’ Set, So ‘We Had to Drive Ourselves’ 2 days ago Ben Affleck Calls ‘Justice League’ Reshoots the ‘Low Point of My Career’: ‘It Was So Gross’ How the Studio Replaced Zack Snyder With Joss Whedon 2 days ago Amanda Seyfried Rejects Sex Scenes and Turned Down a TV Series Where ‘I’d Have to Have Sex All the Time’: I Don’t Want to Be ‘Naked With a Stranger’ 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images for The Rock and Ro Paul McCartney has a bone to pick with Sam Mendes , the director of the upcoming four Beatles movies starring Paul Mescal as McCartney, Harris Dickinson as John Lennon, Joseph Quinn as George Harrison and Barry Keoghan as Ringo Starr. What’s the issue? It all comes down to how tall Mescal is compared to his co-stars. “We were all the same height!” McCartney declared on the “Good Hang” podcast, noting how movies based on the Beatles wrongly depict him as shorter than his bandmates. “We were all the same height, and Ringo was a bit smaller. And if you look at photos, we’re all the same height.” Related Stories Skydance to Fully Reorganize International; Kevin MacLellan Will Not Lead Key Group 'Cyberpunk 2077' Movie in the Works at Paramount “Guess what?” McCartney added about Mescal. “He is smaller than the guy who plays John. Sam Mendes is making the film. I said, ‘Sam, I’ve got just one thing that I need to say to you. You know, Paul [Mescal is] a bit smaller.’ I don’t know how Sam’s gonna deal with it. He sent me a picture, a still from the filming they were doing, and they’re crossing the Abbey Road crossing, and the Paul character is markedly smaller. I texted him: ‘Sam! Smaller? Don’t do this! You said you wouldn’t do it.’” Popular on Variety McCartney also once expressed his frustration to Sam Taylor-Johnson, director of 2009’s “Nowhere Boy,” which starred Aaron Taylor-Johnson as a teenage John Lennon. Thomas Brodie-Sangster had a supporting role as McCartney in the biographical drama but is shorter than Taylor-Johnson. “The John character, who she later married, Aaron — he’s bigger than me in the film,” McCartney said. “My character is kind of wimpy. Smaller than John. John knocks me to the floor. And it’s like, ‘Sam, this is not true!’ Her only explanation, bless her, because she’s still a good friend, she said, ‘This is a movie, it’s not a documentary.’ And I thought, ‘Well, I don’t like that explanation.’ But I couldn’t do anything, because by now she’d made the film. There was I, little Paul. John, the great big hero, and it’s like: No! It’s not true.” Mendes is directing four Beatles movies, one centered on each of the band members. The project, officially titled “The Beatles – A Four-Film Cinematic Event,” has the backing of Sony Pictures and is currently in the middle of its year-long production. All four movies will be released theatrically in April 2028. “We want people to be able to experience them in the cinema at the same during the same period,” producer Pippa Harris recently said at the BFI London Film Festival , noting she does not expect audiences to “see all four films on the same day.” “Within the same month — you might see one a week, or you might see one weekend and two the next and one the next. However you see it, I think our hope is that people will see all four films,” she added. articles.title: Ben Frow To Leave Skydance’s UK Network 5 After 14 Years
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Netflix Layoffs Underway, Streamer Eliminating About 1,000 Jobs, 6% Of Its Workforce Read the full story By Jake Kanter , Jesse Whittock , Max Goldbart October 14, 2026 4:14am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ben Frow Edinburgh TV Festival EXCLUSIVE : The end of an era is approaching at 5 , the UK television network that sits within David Ellison ’s newly minted Skydance empire. Deadline can reveal that Ben Frow will step down as Paramount UK’s chief content officer next year, a role in which he has overseen 5 (formerly Channel 5) for 14 years. A charismatic creative executive, Frow is comfortably 5’s longest-serving content chief, joining in 2012, when British media baron Richard Desmond owned the network. Frow has decided to leave on his own terms, but his anticipated exit comes just a week after Paramount completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, creating the Skydance empire and precipitating a major executive reshuffle. Related Stories News Discovery+ Raises Prices In One Of Skydance's First Streaming Moves After Merger Close News 'M+/HBO Originals': Movistar Plus & Skydance Extend Partnership Kevin MacLellan, the Paramount international chief who oversaw 5, is exiting the business, as is his Warner Bros. Discovery counterpart Gerhard Zeiler. JB Perrette, one of the big winners of the $110 billion merger, will take on streaming and networks outside of the U.S ., with CBS chief operating officer Bryon Rubin put in temporary charge of 5 and Australia’s Network Ten. Watch on Deadline In an internal email seen by Deadline, 5 president Reemah Sakaan said Frow would step down from his day-to-day role in the summer of 2027. He will remain employed by Skydance until the end of next year. “His exceptional creative skills, obsession with our audience and fiery competitive spirit has led an acclaimed creative transformation of the network and has overseen a phenomenal range of hits,” Sakaan said. “I have only worked with Ben for a short while this year, but it has been an utter joy, so I have some sense of just how much he will be missed.” In the internal email, Frow added: “I have always said that this was the best job in the world, and I’ve absolutely loved my time at 5. But after 14 years where I’ve achieved everything I wanted to and more, it seems like the right time to hand over and give someone else a go. This isn’t a goodbye just yet and I’ll be around to support Reemah and the team with a smooth transition.” During his tenure, Frow has revitalized 5, transforming it from a broadcaster that was largely associated with overseas acquisitions like CSI to become a fleet-footed and risk-taking creative force. Frow’s legacy will perhaps be defined by his decision to cancel Big Brother in 2018. He took the cash from the Banijay-owned reality series and reinvested it into drama and high-end factual content. This gave rise to one of Frow’s biggest hits: All Creatures Great and Small , the Playground-produced drama based on the early career of veterinary surgeon James Herriot. All Creatures , which is co-produced by PBS Masterpiece, consistently delivers big audiences and was the most-watched scripted series on 5’s streaming platform last year. Other hit dramas have included Power: The Downfall of Huw Edwards and The Teacher . In factual, Frow has welcomed big names to the network like Monty Python star Michael Palin, who has journeyed to North Korea and the Philippines for documentary series. 5 scooped BAFTA and Royal Television Society awards in 2024 for White Nanny, Black Child , while Suicidal: In Our Own Words won a Grierson. The network was named Channel of the Year at the Edinburgh TV Festival in 2025, and posted a record operating profit of £71.7 million ($95M) in 2021 . Frow has many admirers in the UK television industry. He is respected by producers for his creative instinct and quick decision-making, while he inspires fierce loyalty among his small team of commissioners. He is an entertaining presence on public platforms: Honest, direct, quick-witted, and unafraid to have a dig at 5’s closest competitors . His mischievous twinkle saw him attend meetings this year wearing a Make Paramount Great Again hat — including during a sit-down with Ellison himself. On stage at the Edinburgh TV Festival in 2023, Frow revealed that he secretly resigned in April 2022 as a result of burnout following the pandemic, saying he felt as if he were being “pecked” alive. He later reversed his decision after his mental health improved. articles.title: Launch Financing To Expand Short-Term Indie Film Lending On Back Of New $15M Senior Credit Facility
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Netflix Layoffs Underway, Streamer Eliminating About 1,000 Jobs, 6% Of Its Workforce Read the full story By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Berlinale 2027 Retrospective To Explore Visions Of The Future In Nod To Centenary Of Fritz Lang’s ‘Metropolis’ ‘La Bola Negra’, ‘Woman Unknown’, ‘NAZA’ & ‘Fjord’ Among 68 Films On Shortlist For 39th European Film Awards Reese Witherspoon Partners With Mediawan To Buy Hello Sunshine View All October 14, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source André Holland and Kate Mara in 'The Dutchman' Frank DeMarco/Andre Gaines EXCLUSIVE: Beverly Hills-based film finance specialist Launch Financing is poised to scale up its short-term gap loan services for indie productions in the U.S., Canada and the UK having secured its first ever institutional $15M senior credit facility. The film-lending arm of producer-financier Chris K. Daniels’ The Launch Company , has previously funded more than 60 media loans against tax credits, pre-sales and other committed production receivables. Past recipient productions include thriller The Dutchman , black comedy Thumb and coming-of-age comedy The Marshmallow Experiment . Related Stories Casting Eric McCormack Set For Nimisha Mukerji's Psychological Thriller 'You're Safe Now' News 'A Long Winter': Watch First Trailer For Andrew Haigh Drama Starring Fred Hechinger, Ebon Moss-Bachrach, Caitríona Balfe & Kit Connor The new $15 million senior credit facility has been provided by specialty lender Pier Asset Management and is Launch Financing’s first institutional warehouse facility. Watch on Deadline The line, extendable to $25 million over time, will enable Launch Financing to scale its short-term production lending to independent films in the U.S., Canada and the UK. “A production’s money always comes slower than the production wants it to. Tax credits, bank closings, equity cashflow and distributor payments arrive on their own schedule, and the schedule is not the shoot’s,” said Daniels. “We built a standardized loan structure that clears diligence in two to five business days and wires within forty-eight hours of signing, because that is the only thing a producer in prep actually needs from a lender. This facility allows us to expand beyond our current pipeline and work more closely with high-quality producers, production companies, agencies and studios, improving the process one film at a time.” Launch Financing advances senior secured capital against money a production is set to receive and is repaid when that money arrives. Loans run eight to twenty-six weeks and are secured in first position against government production incentives, distributor minimum guarantees, pre-sales, committed equity, institutional capital and library-backed corporate guarantees. The money typically covers production cashflow while a bank or institutional lender closes, as well as cast escrow and union deposits, production payroll and finishing funds. Launch Financing sits inside The Launch Company alongside Launch Development, which develops and packages film projects; Cinelaunch, the company’s business-affairs and back-office platform; and Launch North, its physical production operation in Toronto. The lending team has sat on both sides of the table, as producers who have borrowed against tax credits and pre-sales and as the institutional capital that structures those loans. Daniels, who is also a strategic partner at Esme Grace, the boutique firm behind Michael Mann’s Ferrari , serves as chief executive officer of The Launch Company and its lending arm. Wyatt Cavalier is Launch Financing JV’s chief investment officer , and Jess Mastro is head of development for The Launch Company. articles.title: Moby, Hannah Stocking & Adam Rose Set For Microdrama Slate From TikTok & Made By Us Studios
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Netflix Layoffs Underway, Streamer Eliminating About 1,000 Jobs, 6% Of Its Workforce Read the full story By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Avatar Entertainment Adapting Vicente Vallés Novel ‘La Caza Del Ejector’ As TV Series Hearst Networks UK & Super Channel Search For Black Watch Entertainment’s ‘Missing Pieces’ Urban One Lines Up ‘Foul Play’ And ‘Power & Influence’ TikTok Microdramas View All October 14, 2026 6:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Moby, Hannah Stocking & Adam Rose Getty/PMC EXCLUSIVE: TikTok and creator economy firm Made By Us Studios have vertical video on the mind, and have enlisted major digital and music stars to help them. The two have partnered on a multi-year deal to make a slate of creator-led micro-series for TikTok and its app, PineDrama. Deadline has the news for you ahead of a MIPCOM session today officially unveiling the pact. The first two productions are Player , a romantic revenge thriller produced by Jonas Barnes, starring creator and actress Hannah Stocking , written by Arun Blair-Mangat and Chela Reyna. Stocking, who also serves as an executive producer, has also contributed to the script, with Louiza Zouzias the director. Related Stories News Urban One Lines Up 'Foul Play' And 'Power & Influence' TikTok Microdramas News Fox Entertainment & Kevin Hart's Hartbeat Strike Microdrama Deal The Knock , meanwhile, is being billed as a genre micro-series created and directed by R.H. Stavis, executive produced by Paranormal Activity and Weapons producer Spooky Pictures in collaboration with Moby ‘s Little Walnut Productions. Watch on Deadline The series stars actor, filmmaker and digital comedy performer Adam Rose opposite Zaria Simone ( Pretty Little Liars: Original Sin ). Moby also composed the series’ music. This is the latest example of how vertical video and microdrama is becoming central to major social media services’ video strategies. Microdrama has been a hot topic here in Cannes this week, as companies wrestle with how they invest and what creatives resources they employ. It comes after TikTok teamed with Issa Rae’s Hoorae to make micro-series Screen Time , which has amassed nearly 580 million views globally and become the top-performing show on the social platform and PineDrama. “Micro-series are pioneering a new language of storytelling,” said Dawn Yang, Global Head of Entertainment & Micro-Series at TikTok. She added the slate would put “creators at the center, alongside established producers and industry talent, to tell stories designed for the feed from the start. This is an exciting step forward in our continued investment in the next generation of premium vertical storytelling on TikTok and PineDrama.” Tanya Cohen, co-CEO of Made By Us Studios, added: “Creators have already transformed how audiences discover talent, culture and entertainment. Vertical series are the next evolution of that relationship. “The opportunity isn’t to make smaller versions of television – it’s to build an entirely new premium storytelling language around the way audiences actually consume entertainment today. TikTok understands that behavior at a global scale, and together we have the opportunity to build franchises with creators who arrive with audience, community and cultural relevance already built in.” “For over a decade, I’ve represented creators with the ambitions to develop premium IP and build careers in Hollywood,” said Leanne Perice, the other Made By Us Studios co-CEO. “Now, as a studio, we get to help bring those ambitions to life, working with them from the first idea through production. This partnership with TikTok opens an exciting new path for creators to develop scripted stories, take on leading roles and help shape the projects they’re part of.” Made By Us Studios launched earlier this year as social marketing firm Made By Us moved into digital production for the creator economy. TikTok, meanwhile, has been working with the likes of Tubi on creator-led content initiatives this year. articles.title: Netflix Layoffs Underway, Streamer Cutting 1,000 Jobs, 6% Of Its Workforce
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Netflix Layoffs Underway, Streamer Eliminating About 1,000 Jobs, 6% Of Its Workforce Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘The White Lotus’ Filming In Cannes As Season 4 Production Enters Final Stretch, Hôtel Martinez Transformation Confirms New Resort Logo Steve Stark’s Toluca Pictures Extends MGM TV Overall Deal, Expands Amazon MGM Studios First-Look Pact & Taps Max Kisbye As President ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ EP On How Harry Shum Jr. Juggles Medical Drama & ‘Dancing With The Stars’ & If It Affects His Presence On ABC Show View All October 14, 2026 6:27am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images Netflix has initiated a major round of layoffs today, eliminating about 6% of its global staff or some 1,000 jobs for its biggest round of job cuts in four years. The product, tech, legal and HR teams are among the most impacted by the cuts, which have been expected as the company faces slower growth and competition. Co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters unveiled the move in a memo to employees Wednesday, a copy of which was obtained by Deadline. A rep for Netflix had no comment. “Decisions like these are never easy, and we don’t take them lightly,” the CEOs said in the company email, which you can read in full below. “Our mission – to entertain the world – is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources. Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full-year forecast. We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors.” Related Stories Ratings 'Below' Attracts Record Debut For A Netflix Canadian Series Books First Trailer For Greta Gerwig's 'Narnia: The Magician's Nephew' Teases Punk Rock Multiverse & Cosmic Creation Of Aslan Sarandos and Peters acknowledged the challenging media environment, calling it “one of the most dynamic times in the history of entertainment” that is “perfectly suited to a company like ours that’s built at the intersection of technology and entertainment,” adding, “Now it’s on us to step up and meet the moment.” Watch on Deadline Netflix had not undergone significant layoffs since the big staff reduction of 2022, with the February product division cuts of several dozen employees among the most notable ones. The share price of the giant streamer has dropped more than 40% over the past year as Wall Street has increasingly scrutinized its viewer engagement, which increased only 2% over the first half of the year to 97 billion hours viewed. Sarandos addressed the topic of growth earlier this month at a Bloomberg conference. “Overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to, and we’re working on making that move faster,” he said. The company’s unsuccessful bid for Warner Bros. studio and streaming assets also spooked Wall Street a bit as investors took it as as sign that the company felt it needed a major deal to continue to grow, a notion Netflix’s top executives have dismissed. Additionally, the streamer has gone through one of its longest draughts without a breakout new series that has captured the zeitgeist the way shows like Stranger Things, Squid Game, Bridgerton, Queen’s Gambit, Wednesday, Baby Reindeer, and, most recently Adolescence, did. (It recently found success with its latest Harlan Coben adaptation, I Will Find You , which landed on the Most Popular English series list.) Netflix also is coming off a rare third-place finish at the Emmys behind rivals Apple TV and HBO. Interest in Netflix’s existing series is showing signs of waning too, with many returning series posting season-to-season viewership declines. The streamer has been shifting strategy by leaning into live events, including sports — including the upcoming NFL Thanksgiving Eve and Christmas Day games and the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua boxing match — podcasts and creator-driven content. Netflix also has been increasing theatrical distribution, with its upcoming movies The Misadventures of Cliff Booth, La Bola Negra and Possible Love all getting theatrical release before hitting the platform. Coming up on the series front are The Hunting Wives S2, The Diplomat S4, final season of Emily in Paris, Pride and Prejudice, and Lupin: Part 4 . In the most recent third quarter, Netflix reported revenue growth of 13% year over year to $12.6B, and operating margin was 33%. The company will report Q3 earnings on Oct. 20. Here is Sarandos and Petrers’ memo in full: Team – We wanted to share that we are making a number of organizational changes and, as a result, we’ll be letting go of roughly 6% of our colleagues, with the greatest impact to our product, tech, legal, and HR teams. Decisions like these are never easy, and we don’t take them lightly. Our top priority today is to support those who are leaving Netflix. The process will vary somewhat by country, but leaders will be connecting with impacted employees soon. If you are leaving, please know that we will support you throughout this transition and make sure you have as much clarity and context as possible. We also want to say thank you. What you’ve built, and the care you brought to Netflix, have made a lasting difference and we will always be grateful. For the rest of the team, we know you have questions, too. Our mission – to entertain the world – is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources. Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full-year forecast. We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors. We know changes like this are tough, but let’s stay focused. This is one of the most dynamic times in the history of entertainment – and it’s a moment perfectly suited to a company like ours that’s built at the intersection of technology and entertainment. Now it’s on us to step up and meet the moment, together, like we always do.
