articles.title: ‘Crystal Lake’ Review: Peacock’s Linda Cardellini-Starring Series Is the Best ‘Friday the 13th’ Property Yet (Which Isn’t Saying a Lot)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Daniel Fienberg Plus Icon Daniel Fienberg Chief Television Critic TheFienPrint Follow Sign Up View All October 13, 2026 8:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Linda Cardellini in 'Crystal Lake.' Matt Infante/PEACOCK Logo text As somebody who spent countless hours in the ’90s trawling Blockbuster shelves with friends looking for or awaiting the return of Friday the 13th entries we hadn’t seen, or hadn’t seen recently — my apologies for the wasted time, guys — it gives me no pleasure to admit that “What is the best Friday the 13th movie?” is a trick question. Unlike the Halloween and Nightmare on Elm Street franchises, there’s no clear prestige Friday the 13th film — just minor gradations in the quality of makeup effects or the creativity of the kills. I appreciate The Final Chapter for the weirdness of Crispin Glover’s performance, Part III for the hilarious vestigial 3-D effects, and even Part II because director Steven Miner knew where to put the camera, which can’t be said for all of his successors. Related Stories TV 'Crystal Lake' Will Offer More Brutal Kills Than Films, Go Deep on Jason's Background TV Alexander Brothers' Sex Trafficking Trial Tackled in Peacock's 'Wolves of Real Estate' Trailer Crystal Lake The Bottom Line Bloody well exceeds the low bar set by the movies. Airdate: Thursday, October 15 (Peacock) Cast: Linda Cardellini, William Catlett, Davin Kessler, Cameron Scoggins, Gwendolyn Sunstrom Developed by: Brad Caleb Kane Still, it was possible to assume that Peacock ‘s Crystal Lake would be the best entry in the franchise; the presence of Linda Cardellini getting eight hours to play Pamela Voorhees generated hopes for a level of quality none of the earlier films could muster, with or without such tantalizing revelations as “Where Jason’s mother got that spectacular sweater.” Indeed, thanks to newly minted Emmy winner Cardellini, giving the best Friday the 13th -adjacent performance to date, Crystal Lake lives up to that very reasonable level of potential. Is the series beyond Cardellini any good? It’s hard to always say. Following a template that eventually worked extremely well on A&E’s Bates Motel , occasionally well in Amazon’s newly released Carrie and barely at all on Netflix’s Ratched , Crystal Lake deserves some credit for taking a narrative expansion that could have been silly and making it earnest and nuanced, albeit in familiar prestige TV ways. But that also means that Crystal Lake takes itself more seriously than its auspices demand or can justify. Most of the episodes run at least 50 minutes and, after a fairly promising start, there’s a multi-episode lag before a season-closing rush of episodes that include a wild reconfiguring of the events of the first movie, as well as a wholly original flashback installment that plays like the bizarre love child of David Cronenberg and Douglas Sirk. Ultimately, Crystal Lake is better than it needed to be, occasionally because it’s twisted, gory fun and occasionally just because of the easy comfort of low expectations. After an in medias res introduction with Cardellini’s Pamela starring at herself in the mirror, drenched in blood, the story goes back nine months and we’re introduced to a cleaner Pamela working the kitchen at Camp Crystal Lake in New Jersey. Initially, camp is heaven for 11-year-old Jason Voorhees (Callum Vinson). Jason has a variety of birth defects that cause the cruel campers to make fun of him, but he does have one friend, fellow outcast Grace (Gwendolyn Sundstrom). He also has the doting love of Pamela, who tries to be a constant presence in Jason’s life and even gets him a mail-order box of camping supplies like a tent, nature cooking provisions and a machete. “You use it to clear brush and get rid of obstacles, make your own path,” Pamela explains helpfully, a line of dialogue most viewers are likely to miss because of the maniacal giggles elicited by “How Jason Voorhees Got His First Machete” origin story. Things do not work out well for poor Jason, who isn’t a very good swimmer to begin with — his malformed head makes him buoyancy-challenged — and then goes on an unsupervised swim. Why does he lack supervision? Because counselors Claudette (Danielle Kotch) and Barry (Phoenix Panevik) chose to go to a barn for nookie rather than watching their campers. Bad decision, Claudette and Barry. Back in the present day, which is actually 1971 or 1972, we see a distracted and grieving Pamela. The community of Crystal Lake wants to be supportive, especially Levon ( William Catlett ), a widower with a dark past and big ole crush on Pamela and her exceptional sweater. Levon, the local sheriff, wants Pamela to bowl and go to town picnics, but Pamela can’t move forward — especially since Jason’s body was never retrieved after his drowning. For a while, Crystal Lake hews closely to the very rudimentary mythology introduced in Sean Cunningham’s original movie. It’s structured so that dedicated fans are able to point in happy recognition at town landmarks, the architecture of the camp and the appearance of familiar characters including Ralph (Nick Cordileone), the crazy “Don’t go to Crystal Lake!” guy in the movies, now a Vietnam veteran suffering from serious PTSD. Then strange things start happening that don’t align with anything in the movies, including the arrival of two threatening men who show up asking questions about Pamela’s past and bring out the worst — or best, since Pamela Voorhees: Non-Violent Lunch Lady is not a show anybody would have watched — in our heroine. For a while, Crystal Lake suffers from many of the same issues that plagued the first season of Bates Motel — namely, a whole lot of incongruous elements that don’t even feel thematically connected to the things (hockey masks, nudity) that resonate about the movies. It feels like series developer Brad Caleb Kane is throwing random things against the wall, particularly seeding elements for a vast conspiracy that’s like something out of a half-dozen Stephen King novels rather than Friday the 13th . There’s a dogged journalist (Devin Kessler as Levon’s sister, Briana), who serves no purpose for a long time. Even when she becomes useful, it’s in a complementary way that could have very nearly been removed from the story entirely. There’s even a full episode set at an EST-style retreat, an over-extended if amusing gag suggesting that Pamela’s road to empowerment reaches a fork at which she has to choose between harmless self-actualizing platitudes or chopping negligent counselors to bits. I didn’t mind the EST episode, because it’s one of the moments that the series’ early-’70s setting pays off. It doesn’t quite make Pamela Voorhees into a feminist icon, but if you set your story in the days of Manson-inspired paranoia, Nixon-inspired institutional distrust and a burgeoning ERA ratification movement, the extreme reaction of a doting mother struggling to raise and then mourn her special needs child gains some resonance. The early episodes have a gritty, grindhouse-friendly look, with washed-out colors and grimy, dilapidated cars and exteriors. Michael Lennox, whose credits run the wide gamut from Derry Girls to Say Nothing , strikes an interesting balance among grounded realism, campy performances, gloomy settings, cheery soundtrack choices and wildly extreme violence. Very extreme. People in Crystal Lake are constantly being dispatched in ways that offer the most shredded flesh, spurting blood and oozing viscera possible. Why simply stab somebody when you could flay their face off and then do something even more disgusting to finish the job, before disposing of the body in an additional nasty way? It’s my instinct that more of the violence is CG-driven than practical, but if you come to Crystal Lake hoping to go “Ew!” and episodes require you to sit around for 45 minutes during which nothing happens, at least the kills should deliver. And they do. Without spoiling much, it’s the sixth and then seventh episodes directed by duo Celine Held and Logan George and then former cinematographer Quyen Tran that kick the show into a higher gear before an okay finale. The flashback episode, with a color scheme and overall tone lifted from 1950s melodramas and 1970s conspiracy thrillers, was the one hour I found myself wholly and unapologetically loving Crystal Lake , as opposed to mostly being curious about what the spine of the show would be once the homages ran dry. The primary reason to keep watching is Cardellini, who makes Pamela her own with few traces of Betsy Palmer’s fine, very broad work in the first film. Cardellini plays her as a strong but brittle woman, looking for a purpose without the child she built her life around, but always right on the edge of going to pieces. Don’t worry, the breakdown starts in a hurry and Cardellini is terrifying, if perhaps not as sympathetic as the series requires long-term. Fortunately, Sundstrom generates enough sympathy on her own, giving a sweet and vulnerable performance as the only Crystal Lake character you really don’t want to see die. Kotch and Parnevik, as the negligently canoodling counselors, inspire the opposite reaction as two characters whose destiny is inevitable and earned. Catlett’s character is an arbitrary addition to the series, and I never cared what his secret was from his days as a cop in Newark, but the actor is an assertive screen presence and there’s borderline sweetness to the flirtations between him and Pamela, two damaged souls. Other standouts include Manon Gage as a trouble-making hippie; a very hungry brown bear; Joy Suprano as a budding feminist who befriends Pamela; and a prolific TV presence who guest stars in the second half of the season. That’s already more standout performances than in the entire run of films, a reminder that working with trashy IP is a safer bet than attempting to embellish a classic. (Of course, Bates Motel got better and better as it went along, even though it got closer and closer to the key events from Psycho .) Crystal Lake may already have moved beyond the parts of the Friday the 13th franchise that made me keep watching film after film without thinking any of them was truly “good.” So even though the seeds planted for future seasons don’t fill me with optimism for more Crystal Lake , my low expectations have already been exceeded once. THR

articles.title: From ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ to a Stick-Figure YouTuber: THR’s First Animation Power List
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content (L to R): 'Wildwood,' 'K-Pop: Demon Hunters,' 'Simpsons' creator Matt Groening, 'Acme vs. Coyote' Laika, Netflix, Fox, Ketchup Entertainment Animation has never been bigger or more difficult to pin down. In the past year alone, a K-pop-fueled Netflix phenomenon swept the Oscars, a Chinese sequel became the highest-grossing animated film of all time and a stick-figure animator built an audience of 34 million-plus without ever setting foot in a studio. Meanwhile, a family of Australian blue heelers is teaching parents around the world how to raise their kids. Animation’s center of gravity isn’t just shifting — it’s multiplying. THR Which is why The Hollywood Reporter is launching its first-ever Animation Power List, a representative snapshot of the most important and influential figures working in animation today, across film, television and online. Box office and ratings matter, of course, and plenty of the names here have the billions to prove it. But commercial success is only part of the equation. We also weighed the more subjective, harder-to-quantify question of influence: Who is setting the aesthetic agenda, shaping the business models, launching new talent or simply making the rest of the industry look over its shoulder? We tried to strike a balance, pairing the studio heads and A-list directors who steer the biggest projects with the character designers, animators, FX supervisors and art directors whose craft, all too often, goes unsung. This is a snapshot, not a definitive ranking or a comprehensive census. In a business this big and this global, someone is bound to have been unjustly left off. To those we missed: We’re sorry, we’re big fans and there’s always next year. Consider this an opening sketch. Eric Bauza Image Credit: Storm-Santos Voice Actor ( Coyote vs. Acme, Teen Titans Go! ) Bauza has quietly become the voice of an entire cartoon universe. One of the successors to the legendary Mel Blanc as the voice of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Marvin the Martian and a dozen more iconic characters, the Canadian actor outdid himself with Coyote vs. Acme , voicing everything from Bugs Bunny to Foghorn Leghorn and Tweety Bird. Says Bauza: “A lot of talented folks worked really hard to make this film, and to be able to see it celebrated by so many people across the globe has really made the wait worth it.” Alan Becker, aka Noogai Animator/Influencer Becker built an empire out of stick figures. The self-taught animator behind Animator vs. Animation — known to 34 million-plus YouTube subscribers as Noogai — Becker turned a scrappy Flash experiment into a launchpad for a new kind of animation career, one built on tutorials, software tools and brand collaborations rather than a studio contract. Eric Beckman Image Credit: Leon Bennett/Getty Images CEO, GKIDS Beckman has brought international indie animation to the American mainstream, from The Secret of Kells and The Breadwinner to the Studio Ghibli catalog. GKIDS has built an audience, and an awards platform, for non-Hollywood animation, creating a sustainable distribution model for ambitious features made outside the major studios. Kristine Belson & Damien de Froberville Image Credit: SonyPicturesAnimation Presidents, Sony Pictures Animation Sony Pictures Animation’s presidents are having a moment. Belson oversaw the development and production of Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse , Sony’s first best animated feature Oscar winner, then, after de Froberville joined as president in 2025, conquered the world with KPop Demon Hunters . The duo say their proudest moment of 2026 is the commercial success of sports comedy GOAT : “Seeing audiences embrace an original story with such a distinctive point of view has been enormously gratifying.” Brad Bird Director ( The Incredibles , Iron Giant , Ray Gunn ) Bird doesn’t make small movies. The Oscar-winning director has spent decades proving animation can carry the same emotional and visual weight as any big-budget tentpole. After stints at Pixar and Disney, Bird returned to original feature animation this year with sci-fi noir Ray Gunn for Netflix, a passion project 30 years in the making. Brad Bird’s Ray Gunn hits theaters Dec. 4 and will be available on Netflix on Dec. 18. Skydance Animation/Netflix Jared Bush Image Credit: Disney Animation Studios Chief Creative Officer, Walt Disney Animation Studios Bush has become a key creative force shaping the next phase of Disney Animation. Under his leadership, the studio is expanding established franchises while developing new original features, including the upcoming Hexed . His latest effort behind the camera, on Zootopia 2 , which grossed $1.87 billion worldwide, wasn’t too shabby either. Enrico Casarosa Image Credit: Deborah Coleman / Pixar Director ( Luca , Gatto ) Italian-born auteur Casarosa first caught the world’s attention with the lyrical Pixar short La Luna , a visual poem about family rituals set against a moonlit seascape. Casarosa’s style, which brings the warmth, looseness and imperfection of hand-drawn illustration into 3D animation, will be on full display in his upcoming feature, the animated gangster comedy Gatto . The film will be Pixar’s big spring release of 2027. Arden Cho, May Hong & Ji-young Yoo Image Credit: Courtesy of Netflix Voice Actors ( KPop Demon Hunters ) In 2025, KPop Demon Hunters didn’t just become Netflix’s biggest movie of all time, it also turned Cho, Hong and Yoo, as Rumi, Mira and Zoey of fictional K-pop girl group Huntrix, into a genuine voice-cast phenomenon (with EJAE, Audrey Nuna and Rei Ami singing the Huntrix tracks). Cho’s combination of confidence and vulnerability, Hong’s sardonic self-assurance, and Yoo’s playful energy and comic timing combine into a chemistry that couldn’t have worked without all three. Sean Clarke Image Credit: Aardman Animations Managing Director, Aardman Animations Clarke runs the studio that refuses to give up the clay. As managing director of Aardman Animations, he’s kept the British stop-motion house behind Wallace & Gromit , Shaun the Sheep and Chicken Run in business without losing the handmade charm that’s kept audiences coming back for decades (Aardman celebrates its 50th anniversary this year). What would Clarke love to have made in the past year? “It would have to be Toy Story 5 ,” he says. “I worked at Disney when the first film was released and thought it was groundbreaking both in terms of its technique and storytelling.” Pierre Coffin Image Credit: Alex J. Berliner/ABImages Director ( Despicable Me , Minions ) The French director and co-creator of Despicable Me — who came up with the Minions’ multilingual nonsense language and still voices all the little yellow men — has built one of the world’s most successful animated franchises on slapstick timing and character design alone. Coffin continues to develop new animated concepts, but the Minions remain his calling card. Banana! Margie Cohn Image Credit: Alex J. Berliner/ABImages) President, DreamWorks Animation Since taking over as president in 2019, Cohn has pushed DreamWorks toward a broader creative slate and greater stylistic diversity, supporting films such as The Wild Robot . She has argued for a studio without a single house style, emphasizing distinctive filmmaker-driven approaches across both original films and established franchises. Joel Crawford, Januel Mercado Image Credit: Music-Factory Directors ( Forgotten Island ) Crawford and Mercado have been creative collaborators since meeting as storyboard artists on Kung Fu Panda 2 , their shared sensibility for broad comedy, kinetic action and character-driven storytelling finding expression in their work together on The Croods: A New Age and the Oscar-nominated Puss in Boots: The Last Wish . Forgotten Island , their first original feature as writers/directors, stylistically combines 3D CGI with expressive 2D shifts inspired by 1990s anime. Bill Damaschke Image Credit: VALERIE MACON/AFP via Getty Images President & Chief Creative Officer, Warner Bros. Pictures Animation Damaschke is leading Warner Bros. Pictures Animation’s theatrical comeback after a turbulent stretch of shelved projects ( The Day the Earth Blew Up , Coyote vs. Acme ). At Annecy this year, he unveiled a new studio logo and a seven-film slate that starts with the long-awaited The Cat in the Hat feature. “[This year] marks a defining milestone for Warner Bros. Pictures Animation,” says Damaschke. “After three and a half years of building this studio from the ground up, we finally get to share what we’ve been creating with the world!” The Disability Loop Group Image Credit: The Disability Loop Group Voice & Sound Artists The collective of disabled voice actors, singers and sound artists was formed in 2025 through the Easterseals Disability Film Challenge, which advocates for disability inclusion in the entertainment industry. This year they made history on Sony Pictures Animation’s GOAT , becoming the first disability loop group to work on a major studio production. “Having so many talented, disabled voiceover artists working on GOAT was our proudest achievement,” says Nic Novicki, who set up the Disability Loop Group (and is a member) through a partnership with the EDFC. Jaiden Dittfach YouTube Animator Dittfach turned her own life into a cartoon and built an audience of more than 15 million subscribers doing it. Since launching Jaiden Animations on YouTube in 2014, she’s pioneered a format that mixes autobiographical storytelling with whimsical illustration, expanding from web series into merchandise, live events and brand collaborations — proof of how far creator-driven animation can travel. Pete Docter Image Credit: Deborah Coleman / Pixar) Chief Creative Officer, Pixar Animation Studios With three Oscars and a body of work that has redefined what emotional storytelling can look like in animation, Docter needs no introduction. As Pixar’s chief creative officer since 2018, he’s overseen the studio’s next wave, balancing new voices and IP — with the likes of Elio and Hoppers — with careful curation of the studio’s blockbuster franchises. Jennifer Dodge Image Credit: Paramount Animation President, Paramount Animation Since taking over Paramount Animation in January, amid the shake-up that accompanied the studio’s $8 billion merger with Skydance, Dodge has quickly moved to build her own slate, drawing on the experience, at PAW Patrol producer Spin Master, of developing, producing and expanding global franchises. She has moved forward with a wide range of new titles, including Robert Rodriguez’s original Christmas feature The Naughty List , Dan Trachtenberg’s animated horror comedy Freddy the 13th and Bollywood-set animated musical Diya from Nitya Mehra. Holly Edwards Image Credit: Alex J. Berliner/ABImages President, Skydance Animation Edwards joined Skydance in 2019 after two decades at DreamWorks working on such global juggernauts as Kung Fu Panda and How to Train Your Dragon . Under her watch, Skydance’s Swapped became one of Netflix’s biggest animated hits, while Brad Bird’s Ray Gunn , also released by Netflix, is leading this season’s awards conversation. Matt Groening Image Credit: ©2004 THE SIMPSONS and TCFFC ©2004FOX BROADCASTING CO. Creator ( The Simpsons , Futurama ) Groening changed what animation could be on American television, and The Simpsons is still proving it. The longest-running primetime scripted series in TV history hit its 800th episode in February and, thanks to Disney+’s library of all 37 completed seasons, a new generation is being introduced to Bart, Maggie, Lisa, Marge and Homer. (A new Simpsons film is set for 2027.) What Groening did for the family sitcom, he repeated for sci-fi with Futurama , which is set to finish its revived Hulu run with three extended specials next year, and with fantasy with Disenchantment on Netflix. Animation’s living legend says he is not worried about an AI-dominated future. “I, for one, welcome our new A.I. overlords,” Groening says. “I’d like to remind them that, as a trusted TV personality, I can be helpful in rounding up others to toil in their underground data caves.” Jorge R. Gutierrez Image Credit: Vivien Killilea/Getty Images for IMDb Director ( Maya and the Three ) Gutierrez has spent his career putting Mexican folklore front and center in his animation, from the Guillermo del Toro-produced feature The Book of Life to Netflix’s Maya and the Three . Now he’s bringing that sensibility to Speedy Gonzales , the Warner Bros. Pictures Animation feature he is developing to reimagine the classic Looney Tunes character for a modern, more culturally attuned audience. Mark Henn Image Credit: Photofest 2D Animator Henn’s fingerprints are on some of the most iconic hand-drawn characters in Disney history — Ariel, Belle, Aladdin, Mulan — and he has been a key figure in linking the studio’s 2D past with its CGI present, serving as consultant on projects from Frozen to Big Hero 6 to Ralph Breaks the Internet . Takeshi Honda Image Credit: Courtesy of GKIDS Animation Director ( Neon Genesis Evangelion , The Boy and the Heron ) Honda is the animator’s animator, equally adept at crafting epic action sequences — see his work on the Neon Genesis Evangelion series — and subtle, emotional scenes with delicate human figures, a trait the great Hayao Miyazaki relied on when he brought Honda in as animation director on his 2024 Oscar winner The Boy and the Heron . Mike Judge Creator ( Beavis and Butt-Head , King of the Hill ) Judge has been animation’s sharpest cultural barometer since Beavis and Butt-Head first premiered on MTV back in the early ’90s. But his animation legacy arguably sits on the shoulders of King of the Hill , the Texas-set family comedy, rebooted last year, which somehow manages to bridge the political divide while being heartfelt and deeply funny. Maggie Kang & Chris Appelhans Image Credit: The Chosunilbo JNS/Imazins via Getty Images Directors ( KPop Demon Hunters ) Kang and Appelhans cemented their arrival as major animation players with 2025 phenom KPop Demon Hunters , which combined American 3D CGI style with elements of anime and Korean aeni to become a two-time Oscar winner and Netflix’s most watched film of all time. Jin Kim Image Credit: Courtesy of Jin Kim/Disney Character Designer ( Frozen , Zootopia ) Kim worked on Elsa’s visual development in Frozen and supervised character design on Big Hero 6 . His work across Wreck-It Ralph and Moana , Zootopia , Encanto , Strange World and more helped define Disney’s contemporary approach to characters. As the first Korean animator to work at Disney, his career also marked an important opening for Korean artists at the studio. Travis Knight Image Credit: Roy Rochlin/Getty Images President & CEO, Laika Knight has pushed stop-motion into spectacular new territory through 3D-printed facial animation and elaborate action, earning Oscar nominations for producing The Boxtrolls and directing Kubo and the Two Strings and Missing Link . His new feature, Wildwood , promises to take stop-motion places it’s never been before. Hikaru Kondo Image Credit: Koyoharu Gotouge/Sony Pictures Releasing/Courtesy Everett Collection CEO, Ufotable Kondo has overseen Ufotable’s transformation into one of anime’s most globally recognized names. The 2020 release Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba — The Movie: Mugen Train was Japan’s highest-grossing film ever, taking in more than $500 million worldwide, a feat topped by 2025’s Infinity Castle , which has earned more than $790 million, confirming anime’s arrival in the global mainstream. Anthony Leo CEO, Cartoon Saloon Leo hasn’t changed much about the animation being done at the Kilkenny-based studio set up by Tomm Moore, Nora Twomey and Paul Young back in 1999. The outfit behind Oscar nominees The Secret of Kells , Song of the Sea and Wolfwalkers is still making hand-drawn tales steeped in the stories and aesthetics of Celtic folklore. Leo has been expanding its global reach, forging co-production deals with the likes of Netflix and Apple TV. Phil Lord & Chris Miller Image Credit: Eric Charbonneau/Getty Images Producers & Directors ( The Lego Movie , Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse ) Lord and Miller have helped rewrite the rules of mainstream CG animation, with pop culture savvy and an anarchic approach to visual storytelling, from Cloudy With a Chance of Meatballs and The Lego Movie to the groundbreaking, Oscar-winning Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse , which pushed animation pipelines and comic book aesthetics further than most thought possible. Filippo Maccari Image Credit: Filippo Maccari FX Supervisor, Sony Pictures Imageworks Maccari’s visual effects work has powered some of the decade’s most striking animated films, from the Oscar-winning Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse and its sequel, to KPop Demon Hunters . His command of particle simulation, lighting and compositing turns ambitious director visions into fully realized worlds. Seth MacFarlane Image Credit: Pamela-Littky Creator & EP ( Family Guy , American Dad! ) MacFarlane built a media empire out of Family Guy , American Dad! and, through his Fuzzy Door banner, a willingness to push every boundary in sight. Family Guy premiered its 24th season on Fox this year, with a milestone 450th episode, and American Dad! hit 400. “I’m really not involved over there. I should probably send them a taco truck or something,” quips MacFarlane. Ted: The Animated Series , a spin-off of MacFarlane’s feature film franchise, hits Peacock Dec. 17, and he has a new Family Guy spinoff, Stewie , which received a two-season order for Fox and Hulu, starting for the 2027-28 season. As a voiceover artist, MacFarlane has a record-tying four Emmy wins for outstanding voiceover performance. But his proudest work achievement of the past year? “Despite all the temptation, never even coming close to starting a podcast.” Vivienne Medrano, aka VivziePop Image Credit: Ilya S. Savenok/Getty Images for Prime Video Animator ( Hazbin Hotel , Helluva Boss ) Medrano, aka VivziePop, has become one of the breakout creators of the online animation boom, turning her self-produced 2019 YouTube pilot for Hazbin Hotel into a global adult animation franchise, partnering with A24 and Bento Box Entertainment to turn it into a Prime Video series. At Annecy, Medrano announced she will make her feature debut with Prehistoria , an original animated musical, which Warner Bros. will produce. Chris Meledandri Image Credit: Alex J. Berliner/ABImages Founder & CEO, Illumination Meledandri has built Illumination Entertainment into one of the industry’s most profitable animation studios on the back of hits from Despicable Me and Minions to Sing and The Super Mario Bros. Movie . Meledandri’s cost-efficient, data-driven production model has kept the studio’s development cycles fast and its merchandising machine humming, while still providing space for individual creative expression. Yvett Merino Image Credit: Dan Abraham Producer ( Moana 2 , Zootopia 2 , Hexed ) Merino made animation history by becoming the first Latina producer to win the Oscar for best animated feature ( Encanto ), and the first animation producer ever to have back-to-back billion-dollar hits (with Moana 2 and Zootopia 2 ). Disney’s hit machine is looking to continue her run with the upcoming original film Hexed , which comes out in November. Hannah Minghella Image Credit: Hannah-Minghella Head, Netflix Animation Minghella oversaw Netflix’s biggest-ever animated hit with two-time Oscar winner KPop Demon Hunters , produced with Sony Pictures Animation, and helped shepherd through the summer hit Swapped and Brad Bird’s Ray Gunn , both with Skydance. Her upcoming slate includes Steps , a revisionist take on Cinderella, and the Roald Dahl spinoff Charlie vs. the Chocolate Factory . Hayao Miyazaki Image Credit: Photo by Steve Granitz/WireImage Director ( Spirited Away , The Boy and the Heron ) Miyazaki, the great master of Japanese animation and co-founder of Studio Ghibli, has built, after only perhaps Walt Disney, animation’s most influential body of work. Miyazaki films have set a global standard for lush hand-drawn animation, richly painted backgrounds and worlds that balance fantasy with deeply human stories. Officially retired or not, Miyazaki’s influence on the medium remains enormous. Japanese animation legend Hayao Miyazaki hired veteran Takeshi Honda for The Boy and the Heron, which won the best animated feature Oscar in 2024. Courtesy of Toho Manabu Otsuka Image Credit: Daniel Zuchnik/Getty Images for Sony Pictures CEO, MAPPA Since becoming president of MAPPA in 2016, Otsuka has built the Japanese anime studio into a global powerhouse, with such crossover hits as Jujutsu Kaisen and Chainsaw Man , whose feature spinoff Chainsaw Man — The Movie: Reze Arc , directed by Tatsuya Yoshihara, was a surprise cross over hit, earning more than $43 million domestically and $162 million worldwide. MAPPA marked its 15th anniversary this year with an expanded strategic partnership with Netflix aimed at developing and distributing new anime globally. Nick Park Image Credit: ©MattCrockett Director ( Wallace & Gromit , Chicken Run ) Park’s painstakingly crafted Oscar-winning shorts — Creature Comforts , The Wrong Trousers and A Close Shave — turned Aardman Animations’ handmade aesthetic into an international signature, while Chicken Run , co-directed with Peter Lord, showed that clay animation could power a major theatrical feature, grossing more than $220 million worldwide. Park remains an executive director at Aardman, where his influence extends through a generation of animators. On the subject of AI, Park is measured but firm: “We at Aardman must stick to our values. It will always be about the human touch for us.” Trey Parker & Matt Stone Image Credit: Leon Bennett/Getty Images Creators ( South Park ) Parker and Stone rewired adult animation with South Park , pioneering a rapid production model that allows the show to turn around topical satire while events are still unfolding. That approach has taken on new relevance in the Trump era , as the series has repeatedly used its speed and anything-goes irreverence to tackle Trump, his administration, political polarization, media pressure and the increasingly blurred line between politics and spectacle. Daley Pearson & Charlie Aspinwall Image Credit: Charlie Aspinwall, Daley Pearson Co-Founders/Directors, Ludo Studio Pearson and Aspinwall’s Ludo Studio turned an Australian blue heeler into a global children’s entertainment phenomenon with Bluey , whose warm, sharply observed depiction of family life has earned two International Emmy Awards and made the Brisbane-based studio one of Australia’s most successful animation exporters. A special mention has to go to Bluey creator Joe Brumm, who stepped away from the series in 2024 to focus on the upcoming Bluey movie, set to hit theaters Aug. 6, 2027. Marc du Pontavice Image Credit: Sameer AL-DOUMY / AFP via Getty Images Founder, Xilam Du Pontavice built Xilam into one of Europe’s most durable animation exporters, launching the French studio in the mid-1990s and steering it toward family-friendly slapstick hits like Oggy and the Cockroaches and Zig & Sharko , as well as the Oscar-nominated I Lost My Body and Zack Snyder’s Norse mythology series Twilight of the Gods for Netflix. Marci Proietto Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Head, 20th TV Animation Proietto’s tenure has been defined by extending the commercial life of animation’s biggest franchises across broadcast and streaming: In 2025, she helped secure unprecedented four-season renewals for The Simpsons , Family Guy and Bob’s Burgers , while bringing American Dad! back to Fox through the 2028-29 season. Says Proietto: “After 30 years in the business, getting to work alongside the best teams in animation is, hands down, what I’m proudest of.” Chris & Shannon Prynoski Co-Founders, President and Co-President, Titmouse Chris and Shannon Prynoski turned a T-shirt company they launched in 2000 into Titmouse, one of the most distinctive independent forces in contemporary animation. From Metalocalypse to The Legend of Vox Machina , the Prynoskis have built a studio, now with more than 700 employees in L.A., New York, Vancouver and Paris, that has repeatedly given animators room to experiment across styles, genres and platforms, proving that an animation company can operate at scale without adopting a conventional studio identity. Rahul Purini Image Credit: Crunchyroll President, Crunchyroll Once a niche anime streaming service, Crunchyroll, under Purini’s leadership, has become a major force in the U.S. entertainment business and done more than pretty much anyone else to bring Japanese animation directly into the American mainstream. Crunchyroll’s release of Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba — Infinity Castle became the highest-grossing anime film ever in the U.S., earning more than $136 million stateside. Chris Sanders Image Credit: Alberto E. Rodriguez/Getty Images Director ( The Wild Robot , Lilo & Stitch ) Sanders has helped shape mainstream animation for four decades, from story work on Disney classics including Beauty and the Beast and Aladdin to writing and directing Lilo & Stitch and How to Train Your Dragon . A four-time Oscar nominee, Sanders has shown that big-studio animation can combine commercial appeal with adventurous design and deeply emotional storytelling. Brad Schiff Image Credit: Courtesy of Laika Head of Animation, Laika Schiff oversees Laika’s stop-motion pipeline, the one responsible for Coraline , ParaNorman and the eagerly anticipated fantasy epic Wildwood . His work, pairing painstaking practical craftsmanship with newer tools like 3D-printed facial rigs, keeps Laika’s tactile, handmade identity intact even as the studio pushes into hybrid CGI territory. Matt Selman Image Credit: © Frank Micelotta/FOX Showrunner ( The Simpsons ) Seven-time Emmy winner Selman came up writing for Seinfeld before landing at the show he now runs day-to-day, charged with keeping its satirical edge and protecting its legacy. “You don’t want to be the person who ruins The Simpsons ,” he notes. Four decades in, he still sounds like a fan: “I’m so very, very, very proud that the writers of this 40-year-old show are still whipping up weird, funny, deep, surprising stories that are worthy of these iconic characters.” Domee Shi Image Credit: Deborah Coleman / Pixar Director ( Turning Red , Elio ) Shi has risen through the Pixar ranks, starting as a story intern, working on Inside Out , Incredibles 2 and Toy Story 4 , before writing and directing the Oscar-winning short Bao in 2019. Shi is now a Pixar vp creative, involved in key creative decisions across the studio. Makoto Shinkai Image Credit: Courtesy of Suzume Film Partners Director ( Your Name. , Suzume ) Shinkai has turned hyper-detailed backgrounds and aching romantic longing into box office gold, with Your Name. and Suzume both breaking records in Japan and helping spark a broader global anime moment. His meticulous, digitally driven visual style and commercial success won over Crunchyroll, which has picked up worldwide rights outside Asia and India to his next, unnamed feature. Nishimoto Shu President, Aniplex Nishimoto oversees an anime giant whose portfolio includes major franchises such as Demon Slayer , Fate and Sword Art Online , alongside games, theatrical distribution, licensing, merchandise and live events. Under Nishimoto, Aniplex is putting greater emphasis on international markets, working with Crunchyroll on global distribution. Andrew Stanton Image Credit: Deborah Coleman / Pixar Director ( WALL-E , Finding Nemo , Toy Story 5 ) A four-time Oscar winner, Stanton has spent more than three decades at Pixar as a writer, director and creative force behind some of the studio’s most influential films. After his triumphant animated return with Toy Story 5 , Stanton has said he wants to shift his focus to live action, but will keep a foot in Pixar, if only to help protect up-and-coming talents, like Daniel Chong, whose debut, Hoppers , Stanton helped defend against studio skeptics. Barbara Stephen Image Credit: Babara Stephen CEO, Flying Bark Stephen has helped transform Flying Bark Productions from an Australian children’s animation company into an international production powerhouse, combining original productions with animation services for global partners including Disney, Marvel, Netflix, Paramount and Nickelodeon. On AI, she takes a pragmatic view. “To me, the role of all emerging technologies is as a tool in service of the craft, to find real efficiencies in the pipeline, free up our crew to focus on higher-value work and facilitate more original storytelling,” she says. Tara Strong Image Credit: Tara Strong Voice Actor ( The Powerpuff Girls , Teen Titans Go! , Samurai Jack ) Strong is animation’s woman of a thousand voices, a prolific performer who has helped define the sound of multiple generations of animated characters, from Bubbles of The Powerpuff Girls and Twilight Sparkle in My Little Pony , to Batgirl, Raven and Harley Quinn in the DC animated universe. Toshio Suzuki Image Credit: Walt Disney/Courtesy Everett Collection Chairman, Studio Ghibli Suzuki has spent his tenure as Studio Ghibli’s chairman protecting the studio’s handcrafted legacy while still finding room to grow — expanding into digital distribution and international collaboration without diluting what made classics like Spirited Away , Princess Mononoke and Howl’s Moving Castle work in the first place. Genndy Tartakovsky Image Credit: Genndy Tartakovsky Director & Creator ( Hotel Transylvania , Samurai Jack ) Tartakovsky created Samurai Jack and the Hotel Transylvania franchise on the strength of a kinetic visual style and sharp comedic instincts that have carried through decades of work, including Dexter’s Laboratory and Primal . He’s now developing an animated Conan the Barbarian series for Prime Video, as executive producer and showrunner, that promises to bring the legendary swordsman into a fresh, action-driven format. Ami Thompson Image Credit: Courtesy of Disney Art Director ( KPop Demon Hunters , Raya and the Last Dragon ) As an art director, Thompson’s distinctive strength is her ability to combine characters and visual influences from very different worlds into a unified, graphic identity, whether that’s bringing together Disney princesses from multiple eras into a contemporary 3D aesthetic on Ralph Breaks the Internet or her bold mashup of K-pop glamour, anime-influenced character design and Korean mythology and shamanism on KPop Demon Hunters . Jae-myung Yoo CEO, Studio Mir Yoo has built Studio Mir into one of Korea’s most prominent animation studios for international productions, working on Nickelodeon’s The Legend of Korra and Voltron: Legendary Defender for DreamWorks and Netflix and on Netflix’s The Witcher animated spinoffs. He has used Mir’s blend of 2D animation craft and CGI production to move the studio from an overseas production partner toward a creator and production company in its own right. Fumio Yoshimura Image Credit: Netflix President & CEO, Toei Co. Yoshimura has led Toei Co., the parent company of Toei Animation, as president and CEO since 2023, bringing a background in content, media and international business to the company behind some of Japan’s most enduring entertainment franchises. His remit extends beyond animation to Toei’s film, television and live-entertainment operations, while Toei Animation remains the engine behind global properties including One Piece , Dragon Ball and Sailor Moon . Yang Yu Image Credit: Courtesy of A24 Director ( Ne Zha 2 ) Better known as Jiaozi, Yang directed Ne Zha 2 , the Chinese animated sequel that became a global box office phenomenon in 2025, earning $2.27 billion at the box office to become the most successful animated movie in history. (Disney’s Zootopia 2 , Hollywood’s top earner, is a distant second at $1.87 billion.) Unlike Japanese anime, Chinese animation hasn’t yet made the leap to mainstream success in the West, but with these numbers, it’s not clear why it needs to. Gints Zilbalodis Image Credit: Gints Zilbalodis Director ( Flow ) Zilbalodis turned an intimate, dialogue-free survival story into one of animation’s most unlikely recent breakthroughs with Flow , his independently produced feature about a cat navigating a world submerged by a catastrophic flood. Made mainly in Latvia on Blender, a free and open-source 3D graphics software, Flow won the 2025 best animated feature Oscar, becoming the first independent film to take the prize (as well as the first-ever Latvian Oscar). Zilbalodis is already chasing that same spirit of risk on his follow-up. “I’ve been working on my new film Limbo ,” he says. “With my team, we have been challenging ourselves to try some crazy ideas and to do things in very unconventional ways, which have been scary, but also very rewarding.” This story appeared in the Oct. 7 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

articles.title: ‘Queen Silvia’ Ditches the Glass Slipper for Un-Cinderella Royal Romance
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All October 13, 2026 8:40am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Queen Silvia' Amazon-Joyn-Pyjama-Pictures Every royal romance eventually gets the Cinderella treatment: the humble girl, the dashing prince, the ball, the happily-ever-after. Not so Queen Silvia . The new European aristocratic romance, which has its world premiere at international TV conference Mipcom tonight , ditches the fairy tale for a more realistic take on an ordinary girl who finds her prince. The six-hour limited series, produced by Berlin’s Pyjama Pictures with Sweden’s Unlimited Stories, follows the real-life romance between Silvia Sommerlath, a German-Brazilian interpreter working at the 1972 Munich Olympics, and Sweden’s Crown Prince Carl Gustaf, the games’ guest of honor. Their first meet cut is cut short by a terrorist attack — the Black September attacks on the Israeli team. Silvia holds her own under pressure, and the prince is smitten. But Silvia is not quite ready to trade her career for a tiara. Related Stories TV The Asylum Is Bringing 'Z Nation' Back From the Dead (Exclusive) Movies Amsterdam's IDFA Sets Int'l, Envision Competition Lineups, Adds 'Musk,' 'You Can See Everything' “Silvia is not a woman who wants to become queen,” series director Miguel Alexandre tells The Hollywood Reporter . “She was a very independent woman, following a great career, and was not at all impressed by all this royal baggage. But she falls in love with a man who brings this baggage with him.” “She was such a powerhouse herself already at such a young age, very independent,” says German actress Alicia von Rittberg, star of Charité and Becoming Elizabeth , who plays Silvia. “It was a struggle for her, to fit in with the royal world, to make that work.” Starting from 1970s Munich, the series carries through to the couple’s 1976 wedding, an event made world famous for its soundtrack. Swedish supergroup ABBA composed their hit “Dancing Queen” as a wedding gift for Queen Silvia, and performed the song live at a televised gala on June 18, 1976, the night before the royal wedding. Beta Film, which is selling Queen Silvia worldwide, leaned into the ABBA connection at Mipcom , hiring German-US singer Caro Kelley to perform a live version of “Dancing Queen” both at the company’s Beta Brunch sales event, at at the series’ world premiere gala. Swedish actor Edvin Endre ( Vikings , Fortitude , Eddie the Eagle ), who plays Carl Gustaf in the series, says Queen Silvia ‘s “more realistic, more grounded” take on the monarchy, could be a revelation for Swedes as well, who often view their King Gustaf in a less-than-favorable light. “When [the King] is portrayed, it’s usually as the butt of the joke,” says Endre. “He’s presented as being silly, goofy, not all that smart. I don’t think that’s the truth at all. I think he takes his job very seriously. So for this role, I wanted to go in the opposite direction.” Endre points to the king’s dyslexia as the root of the teasing. “Whenever he would give speeches from a very young age, he would stumble and he would struggle, and this is kind of the reason why people don’t take him seriously,” he says. “People were so brutal to him in the press.” The show’s approach, he says, is “a lot of sympathy and… making him as human as possible.” Endre describes the story of the two 20-somethings as being as much “a coming-of-age story” as a royal romance. “At the end of the day, they’re two young people sitting alone in a palace, trying to figure out each other and like if they can go on this journey together…being scared and being in love and all that stuff.” Adds Von Rittberg: “and both of them are trying to break free from the expectations of their parents.” Making a drama about a living king and queen is a risky business, as the show’s producers are well aware. Alexandre says Unlimited kept the Swedish court informed at every stage in the production, but that the royal family did not ask to participate. When asked about the show, the king said publicly that making a series about them while they are still alive was “a horrible idea.” But Endre is quick to allay fears that Queen Silvia is a hatchet job. “Everyone involved in this has really approached this project with a lot of like integrity and love and respect,” he says. He calls the real couple “the most progressive royals in the world,” who “really changed the monarchy in Sweden, made it more relevant and more approachable.” The royal family, however, will not be in attendance for Queen Silvia ‘s Mipcom premiere. The producers say the court was informed of the screening and replied with a curt “thanks and good luck.” A screener was also offered. No word yet on whether anyone is clearing a spot on the royal couch. THR

articles.title: How ‘Breaking Bad’ Actor R.J. Mitte Made an Impact as a Disability Rights Activist
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 13, 2026 8:49am Add us as a Google Preferred Source R.J. Mitte. Hatnim Lee/Getty Images R.J. Mitte was best known for playing the son of Walter White on the iconic TV drama Breaking Bad . But the actor also held another pivotal role. Mitte did a lot of good off the screen , via his family connected Mitte Foundation and through a host of health non-profits before his unexpected death on Monday. The actor, at age 34, died by suicide in Brownsville, Texas, his rep confirmed to The Hollywood Reporter. Mitte was diagnosed with Cerebral Palsy at age 3. He famously exaggerated his condition while playing Flynn, the son to Walter (played by Bryan Cranston ) and Skyler White (Anna Gunn), for five seasons on the Emmy-winning AMC drama that aired from 2008 to 2013. Mitte used his Breaking Bad platform to challenge stereotypes around people with disabilities. He advocated for greater inclusion as president of The Mitte Foundation , a Texas-based philanthropic organization launched by the late Roy F. Mitte and Joann Cole Mitte, his adoptive parents. In addition to driving disability rights awareness, the family connected foundation also offered scholarships and arts programs, and funded community initiatives. Related Stories TV 'Breaking Bad' Stars Bryan Cranston, Aaron Paul, Others Remember R.J. Mitte: "Sweetheart of a Young Man" TV R.J. Mitte, Walter White's Son on 'Breaking Bad,' Dies at 34 Mitte’s lifelong activism also included being an honorary trustee and spokesperson for United Cerebral Palsy after he was diagnosed with the neurological condition. In a 2015 interview with the BBC , Mitte recalled nabbing the role of Walter “Flynn” White Jr. at age 14 as a disabled actor as a part that “gave me an opportunity to bring light to subjects like this and disabilities that need to be heard and to show people how normal a disability really is.” He made his way to Hollywood by following his younger sister, Lacianne, after she got a job offer to work in film production. He first appeared uncredited a year later on an episode of Hannah Montana , and had early acting roles on 7th Heaven and Weeds. Mitte’s big break came with the Vince Gilligan drama, and his performance on 56 episodes of Breaking Bad drew on his real-life experiences with CP. Mitte also served as an ambassador for the Shriners Children’s nonprofit medical network as he urged more care for children with specialized health needs. The health non-profit supports research to develop new treatments for the benefit of physicians and other healthcare professionals and their patients. Mitte helped fundraise for Shriner’s Children after being treated at Shriners Hospital for Children in Shreveport, Louisiana, after his diagnosis and for most of his childhood to overcome physical and verbal impediments. “I can’t thank Shriners Hospitals for Children enough for what they did to help me overcome the effects of cerebral palsy,” the actor said in a 2014 statement as he joined a Love to the Rescue fundraising campaign. “Had it not been for my doctors and therapists, I would not be walking and talking as well as I am today. I know first-hand that Shriners Hospitals for Children is a special place where kids are given a life of possibilities because they send Love to the rescue every day.” At the 2013 Media Access Awards, Mitte received the SAG-AFTRA Howard Russell Award for his disability activism and portrayal of Walt Jr. That came on top of receiving a Screen Actors Guild Award for best drama ensemble for the final season of Breaking Bad. “Beyond his acting, Mitte advocated for people with disabilities and worked to raise awareness of a variety of conditions while pushing for expanded roles for people with disabilities in Hollywood with disabilities,” SAG-AFTRA said in an Instagram post on news of Mitte’s death. His Breaking Bad co-stars, meanwhile, led the Hollywood tributes that praised both his acting, as well as his activism. “That kid was pretty raw when we started shooting the pilot in February of 2007, but little by little we watched him grow into a really fine actor. He parlayed his experience on the show to be a vocal advocate for performers with disabilities, and was the head of a philanthropic organization with a focus on helping the disabled community,” Cranston shared , in part, in a lengthy post on Instagram. “We were texting each other just a few weeks ago — figuring out when we could meet for lunch. I don’t know if that lunch would have changed his future… But I do know that I loved him, and thoroughly enjoyed being with him throughout the years on the series, and after the spotlight on Breaking Bad dimmed… I’ll miss you,” son.” THR

articles.title: Ryan Coogler’s ‘X-Files’ Update Scores Hulu Series Order
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All October 13, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Danielle Deadwyler, Himesh Patel and Ryan Coogler Melissa Alexander; Courtesy of Subject; Arturo Holmes/Getty Images Logo text The truth is still out there. A reboot of The X-Files shepherded by Ryan Coogler has landed a series order at Hulu . The Sinners filmmaker has been developing the project for several years , and he wrote and directed the pilot episode. Coogler will be an executive producer on the series, with Jennifer Yale ( Underground, See ) serving as showrunner. Onyx Collective and 20th Television produce along with Coogler’s Proximity Media. Danielle Deadwyler ( Rooster, The Harder They Fall ) and Himesh Patel ( The Odyssey ) will star in the series as “two highly decorated but vastly different FBI agents who form an unlikely bond when they are assigned to a long-shuttered division devoted to cases involving unexplained phenomena,” per the show’s logline. Related Stories TV 'All's Fair' Season 2 Is Back With a Vengeance -- and a Release Date TV Jamie Foxx Does Not Want to Be Canceled Over New Hulu Stand-up Special: "After That Kevin Hart Roast, I Had to Cut Everything" “I’ve loved The X-Files for a long time, so getting the chance to write and direct the pilot has meant a great deal to me,” said Coogler. “What Chris Carter created is special, and we wanted to honor everything that made the original series connect with so many people while also finding our own way into that world. Danielle and Himesh, along with the rest of our cast, have brought such original perspectives and performances to these characters, and watching that come together has been one of the most rewarding parts of the experience. I couldn’t have asked for better collaborators than my crew, colleagues at Proximity Media and our partners at Onyx Collective and 20th Television. I’m grateful for the trust and support they’ve given us as we take on this new chapter.” Created by Carter, The X-Files originally ran from 1993-2002 on Fox and spawned two feature films. Gillian Anderson and David Duchovny starred for most of the original run and in the two movies; Robert Patrick and Annabeth Gish starred in the latter stages of the show. Fox revived the show for two more seasons in 2016 and 2018, with Anderson and Duchovny returning to their roles as agents Dana Scully and Fox Mulder. Carter is an executive producer on the Hulu series alongside Coogler, Yale and Proximity Media’s Zinzi Coogler and Sev Ohanian. Deadwyler, Patel and Proximity’s Simone Harris are co-EPs. “We’re looking forward to continuing this journey as executive producers and especially excited to work closely with Jennifer Yale, Simone Harris, and the entire cast and crew as we bring this new chapter of The X-Files to life,” said Zinzi Coogler, Ohanian and Ryan Coogler in a statement. “It was also incredibly special to have our fellow Proximity co-founder Ludwig Göransson contribute the score for the pilot, making this a true collaboration across the Proximity family.” THR

articles.title: Kim Kardashian Endorses On-Demand Apparel Delivery With New Skims x DoorDash Partnership and Ad Spot
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Stacia Datskovska Plus Icon Stacia Datskovska View All October 13, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Daniel Sachon, Doordash, Skims If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission. It’s a tired industry trope: Missing that one essential item on set and failing to acquire it fast enough, no matter how many PAs are tapped for the task. And it turns out that Kim Kardashian is all too familiar with this pain point — so much so that she’s partnering with DoorDash to make her $5 billion apparel company, Skims , available for on-demand delivery via a platform that, in the past, strictly operated in the realm of food. As of Oct. 13 at 9 a.m. PT/12 p.m. ET, shoppers in more than 10 states can get almost-instant access to 29 Skims stores without ever stepping out of the house, as the purchases will be delivered straight to their door in as little as under an hour (delivery times may vary, according to DoorDash ). Related Stories Lifestyle 30 of the Most Fool-Proof (and Romantic) Anniversary Gifts for Him Lifestyle Nostalgia Fuels Halloween Decor Trends as Retailers Tap Into the 'Practical Magic' Aesthetic SKIP THE DELIVERY FEES WITH DASHPASS In that, Skims joins retailers like Urban Outfitters, The North Face, Gap and Anthropologie , which are already shoppable on DoorDash’s website and app under the “Retail” category, having become part of a growing trend that’s subjecting traditional retail to a kind of “quick commerce,” grocery- style treatment. Thanks to a limited-time promotion from DoorDash and Skims, users can also save 15 percent on Skims orders of $125 or more (up to $25 off) with promo code SKIMS15 at checkout. ”[The partnership] was inspired by conversations I had with my friends and family members, who think that I am Skims customer service. They call me all the time asking for a bodysuit , underwear or bra , and they need it now . They assume that I have a warehouse on speed dial,” Kardashian tells The Hollywood Reporter . “Out of my frustration, I thought, ‘How easy would it be if we were just connected to an app that, in a few taps, could get you the product, typically within an hour?'” View this post on Instagram The solution manifested quicker than expected: “Well, that’s DoorDash, actually,” Kardashian continues. “[I realized] this would be such a genius idea, so we made it happen. Now, if someone is demanding something from me, I just say, ‘Go to DoorDash. Leave me alone.'” DoorDash is Skims’ first-ever on-demand delivery partner, effectively revolutionizing the way devotees of the brand are able to get their hands on nonnegotiable, everyday staples (think Seamless Sculpt Brief Bodysuit ) and internet-viral, seasonal drops, like the label’s knitwear-forward Alpine Collection release . shop skims’ new alpine collection Eleventh-hour fashion emergencies happen — from not packing that one pair of compression shorts to realizing you have nothing to wear on the third date, despite an overflowing closet — and Skims is, famously, a problem solver by nature. “ My friends are all going to a wedding this weekend, and one of them was like, ‘Oh my gosh, I totally forgot to pack [a certain Skims piece] and I can’t get to the store in time.’ DoorDash is the most convenient thing for that,” Kardashian shares. The 45-year-old reveals another complication she has experienced in her professional life that could’ve easily been avoided with the Skims x DoorDash linkup : “ I was in a fitting, and there was a dress that was really tight, to the point of it flattening my chest. I needed a fuller bra that had padding in it to expand the dress, but I didn’t have it with me because I wasn’t at my house.” Daniel Sachon Besides bras, Skims’ core shapewear line is also something she envisions selling with success on DoorDash. shop skims’ shapewear “I wear shapewear under my dresses so that they’re not sheer. If you have a dress and you find out, right before going out, that it’s maybe a little bit more sheer than you imagined, this could be the quickest fix,” Kardashian offers. Customers can shop over 23,000 SKUs across Skims’ portfolio through DoorDash, and buying them there proves as simple and intuitive as ordering Chef Kim’s Magic Mineral Broth from Goop Kitchen when you’re sick. Skims’ unexpected landing at DoorDash was announced through a campaign directed by Daniel Sachon, produced by branded content studio OBB Bolded and shot at OBB Studios in Hollywood. In the ad spot, Kardashian can be seen urgently shopping for Skims push-up bras , nipple bras and other pieces on the DoorDash app: spotting elements of her look that need to be tweaked amidst an already high-stress photoshoot. She’s in pursuit of the perfect shot, after all, and, after a few deliveries, she nails it. “DoorDash was built on one idea: You should be able to get everything you need in your neighborhood, right now. And increasingly, that’s not just dinner, it’s what you’re wearing to dinner too,” Shanna Prevé, chief revenue officer at DoorDash, says in a press release. Whether it’s a sculpting savior that you plan on layering under your favorite denim or the Signature Swim Cut Out One Piece that’s going to save the day when none of your swimsuits fit the vibe for the bachelorette weekend (and airport check-in is in three hours), stocking up on Skims has never been more effortless. Forget what the psychologists told you: Instant gratification is highly encouraged. Kim Kardashian’s Skims Shopping List for Fall NikeSkims Matte V-Line 26″ Legging $118 at skims “ It’s cooler in the mornings here now, so I’ve been wearing our NikeSkims Matte Leggings ,” Kardashian tells THR . “I put one of our Skims sweats in a bigger size on top, and I roll [the waistband] down so that you can see the leggings a bit.” Skims Cotton Fleece Straight Leg Pant $88 at skims “ I drop off the kids, and when I go to work out, I just take the sweats off,” she adds. “I don’t want to be in a full workout outfit at their school, and the double-layering really does look cute with the leggings.” Skims Cotton Fleece Logo Classic Hoodie $108 at skims Other constants in Kardashian’s daily Skims equation? “ A NikeSkims sports bra and one of our hoodies on top.” NikeSkims Fanny Pack $50 at skims When she’s ”doing the morning madness, getting the kids out the door, and taking each one to their class,” Kardashian also turns to NikeSkims’ Fanny Pack and Harness Waistpack for staying organized and keeping track of all her must-haves. THR

articles.title: ‘14th’ Leads Critics Choice Documentary Awards Nominations
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All October 13, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ava DuVernay with sitting Librarian of Congress Carla Hayden while making '14th.' Paul Garnes/Netflix Just days after making its world premiere at the New York Film Festival, Ava DuVernay’s 14th has landed the most nominations at the 2026 Critics Choice Documentary Awards . The Netflix film about the significance of and ongoing challenges to the 14th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution is nominated for best documentary feature, best director (DuVernay), best editing (Spencer Averick), best score (Jason Moran), best political documentary and best historical documentary. A number of documentaries landed the second-most nominations this year, with five nods apiece. The buzzy Elizabeth Holmes doc You Can See Everything , directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, is up for five awards, as are Once Upon a Time in Harlem and Nuisance Bear . Related Stories Movies Why 'Social Reckoning' Went Silent as More Tech Movies Face Box Office Test Movies Gaza Doc 'NAZA' Surpasses $500K Without Distributor After Sparking Protests Four-time nominees are Everybody to Kenmure Street, Remake , John Wilson’s The History of Concrete , Everest: The Other Side , EPIC: Elvis Presley in Concert , Lion and Rehearsals for a Revolution . Alex Gibney’s four-hour Elon Musk examination , Musk , and controversial Israel-Gaza war doc, NAZA , each landed three nods. The best documentary feature nominees are 14th, Everest: The Other Side, Everybody to Kenmure Street, The History of Concrete, Musk , NAZA , Once Upon a Time in Harlem, Rehearsals for a Revolution, Remake and You Can See Everything . “This year’s nominees reflect the range of voices, perspectives and stories that make documentary filmmaking so compelling,” The Critics Choice Association’s vp, documentary, Christopher Campbell, said in a statement. “These films challenge us to see the world in new ways and reinforce the vital role documentaries play in informing, engaging and inspiring audiences. We are proud to recognize the exceptional talent and creativity behind this year’s nominated films.” It was previously announced that Ron Howard would receive the Critics Choice Impact Award and Jehane Noujaim will receive lifetime achievement honor the Pennebaker Award. The 11th annual Critics Choice Documentary Awards , hosted by Ross Mathews, will take place on Sunday, Nov. 8, from New York’s Edison Ballroom. A complete list of this year’s nominees follows. articles.title: Fresh Off His Memoir, Ari Emanuel Is Bringing Back His Podcast for Season Two
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 13, 2026 9:22am Add us as a Google Preferred Source (L to R) Ben Persky, Larry David, Jerry Seinfeld and Ari Emanuel at the Netflix Is A Joke Festival at Saban Theatre on May 4, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Cr. Andrew Levy/Netflix © 2026 Fresh off of his memoir Roll The Calls hitting The New York Times best seller list, WME executive chairman and TKO CEO Ari Emanuel is returning to his podcast. Emanuel and co-host Ben Persky will bring back their Rushmore podcast Oct. 20, seeing the pair team up with high-profile guests to debate the greatest people, events, and teams of all time. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell will be the guest on the season two premiere, debating the Mount Rushmore of NFL comebacks. Future episodes will include appearances from Pat McAfee (who is also a producer on the show), Shaquille O’Neal, Kevin Durant, Larry David, and Jerry Seinfeld. Season two is presented in partnership with nativ.ly and produced by Pantheon Media Group, filmed primarily in WME’s Beverly Hills headquarters. Episodes will be available on YouTube and other podcast platforms. “Everyone has their own Rushmore , and everyone thinks theirs is right,” said Emanuel. “Season Two turns up the volume with bigger debates, bigger personalities and even more people willing to tell us why we’re wrong.” “The debate is what gets us started, but the fun is in the stories and history that paint the conversation,” added Persky. “When you dig into what makes people the greatest, with the foremost experts of those fields, you get world-class perspective about the things we all obsess over.” Rushmore debuted last year , with guests that included Tom Brady, Elon Musk, Peyton Manning, Jeff Koons and Doris Kearns Goodwin, among others. “Ben and I have been on multiple vacations together, and we get into these conversations about the Mount Rushmore of all different topics,” Emanuel told THR last year of the show’s origins. “Finally, after a little bit, I said to him, we need to talk to an expert and get his point of view, because he thought my point of view was horrible and I thought his point of view was horrible.” Emanuel added, “It was just a conversation, and we picked subject matters that we were interested in at the time and that we thought we had really great people that were experts to engage with, and they did, and that’s what we wanted to do, and then it just kept on snowballing.” THR

articles.title: Fox Entertainment, Kevin Hart’s Hartbeat Sign Vertical Drama Deal
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All October 13, 2026 9:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Kevin Hart Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images Fox Entertainment and Kevin Hart ‘s Hartbeat have struck a partnership that will see Fox tap Hartbeat’s original vertical series output as a development pipeline for future film and television projects. Under the agreement, announced at MIPCOM on Tuesday, Fox Entertainment Studios will have first-look rights for vertical series released under Hartbeat’s Codeblack, Essence and Revolt labels to develop the short-form series into feature and TV projects. Fox Entertainment Global will also distribute the original vertical series worldwide after each title’s initial platform run. Related Stories Business Fox Entertainment and Hartbeat Ink Deal to Mine Microdramas for Film and TV Adaptation TV 'Queen Silvia' Ditches the Glass Slipper for Un-Cinderella Royal Romance The pipeline launches with 25 live-action titles across the thriller, drama and faith-based genres. The series will premiere on a new Codeblack-branded channel on My Drama, a vertical video platform operated by Holywater Tech , a microdramas group in which Fox acquired a strategic stake last year. According to Fox, the Codeblack, Essence and Revolt labels have a combined social following of more than 20 million for their vertical drama content. The brands will program the My Drama channel with original verticals and direct their audiences to the content. Fox said the vertical dramas will be used to test stories and characters with audiences before committing to longer formats, including feature films and full-length TV series. “This partnership gives us an opportunity to identify bold ideas in the vertical space, see what resonates in real time, and give those stories a path to grow into film and television,” said Hannah Pillemer, head of scripted at Fox Entertainment Studios. “The culture builds the audience, the audience chooses the stories, and with Fox the stories that win become film and television for the world,” said Jeff Clanagan, founder of Codeblack and president and chief distribution officer of Hartbeat. articles.title: Peacock App Launches ‘Your Bravoverse,’ Featuring a Personalized TikTok-Style Video Feed Hosted by AI-Generated Andy Cohen
articles.full_text: Oct 13, 2026 9:00am PT Peacock App Launches ‘Your Bravoverse,’ Featuring a Personalized TikTok-Style Video Feed Hosted by AI-Generated Andy Cohen By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Peacock App Launches ‘Your Bravoverse,’ Featuring a Personalized TikTok-Style Video Feed Hosted by AI-Generated Andy Cohen 28 minutes ago Hillary Clinton to Co-Host Podcast on 2026 Midterm Elections With Kara Swisher for Vox Media, Owned by James Murdoch 2 hours ago Ex-HBO Max and Legendary Execs Launch Twin Pines Entertainment, Studio Focused on Pro-Sports Movies and Series for America’s ‘Overlooked’ Heartland 2 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of NBCUniversal NBCUniversal ‘s Peacock is rolling out up a new way to try to get Bravo fanatics even more engaged in the network’s galaxy of reality programming drama and dish-worthy moments. On Tuesday, Peacock is bowing “Your Bravoverse,” a personalized stream of clips from Bravo shows, inspired by apps like TikTok, brought to you by a chatty AI avatar of Andy Cohen. NBCU announced the Your Bravoverse feature in the spring, as part of its broader road map for the Peacock app, and began testing it over the summer. Related Stories WWE Enters Microdrama Space With 'Agent of Shadows,' Drew McIntyre Takes Central Role Telly Awards Adds Microseries Competition Track, With Dozens of New Categories (EXCLUSIVE) Your Bravoverse, available now in the Peacock mobile app for all subscribers, serves up a “personalized feed of Bravo moments tailored to each fan,” including classic one-liners, meme-able moments and shocking reveals. An AI-generated avatar of Cohen, host of Bravo’s “Watch What Happens Live,” guides users through the experience with insider commentary. Popular on Variety “Bravo fans never watch just one episode,” Cohen said in a statement. “They want the backstory, the receipts and what happened three seasons later. Your Bravoverse on Peacock is built for exactly that! It’s a new way to go down every Bravo rabbit hole, rediscover iconic moments and find new ones based on what you love.” The Your Bravoverse personalized playlist of swipeable video clips is automatically built from more than 5,000 hours of Bravo footage — and, according to NBCU, there are more than 600 billion unique viewing variants. The feeds are assembled using a combination of AI technology and human editors, per NBCU. A key component: Peacock app users can tap directly from a clip into the full episode or season. That’s designed to provide a new front door for content discovery that (ideally) drives long-form viewing, all within a single experience. Your Bravoverse also promises “exclusive, never-before-seen content” from current seasons and the Bravo archive. NBCU also has an advertising play with Your Bravoverse. In addition to sponsoring custom moments and video clips in the Peacock app, NBCU says, Cohen’s avatar can audibly reference a sponsor’s brand. Wendy’s joins as the first sponsor of Your Bravoverse at launch, building on its longstanding relationship with Bravo. NBCU is positioning Your Bravoverse as the latest Peacock feature that differentiates it from other streamers. The app includes real-time vertical highlights and clips, original unscripted microdramas, multiview capabilities, mini-games and other interactive experiences. Why is Peacock leaning into Bravo? It’s a very active fandom: According to the company, in 2026, Bravo superfans watch up to 75 episodes of its shows per month, and BravoCon 2025 drew 30,000 fans in person and 3 million streaming viewers. In addition, Bravo viewers on Peacock watch 92% more non-Bravo content than the platform user average — a key stat that underscores by NBCU kept Bravo in the fold while spinning off its other cable networks like CNBC and USA into Versant Media. NBCU makes all of Bravo’s content available day-after-air on Peacock. The streaming platform also will serve as the exclusive streaming home of Bravo Fan Fest Charleston on Saturday, Oct. 24, featuring live coverage of panels, interviews and behind-the-scenes moments. articles.full_text: Oct 13, 2026 9:00am PT ’14th,’ ‘You Can See Everything’ and ‘Once Upon a Time in Harlem’ Lead Critics Choice Documentary Awards Nominations By Clayton Davis Plus Icon Clayton Davis Chief Awards Editor byClaytonDavis Latest ’14th,’ ‘You Can See Everything’ and ‘Once Upon a Time in Harlem’ Lead Critics Choice Documentary Awards Nominations 33 minutes ago Olivia Wilde Eyes Oscars History With ‘The Invite’ as the First Woman to Direct Herself to an Acting Nomination 4 days ago ‘I Play Rocky’ Star Anthony Ippolito on Sylvester Stallone’s Reaction, Drinking Raw Eggs and Why Hollywood Needs ‘More Raw, Human Stories’ 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Â© 2026 Netflix, Inc. Ava DuVernay’s timely and viscerally moving “ 14th ” leads this year’s Critics Choice Documentary Awards nominations with six, including best documentary feature. Close behind with five nominations apiece are Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s examination of Elizabeth Holmes, “ You Can See Everything ”; Gabriela Osio Vanden and Jack Weisman’s polar bear migration story, “Nuisance Bear”; David Greaves’ archival portrait of Black cultural history, “Once Upon a Time in Harlem” and Pegah Ahangarani’s Iranian historical documentary, “Rehearsals for a Revolution.” Related Stories Raindance to Launch U.K.'s First Major Vertical Festival and Market (EXCLUSIVE) Telly Awards Adds Microseries Competition Track, With Dozens of New Categories (EXCLUSIVE) Netflix led all distributors with 17 nominations, nearly double the nine earned by runner-up Neon. Popular on Variety DuVernay, Fielder and Oppenheim are among the directing nominees, alongside Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor for “NAZA,” Felipe Bustos Sierra for “Everybody to Kenmure Street,” Ross McElwee for “Remake” and Orlando von Einsiedel for “The Cycle of Love,” the only directing nominee whose film did not land a documentary feature nom. Now in its 11th year, the Critics Choice Documentary Awards will take place Nov. 8 at the Edison Ballroom in New York City, with television host and producer Ross Matthews serving as host. The awards celebrate excellence in nonfiction filmmaking. The organization’s track record of predicting Oscar success has been mixed over the years. Its inaugural top prize winner, “O.J.: Made in America” (2016), went on to win the Academy Award for documentary feature. Since then, only three other top prize winners or nominees have crossed over to the Oscars: winner “Summer of Soul (…Or, When the Revolution Could Not Be Televised)” (2021) and nominees “Will & Harper” (2024) and last year’s “The Perfect Neighbor” (2025). All others failed to be nominated, or in some cases, not even make the preliminary shortlist (i.e., 2022’s “Good Night Oppy”). As previously announced, Ron Howard will receive the Critics Choice Impact Award. Visionary filmmaker Jehane Noujaim will receive the CCA’s Pennebaker Award, presented by Chris Hegedus, Pennebaker’s widow and longtime collaborator. Named in honor of trailblazing documentarian D.A. Pennebaker, the award, formerly known as the Critics Choice Lifetime Achievement Award, recognizes filmmakers whose careers have made a profound and lasting contribution to documentary storytelling. Feature-length documentaries, two-part documentaries and short-form documentaries are eligible for nomination if they were first released commercially in the U.S. between Jan. 1 and Dec. 31, 2026.
