articles.title: Taiwan Gets Its Own Spotlight at Lumière, Led by Restored ‘Osmanthus Alley’ in Its Original Language
articles.full_text: Oct 13, 2026 9:12am PT Taiwan Gets Its Own Spotlight at Lumière, Led by Restored ‘Osmanthus Alley’ in Its Original Language By Lin Ying-Hsuan Plus Icon Lin Ying-Hsuan Latest AI-Native Studios Can Create Original IP While Traditional Studios Keep Their Edge, VFX Veteran Hong Jae Cheol Says at Busan 2 days ago ‘Squid Game’ Producer Reads Founding Declaration as Asian Independent Producers Form Cross-Border Alliance at Busan 2 days ago Taiwan’s Sole Busan Competition Title ‘To Be Ordinary’ Marks Lee Yun Chan’s Return to Features After Two Decades 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Image Courtesy of NFAI Taiwan is getting a dedicated national focus at the International Classic Film Market ( MIFC ), the industry arm of Lyon’s Lumière Festival, the first for a non-European country, according to the Taiwan Film and Audiovisual Institute (TFAI). A new 4K restoration of Chen Kun-hou’s “ Osmanthus Alley ” leads the Taiwan in Focus program, which runs alongside this year’s guest country, Greece. Related Stories Raindance to Launch U.K.'s First Major Vertical Festival and Market (EXCLUSIVE) WWE Enters Microdrama Space With 'Agent of Shadows,' Drew McIntyre Takes Central Role TFAI is using the showcase to seek international distribution and programming partners for the island’s restored classics. “Osmanthus Alley” made its world premiere at the festival on Oct. 12, with Chen and star Lu Hsiao-fen in attendance. TFAI says distributors it has previously worked with have expressed interest, with release terms and timing still under negotiation. Adapted from Hsiao Li-hung’s novel, the film follows Thik-hông (Lu), an orphan who marries into a wealthy family, is widowed young and sees her son sent away to Japan, leaving her isolated behind the walls of the family estate. Simon Yam and Tuo Tsung-hua appear in guest roles. Lu won best actress at the 1987 Asia Pacific Film Festival, and the theme song, with lyrics by Wu Nien-jen, took the Golden Horse for best original film song. Popular on Variety The restoration also brings back the film’s original Taiwanese soundtrack. Chen insisted on shooting in Taiwanese, but state-run Central Motion Picture Corporation (CMPC) chose to release the film in Mandarin, in line with the government’s policy of promoting the language at the time. Chen eventually persuaded the studio to produce a Taiwanese version, but it played in only a limited number of theaters and gradually faded from view. Its selection coincides with the 70th anniversary of Taiwanese-language cinema, which TFAI traces to 1956’s “Xue Pinggui yu Wang Baochuan.” An estimated 1,200 Taiwanese-language films were made between the 1960s and 1981, but only about 200 survive in TFAI’s collection. The restoration also anticipates TFAI’s 2027 focus on literary adaptations, while Chen’s lifetime achievement award at the 2023 Golden Horse Awards prompted renewed interest in his work. Chen began as a cinematographer, winning a Golden Horse for “He Never Gives Up” (1978), and from 1979 worked closely with Hou Hsiao-hsien, the pair often trading roles behind the camera. Chen’s “Growing Up” won him the Golden Horse for best director in 1983. TFAI restored “Osmanthus Alley” from its original 35mm negative, filling missing frames from an interpositive, with audio drawn from the 35mm Taiwanese sound negative. The source was generally in good condition, but mold spots and dense clusters of small white specks required careful treatment. Aggressive cleaning settings risked erasing image detail, so technicians used masks and adjusted processing settings before completing frame-by-frame manual repairs. In line with FIAF’s code of ethics, Chen was repeatedly consulted. An intermediate version had more saturated, vibrant colors, but discussions with the director led to a more subdued final grade, closer to the original photography. Tu Duu-chih, who handled the film’s original sound mix, returned to help restore the Taiwanese soundtrack from six primary audio reels. The team synchronized the material, repaired damaged sections and reduced noise through multiple passes using light processing settings. The soundtrack holds another connection to Taiwanese cinema history. Cast members who did not speak Taiwanese were dubbed in post-production: co-star Lin Hsiu-ling voiced Lu’s dialogue, while Hou provided the voice for Tuo. TFAI, which holds about 20,000 film titles, restores 10 to 12 films a year and has restored more than 100 since 2013. Physical deterioration prompts climate control and emergency digitization, but a full restoration depends on whether a film has “a clear purpose and an audience ready to experience it right now,” the institute says. Recent restorations include Tsai Ming-liang’s “Vive L’Amour,” which screened in Venice Classics in 2025, and “The Dull Ice Flower,” chosen by Taiwanese audiences in a public poll and selected for Cannes Classics this year. Taiwanese-language titles “Love Never Ceases” and “Zhang Di Seeks A-Zu” were restored for the anniversary. Overseas, TFAI prioritizes in-person screenings to introduce lesser-known titles before pursuing distribution and streaming partnerships. “We want audiences to discover Taiwan cinema beyond Taiwan New Cinema and see the many different facets of Taiwan,” TFAI tells Variety . TFAI will also pitch its ongoing restoration of Yao Feng-pan’s “All in the Dim Cold Night” (1974) at MIFC’s Re>birth program on Oct. 15, seeking distributors and festival slots for the horror film. Often called Taiwan’s “King of Horror,” Yao built the film’s eerie atmosphere without modern visual effects, relying on practical techniques such as low-angle green lighting and burning straw on location. Taiwan in Focus also includes a round table with TFAI chair Arthur Chu and programmer Howard Yang, a networking event and an exhibition of original Taiwanese film posters. The institute hopes to build longer-term programming partnerships with international archives, giving restored Taiwanese films a life beyond their festival premieres. The special edition is being released in celebration of this year’s 70th anniversary of the French New Wave, the upcoming 70th anniversary of the film in 2028 and, in the same year, the centenary of Moreau’s birth. Released 1958, “Elevator to the Gallows” marked the directorial debut for the young Malle, who was 25 years old at the time. Related Stories Open to AI: Hollywood Is Embracing Artificial Intelligence Tools Despite Doomsday Fears Set in Paris over the course of a night, the film stars Moreau and Maurice Ronet as lovers who set out to murder her husband and his boss (played by Jean Wall), only for the plan to go awry. Distinguished by Miles Davis’ award-winning jazz score, the film established both Malle and Moreau as verifiable talents. Popular on Variety Betty Blue Courtesy of Gaumont Another Gaumont classic, “Betty Blue,” Jean-Jacques Beineix’s iconic tale of amour fou run rampant, is making its long-awaited return to the big screen at this year’s Lumière Film Festival . Originally released in 1986 as “37°2 le matin,” the award-winning erotic drama chronicles the doomed romance between Zorg (Jean-Hugues Anglade), a handyman and aspiring writer in his 30s, and the volatile, impulsive and fragile 19-year-old Betty (Béatrice Dalle). The film is also one of this year’s highlights for Gaumont, which is presenting the new 4K master of the full 185-minute version — “a film that has been invisible in theaters in this version since 1991,” noted Jérôme Soulet, head of catalogue at Gaumont. The 4K restoration of “Betty Blue” was carried out by Gaumont at the GP Archives laboratory. articles.full_text: Oct 13, 2026 9:17am PT Lucian Piane, ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race’ Music Producer, Dies at 46 By Jazz Tangcay Plus Icon Jazz Tangcay Artisans Editor @jazzt Latest How ‘Ink’ Production Designers Recreated The Sun Newsroom Using Functional Linotype Machines, Working Rotary Phones and Old Typewriters 20 hours ago Universal Launches Fourth Film Composers Initiative 24 hours ago Ava DuVernay on Her Latest Doc ’14th’: ‘We’re in the Midst of Something Very Sinister, Something Very Dangerous’ 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images for MTV Lucian Piane , a music producer on “RuPaul’s Drag Race” has died. He was 46. According to Los Angeles County Medical Examiner records, Piane died on Monday after reportedly being struck by a car in Glendale, Calif. Piane worked on the main “Drag Race” show from Seasons 1-8 and composed the music and the Rusical numbers during that time. He also worked on “Drag Race: All Stars.” In addition, Piane also collaborated with RuPaul and wrote some of the host’s biggest songs including “Cover Girl,” “Sissy That Walk,” “Jealous of My Boogie,” “Born Naked,” “Champion” and “Main Event.” Related Stories Open to AI: Hollywood Is Embracing Artificial Intelligence Tools Despite Doomsday Fears He also earned a Grammy nomination for his work on the soundtrack to the 2007 “Hairspray” film. Popular on Variety Before his death, Piane battled with substance abuse and mental health issues. Fans and friends had been voicing concern for Piane online after he posted a series of alarming videos on Instagram . Many were asking him to “get sober and stay sober” and writing “This is so sad to see. Lucian please seek help.” Journalist Larry Flick wrote a tribute to Piane, writing, “Lucian was my friend. It wasn’t always easy. He was troubled, complicated, and filled with rage that he didn’t know how to manage. Like many, I tried to help until he made it impossible. Guilt right now is real. The way he left this life was tragic and brutal. But I pray rest and peace await him on the other side.” Piane was born on Oct. 4 in Kansas City, Mo. Variety has reached out to representatives at “RuPaul’s Drag Race” for comment. articles.title: From Haunted Morgues to Horror Movie Cabins, Airbnb’s Spookiest Stays Are Drawing Gen Z Travelers This Halloween
articles.full_text: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission. Halloween is falling on a Saturday this year, and Gen Z is apparently looking to make a weekend of it. According to new data from Airbnb , searches for Halloween weekend stays have jumped nearly 45% among Gen Z travelers compared to last year, as younger vacationers look for more elaborate — and occasionally haunted — getaways. Overall searches for the Oct. 30-Nov. 1 weekend are up nearly 15% year-over-year, while wishlists with Halloween-inspired titles have increased almost 60%. Salem, Mass., perhaps unsurprisingly, ranks as the most popular trending U.S. destination for the holiday. Related Stories ‘Sin Filtro’ Producer JK Media Producing First Original Microdramas Shot in the U.S. for TelevisaUnivision’s ViXMicrO (EXCLUSIVE) Telly Awards Adds Microseries Competition Track, With Dozens of New Categories (EXCLUSIVE) To capitalize on the interest, Airbnb has rounded up 31 properties designed for different Halloween sensibilities, from cozy New England retreats that could double as the setting of “Gilmore Girls” to secluded horror-themed cabins and historic homes with reported paranormal activity. Some lean into the season with elaborate movie-inspired sets and interactive mysteries; others have histories that are unsettling enough on their own. Among the more unusual options is a former Missouri morgue equipped with ghost-hunting gear, a Nevada mining cabin previously featured on a paranormal reality series and a Big Bear retreat that borrows a particularly memorable bathroom scene from a horror classic. Here are seven stays worth considering for a Halloween weekend away — or a spooky getaway any time of year. BIG BEAR LAKE, CALIFORNIA Horror-Themed Cabin! Retro & Scary Movie Inspired For horror fans who would rather spend Halloween inside a scary movie than watching one, this Big Bear cabin goes all in on the genre. The retro-inspired rental features an elaborate bathroom modeled after a famous horror movie scene, complete with an axe lodged in the door. Ghostly special effects and an interactive escape-room mystery add to the atmosphere, making this one of the more theatrical options on Airbnb’s list. It’s an especially fitting getaway for fans planning a marathon of classic slasher films. BOOK Now OZARK, MISSOURI Historic Morgue and Paranormal Investigation! This Missouri property doesn’t have to manufacture much of its Halloween atmosphere. The building previously served as a morgue, funeral home, church and museum, and its current owners have leaned into that unusual history with mortuary-inspired decor. Guests staying in the loft can also try their hand at paranormal investigation with an included spirit box, electromagnetic field detector and dowsing rods. Whether any ghosts actually turn up is another question, but it’s a considerably more immersive alternative to watching an episode of “Ghost Hunters.” BOOK Now PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA The Hewitt For travelers whose Halloween tastes skew more gothic mystery than slasher film, Philadelphia’s Hewitt offers a suitably dramatic setting. Occupying the 2,500-square-foot third floor of an 1886 Queen Anne Victorian mansion in historic Germantown, the rental comes with period architecture and a hidden east wing accessible through a bookcase door. The setting lends itself to a weekend of murder mysteries, candlelit dinners and Victorian-era intrigue — without any actual haunting required. BOOK Now GREAT BARRINGTON, MASSACHUSETTS Berkshires Black Abbey A former church built in 1862 has been transformed into one of the more unusual group getaways in the Berkshires. The 4,000-square-foot property underwent a four-year conversion while retaining its original stained-glass windows and much of its ecclesiastical character. Modern additions include a cedar sauna and a game loft with a speakeasy-style bar. It’s an appealing option for groups looking to combine a foliage-filled New England weekend with something a little more gothic. BOOK Now BEATTY, NEVADA Haunted Mining Cabin Located roughly eight miles from the entrance to Death Valley National Park, this remodeled miner’s cabin dates back to the early 1900s and comes with a supernatural reputation. The property was previously featured on a paranormal reality series, though its reported haunting remains a matter of local lore rather than established fact. Its remote desert setting and mining history should appeal to travelers looking for something closer to a real-life ghost story than a conventional vacation rental. BOOK Now EAGLE HARBOR TOWNSHIP, MICHIGAN Anam Cara Cabin Not every Halloween getaway requires a ghost. Tucked away at the end of a winding gravel road in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula, Anam Cara Cabin is constructed from stone, timber and bark, with handmade lighting, a wood-burning fireplace and half a mile of shoreline. The remote lakeside property is especially suited to travelers interested in the quieter side of spooky season: dark skies, dense woods and the kind of solitude that would make a horror movie protagonist nervous. BOOK Now EXETER, NEW HAMPSHIRE The Word Barn For those who prefer the cozy side of fall, The Word Barn offers a more low-key New England escape. Located in a renovated farm barn in Exeter, New Hampshire, the apartment sits beside a literary and live-music venue in the countryside. Rather than haunted corridors or staged scares, the appeal here is autumn scenery and a weekend organized around books and performances. Think more “Gilmore Girls” than “The Conjuring.” BOOK Now Loading comments...

While the film already won two awards after its world premiere at this year’s Angoulême Film Festival, it will begin its international tour with the Cairo Intl. Film Festival in November. Popular on Variety The plot delves into Charlie and Hicham’s love story and desire to start a family, as they navigate through the struggle of infertility and assisted reproductive treatment. Over the course of three years, through hope and heartbreak, they will put their love and their bodies to the test. The cast is led by César award-winning actress Nina Meurisse (“Souleymane’s Story,” 2024; “The Rapture,” 2023) as Charlie, Sofian Khammes (“My Brothers and I,” 2021; “The Big Hit,” 2019) as Hicham, and Jeanne Balibar, who won the Cesar for best actress in 2018 for “Barbara.” Connection and relationships are recurring themes in Cherti’s work, whether he chooses to relate complicated family bonds (“Wherever Comes the Pain From,” 2013 – selected at Locarno and awarded at Clermont-Ferrand) or the deepness of love in the face of life challenges (“Je, d’un accident ou d’amour,” 2025 – selected at Tribeca and Clermont-Ferrand; “T’embrasser sur le miel,” 2021). For his first feature film, the director says he wanted to capture one of the most important relationships in a person’s life, as in his opinion, simply being a couple is “an odyssey.” Cherti added: “I made this film because there is something quietly moving about two people trying, together, through years of hardship, to reinvent themselves.” Paul Jullien, head of sales at Salaud Morisset, said: “With ‘Our Way to You,’ Khalil Cherti explores the universal themes of parenthood, love and family with remarkable depth and sensitivity, turning an intimate story into something that resonates with us all.” Amaury Ovise, producer, said the film “sensitively captures the joy and pain of a couple navigating the challenges of assisted reproduction. articles.full_text: Oct 13, 2026 9:30am PT Kevin Hart’s Hartbeat Inks Vertical Series Deal With Fox Entertainment By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest J.K. Rowling Docuseries Set at BBC 6 hours ago Appetite for Agatha Christie Shows No Signs of Slowing 50 Years After Her Death: ‘She Has Such Enduring Appeal’ 18 hours ago The Muppets Turn 50 This Year but They Nearly Didn’t Get Made at All: ‘It Was a Real Study in Perseverance’ 19 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images for Netflix Kevin Hart ’s production company Hartbeat has inked a vertical series deal with Fox Entertainment . The deal will see Fox Entertainment Studios have first look rights to developing feature film and television series from vertical series released under Hartbeat subsidiary brands Codeblack, Essence and Revolt, which have a combined social following exceeding 20 million. Codeblack has partnered with Fox partner Holywater Tech, which runs vertical video platform My Drama, to have its own first dedicated branded channel. Hartbeat’s vertical series will launch on the platform first with Fox Entertainment Global subsequently distributing worldwide after their initial runs. Related Stories Telly Awards Adds Microseries Competition Track, With Dozens of New Categories (EXCLUSIVE) WWE Enters Microdrama Space With 'Agent of Shadows,' Drew McIntyre Takes Central Role There are already 25 live-action titles in the works, spanning a range of genres from dramas and thrillers to faith-based content, designed as “the first stage of intellectual property development,” according to the press release. The plan is for stories that connect with audiences to advance into development for film and television, with Fox Entertainment Studios holding the first look. Popular on Variety “Hartbeat has a powerful creative voice and an exceptional instinct for stories that connect with audiences,” said Hannah Pillemer, Fox Entertainment Studios’ head of scripted. “This partnership gives us an opportunity to identify bold ideas in the vertical space, see what resonates in real time, and give those stories a path to grow into film and television. This strategic, audience-driven approach to developing IP fits naturally with how we’re growing Fox Entertainment Studios.” “My vision has always been to bring the biggest cultural brands serving our audience together in one destination, and the partnership with Essence and Revolt makes that real,” said Jeff Clanagan, founder of Codeblack and President and Chief Distribution Officer of Hartbeat. “Codeblack, Essence and Revolt have spent decades earning this audience’s trust. Now that audience has one home for stories made for them, in the format where they already spend their time. Holywater Tech brings the technology and platform expertise to deliver that experience the way this audience expects it. Vertical is where those stories start, not where they stop. The culture builds the audience, the audience chooses the stories, and with Fox the stories that win become film and television for the world.” Last year Hartbeat inked a first-look deal with Fox Corp.-owned Tubi for four creator-driven films including “Sundown,” a supernatural feature written, directed and starring Kinigra Deon. The Bay Theatre in Pacific Palisades, which was formerly operated by Netflix and before that by Cinepolis, will be taken over by Paramount Pictures with San Diego’s The Lot handling operations. The opening is planned for later this year. The Bay Theatre has been closed since the wildfires damaged much of the upscale Los Angeles community in January 2025. The five-screen multiplex is located in Rick Caruso’s Palisades Village shopping area, which reopened in August after extensive remediation and repairs due to the fires. The theater’s vintage-looking sign is a nod to the community’s historic Bay Theatre, which stood nearby on Sunset Boulevard until closing in 1978. We’re inspired by the resilience of Pacific Palisades residents, and we’re honored to help support this community’s comeback.” Caruso said, “Paramount is one of the world’s leading entertainment studios, with an extraordinary legacy of cinematic storytelling and, importantly, a deep commitment to the City of Los Angeles and to the future of the theatrical experience. I’m not into it right now.” Seyfried, who has in the past done racy projects like Jennifer’s Body and Lovelace , says she’s in a different place in her life. “I have kids now who are paying attention to what I do,” she told interviewer Alec Baldwin during the conversation. articles.title: Ben Affleck Says ‘Justice League’ Was A “Low Point” In His Career
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Ego Nwodim Reacts To Shane Gillis’ Controversial ‘SNL’ Joke: “Whore Reporting For Duty” Robert Pattinson Shares Update On ‘The Batman Part II’: “We Are Going To Figure It All Out” ‘Coven Academy’s Devon Sawa Struggled With Being Recognized For ‘Casper’ Years After Starring In Role: “I Gotta Embrace It” View All October 12, 2026 4:11pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ben Affleck filming 'Justice League' Clay Enos / Warner Bros. Pictures Ben Affleck is getting real about the “low point” of his career, pinpointing it to the time he was filming Justice League . In a new interview, the actor opened up about the reshoots and how Warner Bros . handled the whole situation. “The truth is, the experience of Justice League was so, so negative for lots of different reasons,” Affleck said on the Happy Sad Confused podcast. “Some of which having to do with where I was personally, some of which having to do with the tragedy that happened during the time, and also the fact that I really saw how not to make a movie like that when the studio is at odds with the filmmaker. You’re really making a mistake. That was what really doomed that.” Related Stories Reviews 'Animals' Review: Ben Affleck And Kerry Washington Fight A Lot In Netflix Kidnap Thriller That Is Stretched Too Thin Politics Ben Affleck Campaigned For Mayor In L.A. As 'Animals' Character: "Do Not Vote For Me!" After Batman v Superman disappointed at the box office, the studio felt pressure to make Zack Snyder’s Justice League lighter and more appealing to audiences. During post-production, Snyder experienced a family tragedy, and Warner Bros. hired Joss Whedon to oversee reshoots, which drastically shifted the film’s storyline and tone. Watch on Deadline “Boy, that was shitty,” he said. “Him being taken off that movie, and the reshoots that we did–if you want the low point of my career, [it] was that.” Affleck noted that “Somebody’s death by suicide, that eclipses everything. And the way that was, I thought, frankly, used as an excuse… I just thought that was one of the shittiest things I’ve ever seen. It was so gross. And then the whole environment and vibe, much of which I wasn’t privy to, but that I sort of heard about secondhand in terms of Ray [Fisher] and Gal [Gadot] and other people’s experiences. It was just like ‘Wow, this is about as gross as it gets.'” Watch Affleck’s full interview in the video below. articles.title: ‘Half’ Review: Hip-Hop Beats & Brutal Beatings In Samjad’s Fast, Fun, Super-Violent Indian Vampire Horror Movie – Sitges Film Festival
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Damon Wise Damon Wise Film Editor, Awards yo_damo More Stories By Damon ‘Half’ Review: Hip-Hop Beats & Brutal Beatings In Samjad’s Fast, Fun, Super-Violent Indian Vampire Horror Movie – Sitges Film Festival Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo On Directing Rwanda’s Oscar Submission ‘Ben’Imana’: “We Need To Understand What Happened” – Contenders London ‘Wildwood’ Director Travis Knight On Laika’s Stop-Motion Fantasy Epic: “It Took Us 16 Years To Make This Movie” – Contenders London View All October 12, 2026 4:32pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Half’ TIFF Two halves make a satisfying whole in this lean, mean action-horror, in which twin vampires stalk a scorching-hot Madras Max: Fury Road dystopia in the none-too-distant future. The 1996 Robert Rodriguez/Quentin Tarantino collaboration From Dusk Till Dawn springs immediately to mind, but, compared to that, director Samjad sinks his teeth into the meat of his movie in next to no time. Scored with an urgent techno-bhangra beat by Midhun Mukundan, the result is a violent revenge thriller that has been lapped up on the genre circuit since it premiered in the Midnight Madness strand at TIFF this year. Related Stories News Top 50 Halloween Movies Photo Gallery: Creepy Classics From ‘Psycho,’ ‘The Shining’ To ‘Obsession’ & ‘Get Out’ News Horror Movies’ Next Wave: What’s Coming In 2026, From Auteur Nightmares To Indie Breakouts The film starts with the minimum of backstory, which is at odds not only with the norms of Indian cinema but also the press book, which suggests that a whole lot of exposition about the genesis of the story’s two siblings has been cut. This might be for the better; our introduction to Ethan and Ivy (Ranjith Sajeev and Aiswarya Raj) is brief but suitably ominous. “Born of mortal dust and vampire blood, the twins walk in darkness,” a title card tells us, before we’re shown a brief flashback to their seemingly idyllic childhood where the two fight like cat and dog (“Raising you two will be the end of me,” says their mother). Cut to the present, where the two are taking a road trip to the much busier Mumbai district of Pai Nagar in shades that not only protect them from the sun but, conveniently, make them also look very, very cool. As they make their way, we cut to a family of four making the same trip across the desert, passing Babu’s Puncture Shop, whose owner makes a phone call. Soon the family is being tailed by a couple on a scooter, carrying what appears to be a baby and yelling, “Sir! Sir! Oil leak!” The father pulls over, and the car is immediately swarmed over by bandits, who brutally kill him — plus his wife and two kids — with no mercy. Watch on Deadline The aftermath of the crime is cleaned up with ruthless efficiency, the gang hauling off the car, stripping it for parts and burning the bodies of the victims, a process that threatens to rinse and repeat when Ethan and Ivy follow almost immediately in the same slipway. The murder of the family is graphic enough, but what happens to Ethan and Ivy is far more perverse, especially when Ivy’s apparently dead body is defiled by one of the feral desert gang members. Samjad keeps the twins’ superpowers under wraps for an agonizingly long time, until the sun goes down and their bodies are able to regenerate. The wait is worth it; when Ethan and Ivy finally take their revenge on this criminal outfit — one by one, piece by piece — it’s with a satisfying sense of bone-cracking justice, orchestrated like S. S. Rajamouli’s 2022 breakout hit RRR at 200mph. The genius of Samjad’s conceit, however, is that, for all their superhuman abilities, the twins are vulnerable — not only is sunlight their only weakness, Ivy also is deaf and non-verbal, which adds a real sense of threat towards the end, when things look very bleak indeed. Part of this is down to Samjad’s fantastic sense of world-building; like Peter Weir’s 1974 black comedy The Cars That Ate Paris , Half is a sardonic comment on the sleazy eco-system of crime: Babu’s Puncture Shop is just one layer in a pyramid that goes surprisingly high and eclipses even the bumbling, paid-off police force, which willfully sees no evil and nervously treats each investigation as “extra paperwork.” There’s also a twitchy paranoia at play, since Ethan and Ivy, as outsiders, inevitably spark a turf war as various warring factions try to figure out who is killing their men. There aren’t too many directors that can sustain this level of inventive carnage — even Takashi Miike has yet to show a man choking to death on the stump of his own severed hand — but Samjad directs the action with clarity and skill, helped immeasurably by Very Tri Yulisman’s incredible fight choreography. A puzzling coda means the film ends later than it probably should, but Samjad already has established his impressive cult bona fides: If you only see one gory Malayalam neo-noir spaghetti western vampire beat-’em-up in your life, make it this one. articles.title: Antitrust Experts Doubt Donald Trump’s DOJ Has A Case In Going After Networks For Suspending White House TV Pool
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted New White House Press Secretary Debuts With A Very Short Briefing, Some Breaking News And Lots Of Praise For Donald Trump ABC Tells Judge That FCC Showed “Retaliatory Motive” By Ordering Early License Review Despite “Less Intrusive” Options Judge Orders Trump Administration To Stop Running Taxpayer Funded Ads That Promote POTUS View All October 12, 2026 5:20pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source The U.S. Department of Justice building in Washington, D.C. Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images News that the Justice Department is investigating five major networks for suspending the White House TV pool last month was met with outcry that it was another example of Trump administration retaliation against the media . Alarming as it may be to First Amendment groups, among antitrust experts, there are doubts that the DOJ would have much of a case. Related Stories News White House Video Coverage Returns As Networks Resume TV Pool; CNN Says It’s Being Allowed Back In After Judge Sidelines Trump Ban News CNN, MS NOW And Politico Sue Donald Trump Over His White House Ban Section 1 of the Sherman Antitrust Act restricts competitors that restrain competition. In this case, the five networks that make up the TV pool — CNN , Fox News , ABC News , CBS News and NBC News — last month withheld their participation to protest the White House’s exclusion of CNN . For about four days, that meant fewer video images and other coverage of Trump that week, including the ceremonies surrounding the visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping. William Kovacic, global competition professor of law and policy at George Washington University, said, “I think you have to take any lawsuit from the Department of Justice seriously.” Watch on Deadline But he said an antitrust claim against the networks likely would have a “very remote prospect of success.” At issue is “what is the predominant character of the behavior: Is it a commercial interest or is it designed to achieve some form of First Amendment expression?” “To me, if there is a commercial aim to this, it is well hidden,” said Kovacic, a former chairman of the Federal Trade Commission. Diana Moss, vice president and director of competition policy at the Progressive Policy Institute, said via email, “Group boycotts are illegal when they stifle competition, such as forcing a competitor(s) out of the market.” She added, “Presumably, the arrangement among the five networks is designed to increase coordination and efficiency in the distribution of news footage. There is no anti-competitive intent or effect. The networks were responding in solidarity to repression of a free press (1st Amendment).” Court Precedence The lines between commercial conduct and protected First Amendment activity can be blurred, but courts have sided with boycotting parties even then. Sam Weinstein, professor at Cardozo School of Law and former attorney in the DOJ’s Antitrust Division, said that “typically a non commercial boycott is protected by the First Amendment.” “It would seem to be a non starter,” he said. He cited the Supreme Court’s 1982 decision in NAACP vs. Claiborne Hardware Co., involving an organized 1960s-era boycott of white-owned businesses in Mississippi. The justices held that the state could not hold the protesters liable for damages when they engage in lawful activity protected by the First Amendment. Weinstein also referred to another Supreme Court case, FTC vs. Superior Court Trial Lawyers, when the justices ruled that a boycott by court-appointed lawyers for indigent defendants violated antitrust law, as its purpose was to to gain increased compensation. The majority compared it to horizontal price fixing. The latter case, Weinstein said, is different from what happened with the TV pool. Prices and compensation were not at issue. It’s still unclear whether the networks will comply with the DOJ investigative request, but the networks already made it clear that they were jointly suspending participation in the pool, releasing a statement that “no administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.” “The real question is a question of law, not a question of fact,” Weinstein said. In a statement, a spokesperson for the DOJ said over the weekend, “Members of the television press pool have boycotted covering White House events. Group boycotts among commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act. The Antitrust Division is simply investigating to determine whether these news organizations have violated the antitrust laws.” “An End Run Around” Democrats already have accused the Trump administration of politicizing the Antitrust Division, violating the norms that have separated the White House from the DOJ since the Nixon era. The investigation of the networks is likely to add another example to their arguments. Bob Corn-Revere, chief counsel for the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression, said via email, “Threatening an antitrust investigation is just another example of this Administration misusing regulatory authority to punish the media for doing something the President dislikes. Political boycotts are part of a longstanding American tradition and are protected under First Amendment law.” He added, “Whether the government’s excuses are dressed up as ‘national security’ or antitrust law, this is another attempt by the Administration trying to make an end run around the First Amendment to control news coverage.” White House Press Secretary’s Debut: Very Short, Some News, Much Trump Praise The YouTube Age: Content Creators Making Waves In Europe Toon Comedy ‘Merrick & Treves’ From ‘Archer’ Team Lands Two-Season HBO Order Cranston & Other ‘Breaking Bad’ Alums Mourn Actor Who Played Walt Jr. Read More About: 2 Comments

articles.title: ‘High Potential’ Gets Post-Super Bowl Slot, Eyes ‘Grey’s Anatomy’-Style 2-Parter On ABC & Disney+
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Steve Stark’s Toluca Pictures Extends MGM TV Overall Deal, Expands Amazon MGM Studios First-Look Pact & Taps Max Kisbye As President ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ EP On How Harry Shum Jr. Juggles Medical Drama & ‘Dancing With The Stars’ & If It Affects His Presence On ABC Show ‘High Potential’ Gets Post-Super Bowl Slot, Eyes ‘Grey’s Anatomy’-Style 2-Parter On ABC & Disney+ View All October 12, 2026 5:30pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source ABC ‘s last time carrying the Super Bowl in February 2006 was a memorable one, with then-hot sophomore drama Grey’s Anatomy delivering one of the most talked about lead-out programs in the history of the Big Game, Part 1 of a bomb-themed two-episode arc that drew 38.1 million viewers. Twenty years later, ABC is picking up where it left off, slotting its flagship series that is also early in its run, High Potential , immediately following Super Bowl LXI on ABC and Disney+ on Sunday, Feb. 14, 2027. Like Grey’s Anatomy , I hear High Potential is planning a two-parter, with the special post-Super Bowl episode as Part 1, ending on a cliffhanger that will be resolved in Part 2 airing in the show’s regular time slot the following Tuesday. Related Stories News ABC Tells Judge That FCC Showed "Retaliatory Motive" By Ordering Early License Review Despite "Less Intrusive" Options Casting Catherine Laga'aia & Deacon Phillippe To Lead Disney+ Pilot 'Spaceship Earth' The upcoming Season 3 of High Potential will not launch after the Super Bowl; the series starring Kaitlin Olson is expected to return earlier, likely in January. (For the first time in its run, High Potential is not on the fall schedule this season.) Watch on Deadline Olson — as her character Morgan in front of High Potential ‘s signature murger board — announced the news of the special post-Super Bowl episode Monday night in a promo that ran on-air and online during Monday Night Football . Super Bowl LXI will air on ABC, ESPN and Disney+, which explains why High Potential will stream on Disney+ for the first time outside of the bundle. Its streaming home is on fellow Disney platform Hulu, both for next day episodes and previous seasons. In 2000, ABC also aired Part 1 of a two-part episode of a popular drama series, The Practice , after the Super Bowl. High Potential finished the 2025/2026 broadcast season as the No. 1 show in adults 18-49 (3.35 rating) and the No. 3 show among total viewers (16.01 million) over 35 days of viewing on ABC, Hulu, Hulu on Disney+ and digital platforms. The series follows a single mom with an exceptional mind (Olson), whose unconventional knack for solving crimes leads to an unusual and unstoppable partnership with a by-the-book seasoned detective. High Potential stars Olson as Morgan, Daniel Sunjata as Karadec, Javicia Leslie as Daphne, Deniz Akdeniz as Lev “Oz” Ozdil, Amirah J as Ava, Matthew Lamb as Elliot, and Judy Reyes as Selena. 20th Television produces the series, which is based on the French format Haut Potentiel Intellectuel (HPI) and was created in the U.S. by Drew Goddard. Goddard and Sarah Esberg of Goddard Textiles, new showrunners Nora and Lilla Zuckerman and Olson serve as executive producers. Andrea Massaro (Goddard Textiles) is a co-executive producer. In a recent interview, the Coven Academy actor revealed why it was difficult for him to talk about the role that many millennials remember him for. “Doesn’t matter what I do nowadays. One of the most memorable scenes has Sawa asking, “Can I keep you?” Because of the film’s popularity, Sawa was constantly reminded of that line and role, which took him time to embrace. articles.title: met with backlash
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Danny Trejo’s Son Claims Actor “Never Heard” Of Ben Shapiro Until 2 Weeks Into ICE Film Production: “He’s Handcuffed To This Stupid Project” ‘Artificial’s Ike Barinholtz Teases What Makes His “Menacing” Elon Musk Performance “A Little Ridiculous” Robert Pattinson Approached Chris Hansen Portrayal In ‘Primetime’ As “A Fan”: “I Was Trying To Make Him Cool” View All October 9, 2026 6:02pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Danny Trejo breaks his silence on backlash to Daily Wire's pro-ICE film. William Campbell/Getty Images/Hernando Rodriguez Danny Trejo has broken his silence amid backlash around his role in Daily Wire ‘s latest controversial production, Pawn Shop . On Friday, the LA-born Mexican-American actor insisted he’s “pro-immigrant,” despite his casting in the pro- ICE film from Ben Shapiro ‘s production company and Dallas Sonnier’s Bonfire Legend, which has been protested by locals in Livingston, Montana, where filming has been underway. “Hey everyone. I want to address some social media comments about me,” wrote Trejo in a statement on social media. “Make no mistake. I am a proud Mexican who has always been and will always be a supporter of my community. I am also obviously, pro-immigrant. I am not pro-ICE. I know where I come from and I know our struggles. I am an actor. My job is to tell a story. God Bless you, Danny.” Related Stories News Daily Wire Filming Temporarily Suspended In Montana After Special City Meeting News Jonathan Majors’ Daily Wire Action Flick Picketed By IATSE Crew In South Carolina The actor’s statement comes after production was temporarily suspended last weekend, resuming with a revised film permit on Tuesday, requiring the crew to ensure food pantry access for locals to the Livingston Food Resource Center, and shielding the public both from the shooting of violent scenes, as well as from noise. The production also agreed to address backlash to their use of private security, ensuring there would be no policing or harassing of locals on nearby public streets. Watch on Deadline Shapiro decried the suspension as “a violation of the First Amendment,” calling the film’s critics “censorious jackasses” who oppose free speech. View this post on Instagram Since filming began, locals have protested the alleged use of blank gunshots, pyrotechnics and a staged car wreck without properly notifying residents and businesses, as well as its opening scene, which appears to dramatize ICE’s fatal shooting of Renée Good in Minnesota back in January. With Rust producer Carter Boehm serving on the production team, the latest collaboration between Bonfire Legend and Daily Wire comes after their last film, Run Hide Fight: Infidels , was picketed by IATSE . Several crew members walked off over labor issues in South Carolina, shortly before Jonathan Majors was involved in an on-set accident that resulted in his co-star JC Kilcoyne needing stitches “all over his hands” after falling through a window. Deadline has confirmed that the Pawn Shop production is not under an IATSE contract either, while it is under a “conditional start” with SAG-AFTRA. Daily Wire's new pro-ICE movie production has attracted local protesters in Livingston, Montana. articles.title: Danny Trejo’s Son Claims Actor “Never Heard” Of Ben Shapiro Until 2 Weeks Into ICE Film Production: “He’s Handcuffed To This Stupid Project”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Danny Trejo’s Son Claims Actor “Never Heard” Of Ben Shapiro Until 2 Weeks Into ICE Film Production: “He’s Handcuffed To This Stupid Project” ‘Artificial’s Ike Barinholtz Teases What Makes His “Menacing” Elon Musk Performance “A Little Ridiculous” Robert Pattinson Approached Chris Hansen Portrayal In ‘Primetime’ As “A Fan”: “I Was Trying To Make Him Cool” View All October 12, 2026 7:54pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Danny Trejo and Gilbert Trejo attend the premiere of Neon's 'Ferrari' on Dec. 12, 2023 in Los Angeles, California. Kevin Winter/GA/PMC via Getty Images As Danny Trejo is met with backlash over his involvement in Daily Wire ‘s latest project, his son is coming to the actor’s defense. This weekend, Gilbert Trejo claimed that his father had “never heard of Ben Shapiro ” or “what kind of guy he is” until two weeks into production own Daily Wire and Bonfire Legend’s Pawn Shop , which has been described as a pro- ICE film that seemingly dramatizes the killing of Renée Good . “For anyone seeing this shit with my dad…” he begain a statement on his Instagram Story, which was shared by The San Fernando Valley Sun . “He was booked on a film, it’s not pro-ICE, it’s not overtly pro anything. His agent described it as ‘a complicated story about a complicated time, where everyone looks bad except you, the hardworking Mexican shop owner who just wants peace.’ Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Danny Trejo Insists He’s “Pro-Immigrant” & “Proud Mexican” Amid Backlash To Daily Wire’s ICE Film: “Make No Mistake” News Montana Locals Protest Daily Wire’s Pro-ICE Production As Filming Disrupts Businesses With Apparent Dramatization Of Renée Good Shooting “He jumped at the idea of playing a good guy. About 2 weeks into shooting everyone, including us, found out Ben Shapiro was involved. My 82-year-old dad has never heard of Ben Shapiro, I had to explain to him who that is, and what kind of guy he is. My dad contractually can’t bad mouth him, the film, or walk away without being sued for breach of contract. He couldn’t even release the statement he wanted to.” Gilbert continued, “It’s fucked up. He’s handcuffed to this stupid project, and swaths of people have instantly turned their back on him without knowing any of the facts. Ben Shapiro got Mexicans to abandon one of their heroes, got his own name to the top of google’s searches, and made us look like angry fools lacking any nuance. He wins.” Fake protesters film a scene for the Daily Wire production ‘Pawn Shop’ on Oct. 2, 2026 in Livingston, Montana. William Campbell/Getty Images Last week, Danny Trejo broke his silence following backlash to his role in the movie. “Hey everyone. I want to address some social media comments about me,” he said. “Make no mistake. I am a proud Mexican who has always been and will always be a supporter of my community. I am also obviously, pro-immigrant. I am not pro-ICE. I know where I come from and I know our struggles. I am an actor. My job is to tell a story. God Bless you, Danny.” The synopsis for Pawn Shop reads: ‘When chaos hits the streets of Minneapolis, a young federal agent is left alone after his partner is seriously hurt and must find a way to survive an increasingly dangerous situation. Seeking shelter inside a neighborhood pawn shop, he becomes trapped with a traditional Hispanic father and his progressive college-age son, forcing three very different men to confront fear, conflicting beliefs and a crisis that tests their courage and humanity.” Since filming began, locals have protested the alleged use of blank gunshots, pyrotechnics and a staged car wreck without properly notifying residents and businesses, as well as its opening scene, which appears to dramatize ICE’s fatal shooting of Renée Good in Minnesota back in January. Daily Wire's new pro-ICE movie production has attracted local protesters in Livingston, Montana. Filming under the working title 'Pawn Shop', the latest project from Ben Shapiro's Daily Wire and Dallas Sonnier's Bonfire Legend has upset locals — not just because of its alleged… pic.twitter.com/LBCQh4rEkh — Deadline (@DEADLINE) October 2, 2026 Production was temporarily suspended earlier this month, resuming with a revised film permit last Tuesday, requiring the crew to ensure food pantry access for locals to the Livingston Food Resource Center, and shielding the public both from the shooting of violent scenes, as well as from noise. The production also agreed to address backlash to their use of private security, ensuring there would be no policing or harassing of locals on nearby public streets. Shapiro decried the suspension as “a violation of the First Amendment,” calling the film’s critics “censorious jackasses” who oppose free speech. Son” Sean Combs Injured In Prison; Release Date Pushed Back Again Amid Controversies & Violations Disney’s Former Top IP Lawyer Sues House Of Mouse For Ageism & Wrongful Termination: “Sleepless Nights & Days” View All October 12, 2026 8:02pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source (L-R) Breaking Bad stars RJ Mitte, Anna Gunn, Bryan Cranston, & Aaron Paul at the 30th Annual SAG Awards Getty Almost 20 years after Breaking Bad began, Bryan Cranston tonight lamented the death Monday of the man who played his son on the acclaimed series. “I’m in deep despair as I write this tonight. RJ Mitte , my sweet son on Breaking Bad has died,” Cranston said on his Instagram feed today. Actor and disability-rights activist Mitte died Monday at the age of 34 at his home in Brownsville, Texas In his post Cranston mourned Mitte, who played Walter White Jr, to the fictional father who sometimes went by his meth kingpin moniker of the surname German physicist Werner Heisenberg. Related Stories Obituaries RJ Mitte Remembered By 'Breaking Bad' Co-Stars: "This Is So Heartbreaking" Obituaries RJ Mitte Dies: 'Breaking Bad' Actor Was 34 For most of the five season run of the Vince Gilligan created show, Mitte’s cerebral palsy-afflicted Mitte’s character did not know his science teacher farther was one of the southwest’s biggest drug dealers. The younger White only found out near the end of the final season in the heartbreaking “Ozymandias” episode Watch on Deadline Praised as one of the great TV series ever, Breaking Bad ran from 2008 to 2013. Bryan Cranston & RJ Mitte in ‘Breaking Bad’ AMC/Everett Collection As Cranston wrote tonight, Mitte “was only 14 years old” when the show started production. “That kid was pretty raw when we started shooting the pilot in February of 2007, but little by little we watched him grow into a really fine actor,” Cranston said of his co-star. “He parlayed his experience on the show to be a vocal advocate for performers with disabilities, and was the head of a philanthropic organization with a focus on helping the disabled community.” “All that promise and potential now is such a loss.” Noting his on-air son’s cause of death, Cranston added: “It is especially devastating to hear that he took his own life. Why? We were texting each other just a few weeks ago – figuring out when we could meet for lunch. I don’t know if that lunch would have changed his future…” “But I do know that I loved him, and thoroughly enjoyed being with him throughout the years on the series, and after the spotlight on Breaking Bad dimmed… I’ll miss you, son.” View this post on Instagram Along with co-stars Anna Gunn and Aaron Paul , Cranston and Mitte were together on stage at the 2024 SAG Awards in a BB reunion of sorts. The quartet were presenting the award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series. Breaking Bad actually won that particular SAG Award in 2014. An autopsy of Mitte will be performed in the coming days, Cameron County officials said Monday. If you or anyone you know is having thoughts of suicide, call or text 988 to reach the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline. articles.title: Discovery+ Raises Prices In One Of Skydance’s First Streaming Moves After Merger Close
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Discovery+ Raises Prices In One Of Skydance’s First Streaming Moves After Merger Close Prime Video Adds Golf’s Revived Skins Game To 15-Hour Live Sports Blitz On Black Friday Sony Ups Tim Erickson To CEO Of Peanuts Worldwide, Appoints Ken Ohtake As Chairman View All October 13, 2026 8:28am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Discovery's Shark Week programming is featured on streaming service Discovery+ Courtesy As it begins its second week as a bulked-up public company, Skydance has raised prices of stand-alone streaming service Discovery+ . The base-level, ad-supported tier now costs $6.99 a month, up $1, and the “ad-light” higher tier is $11.99, a $2 increase. Skydance was formed from the merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery , which officially closed last week. The new company is saddled with nearly $80 billion in debt and has pledged to whittle it down along with delivering $6 billion in cost savings. Along with back-end efficiencies, real estate sales and layoffs, higher streaming rates are expected, in keeping with inflation across the media sector of late. Related Stories News 'M+/HBO Originals': Movistar Plus & Skydance Extend Partnership News Who Is In Charge At Skydance International - For Now At Least Discovery+, which features programming from a range of cable networks, has remained a stand-alone since its launch in 2021. It initially was priced at $4.99 for the base tier and $6.99 for the plan with fewer ads, offering 50,000 hours of programming from networks like TLC, Discovery, HGTV and the Food Network. Watch on Deadline After former parent Discovery Communications merged with WarnerMedia in 2022, the new parent looked at combining Discovery+ with HBO Max and went so far as to rebrand the latter as Max to reflect a broader content offering. Audiences and partners balked at the mixture of upmarket HBO fare with lifestyle and unscripted fare, and the corporate bosses preserved Discovery+ as a lower-priced option for consumers. In part because the company does not commission originals for Discovery+, it has been profitable for most of its existence. HBO Max announced a round of price hikes last fall, with the basic ad-tier rising $1 to $10.99 a month and the popular Standard plan climbing to $18.49. articles.title: Reinaldo Marcus Green Launches Film Fellowship At His Alma Mater NYU Tisch School Of The Arts, Reveals Inaugural Class
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Patrick Hipes Patrick Hipes Executive Managing Editor More Stories By Patrick Reinaldo Marcus Green Launches Film Fellowship At His Alma Mater NYU Tisch School Of The Arts, Reveals Inaugural Class ‘Being Heumann’ Trailer: First Extended Look At Siân Heder’s ‘CODA’ Follow-Up Sony’s Screen Gems Sets YouTube Exec Fede Goldenberg To Top Genre Label; Ashley Brucks Segues To Producer Role View All October 13, 2026 8:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Reinaldo Marcus Green Arturo Holmes/Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: King Richard and Bob Marley: One Love director Reinaldo Marcus Green has launched Office Hours, a new filmmaker fellowship at his alma mater the NYU Tisch School of the Arts. The fellowship has also selected its inaugural class of five filmmakers who are all recent alums or current students in the graduate film program. The fellowship, created to provide emerging filmmakers with access, mentorship and candid conversation about the creative and professional realities of building a career in film, will bring its fellows together with Green for a series of intimate sessions throughout the academic year on topics like developing a voice, choosing material, working with actors and collaborators, navigating representation and relationships, dealing with setbacks, and building a sustainable career. Related Stories News David Oyelowo & Viola Prettejohn To Star In ‘The Girl With The Dragon Tattoo’ TV Series For Sky News ‘King Richard’ Director Reinaldo Marcus Green To Helm Roberto Clemente Biopic For Teton Ridge This year’s cohort — Alex Jiang, Maissa Lihedheb, Skyla Page, Andre Shen and Taylor Sanghyun Lee — were selected by a committee of filmmakers including Kasi Lemmons, John Tintori, Chiara Bernasconi and Mia Cioffi Henry. (See details about the inaugural class below.) Watch on Deadline “When I was coming out of NYU, what I needed as much as anything was access — someone I could call, ask the questions I didn’t know how to ask, and have an honest conversation about what this career actually looks like,” Green said. He added: “Office Hours is my attempt to create that space for the next generation of filmmakers. These five filmmakers already have extraordinary voices. My job isn’t to tell them what kind of filmmakers to become. It’s to listen, challenge them, share what I’ve learned, and hopefully help them get where they’re trying to go.” Green directed 2021’s King Richard , the story of the rise of tennis’ Venus and Serena Williams and their father-coach. The pic scored six Oscar nominations including Best Picture, and earned star Will Smith the Best Actor Oscar. He follow that up co-writing and directing 2024’s Bob Marley: One Love . His credits also include the TV series We Own This City and Netflix’s Top Boy . His debut feature, Monsters and Men starring John David Washington, Anthony Ramos and Kelvin Harrison Jr., world premiered at the 2018 Sundance Film Festival. He’s now working on Sky’s TV adaptation The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo , on which he directs and executive produces. “Having this kind of guidance from an established filmmaker like Rei is an incredible opportunity for our students and recent alumni as they navigate their first steps in the industry,” says Andrew Okpeaha MacLean, chair of the Tisch Department of Graduate Film. Below are more details on this year’s fellows, per Office Hours: ALEX JIANG Alex Jiang is a Hong Kong-born, New York-based filmmaker exploring bodily autonomy and queer desire through folklore and a feminist, Asian diasporic lens. A USC BFA graduate and NYU Tisch MFA candidate, her shorts have screened at Palm Springs ShortFest, Los Angeles Asian Pacific Film Festival and Taiwan International Queer Film Festival. She participated in the Shanghai International Film Festival Director’s Lab and Diverso Fellowship and is a member of the 2026 Film at Lincoln Center Artists Academy. As a producer, she is developing Circle, one of 12 projects selected for the 15th Biennale College Cinema. MAISSA LIHEDHEB Maissa Lihedheb is a German-Tunisian filmmaker whose work explores identity, performance and the contradictions of belonging through dark humor and emotionally charged storytelling. Her films have screened at Tribeca, BFI London, Palm Springs ShortFest and El Gouna. Her work has been featured by Vogue Arabia, Rolling Stone MENA, ARTE and Highsnobiety. A two-time Ang Lee Scholar, Spike Lee Grant recipient and Princess Grace honoree, she completed her MFA at NYU Tisch Graduate Film and is currently developing the feature films Wedding and a Funeral, Carapace and The Good One. SKYLA PAGE Skyla Page is a writer, director and cinematographer from Chicago, now based in Brooklyn. She earned her MFA from NYU Tisch Graduate Film. As a cinematographer, she received the Nestor Almendros Craft Award for Cinematography, and her work has screened at the First Run and Atlanta Film Festivals. She received the Spike Lee Production Fund for her upcoming short Rise & Fly and is currently developing her debut narrative feature, Full Bloom. ANDRE SHEN Andre Shen is a Shanghainese writer-director and graphic designer based in New York. His work explores queer longing and emotional exposure through pop culture, orbiting an obsession with performance across gender, theater and sex. His films have screened at BFI Flare, MiXMilano and FiveFilmsForFreedom in partnership with the British Council. His upcoming short Hit It Out of the Park follows a rising pop star and his self-proclaimed creative director as their music video shoot unravels. He is currently preparing his feature. TAYLOR SANGHYUN LEE Born and raised in California, Taylor Sanghyun Lee is a New York-based filmmaker whose work spans writing, directing and cinematography. His directorial debut feature, ROUNDS, was selected for the 2026 Sundance Directors & Screenwriters Lab, the 2026 NYU Purple List and the 2025 TIFF & CJ K-Story Fund. He earned his MFA in Directing from NYU Tisch Graduate Film, where he received the Ang Lee Scholarship. His upcoming short Parkside East won the 2026 DGA Student Spotlight Award and was a semifinalist for the 2026 Student Academy Awards. articles.title: ‘Bella From Barneys’ Lands Series Order At Amazon From Josh Schwartz, Stephanie Savage, Susan Rovner & Rachel Kaplan
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Peter White Peter White Executive Editor, Television @peterzwhite More Stories By Peter Animated Comedy Series ‘Merrick & Treves’ From ‘Archer’ Team Lands Two-Season HBO Order Disney Heist Doc ‘Stolen Kingdom’ Heads To Mipcom Skydance’s JB Perrette Makes First Moves After Re-Upping Contract View All October 13, 2026 8:45am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Barneys New York Mario Tama/Getty Images EXCLUSIVE : Amazon has greenlit a drama series about a newly revived Barneys New York. The streamer has handed a series order to Bella from Barneys , which comes from Fake Empire founders Josh Schwartz and Stephanie Savage, known for series including Gossip Girl, Susan Rovner and Rachel Kaplan . Related Stories News Josh Schwartz & Stephanie Savage Strike First-Look Deal With Amazon; Barneys New York Drama In The Works With Susan Rovner As EP Cancellations and Renewals ‘Sterling Point’ Renewed For Season 2 By Prime Video Bella from Barneys follows Bella Baldwin, an outer-borough outsider with an eye for style, who lands a job in the stock room of the newly revived Barneys New York. When she talks her way into becoming a personal shopper to the store’s most notorious socialite client, she’s pulled into a cutthroat world of fashion and family secrets, and into the orbit of the heir fighting to save the family business. Deadline revealed the project was in development last year as part of a new first-look deal between Amazon MGM Studios and Schwartz and Savage. Since then, the pair’s Sterling Point , which they partnered with creator Megan Park on, has become a hit on the streamer and was recently renewed for a second season. The duo are also involved in Paramount+’s sequel event series Clueless . Watch on Deadline Schwartz and Savage will serve as executive producers alongside Aha Studios’ Susan Rovner and Absecon Entertainment’s Rachel Kaplan as well as Corey Salter, Colin Smeeton, and Matthew Gross, who exec produce for Authentic Studios, the production arm of Barneys owner Authentic Brands Group. Barneys was a New York institution; a high-end department store that was founded in 1923. After being acquired by Authentic Brands Group, it closed its brick-and-mortars stores but remained as a brand, particularly as a partnership with Saks Fifth Avenue as well as its own beauty line. In 2024, there was also a pop-up Barneys in Soho. Josh Schwartz & Stephanie Savage (Jason Mendez/Getty) “We’re thrilled to be continuing our partnership with Amazon and are excited for what’s ahead,” said Schwartz and Savage. “The response to Sterling Point has been incredibly gratifying, and we’re so happy to be returning for a second season alongside creator Megan Park and producing partners LuckyChap. At the same time, the opportunity to build the fictional world of Barneys is a dream for us. Barneys was more than a store; it was a New York institution, a cultural touchstone, and a world unto itself. We’re so excited to open those doors along with our partners at Authentic Brands Group, and our fellow producers Susan Rovner and Rachel Kaplan, who we have worked with since the beginning of our careers.” “Josh and Stephanie at Fake Empire have this rare gift for creating worlds that feel both electric and cozy all at once, and Bella from Barneys is a perfect example,” added Peter Friedlander, Head of Global Television, Amazon MGM Studios. “Barneys New York was more than a department store — it was a fashion institution, and when it closed, people genuinely mourned it. This series brings it roaring back to life in all its impossibly chic glory. Fashion, ambition, and intrigue await inside the doors that our partners Susan, Rachel, and the team at Authentic Brands Group will help reopen.” “At Authentic, our brands are stories, and Bella from Barneys shows what’s possible when iconic IP meets world-class storytelling. We’re excited to bring its legacy to the screen with Fake Empire. Josh Schwartz and Stephanie Savage, who are unmatched at creating stylish, character-driven drama, are the perfect stewards for the Barneys brand,” said Corey Salter, CEO Entertainment, Authentic. articles.title: Ryan Coogler’s ‘The X-Files’ Reboot Picked Up To Series At Hulu
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Denise Petski Denise Petski Senior Managing Editor More Stories By Denise Ryan Coogler’s ‘The X-Files’ Reboot Picked Up To Series At Hulu Maddie Hasson Joins Julia Garner & Lewis Pullman In Apple TV’s ‘Guilty Creatures’ Amber Siyavus Dies: ‘Big Brother’ Season 8 Contestant Was 46 View All October 13, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Himesh Patel and Danielle Deadwyler Nat Jamieson/Deadline Ryan Coogler ‘s long-gestating The X-Files reboot, starring Emmy nominee Himesh Patel ( The Odyssey, Station Eleven ) and Danielle Deadwyler ( The Bell Jar, The Chaperones ), has been ordered to series at Hulu . From Onyx Collective and 20th Television, the reimagining of Chris Carter ‘s classic series follows two highly decorated but vastly different FBI agents, played by Deadwyler and Patel, who form an unlikely bond when they are assigned to a long-shuttered division devoted to cases involving unexplained phenomena. Sinners filmmaker Coogler wrote, directed and executive produced the pilot via his Proximity Media. He executive produces with showrunner Jennifer Yale. Executive producers also include Zinzi Coogler and Sev Ohanian for Proximity Media and The X-Files creator Carter. Co-executive producers are Simone Harris for Proximity Media, along with Deadwyler and Patel. Related Stories News 'Bob's Burgers' Sets Premiere For Hulu Holiday Short; Releases First-Look Clip News Himesh Patel & Maxine Peake Among The Stars In Latest Booker Prize Short Films “I’ve loved The X-Files for a long time, so getting the chance to write and direct the pilot has meant a great deal to me,” said Coogler. “What Chris Carter created is special, and we wanted to honor everything that made the original series connect with so many people while also finding our own way into that world. Danielle and Himesh, along with the rest of our cast, have brought such original perspectives and performances to these characters, and watching that come together has been one of the most rewarding parts of the experience. I couldn’t have asked for better collaborators than my crew, colleagues at Proximity Media and our partners at Onyx Collective and 20th Television. I’m grateful for the trust and support they’ve given us as we take on this new chapter.” Watch on Deadline The series order caps a more than three-year journey for the project, which falls under Coogler’s five-year exclusive television deal with Disney , the parent company of Hulu, 20th TV and Onyx. Carter first revealed during a 2023 podcast interview that he had spoken with Coogler who was “going to remount The X Files with a diverse cast,” adding, “He’s got his work cut out for him because we covered so much territory.” “We’re looking forward to continuing this journey as executive producers and especially excited to work closely with Jennifer Yale, Simone Harris, and the entire cast and crew as we bring this new chapter of The X-Files to life,” said Zinzi Coogler, Sev Ohanian and Ryan Coogler, founders of Proximity Media. “It was also incredibly special to have our fellow Proximity co-founder Ludwig Göransson contribute the score for the pilot, making this a true collaboration across the Proximity family.” Carter’s original X-Files starred Gillian Anderson and David Duchovny as FBI Special Agents Dana Scully and Fox Mulder, who investigate cases involving paranormal phenomena. The series premiered on Fox in 1993 and ran for nine seasons. It spawned two feature films, The X-Files (1998) and The X-Files: I Want to Believe (2008), as well as a 2016 revival, which aired on Fox for two seasons. Ava DuVernay’s documentary examining threats to the 14 th Amendment , which held its world premiere Friday at the New York Film Festival, earned a leading six nominations Tuesday as the 11 th annual Critics Choice Documentary Awards announced its nominees. Close behind with five nominations each: You Can See Everything , the documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim; Once Upon a Time in Harlem , directed by David Greaves and produced by Liani Greaves ; and Nuisance Bear , directed by Gabriela Osio Vanden and Jack Weisman. We are proud to recognize the exceptional talent and creativity behind this year’s nominated films.” Critics Choice Documentary Awards As previously announced, Ron Howard will receive the Critics Choice Impact Award, an honor recognizing “filmmakers whose work, influence, and commitment to nonfiction storytelling have made a significant and lasting impact on the documentary form, broadening its reach and championing its continued evolution.” Howard’s documentaries include Avedon (2026), Jim Henson Idea Man (2024), We Feed People (2022), Rebuilding Paradise (2020) and Pavarotti (2019). articles.title: Katherine Waterston Joins Post-9/11 Limited Series ‘The Best Of Us’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy Anthony Mackie Is Seeking Revenge In ’12 12 12′ Trailer Andy Allo To Guest Star On ‘The Rookie: North’ Ed Quinn & Stephanie Koenig To Recur On ‘Scrubs’ For Season 2; Punkie Johnson & Kellan Tetlow To Guest Star View All October 13, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Katherine Waterston Jeff Spicer/Getty Images for The Clooney Foundation For Justice EXCLUSIVE: Katherine Waterston ( The Agency, The Uprising ) is the latest star to join the cast of Paramount+ ‘s limited series The Best of Us , which has been shooting in New York City since last month. She will star opposite Jeremy Strong in the upcoming six-episode limited series inspired by the David vs. Goliath fight that won justice for 9/11’s ailing heroes. Waterston will play Amy Smith, a lawyer and the soon-to-be ex-wife of Jason (Strong). From writers Tobias Lindholm and Frank Pugliese, the 6-episode series The Best of Us dramatizes a landmark case that reshaped the fight for accountability: a relentless legal war that stretched nearly a decade to secure almost $1 billion in compensation for first responders who fell gravely ill in the wake of 9/11. Related Stories Casting 'Star Trek: Starfleet Academy: Season 2 Release Date & Photos; Bill Nighy & Rosemarie DeWitt To Guest Star Cancellations and Renewals 'Avatar: Seven Havens' Renewed For 2 More Seasons At Paramount+, New Animated Series 'Avatar Kuruk: Wave of Chaos' Ordered Strong leads the cast as renowned class action lawyer Jason Smith, who risked everything to take on entrenched institutions, exposing the politics, greed, corruption, and betrayal that compounded tragedy, set against the emergency workers’ remarkable unity and bravery as the World Trade Center was collapsing. Watch on Deadline In addition to Strong, the previously announced cast also includes Barry Pepper as Coach, a former NYPD police officer and 9/11 first responder suffering from leukemia due to his work at Ground Zero; Andrea Riseborough as Molly, Coach’s resilient wife; Neal Huff as Peter Allen, Jason’s pragmatic colleague at the law firm; Gaby Hoffmann as Kathleen McCormick, a seasoned FDNY firefighter and activist; Sky Yang as The Lost Son, a young and mysterious homeless man; and John Slattery as James Leavitt, a highly experienced and formidable defense lawyer. The guest cast includes LaChanze, Richard Schiff , Elizabeth Rodriguez, Joe Morton, Jen Tullock, William Baldwin, and Keith W. Richards. Produced by Paramount Television Studios and Sister, the limited series is written, directed, and executive produced by Lindholm and written and executive produced by Pugliese. Strong is also an executive producer, along with Tony Hernandez. Waterston was recently seen in Paul Greengrass’ The Uprising and in the Paramount+ series The Agency alongside Michael Fassbender. Before that, she starred in Fackham Hall , a British Period Comedy written by Jimmy Carr. Additional credits include the latest installment in the Fear Street franchise, Prom Queen, The End We Start From , Slow Horses , Perry Mason , They Listen , Babylon , Inherent Vice , Alien: Covenant, and the Fantastic Beasts film series. Waterston is represented by UTA, Strand Entertainment, LARK Management, and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller. articles.title: Fox Boss Rob Wade Commits Long Term To Creator Studios: “We’re Not Here To Flip A House”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Channel 4 Unveils First-Ever Microdrama: Female Friendship Series Stars ‘You’s Jadesola Odunjo We Will Never “Lie To The Audience” Over Artificial Intelligence, Says BBC Content Chief Kate Phillips BBC Studios Launches Scripted Fund & Tasks Ben Donald With Helping Unearth Next Generation Of European IP View All October 13, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Rob Wade Banff EXCLUSIVE: Fox Entertainment CEO Rob Wade has committed long into the future to his company’s creator studio, telling Deadline: “We’re not here to flip a house.” Fox Creator Studios (FCS), a “digital-first division,” was unveiled at the start of this year with partnerships including a food roster headed by Gordon Ramsay, but the idea had been percolating in Wade’s mind for more than a decade. Wade feels that plenty of big companies are investing in the creator, AI and tech space simply in order to “sell for hundreds of millions and get out,” but Fox won’t be following suit. “The game is built around that, which is not a recipe for long-term success,” said Wade. “But we’re in it for the long term. We’re not here to flip a house. If I want to invest in something, my bosses and board will say that if it’s successful they want to build on it. We will never sell [Fox Creator Studios].” Related Stories News 'Baywatch' Reboot Full Trailer Release Ahead Of January 2027 Premiere On Fox News The YouTube Age: Meet The Content Creators Making Waves In Europe Wade was speaking to Deadline in the days leading up to MIPCOM , where he has just been joined on a Deadline-hosted panel by FCS boss Billy Parks , Prentiss Fraser, who runs distributor Fox Entertainment Global (FEG), and Fox-backed creators Josh Richards and Chris Sawtelle. Watch on Deadline Wade, Parks and Fraser have grand plans, with the former positioning the main goal as “creating a path to IP creation on the internet.” In this vein, FCS is doing things a bit differently to its rivals in what is becoming an increasingly crowded space both in the U.S. and internationally, with content creators one of the big topics at this year’s MIPCOM, a traditional TV sales market. FCS is seeking to tie with content creators across a whole range of genres but won’t necessarily air their work solely on Fox or Fox-owned platforms like Tubi. Instead, it will leverage resources and advertising infrastructure to create content spanning different platforms and territories. Content creators can then diversify revenue streams, while FEG boss Fraser and her team shop their wares around the world. The studio has so far struck deals with long-time Fox collaborator Ramsay, comedian Tom Segura and creators like Richards, who makes YouTube sketch comedy Read the Room. This approach sets Fox apart from its competitors in two key ways, Wade believes, “going direct and investing in original content by creating finance for new shows,” and providing “very significant advertising infrastructure” via an ad sales division that has the likes of the NFL and World Cup in its portfolio. Parks, who joined Fox from The Chernin Group, said the studio offers hands-off support to creators who are “being pulled in many different directions.” “We’re not greenlighting their ideas through a long, traditional development process,” he added. “Instead, we’re available for notes and feedback in an equitable way, without approaching the relationship as a top-down studio-to-creative model.” In this way, Parks said creators “who are trying to do something outside their comfort zone” can be supported with capital and an IP-sharing vision. “Many platforms that work with creators option their libraries or make shows with them to drive audiences to their own platforms,” he added. “That’s how companies such as Netflix, Amazon and Hulu are structured to work. That isn’t necessarily better or worse. Every creator will make different choices at different points in their career. But those platforms are primarily built to acquire subscribers, and that’s what they do with creators.” Parks was recently at creator economy market VidSummit, where he said bosses at CAA, UTA and WME were all present along with leaders from platforms like Netflix and Tubi. “Everyone is thinking about the different types of deals available to creators, whether that involves investment, production or intellectual property,” he added. All started with ‘Dancing With The Stars’ But while creators may be the talk of today, Wade and Parks have been thinking about this for a long while. Wade says FCS’ inception harks back more than 15 years to when he was a producer on Dancing with the Stars and booked the show’s first ever YouTuber, Bethany Mota. “She did very well but we learned a few things,” he added. “I was expecting an avalanche of YouTube views and imagined the votes for her would heavily skew young but there was no sudden mass of views or a sudden mass on YouTube. Our knowledge of the internet back then was very different.” He realized that YouTube success does not always translate to traditional TV in obvious ways and figured out over the years that a studio’s infrastructure could be used in smart ways in this space. Things solidified with the success of Prime Video and A24’s Hazbin Hotel, which was produced by Fox-owned Bento Box and started life on YouTube via its creator Vivienne Medrano. “We thought to ourselves, ‘We’re not a library, we’re a studio’,” added Wade. “What a studio does is back creators and put bets on them. That is something we know how to do.” White House Press Secretary’s Debut: Very Short, Some News, Much Trump Praise The YouTube Age: Content Creators Making Waves In Europe Toon Comedy ‘Merrick & Treves’ From ‘Archer’ Team Lands Two-Season HBO Order Cranston & Other ‘Breaking Bad’ Alums Mourn Actor Who Played Walt Jr. Read More About: Comments
