articles.title: Tilly Nollywood? African Filmmakers — Ready or Not — Get Set for the AI Revolution
articles.full_text: Oct 12, 2026 11:36am PT Tilly Nollywood? African Filmmakers — Ready or Not — Get Set for the AI Revolution By Christopher Vourlias Plus Icon Christopher Vourlias Latest How South Africa Rescued Its Rebate and Pulled the Industry Back From the Brink: We’re ‘Back in Business’ 14 minutes ago ‘Mami Wata’ Director C.J. Obasi, ‘Khartoum’ Filmmaker Ibrahim Ahmad and More Take New Projects to Durban FilmMart’s Co-Production Forum 5 days ago Durban FilmMart Head on Why This Year’s Event Is ‘Looking Inward’ as African Screen Industries Strive to ‘Create Solutions’ on Their Own Terms 2 weeks ago See All "Mystery of Osu Land" (Courtesy Mysterious Tech Studio) The world premiere of what’s been billed as the first photorealistic, AI -generated feature film in the Yoruba language fizzled out last week when user demand overwhelmed the servers of Docuth, the streaming platform that hosted the launch. After months of hype building to the release of “Asiri Ilu Awon Osu” (Mystery of Osu Land), the film’s Nigerian producers, Mysterious Tech Studio, took to social media to apologize for the glitch, telling their followers: “To everyone at home and abroad who has tried to watch and could not get through, please do not be offended or discouraged.” Related Stories Charlie Brooker's New Netflix Series Gets Title, 'Blackmere,' as Rory Kinnear Joins Cast and First-Look Photos Revealed The episode felt somehow symbolic for this moment in the history of AI in Africa, where excitement over the technology’s transformative potential for the continent’s filmmakers often runs counter to the practical realities on the ground. Popular on Variety As African industry professionals convened at this year’s Durban FilmMart , both the potential and pitfalls of artificial intelligence were high on the agenda. Among the chief concerns for many stakeholders are the barriers to entry. AI tools that are widely available elsewhere in the world face unique challenges in reaching African consumers, from high data costs and low broadband speeds to payment-processing headaches. Tamara Dawit, of Ethiopian Canadian production company Gobez Media, noted that those challenges represent significant “systemic barriers” to the adoption of the latest tech tools on the African continent. “How do we address those issues so that everyone is benefitting from the advancements in technology?” she said. “If these are great opportunities for the industry, can everybody actually access them?” Zukisani Karabo Mabece, of media-tech and production company Digicine Motion Picture, agreed. “AI isn’t necessarily a magic pill,” said Mabece, whose Johannesburg-based company has leaned into generative AI with a host of digital tools designed to democratize access to cutting-edge technology for African filmmakers. “It’s very biased. It’s very Western,” he said. “We’re having to build our own language models to accommodate the languages that we have here locally. We took it upon ourselves to build models that serve our market and our geography.” In some instances, the rapid adoption of AI technology has had unintended consequences that aren’t unique to Africa. Earlier this year, the South African government drafted an ambitious AI policy that was summarily withdrawn when journalists discovered that at least six of its 67 academic citations were the by-products of AI hallucinations, referring to journals and authors that did not exist. The drafters appeared to have used a large-language model to compose the policy without verifying its claims. While the blunder was a PR disaster for South African policymakers, Amilcar Patel, who serves as co-chair of the South African Screen Federation (SASFED), noted that there are more pernicious dangers lurking for Africans when it comes to using AI tools developed in the Global North. “We need to be very careful when we’re using AI in our work, especially in our policy and legal work, because we’re infusing a very different culture that doesn’t protect women, that doesn’t protect the poor, that doesn’t protect the vulnerable, into our legislative framework,” said Patel. “And then it becomes law.” For African creatives, there are additional ethical factors to consider. “AI mirrors society,” said Dawit. “Society has a lot of systemic inequities within it, and those show up [in AI models].” “Those that are building AI don’t look like us. Biases are already built into the AI systems,” added Samantha Kaine, of the Independent Media Producers Assn. of Creative Talent (I.M.P.A.C.T.). “When the major AI models are trained largely on Western data and Western culture, what does it take to use these tools without importing someone else’s aesthetic or erasing who we are — erasing our own identity?” Such concerns are likely to be on the agenda next month when Cape Town plays host to the Africa AI Summit, a three-day event that gathers heads of state and global tech and business leaders to draw up a roadmap that will shape the future of AI across Africa and the Global South. Backed by partners including the World Bank, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Nvidia, the event is built around a billion-dollar AI initiative that’s designed to accelerate the deployment of artificial intelligence across the continent. In the meantime, African filmmakers will continue to find uses for AI tools, even as the continent’s digital infrastructure and policy frameworks are forced to play catch-up. One week after the failed rollout of “Mystery of Osu Land,” Kafilat Yusuff, of Mysterious Tech Studio, told Variety that after “viewers experienced intermittent access due to high traffic at launch,” the platform “has now been stabilized.” The film, which incorporated roughly 80% AI-assisted scenes with 20% live-action scenes utilizing real actors and their voices, is now available to stream on Docuth. “Our experience has shown us that AI offers independent African filmmakers new ways to explore ambitious stories and visual worlds,” Yusuff said. “However, it also raises important questions about the role of human performers, consent, compensation, creative ownership and how audiences receive AI-assisted films.” As for future plans, she said that the company is holding off on a follow-up until “Mystery of Osu Land” has had time to enjoy a “full run.” “We spent a lot of time building this, and with the premiere traffic we just saw on Docuth, it’s clear there’s a lot of global curiosity. So our focus now is festivals, wider press and securing a stable global streaming release so everyone who wants to see it can,” she said. “We are documenting everything we learned from this hybrid 80% AI-20% live-action pipeline, which will eventually help us and other African filmmakers make future projects at lower cost.” The Durban FilmMart runs Oct. 9 – 12 in Durban, South Africa. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Disney’s Former Top IP Lawyer Sues House Of Mouse For Ageism & Wrongful Termination: “Sleepless Nights & Days” Skydance CEOs Pressed On Layoffs & Donald Trump Interference As They Outline Future At Town Hall ‘SNL’ Cold Open Goes Full MAGA Midterms Desperation With Hegseth’s “Schlong Donkeys”, Trump’s Rambles & A Sad VP View All October 1, 2026 3:09pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Sean "Diddy" Combs Getty Images Sean “Diddy” Combs’ sweet ride behind bars has come to an end. No official word has come down yet from the federal Bureau of Prisons in response to a NBC News segment this week revealing the Bad Boy Records founder has been using banned cellphones, allegedly smuggling in booze and having a paid for a de facto posse and cleaning staff during his incarceration. However, sources tell me authorities at FCI Fort Dix that Combs’ actions will have “serious consequences.” Among them, Combs has now been placed in solitary confinement at the low-security New Jersey facility. Related Stories News DOJ Launches Investigation Of Networks For Suspending TV Pool Amid Trump's Ban On CNN News 'Walker' & 'Pretty Little Liars' Actor Keegan Allen Pistol-Whipped And Robbed In West Hollywood Convicted of two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution in July 2025 and sentenced to a 50-month stint (with time served ), Combs was moved out of the prison’s general population late Wednesday, I hear. How long Combs will stay in the hole is TBD, but also under consideration is pushing back the Grammy winner’s early 2028 release date. After several shifts in Combs’ release date in part due to his participation in a drug treatment program, he most recently saw his date moved up to January 21, 2028 from the date of May 8, 2028 date he had when he entered Fort Dix. That date was a far cry from the June 4, 2028 date he was assigned in November of last year. Now, because of the violations revealed on camera by NBC, Combs could be looking at months being re-added. The BOP had no specific comments on Combs or the images and reports of his champagne lifestyle behind bars but told Deadline: “Like all correctional agencies, contraband, particularly cell phones, narcotics, and weapons, remains a constant challenge, and we continue to tackle the problem of contraband being introduced into our facilities. Inmates are not permitted to have access to cell phones, and all incarcerated individuals in the Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) who are found to violate the ‘Inmate Discipline Program’ policy are subject to sanctions.” All of this would be moot if Combs received the pardon he begged Donald Trump for, or if NYC jurors last year had found Combs guilty of racketeering conspiracy and sex trafficking charges, as prosecutors in the high-turnover Southern District of New York’s U.S. Attorney’s Office had hoped. That verdict in the 2025 trial over filmed sex parties and freak-offs, Cassie Ventura beatings, drug binges, threats, exploding cars and allegedly hanging people off balconies, would have seen Combs, 56, receive a life sentence behind bars. Combs’ rep Juda Engelmayer on Thursday had nothing to say about the once mini-mogul being in solitary or a possible delay in his release from prison, but he certainly had questions about who should be getting punished, who else is in the wrong and how. “There is something odd about all of this. Someone was apparently able to record Sean inside the prison, and numerous stories continue to emerge from inside the facility in real time,” the crisis communications veteran told Deadline. “Yet the focus inevitably lands on the celebrity because he is the person everyone recognizes. There are legitimate questions about how recordings and information are making their way out of a federal prison in the first place. Focusing almost exclusively on the famous inmate may make the easiest headline, but it overlooks the broader question of how this material is being obtained and circulated.” As Combs’ East Coast case is in the middle of a fast-tracked appeal, the L.A. County District Attorney’s office still has a LAPD sexual battery report on him “under review,” a spokesperson for Nathan Hochman ‘s team tells Deadline. Handed over to the DA in late 2025 , the LAPD case concerns music producer Jonathan Hay. Goldfish centers on a 17-year-old high school senior who presents as detached, ironic and emotionally armored, but underneath is quietly paralyzed by fear of failure, abandonment and becoming his parents. articles.title: ‘Beatles’ Producer Pippa Harris Shares Update On Sam Mendes Film Series & Explains Staggered Release Strategy — LFF
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Antonio Banderas To Star As Spanish Conquistador Hernán Cortés In Feature From Paul Mignot & Nicholas Kazan ‘FREEAgent:’ Streetwear Pioneer Jeff Staple Among First Guests On Season Two Of Kenny Annan-Jonathan’s Podcast James Gray Says He Considers ‘Two Lovers’ His First Successful Feature: “I Don’t Regard The Films I Made Before This Very Highly” View All October 12, 2026 8:39am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Clockwise from left: Barry Keoghan is Ringo Starr, Paul Mescal is Paul McCartney, Joseph Quinn is George Harrison and Harris Dickinson is John Lennon in Columbia Pictures 'The Beatles – A Four-Film Cinematic Event' Columbia Pictures “We’re on day 180 of the shoot today,” Pippa Harris , the producer behind Sam Mendes ’ The Beatles – A Four Film Cinematic Event, said with a pointed smile this afternoon during a career Q&A at the London Film Festival. “I stepped away for this hour and am going back afterwards. It is a big endeavour,” Harris continued before politely swerving specific questions about the films. Harris did, however, speak about the unique release strategy behind the films. All four of Mendes’ Beatles films will be released in cinemas in April 2028 in what Mendes described at CinemaCon 2025 as the first “bingeable moment in cinema.” Related Stories News Sam Mendes' Beatles Biopic Recreates 'Abbey Road' Album Cover In Behind-The-Scenes Video -- Watch Festivals 'Hamnet' & 'The Beatles' Producer Pippa Harris & 'The Zone Of Interest' Producer James Wilson To Headline LFF's Industry Forum “At the moment, the films will come out in 2028, and we want people to be able to experience them in the cinema at the same time, during the same period,” Harris told the audience at the LFF. Watch on Deadline “Now that doesn’t necessarily mean we’re thinking that people will go and see all four films on the same day. But within the same month, you might see one a week, or you might see one film one weekend and another the next. However you do it, we hope that people will see all four films.” Pippa Harris Photo by Leon Bennett/Getty Images. The Beatles – A Four Film Cinematic Event stars Joseph Quinn as George Harrison, Paul Mescal as Paul McCartney, Barry Keoghan as Ringo Starr, and Harris Dickinson as John Lennon. The films are essentially four separate theatrical biopic films about the iconic British quartet. “They stand alone as individual stories of each of those four men,” Harris said of the four films, “but they have a cumulative power, which I think is greater than the sum of the parts.” Harris added: “They are the greatest band in history, and we’re trying to do our best to do them justice. So hence the four films. I don’t think there’s probably another band that you could legitimately say you wanted to see four films about.” Mendes is directing from scripts written by Jez Butterworth, Peter Straughan and Jack Thorne. A collaboration between Sony Pictures Entertainment and Mendes’ Neal Street Productions, the films are being produced by Mendes, Harris and Julie Pastor of Neal Street, as well as Alexandra Derbyshire, in association with Apple Corps for Sony Pictures. This marks the first time that The Beatles and Apple Corps Ltd. have authorized the use of the band members’ life stories and music in scripted films. articles.title: Director Rory Kennedy On ‘The Trial Of Alec Baldwin,’ And Why ‘Rust’ Star At First Reacted Negatively To Her Film
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Bend Film Festival Prizes Go To ‘Hot Water,’ ‘Edward Said: Between Worlds,’ ‘Kikuyu Land,’ ‘The Lake’ & More ‘14th’ Review: Ava DuVernay’s Impassioned Defense Of Constitution Takes Aim At Trump & Attempted Rescission Of Rights Geeta Gandbhir, Sam Pollard, Alisa Payne Board ICE-Themed Oscar Contender ‘Water Cooler’ As EPs View All October 12, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Alec Baldwin in 'The Trial of Alec Baldwin' Moxie Films/Abramorama Mystery still surrounds the fatal shooting on the set of Alec Baldwin ’s Western Rust , an incident that claimed the life of cinematographer Halyna Hutchins. Did the actor pull the trigger on a prop gun as he rehearsed a scene (he denies that), or did the weapon malfunction and misfire? How did a live round get into the revolver and who brought the lethal ammunition to the set? Why were prosecutors in Santa Fe, NM so intent on charging Baldwin with a crime for what many impartial observers — though not all — saw as a tragic accident? The answers to some of those questions are provided in the new documentary The Trial of Alec Baldwin , directed by Rory Kennedy , which opens in Los Angeles on Friday. The film begins by dispelling one false rumor – that Baldwin initiated the project as some sort of attempt to repair his damaged reputation. Text on screen states flatly, “Baldwin was given no editorial control, nor did he provide any financial support or receive any compensation.” Related Stories News Alec Baldwin Joins Chris Hemsworth, Taron Egerton & Zazie Beetz In Matt Ross-Helmed ‘Kockroach’ News Halyna Hutchins’ Mother & Sister Encourage You To See ‘Rust’ Kennedy underscored that point at the Bend Film Festival in Oregon over the weekend, where the documentary played. At a Q&A that followed the screening, the Oscar-nominated filmmaker told the audience it wasn’t Baldwin who came up with the documentary idea, but the other way around. “I approached him,” she clarified. Watch on Deadline They had met many years before the Rust tragedy. “I have known Alec probably for 20 years,” Kennedy said. “I would say we were friends. We wouldn’t go out and have dinner, but I knew him. Alec is actually a great supporter of documentaries and is associated with the Hamptons Film Festival and also does a summer doc series. And so I’ve been lucky enough over the years to have a number of my films be a part of that. I’ve gotten to know him largely through that.” The documentary project began at a point when it didn’t appear the actor would face criminal allegations. Alec Baldwin in ‘Rust’ Rust Movie Productions LLC “When we entered this story,” Kennedy told the festival audience, “it really seemed like the Rust story was going to be resolved pretty early on and that [the documentary] was really going to be much more of a biopic with the Rust story interwoven maybe as a through line, kind of the backbone of it, but would be pretty thin. And then it just kept coming back and continuing. And we were always there when it had sort of dramatic turns.” Alec Baldwin hugs his attorney Alex Spiro at the conclusion of his trial for involuntary manslaughter in First Judicial District Court on July 12, 2024 in Santa Fe, New Mexico. Ramsay de Give-Pool/Getty Images Those dramatic turns included Baldwin and Rust armorer Hannah Gutierrez-Reed being charged in January 2023 with involuntary manslaughter. A few months later, the charges against Baldwin were dropped. But then in January 2024 a grand jury indicted Baldwin on felony involuntary manslaughter charges and special prosecutors re-filed their case. The prosecution of Baldwin, the film strongly suggests, had less to do with the evidence than with the special prosecutor’s personal animus toward him as a Hollywood star with a history of volcanic behavior. “It just seemed pretty clear that people were going after him and he was being taken to task [for the Rust shooting] in a way that seemed not entirely justified or fair,” Kennedy observed. “And then it started raising questions about how in this day and age with the internet and social media, we hold people to justice outside of the judicial system. Then as the film and the story unfolded, you started seeing how that narrative in social media started impacting the justice system.” Director Rory Kennedy at the Deadline Hollywood Portrait Studio during the 2026 Sundance Film Festival on January 25, 2026 in Park City, Utah. Josh Telles for Deadline Kennedy described the larger concerns raised by the Baldwin prosecution. “You start thinking, okay, how does this kind of [social media] chatter that we’re all doing… how is it affecting our larger institutions? How is it affecting government, for example? …How is it affecting the judicial system? I think it’s an important question that we should be observing and asking ourselves.” Baldwin, it becomes clear, was being tried twice – in the court of public opinion and in a court of law. The film builds to an astonishing crescendo, resulting in the case being dismissed in the middle of the trial (I won’t give away what happened. Close watchers of the case, including my colleague Dominic Patten who covered it for Deadline and appears as an expert in the documentary, know the ins and outs, but they came as a revelation to me). Hilaria Baldwin (R) speaks to her husband Alec Baldwin during his trial on involuntary manslaughter in First Judicial District Court on July 12, 2024 in Santa Fe, New Mexico. Ramsay de Give-Pool/Getty Images There would seem to be plenty for Baldwin to appreciate about Kennedy’s film, given how the court case ended. And yet… “When they [Baldwin and wife Hilaria] initially saw the film, they did not like the film,” the director reported. The cause of their displeasure has to do with scenes woven throughout that illustrate how Baldwin got his reputation for angry outbursts – confrontations with paparazzi through the years, for instance. Kennedy also explores a serious stain on Baldwin’s reputation from 2007 – the infamous voicemail he left for his then 11-year-old daughter Ireland in which he called her a “rude, thoughtless little pig.” That ugly lambasting came in the context of a bitter custody battle over Ireland between Baldwin and his ex-wife Kim Basinger. It’s a crucial piece of background because the special prosecutor referred to that incident in private communications in which she expressed loathing for the actor. “Because the prosecutors were, in my opinion, going after his reputation and not after what he did on the set,” Kennedy said, “we had to show what that reputation was, and we had to show it honestly.” A bit too honestly, perhaps, for Baldwin’s liking. “I think it was just very hard [for him] to see all that… showing his ex-wife in there and then [him wondering], ‘Why are we doing that?’ Well, the only way to really get to the voicemail is to understand that history, to understand what the motivation of the voicemail was. And you can’t get there without having that context.” Baldwin seems to be warming to the film, after hearing feedback from viewers. “I think he’s now come around and is much more supportive of it,” Kennedy noted. “I think there are a lot of people who say… this film is important and in many ways redeems him and also really helps people understand him and understand what he went through and understand the injustice of what happened to him.” ‘The Social Reckoning’ Bombs With $5.5M; ‘Other Mommy’ Rules Frame Catherine Laga’aia & Deacon Phillippe To Lead Disney+ Pilot ‘Spaceship Earth’ ‘Baywatch’ Team On Shooting In L.A.; Prime Swoops For Princess Diana Series 2026 Domestic B.O. articles.title: Netflix’s Bela Bajaria Has No Regrets Over Failed Warners Buy: “It Was Always A Nice To Have At A Certain Price”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max The BBC’s Content Chief Has A Message For Reality TV Snobs ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race UK All Stars’ Will Still Be Produced In Britain Once Show Leaves BBC ‘Baywatch’ Showrunner & Stars On “Reminding The Hollywood Community” Of The Power Of Shooting In Los Angeles & Casting TikTok Star Noah Beck: “There’s A Massive Responsibility When You Put On Those Red Shorts” View All October 12, 2026 9:03am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Bela Bajaria Jessica Chou/Netflix Bela Bajaria has moved on from Netflix ‘s failed attempt to buy Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD). As the ink dries on the Paramount -WBD deal, and the newly-minted Skydance plots its vision, the content chief backed up her boss Ted Sarandos in saying that WBD was “always a nice to have at a certain price, not a must have at any price.” Related Stories News Banijay Plots U.S. Expansion As Marco Bassetti Says ‘Peaky Blinders’ Maker Is Not “Jealous” Of Hollywood Studios News Netflix Eyes Major Layoffs – The Dish “We were never going to [spend over the odds],” she told an audience at MIPCOM . “We are financially disciplined. We knew what we had and what the opportunity was.” She was of course referring to Netflix’s eventually failed $83B bid to buy the storied studio , which ended up selling to David Ellison’s Paramount-Skydance for a far superior $110B , creating Skydance. Bajaria said Netflix is now focused instead on the goal of “keeping doing what we’re doing with the same investment, keeping our eye on the ball, making great things that people love around the world.” Watch on Deadline And there’s plenty of room still to grow, she added, pointing out that Netflix occupies around 5% of global audiences’ TV time, leaving a huge slice of the pie. Bajaria was in Cannes talking up Netflix’s global strategy, which goes well beyond huge hits like La Casa de Papel and Squid Game. “There are so many of these titles that go all around the world,” she added, pointing out that Canadian original Below is currently number one in more than 80 countries including France. Bajaria didn’t address the reported layoffs taking place at the streamer but said Netflix will continue to “expand,” something it has always done despite opposing moves from the competition. “When others have scaled back at different times we have continued to be consistent and grow our investment and expand what we do,” she added. “For me that is the most important thing.” She was also robust in responding to the notion that there is too much content out there. “We can see on Netflix our members watch a lot and they have lots of different moods and tastes,” she added. “We don’t programme for a narrow demographic. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Patrick Hipes Patrick Hipes Executive Managing Editor More Stories By Patrick Sony’s Screen Gems Sets YouTube Exec Fede Goldenberg To Top Genre Label; Ashley Brucks Segues To Producer Role Taylor Swift To Perform At Academy Museum Gala This Month In L.A. ‘Michael’ & ‘Friday’ Sequels Among Films To Get California Tax Credits In Latest Funding Round View All October 12, 2026 9:20am Add us as a Google Preferred Source UPDATED, 9:20 AM: Apple Original Films has released the first extended trailer for Being Heumann , the new film from Oscar-winning CODA filmmaker Siân Heder. Watch it above, and see the first-look teaser below. Apple Original Films on Wednesday released a teaser trailer for Being Heumann , the new film from Oscar-winning CODA filmmaker Siân Heder that is gearing up for its world premiere next week as the opening film of the Toronto Film Festival . Related Stories Festivals TIFF’s 51st Edition Sets Siân Heder’s ‘Being Heumann’ As Opening-Night Film Casting Mark Ruffalo To Star In Apple’s ‘Being Heumann’ From ‘CODA’ Director Siân Heder The film tells the true story of disability-rights advocate Judy Heumann, played by Doctor Who alum Ruth Madeley . Based on Heumann’s memoir, it centers on the year 1977, when Heumann led more than 100 disabled people to take over the San Francisco Federal Building, kicking off a 28 day sit-in — the longest occupation of a federal building in U.S. history. Watch on Deadline The protesters form a tightly bound community, refusing to leave until the government enforces section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, which required all federal spaces to become accessible. Mark Ruffalo plays the bureaucrat who stands in the protesters’ way. Dylan O’Brien, Jon Beavers, Rob Delaney and Ray Fisher also star in the pic, which will debut in select theaters November 6 before dropping on Apple TV on November 13.

articles.title: Sean Combs Injured In Prison; Release Date Pushed Back Again Amid Controversies & Violations

Amidst tales of high-living indulgences , contraband and other luxuries behind bars at FCI Fort Dix, the much-accused Bad Boy Records founder has seen his release date pushed back by almost two more months. With a release date that has gone up and down literally since Diddy was sentenced in September 2025 to a 50-month stint (with time served) after being convicted of two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution by a NYC jury in July 2025, the Grammy winner most recently was set to get out on January 21, 2028. A bounty placed on his head threatens his existence lying low and sends him on the run with the mysterious Thomas Shepherd (Ruaridh Mollica), who might be Vision’s son reincarnate and brother to Joe Locke’s Billy Maximoff, formerly Billy Kaplan. Vision must get to the root of Thomas’ identity while resisting Ultron’s influence, evading capture and confronting his true nature. Who is in the cast of VisionQuest ?
