articles.title: Faith & Family Outfit Ark Clb Launches With Former eOne Exec
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Craig Ferguson & Megyn Price Starring In Addiction Dramedy Series ‘Quitters’ For Angel Faith & Family Outfit Ark Clb Launches With Former eOne Exec Venice Winner ‘A Day In The Life Of Jo: Chapter Phaedra’ Gets North American Deal With 1-2 Special View All October 9, 2026 7:48am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Greg Maurice and Stephon Chaney Jael Pertigrew EXCLUSIVE : Greg Maurice, who has worked at 1091 Pictures, eOne and Fox Sports, has teamed up with pastor Stephon Chaney to launch Ark Clb , a media company aimed at acquiring, financing, producing and distributing films and TV in the faith and family space. The company will be based in Atlanta and Los Angeles. Maurice has acquired for online platform Filmhub for two years and previously served as Senior Director, Global Acquisitions & Co-Productions for 1091 between 2020-2024, and Director of Marketing & Acquisitions at Entertainment One between 2012-2018. He was a Content Director at Fox Sports between 2010-2011. Related Stories News ASOB Media Offers MIPCOM Buyers 'A Study On Beauty' News Robby Hoffman Sets Second Netflix Special “I’ve spent much of my career sitting between filmmakers and studios, and I’ve seen extraordinary stories struggle not because the audience wasn’t there, but because the infrastructure and advocacy weren’t,” Maurice said. “Ark is about changing that. We want to combine commercial discipline with purpose, finding stories that can perform in the marketplace while giving audiences something meaningful to carry with them after the credits.” Watch on Deadline According to Maurice, the company won’t only work in faith-based film and TV but will work on stories “rooted in redemption, resilience, family, forgiveness, purpose and hope stories designed to connect with audiences grounded in Kingdom values.” Chaney serves as Co-Founder and Head of Strategic Partnerships at Ark Clb. He has previously worked at Salesforce, BetterUp and Thrive Global before transitioning into full-time ministry in Atlanta, Georgia. He explained about the company: “In today’s information age, families in the faith community are increasingly intentional about what they allow into their homes. Finding entertainment that is both compelling and appropriate for the entire family has become more difficult than ever. But people shouldn’t have to choose between exceptional storytelling and values they can trust. At Ark Clb, we’re committed to filling that void by offering premium entertainment that is inspiring, culturally relevant, and appropriate for the entire family.” Maurice added: “The most valuable asset I’ve built isn’t a catalog of films or licensing deals, it’s trust. Trust from filmmakers who believed I’d fight for their stories. Trust from buyers who knew I’d bring them quality content. Ark Clb exists to protect that trust every day. Integrity isn’t just good ethics, it’s good business, and it’s the foundation for every relationship we build.” Netflix Eyes Major Layoffs; Would Be First Big Staff Reduction Since 2022 Int’l Boss Gerhard Zeiler Exits; Zaslav Cashes In; TCM To Film Group; Latest Skydance UK Network 5’s Profits Slump Amid Streaming Investment HBO Orders ‘Crazy Rich Asians’ Series From Adele Lim, Jon M. They join the previously announced Emilia Jones, Jessica Chastain, Amy Ryan, Fabien Frankel, and Will Harrison. Inspired by the Peabody Award-winning New York Times podcast by Susan Burton, The Retrievals follows an unlikely community of IVF patients who come together to crusade against Yale University after they are operated on without anesthesia–because a nurse stole their fentanyl. The Retrievals is a powerful call to justice and a surprisingly moving story of friendship and perseverance. Related Stories News Robby Hoffman Sets Second Netflix Special News Netflix Eyes Major Layoffs - The Dish Moayed will play Amir, Kaitlyn’s (Chastain) husband and biggest champion throughout their harrowing experience with IVF at Yale. Watch on Deadline Walker will play Bella, Ian’s (Frankel) teenage daughter who becomes Gabby’s (Jones) impromptu roommate, beauty consultant, and confidante. Oduye will play Nurse Sam, a registered nurse who has worked at the Yale Fertility Clinic for over a decade. As a close friend of Carla Russo (Ryan), Sam was blindsided by Carla’s arrest (and drug addiction). Oh will play a fellow student-teacher at Gabby’s elementary school who proves to be a true friend to Gabby. Metzler is showrunner, writer and executive producer for The Retrievals , which is produced by LuckyChap and her Quiet Coyote. articles.title: Geeta Gandbhir, Sam Pollard, Alisa Payne Board ICE-Themed Oscar Contender ‘Water Cooler’ As EPs
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew IDFA Announces Forum Lineup: Projects From Wang Bing, Rachael Leah Jones, Vitaly Mansky, Juanjo Pereira, Liang Zhao & More Lightdox Acquires Sales Rights To ‘Nostalgia For The Future,’ Documentary On Enigmatic Filmmaker Chris Marker Narrated By Charlotte Rampling ‘Ash And Crayons’ Trailer: In Evgeny Afineevsky’s Film, Wounded Ukrainian Children Show Will To Survive And Thrive View All October 9, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source A masked ICE agent in 'Water Cooler' Spoonbill Stories/Message Pictures EXCLUSIVE: Academy Award nominees Geeta Gandbhir , Sam Pollard , and Alisa Payne are joining the Oscar-contending short documentary Water Cooler as executive producers. Emma V.F. directed the film, which she shot in the corridors of immigration court at Federal Plaza in New York City. Filming openly, V.F. captured scenes of jarring contrast: ICE agents engaged in mundane “water cooler” talk and then those same agents seizing migrants in the hallways who were following proper procedures to seek legal status in the U.S. At one moment, the agents – most of them masked – would be talking amongst themselves about shopping for Black Friday deals, for instance, or the latest taser models. The next moment, they were forcibly detaining someone who had showed up to immigration court little expecting to be grabbed before they walked into court. Related Stories News London Film Festival: Sam Pollard To Lead Official Competition Jury News Sports & News/Doc Emmys Set 2026 Lifetime Achievement Award Recipients; 'Have I Got News For You' Trio To Host Ceremonies A masked ICE agent in ‘Water Cooler’ Spoonbill Stories/Message Pictures “The observational documentary — which [V.F.] filmed from November 2025 through January 2026 — juxtaposes agents’ casual conversations with tense scenes of the agents arresting immigrants who attended required court hearings to seek legal status,” notes a description. Water Cooler won Best Documentary Short at Palm Springs International ShortFest 2026, qualifying the film for Oscar consideration. “ Water Cooler is an urgent documentary short that sends a powerful message about a defining issue of our time,” said Pollard ( MLK/FBI , Tutu ). “America is at a tipping point with ICE and their outrageous incursions into our cities, which is why films like this are so important.” Gandbhir ( The Perfect Neighbor , The Devil Is Busy ), observed, “Emma V.F.’s film Water Cooler honors the direct cinema style pioneered by Bob Drew and D. A. Pennebaker while turning her lens on masked federal agents. Even in a short runtime, it does what the films of those pioneers did — immerses you in a world that is crucial to see for yourself.” Masked ICE agents confer in ‘Water Cooler’ Spoonbill Stories/Message Pictures Water Cooler screens on Saturday at the Hamptons International Film Festival in New York, on Sunday, October 18 at the Woodstock Film Festival in New York, and on October 24 at AFI Fest in Los Angeles. Next month, it’s programmed at the St. Louis International Film Festival. In addition to Palm Springs International ShortFest, the documentary has screened at DC/DOX in the nation’s capital. The documentary is a production of Spoonbill Stories and Message Pictures , the latter a company founded by Gandbhir, Pollard, and Payne (Payne earned an Oscar nomination earlier this year for producing The Perfect Neighbor ). Water Cooler is directed, produced, filmed and edited by Emma V.F. Along with Gandbhir, Pollard, and Payne, Blair Foster ( Marty, Life is Short ; Taxi to the Darkside ) serves as an executive producer. Robert Aiki Aubrey Lowe ( Seeds , Union , Power ) composed the original score. V.F. directed the 2023 documentary feature Queen of New York . Her producing credits include In the Same Breath (HBO); Silver Dollar Road (Amazon Studios); Take Your Pills: Xanax (Netflix) and Once Upon a Time in Uganda . “As the granddaughter of Italian immigrants and Jewish New Yorkers who would be outraged to see masked federal agents disappearing law-abiding people down stairwells in their city, I knew this was a film I needed to make,” Emma V.F. said in a statement. “I’m thrilled to partner with Message Pictures to share the film more widely in hopes that it inspires collective action opposing ICE.” Watch a teaser-trailer for Water Cooler here: Netflix Eyes Major Layoffs; Would Be First Big Staff Reduction Since 2022 Int’l Boss Gerhard Zeiler Exits; Zaslav Cashes In; TCM To Film Group; Latest Skydance UK Network 5’s Profits Slump Amid Streaming Investment HBO Orders ‘Crazy Rich Asians’ Series From Adele Lim, Jon M. articles.title: Sarah Snook & ‘Game Of Thrones’ Stars Shows Adapted As Microdramas For Snips
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Sarah Snook & ‘Game Of Thrones’ Stars Shows Adapted As Microdramas For Snips ASOB Media Offers MIPCOM Buyers ‘A Study On Beauty’ Icelandic Drama ‘Elma’ Set For Siminn Bow As Glassriver Debuts ‘NCU’ At MIPCOM View All October 9, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Snips Snips EXCLUSIVE: Succession star Sarah Snook and Game of Thrones actors Maisie Williams , Liam Cunningham, Iain Glen and Kit Harington are making their microdrama debuts. Vertical video platform Snips is adapting series that each actor or actress has starred in for the new medium, as the platform continues to seek films and TV shows to repurpose in 9:16 ratio. The show are Australian drama The Beautiful Lie , an ABC series starring Snook; Sky dark comedy Two Weeks to Live , starring Williams and Sian Clifford ( Ludwig ); Rome drama Domina , starring Cunningham; BBC drama Prisoners’ Wives , starring Glen, and BBC and HBO co-production Gunpowder , starring Harrington. Related Stories News PBS Masterpiece's 'Maigret' Finds UK Home News Alternativa Distribution Takes 'No Good Men' & 'Four Daughters' To MIPCOM Each show will be transformed from its full-length format into 45-second to two-minute episodes. Watch on Deadline The Beautiful Lie debuted on ABC in Australia in 2017 as a modern reimagining of Tolstoy’s Anna Karenina , with Snook (known best as Succession ‘s Shiv Roy) playing a retired tennis champion married to another tennis legend, who flies home to help her brother’s crumbling marriage, only to meet and feel an instant attraction to a charismatic music producer – who happens to be the brother of her sister-in-law. Two Weeks to Live debuted on Sky in the UK in 2020, and follows Williams as a young woman on a secret mission to avenge her father’s mysterious death when she was a child, who along with her mother joins a pair of socially awkward brothers and goes on the run from murderous gangsters and the police. It was Williams’ first lead role after her run as Arya Stark in GOT . Domina , another Sky show, debuted in 2021, when Cunningham playing the father of young Livia Drusilla (Kasia Smutniak), whose lose of her family sets her on a path to seizing power in Rome. Isabella Rossellini and Claire Forlani joined Cunningham, who played Ser Davos Seaworth in GOT . Glen stars in Prisoners’ Wives , a two-season BBC drama from the early 2010s. The show follows the wives, girlfriends and partners of prisoners, with Glen playing a career criminal whose lavish lifestyle is running out, along with his money. Polly Walker ( Rome ); another GOT star, David Bradley; and a yyoung Phoebe Dyvenor ( Bridgerton ) also had roles in an ensemble cast. Gunpowder , a miniseries from 2017, was set in 1603 with Harington playing Robert Catesby, a charismatic Catholic nobleman, who decides to blow up the Houses of Parliament with the King inside. Harington who starred as Jon Snow in GOT , is a real-life descendant of Catesby, and lead a cast also including Liv Tyler ( The Lord of the Rings ), Mark Gatiss ( Sherlock ) and Peter Mullan ( My Name is Joe ). Snips model Snips has sought to set itself apart from other microdrama apps by focusing on repurposing existing shows and films for the vertical space, rather than making its own originals. “Viewing habits are changing, and people’s preferences are changing with them,” said Or Ben Shimon, co-founder and CEO of Snips. “That shift is exactly why the micro-drama industry has exploded the way it has. Now we’re seeing big-name actors get into the space, and that tells you everything about where this format is headed. We believe good shows are like music — they just need to be on the most modern format.” Snips has been offering rights owners a revenue-share model that allows earnings to grow based on performance over the more traditional flat license fee agreement. Shimon believes this gives actors a direct stake in their titles’ performance, incentivizing them to promote the work to fans and followers. Shimon is set to hit MIPCOM Cannes next week, meeting with sellers and content owners to acquire more titles for adaptation. articles.title: International Insider: ‘Doctor Who’ Regeneration Underway; MIPCOM Preview; Busan Takeaways
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse ASOB Media Offers MIPCOM Buyers ‘A Study On Beauty’ Icelandic Drama ‘Elma’ Set For Siminn Bow As Glassriver Debuts ‘NCU’ At MIPCOM Reelz To Follow The CW’s ‘Police 24/7’; Sky Remains On The Case For Season 3 View All October 9, 2026 8:05am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The 15th Doctor regenerates into Billie Piper on 'Doctor Who' Disney+ Don’t blink, Insiders. Jesse Whittock is here with you in the week Skydance took over Warner Bros. Discovery and Doctor Who began planning for the future. Here we go. Ready? ‘Doctor Who’ Regeneration Underway David Tennant in ‘Doctor Who’ BBC Studios Sonic screwdrivers at the ready: Stories about the Good Doctor with a question mark for a real name always do well on Deadline, and so it proved again with Jake and Max’s top scoop on the latest regeneration of the British sci-fi franchise. After the recent Russell T. Davies seasons were not brilliantly received by fans, Disney exited the show and rights owner BBC Studios (BBCS) put its future out to tender, asking the UK production community for their visions of a reimagined Doctor Who . One eye-catching bid in the “bake-off-style” process saw Line of Duty creator Jed Mercurio and his Hat Trick Mercurio indie throw its hat in the ring. Elsewhere, Line of Duty maker World Productions is down as is Criminal Record ‘s STV Studios, along with a pair of unnamed BBCS-owned labels , proving that while the show has become divisive and a difficult beast to tame, there will always be love for The Doc on British shores. Each producer sees a different future, with STV Studios’ plan being to move production north of the English border into Scotland for the first time in the franchise’s history. The deadline for pitches has now passed and our list isn’t exhaustive – another Scottish bid is rumored, for example. A24 UK, Playground, Mammoth Screen, New Pictures, Big Talk Studios, Expectation and Quay Street have, however, counted themselves out. The new series will premiere on BBC screens during the 2028/29 season, with the winner of the pitch selected in March. For the BBC, the news came in the same week that Director General Matt Brittin urged his staff to channel Elvis, i.e. “a little less conversation, a little more action.” Brittin wants the British public broadcaster to move faster, try more things and hone specialisms quicker. How it does that in a world of declining funding and ultra-competition isn’t clear. As some pretty snarky below-the-line comments on Jake’s scoop revealed, some aren’t convinced. “Be more Elvis, you mean, dead?” read one stinging post. Ouch. With Brittin also telling staff he’s been meeting U.S. streamers, it’s been another intriguing week at the BBC. Related Stories News ASOB Media Offers MIPCOM Buyers 'A Study On Beauty' News Icelandic Drama 'Elma' Set For Siminn Bow As Glassriver Debuts 'NCU' At MIPCOM MIPCOM Preview VALERY HACHE/AFP via Getty Images Croisetting the scene: As you read this, plenty of creatives, sellers and execs will be jumping on planes to Nice Airport for this year’s MIPCOM Cannes , which officially starts Monday. For me, it will be the 4,253,749th MIP in a row. The French event will be seeking to burnish its reputation as international TV’s biggest annual market and conference, and to do that, it needs the best new shows. This week, we dropped our latest Deadline Dozen run downs of the major titles launching at MIPCOM – and you can read about the unscripted 12 here and the scripted batch here . We’ve been ramping up coverage over the last few weeks and will be out in Cannes in force, scribbling up breaking news stories from keynotes and the Croisette, and on stage at several high-profile events and screenings. You’ll be able to read all the coverage by following this MIPCOM link (plenty of scoops there already), but for now, enjoy an interview with Banijay Deputy CEO Jane Turton , another with the bosses at Heated Rivalry streamer Crave and this chat with the producers of buzzy Princess Diana doc Diana Unheard. Watch on Deadline The Deadline Interview: Vikram Malhotra ‘Subedaar’, ‘Maa Behen’ and ‘Daldal’ Vikram Malhotra (inset) Netflix/Prime Video/Abundandia Entertainment For all the talk of AI use, whether the U.S. studios are secretly using it to cut production costs or if Tilly Norwood will ever win an Oscar, there are surprisingly few legacy players who have opened AI-led studios. Vikram Malhotra from India’s Abundantia Entertainment , is one of those few. In our exclusive interview, he explains how staying ahead of the curve means putting his money where his mouth is on “human-first and AI-empowered” creative arm Abundantia AiOn. In 2027, he reveals, this will become a “fully fledged, fully native” standalone AI studio. What does that mean exactly? Click through to find out, along with insights into how Malhotra tempted Anil Kapoor back into an action movie lead and how the market is changing before our eyes. >>> Read the Interview Based In Busan Woohae Cho/Getty Images Korea prospects: Liz Shackleton was in Korea for the Busan International Film Festival (the fantastically-acronymed BIFF) this week, where she heard from the likes of Michelle Yeoh, Maggie Gyllenhaal and Alfonso and Jonas Cuaron, along with Chinese director and Busan jury president Zhang Yimou and fest director Jung Hanseok. Everything Everywhere All at Once star Yeoh, in town for the first time in 15 years to receive an Asian Filmmaker of the Year award, told a press conference about her experiences making Prime Video series Blade Runner 2099 and returning to Asian cinema. The likes of Fan Bingbing and Charlotte Gainsbourg hit the red carpet, along with the stars of The Table: Day and Night , the festival’s opening night screening, who you can see above. All your BIFF needs are here . articles.title: Craig Ferguson & Megyn Price Starring In Addiction Dramedy Series ‘Quitters’ For Angel
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Craig Ferguson & Megyn Price Starring In Addiction Dramedy Series ‘Quitters’ For Angel Faith & Family Outfit Ark Clb Launches With Former eOne Exec Venice Winner ‘A Day In The Life Of Jo: Chapter Phaedra’ Gets North American Deal With 1-2 Special View All October 9, 2026 8:08am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Craig Ferguson & Megyn Price Ian Cunningham/Courtesy EXCLUSIVE : Former late-night host Craig Ferguson ( The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson ) and The Ranch and Rules Of Engagement star Megyn Price have been set to star in Quitters , a half-hour dramedy series whose eight-episode first season is now in production in Utah. The series will be distributed by Angel , the distributor-producer best known for its faith-leaning content. The synopsis reads: “After Liza (Price), an upbeat soccer mom, falls into the cycle of opioid addiction, she lands at Unplugged, an unconventional recovery center run by Nick McTavers (Ferguson), a former heavy-metal legend. To put her life back on track, Liza must learn to rely on an eclectic family of patients and counselors who help her navigate the long road of recovery.” Related Stories Acquisitions Angel Acquires Michael Keaton-Morgan Freeman Western 'Rode To Ruin', Launches Sales Arm Ahead Of TIFF Market News State Department To Screen 'Young Washington' At U.S. Embassies Producers are Eric Handler, Chase Vergari and Ibrahim Mohammed. It is being directed by Darrin “Fletch” Fletcher and Chet Thomas and produced through their FletChet Entertainment banner, which recently produced the Lionsgate title The Best Christmas Pageant Ever. Quitters was written and created by Dave Parkin. Watch on Deadline Executive producers on the series include Chet Thomas, Darrin Fletcher, Eric Handler, Chase Vergari, Ibrahim Mohammed, series writer and creator Dave Parkin, RoboCop and Starship Troopers writer Edward Neumeier, Rob Gibbs, HR Brown and Alema Harrington. Handler brought the package together and paired it with financing from Script 2 Screen Capital. Handler most recently served as executive producer on the Walton Goggins action-comedy Mister , the Samuel L. Jackson action film The Beast , and Maserati: The Brothers , starring Anthony Hopkins and Al Pacino. Vergari and Mohammed produce and finance through Script 2 Screen Capital, whose credits include By Any Means (Paramount Pictures), starring Mark Wahlberg, and Iconoclast , which premiered at the 2026 Tribeca Film Festival. “This is a world I have wanted to explore for as long as I can remember, and Nick McTavers is a character I understand in my bones. There is real truth in this story, and a lot of heart and humor too, and that is exactly the kind of thing I want to be making,” commented How To Train Your Dragon voice star Ferguson who has previously discussed his own addiction issues in his late 20s. “I’m so grateful for the opportunity to help tell Liza’s story. She’s funny and stubborn and heartbreakingly human, and her struggles through addiction and recovery are shared by so many people. My goal is to shed some light, hope and humor onto this issue, and remove the shame that acts as a barrier to asking for help,” added Megyn Price. “Ten years ago, HR and Alema, who have walked the road of addiction and recovery themselves, brought us this idea. Having Craig and Megyn lead the series now is the culmination of everything we’ve worked toward,” said Darrin Fletcher. Chet Thomas commented: “We want anyone struggling with addiction to know help is out there, and their families to understand what their loved ones are facing. We tell that story honestly but with the humor that so often keeps the people going through it alive.” “Nobody could play Nick McTavers the way Craig Ferguson does, and Megyn is going to break your heart and make you laugh in the same scene. I go back decades with Chet, from our DreamWorks days, and with Craig too, so having them both come together on a show that inspires hope means everything,” said producer Eric Handler. Angel’s slate of original series also includes the post-apocalyptic drama Homestead: The Series , now in its second season. Ferguson is represented by WME, Vault Entertainment, and Gang, Tyre. Price is represented by Independent Artist Group, Leslie Allan-Rice Management, and Myman Greenspan. articles.title: Court TV Parent Law & Crime Ups Rachel Stockman To CEO; Founder Dan Abrams To Remain As Chairman
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Skydance Shares Rebound After David Ellison And Top Execs Ring Opening Bell At New York Stock Exchange Joe Rogan Sets Multi-Year Extension With Spotify Eyeing More ‘Minecrafts’ And ‘Fallouts’, Microsoft Xbox Launches XP Unit To Take Properties Beyond Video Games View All October 9, 2026 8:17am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Rachel Stockman, CEO of Law & Crime and Court TV Courtesy Rachel Stockman , longtime president of Court TV parent Law & Crime, is becoming CEO of the company as founder Dan Abrams steps down from the role. Abrams, chief legal analyst for ABC News, is staying on as chairman of Law & Crime. The company has been owned since 2023 by Jellysmack , a holding company for creator-led media businesses. Court TV, a digitally focused revival of the longtime cable TV mainstay known for gavel-to-gavel trial coverage, was sold by E.W. Scripps to Law & Crime earlier this year. Related Stories Executives Paramount-WBD Deal Architect Gerry Cardinale Says Most Of $6B In Expected Cost Savings Will Not Be From Layoffs Executives Ex-Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz In Line For High-Level Paramount Exec Post Stockman has been at Law & Crime for more than a decade, initially serving as editor-in-chief before a promotion to president. Along the way, she has also executive produced dozens of documentaries and series for Netflix, Paramount+, A&E, Fox Nation and HBO Max/ID. Earlier this fall, she oversaw the launch of “Partners in Crime,” a programming initiative featuring six original series developed with some of true crime’s most-followed creators. Watch on Deadline After spearheading the acquisition of Court TV, Stockman has built Law & Crime into a top true-crime brand. It operates four FAST channels and multiple subscription channels on YouTube, which have collectively generated billions of video views and more than 700 million hours watched across platforms over the past year, according to the company. “Rachel’s ability to direct the business at the highest level while also making so many smart, granular decisions has helped lead us to where we are today,” Abrams said in a statement. “She has truly earned this. I can’t wait to see where she takes us next.” Stockman praised the “extraordinary team” at Law & Crime. “I’m honored to lead this next chapter as we continue to push boundaries, embrace bold ideas and help shape the future of media,” she said. articles.title: Danny Boyle Says ‘28 Years Later: Part III’ Is Currently On The “Back Burner”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Danny Boyle Says ‘28 Years Later: Part III’ Is Currently On The “Back Burner” TIFF Lightbox Sets Animation Season Guest Curated By Masaaki Yuasa Grace Harper Brighouse On Bringing Her Camden Film Festival-Winning Doc ‘Dependence’ Back Home To London — LFF View All October 9, 2026 8:20am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ralph Fiennes in '28 Years Later: The Bone Temple' Miya Mizuno/Sony “It’s on the back burner at the moment,” Danny Boyle concluded this afternoon during a Q&A at the London Film Festival when asked about the current status of 28 Years Later: Part III . The veteran British filmmaker continued to say he “hopes” the film will be made if financing can be locked in. Boyle added that the pause in the film series has also been prompted by Alex Garland’s busy schedule. “Alex has been off doing his own film, which is a huge project,” Boyle said. Alex Garland is currently working on A24’s big-screen adaptation of the hit video game Elden Ring. Related Stories News 'NAZA' Producer James Wilson Addresses "Hysterical, Vituperative" Israeli Government Backlash Against Directors News Grace Harper Brighouse On Bringing Her Camden Film Festival-Winning Doc 'Dependence' Back Home To London -- LFF Boyle is at the LFF this year with his latest feature Ink , which screens as one of the festival’s headline galas. Directed by Boyle from a screenplay written by James Graham (Dear England), the film charts the rise of the UK’s notorious tabloid newspaper The Sun in the 1970s under the editorship of Larry Lamb, after he was poached from the Daily Mirror in 1969 by then budding media mogul Rupert Murdoch. Watch on Deadline Boyle told the LFF crowd that he and his producing team felt specific “pressures” while trying to finance Ink. “We found it very difficult to raise the money for this,” Boyle said. “I have no idea why. They didn’t say why they wouldn’t give us the money. We managed to get the money from StudioCanal. They didn’t give us enough money, but they were brave, whereas a lot of people wouldn’t give us the money.” Boyle said his personal theory about why StudioCanal coughed up the money for Ink is because his producer, Tessa Ross, previously worked on the box office hit Conclave with the company. “She’d made them so much money,” Boyle said, adding he was very lucky that “StudioCanal hooked up with Netflix and they bought it for America. They’ve been really good partners because there have been pressures.” Boyle said he will next work on an Antarctica-set film if he can raise the budget. “That’s the next priority,” he said. The LFF runs until October 18. articles.title: Focus Features & Blumhouse-Atomic Monster Snap Up Micro-Budget Horror Film ‘Play House’ From Nicolas Curcio
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Robby Hoffman Sets Second Netflix Special Paramount Teaming With Medieval Times On Family Comedy Movie; Eric Appel Directing From Script By Blaise Hemingway Paul Walter Hauser Set For Crime Drama ‘Garden City’ From John Curran, Magenta Light Studios View All October 9, 2026 8:31am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Nicolas Curcio Gilbert Flores/Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: Focus Features and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster have snapped up Play House , a micro-budget horror film from Nicolas Curcio , in a competitive situation, sources tell Deadline. We’re told this was a seven-figure deal for worldwide rights, excluding Latin America and India. This is a major coup for Curcio’s debut feature, a film made for not much more than $100,000 — roughly 13% of the reported budget of Curry Barker’s low-budget Focus phenomenon Obsession . Related Stories News Top 50 Halloween Movies Photo Gallery: Creepy Classics From ‘Psycho,’ ‘The Shining’ To ‘Obsession’ & ‘Get Out’ News Horror Movies’ Next Wave: What’s Coming In 2026, From Auteur Nightmares To Indie Breakouts Curcio set the project in motion last September after winning the inaugural Fantastic Pitches contest, a micro-budget genre initiative spearheaded by Alamo Drafthouse’s Fantastic Fest and indie studio Chroma, thereby securing funding and distribution. He returned to Fantastic Fest to premiere the film last month. Play House will release in theaters in 2027, with Universal Pictures International handling international distribution. Watch on Deadline Written by Curcio and wife/creative partner Kirby Gladstein, the film follows Elliott (Will Harrison), who while renovating a dilapidated house to win back his ex, discovers VHS tapes of an unaired children’s TV show which begins to seep into his life, threatening his last chance at reconciliation. Pic’s cast also includes Jessica Sula, Jordan Gonzalez, and James Urbaniak. Curcio and Gladstein produced for Skinny Ghost, alongside Ben Gojer, Jack Forbes, and Derek Tramont. Exec producers include Ahbra Perry via Chroma, Daniel Levin via Narrative, Adam Hendricks and Greg Gilreath of Divide/Conquer, and Jason Blum of Blumhouse Atomic-Monster. NPerry repped the film for sales via Narrative Distribution. While Universal art-house label Focus Features has not historically been known as a major horror distributor, outside of recent work with Robert Eggers on titles like Nosferatu and the upcoming Werwulf , they’re now aggressively expanding into the space as supporters of emerging filmmakers, after seeing Obsession break out as their highest-grossing film ever at over $522M worldwide. Divide/Conquer’s Hendricks and Gilreath — EPs on Play House — previously brought that film to Blum, who set it up at Focus, along with his follow-up Anything but Ghosts , dated for May 7, 2027. You can expect much more to come from the collaboration between Focus Features and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster. Most recently, they announced their partnership on director Josh Giuliano’s Occupant following the buzzy TIFF debut of his first horror film, River . Curcio is a rising filmmaker who recently set up his high-concept thriller spec Sweet Spot , penned with Gladstein, at Paramount Primal, as we first reported. A writer on Sony Pictures Animation’s hit GOAT , he has developed projects for multiple studios, including a live-action Magic School Bus for Universal and an adaptation of Planet of the Nerds for Paramount. His script Barron made the Black List in 2019. Curcio is also known for running a popular screenwriting TikTok account with nearly 200K followers and over 10M likes, and has partnered with studios like Neon, A24 and Paramount to promote films. He is repped by 3 Arts, UTA, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman. articles.title: Netflix’s ‘Little House On The Prairie’ Season 2 Casts Peter Ingalls, Mrs. Nelson & More As Production Wraps
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi Owen Wilson’s Pryce Cahill Makes Play At U.S. Open In ‘Stick’ Season 2 Trailer All The Songs In ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 So Far ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 Finale Recap: The Last Match Of The Season & A Shareholders’ Showdown View All October 9, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Clockwise from top left: David Wronko, Elyse Levesque, Erik Althavale, Graham Harvey, Jacinta Forest Lewitski, Lyla Porter-Follows, Martin Roach, Paul Greene, Ryan Northcott and Scott Porter Cameron Radice/Jenna Berman/Kevin McIntyre/Monica Gosselin/Benjamin Laird/Sarah Jane Murray/Time Leyes/Laurent Levy/Kevin Clarke/Malik Daniels The second season of Netflix ’s Little House on the Prairie reimagining has rounded out its ensemble cast with a wrap on production. Ten names have boarded Season 2: David Wronko , Erik Athaval ( American Hostage ), Elyse Levesque ( Ready or Not, Orphan Black ), Graham Harvey ( The Night Agent ), Jacinta Forest Lewitski , Lyla Porter-Follows ( High Potential ), Martin Roach ( Cross ), Paul Greene ( When Calls The Heart, Autumn and the Black Jaguar ), Ryan Northcott ( Anna Pigeon) and Scott Porter ( Ginny & Georgia, Friday Night Lights, Hart of Dixie ). Related Stories Casting Rachelle Lefevre & Charlotte Sullivan Join ‘Little House On The Prairie’ Season 2 At Netflix Books Everything We Know About Netflix’s ‘Little House On The Prairie’ Season 2 So Far Athavale will portray energetic minister Reverend Alden, who leads Walnut Grove’s Congregational church. Levesque will play Emma Perry, wife of Luther Perry and mother to Maud and Thomas, who secretly calls the shots for her husband’s business. Harvey will play Johnny Johnson, son of Norwegian immigrants and farm boy who has never attended school. Lewitski will play Hannah Walker, Lena Nelson’s farm manager, who is part Dakota and plays first base for the Prairie Clippers. Porter Follows will portray Mrs. Lena Nelson, an outspoken young widow in charge of the farm her husband left behind. Watch on Deadline Roach will portray civil war veteran Simon Hughes, a widower who owns the Blacksmith Shop. Greene will play Luther Perry, husband to Emma Perry and father of Thomas and Maud. Luther is a grain buyer and town baker who poses a threat to the farmers. Northcott will play William Oleson, husband to Margaret Oleson (Charlotte Sullivan) and father to Nellie Oleson (Willa Dunn). And, last but not least, Porter will portray Uncle Peter, older brother to Charles aka “Pa” Ingalls (Luke Bracey) All but Porter’s are recurring guest stars. Uncle Peter is a guest star role in the second season. L-R: Skywalker Hughes as Mary Ingalls, Alice Halsey as Laura Ingalls behind the scenes of episode 207 of ‘Little House on the Prairie’ Eric Zachanowich/Netflix In On the Banks of Plum Creek , Mrs. Nelson is married to a Mr. Nelson, and both are Norwegian neighbors to the Ingalls in their new home in Minnesota. They share a daughter named Anna. Pa also works for Mr. Nelson in Laura Ingalls Wilder’s novel. Mixing hopeful family drama and survival tale suspense, Little House on the Prairie tells the story of one family’s adventure and origin story settling the American West. It is based on Wilder’s semi-autobiographical book series. Rebecca Sonnenshine ( The Boys, Vampire Diaries, Archive 81) serves as showrunner and executive producer. Executive producers include Joy Gorman Wedtels for Joy Coalition, Trip Friendly for Friendly Family Productions, Dana Fox and Pascal Verschooris, who also directs the Season 2 finale episode. More directors include Kat Candler (201), Kyle Patrick Alvarez (202), Julie Anne Robinson (203), Liza Johnson (204), Sarah Boyd (205), Ellen Kuras (206) and Sydney Freeland (207), The adaptation is produced by CBS Studios and Anonymous Content Studio.

articles.title: Netflix Plans Oscar Push for Lee Chang-dong’s ‘Possible Love,’ Promoting Jeon Do-yeon for Best Actress (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Feinberg Plus Icon Scott Feinberg Executive Editor of Awards ScottFeinberg Follow Sign Up View All October 8, 2026 7:47am 'Possible Love' Courtesy of Netflix Seven award seasons after the Korean film Parasite broke the glass ceiling for non-English-language films at the Oscars by winning best picture, Netflix is angling to get another hugely acclaimed film from Korea the same sort of recognition: Lee Chang-dong ’s Possible Love . The Hollywood Reporter can exclusively report that the company is planning a multi-category Oscar push for the film, which is the first in eight years from Korean master Lee, and already has been awarded the Venice Film Festival’s Grand Jury Prize, placed second for the Toronto International Film Festival’s international audience award and is among 2026’s best-reviewed releases, with scores of 100 percent on Rotten Tomatoes and 93 on MetaCritic. Related Stories TV 'The Altruists': Anthony Boyle's Sam Bankman-Fried Caught in Crypto Crisis in Netflix Series Trailer Movies Oscars: Rwanda Picks 'Ben'Imana' as Its First-Ever Best Int'l Feature Submission In addition to an Oscar nom for best international feature (Korea chose the film as its official entry way back in August ), Oscar noms for best picture, best director and best original screenplay (Lee and Oh Jung-mi) are high-priority targets and seem achievable based on the success of non-English-language films in those categories over the decade since the Academy began significantly increasing the number of its members who are based outside of the United States (and are therefore less deterred by subtitles). But Netflix feels that its strongest bet may be the performance of Jeon Do-yeon as Mi-ok, the outspoken half of a working-class couple that is opportunistically befriended by a very wealthy couple, and the company has decided to lobby hard for the 53-year-old to land a best actress Oscar nom. (She previously worked with Lee on 2007’s Secret Sunshine , for which she became the first Korean to win the Cannes Film Festival’s best actress prize, and is now one of Korea’s biggest stars.) Unlike Netflix’s other 2026 ensemble-centric non-English-lanauge film, La Bola Negra , the full cast of which is being promoted in the supporting acting categories, the company has decided to promote the four principal stars of Possible Love in different categories. In addition to Jeon in the best actress race, it will ask voters to consider Sul Kyung-Gu, who plays Mi-ok’s traumatized husband Ho-seok, for best actor; Cho Yeo-jeong, a Parasite alum who plays Ye-ji, a wealthy woman pursuing an interview with Ho-seok for a documentary, for best supporting actress; and Zo In-sung, who plays Ye-ji’s playboy husband Sang-woo, for best supporting actor. The streamer is hoping that the Actor Awards (formerly the SAG Awards), which embraced Parasite with an historic best ensemble nomination (and later an historic best ensemble win), will also recognize Possible Love with a nom in that category. Another key barometer of the film’s prospects may be the increasingly critics-aligned voting body of the Golden Globes, to which Possible Love is being submitted for consideration in the drama categories (as opposed to the musical or comedy categories). Given that two of the highest-profile best actress Oscar contenders — The Debut ’s Julianne Moore and, somewhat surprisingly, Obsession ’s Inde Navarrette — will be competing in the Globes’ musical/comedy actress race, the Globes’ drama actress race looks fairly open, which could bode well for the prospects of Jeon.
