articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac London Film Festival Opens With Passionate ‘Elsinore’ Homecoming Screening Andrew Lloyd Webber’s ‘Phantom Of The Opera’ To Be Recorded Live & Released In Cinemas ‘The Complete Kubrick’: How Michael Chaiken & Criterion Created The First Full Collection Of Stanley Kubrick’s Filmworks View All January 16, 2026 4:04am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'No Good Men' Anwar Hashimi, Shahrbanoo Sadat in No Good Men by Shahrbanoo Sadat © Virginie Surdej No Good Men , the latest feature from Afghan filmmaker Shahrbanoo Sadat, will open the 2026 Berlin Film Festival. The film follows Naru, the only camerawoman at Kabul TV, who is convinced that there are no good men in Afghanistan. But when the reporter Qodrat takes her on assignment just before the Taliban’s return, sparks fly – and she begins to question this belief. The film was shot in several locations across Germany. No Good Men is an international co-production between Germany, France, Norway, Denmark, and Afghanistan. Production companies are Adomeit Film, La Fabrica Nocturna Cinéma, Motlys, Amerikafilm, and Wolf Pictures. Related Stories News Quiver Distribution Takes U.S. For Jérémy Comte's Ghana & Canada-Set Drama 'Paradise' News Wim Wenders Revisits Berlin Comments On Filmmakers & Politics That Led To A Firestorm -- Venice The feature follows Sadat’s last works, Wolf and Sheep (2016) and Parwareshgah ( The Orphanage , 2019). Both films screened at Cannes’ Directors’ Fortnight. No Good Men is also the third of five planned films based on the autobiographical writings of author and actor Anwar Hashimi. Hashimi stars in the film alongside Sadat, who is in the lead role. Watch on Deadline “Shahrbanoo Sadat is one of the most exciting voices in world cinema and No Good Men really delivers on the promise of her first two features,” Berlinale Director Tricia Tuttle said in a statement this afternoon. “Sadat continues her vital work spotlighting Afghan women’s lives, here bringing romance and touches of humour to a rousingly political story. That it is based on real events, and the director risked so much to get this film made makes No Good Men even more meaningful as our Opening Gala of the 76th Berlinale.” Earlier this week, Berlin made several additions to its Panorama, Forum, and Expanded competition strands. Features set for the fest include Charli XCX ’s buzzy flick The Moment , which will screen in the Panorama competition. The Moment will travel to Berlin following its Sundance debut and screen in the European festival’s Panorama competition section. Panorama will screen new works by Hong Sangsoo, Joaquín del Paso, André Novais Oliveira, and Elle Sofe Sara. Directed by Aidan Zamiri from a screenplay he wrote with Bertie Brandes, the film is based on an original idea by Charli xcx. The “Brat” singer-songwriter also stars in the film, which follows a rising pop star as she navigates the complexities of fame and industry pressure while preparing for her arena-tour debut. The 2026 Berlin Film Festival runs from February 12–22. ‘Baywatch’, ‘Shaka iLembe’ & ‘Maya’ In Deadline Dozen; ‘Heated Rivalry’s Crave Brad Bird On The Long Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To Cinemas Maggie Gyllenhaal, Michelle Yeoh, Alfonso & Jonás Cuarón On Cinema’s Future Skydance Film Bosses & WB To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In Works Or On Fire Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Alternativa Distribution Takes ‘No Good Men’ & ‘Four Daughters’ To MIPCOM
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart Alternativa Distribution Takes ‘No Good Men’ & ‘Four Daughters’ To MIPCOM ‘World War Z’ Director Marc Forster Adapting Jamie Scallion’s Revenge Thriller ‘Nines’ For TV With Renée Wolfe, Me+You Productions & Fremantle The Deadline Dozen: The Hottest Scripted Shows Heading To MIPCOM Including ‘Baywatch’, ‘Einstein’ & ‘Maya’ Starring Bella Ramsey View All October 8, 2026 1:43am Add us as a Google Preferred Source No Good Men Virginie Surdej EXCLUSIVE: Alternativa Distribution has acquired selected rights to features including Berlin Film Festival opener No Good Men ahead of making its debut at the MIPCOM market in Cannes. The fledgling distributor has acquired several other festival and award-nominated movies ahead of MIPCOM. It will present Akio Fujimoto’s Lost Land to buyers, as well as Abinash Bikram Shah’s Elephants in the Fog and Kaouther Ben Hania’s Four Daughters . Alternativa Distribution will shop Elephants in the Fog in multiple territories across Asia and Latin America; No Good Men in multiple territories across Asia and the MENA region; Four Daughters in multiple territories across Latin America and Asia; and Lost Land across Southeast Asia, ex-Malaysia, the Nordics, Poland and Portugal. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News The Deadline Dozen: The Hottest Scripted Shows Heading To MIPCOM Including 'Baywatch', 'Einstein' & 'Maya' Starring Bella Ramsey News North Stars: How 'Heated Rivalry' Made Canadian TV Red Hot Alternativa launched its distribution arm earlier this year to sell impact-driven films to broadcasters and streamers. The Alternativa Distribution division is run by former yesDocu and TikTok exec Avital Lavi. It launched with a ten-film slate including the Un Certain Regard titles If Only I Could Hibernate and A Poet . The new acquisitions come with strong awards and festival pedigree. Elephants in the Fog competed in the Un Certain Regard section at the Cannes Film Festival this year, winning the Jury Prize. It was also Nepal’s submission for the Best International Feature Film at the Academy Awards. Lost Land won the Orizzonti Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival . Four Daughters shared the L’Œil d’Or for Best Documentary at Cannes. It was nominated for Best Documentary Feature at the Academy Awards. Alternativa is a not-for-profit org that supports films from the Global South. Having started out as an awards program for films from Central Asia, Alternativa then initiated a full-fledged festival with editions in Indonesia and Colombia. “With our second film slate, we are expanding our global reach to give buyers and audiences access to even more exceptional, high-impact storytelling,” Lavi said. “Our latest acquisitions have already proven themselves on the world stage – from a Cannes prize-winner to acclaimed titles featured at Venice and the Berlinale. We’re incredibly proud to represent them and look forward to getting them in front of broadcasters and streaming platforms.” ‘Baywatch’, ‘Shaka iLembe’ & ‘Maya’ In Deadline Dozen; ‘Heated Rivalry’s Crave Brad Bird On The Long Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To Cinemas Maggie Gyllenhaal, Michelle Yeoh, Alfonso & Jonás Cuarón On Cinema’s Future Skydance Film Bosses & WB To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In Works Or On Fire Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Marco Bellocchio’s ‘Falcon’ Sets Sales & Announces Louis Garrel In Role Of Fiat Boss John Elkann
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie ‘NAZA’ Producer James Wilson Addresses “Hysterical, Vituperative” Israeli Government Backlash Against Directors Oscars: Rwanda Makes History As ‘Ben’Imana’ Becomes First Official Entry; Alexander Set U.S. & UK Release Hande Erçel To Star In Nader Saeivar’s Berlin-Set Drama ‘Diaspora’ View All October 8, 2026 2:02am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Louis Garrel, Marco Bellocchio, Pierfrancesco Favino Riccardo Ghilardi, Anna Camerlingo, Pablo Arroyo Rai Cinema International Distribution has boarded sales on Marco Bellocchio ’s financial thriller Falcon , inspired by the life of late Fiat-Chrysler automobile exec Sergio Marchionne, as it films in Toronto. In new casting additions, previously announced lead Pierfrancesco Favino is being joined by Louis Garrel , Benedetta Cimatti and Barbara Ronchi, with the participation of Valeria Bruni Tedeschi. The picture delves into the story of the Marchionne, the Italian-Canada automobile exec credited with reviving Italy ’s Turin-based car company Fiat in the 2000s and merging it with then ailing U.S. auto manufacturer Chrysler. Related Stories News 'Maserati: The Brothers' Actress Maya Talem Signs With MAD Celebrity News Oscars: Italy Submits Paolo Strippoli's 'The Spiral' For Best International Feature Film It will recount how Sergio Marchionne (Favino) came to the rescue of Italy’s most famous car manufacturer in 2004 as it lay on the verge of collapse in the wake of the death of its longtime boss, the legendary industrialist Gianni Agnelli. Watch on Deadline Ruthless and visionary, Marchionne axed the top management. He then took Agnelli’s grandson, John Elkann (Garrel), under his wing to teach the young heir, suddenly burdened with the family’s legacy, the art of command. Marchionne then took on the U.S. car manufacturer General Motors, disentangling Fiat from a disadvantage strategic alliance, and went on to save rival Chrysler from bankruptcy by merging it with Fiat. Falcon is co-written by Marco Bellocchio with Ludovica Rampoldi, Andrea Di Stefano, Stefano Rulli and with the participation of Oliviero Del Papa. Talking to Deadline about the project last year , Bellocchio said of Marchionne: “I’m fascinated by his journey and his ability, as an Italian who stood up to American big business, to defend Fiat and then even take over Chrysler, which was bankrupt, to make a major group.” He also revealed that the title of Falcon is inspired by the fact that Marchionne would always travel on a Falcon business jet. “He would travel went back and forth from Turin on a Falcon, so we’ve given it this title,” he said. Falcon is produced by Kavac Film, Rai Cinema, with Emotion Network in collaboration with STLA Europe. The feature has already shot for two weeks in September in Toronto and Niagara Falls, moving to the Piedmont region of Italy and to Rome, and then returning to Canada and the United States in early 2027. 01 Distribution will release the film in Italy. The project reunites Bellocchio with a number of longtime creative collaborators, including production designer Andrea Castorina, costume designer Daria Calvelli, and editor Francesca Calvelli, all of whom worked on Bellocchio on projects including The Traitor , Exterior Night and Kidnapped . He is also joined for the first time by director of photography Matteo Cocco ( The Weight , Hidden Away ). articles.title: Niamh Algar & Fanny Ardant Starring In UK-Greek Series Set In AI-Controlled Luxury Resort
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max UK Police Acknowledge Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor Search Warrants Were Unlawful Joe Sugg & Caspar Lee’s MVE Hires CAA & WME Agents In U.S. Apple TV Buys Tropic Noir Series ‘Dustfall’ Starring Anna Torv View All October 8, 2026 2:59am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Niamh Algar (left) and Fanny Ardant Alex Johnson / Carole Bellaiche Niamh Algar and French cinema legend Fanny Ardant are leading a thriller series set in an AI-controlled, high-end luxury resort. Harmonia is a rare UK-Greek co-pro coming from Adolescence co-producer Warp Films , Athens’ Neda Films, ITV Studios and Greek pubcaster ERT. In Harmonia, Algar is the AI’s creator, Shona Casey, while Ardant plays the resort’s former owner. In the resort and wellness facility, technology meets escapism and every guest’s desire can be fulfilled. It reflects things we all aspire to, but also fear. It’s a modern-day Frankenstein story of a scientist who would be God, and their extraordinary creation, where it becomes increasingly unclear whether the AI is the monster, or whether the humans are. Related Stories News Nick Curwin, Founder Of British Production Houses Dragonfly & The Garden, Retiring From Indie Incubator Matisse News 'Smilla's Sense Of Snow' Series Settles At AMC+ Chloe Lea ( Dune: Prophecy, A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms ) plays a young member of staff that the AI becomes obsessed with, while the cast includes Oliver Chris ( Rivals, The Crown ), Abubakar Salim ( House of the Dragon, Raised by Wolves ), Goran Bogdan ( Legacy of Spies, The Last Panthers ), Theo Augier ( XO Kitty, Jay Kelly ) and George Ioannides ( Guys and Dolls, Industry ). Completing the ensemble are Greek stars Pygmalion Dadakaridis ( The Other Me, Rififi ), rising TV and theatre actor Konstantinos Zografos (The Judge, Derti) Antigoni Frida ( Grand Hotel, Sauté ) and newcomer Zoe-Stella Nikolaou. Watch on Deadline The coming together of UK and Greek teams sees the series created by Peter Carlton, Lefteris Charitos, Amanda Livanou and Hanna Jameson. Charitos, director of Wild Bees , one of Greek television’s biggest ever successes, directs all six episodes. Jameson, best-selling author of The Last and writer on the upcoming Netflix series The Twin starring Jamie Dornan, is lead writer, with episodes from Alki Papastathopoulos and Panayotis Christopoulos. Jameson said: “With this project, I had the chance to tell a truly meaningful story full of funny, strange, and complicated characters, reminiscent of the legendary genre shows I grew up watching. It’s been so exciting to explore how our relationship with technology has changed so fast in such a short period of time, evolving faster than our ability to understand the personal and global consequences. When I’m gripped by a great show everything else falls away, the house could burn down around me and I wouldn’t notice, and I hope that people feel the same way about Harmonia .” Shooting takes place on location in Athens at Cape Sounio resort and Kapa2 Studios ahead of launch in 2027. Harmonia is produced in association with and distributed internationally by ITV Studios. It is co-financed by ITV Studios, and Greek public broadcaster ERT, with development support from the Hellenic Film & Audiovisual Fund and Creative Europe Media. The predominantly English-language series is an international co-production between Warp, which co-produced Adolescence with Brad Pitt’s Plan B, and award-winning Greek feature film producers Neda Film ( Pity, Gorgonà ). ‘Baywatch’, ‘Shaka iLembe’ & ‘Maya’ In Deadline Dozen; ‘Heated Rivalry’s Crave Brad Bird On The Long Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To Cinemas Maggie Gyllenhaal, Michelle Yeoh, Alfonso & Jonás Cuarón On Cinema’s Future Skydance Film Bosses & WB To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In Works Or On Fire Read More About: Comments

articles.title: BBC Apologizes “Unreservedly” And Removes Article Accusing PinkNews Founder Of Sexual Misconduct
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Joe Sugg & Caspar Lee’s MVE Expands With CAA & WME Hires In U.S. Apple TV Buys Tropic Noir Series ‘Dustfall’ Starring Anna Torv PBS Masterpiece’s ‘Maigret’ Finds UK Home View All October 8, 2026 3:53am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Leon Neal/Getty The BBC has “apologized unreservedly for the defamatory allegations” made in a documentary and accompanying article about the founder of one of the UK’s leading LGBTQ+ publications and his husband. The BBC this morning removed from its website the original PinkNews article. The documentary came off iPlayer last year after its window ran down. The corporation has agreed to pay compensation to PinkNews founder Benjamin Cohen and his husband Anthony James. In a joint statement on PinkNews, Cohen and James said the BBC had “reinforced one of the most damaging homophobic tropes” by “falsely portraying us as engaging in sexual misconduct and pressuring female employees over surrogacy.” Related Stories News BBC Boss Matt Brittin Sets Out Silicon Valley-Style Revolution At British Broadcaster News 'Doctor Who' Bids Revealed: Jed Mercurio Leads Pitch To Regenerate BBC Series, As STV Studios Plans To Transport TARDIS To Scotland The BBC launched the documentary, PinkNews: Behind Closed Doors, and an accompanying article titled “PinkNews bosses accused of sexual misconduct” in late 2024. The doc and article said the BBC had spoken with 30 current and former employees, some of whom told the BBC they had experienced bullying and sexual misconduct from Cohen and James. The BBC also reported that several people had said some young female members of staff had been asked to act as the couple’s surrogates. Watch on Deadline Cohen and James’ High Court statement read out after the settlement called the allegations “serious, false, defamatory… and extremely harmful to the claimants’ reputations.” It noted that, as a result of the doc and article, Cohen and James were subject to additional investigations by CAFCASS (Children and Family Court Advisory and Support Service) ahead of a parental order hearing at the Family Court in respect of their son, who had been born via surrogate. The BBC’s counsel responded by saying the corporation “accepts everything” and “retracts and apologises unreservedly for the defamatory allegatios made in the programme and the article.” A BBC spokeswoman told Deadline: “The BBC has reached a settlement with Ben Cohen and Anthony James. We will not be issuing any further comment.” Cohen and James’ PinkNews statement said: “By falsely portraying us as engaging in sexual misconduct and pressuring female employees over surrogacy, the BBC reinforced one of the most damaging homophobic tropes: that gay men are sexual predators who pose a threat to others. These were allegations that should never have been broadcast.” They added that while they can now “finally begin to move forward,” the BBC “needs to carefully consider and learn from the impact that its reckless journalism has had on a young family’s lives.” ‘Baywatch’, ‘Shaka iLembe’ & ‘Maya’ In Deadline Dozen; ‘Heated Rivalry’s Crave Brad Bird On The Long Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To Cinemas Maggie Gyllenhaal, Michelle Yeoh, Alfonso & Jonás Cuarón On Cinema’s Future Skydance Film Bosses & WB To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In Works Or On Fire Read More About: 1 Comments

articles.title: Lauren Ash, Mae Martin & Randall Park Join Crave Comedy ‘Meatballs’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Prime Video Thriller ‘The Assassin’ Gets Season 2 Trailer And Launch Date In UK & Ireland Lauren Ash, Mae Martin & Randall Park Join Crave Comedy ‘Meatballs’ The Deadline Dozen: The Hottest Scripted Shows Heading To MIPCOM Including ‘Baywatch’, ‘Einstein’ & ‘Maya’ Starring Bella Ramsey View All October 8, 2026 4:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Lauren Ash, Mae Martin and Randall Park Getty/PMC EXCLUSIVE: Lauren Ash ( Superstore ), Mae Martin ( Wayward ) and Randall Park ( Wandavision ) are joining the campers at Crave comedy Meatballs . The trio will be guest cast in the series, which is billed as a “raunchy, irreverent reimagining of the beloved 1979 Canadian comedy classic” that starred Bill Murray. They will join Gen V star Maddie Phillips is taking on the role as Skipper, the head camp counselor, in a reimagined version of Murray’s original character, and Heated Rivalry breakout Robbie G.K., who plays Dale. articles.title: Hande Erçel To Star In Nader Saeivar’s Berlin-Set Drama ‘Diaspora’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Oscars: Rwanda Makes History As ‘Ben’Imana’ Becomes First Official Entry; Alexander Set U.S. & UK Release Hande Erçel To Star In Nader Saeivar’s Berlin-Set Drama ‘Diaspora’ Marco Bellocchio’s ‘Falcon’ Sets Sales & Announces Louis Garrel In Role Of Fiat Boss John Elkann View All October 8, 2026 4:20am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Hande Erçel Atwood Films, Sky Films EXCLUSIVE: Turkish star Hande Erçel has been unveiled as the lead actress in Iranian director and screenwriter Nadar Saeivar ’s upcoming Germany -set drama Diaspora ahead of an early 2027 shoot. Berlin-based director Saeivar, whose recent directorial credits include No End (2022), The Witness (2024) and Hijamat (2026), is also known internationally for his work with Jafar Panahi. He shared an original screenplay Oscar nomination this year with Panahi for Cannes Palme d’Or winner It Was Just An Accident , and has also collaborated with the director on a number of other works. Related Stories News 'Where's Wanda' Season 2: Watch Trailer For Apple TV's Darkly Comic German Series From UFA Fiction News Studiocanal Announces Wrap Of Final Film In Ambitious German-Language 'Woodwalkers' Trilogy Saeivar’s upcoming feature in the director’s seat will star Erçel as Merve, an educated, middle-class Turkish woman trying to rebuild her life and that of her 12-year-old son in Germany after the tragic death of her husband in Turkey . Watch on Deadline As she attempts to move on from a painful past, she finds works in the language school of a German family expecting their second child. After a meet-up between Merve, her son and the German family, she falls victim to inappropriate physical contact by the family’s 15-year-old son named Luca. Torn between remaining silent and speaking out, she decides to inform the boy’s father after the harassment recurs. However, the family refuses to believe Merve and turns the accusations against her, making her the target of severe slander. As a widowed immigrant living alone with her 12-year-old son in a foreign country, she is forced into a gruelling battle against both the justice system and societal prejudices. The family’s refusal to accept their child’s wrongdoing deepens Merve’s isolation. Striving to stay strong for her son, the young woman finds herself dragged into an exhausting struggle between law and conscience to prove her innocence. Erçel, who is known for her roles in Turkish box office hit Intoxicated by Love and Netflix show Chasing the Wind , will travel to Berlin about a month prior to shooting to begin character development, language training and creative rehearsals. She will be joined in the cast by Moritz Bleibtreu as the father of the German family with further international cast members due to be unveiled in the coming weeks. Produced jointly by Said Nur Akkus at Berlin-based Arthood Films and Emre Oskay at Istanbul-based Sky Films, Diaspora will take place entirely in Berlin, and the production will be in German, English, and Turkish. Saeivar, who was born and grew up in northwestern Iran with Turkish roots, previously explored the migrant experience in his adopted home of Berlin in Hijamat about a man hailing from the city’s Turkish community who discovers his brother is gay. “ Diaspora is born from an urgent need to re-examine the intricate, often silent dynamics between the East and the West, a relationship too frequently shaped by systemic misunderstandings, subtle prejudices, and historical projections,” said Saeivar in a director’s note. “For decades, the Western gaze has tended to view the East through a lens of either exoticism or perpetual trauma, reducing individual human complexities to mere cultural stereotypes or political statistics. When individuals from the East arrive in the West seeking peace, they often find themselves navigating an unwritten social hierarchy where their voices are muted, their boundaries violated under the guise of “cultural differences,” and their dignity traded for survival.” “This film is not merely a story of displacement; it is a call for a profound shift in perspective. True coexistence cannot be built on passive tolerance or structural superiority. A peaceful shared future demands authentic empathy.” ‘Baywatch’, ‘Shaka iLembe’ & ‘Maya’ In Deadline Dozen; ‘Heated Rivalry’s Crave Brad Bird On The Long Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To Cinemas Maggie Gyllenhaal, Michelle Yeoh, Alfonso & Jonás Cuarón On Cinema’s Future Skydance Film Bosses & WB To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In Works Or On Fire Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Grace Harper Brighouse On Bringing Her Camden Film Festival-Winning Doc ‘Dependence’ Back Home To London — LFF
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Grace Harper Brighouse On Bringing Her Camden Film Festival-Winning Doc ‘Dependence’ Back Home To London — LFF Brad Bird On The 30-Year Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To The Big Screen — London Film Festival London Film Festival Opens With Passionate ‘Elsinore’ Homecoming Screening View All October 8, 2026 4:36am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The 2026 London Film Festival rolls into action this week. And among the headline international galas, there is once again a strong collection of homegrown titles. The most exciting is perhaps Dependence , a moving, formally experimental documentary directed by debut filmmaker Grace Harper Brighouse . Dependence premiered earlier this year at Camden, where it won the festival’s Harrell Award. The film examines the filmmaker’s strained relationship with her father, an estrangement caused by his OxyContin addiction, using a collection of home movies she shot from childhood through to adulthood, including film school rushes. Related Stories News Brad Bird On The 30-Year Journey To Bring 'Ray Gunn' To The Big Screen -- London Film Festival News London Film Festival Opens With Passionate 'Elsinore' Homecoming Screening “It was in 2013. I was making my first film at film school, about a strip pub in High Wycombe. I was having the best time,” Brighouse explains of the film’s origins. “But I was very aware that I didn’t know what I was doing. I didn’t have enough time to make the film the way I wanted.” Brighouse says her brother suggested returning home to make a film about their dad and his dying dog, Charlie. “Every year, if my dad and I hadn’t been speaking, he would say, ‘Charlie’s going to die. He’s never going to make it through the winter.’ It gave us both an off-ramp: we could be together without having to apologise to each other for whatever the reason was that we weren’t speaking,” she says. “So I came back. I’d been watching a lot of Russian documentaries, and I was really enjoying the smoke, the framing, and the very pretentious, arthouse documentary shots that I still love so much. But I realised that it had been quite a long time. I guess this is what a camera does: it lets you observe things that you don’t usually observe, particularly in your closest relationships.” Brighouse’s brother died suddenly, and the footage sat dormant for many years. “I couldn’t really watch it for a very long time. A dear friend of mine, Eleanor Mortimer, logged it for me so I could look at it without having to watch it. It was such a gift because I couldn’t do it myself.” Brighouse says she later felt an unexplainable urge to return to the material. “I would look at it and think, ‘Okay, what was here? Let me look at this.’ Slowly, I understood that I wasn’t done with that film, but it wasn’t the film I was making anymore,” she says. “So, what had it become?” The Camden programmers described Dependence as “a funny, tender, and poignant essay on family bonds.” Indeed, Dependence is a thoughtful exploration of addiction and the unique power of paternal love. The film has a breezy construction. There are time jumps, and images are presented in multiple formats. Brighouse also avoids talking heads or any of the visual tropes we’ve come to associate with films about families and addiction. She cites RaMell Ross’s wonderfully transgressive Hale County This Morning, This Evening as an influence. “That film unlocked a way for me to think about storytelling and time, and about creating a visual language that is different from the guidebook,” Brighouse says. Brighouse is credited as the director and cinematographer on Dependence . There is additional cinematography by Roger Chapman, Ronnie McQuillan, and Tom Besley. Vera Simmonds was the editor, and the film was produced by Caitlin Mae Burke and Alistair Payne-James (140 Films). Brighouse describes a scrappy production. “We had to get to a rough cut by scraping together very little money through artist residencies and paid time. Everyone had other jobs while doing it,” she says, adding that she hopes the film can find and engage with a large audience. “I hope we’ve made something where, in the end, you think, ‘I really just want to talk to my family member and tell them I love them,’” Brighouse says. “That sounds trite, but I hope the film can sit in that space of complex, messy familial love, as well as all the issues it touches on.” 140 Films is heading sales on the project. The film screens Sunday, October 11th, at the LFF . articles.title: PBS Masterpiece’s ‘Maigret’ Finds UK Home

BBC Studios-owned UKTV has taken both seasons of the Georges Simenon adaptation for its U&Drama network plus U streaming service, coming as part of a 114-hour content deal with Banijay Rights. Produced by Wolf Hall maker Playground in association with Banijay Rights, the series stars Benjamin Wainwright as Chief Inspector Jules Maigret, Stefanie Martini as Madame Louise Maigret and Blake Harrison as Joseph Torrence. It reinvents one of the world’s most recognizable crime brands, following the chief inspector and his team of loyal, maverick detectives solving crimes in Paris. It has been adapted plenty down the years including for a 2016 ITV series starring Rowan Atkinson. Related Stories News Alternativa Distribution Takes 'No Good Men' & 'Four Daughters' To MIPCOM News The Deadline Dozen: The Hottest Scripted Shows Heading To MIPCOM Including 'Baywatch', 'Einstein' & 'Maya' Starring Bella Ramsey The deal between UKTV and Banijay Rights is also for the second season of A Remarkable Place to Die , Agatha & The Midnight Murders , Ambulance (Series 12 and 13), Lost and Found in the Lakes , Saving Lives at Sea (Series 9 and 10) and Tribe with Bruce Parry . Watch on Deadline Karin Marelle, Global Head of Acquisitions, UKTV and BBC Studios, said: “ Maigret is one of the most recognisable detective brands in the world, so we are delighted to be bringing this brand-new adaptation to viewers on U and U&DRAMA.” The news comes ahead of next week’s MIPCOM Cannes, where Banijay Rights executives will be out in force with a new-look catalog incorporating All3Media International’s fare. Maigret is a Playground co-production for Masterpiece in association with Banijay Rights, Windhover Films, and Georges Simenon Limited. Executive producers are Hilary Strong and Patrick Harbinson, with David Stern and Colin Callender for Playground. Executive producer for Masterpiece is Susanne Simpson. Executive producers for Banijay Rights are Cathy Payne and Simon Cox. The series is produced by Tim Whitby and created for television and written by Harbinson. articles.title: BBC Chief Meets Netflix CEO & Other Streamers In Bid To Forge “Strategic Partnerships”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake BBC Staff Raise Concerns About Director-General’s Praise For AI-Generated ‘Doctor Who’ BBC Chief Meets Netflix CEO & Other Streamers In Bid To Forge “Strategic Partnerships” ‘Baby Reindeer’ Battle Reignites: Netflix Suffers Blow In Bid To Get Fiona Harvey Lawsuit Spiked View All October 8, 2026 5:07am Add us as a Google Preferred Source BBC boss Matt Brittin Getty EXCLUSIVE : BBC director general Matt Brittin has spent time in recent weeks meeting with the leaders of U.S. streamers in an effort to showcase more of the corporation’s content. Brittin, a former Google executive, told staff on Wednesday that he had met with the “global leadership” of Netflix , Amazon Prime Video , Apple TV, and YouTube in an effort to forge “strategic partnerships.” Deadline understands, for example, that Brittin sat down with Greg Peters when the Netflix co-CEO visited London in recent weeks. Related Stories News BBC Apologizes "Unreservedly" And Removes Article Accusing PinkNews Founder Of Sexual Misconduct News Brad Bird On The 30-Year Journey To Bring 'Ray Gunn' To The Big Screen -- London Film Festival Brittin has put partnerships at the heart of his agenda in his early months at the BBC, though it is not yet clear how closer collaboration could work with U.S. streamers. Watch on Deadline The director general told staff: “Since I’ve been here, we’ve met with the global leadership of Netflix, Amazon, Apple and YouTube to talk about not just the individual things that we’re doing, but what if we step back and say, ‘What are all the things we could do to help the BBC to transform at this time?’ “Because of our reputation and our trust internationally, I think we can get a lot more out of players like that, as well as the many partners we have in other parts of the BBC as well.” Brittin added that he wants to ensure that the BBC’s content is more “prominent” on Netflix and YouTube, and has previously spoken about making more BBC News output available on these services. In a deal that predated his arrival, the BBC agreed to produce original YouTube shows for the first time under a pact with the Google-owned video service. Brittin’s proposals are also in step with the British government’s plan to compel YouTube to promote public service content. YouTube has expressed reservations about this, calling it “forced prominence.” Brittin’s comments on streamer partnerships come as Reuters reported that the BBC and Channel 4 are scoping out a joint-venture deal. This could include BBC Studios combining UKTV with Channel 4’s advertising operations, channels including E4 and Film4, and its streaming service. Channel 4’s main network would not be included in such an arrangement, Reuters reported. Brittin and Channel 4 CEO Priya Dogra have spoken openly about a partnership, including iPlayer hosting Channel 4 shows. Dogra has, however, warned against the BBC acquiring full control of Channel 4. A BBC spokesperson said: “We won’t be providing any comment, but as we’ve said before, we believe increased collaboration between all public service broadcasters is vital to ensure the industry thrives in a highly competitive global marketplace.” Channel 4 said: “We won’t be commenting on any speculation but we welcome and support greater collaboration between public service media and strongly believe working together can strengthen impact, innovation and sustainability in UK broadcasting. Channel 4 and the BBC already have a successful commercial relationship, involving ad sales for UKTV and the carriage of U on 4Streaming.” ‘Baywatch’, ‘Shaka iLembe’ & ‘Maya’ In Deadline Dozen; ‘Heated Rivalry’s Crave Brad Bird On The Long Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To Cinemas Maggie Gyllenhaal, Michelle Yeoh, Alfonso & Jonás Cuarón On Cinema’s Future Skydance Film Bosses & WB To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In Works Or On Fire Read More About: 1 Comments

articles.title: Eyeing More ‘Minecrafts’ And ‘Fallouts’, Microsoft Xbox Launches XP Unit To Take Properties Beyond Video Games
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Joe Rogan Sets Multi-Year Extension With Spotify Eyeing More ‘Minecrafts’ And ‘Fallouts’, Microsoft Xbox Launches XP Unit To Take Properties Beyond Video Games ‘Beyond The Spider-Verse’ Director Bob Persichetti On “Limitless” Fan Expectations And “Never Saying No” View All October 8, 2026 5:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jack Black promotes 'A Minecraft Movie' Courtesy Microsoft Xbox , hoping to replicate the success of franchises like Minecraft and Fallout , is launching a new division called XP designed to extend properties beyond video games . The XP name is described as a play on “experience points.” It has four main components: Xbox Pictures for film and TV adaptations; Xbox Products for licensing and merchandise; Xbox Partnerships for sponsors and brand partners; and Xbox Places for broadcast and in-person events. “Our franchises can mean more to people than the time they spend playing them,” CEO Asha Sharma explained to employees in a staff memo Thursday. Related Stories Casting Walton Goggins Joins Michael B. Jordan And Austin Butler In 'Miami Vice '85' At Universal News Xbox Continues "Reset" With Additional Layoffs And Restructuring Expanding properties beyond video games then creates a virtuous cycle, Xbox says. Fallout titles on Xbox Game Pass saw a 5x increase in hours played during Fallout ‘s first season on Prime Video. Minecraft saw over a 75% increase in weekly active users of the game year-over-year since the movie’s release in the spring of 2025. Watch on Deadline Hollywood, meanwhile, has finally found its groove with adapting games into films and series. Sony revived Resident Evil last month and HBO drew big viewership and critical praise with The Last of Us , just to name a couple of recent success stories. The XP news comes after Xbox has initiated a self-described “reset” with multiple rounds of layoffs and restructured its studio businesses to adapt to a changing operating environment in the games sector. In 2023, Microsoft acquired Activision Blizzard for $69 billion at a moment when mobile and casual gaming was starting to upend the traditional console business. Kayleen Walters, a former Lucasfilm executive, has been named president of XP. She is expected to build a team at the division from staffer both internal and external. Maria Angelidou-Smith is joining Xbox as CEO of Mojang and Minecraft after nearly a decade at Meta. After spending 13 years at Lucasfilm working on Star Wars, Walters helped grow Xbox’s consumer products arm into a mult-billion-dollar business with more than 250 licenses. She was an executive producer of A Minecraft Movie , and is a full producer on its sequel, which is currently in production. “Fans don’t just play our franchises,” Walters wrote to employees in an email to her team. “They watch them, wear them, attend them, celebrate them, and connect with them in countless ways.” ‘Baywatch’, ‘Shaka iLembe’ & ‘Maya’ In Deadline Dozen; ‘Heated Rivalry’s Crave Brad Bird On The Long Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To Cinemas Maggie Gyllenhaal, Michelle Yeoh, Alfonso & Jonás Cuarón On Cinema’s Future Skydance Film Bosses & WB To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In Works Or On Fire Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Skydance Co-CEO Ynon Kreiz Says Jobs Cuts Will Be Handled “Respectfully, Transparently” As Company Restructures
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill Skydance Co-CEO Ynon Kreiz Says Jobs Cuts Will Be Handled “Respectfully, Transparently” As Company Restructures Skydance Stock Struggles In First Days Of Trading Skydance Sets Heads Of Games, Products, HR View All October 8, 2026 7:24am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc Ynon Kreiz Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images Ynon Kreiz , the new co-chief executive of Skydance, said a planned $6 billion in cost savings will come from “technology, marketing consolidation, real estate optimization, and some labor. Although labor is not the majority of the savings.” Related Stories News David Ellison Calls Skydance “Solution” To Mistakes Ten Years Ago When Big Tech Moved In On Media News Skydance Film Bosses Dana Goldberg & Josh Greenstein & The Warner Bros To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In The Works Or On Fire But “we’ve been public” that synergies will involve some workforce reduction, he said during a Q&A on CNBC this morning alongside Skydance chairman and CEO David Ellison . “When it comes to making those decisions, of course we’re thinking of our people. We’re going to do it in the right way, respectfully, transparently, and communicate our plans. This will be part of the plan. This is part of the plan. Will be part of the process,” he said. The comments echo those Ellison made yesterday at a town hall meeting of global staffers. Watch on Deadline “It’s important also to say this is not about cost reduction. This is about reengineering how we work. This is about reinventing the business model. So it’s not just synergies and reducing costs; it’s also improving how we perform. And we’re looking to build a high-performing company, leveraging technology, leveraging capabilities [to] build something that will stand out for years to come.” The merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery closed Tuesday, with the combined companies now called Skydance. Executives are targeting the $6 billion in cost savings by the end of 2028, but the co-CEOs indicated in the interview today that they think the number could be greater. They noted that the earlier Paramount-Skydance merger “over delivered” on synergies, projecting $2 billion and hitting $2.7 billion. Kreiz, a seasoned executive, joined Skydance from Mattel where he announced a 25% workforce reduction shortly after coming on in 2018 as profits plunged amid the liquidation and bankruptcy of giant retailer Toys ‘R’ Us. He will oversee the day-to-day operations while Ellison focuses on creative and strategy. “I feel like if I’m there [at Skydance], I feel like I’m happy to see him,” CNBC host David Faber joked, gesturing at Ellison. “I’m not so sure if I’m happy to see you coming down the hall.” “We’re in it together,” the co-CEOs said in unision. ‘Baywatch’, ‘Shaka iLembe’ & ‘Maya’ In Deadline Dozen; ‘Heated Rivalry’s Crave Brad Bird On The Long Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To Cinemas Maggie Gyllenhaal, Michelle Yeoh, Alfonso & Jonás Cuarón On Cinema’s Future Skydance Film Bosses & WB To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In Works Or On Fire More from this Story Arc Skydance October 8, 2026 David Decker Lands Top Content Sales Role At Skydance With Jay Askinasi Overseeing Ads, Ray Hopkins Leading Distribution October 8, 2026 David Ellison Calls Skydance “Solution” To Mistakes Ten Years Ago When Big Tech Moved In On Media View All Story Arc Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘NAZA’ Producer James Wilson Addresses “Hysterical, Vituperative” Israeli Government Backlash Against Directors
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie ‘NAZA’ Producer James Wilson Addresses “Hysterical, Vituperative” Israeli Government Backlash Against Directors Oscars: Rwanda Makes History As ‘Ben’Imana’ Becomes First Official Entry; Alexander Set U.S. & UK Release Hande Erçel To Star In Nader Saeivar’s Berlin-Set Drama ‘Diaspora’ View All October 8, 2026 7:31am Add us as a Google Preferred Source James Wilson at the 2026 Annual Golden Globe Awards Amy Sussman/Getty Images) NAZA producer James Wilson has addressed the Israeli government and military backlash against co-directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor over their bombshell documentary exposing Israel ’s deliberate targeting of civilian targets in Gaza. Wilson told an onstage conversation on his career at the BFI London Film Festival that criticism of the film and threats against the directors were largely from people who had not seen the work. He said the “hysterical, vituperative, aggressive backlash” from members of the Israeli government and threats to revoke the directors’ citizenship had been been “very difficult, stressful, horrible and scary”. Related Stories News Grace Harper Brighouse On Bringing Her Camden Film Festival-Winning Doc 'Dependence' Back Home To London -- LFF News Brad Bird On The 30-Year Journey To Bring 'Ray Gunn' To The Big Screen -- London Film Festival “They are safe, and they are okay,” he added, suggesting that the reaction from the Israeli government also came with the territory. Watch on Deadline “I think it’s part of the film,” he said citing a piece by an Israeli journalist in the Jewish American newspaper Forward. “She wrote about the reaction to the film being part of the film, and how the sort of cognitive dissonance, around that reaction of people who haven’t seen the film talking about the film, was sort of what the film was also about,” he said. “There’s a sort of meta aspect to that reaction to the film that the film embodies.” Wilson emphasized, however, that the overwhelming response to the documentary had been positive, even if the subject-matter is difficult. “The majority reaction to the film has been, from my point of view, extremely positive, and I’m personally very pleased at that. The critical reaction to the film has been extraordinarily positive,” he said. “One thing that’s been particularly pleasing to me is how many serious film critics have discussed and thought into the cinematic formal ideas in the film… it’s a really important piece of cinema in terms of its content, but also its form.” Framed around nighttime rooftop interviews against the backdrop of the Tel Aviv skyline with 24 Israeli intelligence officers and soldiers, the documentary exposes the AI, phone surveillance and crude points-based systems deployed by the Israeli military in Gaza to decide targets, Hamas-related or otherwise. It probes the Israeli military’s strategy of taking out targets in their homes regardless of whether children and other family members are likely to be killed in the strike as well. The title NAZA is taken from the Israeli military’s Hebrew acronym to describe the number of civilians that could die when tallying up an estimated death-toll ahead of a strike. articles.title: Prime Video Thriller ‘The Assassin’ Gets Season 2 Trailer And Launch Date In UK & Ireland
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Prime Video Thriller ‘The Assassin’ Gets Season 2 Trailer And Launch Date In UK & Ireland Lauren Ash, Mae Martin & Randall Park Join Crave Comedy ‘Meatballs’ The Deadline Dozen: The Hottest Scripted Shows Heading To MIPCOM Including ‘Baywatch’, ‘Einstein’ & ‘Maya’ Starring Bella Ramsey View All October 8, 2026 7:34am Add us as a Google Preferred Source “If anyone can get this done, it’s your mother,” Freddie Highmore ‘s Edward hears in the first trailer for Prime Video thriller The Assassin Season 2. Amazon’s streaming service has released a trailer and penciled in a November 6 launch date for the show in the UK and Ireland. Banijay Rights is selling piecemeal elsewhere, except in Germany, where ZDF has the show, and Australia, where it is on Stan. The Assassin stars Keeley Hawes as the mother in question, Julie, opposite Highmore, who plays her son. Season 2’s trailer shows hitwoman Julie reluctantly teaming up with Edward once again, when his dream honeymoon with Kayla (Shalom Brune-Franklin) is hijacked and his new wife taken hostage. “The honeymoon… couldn’t get any worse,” deadpans Edward as he reveals the news to his mom. Related Stories News Bryan Fuller & Don Mancini Make Surprise Cameo In 'Carrie' Prom Scene News 'Carrie's Matthew Lillard & Amber Midthunder On How The "Catastrophic" Finale Deviates From The Book: "It's Part Of The Tragedy" The pair are then thrown back into a world of high-speed car chases, international crime and kidnapping in Spain, as their fragile relationship is tested to the core. Watch on Deadline Also returning alongside Hawes, Highmore and Brune-Franklin is Devon Terrell, with Arnaud Bindard, Natalia Tena, Boris Van Severen, Jacqueline Boatswain and Monic Hendrickx joining the cast along with Karl El-Santos, Mehdi Regragui, Casimiro Aguza, Tony Corvillo, Amin Hamada and Lolo Herrero. Two Brothers Pictures produced the show for Prime Video UK and Ireland, ZDF in Germany and Stan in Australia in association with Banijay Entertainment stablemate Banijay Rights. Harry and Jack Williams, who both also serve as executive producers, are the writers, with Sarah Hammond, Alex Mercer and Daisy Mount also serving as EPs for Two Brothers Pictures, and Hawes and Highmore also serving in the same roles. John Griffin is producer with Terry McDonough, another executive producer – directing episodes 1-3 and Sarah O’Gorman directing episodes 4-6. Jessica Mescall serves as casting director. articles.title: Michael Douglas Was Third Choice For Gordon Gekko; How He Rode ‘Wall Street’s Slick Villain To Oscar Glory
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Michael Douglas Michael Douglas More Stories By Michael Michael Douglas Was Third Choice For Gordon Gekko; How He Rode ‘Wall Street’s Slick Villain To Oscar Glory View All October 8, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Wall Street' Courtesy 'One Helluva Ride' EXCLUSIVE: Editor’s note: Mike Fleming Jr . here. For the better part of last year, my day began with a 6 a.m. call and an hour with Michael Douglas for his memoir One Helluva Ride . It was early for me, but always worth catching MD someplace in Europe, where he enjoys the fruits of his long run as Hollywood superstar with his wife Catherine Zeta-Jones and their family. Written by Douglas, Shane Salerno and me, the memoir One Helluva Ride was released Tuesday by Grand Central Publishing. Details revealed by Douglas about his colorful personal life have dominated headlines this week; we thought Deadline readers would be most interested in the dissection of the seminal film that helped forge a great career. Related Stories News Oliver Stone: Director’s Career In Photos Casting Michael Douglas, Willem Dafoe, Ellen Barkin, Homer Gere And Yvonne Chapman Join Oliver Stone’s Next Pic ‘White Lies’ Douglas started with a difficult task, trying to forge an identity out of the long shadow cast by his father, Kirk Douglas. Douglas got his first movie boost as a producer, sharing the Best Picture Oscar for One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest, and capturing the Zeitgeist with The China Syndrome. His onscreen rise took longer. The producer in Douglas helped the actor in him by prizing good scripts above all else. The best of those meant playing flawed characters, and Douglas came to relish seeing how far he could push that envelope and still have audiences on his side. The book tells Douglas’ story through a dozen of his most memorable films – Romancing the Stone, Fatal Attraction, Basic Instinct, Traffic, Falling Down and The War of the Roses among them — and The Streets of San Francisco, the TV series with Karl Malden that helped forge Douglas’ work ethic and prepared him to produce Cuckoo’s Nest with the late Saul Zaentz . The following excerpt focuses on Wall Street , the film that emboldened Douglas to take the kind of risks many of his actor peers didn’t dare. Pushed relentlessly by Oliver Stone, Douglas turned the corporate raider Gordon Gekko into a defining villain of ’80s films. That turn paved the way for everything that followed. As Michael writes in the book’s intro, “I can’t think about my life without thinking of my movies. Six of the eight decades I’ve lived on this planet have been spent making films—they have always been my landmarks, the way I mark time.” Here, he takes us back to Wall Street, the film that allowed him to play any role and have audiences show up on the weekend, just to see what he got himself into next, and how he was going to get out of it. ‘I had never played the bad guy’ I’d never played the bad guy. In Fatal Attraction I had played a guy who made a bad decision and spent the rest of the movie trying to make up for it. But he wasn’t a real villain. Dad always thought I should play a part as cunning and manipulative as his famous character in The Bad and the Beautiful , the ruthless Hollywood producer Jonathan Shields. He told me, “You’re so likable, Michael, but when you finally play a bad guy, you’re going to surprise a lot of people who think you can only do the nice-guy stuff. I know the darkness under there.”

articles.title: Oscars: Democratic Republic Of Congo Selects ‘Rumba Royale’ For Best International Feature Film Race; The Fally Ipupa Starrer Is Country’s Second Ever Submission
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Diana Lodderhose Diana Lodderhose International Features Editor @dianalodderhose More Stories By Diana ‘Fjord’, ‘All Of A Sudden’, ‘Minotaur’ & ‘Coward’ Among Titles Set For 30th Edition Of The American French Film Festival In L.A. It’s a historic milestone for Congolese cinema in that the film is the second ever film submitted by the country for the category following its first submission in 1997 with Macadam Tribu . Directed by Yohane Dean Lengol and Hamed Mobasser, Rumba Royale is set in 1959 Leopoldville, the former capital of Belgian Congo (which is now called Kinshasa), in the final months of Belgian colonial rule. It was a time when the pulsating rhythms of rumba set nightlife alight. The story takes place around the Club Rumba Royale, where white Europeans and Congolese citizens rub shoulders, and where the captivating melodies of rumba merge with aspirations and fiery debates of independence. Related Stories News Oscars: Rwanda Makes History As 'Ben'Imana' Becomes First Official Entry; Alexander Set U.S. & UK Release News Oscars: Saudi Arabia Submits 'A Matter Of Life & Death' For Best International Feature Film The story follows photographer Daniel, played by African rumba star Fally Ipupa , as political change, personal ambition and tragedy reshape the world around him. Watch on Deadline Produced and filmed in Kinshasa, the project brought together Congolese actors, technicians, craftspeople, musicians and emerging film professionals in an environment where the local industry continues to develop despite limited infrastructure, production resources and financing opportunities. The project is the brainchild of writers Kevin Dwyer and Mobasser, the latter of whom is a Belgian diplomat based in Washington D.C. who also co-directs the title. “ Rumba Royale demonstrates the extraordinary stories that can emerge when local talent is given the opportunity to create at scale,” said the filmmakers. “This selection is a celebration of Congolese creativity, resilience and ambition. We hope it helps shine a light not only on this film, but on the growing community of filmmakers across the region whose work deserves greater international attention and support.” ‘Baywatch’, ‘Shaka iLembe’ & ‘Maya’ In Deadline Dozen; ‘Heated Rivalry’s Crave Brad Bird On The Long Journey To Bring ‘Ray Gunn’ To Cinemas Maggie Gyllenhaal, Michelle Yeoh, Alfonso & Jonás Cuarón On Cinema’s Future Skydance Film Bosses & WB To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In Works Or On Fire Read More About: Comments

articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy How ‘Chicago Fire’ Star Dermot Mulroney Exits Series Hulu Legal Drama ‘Conviction’ Casts Michael Gaston, F. Murray Abraham & Peter Friedman Apple TV’s ‘Beat The Reaper’ Casts Paul Schulze & Tony Macht View All October 8, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Karen Read / Elizabeth Banks Getty Images Prime Video has ordered a new series about Karen Read , starring and executive produced by Elizabeth Banks ( Cocaine Bear, Pitch Perfect ). The as-yet-untitled project is inspired by the Law&Crime and Audible Original podcast Karen, about the woman who was at the center of a high-profile murder case that accused Read of killing her boyfriend, Boston police officer John O’Keefe, on a snowy night in 2002. Following a highly watched and discussed trial, Read was acquitted of second-degree murder and manslaughter, but was found guilty of other charges. Deadline exclusively announced the project was in development back in August . Related Stories News Bryan Fuller & Don Mancini Make Surprise Cameo In 'Carrie' Prom Scene News 'Carrie's Matthew Lillard & Amber Midthunder On How The "Catastrophic" Finale Deviates From The Book: "It's Part Of The Tragedy" The drama series will be written, showrun, and executive produced by Justin Noble ( The Sex Lives of College Girls , Brooklyn Nine-Nine ) and hails from Warner Bros. Television, Brownstone Productions, David E. Kelley Productions, Audible, and Law&Crime. Watch on Deadline Based on a true story, the series tells the story of a Boston police officer who is found dead in the snow during a blizzard; all eyes are on his girlfriend, Karen Read. But when she and her legal team claim she’s not only innocent, but that she’s the victim of a conspiracy protecting the real assailants, the story spreads like wildfire, dividing a community in ways they’ve never seen. As endless suspicion mounts in multiple directions, this genre-bending true crime series explores society’s explosive obsession with true crime. “I grew up in Massachusetts, and like so many people there, we watched this case divide families, friends, and entire towns,” said Banks. “We have spent years with this material because the questions it raises go far beyond one courtroom: why we choose the stories we believe, and what happens when trust in our institutions breaks down. Justin has written a series that respects and treats with care the complexity of what happened and the public reaction to it,” she added. Adding, Noble said, “This case has more twists and turns than any story I’ve ever consumed, real or fictional. “It makes M. Night Shyamalan look like Nora Ephron. But the reason this story resonates and must be told is because of the profound takeaways it leaves us with: about a deeply imperfect justice system that urgently needs change, about the mistreatment of women by those who weaponize and abuse their power, and about a victim who deserves to be remembered.” In addition to Banks and Noble, the project is executive produced by Max Handelman, as well as Krissy Wall via Brownstone Productions; David E. Kelley and Matthew Tinker via David E.
