articles.title: Pixar, Lionsgate and Paramount Nab $100 Million in California Tax Credits
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Winston Cho Plus Icon Winston Cho View All October 7, 2026 8:00am Jaafar Jackson stars as his real-life uncle in the biopic 'Michael.' Kevin Mazur/Lionsgate Pixar, Lionsgate and Paramount led the way in the latest round of tax credits granted to productions by California’s film office for shooting in the state. Combined, the 35 movies that will spend roughly $635.3 million across 1,049 shoot days were awarded $226.1 million. They include 28 independent movies, eight of which have budgets above $10 million. Pixar took the largest award, receiving $40.1 million for an untitled animated feature, as animated productions continue to emerge as a force in California’s tax credit program. The jobs ratio used to select productions appears to favor animation since the category is often more labor-intensive than live-action, generating higher below-the-line spending relative to the total production budget. Family Guy spinoff Stewie , Dan Harmon’s President Curtis and four animated titles from Disney, DreamWorks and Pixar, among others, have already been tapped to get subsidies. Next up, Lionsgate’s Michael 2 (working title), the sequel to the studio’s Michael Jackson biopic, nabbed $30.8 million. with an untitled crime thriller from Paramount coming in third with a $29.3 million award. Disney was another major recipient for an untitled live-action feature, which got $18 million. Warner Bros. also received $13 million for an untitled comedy, while 20th Century Studios was awarded $12.2 million for an untitled horror film. “California is the home of entertainment, full stop,” said Gov. Gavin Newsom in a statement. “We’re not just protecting that legacy; we’re investing in its future by expanding our film and television tax credit, launching a new post-production credit, and standing up for performers in the age of AI.” New Line Cinema’s Last Friday , the latest installment to the Ice Cube-led franchise, also received $11.4 million. “I’m thrilled to produce Last Friday right here in Southern California, where our cast and crew lives,” said Ice Cube in a statement. “This story has been part of the fabric of South Los Angeles since our first film 31 years ago so producing the film here with more than 180 local cast and crew underscores the value of the California production incentive program. Among the larger awards for independent productions: $7 million for South Beach ; $6.7 million for Maniac Cop ; $5.8 million for animated feature Shine ; and $5.5 million for Jump Off . “Our film is set in the Chicano communities of Los Angeles, and it simply wouldn’t exist if we couldn’t shoot here,” said Victoria Alonso and Tom Culliver, producers of Leaves of Glass. “We are incredibly excited to showcase a side of Los Angeles rarely seen on camera, and work with the greatest crews in the world. We are deeply grateful to the California Film Commission for making this film possible.” THR

articles.title: Disney+ Will Stream the 2027 Super Bowl and ‘New Year’s Rockin’ Eve’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 7, 2026 8:33am The Vince Lombardi trophy. Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images What may be the biggest live event in the history of The Walt Disney Co. is coming to Disney+ . Next year’s Super Bowl LXI will be the first for ESPN in the sport media brand’s history, and its parent company is going all-in to make it as widely accessible as possible. That includes a simulcast on ABC, of course, alternate broadcasts like the Manningcast, and, Disney announced Wednesday, streaming simulcast available on Disney+ in both English and Spanish. Disney will also make two Monday Night Football games available to stream on Disney+ later this fall, expanding the roster of included live sports (meant to entice streaming users to ESPN, which streams every game), as well as Dick Clark’s New Year’s Rockin’ Eve with Ryan Seacrest , the company’s flagship New Year’s show, and one of the top live broadcasts of the year. Related Stories Business Disney+ Strikes Streaming Bundle and Content-Sharing Deal With Indonesia's Vidio TV 'Dancing With the Stars' Sets Super Bowl Night Seacrest will once again be joined by Rita Ora in New York and Julianne Hough and NFL legend Rob Gronkowski in Las Vegas, with Druski hosting from Chicago. The Super Bowl stream will make the game widely available to consumers given the accessibility of both ABC and Disney+, not to mention pay-TV. While Disney+ is a paid service (and the company no longer reports subscriber figures) it is widely accepted as the second most-scaled streamer in the U.S. after Netflix. The Disney+ partnership underscores how Disney is leaning into the Super Bowl, which it kicked off right after this year’s Super Bowl ended. The company plans to leverage every part of its portfolio, from theme parks to films to products and experiences to drive awareness to the 2027 Super Bowl and the fact that it will be ESPN’s first (the company will turn Santa Monica Beach into ESPN Beach as part of the takeover). The company is sold out of advertising inventory, but is seeking advertisers willing to get on a reserve list in case extra inventory becomes available. Both the 2027 Super Bowl and New Year’s Rockin’ Eve also epitomizes the company’s digital strategy under CEO Josh D’Amaro, who wants Disney+ to become the “digital centerpiece” of the company . That will ultimately include experiences and games, but it also means that the biggest live events will need to be there too. THR

articles.title: DEVO Frontman Mark Mothersbaugh on 1970s Pop Band Predicting Today’s Politics: “It’s Gone Really Dark Again”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 7, 2026 8:39am Mark Mothersbaugh Courtesy of subject It’s déjà vu all over again for DEVO frontman and veteran composer Mark Mothersbaugh, who co-founded the iconic 1970s and 1980s rock band during its own dark political era. “It’s gone really dark again. We’re in a really dark place now, where we have greed and racism not hiding at all. They’re proud and displaying themselves, and it’s shocking that it could be this strong,” Mothersbaugh tells The Hollywood Reporter from the Vancouver Film Festival . Mothersbaugh and his fellow DEVO co-founders, including Gerald “Jerry” Casale, formed the band in the wake of the May 4, 1970 Kent State University shootings of students by National Guardsmen, where they were also students. As they attempted to make sense of the tragedy, their resulting rock band was named DEVO, or short for de-evolution. Related Stories TV 'The Cadburys': BritBox Drops First Look at Chocolate Empire Drama (Exclusive) Movies 'Prince' Is a Stylized Cinematic Battle Royal With a Show Dog, His Owner, Her Butler and Their Family That way, the band members as “social scientists” aimed to satirically comment on humanity descending into a state of moral and physical regression. And they shot the 1976 short film In the Beginning Was the End: The Truth About De-Evolution , directed by Chuck Statler and starring Castle, Jim Mothersbaugh, Mark Mothersbaugh and Robert Mothersbaugh. DEVO Courtesy of Sundance Institute “It had two songs, but we were doing music with pictures pretty much from the beginning,” Mothersbaugh recalled. DEVO also gained a following with hit satirical songs like “Whip It” and “Mongoloid” in the wake of the 1950s Atomic Bomb scare and the 1962 Cuban missile crisis that, like generative artificial intelligence today, posed a possible extinction risk for humanity, the band frontman insisted. “With the atomic bomb, there were a lot of different opportunities for something really stupid and horrifying to happen. It could be the same with AI, with many things that are dark and not for the betterment of humans,” Mothersbaugh explained. While occasionally touring with DEVO, he has become a prolific composer of music for movies, TV series and commercials and video games. “It’s like another set of colors of paint to work with,” Mothersbaugh adds about composing being a part of his wider ambition as a multi-media artist that includes scores to The Lego Movie and 21 Jump Street . Having written music for around 100 film and TV series, he has worked extensively with Wes Anderson on Bottle Rocket, Rushmore, The Royal Tennenbaums and The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou. “He’s a true artist,” Mothersbaugh says of his symbiotic collaboration with Anderson in his Sunset Boulevard studio in Los Angeles where they would discuss original DEVO synthesizers and other vintage gear to create quirky soundscapes for movie orchestrations. “(Anderson) spent more time with me than a lot of directors did.” DEVO Courtesy of Sundance Institute Mothersbaugh also worked closely with Taika Waititi on his 2017 Marvel superhero pic Thor: Ragnarok , which led to an ‘80s-tinged score with hints of superhero anthems. And to his side on set was often a curious Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige, the producer behind the most successful run of movies in Hollywood. “I didn’t even know who he (Feige) was at first. He’d come in when I was playing music for Taika, and there’d be this guy sitting there. And then we started talking and he was really interested,” Mothersbaugh recounted. And he was also working with Waititi as he graduated from making arthouse movies to the big-budget superhero movie world. “Taika went from being this little guy in New Zealand to all of a sudden being in charge of this giant film costing $100 million, $150 million, whatever it costs,” Mothersbaugh said of the Oscar-winning Jojo Rabbit director making his mark in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. The DEVO frontman is currently juggling composing music for three feature films, alongside TV series and video games. “I do love writing music and I do love making art and I feel so fortunate,” he said. That leaves little room for thoughts of retirement, which Mothersbaugh did bring up with his wife and manager Anita Greenspan, but only briefly. “My wife told me, you’re not going to retire. You’ll slump over the podium and they’ll lift you up and carry you out of the room. That’s how you’re going to go,” he recalled of her response. That grim death foretold concerns Mothersbaugh, he admits. “It makes me nervous, because she’s also my agent,” he said. THR

articles.title: Grammy Predictions: It’s a Race Between Olivia and Olivia
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Illustration by Andrew Archer If you knew a year ago that the next 12 months would yield albums from Taylor Swift, Harry Styles and Bruno Mars, you probably would have placed your bets on Grammy nominations right then. But as the announcement of the finalists for the 2026 awards approaches, none of those juggernauts feels like frontrunners for the big prizes. Instead, the spotlight has pivoted to two 20-something women named Olivia. Those superstar releases certainly weren’t flops; Swift’s The Life of a Showgirl was the fastest-selling album of all time, and Styles is in the middle of a record-breaking 30-night stand at Madison Square Garden, while Bruno Mars spent much of the year near the top of the charts with The Romantic lead single “I Just Might.” But for three historic Grammy darlings who’ve all won album of the year over the course of the past decade, they all ultimately seemed to come up short either commercially or critically and don’t quite carry the expected enthusiasm or momentum into awards season. Related Stories Movies Actor Jack Reynor to Be Honored at the Oscar Wilde Awards (Exclusive) THR Cover Story Olivia Rodrigo: The Queen of Sad Finds Her Happy Place Bruno Mars Kevin Mazur/Getty Images As Grammy season comes into full swing, one of the biggest questions the Recording Academy will need to wrestle with is how to handle the current surge in popularity for country music. In September, for the first time ever, the top five slots on the singles chart were all held by country songs — most notably, Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas,” which recently broke the record for longest stay at No. 1. Langley seems an obvious lock for best new artist, but the academy has steered clear of Nashville when it comes to the big awards; the only “mainstream” country releases ever to win album of the year were Swift’s 2010 Fearless and Glen Campbell’s By the Time I Get to Phoenix in 1968. (Kacey Musgraves’ Golden Hour won in 2019, though that’s more of an alternative country album than a traditional country radio-friendly project.) Ella Langley Courtesy of Columbia Records Meanwhile, Morgan Wallen (whose Still the Problem Tour just became the highest-grossing country tour in history) continues to boycott the Grammys, as does Drake, whose three 2026 albums and summer anthem “Janice STFU” may otherwise have been in awards contention. Adding to this ongoing mess, BTS opted not to submit their album Arirang , protesting the addition of a new K-pop category, which they believe will hinder Korean artists’ chances for consideration for the general pop awards. So with all of those options either off the table or looking at diminished expectations, that brings us to Olivia Rodrigo and Olivia Dean . Both previous best new artist winners, both beloved across multiple genres, they’re clearly the acts in pole position in a year when it’s unlikely that any one artist is going to dominate the ceremonies. Rodrigo’s New Wave-inflected You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love tips toward younger fans and garners more of a rock following, while Dean’s The Art of Loving leans R&B with a more mature audience. Rodrigo’s album, released in June, could benefit from recency bias, coupled with the buzz around her Daisy Chain Fields Music Festival, but Dean has a case for longevity, still parked in the top 10 after a full year. Olivia Rodrigo, Noah Kahan and Olivia Dean JMEnternational/Getty Images; Joseph Okpako/WireImage; Christopher Polk/Billboard/Getty Images Both are sure things for album of the year nods, with a possible slight edge to You Seem Pretty Sad , constructed as more of a top-to-bottom “album” chronicling the beginning, middle and end of a relationship. Elsewhere in the category, British soulstress Raye’s This Music May Contain Hope wasn’t the same commercial smash, though she’s still the kind of ambitious, old-school artist that Grammy voters like — as is Noah Kahan, whose The Great Divide will get the recognition that his powerhouse Stick Season was denied. Even if Swift’s Showgirl and Bruno Mars’ The Romantic haven’t gotten the same reception as their best loved works, they still seem too big to fail and likely will get nominated. If any “legacy” artists make the cut, signs point to Madonna — whose Confessions II was widely lauded as her strongest effort in 20 years, a more compelling story than steady new albums from Paul McCartney and The Rolling Stones. At the cool kids table, Rosalía’s jaw-dropping Lux was a (deserving) critical favorite and, following last year’s win for Bad Bunny’s Debí Tirar Más Fotos , it would be a bad look not to include a Spanish-language artist. From the indie rock world, Phoebe Bridgers’ Lost Weekend is her acclaimed solo return after 2023’s seven-times-nominated, three-time Grammy-winning boygenius album The Record . Rosalía Kevin Mazur/Getty Images It was a quiet year for hip-hop, so while J. Cole’s “farewell album” The Fall-Off and Don Toliver’s Octane are remote possibilities to sneak into a nomination slot, for the Grammys, it increasingly feels like Kendrick Lamar or nothing. Musgraves’ Middle of Nowhere was considered a return to form, but if voters lean into a country project, it’s hard to imagine anything other than Langley’s Dandelion getting the nod this year. Which leaves Styles as the odd man out. If the sin of Mars’ album was being too predictable, Styles’ bold and unexpected Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally was tougher for fans and, likely, for Grammy voters; the album sunk rapidly on the charts and (despite the support that led to Harry’s House winning the album prize in 2023 over Adele, Beyoncé and Lamar) could come up short this time. Both Olivias also will feature in the record and song of the year categories, with Ms. Dean’s breezy, omnipresent “Man I Need” a favorite. It’s not clear which songs Rodrigo will submit where — maybe “Drop Dead” goes stronger as a recording and “The Cure” is a better fit for the songwriters’ award, but we shall see. Raye’s irrepressible “Where Is My Husband!” is a clear record of the year contender, and “Choosin’ Texas” feels certain to make it to the finals. Kahan’s title track, Tame Impala and Jennie’s collaboration “Vampire” and Mars’ “I Just Might” are in the running, and Sienna Spiro’s “Die on This Hill” has made her the latest U.K. pop-soul crossover (in the tradition of Amy Winehouse, Adele, etc.), a sound that consistently plays into Grammy voters’ tastes. Song of the year will offer most of the same names as the record of the year picks, though here Dean might switch her entry to “So Easy (To Fall in Love),” co-written by Grammy favorite Amy Allen. Longer shots include Styles’ “Aperture,” PinkPantheress and Zara Larsson’s “Stateside” and Brandi Carlile’s battle cry for the U.S. Constitution, “Church and State.” Then of course there’s T-Swift, who despite her legendary legacy has never won for record or song of the year. “The Fate of Ophelia” was a huge hit, spending 12 weeks at No. 1. But “I Knew It, I Knew You,” from the Toy Story 5 soundtrack, marked her return to country radio and might read as more of a “songwriter” song; when she recently did a rare interview event with Grammy CEO Harvey Mason Jr., it was the one Grammy-eligible song she performed. Taylor Swift, The Life of a Showgirl Courtesy of Mert Alaz & Marcus Piggott/TAS Rights Management The smart money says that she splits the difference, putting “The Fate of Ophelia” up for record and saving “I Knew It, I Knew You” for song. Overall, her focus seems set on winning an Oscar for “I Knew It, I Knew You,” which seems inevitable. In a year when there’s a strong chance four different women will carry away the Big Four trophies, Swift will have positioned herself to wind up, once again, as Music’s Biggest Story. This story appeared in the Oct. 7 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

articles.title: ‘The Hunting Wives’ Lands Early Season 3 Renewal at Netflix
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jackie Strause Plus Icon Jackie Strause Managing Editor, East Coast jackiedstrause Follow Sign Up View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Malin Akerman and Brittany Snow in 'The Hunting Wives' season one. Kent Smith/Netflix Logo text The Hunting Wives have hit their mark — and landed an early renewal. The Netflix series from Rebecca Cutter starring Malin Akerman and Brittany Snow , who lead a cutthroat yet soapy set of Texas housewives, has nabbed a season three renewal ahead of season two’s return. Season two, which was announced in September, returns Thanksgiving Day (Nov. 26) with the original (surviving) cast reprising their roles. The third season will be another eight episodes, with a release date and cast yet to be announced. Related Stories Movies Ava DuVernay Returns With One of Netflix's Most Political Docs Ever: "This Movie Kicked My Butt" TV Jamie Foxx Does Not Want to Be Canceled Over New Hulu Stand-up Special: "After That Kevin Hart Roast, I Had to Cut Everything" The Hunting Wives , adapted by showrunner Cutter from the bestselling novel of the same name by May Cobb, became a 2025 summer sensation for Netflix when it released season one . “I’m so stoked to be heading back to Maple Brook, and I promise that once you’ve finished season two, you’ll be desperate to see what happens next. Buckle up, because season three will be even more scandalous and twisted,” Cutter said on Wednesday in a statement about the early renewal. Cutter’s statement implies that similar to season one , season two could also end on a cliffhanger. ( Snow has already teased a big death to come.) The sexy and binge-y thriller, which was originally developed for Starz, is a Lionsgate Television and 3 Arts Entertainment production and will release both season two and three on the streamer as a Netflix-branded series. Producers pivoted the series to Netflix in the lead up to Starz’s official split from Lionsgate and released The Hunting Wives weeks later, on July 21. It became the most-viewed streaming series in the U.S. and spent six weeks in Nielsen’s top 10 chart of streaming originals. Created by writer/showrunner/EP Cutter ( Hightown ), Hunting Wives is also executive produced by Erwin Stoff for 3 Arts Entertainment and Cobb. THR

articles.title: ‘Anna Pigeon’ Renewed for Second Season on USA
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Tracy Spiridakos (center) as the title character in USA's 'Anna Pigeon.' Michelle Faye/USA Network Logo text USA Network ‘s rebuild of a scripted series roster continues with the renewal of Anna Pigeon . The cable outlet has picked up a second season of the show, which stars Tracy Spiridakos ( Chicago PD ) as a crime-solving national park ranger. The renewal for Anna Pigeon , which is based on a series of novels by Nevada Barr, comes two days before its Oct. 9 season finale. “It’s been really thrilling to see audiences fall in love with Anna and come to the park every week,” showrunner Morwyn Brebner said in a release announcing the renewal. “We’re so grateful to our cast and crew who brought Nevada Barr’s iconic world to life with such heart and passion; we cannot wait to get back outside for season two.” Related Stories TV Why Now Was the Time for Golf Channel to Revive 'Big Break' TV Medical Drama 'Diplomatic Immunity' Scores USA Series Order Produced by Cineflix and Seven24 Films, Anna Pigeon has drawn decent ratings for USA: Its series premiere drew 2.35 million viewers over seven days, making it the best debut for a USA scripted show since 2018. The show is the No. 1 new scripted drama on ad-supported cable for the year so far. “ Anna Pigeon has connected with audiences in a meaningful way, bringing a compelling new heroine and a fresh perspective to USA Network,” said Michael Sluchan, senior vp scripted content for Versant Entertainment. “We’re thrilled to continue Anna’s journey with Tracy, Morwyn, [director and executive producer Lea Thompson] and our incredible partners at Cineflix.” The Versant-owned USA is slowly building up a slate of scripted series that harken back to the network’s “blue skies” era of the 2000s and 2010s (under NBCUniversal). Along with Anna Pigeon , USA has the John Grisham legal drama The Rainmaker — whose second season premieres Oct. 16 — and the recently ordered Diplomatic Immunity , about a doctor assigned to the U.S. embassy in Rome. Brebner ( Rookie Blue, Crew Girl ) and Thompson executive produce Anna Pigeon with Brett Burlock, Sonia Hosko, Todd Berger, Julie Di Cresce, Tom Cox, Jordy Randall, Peter Emerson and Gordon Gilbertson. Leslie Cowan serves as producer. THR

articles.title: Creator Maurice Kamara Signs With UTA (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Maurice Kamara Courtesy of UTA Maurice Kamara, the cultural tastemaker behind The People Gallery online fashion page, has signed with United Talent Agency for representation . The People Gallery features man-on-the-street style interviews with celebrities like Oprah Winfrey, Pamela Anderson and Michael B. Jordan at fashion shows and other events or just New Yorkers showing their street style when out and about. “Let’s see your fit, describe it for us,” Kamara will often say from behind the camera as he opens the celebrity encounters. Leveraging over 3 million followers across TikTok and Instagram, The People Gallery also increasingly offers an online voice for brands Kamara partners with. “What began as Kamara stopping stylish strangers on the streets of New York has grown into a global platform documenting the people, personalities, and perspectives shaping culture across fashion, music, sports, and beyond,” the agency said in a statement. The UTA Creators division will expand Kamara’s opportunities in digital media, brand partnerships, sports and other platforms. The signing comes as Kamara builds on his brand partnerships and high-profile appearances, including an upcoming collaboration with UGG and a cameo in Drake’s recently released short film FOMO. Brooklyn native Kamara after over 15 years in high end retail also now attends Met Gala and fashion weeks around the world and is the subject of New York Times and GQ profiles. UTA was early to the creators game, launching a dedicated digital talent group in 2006 to identify and represent category-leading creators across emerging and established platforms. THR

articles.title: Julio Peña Joins Josh Heuston, Nicole Wallace in Amazon MGM’s ‘Throttled’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexy Perez Plus Icon Lexy Perez Senior Digital Editor and Producer View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Julio Peña, Nicole Wallace and Josh Heuston Isaac Morell; Pablo Curto; Aurore Marechal/Getty Images Julio Peña has joined the cast of Amazon MGM Studios ‘ Throttled , an upcoming film based on the book from Lauren Ashers’ Dirty Air series. The actor joins previously announced stars Nicole Wallace (the Culpa Mia trilogy) and Josh Heuston ( Off Campus ). In the upcoming romance from Amazon MGM Studios, Peña will play Santi Alatorre, “the older brother of Maya Alatorre (portrayed by Wallace) and a driver on the racing circuit whose teammate and fiercest rival, Noah Slade (Heuston), falls into a forbidden romance with Maya.“ Related Stories TV Peacock's 'The Good Daughter' Trailer: Rose Byrne, Meghann Fahy Attempt to Solve Small-Town Murder in Suspenseful Thriller Series TV Inside the Shocking Decision to End 'Young Sheldon' at Its Peak (Exclusive Excerpt) The trio shared a social media post to announce Peña‘s casting. In their video, Wallace and Heuston are seen talking privately, only for Peña to interrupt and squeeze in the middle of them. “Welcome to the team,” Heuston says to Peña, only for Peña to shake his hand and respond, “Thanks! Just stay away from my sister.“ He then hugs Wallace while Heuston laughs it off saying, “You bet!“ Melissa Osborne ( My Fault: London , My Oxford Year ) will adapt the script and Nzingha Stewart ( Daisy Jones & the Six ) is set to direct. Max Handelman and Elizabeth Banks of Brownstone Productions are producing along with Ethea Entertainment’s Jennifer Gibgot and Andrew Panay, who recently produced The Last Sunrise , Prime’s film adaptation of Anna Todd‘s bestselling romance novel. Garrett Grant is also producing, with Alison Small of Brownstone Productions and Asher executive producing. Asher‘s 2020 book Throttled is the first of four books in the Dirty Air sports romance series. The adaptation marks another addition to Amazon MGM‘s building library of book-to-screen adaptations , including Off Campus , Every Year After and The Love Hypothesis. Peña is best known for his work in the Through My Window t rilogy on Netflix, whose first installment logged 68 million views in its first two weeks. He recently wrapped the untitled Meta series based on A24’s Talk to Me . Last year he starred in The Captive, which premiered at TIFF and earned him a Goya Award nomination for best new actor. Peña also stars in the Money Heist Netflix spinoff Berlin . Peña is represented by Anonymous Content, YouRock Talent Partners, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman Wertheimer Mandelbaum Morris Bernstein Trattner Auerbach Hynick Jaime LeVine Sample & Klein. THR

articles.title: Oscars: Saudi Arabia Picks ‘A Matter of Life and Death’ as Best Int’l Feature Submission
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 7, 2026 9:00am 'A Matter of Life and Death' Courtesy of Front Row The Saudi Film Commission has selected Anas Ba Tahaf‘s A Matter of Life and Death as Saudi Arabia’s official submission for the best international feature film Oscar category at the 99th Academy Awards. Written by and starring Sarah Taibah alongside Yaqoub Al Farhan, the film is produced by Film Clinic, Front Row Filmed Entertainment and Arabia Pictures, with Front Row handling international sales. The film is set in contemporary Jeddah and blends romance, fantasy and black comedy in a highly stylized visual world. “At heart, it is a love story, just not the safe kind,” a description of the movie notes. “At its center is Hayat, a fiercely independent young woman convinced that a generational curse will kill her on her 30th birthday. Having made peace with dying, she crosses paths with Yousef, a brilliant but emotionally detached heart surgeon living with bradycardia. His abnormally slow heartbeat only seems to quicken when he comes close to death – or to killing. As a surgeon surrounded every day by the fragile line between life and death, temptation is never far away.” So, while she wants to die, he wants to kill, but inconveniently, they fall in love with each other. “Hayat is impulsive, funny, stubborn, fearless and spectacularly headstrong, a contemporary Saudi woman written without explanation or apology,” says Front Row. “Her independence is not the story. It is simply who she is.” Related Stories Movies Saoirse Ronan Responds to Rumors That Husband Jack Lowden Will Be the Next James Bond TV BBC Releases 'Blue Planet III' Trailer at London Premiere With Blue Carpet, Splashy Piccadilly Lights Takeover ‘A Matter of Life and Death’ film still, courtesy of Front Row When the mythology behind Hayat’s curse is revealed, live-action briefly gives way to a handcrafted, gothic animated sequence. A Matter of Life and Death received its world premiere at the Red Sea International Film Festival in December 2025, before opening theatrically across Saudi Arabia in late June 25. A Matter of Life and Death was produced by Mohamed Hefzy for Film Clinic, Gianluca Chakra for Front Row Filmed Entertainment, and Abdulelah Alahmary and Ahmad Taema for Arabia Pictures, with support from the Red Sea Fund. Saudi Arabia has never been nominated for the international Oscar. The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences will unveil the 15 films on the best international feature film shortlist on Dec. 15. The five nominees will be announced Jan. 21, 2027. The 99th Academy Awards ceremony will take place on March 14, 2027. THR

articles.title: As New York Comic Con Turns 20, Organizer Teases Coney Island Team-Up, After 3 p.m. Ticket and Possibility of Expanding to Five Days Next Year
articles.full_text: Oct 7, 2026 8:36am PT As New York Comic Con Turns 20, Organizer Teases Coney Island Team-Up, After 3 p.m. Ticket and Possibility of Expanding to Five Days Next Year By Jennifer Maas Plus Icon Jennifer Maas TV Business Writer @jmaasaronson Latest Skydance Sets Leadership Across Games, Experiences, Consumer Products and HR 15 hours ago Jessica Chastain Stands by Criticizing Apple for Delaying ‘The Savant’ After Charlie Kirk’s Assassination: ‘I Had to Go on Record That I Thought It Was a Mistake’ 20 hours ago Skydance Credit Rating Downgraded by Fitch on Massive Debt in Wake of Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger 23 hours ago See All Getty Images New York Comic Con has hit the big 2-0. The East Coast’s biggest fan convention kicks off its 2026 event Thursday, marking its 20th year celebrating comics, film, TV, games, anime and general “geek” culture out of New York City’s Javits Convention Center. What began as a 33,000-attendee event in 2006 will host 250,000 people over the course of its four-day proceedings this year, with more than 500 creators and 650 exhibitors on the ground. Related Stories Charlie Brooker's New Netflix Series Gets Title, 'Blackmere,' as Rory Kinnear Joins Cast and First-Look Photos Revealed 'Icebreaker' Netflix Series: Auliʻi Cravalho, Gabriel Tierney, Chaneil Kular Among Six to Join Cast (EXCLUSIVE) To celebrate the momentous occasion, New York Comic Con organizer ReedPop has set some big birthday plans: a partnership with fellow New York institution Coney Island, expanded cosplay areas and a reduced-price, after 3 p.m. Thursday ticket that aims to make NYCC (which can be a very pricey experience) more accessible to residents of New York. Popular on Variety As its grown over the past two decades, New York Comic Con’s goal has expanded to maintaining its classic fan experiences while offering new opportunities for professionals in attendance over the past couple years. It’s growth that ReedPop is increasingly mindful of when there’s no longer the ability to acquire a larger physical footprint, as the whole Javits Center is taken over by the con Oct. 8-11. “Something important to think about is despite that scale, the team is super focused on preserving that feeling of community,” ReedPop’s senior vice president overseeing all consumer events, Marie Browne, tells Variety . “Preserving the community at an event of this scale doesn’t happen by accident. We’ve created dedicated spaces, stages, panels and meetups where people can share passions and find one another since the beginning.” The show has also progressed from a solely in-person experience to one with main-stage panels that are streamed live for fans around the world via YouTube — a move born out of the COVID-19 pandemic-era virtual cons that has stuck. Outside of its “foundation” of comics, of course, Browne says New York Comic Con “now really spans the full breadth of pop culture” and “Hollywood has become a major part of the event because geek culture has become mainstream culture.” Highly anticipated panels this year include Marvel Television and Marvel Animation’s Thursday event, “Dungeon Crawler Carl” author Matt Dinniman’s Friday spotlight, Saturday’s “Star Trek” universe deep dive and Sunday’s “NCIS: New York” panel. “There’s a lot of special things going on in terms of fan events,” Browne says. “We’re having reunions that fans won’t be able to experience anywhere else, like ‘Brooklyn Nine-Nine.’ There’ll be time to visit not only Artist Alley but our Writers’ Block programming, which will be expanded this year. So it’s really expanding upon everything we’ve done in the past, and certainly there’s a few other theme things to celebrate the fact that we’re 20 years old this year.” Browne has been with ReedPop parent company RX for the past 20 years and moved over to the ReedPop team a few months ago to oversee all consumer events. She was part of the team that launched New York Comic Con in 2006 and hired its first employees, so she finds this year’s event “a full circle moment.” “I never thought I would be here 20 years later, running this great division and I never thought that we would be at 250,000 people and going strong at this point,” Browne says. “I had full faith that it would be successful, but it’s really exceeded all expectations.” As for the next 20 years, Browne has a few things she can tease — including the potential of expanding programming to Wednesdays, which would make New York Comic Con a five-day event. “One of the things that we’re teasing a little bit for next year is really exploring if we’ll offer a Wednesday ticket,” Browne says. “I would say that’s still under exploration. Potentially, we would open it up to press and professionals at first — but not to keep it exclusive because we don’t want to do that. We want to make the event more inclusive. If anything, we would be doing it as an experiment to make sure that we’re doing it right. Anything that we add to the event, we’ll test with the fans first to make sure it’s right. And if it’s right for the fans and it’s right for the event, we’ll consider launching it because we have very little room to grow within our existing venues, so we have to figure out how to grow in other ways and most of that will be with probably deeper experiences than a bigger physical footprint.” Megyn Kelly Tells Olivia Rodrigo to ‘Stick to Singing’ After Speaking Out About Cornell 7 Case: ‘You Don’t Know What the F— You’re Talking About’ Glen Powell Is Staying Quiet on Politics Because ‘I Do Not Like the Discourse,’ Says ‘Running Man’ Flopped After Paramount Laid Off ‘Entire Marketing Department’ Co-Founder Nate Bolotin to Exit XYZ Films After Almost Two Decades With Studio (EXCLUSIVE) Skeet Ulrich Says His ‘Scream’ Arc Couldn’t Be Completed After Melissa Barrera’s Firing: ‘There’s No Billy Loomis’ Without Her Disney+ Will Stream 2027 Super Bowl From ‘Toy Story 5’ and ‘Paw Patrol’ Toys to Baby Gear, These Are the Best Finds from Amazon Prime Big Deal Days Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘Satoko Always’ Review: A Trio of Women Find Their Inner Voice in Shuichi Okita’s Delightful Celebration of the Art of Writing
articles.full_text: Oct 7, 2026 8:53am PT ‘Satoko Always’ Review: A Trio of Women Find Their Inner Voice in Shuichi Okita’s Delightful Celebration of the Art of Writing Kasumi Arimura, Hikari Ishida and young breakout Kashun Himeno play three women with the same name, who tap into their creative sides in this charming Busan competition entry. By James Marsh Plus Icon James Marsh Latest ‘The Table: Day and Night’ Review: Café-Based Korean Romance With Kim Min-ha and Han Sun-hwa Is All Froth, No Kick 18 hours ago See All Three total strangers, with nothing in common except their name, are each inspired to take up writing in “ Satoko Always ,” writer-director Shuichi Okita ’s surprising and inventive celebration of womanhood and the art of literary composition. Kasumi Arimura is the undeniable headliner, but the popular starlet is matched every step of the way by veteran actress Hikari Ishida and especially Kashun Himeno, who unleashes an eye-catching, potentially star-making turn as a junior high school student experiencing her first taste of true love. Related Stories ‘Tyson’ Trailer: Mike Tyson Chronicles His Journey From Dropout to Heavyweight Champion in Netflix Docuseries Danny Boyle Says ‘28 Years Later Part 3’ Will ‘Have a Lot of Cillian Murphy in It’ and Backs Jack O’Connell as the Next James Bond Having already debuted domestically last month, the film makes its international debut in Busan’s competition section, where it is sure to draw praise for Okita’s wonderfully woven screenplay, together with its triumvirate of stellar performances. Similarly, cast and creator’s robust reputation should likely ensure the film secures healthy distribution across Asia and select western markets. Popular on Variety Plucky teenager Satoko Nakai (Himeno) is first introduced with a nebulizer thrust up her nose. She is being treated for allergic rhinitis, which immediately becomes a non-issue when her handsome classmate Hayase (Toharu Ogawa) appears beside her, ready to be administered a similar treatment. They hit it off famously, and although Satoko is initially put off when Hayase blanks her at school, their regular sessions at the ENT clinic soon bring them closer together. Unfortunately, Satoko’s rhinitis interferes with her sleep, causing her to doze off at a kabuki performance she had been assigned to write a report on. Rather than turn in a blank paper, Satoko conjures up a work of pure fiction, which, much to her surprise, is warmly received by her teacher, Ms. Terao (Yoh Yoshida), who encourages her to indulge her passion for creative writing. She is tasked with penning a love letter to her favourite food, and the resulting ode to shiokara (fermented shrimp) is in fact a thinly veiled declaration of her blossoming adoration for Hayase. Okita’s screenplay gleefully challenges cinematic conventions, persistently playing with the viewer’s comprehension of what is actually unfolding, and what is mere fantasy, bursting from the pen of this newly inspired wordsmith. While never allowing this metatextual mischievousness to derail the narrative, these ideas flow seamlessly into the second chapter, in which thirty-something film publicist Satoko Nishida (Arimura) writes and feasts on shiokara when not indulging her passion for ludicrously romantic K-dramas. We are told this is not the same person, and yet they share so many things in common. At work, Satoko attempts to create a campaign for a new Korean baseball drama that her company is releasing, but after hours she is involved in an extramarital affair with a business associate, Muramoto (Joe Odagiri). That dalliance reaches a potentially lethal tipping point that leaves Satoko in the hospital, newly inspired to create a romantic fairytale of her own. Later still, we are introduced to Satoko Iijima (Ishida), who again shares many defining features with her two namesakes, albeit with just enough subtle differences to keep the audience on the back foot. Happily married and the mother of three boys, Satoko has been playing the dutiful housewife for years, but when her youngest, Shota (Mansaku Takada), reveals that he will be moving out when he starts university, the prospect of being an empty-nester sends her into a tailspin. She reminisces about a boy she knew growing up, and from there is inspired to create a story of her own, which the film realises through a visually dynamic combination of live-action and stop-motion animation. To reveal more of Okita’s endlessly surprising and playfully ambiguous script would be to rob audiences of the film’s numerous pleasures, which run the gamut from hearty belly-laughs to heartbreaking melodrama. The veteran storyteller, known for such surprising and rewarding works as “The Woodsman and the Rain” (2011) and “The Story of Yonosuke” (2013), not only dazzles with his dextrous interweaving of character and style, but also honors the craft of writing itself, spotlighting the texture and feel of paper, pencil and eraser. Even when his characters do use a computer screen, Okita shoots so tight on the cursor and characters, even their intricate composition appears tactile and sculpted. A film about indulging our yearning to open our hearts and tell stories, not for the entertainment of others or financial reward, but as a creative and emotional outlet to nurture one’s own sanity and well-being, “Satoko Always” cannot help but inspire the creative voice inside us all. That it is also a film about women, lifting them up without any compulsion to push men down in the process, is the final flourish in a work that achieves much with a gently assured touch. ‘Satoko Always’ Review: A Trio of Women Find Their Inner Voice in Shuichi Okita’s Delightful Celebration of the Art of Writing Reviewed at Busan Film Festival (Competition), Oct. 7, 2026. Running time: 138 min. Production: (Japan) An Amuse Creative Studio production. (World sales: Hakuhodo DY Music & Pictures, Tokyo.) Producers: Ryuhei Tsutsui, Miyuki Sato, Suguru Kubota, Yuya Tanaka. Crew: Director, screenplay: Shuichi Okita. Camera: Akiko Ashizawa. Editor: Masaya Ozaki. Music: Satoko Shibata. With: Kasumi Arimura, Hikari Ishida, Kashun Himeno, Joe Odagiri, Yoh Yoshida, Mansaku Takada, Yuzu Aoki, Michitaka Tsutsui, Toharu Ogawa, Yuko Nakamura, Kanata Hosoda. articles.title: In a Groundbreaking Premium Drama, ‘R91’ Brings a Murder Mystery Aboard Flagship French Aircraft Carrier
articles.full_text: Oct 7, 2026 8:58am PT In a Groundbreaking Premium Drama, ‘R91’ Brings a Murder Mystery Aboard Flagship French Aircraft Carrier In this fictional 6-part drama brought to market at Mipcom by SND, France's R91 Charles de Gaulle becomes the setting of a gritty, realistic thriller powered by M6 and Prime Video, produced by Next Episode (UGC Group) and born out of the mind of co-creator, co-writer and producer Henri Debeurme By Kevin Giraud Plus Icon Kevin Giraud Latest BBC, Bobby Prod, Folivari, Gao Shan Pictures Honored by Europe’s Animation Industry at Cartoon Forum 3 weeks ago Upcoming Canadian Animated Series Shine At Cartoon Forum 2026 3 weeks ago Heartfelt, Rare Animated Belgian Feature ‘Juul’ Headlines Studio 100 Film’s Expanding Slate at TIFF Market 3 weeks ago See All 'R91' Courtesy of SND Mediterranean Sea, present day. France’s nuclear aircraft carrier R91 – Charles de Gaulle aka “Le Charles” has just set sail on a threat-assessment strategic mission. When a crew member is found dead and another goes missing, military investigator Paul Fischer (Alban Lenoir, “Lost Bullet”) is rushed aboard. With second-in-command Helena Duval (Elodie Yung, “Marvel’s Daredevil,” “The Cleaning Lady”), they must hunt for the truth before the killer strikes again in the dark corners of the floating fortress. Related Stories 'Angus, Thongs and Full-Frontal Snogging' Pilot Set at Netflix Pam Levine Exits Netflix as Marketing & Publicity VP (EXCLUSIVE) With 2,000 souls on board, the stakes are high and suspicion spreads, as the mission turned murder investigation slowly transforms into a global security crisis. Popular on Variety Henri Debeurme, co-creator, co-writer, producer of ‘R91’. Credits Fanta Kaba A Series Mania winner “R91” marks the first ever co-acquisition between Amazon Prime Video France and leading free-to-air network M6 , with international sales handled by SND . It was born at the Cannes Film Festival in 2024, as producer, co-creator and co-writer Henri Debeurme at Next Episode Productions, part of UGC Group, exited the world premiere of “Top Gun: Maverick.” As he recalls to Variety ahead of the series’ own world premiere in La Rochelle Fiction Festival , his childhood desire to make such high-end productions in France was triggered once again by the Top Gun’s striking imagery, and by a chance encounter with Brigitte Maccioni, CEO of UGC Group. Maccioni, who had been part of the French Navy citizen reserve, had worked on “Le Charles” and met a few people during her time aboard the ship. “She opened a crack in the door for me, and when you find doors like that, you have to push and open them,” recalls Debeurme. “And that gave me the impetus to imagine a series that could take place on an aircraft carrier such as the Charles de Gaulle.” However, the seasoned creative took his time, building his script with co-writers, co-creators Mathilde Arnaud and Yoann Legave, and discussing with broadcasters and partners at M6, UGC and Prime Video. “The first constraint of such an endeavor is a narrative one,” he explains. “Writing a story set on a warship brings specific challenges, as you have to find plot twists within this defined setting. Series set entirely in a single location are not that common, and they’re often relying on claustrophobia to add tension, such as submarine series or family dramas.” He adds: “With ‘R91,’ we tried something new. A spectacular, closed-room drama also opened to the outside world. Ultimately, the aircraft carrier setting was more of an advantage than an restraint, as we discovered it to be a true floating village, open to the outside world, the sea and the sky. It became a source of ideas, inspiration, and unexpected turns.” Even though “R91” is entirely fictional, the teams wanted credibility and authenticity. And with the ambition of shooting almost the entire series at sea, it was key to have the French Navy on board. Debeurme approached them after refining his concept with his teams and broadcasting partners, and the Navy authorities eventually proved easy to convince. “They were welcoming, without willing to control us in any way. It was accompaniment during the whole process, as long as we didn’t interfere with their actual daily jobs.” With that in mind, Debeurme and his teams set out to build the most intricate, complex shooting schedule he’s ever created. “We had authorization to board the ships during military exercises, and we filmed for 15 days at sea, notably on the Charles, on the sole condition we didn’t disrupt their movements, and that we brought everything we needed with us. The preexisting exercises we joined, such as bridging and catapult launches, were planned a long time before, and we had to match their schedule.” Schedules that would change on a daily basis. By the end of shooting, not a single day had gone as planned, adds Debeurme. “We basically had to film a complex, fictional series as we would a documentary, doing a 10-minute take out of the blue because an helicopter is landing, and we want actors to be getting out of it, or saying their lines in front of it. Sometimes, we’d have to shoot with aircrafts landing or being launched on top of us, which makes tremendous noise. To be honest, it was completely insane and ended up being the most complicated shooting I’ve ever done in my entire career. We had to constantly adapt.” These conditions eventually bonded the teams, as well as helped them connect with the sailors themselves. “Their flexibility and open-mindedness helped us and made us feel like we were fully immersed. In some ways, film crews and navy crews share similarities. Both are very ordered collectives where everyone is an expert in their field, and we all are equally passionate about our jobs.” Using generative AI or stock footage was never Debeurme’s intention. “We filmed on different ships and also built sets in a studio for locations that were too cramped, inaccessible or too complex for VFX. But the vast majority took place on real warships, with working sailors. We wanted to film real people, real things. This authenticity was always at the core of our process, and that involves humans. French, world-class talents and artists that helped us bring this project to life with a fraction of the budget of U.S. dramas.” Expanding on French drama series, Debeurme praised his colleagues and fellow artists presenting audacious, imaginative projects in La Rochelle. “Throughout my career, I’ve had many projects where people told me it was something that could be done only in the US. ‘A series set on an aircraft carrier? No, we are terrible at that,’ people would say. But I actually disagree. I think we have exceptional teams in France, powerful imagination and a wealthy pool of talent, and we shouldn’t be afraid to try new things.” “R91” showcases this boldness, which shone also in La Rochelle with premium period dramas such as “Swapped,” unique in its own way. As he heads to the festival, Debeurme is incredibly thankful for all who helped bring this crazy dream project to life. “It’s a huge source of pride, and a childhood dream of mine. And for me, it still is all about movies and TV series that make my dreams come true. As a writer-producer on this show, I’m glad to see I could pull off such an ambitious project, and that having these two roles in a European context is possible. And beyond my own experience, it also proves that we’re still in a world where, even if matters are very difficult and the industry is under a lot of pressure, you can still do great things when you use your imagination and conviction.” Following up its world premiere, “R91” will debut on Prime Video in the near future, before airing on M6. ‘Will You Still Be My Friend’ Director Lu Po-Shun on Finding Common Ground From San Sebastian to Busan Ray Panthaki Debut, Jose Maria Cabral, Frederic Baillif Pics Make the Cut at Tallinn Black Nights Official and First Films Competitions Prime Day Blu-ray Deals Include 50% Discounts on Dozens of Films and Boxed Sets: ‘Boogie Nights, ‘Pulp Fiction,’ ‘The Sopranos’ and More George Cheeks Addresses Staffers in First Memo as Skydance TV Co-Chair: ‘CBS Remains a Cornerstone’ Saoirse Ronan Responds to James Bond Rumors About Husband Jack Lowden: ‘Not Really a Subject That’s Coming Up in Our House’ Josh Goldstine to Oversee Marketing and Distribution at Warner Bros., Paramount and All Skydance Film Labels (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments...

articles.title: Miami Film Festival GEMS Sets Lineup With ‘The Debut,’ ‘Club Kid’ as Opening and Closing Titles
articles.full_text: Oct 7, 2026 9:00am PT Miami Film Festival GEMS Sets Lineup With ‘The Debut,’ ‘Club Kid’ as Opening and Closing Titles By Jordan Moreau Plus Icon Jordan Moreau Latest ‘The Social Reckoning’ First Reactions: A ‘Solid Sequel,’ ‘Good, Just Not Great Film’ and a ‘Harsh Assessment of Zuckerberg’ 2 days ago ‘Free Elizabeth Holmes’ Group Defends Convicted Theranos Founder at ‘You Can See Everything’ Doc Screening: She’s ‘Innocent and Needs to Be Free’ 2 days ago ‘Lanterns’ Finale: Hal Jordan’s Killer and Manhunter Revealed, Sinestro Creates [SPOILER], John Stewart Powers Up for ‘Superman’ Sequel 3 days ago See All A24 Miami Dade College’s Miami Film Festival unveiled the lineup for its 13th Miami Film Festival GEMS, the festival’s fall midseason event taking place from Oct. 29-Nov. 5. GEMS will open with A24’s “The Debut” from writer-director Jesse Eisenberg and close with A24’s “ Club Kid ” from writer-director and star Jordan Firstman. Julianne Moore stars in “The Debut” as Mona Friedman, a shy, unassuming housewife who is cast in a bit part at a small community theater and becomes a zealous method actor, ready to wage war on the show’s domineering director (Paul Giamatti) to protect the artistic integrity of her role. The musical comedy also stars Halle Bailey, Eisenberg and Bernadette Peters, with music and lyrics by Eisenberg. Related Stories Lego's 'Heartlake the Musical' Heads to Peacock in the U.S., Tencent in China Amid Global Sales (EXCLUSIVE) Disney Licenses Slew of Titles to Netflix, Including All Five 'Ice Age' Movies, 'Percy Jackson and the Olympians,' 'Felicity,' 'Will Trent,' 'Elio' and More (EXCLUSIVE) In “Club Kid,” Firstman stars as Peter, a hard-partying New York City club promoter whose whirlwind lifestyle is upended by the arrival of the 10-year-old son he never knew he had. The film, which had its world premiere in Un Certain Regard at the Cannes Film Festival, also stars Cara Delevingne, Diego Calva and Kirby Howell-Baptiste. Popular on Variety Centerpiece titles include “Being Heumann”, “Behemoth!”, “Bunker”, “Elsinore”, “Paper Tiger”, and “Wild Horse Nine.” The festival also places a focus on international submissions to the Academy Awards, and will feature submitted titles such as Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s “All of a Sudden”, Lukas Dhont’s “Coward”, and Andrey Zvyagintsev’s “Minotaur.” Variety will also honor Emmy Award-winning and Golden Globe-nominated actor, writer and director actor John Turturro with the Variety Creative Vanguard Award during the festival. The award will be presented as part of a moderated conversation about his illustrious career and his latest film, “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York”, hosted by Variety’s co-president and co-editor-in-chief Ramin Setoodeh. “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” written and directed by Noah Segan, will also screen at the festival. Additionally, “Mouse,” from directors Kelly O’Sullivan and Alex Thompson, will screen as part of the lineup, with the filmmakers receiving the Festival’s Art of Light Award. The film premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival and comes from the filmmakers behind “Ghostlight.” Kyle MacLachlan will receive the Precious Gem Award at a special event in partnership with Books & Books in Miami to honor the release of his debut memoir “Fictional Self.” In honor of the 25th anniversary of “Hedwig and the Angry Inch,” the festival will host a special retrospective screening of the cult-favorite rock musical, followed by the Impact Award presentation and Q&A with writer, director and star John Cameron Mitchell. “The 13th edition of GEMS further solidifies the festival as a major awards season stop, bringing together some of the most anticipated films of the year alongside a curated collection of discoveries from around the world,” said Lauren Cohen, Director of Programming. “With 50 titles, this is the largest GEMS line-up yet. To be able to celebrate the work of incredible storytellers such as Danny Boyle, Martin McDonagh, James Gray, Pedro Almodovar, Ryusuke Hamaguchi, Hirokazu Kore-eda, Mike Leigh, Siân Heder, and Brad Bird all in one lineup captures the richness and resonance of world cinema today.” “Audiences can expect GEMS 2026 to be one of our most memorable editions yet,” said James Woolley, Executive Director of the festival. “We are beyond thrilled to honor actor Kyle MacLachlan, filmmaker John Cameron Mitchell and Los Javis for their incredible contributions to the entertainment industry.” The Centerpiece films include: “Being Heumann” – from Academy Award-winning director Siân Heder, who co-wrote the screenplay with Rebekah Taussig, is based on the memoir by disability rights activist Judy Heumann. The film tells the story of the 1977 takeover of the San Francisco Federal Building, when Heumann (Ruth Madeley) and a coalition of disabled activists refused to leave until the government enforced Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, in what became the longest occupation of a federal building in American history. Mark Ruffalo stars as Joseph Califano, the government official standing in their way, and Dylan O’Brien also stars. “Behemoth!” – From Academy Award-nominated director/writer Tony Gilroy follows Alex Serian (Pedro Pascal), a gifted cellist who returns home to Los Angeles after 20 years on the road. Music, which has been the constant all-consuming river of his life, swells him into an adventure that will change him forever. The film also stars Olivia Wilde, Eva Victor, Alexa Swinton, Kaya Ralls, Erik Griffin, JoBeth Williams, Margarita Levieva, with Hank Azaria, and Will Arnett. “Bunker” – From director Florian Zeller (“The Father,” “The Son”) Bunker centers on an architect who takes a morally ambiguous job building a survivalist bunker for a tech billionaire, while his wife begins to question their marriage of 17 years. The psychological thriller stars Javier Bardem and Penélope Cruz. “Elsinore” – From director Simon Stone (“The Dig”) and writer Stephen Beresford (“Pride”) tells the true story of actor Ian Charleson (Andrew Scott), who in 1989 stepped into the role of Hamlet at London’s National Theatre while privately battling AIDS, in a performance that became the triumph of his career. The film also stars Olivia Colman, Billie Piper and Johnny Flynn. “Paper Tiger” – In James Gray’s deeply felt and intense crime thriller, set in 1986 New York, a naïve engineer, Irwin (Miles Teller) accepts a seemingly lucrative business proposition from his brother, Gary (Adam Driver), a former cop. But when Irwin witnesses something he wasn’t meant to see at the Gowanus Canal, the brothers find themselves pulled into a dangerous confrontation with the newly emerging Russian mafia. As the threat of violence escalates, Irwin’s wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) sounds the alarm, Irwin desperately tries to protect his family, and Gary is forced to make an impossible choice to save those he loves. “Wild Horse Nine” – From Academy Award-winning writer-director Martin McDonagh is set shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, when CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched by their bureau chief (Steve Buscemi) from Santiago to Easter Island, where Chris’s bond with a pair of rebellious students threatens to send the trip sideways. The black comedy also stars Mariana di Girolamo, Ailín Salas with Tom Waits and Parker Posey. Two more anniversary screenings round out the program. The festival will host a special 20th anniversary screening of Sofia Coppola’s “Marie Antoinette” at Vizcaya Museum & Gardens. The festival will also present a 10th anniversary screening of Anna Biller’s “The Love Witch” in 35mm on Halloween. The festival will also host two preview night screenings before the festival dates. First will be “ Fjord ” directed by Cristian Mungiu, which will play on October 14 at Silverspot Cinema. Winner of the Palme d’Or at this year’s Cannes Film Festival, the film stars Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve. The second Preview Night title is Sundance hit Wicker directed by Alex Huston Fischer & Eleanor Wilson on October 20. The film stars Alexander Skarsgård, Olivia Colman, Elizabeth Debicki, Peter Dinklage & Richard E. Grant. The complete list of films screening at the 2026 GEMS Festival include: “All of a Sudden” (Director Ryusuke Hamaguchi) “Bedford Park” (Director Stephanie Ahn) “Being Heumann” (Director Siân Heder) “Behemoth!” (Director Tony Gilroy) “Bitter Christmas” (Director Pedro Almodovar) “Bunker” (Director Florian Zeller) “Burgundy” (Directors Michael Dweck, Gregory Kershaw) “Campeón Gabacho” (Director Jonás Cuarón) “Clarissa” (Directors Arie Esiri and Chuko Esiri) “Club Kid” (Director Jordan Firstman) “Coward” (Director Lukas Dhont) “Elsinore” (Director Simon Stone) “Everytime” (Director Sandra Wollner) “First Light” (Director James J. articles.full_text: Oct 7, 2026 9:00am PT ‘Anna Pigeon’ Renewed for Season 2 at USA Network By Joe Otterson Plus Icon Joe Otterson TV Reporter joeotterson Latest Next Generation Collective Launches in Support of Young Hollywood Talent’s Mental Health 19 hours ago Jessica Biel to Play Hugh Hefner’s Wife in ‘Playmates’ Movie for Searchlight 21 hours ago ‘Star Trek: The Next Generation’ Star Gates McFadden to Write Dr. Crusher Comic Book Series (EXCLUSIVE) 23 hours ago See All USA Network “ Anna Pigeon ” has been renewed for Season 2 at USA Network , Variety has learned. The drama series originally debuted on the basic cabler on Aug. 7, with the Season 1 finale set to air on Oct. 9. The show is based on Nevada Barr’s Anna Pigeon book series. “It’s been really thrilling to see audiences fall in love with Anna and come to the park every week,” said series showrunner Morwyn Brebner. “We’re so grateful to our cast and crew who brought Nevada Barr’s iconic world to life with such heart and passion; we cannot wait to get back outside for season two.” Related Stories Netflix Orders Dark Comedy 'All the Rage' From 'Dead to Me' Duo Liz Feldman, Kelly Hutchinson Alfonso Cuaron to Make First Korea Visit at Busan as Festival Also Spotlights European Women+ Filmmakers The series stars Tracy Spiridakos as Anna Pigeon, along with Paulina Alexis, Ronnie Rowe, Tricia Helfer, Kim Coates, Crystle Lightning, Cooper Levy, Manuel Rodriguez-Saenz, Ryan Northcott, Nikki Rae Hallow, Jordan Sledz, and Melanie Scrofano. Popular on Variety The Season 1 logline states that the show follows Pigeon, “a former city slicker who became a park ranger after a devastating loss changed the trajectory of her life forever. While Anna tries to outrun her demons, her focus turns to solving crimes that have taken place within national park grounds, no matter who or what gets in her way. Season two promises continued mystery and adventure, as Anna’s story continues to unfold.” Brebner serves as showrunner, with Lea Thompson directing. Both are also executive producers alongside Brett Burlock, Sonia Hosko, Todd Berger, Julie Di Cresce, Tom Cox, Jordy Randall, Peter Emerson and Gordon Gilbertson. Leslie Cowan serves as producer. The series is produced by Cineflix and SEVEN24 Films for USA Network in association with Bell Media. Cineflix Rights is the exclusive international worldwide distribution partner, excluding the US. “’Anna Pigeon’ has connected with audiences in a meaningful way, bringing a compelling new heroine and a fresh perspective to USA Network,” said Michael Sluchan, SVP of Scripted Content, Entertainment, at Versant. “We’re thrilled to continue Anna’s journey with Tracy, Morwyn, Lea and our incredible partners at Cineflix.” “Anna Pigeon” is one of two scripted series currently airing on USA Network. The network also has Season 2 of the legal drama “The Rainmaker,” which is based on the John Grisham novel of the same name, set to debut on Oct. 16. USA Network has also greenlit the medical drama “Diplomatic Immunity” from Matt Corman and Chris Ord. USA Network was one of the cable channels spun off into the standalone company Versant by Comcast in early 2026. Other channels now under Versant include MS Now (formerly MSNBC), E!, Syfy, and Oxygen. articles.title: Oscars: Saudi Arabia Picks Quirky Comedy ‘A Matter of Life and Death’ for International Feature Race
articles.full_text: Oct 7, 2026 9:00am PT Oscars: Saudi Arabia Picks Quirky Comedy ‘A Matter of Life and Death’ for International Feature Race By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest ‘All’s Fair’ Season 2 to Launch From Rome Film Festival With Kim Kardashian, Naomi Watts, Niecy Nash-Betts and Sarah Paulson Attending 1 day ago Oscars: Syria Selects Doc ‘The Other Side of the Sun’ for International Feature Race, Marking First Entry Since Fall of Assad Regime 2 days ago ‘NAZA’ Rebuttal Doc Surfaces Online, Made by IDF Reserve Members 2 days ago See All Courtesy Front Row Filmed Entertainment Saudi director Anas Ba Tahaf’s romantic black comedy “A Matter of Life and Death” has been selected as Saudi Arabia ’s candidate for the Oscars international feature film category. The quirky movie marks the directorial debut of Tahaf, who previously worked as co-producer, editor and first assistant director on Mahmoud Sabbagh’s groundbreaking rom-com “Barakah Meets Barakah,” which represented Saudi Arabia at 89th Academy Awards a decade ago. Related Stories ‘Sweet Magnolias’ Cancellation: Creator, Stars JoAnna Garcia Swisher and Jamie Lynn Spears React to Netflix Series Ending Lego's 'Heartlake the Musical' Heads to Peacock in the U.S., Tencent in China Amid Global Sales (EXCLUSIVE) “A Matter of Life and Death” pairs actors Sarah Taibah (“Mandoob”) and Yaqoub Alfarhan (“Norah,” “Rashash”) and is set in Jeddah, the city on the eastern shore of the Red Sea known for vibrant youth culture, a mix of modern and ancient architecture and for being the gateway to Mecca. Popular on Variety The film’s plot involves a superstitious young woman named Hayat who is convinced she’s cursed and wants to end her life. She intersects with Yousef, an introverted heart surgeon who suffers from slower than average heartbeats that seem to quicken when he comes close to death or to killing. “She wants to die; he wants to kill, and they should be perfect for each other. Then, inconveniently, they fall in love,” says the synopsis. “A Matter of Life and Death” had its world premiere at the Red Sea International Film Festival in Jeddah in December last year, then opened theatrically in June across Saudi Arabia where it pulled a decent roughly $600,000 in grosses, according to Rentrack. The indie film later received a jury special mention at the Saudi Film Festival, where Taibah won an acting award for her performance as Hayat. “A Matter of Life and Death” is produced by Mohamed Hefzy for Film Clinic, Gianluca Chakra for Front Row Filmed Entertainment , and Abdulelah Alahmary and Ahmad Taema for Arabia Pictures, with support from the Red Sea Fund. Front Row Filmed Entertainment is handling international sales. The shortlist for the 2027 Oscar nominations will be announced by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences on Dec. 15, with the final selection revealed on Jan. 21. The 99th Academy Awards ceremony is scheduled to take place on March 14 in Los Angeles. articles.title: Laika’s ‘Wildwood’ Set to Close Animation Is Film Festival
articles.full_text: Oct 7, 2026 9:00am PT Laika’s ‘Wildwood’ Set to Close Animation Is Film Festival By Mya Copeland Plus Icon Mya Copeland Latest Prime Video Debuts First Look at ‘Bloodaxe’ Series From ‘Vikings’ Creator (TV News Roundup) 2 days ago ‘Coven Academy’ Star Malina Weissman Unpacks Briar’s Backstory, Her Take on the Love Triangle and Her Hopes for Season 2 2 days ago ‘Celebrity Traitors’ Star Richard E. Grant Accidentally Reveals He’s a Traitor to Cast in Premiere, Calls It the ‘Biggest Mistake I’ve Made in My Life’ 5 days ago See All Laika “ Wildwood ” has been set as the closing night film for the Animation Is Film Festival , which runs Oct. 16-19 in Los Angeles. Laika’s animated epic will screen Oct. 19 at the Academy Museum’s Geffen Theater. Following the screening, “Wildwood” director and Laika president and CEO Travis Knight will hold a conversation with filmmaker Jason Reitman. “Wildwood” follows headstrong teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) on a desperate mission to rescue her brother after he is abducted by a murder of crows. Her rescue takes her into the Impassable Wilderness, an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Oregon. Joining Prue is her classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay), and the two enter a world of talking animals, bandits and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must find a way to save her brother while confronting forces that could determine Wildwood’s future. Related Stories Lego's 'Heartlake the Musical' Heads to Peacock in the U.S., Tencent in China Amid Global Sales (EXCLUSIVE) Secuoya Studios Taps Carla Gómez to Lead Latin American Development as Regional Expansion Accelerates (EXCLUSIVE) The cast also features Carey Mulligan, Mahershala Ali, Angela Bassett, Awkwafina, Jake Johnson, Charlie Day, Amandla Stenberg, Jemaine Clement, Maya Erskine, Tantoo Cardinal, Tom Waits and Richard E. Grant. Popular on Variety Directed and produced by Knight, “Wildwood” opens in theaters on Oct. 23. Fathom Entertainment is distributing the film theatrically in the United States, with FilmNation Entertainment handling international sales. The film is inspired by Colin Meloy’s 2011 novel of the same name and illustrated by Carson Ellis in Laika’s classic stop-motion style. The production took 15 years to complete and is Laika’s most ambitious project to date. “Each year, Animation Is Film returns to Hollywood to champion the notion that animation, as an art form, repeatedly redefines what we think cinematic storytelling is capable of,” said Animation is Film director Matt Kaszanek. “We can think of no greater example of that mission than Travis Knight’s ‘Wildwood.’ A new Laika film is a reason to celebrate for every person who loves great films, and we are so proud to be part of its journey.” “Animation Is Film and Laika share a belief that animation is cinema in its fullest sense, capable of telling stories with extraordinary emotional and artistic ambition,” said Laika Chief Marketing & Operations Officer David Burke. “’Wildwood’ represents 15 years of imagination, craftsmanship and commitment from hundreds of artists, so there could be no more fitting place to celebrate its journey to the screen than with AIF.” The ninth edition of AIF Festival runs Oct. 16-19, with the main program hosted at TCL Chinese 6 Theatres in Hollywood. These two came out swinging with another fiery performance, this time dancing a rumba to “Anytime You Need a Friend.” Derek Hough was thoroughly impressed: “It was seriously sophisticated. It was.” SCORE: 24 out of 30 Actor Harry Shum Jr. with Jenna Johnson . They’re looking for another set of solid scores from the judges for their tango to “It’s Like That.” This week, Jenna goes on the Grey’s Anatomy set with her celeb partner to practice in between takes. Fun fact: Harry danced in the original music video for this song, too. “A red hot tango from a man on a mission! Sharp as a knife. So intense. I mean, it gave me whiplash!” Bruno Tonioli says. Bonus points for the Glee reunion with former DWTS champ Amber Riley back in the ballroom to sing for this one. SCORE: 24 out of 30 Actress Jenna Dewan with Val Chmerkovskiy . Jenna is frustrated by her feedback from the judges, but she wants to take their critiques seriously. This week, she wants to focus on showing a softer and slower side to her dancing with a rumba to “My All.” Watch out Season 35, Jenna Dewan found her groove! All Derek Hough could do was stand up and clap. “All I have to say is: There she is.” SCORE: 24 out of 30 Reality star Tyler Cameron with Sharna Burgess . Tyler managed to skate by last week thanks to Taylor’s elimination, but he seems to know he needs to kick things into high gear if he wants to make it any further in the competition. This week, he and Sharna danced a foxtrot to “#Beautiful.” Color, well, nearly everyone surprised! The man can move! “The improvement is incredible. You should be proud of yourself,” Bruno tells him. SCORE: 21 out of 30 Reality star Maura Higgins with Mark Ballas . The Traitors duo is finding their groove, and Maura is settling into her clear natural affinity for dance. This week, they are taking on a waltz to “If It’s Over.” She’s already danced in frame, but now she wants to improve and go for higher scores. “I feel like right now the world needs that kind of beauty!” Carrie Ann exclaimed. SCORE: 25 out of 30 (a 9 from Carrie Ann! Maura falling to the ground in disbelief says it all.) Late-night sidekick Guillermo Rodriguez with Whitney Carson . These two took a trip to New York City for rehearsals this week, since Guillermo is there for his day job. They are dancing a samba to “Obsessed.” As Witney says, “nothing can really prepare you for the samba.” He’s really trying, though. And hey, the steps he did (few as there were) were in time! “Listen, that wasn’t quite a samba, but it was 100% Guillermo,” Derek says. SCORE: 15 out of 30 Savannah Bananas midfielder Jackson Olson with Emma Slater . Jackson took a little break from rehearsals this week to celebrate his birthday, but he’s still putting his all into coming back strong after some lukewarm feedback from the judges in Week 3. He’s performing a waltz to “Without You.” There must be something in the air this week, because he looked like a completely different dancer. “I can see you almost for the first time,” Bruno tells him. SCORE: 21 out of 30 Actress Tatyana Ali with Jan Ravnik . The Fresh Prince star is living ut a childhood dream dancing to Mariah Carey. And she’s got the in-the-know pro this week, because Jan has toured with the pop star. They’re doing a jazz dance to “Fantasy.” After last week, can anyone be surprised that she kills it? Carrie Ann wanted her to have more energy for a jazz routine. Derek and Bruno agree. “But overall, I just love seeing what you’re doing,” Derek says. SCORE: 20 out of 30 Comedian and podcaster Connor Wood with Rylee Arnold . Rylee, Connor isn’t sure if you’ve noticed, but you tend to include grinding choreography in all of your routines. Well, the tradition continues this week, because they’re dancing a rumba to “Touch My Body.” I mean, what’s a girl to do? Unfortunately, the hips were not moving, but he did do a nice worm. “There’s a lot of moments where you’re playing it safe,” Derek says. Bruno loved it. “Frisky!” SCORE: 19 out of 30 Actress Julia Stiles with Ezra Sosa . Julia is riding high after receiving her highest scores last week. She’s really got to impress this week with a Viennese waltz to “Vision of Love” if she wants to keep the positive momentum going. “For me, that was a breakthrough,” Carrie Ann said. Well, ok then! SCORE: 21 out of 30 Olympian Amber Glenn with Pasha Pashkov . It’s a lot of pressure to close out the night, especially as the couple who walked away with the first 8s of the season and tied at the top of the leaderboard last week. This time, they’re dancing a rumba to “Hero.” Pasha calls the dance “the ultimate test” of their synchronicity as a couple. Turns out, they didn’t need to worry at all. “You never lost the ability to fill the room,” Bruno says. SCORE: 23 out of 30 Who goes home? The competition is getting tough, so there’s not very many weeks that Guillermo can keep getting away with this, but somehow Ciara Miller and Brandon Armstrong go home on Tuesday night. Next week is Super Bowl Night. Stay tuned to see what that means.
