articles.title: The Deadline Dozen: The Best Unscripted Shows Heading To MIPCOM Including ‘Wordle’, ‘Marriage Market’ & ‘Hidden Planet’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max The Deadline Dozen: The Best Unscripted Shows Heading To MIPCOM Including ‘Wordle’, ‘Marriage Market’ & ‘Hidden Planet’ ‘Doctor Who’ Bids Revealed: Jed Mercurio Leads Pitch To Regenerate BBC Series, As STV Studios Plans To Transport TARDIS To Scotland FilmNation Strikes Deal With High Road Over TV Slate View All October 7, 2026 1:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Clockwise from top left: 'Wordle', 'Hidden Planet', '100 Cooks', 'Marriage Market' NBCUniversal Formats, BBC Studios, WBITVP, Fox Welcome to our selection of the most scorching titles headed to MIPCOM this year, The Deadline Dozen . Our editorial team has carefully researched and selected the projects we expect to drive the chatter on the Croisette and beyond. We start with unscripted. Check back tomorrow for the best of MIPCOM’s scripted fare. HIDDEN PLANET Image: BBC Studios BBC STUDIOS Length: 5 x 60’ Related Stories News Iconic Japanese Gameshow 'Action Arena' To Be Shopped Internationally For First Time By NBCUniversal Formats News Scripted Veteran Jason Simms Switches On Fusebox Entertainment Producers: BBC Studios Natural History Unit, The Open University Watch on Deadline Networks: BBC (U.K.), BBC America (U.S.) The BBC’s natural history output has set the global benchmark even with many more players in the field today than a decade ago. Hidden Planet is the latest in the canon, this time turning the micro-cameras on the world of insects. The five-part series shines a spotlight on insect societies, highlighting how ants, beetles and other bugs play the roles of parents, builders and sophisticated communicators as they strike alliances with larger animals and perform incredible feats of strength and intelligence. The BBC has equipped the BBC Studios Natural History Unit with a mountain of the latest scientific work and top-of-the-line cameras to aid the filming. In this case, the scientific theory has been combined with bespoke robotic systems and specially designed lenses to get to the heart of insect life. Worryingly, the series will show how their communities are increasingly under threat from humans. With BBC America already on board as a co-producer and backed by research from The Open University, BBC Studios hits Cannes with the closest thing to a sure-fire documentary seller on the Croisette this year. THE BILLION DOLLAR HASH HUNT BLUE ANT RIGHTS Length: 3 x 60’ Producer: Alibi Entertainment Network: Crave (Canada) Since completing a reverse takeover of Canadian compatriot Boat Rocker just over a year ago, Blue Ant Rights has spent time refining its sales and streaming businesses and is hoping the corporate reshuffling leaves it with a stronger distribution operation than before. MIPCOM will be a good test. Among the highlights of its slate is The Billion Dollar Hash Hunt , the latest doc series from Canada’s Crave, the red-hot streamer behind Heated Rivalry . This one is billed as a “true-crime treasure hunt” that chronicles the story of former smuggler Billy Greer, who moved thousands of tons of hash for shadowy Dutch crime network The Octopus. Greer’s caper came to an end when 54 tons of drugs were seized and DEA agent Rick Carter sent him down for 20 years. It’s a familiar story until the plot takes a wild twist: Years later, Greer and Carter join forces to uncover what happened to the missing drugs. This opens the story up to startling confessional interactions, remarkable archive footage and a high-stakes present day search. With most docs in the true-crime space focused on building a picture of the past, Blue Ant will hope bringing the narrative into the modern day gives it the edge with discerning doc buyers who need their shows to cut through. Given it was greenlit by a streamer, this one looks set to work on digital platforms as well as linear TV. MARRIAGE MARKET Image: Fox Fox Entertainment Global Length: TBC Producer: Fox Entertainment Studios Network: Fox (U.S.), Joyn (Germany) The Marriage Market is coming to market. A new reality dating format, the show is for U.S. network Fox, and the finished version and the format are launching internationally at MIPCOM. The Fox show is fronted by actress-comedian-podcaster Whitney Cummings. As well as a stand-up, she is the co-creator of CBS show 2 Broke Girls and creator of NBC’s Whitney . As a host, she fronted HBO’s Friends gameshow, Fast Friends . Billed as an immersive matchmaking experience and a new take on the dating show, the format features singletons who are tired of swiping and first dates and are ready to get hitched. The twist is, the would-be brides and grooms must hand total control of their love lives to their families. When two families think they have the perfect match, the couple are introduced and get engaged on the spot. Then the new pair and their families move in together and the matchmaking is put to the test. The families are still in charge and must decide if they have found them the one, or whether it has not worked out and their loved one needs to be pitched back into the marriage market, giving them another shot at finding the love of their lives. The show has an international pedigree. It is borne out of a formats initiative that saw Fox work with international broadcasters such as ProSiebenSat.1 in Germany and TF1 in France to jointly work up new unscripted shows. Accordingly, The Marriage Market bowed in Germany first, on ProSieben’s streaming platform Joyn. Cheerio Entertainment, part of the German broadcaster’s production and distribution division, made the German version. Fox Entertainment Studios makes the U.S. version, which is slated for Fox’s 2026-2027 season. Alycia Rossiter, who worked on The Bachelor and The Bachelorette , is the showrunner. Fox Entertainment Global is handling distribution and will be looking for love—from buyers—in Cannes. RUINS: RISE & FALL BOSSANOVA MEDIA Length: 8 x 60’ Producer: Like A Shot Entertainment Networks: Warner Bros. Discovery (EMEA), SBS (Australia), Channel 4 (U.K.), TV2 (Norway), Sky New Zealand Every year for a decade, London-based BossaNova Media has held a pitching event dubbed Development Day, which brings together its biggest producers and clients. The idea is to fast-track greenlights and get factual projects out the door at a quicker pace. Paul Heaney’s company itself acts as the central commissioner, putting projects into production and then sells the rights to buyers who have already stated their interest. Ruins: Rise & Fall is one such series. The eight-part show was greenlit in April, with Heaney saying at the time, “Some projects you invest in are a bit of a risk, but Ruins: Rise & Fall isn’t one of them.” The reason for that is the unquenching market need for solid factual projects that can both be popular on linear channels and drive older viewers to streaming services. The series explores 24 sites around the world and is built on one idea: every ruin has two stories—how it rose and how it fell. Viewers are taken to ancient Sri Lankan rock fortress Sigiriya, the ruins of Ephesus in Turkey and Roman auxiliary fort Vindolanda in the U.K. and on to more modern places such as Hitler’s Wolf’s Lair in Poland and vast underground Nazi war factories. Archaeologists and historians tell their stories from the ambition and ingenuity that made them, to the conflict and catastrophe that transformed them into the ruins of today. Digital reconstruction will show sites being stripped back to before the first stone was laid to seeing them rebuilt and then torn apart through war, disaster, abandonment and decay. Given that several of the largest global territories are already off the market is a testament to BossaNova’s strategic foresight, so those buyers in the remaining territories should move fast. 100 COOKS Image: WBITVP Warner Bros. International Television Production Length: 9 x 60’ Producer: Lando Entertainment Network: Food Network (U.S) “Your number could come up at any moment.” That is the logline that greets chefs daring to take on Warner’s 100 Cooks, which found its perfect American host in the shape of Terry Crews. A Food Network original, it is now being served up internationally. There may be a few out there now, but 100 Cooks feels one of the highest-stakes (or should that be steaks?) on offer. The 100 contestants enter the vast kitchen arena ready for a chance to call the shots. A randomized Challenge Mixer reveals the next test: From weeknight meals and party bites to holiday sweets or the best burger. The Cook Mixer then selects which competitors will step forward and take on the challenge. Nobody knows when they will compete, what they will be asked to do, how many cooks will join them, or how many could be sent home. Everyone must be ready for anything, and as 100 becomes 50, the kitchen slowly empties and the competition intensifies until one cook eventually walks away victorious. In the case of the U.S. version, it was Bryce, an oil field worker from Montana. 100 Cooks was a big hit for Food Network and it’s no wonder Warner Bros. International Television Production is prioritizing this one in Cannes. Brooklyn Nine-Nine star Crews is a hugely recognizable name who brings a unique feel to the show, and so 100 Cooks could easily work as finished tape or be shopped as a format, for which territories would then seek a host who can similarly make a big noise. At MIPCOM, Warner is also selling TLC UK format Unacceptable, New Zealand’s Crackhead and the Buried with Michael Sheen doc about the Good Omens star’s investigation into toxic waste. ALL HEART: A RUGBY STORY BOAT ROCKER STUDIOS Length: 4 x 40’ Producers: Boat Rocker Studios Network: Crave (Canada) The second Crave documentary in our Dozen, this four-parter has been selected to satisfy the hunger for sports access docs. The docuseries’ full working title is All Heart: Canada Women’s Rugby and the Quest for Rugby World Cup Glory . It was ordered last year and will stream on Bell Media’s Crave this year. The series follows the Canadian team’s historic run to the World Cup final, where they were ultimately toppled by host country England, going down 33-13 in front of a sellout crowd of 82,000 at Twickenham Stadium in South West London. It goes behind the scenes, showcasing the culmination of years of hard work and sacrifice, with Rugby Canada and World Rugby providing director Kathleen Jayme behind-the-scenes access to the players and coaching staff. James is known for making 2025’s Naomi Osaka: The Second Set , a tennis access doc that was sold to Fox Corp.-owned streamer Tubi for the U.S. market. Exec producers on All Heart include Jay Baruchel—the Canadian actor and filmmaker with credits including Knocked Up , How to Train Your Dragon and She’s Out of My League —and rock band The Tragically Hip, who are long-time supporters of women’s sports and fundraisers for the Canadian women’s rugby team. Boat Rocker founders David Fortier and Ivan Schneeberg are also EPs. The title is only just hitting the market now despite its 2025 order, and takes a key spot in Boat Rocker Studios’ slate this year. WORDLE Image: James Stack/NBC NBCUniversal Formats, a division of Universal Studio Group Length: TBC Producers: Universal Television Alternative Studio, Electric Hot Dog, The New York Times Network: NBC (U.S.) The New York Times daily word puzzle game Wordle is coming to U.S. TV, and the format is coming to the international market. The game is a phenomenon. Developed by Josh Wardle, a Welsh software engineer at Reddit, players have to find a five-letter word. They have six attempts, with colored tiles offering feedback on the correct and redundant letters, and their placement in that day’s word. The New York Times paid a reported $3 million to buy Wordle and it has become a cornerstone of its digital and games offering. The game has racked up billions of users. Getting a word with a small number of guesses is a source of pride for players. The Wordle TV game show will bow on U.S. broadcast network NBC. Broadcaster, journalist, Today anchor and avid Wordle player Savannah Guthrie is set to host. She has form with the game, previously playing a huge version of the game in Times Square, New York. Universal Television Alternative Studio is producing with Jimmy Fallon’s Electric Hot Dog and The New York Times. Fallon, who has increasingly moved into producing, is an exec-producer on the show. He is a Wordle fan, even having a segment on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon in which he and the team played the game live on air. The TV game show has been a few years in the making. It will take place over three super-sized rounds with two teams solving the Wordle puzzles in each half-hour episode. NYT execs have promised the show will stay true to the spirit of the game. The Wordle game show is on trend with several TV adaptations of games in the cards. There are TV versions of Monopoly, Cluedo and The Settlers of Catan being developed. Historically, the likes of Scrabble, Boggle, Trivial Pursuit and Pictionary have all been adapted for TV. In terms of Wordle , NBCUniversal Formats, a division of Universal Studio Group, is across distribution and selling the format. CAPTCHA SEVEN.ONE STUDIOS INTERNATIONAL Length: 10 x 50’ Producer: Thinketers Network: LA 2 (Spain) Spain is known in the unscripted world for the likes of Operación Triunfo and El Conquistador , but it has primarily been an importer of formats, rather than an exporter. Germany’s Seven.One Studios International is hoping to add another name to the canon with Captcha . The game show is based around those ubiquitous internet verification tests that check if the visitor to a website is human or a bot. The format tests the statement ‘I’m not a robot’ by putting four contestants through a series of visual puzzles, logic games and AI-powered, web-inspired challenges to prove their human credentials. Celebrity guests accompany the contestants, ideally helping and not hindering them, to an all-or-nothing final, where one test decides everything, including the true identity of the player. A final verification proves if they are human or not, and if they keep the cash that they have been accruing. The format has been already produced for Spanish broadcaster La 2, where it was a success across its first season. Seven.One Studios International, now part of the expanding MediaForEurope empire, will be looking to captcha interest with the show in a cluttered market for attention- grabbing formats. HISTORY’S STRANGE FORTUNES WITH KEVIN BACON A+E GLOBAL MEDIA Length: 10 x 60’ Producers: A+E Factual Studios, VaynerWatt Network: The History Channel (U.S.) History is filled with stories of the strange ways people won and lost their fortunes. In A+E Global Media’s latest talent-led unscripted series, the aim is to tell as many of those stories as possible. History’s Strange Fortunes with Kevin Bacon will see the Footloose , X: Men First Class and Crazy, Stupid, Love actor examine wild tales such as Elvis dropping $50,000 on a midnight sandwich one evening to million-dollar scams and gold rush windfalls. Expect greed, luck, obsession and the old adage that fortune really does favor the brave (and the strange, according to A+E). The talent-led model has dominated commissioning at The History Channel for some time, with numerous slates pairing well-known faces with lesser-known cases. Indeed, Bacon is just one of four star-fronted series in a March 2026 slate—the others being Extraordinary Origins with Ted Danson , Crime and Justice with Tom Selleck and History’s Greatest Machines with Dolph Lundgren . “Talent-led formats succeed on History because they unite inimitable personalities with amazing storytelling,” says Patrick Vien, Group MD for International at A+E Global Media. “Kevin Bacon’s global fan base paired with our universal fascination with money gives History’s Strange Fortunes broad international appeal.” At MIPCOM this year, both Bacon and Danson’s shows will take center stage for A+E, alongside the likes of Lifetime movie Buried in Barstow and miniseries The Bible Revealed . TERRAIN: BATTLE OF THE FLAGS PRIMITIVES Length: 10 x 25’ Producer: Roses Are Blue Network: ZDF (Germany), YouTube Germany has been the progenitor of some of Europe’s most creative entertainment formats and release windows in recent years with shows such as 7 Vs. Wild and Terrain. Battle of the Flags is now hoping to be its latest success story. The 10-part, half-hour format is the brainchild of German actor, comedian and YouTuber Torge Oerlich, known to his followers as Freshtorge. He began developing the adventure-reality show, which aims to generate an immersive gameplay experience, with Belgian format maker Roses Are Blue. German pubcaster ZDF quickly boarded the project. Inspired by gaming mechanics, Terrain follows ten high-profile creators who divide into five teams and, taking a cue from The Traitors , compete in a purpose-built game environment set against a dramatic Scottish Highlands backdrop. Their mission is simply to capture the other team’s flag and defend their own. Unlike The Traitors , the gameplay does not compel them to form alliances, as the teams are fixed. The teams self-shoot their experience and wear specially developed third-person camera systems integrated into a bespoke vest to give the aesthetic a distinct look and feel of video games. At 25 minutes per episode, the show is designed for streaming services, and it has been given an innovative rollout in Germany this fall, when three episodes will launch on ZDF’s streaming service, with Episode 1 also available on YouTube. The following two episodes join the Google-owned service a day later, and the linear premiere on ZDFneo will follow later. Dedicated companion content will run on a standalone YouTube channel and ‘reaction programming’ will hit ZDF’s Twitch channel. Belgium-based Primitives, has worldwide rights (excluding German-speaking Europe) and will present the show to buyers in the run-up to MIPCOM, with a full market launch also prepared. Having the creators film the action themselves creates a level of authenticity and immediacy that is particularly exciting for younger audiences. DIANA UNHEARD Cineflix Rights Length: 3 x 60’ Producer: Love Monday TV Network: TBC Having gained access to the audio tapes that formed the basis of Andrew Morton’s explosive book about the Princess Diana, Love Monday TV has made Diana Unheard , a documentary series that will air never-before-heard parts of the recordings. The producers hope that hearing Diana talk about her life, loves and family will reframe people’s perception of her, moving away from seeing through a lens of vulnerability and tragedy and showing her as self-aware, determined, and actively taking control of her life. Love Monday has made numerous shows about the British monarchy including Her Majesty the Queen: Behind Closed Doors for ITV and William and Harry: Love and Betrayal for Channel 5. Diana can be heard in revealing form in the tapes, which were conversations recorded with her friend James Colthurst in 1991. She talks about Prince Charles and Camilla (now King Charles III and Queen Camilla), as well as the then Prince Andrew, who has since been stripped of his royal titles following scrutiny of his ties to Jeffrey Epstein. As well as hearing the audio of the Princess, the three-part doc series explains how and when they were recorded, and the extraordinary lengths Diana went to in order to ensure her story could be heard. For example, she devised a daring plan to have the tapes secretly smuggled out of Kensington Palace. Colthurst and Morton appear in the series, as does Michael O’Mara, publisher of Morton’s book, Diana: Her True Story. The recordings and Morton’s tome had a huge impact on the Royal Family and the whole British establishment. The timing of the new doc is appropriate, with 2027 the 30th anniversary of Diana’s death. Cineflix Rights moved for the sales rights and will bring the doc to market at MIPCOM. Stories about the British Royal Family have enduring international appeal. Interest is heightened when royal stories cover Princess Diana, who was one of the most famous women in the world, with people fascinated by her life. THE CHASE AROUND THE WORLD ITV Studios Length: 6 x 60’ Producer: Bright Entertainment Network: ITV (U.K.) Fancy joining the “smartest road trip in the world”? There’s no better way to give a stalwart format a bit of global appeal than by sending its icons and contestants on a journey around the globe. The Chase Around the World does just that, taking a tried-and-tested, colossally successful format and an additional bit of jeopardy, with firm potential for international sales. Much like splashy premium factual shows such as Race Across the World or Destination X, the show sees contestants travel across the globe, this time in a race to find all six Chasers in secret international locations, holding onto the show’s trademark general knowledge challenges but adding an adventure element. In the U.K. version, where the format originated, contestants played for £100,000 ($133,000), although this figure is not fixed for the international remakes. The six pairs went around Rome, haring after two iconic Chasers, the Beast and the Governess, as they journeyed towards Bradley Walsh at the finish line. The route took them through some of the Italian capital’s iconic landmarks as they answered questions that, if incorrect, could lead to serious consequences. The Chase Around the World rated well in the U.K. and is just the latest in a line of entertainment shows that have used travel as a bedrock. It both showcased the spin-off opportunities that such a strong format can open up, and also carries potential to run and run, given that the world is The Chase’s oyster. Local buyers will be licking their lips. articles.title: ‘Dick Clark’s New Year’s Rockin’ Eve with Ryan Seacrest 2027′ To Simulcast On ABC & Disney+
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando ICG Publicists Awards Reveals 2027 Date, Venue & Timeline Saoirse Ronan Addresses Rumor That Husband Jack Lowden Has Been Cast As The New James Bond Chris Colfer On Returning For ‘Glee’ Revival: “I Know Nothing & Have Heard Absolutely Nothing” View All October 7, 2026 8:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Dick Clark's New Year's Rockin' Eve with Ryan Seacrest 2027 Courtesy Dick Clark’s New Year’s Rockin’ Eve with Ryan Seacrest 2027 has set its co-hosts, as the live show will simulcast for the first time on ABC and Disney+. The New Year’s Eve celebration will air live on Thursday, December 31, starting at 8 p.m. ET. Hosted by Ryan Seacrest, Dick Clark’s New Year’s Rockin’ Eve will also feature comedian Druski who will be hosting from Chicago. Rita Ora returns as co-host from New York’s Times Square, while Julianne Hough and Rob Gronkowski will host from Las Vegas. The telecast’s landmark streaming debut follows a record-breaking 2026 edition that further cemented “Dick Clark’s New Year’s Rockin’ Eve” as television’s premier New Year’s Eve destination. The expanded eight-hour celebration, the longest telecast and largest artist lineup in the show’s more than 50-year history, featured 42 performers, four live countdown celebrations, and nearly 100 songs from New York City’s Times Square, Las Vegas, Chicago, Puerto Rico, Nashville, Kansas City and beyond. articles.title: Emilia Clarke & Josh Brolin Latest To Join Series ‘A Roadmap To Happiness’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Tradition Pictures Sets Multi-Project Partnership With Kenan Thompson’s Artists For Artists; Mark Canton, James Maslow & Joseph Sikora Join Advisory Board Meridian Pictures Picks Up Mike Maples Western ‘The Regulator’ Rhys Ifans, Lily Rabe & Sarah Catherine Hook Dramedy ‘Capsized’ Boarded By The Yellow Affair Ahead Of U.S. Festival Bow View All October 7, 2026 8:34am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Emilia Clarke and Josh Brolin Penske Media EXCLUSIVE : Emilia Clarke and Josh Brolin are joining Jason Momoa, Shailene Woodley, Elijah Wood and Alec Baldwin in docuseries A Roadmap To Happiness , which we first announced during this year’s Sundance Film Festival. The show will see author, podcaster and presenter Darin Olien ( Down to Earth with Zac Efron ) travel with actors to different corners of the world in search of the happiest people on Earth. The series will explore what constitutes happiness in different cultures and show the travelers — and viewers — different approaches to contentment. Clarke ( Game of Thrones ) will join the series in Portugal, a country recorded as having some of the happiest children in the world, while Brolin ( Avengers ) will appear in Finland – a country consistently ranked among the happiest in the world – for the series finale. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Casting Emily Blunt, Benicio Del Toro And Josh Brolin Returning For 'Sicario 3' From Black Label And Thunder Road With 'The Weight's Padraic McKinley To Direct Trailers Full 'Whalefall' Trailer: Austin Abrams Experiences All Emotions In The Belly Of The Beast Directed by Cary Floyd and produced by Cary Floyd, Darin Olien, Heather White Rezner, and DP Nick Higgins, the series is lining up a limited VOD release date for 3/20/2027, which is World Happiness Day. Conversations with platforms and broadcasters about other releases continue. Of joining the series finale in Finland, Brolin commented: “We spend so much of life chasing success, answers, or the next thing but happiness is often quieter than that. Being part of this journey in Finland reminded me that connection, simplicity, and presence may be the most powerful things we have. I’m proud to be part of a project asking questions that matter.” “After decades of traveling the world searching for answers to health, sustainability, and the challenges we face as humans, I realized something profound, happiness may be the missing piece connecting it all,” said co-host and executive producer Olien. “This series is about the people, rituals, and perspectives that remind us how to reconnect to ourselves, each other, and what truly matters.” “People and the planet are at the heart of everything I do,” added Momoa of his work on the series. “Getting to go on this journey with Darin, a friend and warrior for the Earth, makes it even more special. We’re exploring what connects us, what sustains us, and why protecting it matters.” “I know a lot of lives and hearts will be touched by this project, simply by how much mine was and it was laughter that renewed my faith in humanity,” noted Woodley. articles.title: David Brindley Confirmed As Channel 4 Content Chief
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke , Jesse Whittock October 7, 2026 8:42am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Channel 4's headquarters Getty UPDATED with confirmation: David Brindley has been confirmed as the new Director of Programmes at Channel 4 . He will have oversight of all scripted and unscripted genres and will join the Channel 4 board. Channel 4 CEO Priya Dogra said Brindley “has a proven ability to nurture the ideas and talent that create truly standout television.” Related Stories News Louisa Compton Appointed To Channel 4 Board Alongside Next Content Chief News Sony Chief Wayne Garvie: “It’s Very Difficult To See How Channel 4 Survives In Present Form” “As we reshape Channel 4 to invest more in distinctive British content and back creative talent across the UK, I wanted a Director of Programmes who would be able to take ambitious risks in programming and deliver powerful shows that make a cultural impact, while sustaining the bold attitude that has always been the calling card of Channel 4,” she added. “With hundreds of hours of award-winning shows under his belt and deep experience working in public service broadcasting, David is the ideal person to join our existing creative leadership team and help us deliver our vision for the future of Channel 4.” Brindley will “work alongside” news and digital boss Louisa Compton and content strategy chief Kiran Nataraja in the new-look commissioning leadership team. Compton will also join the board . Watch on Deadline He said: “I’m immensely proud to be joining the talented team at Channel 4. At a moment of seismic change within the industry and the channel, it has never been more important to ensure Channel 4 thrives creatively, by deepening its connection with audiences and the production community across the country.” PREVIOUSLY, October 6: David Brindley is set to land one of the biggest jobs in UK television, overseeing programming at pubcaster Channel 4. He is being lined up to replace Ian Katz, who leaves this month having been the broadcaster’s longest-serving Chief Content Officer. Channel 4 declined comment. Broadcast was first with the news. Following a long interview process, Brindley, the CEO of Destination X producer Twofour, and former BBC Three boss Stuart Murphy were understood to have been the final two in the running. Brindley has been considered a frontrunner for the role since speculation began over who would replace Katz. His ITV Studios-backed outfit produces both the UK and U.S. versions of Destination X and Apple TV’s The Reluctant Traveler with Eugene Levy , and he is well-established in British unscripted production circles. Brindley previously worked for Channel 4 and was behind one of its most impactful shows of all time, Educating Yorkshire , which he recently revived at Twofour. Considered a savvy operator with commissioning and production experience, he got down to the last four for the top BBC content job last year. His competitor for the role, Murphy, would have been a more left-field choice given he has spent most of the past decade out of television. After playing major roles at the BBC, where he launched BBC Three in 2003, and Sky, where he was Director of Entertainment Channels between 2015 and 2018, he became CEO of the English National Opera in 2018 and held the role for five years. Others understood to have been in the running included BBC iPlayer boss Dan McGolpin, Amazon’s Clarkson’s Farm exec Fozia Khan and Tanya Shaw, who has run British indies Shine and Zinc. Brindley’s job is a tough one. Channel 4 is laying off around 340 staff, the net’s biggest round of cuts in its 40-year history , and this is hitting commissioning hard, with around 50% of roles set to be reduced. Big shifts he will oversee include combining the drama and comedy teams into one scripted unit and a merger of its unscripted divisions. The nature of his role has also changed since Katz left. Brindley will report to new CEO Priya Dogra, as will news boss Louisa Compton and strategy chief Kiran Nataraja. Both Brindley and Compton will sit on the Channel 4 board. Compton and Nataraja previously reported to Katz. Max Goldbart contributed reporting. articles.title: ‘Anna Pigeon’ Renewed For Season 2 At USA Network
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Campione Katie Campione Senior TV & Labor Reporter @katie_campione More Stories By Katherine ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Recap: Lots Of Breakthroughs On Mariah Carey Night Stiffen Competition ‘Abbott Elementary’ To Film 100th Episode At Disneyland WGA East Reveals 2026 Support Staff Basic Training Program Graduates View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Tracy Spiridakos as Anna Pigeon in 'Anna Pigeon' Michelle Faye/USA Network Anna Pigeon has been renewed for Season 2 at USA Network . The news comes ahead of the Season 1 finale, which airs October 9. The series has done well for USA Network so far, becoming the highest-rated original scripted series premiere on the network in nearly eight years, with an average of 2.35 million total viewers within the seven days following the premiere. Across its Season 1 run, Anna Pigeon has reached 18 million total viewers, USA Network says. Based on the New York Times best-selling novels by Nevada Barr, the first season follows Anna Pigeon (Tracy Spiridakos), a former city slicker who became a park ranger after a devastating loss changed the trajectory of her life forever. While Anna tries to outrun her demons, her focus turns to solving crimes that have taken place within national park grounds, no matter who or what gets in her way. Season 2 promises continued mystery and adventure, as Anna’s story continues to unfold. Related Stories News 'The Rainmaker' Sets Season 2 Release Date; Unveils Full Trailer News 'The Rainmaker' Boss Teases Season 2 As First-Look Photos Of Merle Dandridge, Richard Kind & Returning Cast Drop Season 1 also stars Paulina Alexis, Ronnie Rowe, Tricia Helfer, Kim Coates, Crystle Lightning, Cooper Levy, Manuel Rodriguez-Saenz, Ryan Northcott, Nikki Rae Hallow, Jordan Sledz and Melanie Scrofano. Watch on Deadline “It’s been really thrilling to see audiences fall in love with Anna and come to the park every week,” showrunner Morwyn Brebner said in a statement. “We’re so grateful to our cast and crew who brought Nevada Barr’s iconic world to life with such heart and passion; we cannot wait to get back outside for season two.” Adds Michael Sluchan, SVP, Scripted Content, Entertainment, VERSANT: “Anna Pigeon has connected with audiences in a meaningful way, bringing a compelling new heroine and a fresh perspective to USA Network. We’re thrilled to continue Anna’s journey with Tracy, Morwyn, Lea and our incredible partners at Cineflix.” Anna Pigeon is produced by Cineflix and SEVEN24 Films for USA Network in association with Bell Media. Brebner serves as showrunner, with Lea Thompson directing. Brebner and Thompson executive produce alongside Brett Burlock, Sonia Hosko, Todd Berger, Julie Di Cresce, Tom Cox, Jordy Randall, Peter Emerson and Gordon Gilbertson. Leslie Cowan serves as producer. Anna Pigeon is Bell Media’s first co-commission with Versant’s USA Network. articles.title: ‘The Hunting Wives’ Renewed For Season 3 By Netflix Ahead Of Season 2 Release
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Skydance CEOs Meet The Press On Day One Post-Merger With String Of Promises & Few Answers Skydance Co-CEO On Prospect Of TV Studios Merging: “We’re Not Looking To Reduce Output Production” Skydance To Make Paramount & Warner Bros Lots Specialized, Each Housing Film Or TV/Streaming View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Malin Åkerman and Brittany Snow in 'The Hunting Wives' Netflix The frisky wives of Maple Brook will keep hunting. Netflix has given an early Season 3 renewal to The Hunting Wives , its raunchy mystery drama series starring Brittany Snow and Malin Åkerman. Casting for the eight-episode new installment is already underway. The pickup comes a month and a half ahead of the Season 2 release November 26 as a Netflix-branded series from Lionsgate Television and 3 Arts Entertainment in nearly all countries where Netflix is available. Related Stories News ‘The Hunting Wives’ Season 2 First Look Photos & Premiere Date Set At Netflix News Why Is ‘The Hunting Wives’ So Racy? Behind Netflix Series’ Unusual Deal As It Eyes UK Release & Hopes For Season 2 After Strong US Debut The unusual qualifier stems from The Hunting Wives ‘ unusual origin as a U.S.-only acquisition by Netflix of the finished first season, which had been developed and produced for Starz before reverting back to the studio in the network’s split from Lionsgate. Watch on Deadline Despite being only available in the U.S., The Hunting Wives Season 1 spent five total weeks in Netflix’s Global Top 10 English-language TV list, reaching as high as No. 2 in its second week. In light of the success, Netflix made a deal with Lionsgate, which was able to buy the show back in most international markets it had sold it to, making it available on Netflix where it made the Top 10 TV list in 40 countries, reached No. 1 in 10 countries, including the US, and has garnered over 35 million views since its July 2025 release. Once the vast majority of markets were cleared, Netflix also renewed the series created by Rebecca Cutter based on the bestselling novel by May Cobb for a second season. While Season 1 remains an acquisition, starting with Season 2, The Hunting Wives is a Netflix original. The early Season 3 renewal will allow it to return within a year, an early cadence that is increasingly becoming the standard for streamers on shows that do not require elaborate production and post-production. “I’m so stoked to be heading back to Maple Brook, and I promise that once you’ve finished Season 2, you’ll be desperate to see what happens next,” said writer, executive producer and showrunner Cutter. “Buckle up, because Season 3 will be even more scandalous and twisted.” Also executive producing are Erwin Stoff for 3 Arts Entertainment and Cobb. Lionsgate Television is the studio. articles.title: Michael Irby Cast In Universal’s ‘Miami Vice ’85’ As Lt. Lou Rodriguez
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy André Holland Joins Universal’s ‘Miami Vice ’85’ Peri Gilpin To Play Brooke Shields’ Sister In Acorn TV’s ‘You’re Killing Me’ ‘Tulsa King’ Renewed For Season 5 With Move To NY; Scarlet Rose Stallone Promoted & Erik Palladino Among New Cast View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L to R: Michael Irby and Gregory Sierra as Lt. Lou Rodriguez in 'Miami Vice' TV Series Getty, Universal TV EXCLUSIVE: The cast of Universal’s Miami Vice ’85 continues to expand with Michael Irby ( Mayans M.C., Barry) joining the fold. Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler lead the film as Ricardo Tubbs and Sonny Crockett, respectively. Alden Ehrenreich , Whitney Peak , Camila Morrone , John Leguizamo , Danny Ramirez and Walton Goggins also star. Irby will play Lt. Lou Rodriguez, sources close to production reveal. The original character in the hit NBC series Miami Vic e, who was boss of Metro-Dade Police Department’s Organized Crime Bureau, Vice Division, was played by Gregory Sierra. Rodriguez was killed off after four episodes at Sierra’s request to be written out because he didn’t want to move to Miami. His exit made way for Edward James Olmos to take the reins as Lt. Martin Castillo, beginning in Episode 6 of the crime drama’s freshman season. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Casting André Holland Joins Universal's 'Miami Vice '85' Casting Walton Goggins Joins Michael B. Jordan And Austin Butler In 'Miami Vice '85' At Universal The feature puts Irby on the opposite side of the law from his roles in FX’s Mayans M.C. and HBO’s Barry , where he played President of the Mayans Motor Cycle Club Obispo “Bishop” Losa and Bolivian mob boss Cristobal Sifuentes, respectively. Gregory Sierra with Philip Michael Thomas as Ricardo Tubbs and Don Johnson as Sonny Crockett in ‘Miami Vice’ pilot Universal Television From screenwriter Dan Gilroy and director Joseph Kosinski, Miami Vice ’85 explores the glamour and corruption of mid-1980s Miami in an all-new version of Miami Vice . The film is inspired by the pilot episode of the 1984-90 NBC series, titled “Brother’s Keeper,” which aired on September 16, 1984. Written by series creator Anthony Yerkovich and executive produced by Michael Mann, the two-hour series premiere of Miami Vice introduced the world to Vice cop Sonny Crockett (Don Johnson) and New York detective Ricardo Tubbs (Philip Michael Thomas), who are brought together by destiny, though they do not really vibe at first. They eventually become partners, but first they investigate Colombian drug lord Calderone (Miguel Piñero), the show’s main antagonist across Season 1. In the episode, it’s revealed why Crockett and Tubbs have beef that runs deep with Calderone. For Tubbs, he’s visiting SoFla seeking revenge for his slain brother, who was taken down after the cartel leader put out a hit on his life. Crockett also has reason to want Calderone off the streets: the crime boss killed the former’s partner Eddie Rivera (Jimmy Smits) early in the pilot. Despite first appearances, Crockett and Tubbs decide they want to work together, taking down bad guys in the Magic City and having some fun in between. Aside from the Crockett and Tubbs intro, the episode is famously known for a driving scene where the duo is in Crockett’s black Ferrari Daytona Spyder while listening to Phil Collins’ song In the Air Tonight . Also notable, though not from this episode, Leguizamo portrayed Calderone’s son Orlando twice in the series. Leguizamo will also star in Miami Vice ’85 , though it is as yet unknown if he will reprise the role. The movie will be filmed for Imax and is set for release on May 19, 2028. Production will begin this year. Miami Vice ’85 is being produced by Dylan Clark/Dylan Clark Productions ( The Batman , The Penguin ) and Kosinski ( F1 ). Gilroy is writing the script, based on characters created by Yerkovich from the series executive produced by Yerkovich and Mann. Eric Warren Singer wrote an earlier draft of the screenplay. Irby is represented by Independent Artist Group and Coronel Group. articles.title: Oscars: Saudi Arabia Submits ‘A Matter Of Life & Death’ For Best International Feature Film
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Low Light Films Boards Jane Schoenbrun EP’d ‘The Arrow At Rest’ + First Clip The Coven Boards Australian Slasher ‘The Only One’ Starring Mel Jarnson & Saphira Moran ‘Lucy Lost’ & ‘Submarine Jim’ Animation Studio Xilam Sets Management Reshuffle View All October 7, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'A Matter of Life and Death' Film Clinic, Front Row Productions, Arabia Pictures Group, Rotana Studios The Saudi Film Commission has selected Anas Ba Tahaf’s A Matter of Life and Death as Saudi Arabia ’s official submission for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards. Local stars Yaqoub Alfarhan ( Scales , Norah ) and Sarah Taibah ( Mandoob ) play an unlikely couple whose love blossoms against the odds in the Jeddah-set feature, one of the quirkiest local romantic-come-black comedies to come out of Saudi Arabia since the lifting of its 35-year cinema ban in 2017. Related Stories News Oscars 2027 International Feature Film Submissions By Country: Denmark, Italy & Spain Among Latest To Declare Below The Line 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More Taibah, who also wrote the screenplay, plays Hayat, a fiercely independent young woman convinced that a generational curse will kill her on her 30th birthday. Having made peace with dying, she crosses paths with Yousef (Alfarhan), a brilliant but emotionally detached heart surgeon living with bradycardia. His abnormally slow heartbeat only seems to quicken when he comes close to death or to killing. As a surgeon surrounded every day by the fragile line between life and death, temptation is never far away. She wants to die, he wants to kill, and they should be perfect for each other. Then, inconveniently, they fall in love. Watch on Deadline The cast also features Hosam Al Harthy, Fay Fouad, Amani Aljameel, Ghada Aboud, Rahaf Ibrahim and Najla Alabdullah, with production design by Ibrahim Khorma. The film world premiered at the Red Sea International Film Festival in December 2025, before opening theatrically across Saudi Arabia on June 25, 2026 . It later received a Jury Special Mention at the 12th Saudi Film Festival, where Taibah won the Golden Palm for Best Acting for her performance as Hayat. Director Ba Tahaf previously worked as coproducer, editor and first assistant director on Mahmoud Sabbagh’s Barakah Meets Barakah , which represented Saudi Arabia in the Best Foreign Language Film category at the 89th Academy Awards. A Matter of Life and Death is produced by Mohamed Hefzy for Film Clinic , Gianluca Chakra for Front Row Filmed Entertainment, and Abdulelah Alahmary and Ahmad Taema for Arabia Pictures, with support from the Red Sea Fund. Front Row Filmed Entertainment is handling international sales. “Hayat is impulsive, funny, stubborn, fearless and spectacularly headstrong, a contemporary Saudi woman written without explanation or apology. Her independence is not the story. It is simply who she is,” wrote Front Row in a statement announcing the Saudi Oscar entry. “The film’s originality lies as much in how it is told as in its premise. Its heightened visual style moves confidently between romance, fantasy and black comedy, shifting tone without settling neatly into any one genre. When the mythology behind Hayat’s curse is revealed, live action briefly gives way to a handcrafted, gothic animated sequence, adding another unexpected layer to the film’s visual language.” “Together, these elements give A Matter of Life and Death an identity that stands apart within Saudi cinema and feels equally distinctive within Arab filmmaking more broadly. Set and shot in Jeddah, the city is integral to that identity. Its streets, architecture, humour, language and contradictions are woven into the story, grounding its increasingly fantastical world in a recognisable contemporary reality.” Written by and starring Sarah Taibah alongside Yaqoub Al Farhan, the film is produced by Film Clinic, Front Row Filmed Entertainment and Arabia Pictures, with Front Row handling international sales. Saudi Arabia, which first started submitting films to the Oscars in 2013, kicking off with Haifaa Al-Mansour’s Wadjada. Subsequent entries have included Barakah Meets Barakah (2016) and Shahad Ameen’s Hijra last year. The country has yet to be nominated. articles.title: ‘SNL’ Alum Punkie Johnson Sets Debut Stand-Up Special ‘Long Tiddie Short Story’ With Hartbeat
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt David Krumholtz Joins ‘The Trial Of Louise Woodward’ At HBO After Mulling “Indefinite Break” From Acting Ben Shapiro Decries Suspension Of Production On Daily Wire Movie ‘Pawn Shop’ As Shoot Resumes: “Politics, Pure And Simple” Jessica Biel Joins Searchlight Pictures’ ‘Playmates’ View All October 7, 2026 9:06am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Punkie Johnson Van Corona EXCLUSIVE: Former Saturday Night Live cast member Punkie Johnson has announced that her debut stand-up special, Long Tiddie Short Story , will premiere on Hartbeat’s LOL Stand-Up YouTube Channel October 21st. In the special, Johnson steps into the ring to reflect on her time at SNL , her complicated relationship with queerness, and her own questionable life choices. It’s billed as a brutally honest and unfiltered hour about marriage, sex, drugs, and what can transpire when you pretend to be “normal.” Johnson taped the hour at The Comedy Store in Los Angeles. Directed by Steven Feinartz, it’ll be available as a comedy album across audio streaming services on November 13, available for pre-order on October 21. The special is produced by Feinartz and Danielle Lee and exec produced by Johnson, Ethan Stern and Dominic Del Bene. Related Stories Casting 'Barbershop': Roy Wood Jr., Punkie Johnson, Brett Gray & E.J. Bonilla Join Jermaine Fowler In Amazon Series News Punkie Johnson & Chloe Troast Talk "Very Hard" Post-'SNL' Careers: "No Life Jacket" Hartbeat reunites with Johnson after producing her 2023 SiriusXM show, Love Thang , for Kevin Hart’s LOL Radio. Recently, she’s also filmed a role in their upcoming Barbershop TV series for Prime Video. The special joins a growing stand-up slate from Hartbeat, including the second installment of LOL Live at Hulu, with new half-hour specials currently rolling out monthly, as well as Funny AF , the stand-up competition series that was picked up for a second season after drumming up major viewership at Netflix. Watch on Deadline The deal to distribute Johnson’s special was spearheaded by Hartbeat President & Chief Distribution Officer Jeff Clanagan and VP, Comedy Eric Weil. Clanagan told us, “Punkie is exactly the kind of singular comedic voice we want to champion at Hartbeat. We’ve had the opportunity to work with her across radio, television and now stand-up, and bringing her debut special directly to audiences on YouTube reflects our larger strategy of creating more ways for great comedians to reach fans wherever they are. We’re excited to continue building with Punkie and supporting her work across platforms.” Weil added, “Punkie has the rare ability to be completely fearless and deeply personal at the same time. Long Tiddie Short Story is unmistakably her — honest, unpredictable and incredibly funny. We’re proud to be part of her first stand-up special and to continue a creative relationship with Punkie that has grown across radio, television and stand-up.” A comedian, actress and writer from New Orleans, Louisiana, Johnson was with SNL for four seasons beginning in 2020. Touring nationally these days while developing original television and film projects, she’s previously been seen starring in two seasons of Lena Waithe’s The Chi , with additional roles in HBO Max’s Love Life , Netflix’s Space Force , HBO’s A Black Lady Sketch Show and CBS’s Ghosts . Johnson also served as a writer/consultant on Peacock’s reboot of Queer as Folk and appeared in the cult hit comedy film Bottoms opposite Ayo Edebiri and Rachel Sennott. She is repped by Ethan Stern at Underscore, WME and Ziffren Brittenham. articles.title: Theo Rossi, Ron Perlman & Rachelle Goulding Wrap Under-The-Radar Horror Film ‘Renew’, First Look Revealed
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Tradition Pictures Sets Multi-Project Partnership With Kenan Thompson’s Artists For Artists; Mark Canton, James Maslow & Joseph Sikora Join Advisory Board Meridian Pictures Picks Up Mike Maples Western ‘The Regulator’ Rhys Ifans, Lily Rabe & Sarah Catherine Hook Dramedy ‘Capsized’ Boarded By The Yellow Affair Ahead Of U.S. Festival Bow View All October 7, 2026 9:10am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Theo Rossi, Ron Perlman and Rachelle Goulding Penske Media EXCLUSIVE : Theo Rossi has added an under-the-radar horror film to his genre era in the shape of Renew , which will reunite him on screen with his Sons Of Anarchy , Come With Me and The Saviors co-star Ron Perlman . Filming recently wrapped on Renew , “a suspense-driven horror film that begins as an intimate love story before descending into visceral horror”. Directed by Tommy DeNucci from a screenplay he co-wrote with Rossi, the film, which also stars Rachelle Goulding ( Suits LA ), “follows a husband and wife who return to the secluded Montana guest ranch where they were married to renew their vows, hoping to leave the past behind and begin again. But when she mysteriously disappears, he is forced to confront the life he fought to escape as he uncovers a hidden evil lurking beneath the ranch’s idyllic façade.” Below is a first-look image. Related Stories News Ron Perlman, Peter Facinelli, Mark Elias & Serena Wang Starring In Indie Film 'We Could Be Heroes' News Ron Perlman, Shohreh Aghdashloo & Cuba Gooding Jr. Set For Golden Dunes Jury Duty In Dubai The ensemble cast also includes Ronnie Gene Blevins, Allison Dunbar, Sam Daly, Danny Rivera, Rebecca Creskoff, Darko Ostojic, Bonnie Gayle Sparks, Barron Boedecker and Chris Wilks. Diana Hull and Rossi produced the film. Watch on Deadline Production wrapped in Red Lodge and Roberts, Montana. Rossi was joined on the project by longtime producing partner Nicholas Carmona. DeNucci has previously directed Rossi in movies Vault and Play Dirty . Rossi, also known for HBO’s The Penguin , Netflix’s Carry-On , and Emily the Criminal , commented: “What excited Tommy and me most was building the film around two people with a shared history who are trying to find their way back to each other. There’s hope, humor and heart in that, but also the weight of everything they’ve been through. When that hope comes under threat, you find out how far someone will go for the person they love. We wanted audiences invested in Randy and Liz from the very beginning, so they feel the danger right alongside them.” Producer Diana Hull said: “Watching this cast and crew bring Renew to life in Montana was incredibly rewarding. The film asks a great deal of its performers, both emotionally and physically, and their commitment carried through every stage of production. We can’t wait for audiences to experience what we’ve created together.” DeNucci added: “From the very first draft, we wanted audiences to settle into this beautiful Montana escape and genuinely fall in love with Randy and Liz. The more authentic their relationship feels, the more terrifying it becomes when everything begins to unravel. This remarkable cast brought that emotional journey to life in ways that exceeded every expectation.” Rossie and Perlman will also join forces on the upcoming Sons of Anarchy reboot Legends . Vestron Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection Dirty Dancing is coming to Broadway . The musical adaptation of the 1987 film will make a stop at the Lena Horne Theatre on Broadway starting this winter, as part of its national tour. The show will play the theater from Feb. 12 through Sept. 5. The musical features a new book by Eleanor Bergstein, the original screenwriter of the film, direction by Lonny Price (who played Neil Kellerman in the film) and choreography by Darrell Grand Moultrie ( Fat Ham ). The tour launched in St. Paul, Minnesota, in August and will continue this fall in Detroit, West Palm Beach, Boston, Toronto and more cities before the Broadway engagement. The musical will resume its national run after Broadway. articles.title: ‘Ted Lasso’ Star Jason Sudeikis Goes One-on-One With WNBA Great Breanna Stewart (Watch)
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Breaking News Done Deal: Paramount Completes Warner Bros. Takeover, Creating Hollywood Giant close Jason Sudeikis is a fixture of CeLIBrity row, the group of famous New York Liberty fans who go to see Breanna Stewart dominate the opposition. They were photographed Sept. 16 at Splashlight Studios in New York. Sudeikis: Styling by Keith Wagner; God’s True Cashmere shirt; Todd Snyder pants; Nike sneakers; Sudeikis’ T-shirt, cap, watch. Stewart: Styling by Jan-Michael Quammie; Stone Island top, jeans; Stewart’s shoes, jewelry. Photographed by Nina Westervelt; Sudeikis grooming: Chelsea Gehr. Stewart hair: Antoinette Hill; Makeup: Sofia Nikolic “Stewie!” When the New York Liberty’s star forward Breanna Stewart shows up on the THR set, all 6-feet-4 of her, Jason Sudeikis reaches up to embrace her. It’s the kind of hug he’s given her courtside after the team’s major victories, including during their run to the 2024 WNBA championship. The four-time Emmy winner, who played college basketball in his native Kansas before going into comedy and becoming Saturday Night Live’ s resident jock, doesn’t do fandom halfway. It’s why, today, he refuses to remove his Arsenal hat; he became a hard-core supporter of the Premier League team while in London shooting Ted Lasso , which in its fourth season sees the irrepressibly upbeat coach leading a women’s soccer team. It’s why he’s wearing Nikes in UConn colorways to honor Stewart’s alma mater. And it’s why he’s become a fixture of CeLIBrity row, the group of Liberty superfans that includes Spike Lee, Alicia Keys and the cast of Severance . Related Stories TV 'Ted Lasso' Takes the Express Lane in Season 4's Penultimate Episode TV WNBA Playoffs 2026: Where to Watch Post-Season Women's Basketball Games Live Online There are few accomplishments in basketball that Stewart has not achieved. She has four NCAA titles, one WNBA title, four World Cup championships and three Olympic gold medals. The 32-year-old is far from done. “I want to beat all the records,” she tells Sudeikis. Who are we to doubt her? A week after her sit-down with Sudeikis, the eight-seed Liberty will sweep top-seed Minnesota Lynx in the playoffs, toppling the team led by Stewart’s friend and former UConn teammate Napheesa Collier, with whom she co-founded the successful 3-on-3 offseason league Unrivaled in 2023. In this third edition of THR ‘s Game Recognize Game series, Stewart and Sudeikis discuss the surprising parallels in their career paths, the ways in which the WNBA is handling the scrutiny since superstar Caitlin Clark’s arrival ushered in millions of new fans but also culture-war insanity in a league that’s long been a haven of inclusivity, and how she would realistically handle having Ted Lasso as a coach. JASON SUDEIKIS Nice to see you in street clothes. BREANNA STEWART I know, right? We never do this. SUDEIKIS And you never see me out of Liberty gear. We’re doing THR ‘s Game Recognize Game . Athlete, artist, artistic athlete, athletic artist, I’d like to think. … How are the gigs similar? I have my theories, but I’m more interested in what you think. STEWART Well, people ask me why I want to continue to be great, or how I keep winning. There’s this obsessiveness of continuing to go and try to be better. Like, almost an insane confidence. SUDEIKIS Yeah. It doesn’t feel like ambition from the inside. It just feels like, if I have the opportunity to get to continue to do this, why not do it as best as I can, until I can no longer do it? With athletics, though, it seems like, oh, eventually someone younger comes in, with better knees, more athletic, whatever. Rarely is it that they’re hungrier. I don’t know of anybody that’s been in your position that’s just like, “Oh, fuck it, I give up. Let them have it.” That doesn’t happen. STEWART No. Especially when a new person comes in, you’re like, “Oh, I’m going to sauce them.” Like, “Oh, they’re in for a long night.” SUDEIKIS How has the college system changed? It feels like, even from my small understanding, [UConn coach Geno] Auriemma softened in his relationship to the players — we all saw Paige [Bueckers], you know, smack him on the butt. Jason Sudeikis Photographed by Nina Westervelt STEWART He’s so, so soft. Coach Auriemma is so soft. SUDEIKIS Lorne, Lorne Michaels at SNL , I feel like has softened up, too. STEWART When I went to college­ — when I went to UConn, Coach Auriemma was tough. He was an ass. He was really an ass. I was a 17-, 18-year-old that thought I was working hard — and then he just kind of chopped me down. SUDEIKIS Did it help when you look back on it now? Do you go, “Oh, it was worth it”? STEWART It helped. I wouldn’t be where I am without Coach Auriemma. Of course. Did it always need to be like that? Mm, no. SUDEIKIS Same with Lorne, yeah. Has that changed? STEWART Yes. I think the NIL [name-image-likeness] landscape makes it different. He had to soften to keep people around. You could just transfer and not have to sit out. You get paid hundreds of thousands of dollars — millions — to be places. So [as a coach], you’ve got to be nice. SUDEIKIS Exactly! Any idea how that’s going to affect those same 17-, 18-year-olds that you were? Beyond the winning, you get to feel like hot shit. You can go, “Look, Coach, you have to listen to me ’cause I have 250,000 followers. These are my apostles. I am God. They will come after you. They will dox you.” STEWART I think what’s happening with the generation going to college now, their why is not the same. Because my why was, well, I want to be the best player that ever leaves UConn, and I’m going to win four national championships … Breanna Stewart Photographed by Nina Westervelt SUDEIKIS Which you did. No big deal. STEWART … and I want to be great. But, like, their why now is, “Well, I want to get deals. I want to get this money.” That’s my assumption. But when you have the money just being flaunted in front of your face, you’re thinking about it. SUDEIKIS We both come from what are, from the outside view, these cults: SNL and UConn. It teaches you to work hard, probably harder than you thought you needed to. It is the hardest job I ever had. I was there 10 years. I would not be where I am without it. STEWART SNL is incredible. How did that start? SUDEIKIS I mean, it’s not too dissimilar from the journey of a blue-chip athlete on the way in. There are different places that they come and scout. There’s The Groundlings in Los Angeles, that’s where Will Ferrell started or Kristen Wiig. UCB here in New York, where Amy Poehler came from, and a bunch of people behind the scenes. I did a thing called Second City in Chicago. Tina Fey did that. Chris Farley, John Belushi, Gilda Radner back in the day. I was on, like, their JV team, the touring company. A fella named Jeff Richmond, who is Tina Fey’s husband, came out to see our show in Las Vegas. And he was like, “Hey, you ever thought about auditioning for SNL ?” And, at that point, I was like, “No way, Jose. I don’t like that show. I ain’t that.” It was mostly me being a 22-year-old dickhead that was like, “I don’t want something that would never want me.” But I auditioned for it in, like, 2003, and got hired as a writer. Later I had a meeting with Lorne my second year — my sophomore year. I mentioned to him, like, “Hey, you know, to do this, I gave up performing. I’d still really like to do that.” STEWART Yeah. Put me in the game. SUDEIKIS The next show, Tom Brady hosted, and I got to do a bit in one of the scenes that I wrote where I did like the Running Man and the Roger Rabbit and all those silly dances that I still do — that I’ve done on Ted Lasso , that I used to do to make kids on my basketball team laugh. And he put me in the cast, like, two weeks after that. What is it like when Coach says, “Hey, come play for us”? Jason Sudeikis and Breanna Stewart Photographed by Nina Westervelt (2) STEWART It’s not like he’s offering formally. He’s like, “I think you should be here. This place is going to be what makes you better.” And then he’s like, “Well, are you going to come?” SUDEIKIS Did any other place have a shot at you? STEWART Like, for real? I looked at Duke. Beautiful campus. I looked at Maryland, I looked at Penn State. Those were my tops. But no, I wanted to be great. I looked at all the players that came before me and where they were now, and UConn was the only place. SUDEIKIS Fort Scott Community College was the height of my basketball and scholastic career. Which kind of segues into how you kindly invited me to go work out with you with [trainer] Chris Brickley two years ago. STEWART That was great. We should go do that again. SUDEIKIS I’ve never had any kind of masculine macho arrogance of, like, men’s sports versus women’s sports. But if any of that did ever course through my brain and body and soul, it would’ve been eliminated after that afternoon. You’re so good. Like, and you’re so effortlessly good. You’ve been so good for so long that you’re just iconic. … You’re like the Jennifer Aniston of the WNBA. You know what I mean? STEWART Period! Yes. I want to be her. You’ve got to bring her to a game. OK? Thanks. SUDEIKIS I would love to. I think she’s in London right now. STEWART I’m going to write that in my notes: “Bring Jen Aniston to game . “ Handle that. Jason Sudeikis and Breanna Stewart Photographed by Nina Westervelt SUDEIKIS But as we were leaving [the workout], we were just chatting about where [the WNBA] was going, and all these eyeballs, which at least in the past four or five years, sort of gets pushed through the prism of Caitlin [Clark]. And you had said this really wise thing: “We’ve all wanted this success, but with success comes trouble.” And it makes me think of this Nietzsche quote [as paraphrased in Ted Lasso ], “Once you’re at the top of the mountain, what’s left for you but lightning?” You, I think, personally have avoided a lot of that lightning. Why do you think some folks get it and some folks don’t? STEWART I think that the discourse just comes because of the climate. It’s like, if you want the fame and the popularity and the notoriety and all that stuff, like you have to take the good with the bad. SUDEIKIS What’s your relationship with social media? Because that is one of the turbo boosters with all of this. STEWART I’m not doing that. I’m not looking for that. Are you? Do you look for that stuff? SUDEIKIS No. I did for a little bit. STEWART I control what I can control. I detach from judgment. SUDEIKIS That’s a harder thing. It’s very intoxicating, new fame. That was one of those things that I got to view at SNL . If you go seek validation from it, then when they come for you on the other side of it, I think it could just destroy your soul, potentially. STEWART Someone said to me, “Unless I’m going to go to these same people who are telling me how I’m bad at basketball and ask them how I should be parenting my kids, it doesn’t matter.” SUDEIKIS We had our own version of backlash in our little neck of the woods with Ted Lasso . But the discourse doesn’t change the way we go about making the show, for better or worse. And I don’t know how much any of this stuff, these outside influences, affect a locker room. STEWART Well, what I’m having to tell my teammates more and more is to make sure you’re prepared. Don’t let these questions catch you off guard. Obviously, there’s a lot of media surrounding the WNBA, and people are trying to kind of ride the wave, the trajectory of where we’re going. So, now, you’re not only thinking about the next game or next matchup or how am I going to get to the playoffs, but also you have to be ready for the questions that are going to come that are completely outside the court. SUDEIKIS One thing I’ve noticed [going to WNBA games] is that negativity [in the stands], up until maybe this past season, gets rejected like a foreign body in the human. Sudeikis embracing Stewart at a Liberty game in July Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images STEWART I remember when you guys first came to the game. It was 2023. Things are going good, the energy at Barclays is incredible. It’s my first year there. And my teammates were like, “Ted Lasso’s here! We need to get a picture!” Then you brought your kids. You came back. And now, we’re your team. SUDEIKIS A hundred percent, yeah. I remember you early on busting my balls about, like, “Who are you going to cheer for when we play against the [Indiana] Fever [Caitlin Clark’s team]? STEWART Sorry, you can’t come in and cheer for the Fever. We’ll have you removed. SUDEIKIS So you just won, what, your fourth gold medal? STEWART My fourth World Cup medal. SUDEIKIS I went on Wikipedia knowing we were going to do this, and holy moly, it takes three swipes to get through all your [achievements] from your high school days to three days ago. Like, when’s enough enough? ( Laughs. ) STEWART It’s never enough. First of all, I want to beat [four-time WNBA champion, former UConn Husky and Stewart’s former Seattle Storm teammate] Sue [Bird]. So right now I’ve just tied Sue. [ Editor’s note: Stewart beat Bird’s record the following week to become the league’s eighth all-time leading scorer. ] I think winning is addicting. When you win awards and whatnot, you want to do it again, right? When we won here in New York, the parade was insane, and I want to do it again. SUDEIKIS It’d be badass if we pulled it off this year. STEWART Never say never. I plan on playing for a while. I’m newly 32. Virgo. SUDEIKIS The Magic Johnson year. STEWART Yeah, my Magic Johnson year. I want to just keep winning. Stewart at Barclays Center in September Elsa/Getty Images SUDEIKIS I want to ask you about your league, Unrivaled. What was the impetus? It reminds me of the heyday of United Artists and Charlie Chaplin. As I understand it, people were upset with the studio system, specifically actors and the artists themselves, and so they created United Artists. From the outside looking in, there’s a [similar] element to Unrivaled in giving power back to the player. STEWART We’ve exceeded expectations. We have a valuation of $650 million. That’s higher than some WNBA valuations. With Unrivaled, we had the special opportunity to start something new, bring a platform back to the United States, back to our home market during the WNBA offseason, and also pay the players. Give them equity. A league made by players for players. And selling it [to investors] was hard. Like, when you have to sell your show, it’s hard, right? Nobody believes in it. SUDEIKIS Oh my gosh, yeah. We went out to everyone, but only one place [bid for it], Apple. STEWART Yeah. In the beginning, that was the hardest, because you have to get outside investors to believe something that’s just a blueprint. And they’re like, “Well, why is this going to work?” But it starts with the players that agreed to be in it in year one. The strength in numbers is the biggest thing in women’s basketball. SUDEIKIS There was some quote from Del Close, who was an improv guru and a teacher I had for a year before he passed away: “The worst idea with full support will always beat the best idea with no support.” It’s the exact same thing as showbiz. You have this idea about, you know, this universe where people fight with lightsabers and it’s like, I don’t know. “Just do it and give me money on the back end with the action figures.” Like, “OK, dummy.” And then, ha ha, now he has a museum. STEWART So, some people have said that Ted Lasso was dead [after season three]. SUDEIKIS Like, literally? STEWART The show. Not the coach. Hopefully he does not have a heart attack or anything in the finale. SUDEIKIS You’re going to have to watch. Sudeikis (left) as Ted Lasso, and Brendan Hunt as his right-hand man, Coach Beard, in Ted Lasso season four. Courtesy of Apple TV+ STEWART But what made you want to focus on women’s soccer this season? Is it because of the rise in women’s sports? SUDEIKIS It certainly helped open my eyes to it. It’s that experience of those seats we’ve had [at Liberty games at the Barclays Center] the last three seasons and watching these women walk on and off the court that just feels so … gooey with story complexity. When I thought [the show] was done, it really was done. But I just kept hearing the characters’ voices. So it was important for me to just keep jotting down these ideas, and at some point it became too silly — it would almost be selfish — to not do it. STEWART So is there going to be a season five? SUDEIKIS I don’t know. That was smooth. That was smooth. STEWART That scene [in season four] when you went in the women’s locker room with the trash can on your head? That was funny. I really enjoyed that. If Ted Lasso was my coach for the Liberty, I think it would be funny. SUDEIKIS I think we’d have a good time. I don’t know, would you be annoyed? STEWART Maybe. I don’t know if I would be open-minded to some of your, um, practice tactics. I think I would be a little bit grumpy about that. SUDEIKIS Sure. I’d hear that with open arms and an open heart. I’d be like, “All right. All right. Well, you won’t practice tomorrow.” STEWART Great, we get the day off! I saw this thing where this basketball club overseas, Zalgiris, they want you to come coach there. Are you going to do it? SUDEIKIS What, is it the Lithuanian team? Because Sudeikis is Lithuanian? STEWART Yes. Are you going to go do that? You should do that. Doesn’t that sound cool? SUDEIKIS It does sound cool. Will they pay for my flight? If I can bring Brendan [Hunt], who plays Coach Beard, I would literally do anything. So, I just literally found out that Cathy Engelbert, the WNBA commissioner, was stepping down. I would love for her, before she leaves, to give the thumbs-up on a Kansas City franchise. STEWART Yeah. I don’t think that’s going to happen. SUDEIKIS I know, I know, I know. But what would you want out of the next commissioner? It seems like a very difficult job. STEWART I think it is a really difficult job. Honestly, Cathy has obviously gotten a lot of heat. But she deserves some praise, too, as she’s finishing because she helped get an incredible CBA [collective bargaining agreement] done. You can’t look around that. I think that the next commissioner obviously needs to have an incredible business mind because now we’re in the millions, billions type of industry. But also, you need to have some type of sports background just to navigate the space a little bit better. You think of [NBA Commissioner] Adam Silver, and he has a great relationship with the players. And not to say Cathy didn’t. I think that it just took time. It took a little bit longer than it needed to. SUDEIKIS I don’t think you’re brought up enough in the MVP conversation this season. STEWART Clock it. SUDEIKIS You’re just quietly dominating. And I would love to get to a fourth scroll for you on Wikipedia. STEWART I think people just get used to me being great all the time. And it’s expected, so when I do it all the time, it’s not that same brightness because it’s just consistently bright. But I’m definitely going to get you a fourth swipe on Wikipedia. I’m trying to break records here. SUDEIKIS I appreciate it. Which record are you closest to getting the top spot on? STEWART I need another gold medal in the World Cup to break Sue’s record. Diana [Taurasi] has five Olympic gold medals. Let’s just take one thing at a time. So see you in L.A. ’28. This story appeared in the Oct. 7 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

articles.title: How David Ellison’s Skydance Outwitted Everyone
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Done Deal: Paramount Completes Warner Bros. Takeover, Creating Hollywood Giant close A Skydance billboard outside of Paramount Global headquarters in Times Square, on October 6, 2026. Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery closed Tuesday. Adam Gray/Getty Images There is an alternate universe where Warner Bros. Discovery swallowed Paramount. Little did they know that two years later it would be Skydance ’s David Ellison who would own both companies. In late 2023, then-Paramount CEO Bob Bakish had lunch with WBD CEO David Zaslav, where the idea of a potential deal came up. The following month Warners executives went so far as to conduct due diligence on Paramount, before opting not to engage. The talks came just a few weeks after there were rumblings that Ellison was in talks with Paramount’s controlling shareholder, National Amusements, to acquire control of the company. After a process of fits and starts, Ellison and Paramount sealed their deal in July. It was during the drawn-out process to close the Paramount deal that rumors of Ellison coveting Warner Bros. began to spread across town. This story is based on details disclosed in public filings, and from conversations The Hollywood Reporter had with some of the people involved with or familiar with the details of the negotiations and strategy that led to this point. Netflix’s Surprise David Zaslav Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images Ellison and Zaslav would meet for the first time to discuss a potential deal only a month after the Paramount deal had closed at Zaslav’s home Woodland, the Beverly Hills estate that once belonged to the legendary film producer Robert Evans. The first offer was, in the words of one person familiar with the terms, a “lowball.” Ellison had offered a package valued at about $19 per share, with only 60 percent of that in cash, and the remainder in stock. WBD’s board would later write that they felt the offer “undervalued” and “inadequate,” and they unanimously rejected it as they pushed forward with their plan to split the company in two. That’s when the billionaires got involved. David’s father and tech mogul Larry Ellison and Zaslav’s mentor and cable mogul John Malone would enter the picture the following week. On Sep. 24, Zaslav, Malone (then chairman-emeritus of WBD) and Larry Ellison met via Zoom to discuss the first offer, and why WBD rejected it. The next few months saw a flurry of phone calls, Zooms, emails, text messages and in-person meetings, with Ellison raising his offer and reiterating his desire to acquire WBD, at one point floating the idea of Zaslav being co-CEO. WBD, however, remained committed to seeing through the split, with executives there confident that they get more than Ellison was offering if they followed through. They were proven correct just a few weeks later. In October, report leaked that Paramount was actively pursuing WBD, and the floodgates opened. Netflix CEO Ted Sarandos and Comcast’s Brian Roberts reached out to Zaslav, unsolicited, after the media reports, each of them expressing interest in the streaming and studios side of the business. A formal strategic review followed, and the race was on. Comcast proposed an unusual deal, sparked by Mike Cavanagh, that would have seen NBCUniversal spun out and merged with WBD’s streaming and studios business, while Netflix proposed a deal to buy that piece of WBD’s business for $27 per share in a mix of cash and stock. Ellison, meanwhile, continued to up his bid, and began to take meetings with Middle East sovereign wealth funds to shore up the financing for the deal. But as the weeks dragged on, and the talks between the companies continued, Ellison and his team felt that they were not being taken seriously, and that WBD was preferencing other bidders. The Paramount team was flabbergasted: “Every offer [Paramount] made put more money in David Zaslav pocket and put more money to Warner Bros. shareholders, and made it even more certain by going all cash,” one insider recalls. It came to a head on Dec. 4. Sarandos called Zaslav and told him that Netflix was ready to ink its deal for Warners that evening. If they didn’t, the streaming giant would walk away. As the WBD board met to discuss the ultimatum, Ellison sent Zaslav a text message, one that would go unanswered: “Daivd [sic], I appreciate you’re underwater today so I wanted to send you a quick text. Please note when you next meet as a board we wanted to offer you a package that addressed all of the issues you discussed we [sic] me. Those were 1 we wanted to offer complete certainty 2 strong cash value 3 speed to close. Please note importantly we did not include ‘best and final’ in our bid. “Also please know despite the noise of the last 24 hours I have nothing but respect and admiration for you and the company,” he added. “It would be the honor of a lifetime to be your partner and to be the owner of these iconic assets.” Netflix announced its deal the following morning, and the Ellison team went to war. Going to War David Zaslav, Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters as they visited the Warner Bros. Studio lot in December. Warner Bros. Discovery On Monday morning Dec. 8, Paramount announced a hostile tender offer for Warner Bros. At $30 per share, all cash, just hours before Sarandos and Peters were set to take the stage at the UBS building in Manhattan. “Today’s move was entirely expected,” Sarandos told attendees, even as Paramount’s team set up shop just down the hall. “We have a deal done, and we are really happy with the deal for shareholders, for consumers, it’s a great way to create and protect jobs in the entertainment industry.
