articles.title: Iberseries Takeaways: Woody Allen on His New Film, Los Javis Pact With HBO Max, the Tales of Cachou the Brown Bear and More
articles.full_text: Oct 5, 2026 10:54am PT Iberseries Takeaways: Woody Allen on His New Film, Los Javis Pact With HBO Max, the Tales of Cachou the Brown Bear and More More: Erik Barmack on AI; Banijay’s secret, Amazon MGM’s new action breed and the Holy Grail search for original crime By John Hopewell Plus Icon John Hopewell Chief International Correspondent john_hopewell Latest La Oreja de Van Gogh Songs Set to Power an Ambitious Romantic Musical From Fernando González Molina (EXCLUSIVE) 11 hours ago HBO Max Unveils Javier Calvo, Javier Ambrossi Drama Series, Created by ‘Anatomy’ Writer Fran Araújo and ‘Querer’ Scribe Eduard Sola (EXCLUSIVE) 5 days ago Mubi Takes Global on Los Javis ‘La Mesías’ and Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s ‘Riot Police’ as Movistar Plus Rolls Out Iconic Hits Around the World (EXCLUSIVE) 5 days ago See All Woody Allen in Madrid. Oct. 1, 2026 presenting his new film. Credit: Anna Marie de la Fuente When the going gets tough, the tough get going to places like Iberseries & Platino Industria. Its 6th edition, also a pre-Mipcom warm-up, ran over Sept.29-Oct. 2 at Madrid’s Matadero, its rehabilitated orange-red brick former slaughterhouse. That setting seems appropriate. There’s little evidence that Ampere Analysis’ maxim, coined a couple of years ago – a contracting sector chasing a 75% of peak TV business – has not changed. Related Stories 'Voices' Review: Singing Through Fear and Anxiety in a Detroit-Set Musical Thriller ‘Evil Genius’ Review: Courteney Cox Fashions the Pizza Bomber Case Into a Broad, Shrilly Played Farce Some parts of the TV business have hardly altered at all, such as its dependence on great writing, Steve Matthews, Banijay head of scripted, creative, said at an Iberseries company Spotlight. Popular on Variety Yet most companies, from Super Indies and network giants to small former auteur producers are pushing into AI, if only for backroom operations, and microdramas to push back against spiralling costs and diminishing revenues, sustaining cash-flow and not losing out on new growth opportunities. That in turn is driving new mindsets. Making microdramas has made Argentinean producer Lorena Quevedo think of how long certain proceses take in cinema and series. “Suddenly a series we thought had an impossible budget we took up again saying: ‘If we made this microdrama, we cannot not make this series.’” Needful of such insights, delegates broke attendance records up a massive 20% to 3,400 including day passes. Iberseries & Platino Industria is organized by rights collection society EGEDA and Foundation Secuoya, in collaboration with producers’ assn. Fipca and sponsorship from Madrid Film Office and Film Madrid Region. 10 takeaways: Woody Allen The big star at Iberseries, or nearby at least in another part of Madrid, was the 90 year-old New Yorker. Starring an ensemble cast of Marton Csokas, Jemima Kirke Jakob Oftebro, Peter Vives and Alexi Wasser, the provisionally entitled Woody Allen Fall Project rolls Oct. 5 with WestEnd Films handling world sales. Small and debonair, Allen didn’t reveal so much about his upcoming film at an Oct. 1 press conference – he rarely does – though he teased it was a “comedy with romance, intrigue and infidelity.” He also said that Madrid – elegant and beautiful – was perfect for the “diplomatic atmosphere” he wanted for the film. The jury is out how the film will go. “It has to live up to my expectations. That doesn’t mean that it will, but I’ll do my best,” he said. Allen has however made pointed use of seeming postcard settings before, as in “Vicky Cristina Barcelona,” one of his most successful international shoots. Los Javis , Mubi and an HBO Max Coup In one of the biggest news announcements at Iberseries, Mubi acquired global on drama series “La Mesías,” created by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi and sold by Movistar Plus International, which is to TV is what “La Bola Negra” is to cinema. In another, and a coup for HBO Max unveiled development on an enticing new crime series, to be exec produced by Los Javis at their Madrid manner Suma Content. The series is created by Fran Araújo, who co-penned Intl. Emmy-nominated “The Anatomy of the Moment,” and “Querer” co-scribe Eduard Sola, two of Spain’s most exciting writing talents. Most all talk about the Javis’ turns on “La Bola Negra.” They – and indeed HBO Max – are also rapidly creating ever more powerful creative hubs. (L-R) Fran Araújo, Edu Sola (L-R) Fran Araujo, Eduard Sola Credit: Patricia J Garcinuno Erik Barmack on What He Got Wrong About AI, and What He Might Have Got Right, to the Horror of Some Iberseries debated genre.The real horror story for many was AI. Just take the macro stats. Barmack delivered some stats. Revenues for just two U.S. AI companies, Anthropic and OpenAI, are projected to grow to an annual $700 million in the next couple of years, worth 13-15 times the value of Europe and Latin America’s entire media industries. AI is “much more disruptive” than sound, cable TV or streaming. And if “AI companies don’t continue to grow, the entire stock market will crash.” Barmack is a highly respected former Netflix international head. He’s also a recognised AI expert. Could he be wrong? To the relief of much of his producer audience, he did say he’s been wrong on one count. When Sora started, I was sort of convinced that it was over and that we’d be stuck on these loops of of watching 15-second generated clips targeted to your algorithm. That turned out to be wrong because it was too expensive, basically, to make these videos. And there wasn’t a big enough audience for what’s called AI slop.” The Holy Grail: Original Crime and Cachou Presented at Iberseries, the big new Movistar Plus-Arte series “Killing a Bear” is a murder mystery, where the victim is Cachou. A giant Pyrenean brown bear, his death in real life and on screen sparks a criminal investigation, as the event is recounted episode by episode by different characters in six radically warring versions. This originality builds as it feeds into a broader portrait lending historical depth of an ancient Spain battling environmentalists and E.U. regulation to preserve its way of life. Crime still pays, accounting for 27% of scripted TV orders and 24% of first-run scripted TV ordered globally, making it the single most commissioned TV genre, Ampere Analysis’ Guy Bisson tells Variety . But what operators and big indies want is original crime to cut through the crowd, one of the sector’s Holy Grails. Eduard Fernández in ‘Killing a Bear’ Bárbara Sánchez Palomero Banijay’s Secret Mipcom’s conference will kick off with a Jeff Zucker-Marco Bassetti keynote, moderated by Variety co-Editor in Chief Cynthia Littelton, post the Banijay-All3Media $8 billion merger. What’s Banijay’s secret? One obviously is scalable franchises. Another is its network of 170 companies worldwide. “All of these are based on creativity, based on talent, based on writing,” Steve Matthews, Banijay head of scripted, creative, said at an Iberseries Banijay Spotlight. Connecting with great talent, and giving them the trust and resources to make the titles they envision is indeed the key to some of the greatest production operations and producers in the world. Microdramas Open Up Inevitably, Iberseries hosted a vertical drama panel. “I’m from Team Melodrama,” said Argentinean producer Lorena Quevedo, a panelist, arguing the key was “romantic tension.” Her first microdrama – and indeed Argentina’s, – “Dinero, Armas y Feliz Navidad,” released on ReelShort in September 2025, hit 273 million views. Most microdramas are classic melodramas,. The format, however, is opening up in the Spanish-speaking world. Though its slate is primarily made up of vertical dramas, Telemundo Studios has begun to develop 20-episode 10-minute horizontal series, said Telemundo’s Clo Fernandez. 3Pas Studios has recently made a vertical musical, is considering a comedic microdrama, added Javier Williams. Quevedo has produced a vertical actioner. One Direction Amazon MGM is Heading In International: Genre at Scale An Amazon MGM Studios Spotlight was led by Javiera Balmaceda, head of international originals, Latin America, Canada and Australia, and Nicole Morganti, Prime Video head of international originals, Italy & Southern Europe. Both pointed to big action swings – Mexico’s “Venganza,” produced by El Estudio’s Pablo Cruz, and espionage actioner Zeta,” starring Mario Casas as one way to go. Both topped Prime Video Global Top 10 charts. Latin America’s challenge, Balmaceda noted is not necessarily a lack of talent, but a shortage of experience and opportunities to work at scale. Spanish Cinema: Size Matters Scale threaded various panels. Another Example Spain made 423 feature films in 2025, according to the European Audiovisual Observatory. In 2026, as Iberseries unspooled, only four movies can be described as box office hits: “Torrente for President” (€29.1 million: $32.8 million), “Tadeo and the Magic Lamp,” (€7.2 million) “Aida y vuelta” (€5.1 million), “La Bola Negra” (€14.9 million and counting fast) and The Beloved. All are high-end for Spain. Three are based on huge Spanish IP. Another stars Javier Bardem. “The future of Spanish cinema does not lie in making more films, but in getting more people to want to see them,” Atresmedia Cine MD Jaime de Ortiz de Artiñano said late August. That sentiment ran through multiple panels at Iberseries. IPs: Their Power Only 12-14% of new series premieres each year are based on existing IP but existing IP accounts for 40%-50% of the top 100 most in-demand series, Parrot Analytics Jaime Otero said at Iberseries. On average, titles based on IP has 2.3 times more demand than original titles. That rises to 2.9 times titles inspired by real events and 3 times for literary adaptations. Multiples companies are putting large faith in big IPs. At Iberseries, for example, Luis Fernandez, Telemundo president, drilled down at a keynote on its ways forward. One is live events. Another reaching out to YA auds. And another, a 2027 schedule which includes new seasons of “La Reina del Sur,” El Señor de los Cielos” and “Sin Senos No Hay Paraíso,” an awesome franchise trifecta. Spanish-Language New Markets Spanish-language series are successful because they have a captive audience of 600 million native Spanish speakers. Their growth, however, lies elsewhere, Parrot Analytics’ Jaime Otero suggested at Iberseries opening panel. The global demand for series from Spain, Portugal and Latin America series has increased 25% since late August 2024., driven by countries outside the region such as South Korea, up 245%, Japan and China, up 119% in two years, or in Scandinavia where it has doubled. Meanwhile demand in Latin America has edged up or down, according to the territory. Little wonder then that Spanish export and trade board ICEX held an event to boost Spanish talent in Shanghai this July. And a Bake’s Dozen of Deals Announced by Variety at This Year’s Iberseries & Platino Industria: *Movistar Plus International unveiled 33 new sales deals, led by Mubí taking the world on “La Mesias,” and to “Riot Police,” from “The Beloved” director Rodrigo Sorogoyen. International distribution deals were also led by ‘The Anatomy of a Moment,” “Querer,” “The New Years” and ‘The Nameless.’ *HBO Max announced that “La Bola Negra” writer-director-producers Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi are set to exec produce an ambitious new HBO Max drama series created by Fran Araújo and Eduard Sola. *Beta Film has unveiled broad international sales for “Rex – Vienna Calling,” the latest incarnation of the hugely popular three-decade-old “Rex – A Cop’s Best Friend” franchise, as production gets underway on a second season. *Globoplay has greenlit an adaptation of Raphael Montes’ “Uma Mulher no Escuro,” from Banijay Entertainment’s A Fábrica Brazilian banner. The order was announced at an Iberseries Banijay Spotlight panel. *‘Elite’ star Ester Expósito is circling ‘Stink Eye,’ an Iberseries Co-Production & Financing Forum Title. * “The Good Girls” lead Ilse Salas is set to to star in Quijote Films’ “To Die on Your Feet” (“Morir de Pie”) another project pitched at Iberseries & Platino Industria Forum. *”Sin Filtro’ producer JK Media is producing its first original microdramas shot in the U.S. for TelevisaUnivision’s ViXMicrO. *Belgian royalty series “King of Hearts” has secured key VRT backing. The coming-of-age drama series is from Giles Coulier, whose company, De Wereldvrede, is behind such hits as 2019 series “War of the Worlds” and Prix Europa winner, “Albatros.” *‘Plaza Catedral’ director Abner Benaim, Chile’s Daniela Vega and Alfredo Castro have boarded fiction series “School of the Americas.” *France’s Halley Production has boarded thriller ‘Carro Seco,’ about a killer who targets unscrupulous Barcelona real estate speculators. Javier Polo directs the buzz project at Iberseries & Platino Industria’s Co-Production and Financing Forum. *Chile’s Sanfic is set to screen late documentarian Antonio Caro’s swan song “Monguen” among nine Chilean pics in Competition. *”Strawberry and Chocolate” star Jorge Perugorría and Brazil’s Thiago Lacerda lead Havana-Set “Hotel Nacional,” another Iberseries Forum project. articles.title: ‘Imperfect Women’ Renewed for Season 2 at Apple TV With Kerry Washington Returning
articles.full_text: Oct 5, 2026 11:00am PT ‘Imperfect Women’ Renewed for Season 2 at Apple TV With Kerry Washington Returning Justin Hillian will join the series as co-showrunner going into the second season By Joe Otterson Plus Icon Joe Otterson TV Reporter joeotterson Latest As WME’s Literary Media Department Turns 10, It Aims to Keep Pace With How Books Are Adapted: ‘Our Culture Is Shifting’ 2 hours ago ‘Things We Never Got Over’ Amazon Series Adds Six to Cast 3 hours ago ‘The Watcher’ Season 2 to Begin Production 4 Years After Season 1 With Bobby Cannavale, Naomi Watts Returning 3 days ago See All Apple TV “ Imperfect Women ” has been renewed for Season 2 at Apple TV , Variety has learned. Season 1 star Kerry Washington will return to lead the second season. The first season of the show is based on the book of the same name by Araminta Hall, while Season 2 will be based on an original idea built around Washington’s character. “Imperfect Women” debuted on Apple TV back in March. The first season also starred Elisabeth Moss and Kate Mara. Moss’ Love & Squalor Pictures had originally optioned the book for television. Related Stories 'Forgotten Island' Review: A Delightful Animated Celebration of Friendship and Filipino Culture Netflix’s ‘A Different World’ Is a Bold, Fun and Timely Reboot Centering the Uniqueness of Gen Z: TV Review Annie Weisman served as the writer and showrunner on Season 1. She will return for Season 2 as co-showrunner alongside Justin Hillian. The official logline for Season 2 states, “Eleanor (Washington) returns to her hometown roots in the affluent black enclave of Martha’s Vineyard, only to find that beneath it’s idyllic surface, lie secrets and scandals that threaten to upend everything she thought she knew about her past.” Popular on Variety “We were thrilled to see how deeply these women and their stories resonated with audiences around the world, and I’m so excited to step back into Eleanor’s shoes,” Washington said. “She’s intelligent and strong, but she also finds herself navigating complicated and sometimes messy situations. We at Simpson Street along with our incredible partners at Apple and Love & Squalor Pictures can’t wait to explore a fresh chapter for her and share where this story takes us next.” Hillian was most recently the co-showrunner on the Showtime series “The Chi.” He has also worked on shows like “Snowfall” at FX and “I’m Dying Up Here,” also for Showtime. He is repped by WME, 3 Arts, and Yorn Levine. “After a wildly entertaining first season, driven by the performances of Kerry, Lizzie and Kate, we jumped at the opportunity to expand the world of ‘Imperfect Women’ through Kerry’s fan favorite character of Eleanor,” said Matt Cherniss, Apple TV’s head of programming. “Annie and Justin’s thrilling new story felt like an exciting and natural next chapter. We can’t wait for fans to experience it.” Weisman and Hillian are the creators, co-showrunners, and executive producers on Season 2. Washington executive produces via Simpson Street along with Pilar Savone. Moss and Lindsey McManus executive produce via Love & Squalor. 20th Television and Apple Studios produce. The renewal comes ahead of the Season 4 premiere on Oct. 16. Stallone’s daughter Scarlet Rose Stallone, who has played Spencer on all four seasons of the show, has been promoted to series regular. articles.title: ‘I, Addict’ Creator Javier Giner Unpacks ‘This Solitude,’ a Film ‘About ‘Those Who Keep Functioning While Something Inside Them Is Falling Apart’
articles.full_text: Oct 5, 2026 11:09am PT ‘I, Addict’ Creator Javier Giner Unpacks ‘This Solitude,’ a Film ‘About ‘Those Who Keep Functioning While Something Inside Them Is Falling Apart’ 'I wanted to take risks, try new forms, trust more in silence and what happens off-screen. I didn’t want to explain the characters psychologically, but to observe them. Where 'I, Addict' screamed, 'This Solitude' whispers,' says Giner By Roberto Prieto Plus Icon Roberto Prieto Latest Produced by J.A. Bayona, Netflix Documentary Series ‘Beyond Society’ Examines What Happens After the Survivors of the 1972 Andes Plane Crash Return to Uruguay 1 week ago ECAM Incubator Film Project ‘Our Raised Skin’ Explores the Male Body and the Fear of Its Touch 1 week ago Kazakhstan’s ‘Mugalim’ From Director Ayana Nurdinova World Premieres in the New Directors Section of San Sebastián 2 weeks ago See All Marina Salas in 'This Solitude' Courtesy of Filmax Basque director Javier Giner ‘s “ This Solitude ” (“Esta Soledad”) recently premiered at the San Sebastián Film Festival’s New Directors section on Sept. 23. Giner is the creator and co-director of the Disney+ series “I, Addict,” based on his autobiographical book by the same name. It earned lead actor Oriol Pla the International Emmy for Best Actor. Also starring Pla, “This Solitude” follows Leo and Lorea after their five-year relationship has ended. Each of them has to figure out how to continue living life on their own in Bilbao. Leo is a struggling actor who has to work as a grocery clerk to make ends meet while taking care of his disabled father. Lorea is a troubled writer who looks to a former prison inmate for companionship. Both must confront their loneliness and unresolved issues and look for meaning in a world that can sometimes feel cruel and scary. Related Stories ‘The Influencer Project’ Review: Found Footage Terror Takes a Tepid Danish Holiday ‘Vintage Violence’ Review: Cole Sprouse Heads Up a Hyper-Online Gonzo Freakout in Japan Oriol Pla in ‘This Solitude’ “The film is about people who are losing control of their lives. Loneliness may be one of the few truly democratic things in life; what isn’t democratic are the resources we have to survive it,” Giner told Variety . Popular on Variety The film stars Pal, Marina Salas (“Join Me for Breakfast”), Gemma Martínez, Kai Etxaniz and Itziar Lazkano. Giner co-wrote the film with Luisa Matienzo, who is also one of the film’s producers along with Miguel Torrente. The production companies are Balance Media Entertainment, Fuga de Cuerpos, La Embajada TV and Basajaun Filmak. International sales are being handled by Filmax and they will release the film theatrically in Spain on Oct. 30. Director Javier Giner, ‘This Solitude’ Photo Credit: David Herranza Variety interviewed Javier Giner after the film’s premiere in San Sebastián. There is a loneliness epidemic around the world and this film seems to address it. Javier Giner: I didn’t set out to make a film about the loneliness epidemic. I’m a little wary of starting a film with a theme. This began with the desire to create, more than a film, an emotional state that would stay with the audience after they left the theater. I looked around me and saw people with apparently full lives — jobs, friends, partners, phones that never stop, social media — and yet they were profoundly lonely and exhausted. I was fascinated by the contradiction: we’ve never had so many tools to avoid being alone and, paradoxically, so many ways of never truly connecting with anyone. Is this story also autobiographical like your book “I, Addict”? Giner: Everything I write is autobiographical in some way, but not in the sense that “I, Addict” was, where I was explicitly telling the story of a period in my own life. In “Esta Soledad,” the autobiography is in the gaze and in the emotions: Sadness, family relationships, certain ways of loving, the fear of losing someone, the feeling of not knowing what to do with your life. More and more, what interests me is whether what I write is emotionally true. To me, that is a deeper form of autobiography, and something I find endlessly fascinating. The film is also about absent parents, both physically and emotionally. Do you think this is especially true for the new generation? Giner: I think every generation inherits from the previous one not only its traumas, but also its emotional vocabulary, including the things it never had words for. The parents in “Esta Soledad” are not monsters. Even when they cause pain, they love their children and they do the best they can. But loving someone and knowing how to love someone are two very different things. Children end up living with the emotional consequences of decisions they never made. I think we all spend part of our lives trying to understand what we received from our parents, and another part deciding what we’re going to do with it. You chose to work with Oriol Pla again after “I, Addict.” Giner: Oriol and I have something more valuable than simply understanding each other: we trust each other completely. And trust allows for things that are far more interesting and profound than comfort. After “I, Addict,” we had already gone through some very emotionally demanding places together, so now we can arrive on set and barely need to talk. Sometimes a word or a look is enough. Or I can simply tell him, “I don’t know exactly what I’m looking for. Let’s find it together.” Oriol can be explosive, physical, unpredictable, almost animalistic, and five seconds later he can do something tiny that breaks your heart. Very few actors can inhabit both of those extremes. As an actor, he’s a Stradivarius, and on top of that he’s an incredible human being. He’s my brother, my partner. Bilbao seems to be a central character in the film, sometimes portrayed as lonely, dark and gritty. Would you agree? Giner: Yes, although I never wanted to film Bilbao as a sad city, but rather as a state of mind. I wanted to film what almost never gets filmed anymore: not the postcard, but the humidity, the noise, the architecture, the industrial memory, that light that can change completely within a matter of minutes. There is something very physical about the city; at times, it almost seems to weigh on the bodies. That connected with Leo and Lorea. Their external world remains exactly where it was while everything inside them has changed completely. The streets are the same, but they no longer mean the same thing. I believe strongly in that: Cities don’t change when we suffer; the way we look at them does. So Bilbao wasn’t there to illustrate their sadness. It had to remain indifferent to it. And paradoxically, that indifference is what ultimately makes the city so deeply emotional. articles.title: New Skydance Sets Top Executive Structure As Paramount-WBD Merger Set To Close
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News New Skydance Sets Top Executive Structure As Paramount-WBD Merger Set To Close Read the full story By Peter White , Jill Goldsmith October 5, 2026 6:11am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc Clockwise Top L-R: Casey Bloys, George Cheeks, Dana Goldberg, Josh Greenstein, James Gunn, Peter Safran, JB Perette, Mark Thompson, Bari Weiss Skydance After a year of negotiations, false starts, and internal and external politicking, the question of who will run the combined media and entertainment giant created by Paramount acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery has been answered. As anticipated, the company, which will be called simply Skydance , has set top roles for Casey Bloys , as co-chair and chief content officer of Skydance DTC, and George Cheeks as head of Skydance TV. JB Perrette is making the jump from WBD as Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance TV and Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance DTC. Related Stories News Mark Thompson To Remain At CNN As Chairman Under Ellison's Skydance Executives Channing Dungey Poised For Expanded Post-Merger Role Overseeing Paramount & WBD Cable Networks - The Dish Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein will co-chair the motion picture group. James Gunn and Peter Safran will remain atop DC Studios. As reported, Warner Bros Motion Picture Chiefs Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy‘s last day will be Tuesday , when the merger is set to officially close. Watch on Deadline Mark Thompson was named Chairman and Editor-in-Chief of CNN Worldwide , Bari Weiss editor-in-chief of CBS News. See list below. All will be reporting directly to co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz. CEO Corporate Leadership Team Andy Gordon, President Dennis Cinelli, Chief Financial Officer Makan Delrahim, Chief Legal Officer and President, Global Corporate Affairs Dane Glasgow, Chief Product Officer Rebecca Mall, Chief Marketing Officer Melissa Zukerman, Chief Communications Officer CEO Business Leadership Team Casey Bloys, Co-Chair and Chief Content Officer, Skydance DTC George Cheeks, Co-Chair and Chief Content Officer, Skydance TV Dana Goldberg, Co-Chair, Skydance Motion Picture Group Josh Greenstein, Co-Chair, Skydance Motion Picture Group James Gunn, Co-Chairman of DC Studios JB Perrette, Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance TV and Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance DTC Peter Safran, Co-Chairman of DC Studios CEO News Executive Leadership Team Mark Thompson , Chairman and Editor-in-Chief of CNN Worldwide Bari Weiss, Editor-in-Chief of CBS News A complete list of the merged company’s executive leadership team will be issued soon after close. “I’m incredibly proud to introduce the team that will lead Skydance forward, a group that reflects the ambition behind this historic combination,” Ellison said. “Together, Paramount and Warner Bros. will form a creative-first home with the scale, imagination and technology to define entertainment for a generation. The leaders joining me have built some of the most beloved franchises and businesses in the industry, and they share a deep respect for the creative process and a belief that great stories have the power to entertain, unite and inspire audiences around the world. Their talent, experience and ambition are exactly what this moment demands, and together we will build a next-generation global media company that leads the industry in creative excellence and innovation, and delivers for audiences, creators, partners and shareholders alike.” Today’s lineup comes just over a year after news broke that Paramount was exploring a deal to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery , a month after David Ellison’s Skydance closed its $8.4 billion deal to buy Paramount . Ellison founded Skydance in 2010, backed by his father Larry Ellison, the billionaire co-founder of Oracle. He expanded the company over the years, adding sports and animation divisions to film and television production. He launched his recent ambitious sequence of acquisitions by first acquiring Shari Redstone’s majority ownership stake in Paramount in August of 2025 and turning almost immediately to pursuit of Warner Bros. Discovery, ultimately prying it from the arms of Netflix with a series of sweetened offers. The WBD deal, a smaller company buying a much larger one, is one of the biggest leveraged buyouts in history and will load the combined entity with about $80 billion in debt and hefty interest expenses to service it, creating fears of layoffs. Ellison has promised Wall Street $6 billion in cost savings but has insisted most of that will not come from jobs cuts . News of who will run the new Skydance, which brings together brands such as Harry Potter, Mission Impossible , Friends and Yellowstone , had started to emerge over the last week. The org chart began to shape after a court settlement cleared the decks for Paramount-WBD to come together in the massive deal valued at $110 billion. On September 30, former Mattel CEO Kreiz, who was also previously CEO of Endemol, was named Co-CEO of the company alongside Ellison. “Our goals as a team are to establish Skydance as the premier Hollywood content engine and home for the world’s leading storytellers, accelerate our integrated DTC platform with the best content, leading-edge technology and superior consumer experience, and optimize our highly profitable linear TV portfolio, reaching audiences globally across every entertainment vertical,” Kreiz said today. “Together, we will: Win in storytelling by leveraging our creative capabilities, talent relationships, production prowess and expansive library of iconic IP; Build the most technologically capable media company through a modern tech platform to enhance the user experience, improve how we work and achieve operating efficiencies; and Lead in a crowded market by capitalizing on our scale, assets and global reach to compete in an evolving marketplace, drive synergies and grow our business.” Cindy Holland, who was Paramount’s Chair of Direct-to-Consumer, ostensibly running Paramount+, was the first to officially reveal she was stepping down ahead of the deal closing. Holland’s departure answered one of the biggest questions heading into the combination: who would lead streaming. That move telegraphed that Bloys, Chairman and CEO of HBO and HBO Max Content, was in line for this major new role at the new company, as indicated in Holland’s departure note to colleagues on Sept. 29. “David is optimizing for HBO stability,” she wrote. In it’s note today, the company said the new team is “designed to drive transformation and growth, deepen collaboration across the business, and ensure the combined company is positioned to execute on its mission.” Ellison intends to focus on the company’s long-term strategy, creative vision and direction, including talent relationships, strategic partnerships, technology and capital allocation. Kreiz will focus on tday-to-day management and integrating of the combined business. Andy Gordon will work closely with both on strategic priorities across its businesses. All three will serve on the board of directors, with Ellison as chairman. articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News New Skydance Sets Top Executive Structure As Paramount-WBD Merger Set To Close Read the full story By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt ‘Grey Gardens’ Helmer Michael Sucsy Sets Audible Adaptation ‘A Murder To Remember’ With Amazon MGM Studios Paradigm Signs Screenwriter Jim Taylor IAG Signs ‘What Happened To Doris?’ Director Nick Simon Off Fantastic Fest Premiere View All October 5, 2026 9:43am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jim Taylor Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: Jim Taylor , the Academy Award and Golden Globe-winning screenwriter known for his longtime creative partnership with filmmaker Alexander Payne on a series of lauded, darkly comedic character studies, has inked with Paradigm for representation. Payne and Taylor first collaborated on the Laura Dern-led indie satire Citizen Ruth , following that up with the Tom Perrotta adaptation Election , a dark comedy starring Matthew Broderick and Reese Witherspoon that brought them an Oscar nomination for Best Adapted Screenplay and scored Independent Spirit Awards wins for Picture, Director and Screenplay, bringing Witherspoon her first Golden Globe nomination. Related Stories Agencies 'Outer Range' Showrunner Charles Murray Signs With Paradigm Agencies Aaron Dominguez Signs With Paradigm; Joins Cast Of 'Power: Origins' Taylor and Payne won the Golden Globe for Best Screenplay for About Schmidt , an existential dramedy whose stars Nicholson and Kathy Bates earned Oscar nominations. Two years later, the duo won the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay for Sideways , the celebrated wine country dramedy starring Paul Giamatti, Thomas Haden Church, Virginia Madsen and Sandra Oh, based on the 2004 novel by Rex Pickett. The film earned Academy Award nominations for Giamatti, Handen Church and Madsen for acting, as well as Payne for directing. In addition, Taylor and Payne won a BAFTA Award for Best Adapted Screenplay. Watch on Deadline Outside of his collaboration with Payne, Taylor is known for his creative partnership with his wife, Oscar-nominated filmmaker Tamara Jenkins ( The Savages ). Together, they adapted the Nick Hornby novel Juliet, Naked into the 2018 film starring Rose Byrne and Ethan Hawke. Taylor was a producer on Payne’s 2011 film The Descendants , starring George Clooney, which was nominated for five Oscars and won two Golden Globes. Together, they’re currently adapting an Election sequel, based on Perrotta’s 2022 novel Tracy Flick Can’t Win , for Paramount, with Hello Sunshine and Bona Fide producing. Taylor continues to be represented by Untitled Entertainment and attorney John Diemer at Goodman, Genow, Schenkman. The partnership is The Black List’s first with an independent publisher. Spiegel & Grau are best known for award-winning books such as Just Mercy by Bryan Stevenson and Piper Kerman’s Orange is the New Black and recent bestsellers Beartooth by Callan Wink, The Fire Agent by David Baerwald and Margaret Renkl’s The Comfort of Crows. Law Summit: Nina Shaw & Patricia Glaser Honored On Day Of Big Ideas, Big Insights; Watch The Video Presentations News 'The Write Path' Seminar For Emerging Writers Returns For Second Year With Insights From ATX TV, SeriesFest, Sundance Institute & The Black List Film and television adaptations currently underway from the Spiegel & Grau catalogue include Culpability by Bruce Holsinger, under development; Everything/Nothing/Someon e by Alice Carrière, under development with producer Lauri Firstenberg/IF Innovation Foundation; Go As A River by Shelley Read, under development with producers Paula Mazur and Mitchell Kaplan at Mazur Kaplan Company ( The Guernsey Literary and Potato Peel Society, All The Bright Places ), The Boys by Katie Hafner, under development with producers Ross Katz ( In The Bedroom, Lost In Translation ) and Jonathan Krauss; among others. The integration expands access to published books (including fiction and nonfiction titles) as potential IP). Spiegel & Grau books can be found via searching by title, author, genre and other associated book information available on blcklst.com . Metadata provided by Spiegel & Grau includes additional information such as a published book’s imprint, book cover art, book description, and more. This initiative also makes it easier for Spiegel & Grau authors to list their published books in their Black List profile quickly and efficiently, according to S&G. When Spiegel & Grau authors add titles to their Black List profiles, key project fields will be pre-populated, reducing manual entry and ensuring accurate, consistent information across the platform. Liza Wachter, Spiegel & Grau President and Director of Film and Television, said, “This partnership opens our catalog to the film and television industry in a new way. We’re proud to be the first independent publisher to partner with The Black List.” “As a reader, I’ve been a fan of Spiegel & Grau for most of my adult life; it is a dream to be partnering with them on this initiative, The Black List’s second with a trade publisher, our first with an indie publisher. The Spiegel & Grau catalogue will be a great resource for TV/Film industry members searching IP for adaptation,” said Randy Winston, Creative Director of Fiction at The Black List. articles.title: Billboard Acquires ‘Cosmic Symphony,’ Laura Karpman Documentary On Iconic Instruments Lost In LA Wildfires: “A Requiem And A Celebration”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News New Skydance Sets Top Executive Structure As Paramount-WBD Merger Set To Close Read the full story By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew ‘I’m Doing My Job’ Trailer: Six Women ER Docs Combat Covid, Raise Kids In Aneri Shah’s Directorial Debut Brilliance Of The Who’s Leader Shines In ‘Pete Townshend: Behind Blue Eyes,’ Screening At Hamptons & Mill Valley ‘Speak.’ Is Spoken For: Documentary+ To Stream Film About High School Oratory Competitors View All October 5, 2026 10:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The remains of Starr Parodi's piano, an instrument used in the score for 'The Wizard of Oz,' are recovered from the ashes of the LA wildfires. Billboard EXCLUSIVE: Billboard has acquired Cosmic Symphony , the directorial debut of Oscar-nominated composer Laura Karpman that explores irreplaceable musical instruments lost in the Los Angeles wildfires, and the artists who owned them. EGOT winner John Legend, two-time Academy Award winner Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy, and actress, singer and songwriter Rita Wilson are among the executive producers of the short documentary. Billboard plans to launch the film on its digital channels and Billboard TV (available on Amazon Fire and Samsung TV+) on Tuesday, October 27. The night before – Monday, October 26 – the film’s Los Angeles premiere will take place at the Wallis Annenberg Center for the Performing Arts in Beverly Hills. Related Stories News Laura Karpman Hid An Alan Silvestri Homage In Music For 'Captain America: Brave New World' - Sound & Screen Film News Deadline's Sound & Screen: Film Sets Lineup For 2025 Edition, From 'Kpop Demon Hunters' To Kesha, Oscar Winners Ludwig Göransson, Alexandre Desplat, Michael Giacchino & More Each of the four musicians featured in the documentary – bassist and composer John Clayton, pianist and educator Susie Chung, pianist and composer Starr Parodi, and composer, guitarist and pianist Diane Warren – suffered terrible losses in the January 2025 wildfires, including beloved instruments. One of Clayton’s basses destroyed when fire consumed his home in Altadena was almost 200 years old and had been owned formerly by bassist Ray Brown. Watch on Deadline John Clayton on bass in ‘Cosmic Symphony’ (an animation overlays the instrument). Courtesy of Billboard “ Cosmic Symphony explores a truth that every musician knows – that musical instruments have souls,” notes a release. “Four iconic instruments, including The Wizard of Oz and A Star is Born pianos, all lost in the 2025 Los Angeles Fires, are celebrated by John Clayton, Susie Chung, Starr Parodi and Diane Warren, culminating in an animated send-off towards an imagined future, a Cosmic Symphony.” Karpman directed the film and composed the original score. In a statement, she said, “When a musician loses an instrument, they lose a part of themselves – their partner, their voice. In the aftermath of the Los Angeles Fires, I felt a strong sense of urgency; my friends, musicians across Los Angeles, were experiencing profound loss, and their experiences needed to be captured. I envisioned this film, my first as a director, simultaneously as a requiem and a celebration. Somewhere in the heavens, these beloved instruments have formed a glorious orchestra—a cosmic symphony where every lost voice is restored. “ Cosmic Symphony memorializes the instruments, honors their journeys, and affirms the resilience of the human spirit. Each instrument lost represents a story interrupted, a melody waiting to be continued. Music, after all, is the language of survival—the force that keeps us connected even in the face of devastation.” The film is produced by Laura Karpman and Lorenza Muñoz. Along with Legend, Obaid-Chinoy, and Wilson, executive producers include Mike Jackson, Legend’s partner at Get Lifted Film Co, Christina Kounelias, and Peter Rotter. Amy Andersson is a co-producer. Diane Warren at the piano, with H.E.R. on guitar in ‘Cosmic Symphony.’ Courtesy of Billboard “Artists are the beating heart of Los Angeles, the creative capitol of the world,” Legend commented. “As artists, we know that instruments are core to the music we make. Cosmic Symphony is a thank you to all of the musical instruments that help us sing our song. As we look back on the immense tragedy of the fires of 2025, I’m inspired by the stories of loss and resilience that are portrayed in this film. I am so happy to join my friend Laura Karpman in celebrating the music of our city.” Jackson added, “ Cosmic Symphony is a beautiful reminder of how deeply music is tied to memory, identity and community. Laura has created something that honors what was lost while also celebrating the artists and stories that endure. We’re proud to be part of a film that captures the resilience of Los Angeles and the extraordinary role music plays in bringing people together.” Wilson’s work in music includes the albums AM/FM , Rita Wilson , Bigger Picture , and Halfway to Home . “Laura Karpman’s short documentary film, Cosmic Symphony , illuminates for us how instruments are not inanimate objects that have no life,” Wilson observed. “They are our friends, our confidants, our family. And just like those friends and family, they have lives that preceded, sometimes even our own lives. They bring their history to each musician who plays them, and to each of us who listens. It’s been an honor being a part of this film. I doubt I will ever be able to look at an instrument in the same way again without the distinct feeling that each instrument has had a life of its own.” The Los Angeles premiere on October 26 at the Annenberg will be followed by a concert performance featuring the musicians in the film and more. All ticket proceeds will go towards MusiCares, the nonprofit that provides health, financial, and emergency relief services to professional musicians. Composer Laura Karpman seen onstage at Deadline’s 2025 Sound & Screen Film held at UCLA’s Royce Hall on November 5, 2025 in Los Angeles. JC Olivera/Deadline via Getty Images Karpman’s composing credits include 2023’s American Fiction , for which she earned an Academy Award nomination; East of Eden (2026); Give Me the Ball! (2026); The Marvels (2023), and Lovecraft Country (2020). She directed Cosmic Symphony and produced the film alongside Lorenza Muñoz. Michael Wohl and Kate Amend edited Cosmic Symphony . Cinematography is by Christina Dunlap; Temple Hale serves as animation director. Sound is by Paul Hollman. In the film, Clayton likens the bass he lost in the fire to a grail. “It was a masterful bass,” he says. “When I touched it, I really thought to myself, ‘This bass can do anything.’” Chung says of the Steinway she lost, which had been used in the 2018 version of A Star Is Born directed by Bradley Cooper, “I developed this relationship with this piano. I believe my piano has a soul.” Mark Thompson Staying At CNN As Chairman; Channing Dungey Role Expands ‘The Batman Part II’ Filming Paused As Matt Reeves Steps Away For Personal Matter $8M Lowest Cruise Open In 19 Years, Will Lose $150M: What Happened? articles.title: ‘Imperfect Women’ Renewed For Season 2 By Apple Centered On Kerry Washington’s Character Eleanor
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News New Skydance Sets Top Executive Structure As Paramount-WBD Merger Set To Close Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Imperfect Women’ Renewed For Season 2 By Apple Centered On Kerry Washington’s Character Eleanor James Van Der Beek Remembered In Tearful ‘Dawson’s Creek’ Reunion At Greg Berlanti’s Heroes Gala That Also Honored Katherine LaNasa Post-Merger Skydance Keeping Both HBO Max & Paramount+ Streaming Brands View All October 5, 2026 11:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Kerry Washington in 'Imperfect Women Apple TV+ Call it Imperfect Woman . The trend of streaming limited series becoming ongoing ones continues with Apple TV ordering a second season of thriller Imperfect Women . Taking a spinoff approach, it will follow one of the limited series’ three titular characters, Eleanor, played by Kerry Washington . Imperfect Women , based on Araminta Hall’s novel, revolved around best friends Eleanor and Mary (Elisabeth Moss) as they tried to solve the murder of the third member of their friends group, Nancy (Kate Mara), seen in flashbacks. Washington and Moss executive produced the original installment in addition to starring and will also both executive produce Season 2. Related Stories Casting Scott Foley Joins Apple TV's 'Shrinking' For Season 4 News All The Songs In 'Ted Lasso' Season 4 So Far There is no second Imperfect Women book so there is no source material for Season 2. Instead, it is based on an original story from series creator Annie Weisman and Justin Hillian. The two will serve as co-showrunners on the second season, which will change locations from Los Angeles, where Season 1 was set. Watch on Deadline In Season 2, Eleanor (Washington) returns to her hometown roots in the affluent black enclave of Martha’s Vineyard, only to find that beneath it’s idyllic surface, lie secrets and scandals that threaten to upend everything she thought she knew about her past.” For now, there are no plans for Moss’ Mary and Nancy’s widower Robert (Joel Kinnaman) to be in the second installment which picks up on the Eleanor’s flash-forward scene in the finale, which resonated with fans. It showed her moving away from the toxic dynamic of her relationships and enjoying a new life on a yacht with a new love interest. While cast deals are still being worked out, expected to return as part of the new Eleanor-centered installment are Leslie Odom Jr., who plays her brother, and Sheryl Lee Ralph, who plays their mother. As for the lingering question over Mary and Robert’s ambiguous glance at the end of the finale as the two were seen celebrating the birthday of Mary’s daughter together, that may be answered in Season 2 with a reference of the characters’ status. “We were thrilled to see how deeply these women and their stories resonated with audiences around the world, and I’m so excited to step back into Eleanor’s shoes,” Washington said. “She’s intelligent and strong, but she also finds herself navigating complicated and sometimes messy situations. We at Simpson Street along with our incredible partners at Apple and Love & Squalor Pictures can’t wait to explore a fresh chapter for her and share where this story takes us next.” The long list of limited series that have been picked up for additional installments include Apple TV’s Reasonable Doubt, Netflix’s Untamed, Squid Game, The Beast In Me and Beef , HBO’s Big Little Lies, The White Lotus, True Detective and Task , HBO’s Good American Family and FX’s Shōgun. Imperfect Women is a co-production between 20th Television and Apple Studios. The second season is created, co-showrun and executive produced by Weisman and Hillian, and executive produced by Washington for her Simpson Street banner alongside Pilar Savone. Moss and Lindsey McManus, who initially optioned the book, via their production company Love & Squalor Pictures are executive producers alongside author Hall. “After a wildly entertaining first season, driven by the performances of Kerry, Lizzie and Kate, we jumped at the opportunity to expand the world of Imperfect Women through Kerry’s fan favorite character of Eleanor,” said Matt Cherniss, Apple TV’s head of programming. “Annie and Justin’s thrilling new story felt like an exciting and natural next chapter. We can’t wait for fans to experience it.” Mark Thompson Staying At CNN As Chairman; Channing Dungey Role Expands ‘The Batman Part II’ Filming Paused As Matt Reeves Steps Away For Personal Matter $8M Lowest Cruise Open In 19 Years, Will Lose $150M: What Happened?
