articles.title: DOJ Argues CNN & Other Outlets Can Be Banned From White House If Trump Determines They Didn’t Meet “Minimum Requirements Of Professionalism”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Kennedy Center Honors To Move To D.C.’s Capital One Arena Amid Closure Of Arts Complex U.S. Job Growth Slowed To 29,000 In September, With Slight Dip In Movie And Music Employment Fox News Tops September And Q3 Ratings; MS NOW Sees Gains, CNN Shows Uptick In Some Categories View All October 2, 2026 9:36pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Donald Trump Andrew Harnik/Getty Images The Justice Department argued that Donald Trump can legally ban CNN , MS NOW and Politico from the White House because he determined that they didn’t meet the “minimum requirements of professionalism.” Last month, a federal judge granted the three outlets a temporary restraining order that forced the White House to reinstate dozens of their reporters’ hard passes. The outlets are now asking the judge to extend that 14-day order for a longer term via a preliminary injunction, claiming that Trump’s ban is a violation of their First and Fifth amendment rights. U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly, a Trump appointee, has said that he is bound by the precedent set in In a 1977 D.C. Circuit opinion, Sherrill vs. Knight, in which the judges ruled that “the protection afforded newsgathering under the First Amendment guarantee of freedom of the press requires that this access not be denied arbitrarily or for less than compelling reasons.” Related Stories Late Night TV 'Real Time': Bill Maher Tells New Skydance Bosses "Don't Believe What Trump Is Tweeting About Me" News Kennedy Center Honors To Move To D.C.'s Capital One Arena Amid Closure Of Arts Complex In a court filing on Friday , the DOJ claimed that the Sherrill case still would allow for the president to restrict the three outlets from accessing the White House grounds because the White House has a “compelling interest.” Watch on Deadline The DOJ lawyers claimed that the Sherrill decision does not “prevent the President from concluding that bona fide journalists would identify sources instead of relying on anonymous sources, commit to factual accuracy, and provide the White House an opportunity to comment, rather than ‘perform their duties in a way that … interfere[s] with the White House’s daily operations.’ …At a bare minimum, it is a significant violation of decorum to publish classified and sensitive national security information.” The news outlets’ legal team has rejected that assertion, writing in a filing earlier this week that Trump’s “statements also make clear he implemented the ban to coerce more favorable coverage from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, and to deter other journalists and news organizations from newsgathering and reporting that the President might view as negative. And his administration has continued to retaliate against Plaintiffs even after the temporary restraining order, only underscoring that Defendants’ motive is to punish and chill journalism they dislike.” Even as access to the White House grounds has been reinstated, the White House has continued to restrict CNN from coverage of TV pool assignments, including travel with Trump on Air Force One. The outlets’ lawyers, led by Theodore Boutrous Jr., also noted that Trump and other White House officials “overlooked that the First Amendment protects reporting on matters affecting national security.” Kelly has set a hearing for Thursday on the news outlets’ motion for a preliminary injunction. In granting a TRO, Kelly concluded that the White House failed to provide due process to the news outlets. The DOJ has pointed to letters sent to the outlets as evidence that they were given due process. But those letters were sent on Sept. 22, four days after Trump’s ban was started. The judge also has noted that some of the objectionable stories cited by the DOJ do not have to do with national security. Kelly wrote in his order that “even the justifications provided to Plaintiffs after this case was filed are ambiguous about the true purpose of the revocations: while Defendants’ letters to Plaintiffs mention national security concerns, they purport to identify reporting that ‘threatened national security and/or spread falsehoods’ leaving open the possibility that all the stories fall into the later bucket, rather than the former.” Skydance Putting All 3 TV Studios Under George Cheeks: WBTV, CBS Studios, PTVS ‘Verity’ Solid $32M Start; ‘Digger’ At $10M Lowest Cruise Open In 19 Years What’s Next For De Luca, Abdy; Top Film Jobs To Greenstein, Goldberg Post-Merger Skydance Keeping Paramount+ & HBO Brands Read More About: 2 Comments

articles.title: ‘Concrete Turned to Sand’ Dives Into Oyster Farms, With Otherworldly Imagery From the ‘Backrooms’ DP (Exclusive Clip)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 2, 2026 5:45am 'Concrete Turned to Sand' film still Courtesy of Slag Pile Films If the liminal atmosphere in Backrooms , enhanced by the cinematography of Jeremy Cox, gave you a sense of dread, his camera work on Concrete Turned to Sand will take you into a very different space – oyster farms in British Columbia, Canada. Yes, oyster farms! But again, you better get ready for an immersive sensory cinematic experience that will plunge you into a world full of otherworldly, almost sci-fi-esque, images and all sorts of different emotions and sensations. The film from Vancouver-based directors Jessica Johnson and Ryan Ermacora, will screen, starting on Oct. 11, in the BFI London Film Festival ‘s (LFF) Documentary Competition program, but it is not your regular doc. In fact, notes about the film, which is shot on 35mm, describe it as “a radical refusal of the conventional documentary narrative.” Related Stories Business MIA Market Unveils 2026 Program, Lineup For Digital Era TV Daniel Ezra's Full-Circle Goodbye to 'All American' The movie from Slag Pile Films received its world premiere at the Hot Docs Canadian International Documentary Festival in Toronto and will now celebrate its international premiere in London. Audiences can expect natural richness, such as underwater images of glistening shellfish, to encounter ecological dread. After all, the oysters on the coast of the Discovery Islands that are featured in the film take years to reach maturity, but all around them, the pace of environmental change is accelerating. And through Cox’s lens, nature looks, and almost feels, otherworldly. The film’s soundscape, created with sound artist and musician Scott Gailey, adds another key sensory layer. ‘Concrete Turned to Sand,’ courtesy of Slag Pile Films Don’t expect a multitude of data charts and the like, though. After all, the press notes for the film highlight: “Amid accelerated climate change and lives increasingly hyper-mediated by technology, the film resists the impulse to explain, choosing sensation over exposition.” You can catch a trailer for Concrete Turned to Sand right here, but THR can now also premiere an exclusive clip from the film at the end of this post. Through their work, Johnson and Ermacora explore “the convergence of labor, landscape and the political and economic forces that shape them.” As a result, in Concrete Turned to Sand , oyster farming becomes a lens for the collision of different time scales: the years it takes an oyster to mature, the accelerating pace of environmental change, and the geological time of our planet. And that is by design. After all, the creative team explains: “By placing human labor and science within these vastly different temporalities, the film asks us to reconsider not only how we look at the state of the environment, but how we understand our own brief presence – and effect – within it.” The rich cinematic imagery and sound give new forms to the often complex and invisible realities of climate change. ‘Concrete Turned to Sand,’ courtesy of Slag Pile Films “We worked with scientists to provide insight into ocean acidification and its impacts, while offering perspectives on the geological timescale of our ecological circumstances,” say Johnson and Ermacora. “This project explores methods of representing climate change by experimenting with optical and auditory techniques that play with the distanciation between the viewer and the ecological subject of the film. Concrete Turned to Sand creates an encounter between the beauty and strangeness of our world, engaging us to think beyond our atomization and towards broader ecological understanding and context.” For some scientific insight and to get another glimpse into the world of the film, check out an exclusive clip from Concrete Turned to Sand below. THR

articles.title: It’s Skydance: David Ellison Brands Combined Paramount-Warner Bros. With His Studio’s Title
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 6:11am David Ellison David Becker/Getty Images The entertainment business’ newest conglomerate has a name: Skydance . David Ellison on Friday shared on X that once Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery combine, the new corporate brand will take the name of the studio he founded 20 years ago. But while that will be the corporate name, Paramount and Warner Bros. will serve as sub-brands. “Both have distinct identities, extraordinary legacies and brands that have resonated with audiences for generations,” Ellison wrote. “We wanted a name that would give the combined company an identity of its own while allowing Paramount and Warner Bros. — and all our extraordinary brands — to remain in the spotlight.” The name answers one of the bigger unanswered questions about the new company, which will firmly be among the biggest in the business, alongside The Walt Disney Co. and Netflix. In the entertainment business, the truth is that the corporate brand doesn’t always matter. It does for Disney, which is synonymous with a certain type of family-friendly content, and it does for Netflix, which is synonymous with streaming, but the industry past and present has been filled with owners that have names like Comcast, Viacom, News Corp., Versant, Capital Cities, etc. Hardly household names for most consumers. For most public companies, a corporate name is just a corporate name, a “house of brands” to hold the consumer-facing ones, even if they may share the name of a film studio. Ellison founded the Skydance film studio in 2006, and used it as a vehicle to acquire Paramount last year, before pivoting to Warner Bros. Discovery shortly after. He also posted a sizzle video featuring footage from some of the film and TV projects of the combined company, ending with a title card that perhaps tees up just how how is thinking about the individual brands that will live within Skydance. David Ellison’s reveal of Skydance as the holding corporation name. @ellisonskydance/X The card features the Skydance logo in the middle, surrounded by the logos for the Paramount and Warners film studios, CBS, HBO Max, Paramount+, DC Comics, Nickelodeon, and CNN, suggesting the importance of those brands to the larger strategy. Reading between the lines, one gets the sense that the film studios and streaming platforms will retain their own identities, with CBS (sports and broadcast), Nickelodeon (kids and family) and CNN (news) anchoring their own parts of the business. “We have big goals for Skydance, and we intend to pursue them with passion, imagination and a willingness to take smart risks,” Ellison wrote. “At the same time, we will honor what makes Paramount and Warner Bros. special — giving both studios the opportunity to grow, tell more great stories and bring those stories to even broader audiences around the world, powered by the scale and capabilities of Skydance.” The $111 billion mega-merger is slated to close next week, with Ellison joined by former Mattel chief Ynon Kreiz as co-CEO. Other members of the leadership team are still being determined. THR

articles.title: Guillermo del Toro Defends Tom Cruise’s ‘Digger,’ Rips “Petty” Headline
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By James Hibberd Plus Icon James Hibberd Writer-at-Large JamesHibberd Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 6:28am Riz Ahmed in 'Digger.' Courtesy Warner Bros. Pictures Digger has found a big defender in Guillermo del Toro . The Oscar-winning Frankenstein and The Shape of Water director posted a couple of times over the last 24 hours advocating for the beleaguered Alejandro G. Iñárritu film, which has generated polarized ( some scathing ) reviews. The director’s first message on the subject was reacting to a post from the entertainment news site IGN, which had written, “The theater experience won’t change your mind on Digger , and the laughs that are there still will be when it hits HBO Max.” Related Stories Movies Why Is Tom Cruise's 'Digger' Facing Such a Bumpy Box Office Road? Movies Tom Cruise's 'Digger' Was Originally Titled 'Blah, Blah, Blah,' Iñárritu Reveals Del Toro shot back : “Entirely Petty headline. Love it or not. And, yes, I do. The film delivers in scale, ambition and reach at a theatrical screen level. Daring, bold and Cinematically complex. Decidedly a Theatrical experience.” Then, reacting to a post about Ken Russell’s controversial 1971 film, The Devils , del Toro wrote, “I was a kid and I remember this film — released by [Warner Bros.] was [called by critics] ‘excessive, overbearing’ etc and, in my country, Mexico, we were told that the Church explicitly considered it blasphemy. And here we are … I LOVE it more than ever — because it is NOT about possession but what the political narrative does with it. Glad WB takes risks — even now…” Continued the director, now directly referring to Digger : “BTW there is a ‘climate change’ movie in release that Is NOT about climate change but the manipulation of narratives — and yes it is released by WB (possibly the very last movie WB as such will ever release) and has been deemed ‘excessive, overbearing’ so see it in a theatre.” Not too many are expected to see Digger in a theater this weekend, however, with the film eyeing a domestic opening that’s south of $15 million. On the reviews front, the film currently sits at 54 percent positive on Rotten Tomatoes. The audience score is higher at 65 percent (presumably, given all the hubbub in the press, those still going to see the film had at least some idea what they’re going into). Iñárritu and del Toro have been friends for decades and regularly consult with one another on projects. The duo, along with Alfonso Cuarón, have been called Mexican cinema’s “Three Amigos.” In a profile on the trio’s friendship from The Los Angeles Times in 2006, Iñárritu said, “We share, we complain, we fight, we suggest. And then you support.” Del Toro’s next film is The Buried Giant , a stop-motion animated adaptation of Kazuo Ishiguro’s 2015 novel for Netflix. THR

articles.title: Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros.
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Mia Galuppo Plus Icon Mia Galuppo Senior Entertainment Reporter miagaluppo Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 6:57am Pamela Abdy and Michael De Luca attend the 'Digger' London premiere. Stuart C. Wilson/Getty Images Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy are out at Warner Bros, an insider tells The Hollywood Reporter . The news of film chiefs’ imminent exit comes as Paramount Skydance prepares for its landmark $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. The combined David Ellison-owned super studio is now called, simply, Skydance, with the merger expected to be finalized on Oct. 6. Paramount film heads Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein are expected to oversee both movie studios. Abdy and De Luca are said to have told associates they have been in talks for a possible next act at Netflix. De Luca and Abdy‘s tenure heading up Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group began in 2022 and has been marked by highs and lows. The highs have included box office successes like the Minecraft Movie ($960 million, globally) and Ryan Coogler’s Sinners ($370 million, globally), along with critical achievements like last year’s Oscars best picture win for Paul Thomas Anderson‘s One Battle After Another and other wins for Sinners . The misfires have included expensive swings like Maggie Gyllenhaal‘s The Bride! and Tom Cruise starrer Digger , which is tracking to open this weekend to a dismal $8 million to $15 million on a $125 million-plus budget. De Luca and Abdy joined Warner Bros. from MGM, where they oversaw that storied studio’s film slate for two years until its 2022 $8.5 billion acquisition by Amazon Prime Video. At Warners, they inherited a slate from the previous regime, headed by Toby Emmerich, that included Legendary’s Dune franchise and the box office hit Barbie , along with Bong Joon Ho‘s Mickey 17 and Robert De Niro starrer The Alto Knights , the latter of which was personally greenlit by Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav. As for their own auspices, the duo is known for being director-friendly, offering a big studio home (and big studio budgets) to filmmakers like Anderson, Coogler, Alejandro Iñárritu and Emerald Fennell. The auteur-driven titles were buffeted by a series of IP plays and franchise offerings, predominantly hailing from the studio’s New Line division, De Luca’s longtime stomping grounds, like the well-received Final Destination reboot and a Conjuring installment. De Luca and Abdy’s exit comes amid a flurry of other executive announcements at the soon-to-be-combined studio. Earlier this week, Cindy Holland exited her post as Paramount Skydance’s streaming chief, with HBO boss Casey Bloys expected to lead all streaming efforts at the combined studios. Also this week, it was announced that Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz would come on as co-CEO with Ellison. Puck first reported the news of De Luca and Abdy‘s exit. THR

articles.title: SCAD Savannah Film Fest: Keanu Reeves, Seth Rogen, Gemma Chan and Jordan Firstman Among Big Names Set for Honors (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Scott Feinberg Plus Icon Scott Feinberg Executive Editor of Awards ScottFeinberg Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 7:11am Gemma Chan, John Cho, Carrie Coon, Rosalind Eleazar, Jordan Firstman, James Gray, Anthony Ippolito, Billie Piper, Keanu Reeves and Seth Rogen Courtesy of Subject (4); Benjo Arwas; Heather Hazzan; Will Aldersley; Macrae Marran; Simon Emmett; Brian Bowen Smith Later this month, a veritable parade of A-list movie stars and filmmakers — many of whom are in serious contention for Oscars — will head south to attend screenings of their work and collect special honors at the 29th edition of the SCAD Savannah Film Festival , the nation’s largest university-run film festival. The Hollywood Reporter can exclusively report that they will include Josephine supporting actress/producer Gemma Chan (Lumiere Award); Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother supporting actor John Cho (Luminary Award); The Liberation lead actress Carrie Coon (Luminary Award); Misty Green lead actress Rosalind Eleazar (Breakthrough Award); Club Kid writer/director/lead actor Jordan Firstman (Rising Star Director Award); Paper Tiger writer/director/producer James Gray (Auteur Award); I Play Rocky lead actor Anthony Ippolito (Breakthrough Award); Backrooms director Kane Parsons (Next Gen Award); Elsinore supporting actress Billie Piper (Marquee Award); and The Invite supporting actor Seth Rogen (Spotlight Award). Related Stories Movies SCAD Savannah Film Fest: Directors of 10 of 2026's Top Documentaries Set for 'Docs to Watch' Panel (Exclusive) Movies Mariska Hargitay Is Still Processing Her Devastating Doc About Her Mother: "It's Like a Psychic Surgery" Additionally, the four principal stars of Peter Berg’s WWII drama The Mosquito Bowl — Tom Francis, Nicholas Galitzine, Ray Nicholson and Bill Skarsgärd — will be presented with the fest’s Ensemble Award. And beloved screen veteran Keanu Reeves will be presented with the Legend of Cinema Award at a screening of The Matrix , and will separately participate in a panel about BRZRKR , a comic book series that he co-wrote, alongside co-writer Matt Kindt and illustrator Ron Garney. The Mosquito Bowl stars Ray Nicholson, Tom Francis, Bill Skarsgård and Nicholas Galitzine They all join several previously announced honorees: VisionQuest lead actor Paul Bettany (Virtuoso Award); The Good Daughter lead actress Meghann Fahy (Spotlight in Television Award); La Bola Negra lead actor/songwriter Guitarricadelafuente (Discovery Award); The Lowdown lead actor Ethan Hawke and creator/executive producer Sterlin Harjo (Outstanding Collaboration in Television Award); A Talent for Murder lead actress Helen Mirren (Legend of Entertainment Award); The Debut lead actress Julianne Moore (Icon Award); Furious lead actress Emmy Rossum (Outstanding Achievement in Television Award); and Dune: Part Three production designer Patrice Vermette (Creative Impact in Production Design Award). Plus, for the 13th year in a row , the fest has invited 10 outstanding documentaries to be screened at the fest and represented by their directors on its ‘Docs to Watch’ panel, which will be moderated by yours truly on Wednesday, Oct. 28: American Doctor (Poh Si Teng), Avedon (Ron Howard), Cookie Queens (Alysa Nahmias), Everest: The Other Side (Jimmy Chin and Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi), The Last First: Winter K2 (Amir Bar-Lev), My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile (Julia Loktev), Once Upon a Time in Harlem (David Greaves), One in a Million (Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes), The Trial of Alec Baldwin (Rory Kennedy) and You Can See Everything (Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim). (Top row, L to R) ‘American Doctor,’ ‘Avedon,’ ‘Cookie Queens,’ ‘Everest: The Other Side’ and ‘The Last First: Winter K2’; (bottom row, l to r) ‘My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile,’ ‘Once Upon a Time in Harlem,’ ‘One in a Million,’ ‘The Trial of Alec Baldwin’ and ‘You Can See Everything.’ Ibrahim Al-Otia/Watermelon Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection; Susan Middleton/Netflix; Roadside Attractions/Courtesy Everett Collection; Jimmy Chin; Apple TV+; Venice Film Festival; Sundance Film Festival (2); Blue Ant; A24 Christina Routhier, the fest’s senior executive director, tells THR , “Every honoree represents a different path into this industry, and we are so excited to welcome these artists to Savannah for their range, expertise, and stories, which are defining this year in film. Our students don’t just watch these artists on screen — they study them. This October, they will sit across from them in an intimate master class, ask the questions they’ve always wanted to ask, and hear firsthand about the choices, challenges and experiences that shaped their careers. This kind of access is at the heart of what makes this festival, and a SCAD education, so distinct.” The 29th SCAD Savannah Film Festival will take place Oct. 24–31. THR

articles.title: ‘A Different World’ Earns Fast Season 2 Renewal at Netflix
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 7:30am From left: Alijah Kai, Maleah Joi Moon and Kennedi Reece in 'A Different World.' Daniel Delgado Jr/Netflix Logo text Netflix ‘s report card on A Different World is a good one: The streamer has renewed the show for a second season. The renewal for the show, a sequel to the 1980s-90s NBC sitcom, was a quick one. Netflix announced the season two order just eight days after A Different World’ s Sept. 24 debut. The second season will follow Deborah (Maleah Joi Moon) and her Hillman College classmates into their sophomore years. “It’s so validating to be bolstered by our amazing audience. We are beyond excited to return to Hillman and continue to tell meaningful and heartfelt stories that resonate across generations,” creator and showrunner Felicia Pride said in a statement. “I am thrilled for our brilliant cast and our hard-working crew.” Related Stories TV Naomi Bulochnikov-Paul to Lead Series Comms at Netflix TV Ted Sarandos Explains Why the 'Stranger Things' Team Left Netflix A Different World collected 4.2 million views and 23 million hours of watch time worldwide in its first four days of release, according to Netflix’s internal data. The series centers on Moon’s Deborah, the youngest child of Whitley Gilbert and Dwayne Wayne (original series stars Jasmine Guy and Kadeem Hardison), as she follows in her parents’ footsteps at Hillman, a historically Black college. “Halleluja! The people and Netflix have spoken,” said director and executive producer Debbie Allen. “ A Different World brought something everybody needed: joy, romance, relevance, authenticity, and heart.” Added Tracey Pakosta, vp comedy series at Netflix, “We are so excited to see how audiences around the world have embraced the next chapter of this beloved series. We believed in this incredible team from day one, and can’t wait to see what unfolds next year at Hillman College.” Pride told The Hollywood Reporter that she grew up with the original series and wanted to “capture and imbue the spirit” of it in the Netflix show. “The feeling that it gave you, which for me, was warmth,” she said. “The feeling of having this community of students and friends and mentors and elders, also the texture and the culture of HBCUs, and then the political consciousness of the show. Those were the sides of the square.” Along with Moon, Guy and Hardison, the show’s cast includes Alijah Kai, Cornell Young IV, Jordan Aaron Hall, Kennedi Reece, Chibuikem Uche and original series actors Cree Summer and Darryl M. Bell. Jada Pinkett Smith, Glynn Turman, Joe Morton, Jenifer Lewis, Karen Malina White, Ajai Sanders and Charnele Brown had guest appearances in season one, reprising their roles from the NBC show. Pride executive produces A Different World with Allen, Tom Werner , Reggie Rock Bythewood , Gina Prince-Bythewood and Mandy Summers. THR

articles.title: How ‘DWTS’ Pro Hailey Bills Is Using Her Nepo Baby Status to Dance Her Way to the Top
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close Hailey Bills Photograph by Aria Askari As one of only five dancers throughout Dancing With the Stars ‘ history to be promoted from troupe to pro after just one season, Hailey Bills has every right to brag. But that’s not Bills’ style, as she’s just grateful to have made the little dancer growing up in Utah who had big dreams proud. “I haven’t really come to terms with where [and] what my life is,” Bills tells The Hollywood Reporter over a recent Zoom from her trailer outside Los Angeles’ Television City, where the show tapes. “When I see people on the streets and they’re saying, ‘Oh my gosh, are you Hailey Bills?’ I’m like, how on earth do you know who I am? It’s so weird.” Related Stories TV 'Big Brother' Reveals Season 28 Winner: See Who Won the Game (and America's Favorite Houseguest) TV The Record-Breaking 'Celebrity Traitors' U.K. Is Back for Season 2: Where to Watch Online From the States Last year, Bills joined the DWTS dance troupe, a group of dancers who perform supplemental, non-competitive numbers and are not paired with celebrities. After season 34 wrapped in November 2025, she headed out on tour in January for five months, performing alongside the pros as if she was one of them. While she didn’t have pro status just yet, there’s no denying she was already catching people’s attention through the screen and on the road. Bills has since amassed a combined million followers across social platforms, proving to be a bona fide reality and social media star. The DWTS producers clearly noticed. Just as Bills was jumping back into the swing of things on tour, she was told “literally minutes before” one of their performances this past spring that she’d be a pro on season 35. That meant after just one season in the troupe, whereas other pros have spent five seasons before being upped, she would take on her first year competing and teaching a star how to perform ballroom dance. Bills was caught by surprise. “People think I’m lying when I say this; I was not expecting it at all. Like, truly, I was not,” she admits. It’s not shocking that some are skeptical of Bills’ honesty — she skyrocketed as a beloved figure in the DWTS community after her troupe tenure, boosted by her presence in the franchise after appearing on the Juniors spinoff in 2018 alongside her aunt, mirrorball champion Jenna Johnson . However, she also questioned her chances at a promotion due to the new franchise entry DWTS: The Next Pro , which confirmed another new dancer would be added for season 35 onto the already long recurring cast list (and Bills wasn’t competing for that spot). “I was on tour this past year with DWTS , and that’s when they were filming The Next Pro . I thought there was just no way [I’d become a pro] with this Next Pro show happening,” she says. “And I was totally fine with that. I was just praying that I would be asked back on troupe.” Once Bills’ pro casting was confirmed by ABC , it was monumental in itself, as she became part of DWTS ‘ second-ever all-female partnership, being coupled with Sarah Jane Nader, the third-ever same-sex pairing. Bills and Nader’s partnership is also a casting wink; Johnson became the first female pro to be partnered with a woman back in 2021 when she danced with Jojo Siwa. There was pressure on Bills’ shoulders heading into the season 35 premiere; it was her pro debut, and the second time two women would perform as a pair on the ABC program. Her season was unfortunately short-lived, as Bills and Nader were eliminated during the second premiere episode, where only the female celebrities performed. She has no hard feelings about her elimination, but wishes she had more time to showcase what she’s really like as a pro. “I think I speak for me and Adele [Zaikman, the Next Pro winner who was also booted during the first premiere night] when I say we wish we would have had more time to showcase [our talents]. But we also understand that there has to be someone to go, and that’s just how it was this season,” she says while chatting with THR nearly two weeks after being eliminated. It was important for Bills to shift her mindset from the disappointment that came with her elimination into gratitude. She admits “it is a hard balance,” juggling wanting to take the competition seriously while also keeping things light. Adele Zaikman and Hailey Bills perform on Dancing With the Stars . Disney/Christopher Willard “It’s so hard, because this is such a life-consuming thing, to do this show. When I got cut, of course that’s a sad thing, and it was a hard night,” Bills says. “We were sad, disappointed, and all the things. But at the end of the day, I am choosing not to let it beat me up, because I still have 10 weeks on the show, and I could choose to be sad about it, or I can choose to just move on, because there truly isn’t anything I can do about it.” Bills has been dancing since her childhood; her parents initially “made sure to put me in all the sports.” Between soccer, flag football, gymnastics and dance, she had her heart set on pursuing either soccer and dance at seven years old. She chose the latter, partly due to her familiar ties to the craft. “A factor that went into that [choice] is my family,” she says. “A lot of my family members are dancers. My aunt [Jenna], my mom, my other aunt.” Bills hails from Utah’s Center Stage Performing Arts Studio, which she jokes is “a big breeder of all these DWTS pros.” She’s not wrong, as a whopping nine former and current Dancing pros trained at the studio (including host Julianne Hough and her brother, judge Derek Hough). Bills was dancing at Center Stage when ABC began casting for Juniors ; she also doesn’t shy away from her aunt playing a part in her being cast. “Of course, I work so hard in dance, but I think a huge factor into me being on the show is my aunt being Jenna Johnson ,” she says. “I have to give her the credit for that.” She’s not the only DWTS pro to reap the benefits of her family tree; fellow pro Rylee Arnold is the younger sister to season 25 winner Lindsay Arnold; Bills’ uncle, Val Chmerkovskiy, was brought in as a pro after his brother Maks joined in season two; and Derek was cast after Julianne won her first year as a pro in season four. “This is a cast of nepo babies,” she says when asked if the interconnectivity of the DWTS pros makes the cast one of nepotism. “I’m proud to say I’m a nepo baby… I think a lot of us are.” Below, Bills opens up about what she learned from her fast first season as a DWTS pro, the advice Mark Ballas gave her that she holds close, her quick rise to acclaim as a dancer and more. You are one of many pros who have connections to other pros from the show. Do you think that makes the cast of Dancing With the Stars a cast of nepotism? Oh my gosh, 1,000 percent. Like, I won’t even try to deny it. No, I’m proud to say I’m a nepo baby. Like, it’s just how it works, and I think a lot of us are, and that’s so lucky for us. I think I’m lucky to be a nepo baby. I’m lucky to have connections, but I don’t want that to downplay the fact that I and other people have worked really, really, really hard to get into this position. 1,000 percent; this is a cast of nepo babies, but I will say we’ve all worked extremely hard. I love that you carry such a good attitude about that. Why is it important for you to embrace it? I think it’s coming to terms with the fact that it’s just true. I don’t know how I would have gotten on the show if my aunt weren’t Jenna. Who knows if I would have? Truly, I don’t know. But I know that that came into place, and I know that because I had a connection with her, I was presented this role a little bit easier than others would. So I’m just gonna accept that. I’m really grateful for that, and I’m lucky. Hailey Bills and Sarah Jane Nader perform on the Dancing With the Stars season 35 premiere. Disney/Eric McCandless Is there anything you’ve learned as your first year as a pro that you want to take into your next season? I genuinely feel like a changed person after this experience. But I think walking in, if I am lucky enough to be a pro next season, I’ll know a lot more. Just starting from the ground up: how that works, patience levels and adapting to your partner’s learning style. Do you have any unique or special hobbies or talents? I wouldn’t even say this is a talent; this is a hobby that I’m trying to be good at. I’ve been trying to get into piano. I’m, like, obsessed with it. I really want to be good at it. So, with all this free time that I’m having [after being eliminated], I might start doing lessons. I also love reading. I am obsessed with reading right now. I love hiking, being outdoors. Sometimes I’ll go rent a bike or a scooter, and just go be free. What does your perfect day off look like? I wake up, sleep in a little bit, of course, and then go get breakfast. Maybe get a croissant or some sort of pastry. Go work out, because I love working out, and then I would dance for a little bit; I would just go sesh it out. Maybe bring someone with me to do that, and then I would go to the pool, be outdoors. Go to dinner with my friends, watch a movie, have a game night, go to bed. What is something you can absolutely not live without? An unserious thing is Diet Coke. I actually can’t function without Diet Coke, so that’s not healthy and not good. Do you have a favorite thing that you have ever stolen from the Dancing With the Stars set? I am obsessed with hoop earrings. I will always have a hoop earring in, and one time when I was on troupe, I had the cutest silver rhinestone earrings, and I decided to keep them on when I went home. Hailey Bills for Dancing With the Stars season 35. Disney/Andrew Eccles What is the best piece of advice you have received that you’ve actually used? It was from Mark Ballas, actually a couple months ago. It’s just really stuck with me, and he said to me, “I want you to remember, it’s not that serious, but it is, also.” It’s a good message to me that when you need to be in it and lock in, absolutely do that and be 100 percent in. But also, if it doesn’t go your way, it’s not the end of the world. It’s just not that serious, and you shouldn’t let that kill you, and you just need to move on. Having found success and fame now after two years on Dancing With the Stars , is it what you expected to be? Have you been able to process it yet? Honestly, I don’t think so. I haven’t really come to terms with where [and] what my life is. It’s been such a switch. I feel like now that I was announced being a pro, and when I see people on the streets and they’re saying, “Oh my gosh, are you Hailey Bills?” I’m like, how on earth do you know who I am? It’s so weird, but it’s been a big switch-up. I think now, finally, I’m like, OK, this is what life is, and this is how we just need to live. I think I’m processing it a little bit, but I’m still in denial in a good way. THR

articles.title: Mary Louise Weller, Actress in ‘Animal House,’ Dies at 79
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 8:15am Mary Louise Weller NBCU Photo Bank/Getty Images Mary Louise Weller, who portrayed Mandy Pepperidge, the Pi House sorority sister and object of future U.S. senator John “Bluto” Blutarsky’s affection in Animal House , has died. She was 79. Weller died Thursday on the day before her birthday after a brief illness, her longtime partner Michael Roy Curtis announced. A former Ford model and longtime spokesperson for Jean Naté fragrance, Weller also played a Southern guest editor at a New York fashion magazine in the Larry Peerce-directed adaptation of Sylvia Plath’s The Bell Jar (1979) and was the love interest of Chuck Norris ’ character in the Hong Kong-set Forced Vengeance (1982). Related Stories Business Martin A. Grove, Longtime Columnist for The Hollywood Reporter, Dies at 83 TV Peppino Mazzullo, Voice of Topo Gigio, the Italian Puppet on 'The Ed Sullivan Show,' Dies at 100 Weller also showed up on such TV shows as Baretta , Kojak , Starsky & Hutch , Supertrain , Vegas , Fantasy Island , CHiPs and, for her final onscreen credit, a 1983 episode of Quincy, M.E. During her brief acting career, “I was the beautiful girl in trouble or the rich guy’s daughter who owns a Porsche and won’t give you the time of day,” she noted in a 1986 interview with the Los Angeles Times . In the box office sensation Animal House (1978), directed by John Landis, Weller sparkled as the snooty Mandy, who’s dating the arrogant Omega House chapter president Gregory Marmalard (James Daughton). Mary Louise Weller with James Daughton in ‘Animal House.’ Courtesy Everett Collection In one scene, John Belushi ’s Bluto of Delta House climbs a ladder to watch Mandy slowly disrobe in her bedroom, and in the film’s “Where are they now?” epilogue , it’s revealed that the two will marry and live in Washington, D.C., with Blutarsky in the Senate. An only child, Weller was born in New York on Oct. 2, 1946, and raised in Westwood since she was about 10. Famed actor Danny Kaye was her godfather; he was a friend of her father, Alex, a doctor. Her mother, Annette, was a homemaker. In one of her first acting jobs, she appeared uncredited in a party scene in Sidney Lumet’s Serpico (1973), starring Al Pacino. The year 1978 was a big one for her. In addition to Animal House , she portrayed a marine biologist in the NBC telefilm Hunters of the Reef and a college student opposite Andrew Prine in the horror movie The Evil . Weller later had a small role in the supernatural fantasy Q (1982), written and directed by Larry Cohen . Weller acted onstage in New York; wrote a play, Four Alone , that was performed at the Greenhouse Theater in Pasadena with a grant from the National Endowment for the Arts; and sought to produce a film based on the life of jockey Mary Bacon before leaving show business. (Weller had trained with the U.S. Equestrian team as a teenager and loved horses; Curtis designs courses for equestrian events.) Survivors include her cousin Sheila Weller, an author who wrote books including the 2003 family memoir Dancing at Ciro’s: A Family’s Love, Loss, and Scandal on the Sunset Strip and 2008’s Girls Like Us: Carole King, Joni Mitchell, Carly Simon — and the Journey of a Generation. Asked in 2012 if she knew Animal House would be a success, Weller replied she “was pretty sure” and added: “I remember showing [the script] to Brandon Stoddard, who was head of ABC at that time. He also knew it would be an enormous hit … but he warned me that it would be the movie I would always be known for.” THR

articles.title: Jesse Jo Stark and Deadly Doll Sign With BMG
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Nicole Fell Plus Icon Nicole Fell Associate Editor nicolemfell Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 8:16am Jesse Jo Stark Pablo Gonzalez Jesse Jo Stark and her label Deadly Doll have signed with BMG, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. Stark’s also taken on new management in Openstage co-founder Sam Jackson and Liza Owen. “Jesse Jo Stark is a distinctive artist with an unmistakable creative vision and a fearless approach to her music . We’re incredibly excited to welcome her to BMG and partner with Deadly Doll,” BMG’s Eve, Recorded Music, West Coast Dan Gill said in a statement about Stark’s signing. Gill adds, “This new album is a powerful reflection of who she is as an artist, and we look forward to helping bring it to audiences around the world.” Related Stories Music Taylor Hanson Signs With WME (Exclusive) Music Macklemore Says Free Palestine Tour "Sold Out Immediately" Last week, the singer announced her upcoming album Muse , which is set to be released on Nov. 6. The album’s first single, “Colorado,” dropped alongside the announcement. The vulnerable track also featured a music video, which was released at the same time. The upcoming album was recorded over three “snow-covered” weeks in Aspen, Colorado, and it has been described as being sonically similar to the Stark’s earlier releases. “It was the time to speak without boundary,” she said in a release about making the album. “Even though I felt broken, I also felt an immense amount of freedom. Each day felt so precious. Like I was dancing with a woman I had been hiding from. I was clear.” Deadly Doll was named after her 2017 single of the same name. It’s also the brand of the singer’s merchandise and clothing line, which has collaborated with several other high profile brands including luxury streetwear brand Chrome Hearts. The brand, which the singer serves as a VP and creative director, was co-created by her father, Richard Stark, and now run by both her father and her mother, Laurie Lynn Stark. THR

articles.title: ‘God of War Laufey’ Sets Release Date, Preorders Open (Gaming News Roundup)
articles.full_text: Oct 2, 2026 6:52am PT ‘God of War Laufey’ Sets Release Date, Preorders Open (Gaming News Roundup) By Mya Copeland , Tanya Fedak PlayStation “ God of War Laufey ” will release Feb. 16, 2027 from PlayStation’s Santa Monica Studios. Pre-orders go live on Sept. 29. The prequel game in the action-adventure franchise centers on Laufey, also known as Faye. “God of War Laufey” follows the legendary warrior beyond death through the Everywhen, the afterlife of the gods. Fans who pre-order the game will receive a special armor set, cosmetic appearance and in-game resource pack. Related Stories Paranormal Comedy 'Don't F — k With Ghosts' Premieres On Demand, Launches Original YouTube Channel (EXCLUSIVE) Amazon Launches Faster Fire TV Stick 4K and Redesigned Remote, Adds Alexa+ Hub to Fire TV Interface The game also features a new weapon for Faye in the Everywhen. The enchanted bow with a shifting serpent form gives players a powerful weapon in close and ranged combat. Popular on Variety See more gaming news from the week in the roundup below. TECH Discord is launching Discord Ads Manager and Video Quests, allowing advertisers to expand their outreach. Available now, Discord Ads Manager is the platform’s first campaign management platform, and its self-serve access enables Discord advertising to reach smaller studios and marketers. It will also offer an auction-based delivery and a dynamic cost model where advertisers can adjust their bids in real time. Full self-serve access is set for early 2027. Video Quests is available through Discord Ads Manager and serves as a rewarded video ad format where players can watch and earn Orbs, receiving their award in roughly 15 seconds. Designed to drive player engagement, Video Quests shows advertisers how long the player chose to watch. RELEASE DATES “Limerence” will launch for PC on Oct. 29. Suffering from personal loss, Claire seeks comfort from an AI relationship app, LiAIson, where she creates a customized partner tailored to her individual needs. But her online relationship soon starts to carry over into her real life, posing the question of where AI should draw the line. Players will determine Claire’s journey, re-evaluating past conversations and shaping her self-perception. “Limerence” is co-developed by Salix Games and Gameinaframe. * Wizards of the Coast announced on Wednesday “Secret Lair: Corn Maze Superdrop,” a new collection of special, limited “Magic: The Gathering” cards arriving on Oct. 12. This superdrop highlights artists, films and more including Jim Henson’s “Labyrinth,” and Netflix’s “KPop Demon Hunters.” There are eight drops: “Secret Lair x Jim Henson’s Labyrinth: Should You Need Us,” “Secret Lair x Jim Henson’s Labyrinth: Fear Me, Love Me,” Secret Lair x Jim Henson’s Labyrinth: Through the Labyrinth,” “Secret Lair x KPop Demon Hunters: How It’s Done,” “Secret Lair x Marvel: Zombies,” “Artist Series: Veronique Meignaud,” “Manufactured Grounds by See Machine” and “Peace, Love, & Treefolk.” All “Secret Lair: Corn Maze Superdrop” drops will be available at 9 a.m. on Oct. 12 in traditional foil edition for $39.99 and non-foil edition for $29.99. PARTNERSHIPS Media company Critical Role and game studio Lichtund announced a publishing partnership for “Rockbeasts,” an upcoming RPG game where players lead a 90s rock-and-roll band to fame. Set to launch in 2027, “Rockbeasts” allows gamers to “book gigs, manage money and fragile egos, keep equipment running, schedule rehearsals and navigate the music industry’s moral minefield, from predatory record labels and jaded venue owners to hard-nosed executives. Every decision shapes the band’s relationships, reputation and future.” Critical Role will serve as the co-publisher, also offering voice actors for the game. NEW VENTURES Entertainment studio Stone Kite launched from “Halo” and “Destiny” creator Jason Jones in collaboration with best-selling author Margaret Stohl. The studio’s first original universe is a near-future story of a global war between humanity and rogue AI-driven robots, “One Zero One.” The first chapter, written by “Arrival’ screenwriter Eric Heisserer, is available now as a free digital comic. Rather than starting with a game, comic or film and then adapting the concept, Stone Kite will bring creators into the process to build the world together. “I’ve spent my career creating books, games, comics, film and television, and I’ve seen how often the medium that tells the first story ends up defining everything that comes after it,” Stohl said in a statement. “Stone Kite is about breaking down those old media silos. Instead of starting in one medium and adapting outward, we bring the best global creators from different disciplines into the room from day one to shape the world together.” Stone Kite’s founding team includes Marvel Comics editor-in-chief Stephen Wacker and veterans of Activision Blizzard, Marvel and DC. The slate boasts more than 250 creators, including Jay Roach (“Austin Powers,” “Meet the Parents), Akela Cooper (“M3GAN”), Stephen Graham Jones, Christian Ward and Kyle Lambert. NEW RELEASES “The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered” has launched on Battle.net. The new version of Geralt’s adventure will feature updated visuals, improved quest tracking and revamped combat, which includes more reactive enemies and smoother movements. Weapon and armor transmogrification as well as new accessibility features are also included. Available on Battle.net , “The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered” is in partnership with CD Projekt Red. TRAILERS “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4” releases Oct. 23, with the PC trailer now available. As announced earlier this year , “Modern Warfare 4” is “Set against a rapidly escalating global conflict centered on the Korean Peninsula, ‘Modern Warfare 4’ pushes the series into darker and more dangerous territory as a full-scale invasion of South Korea threatens to destabilize the world.” Players who digitally pre-order “Modern Warfare 4” can begin preloading on Oct. 15. Campaign Early Access begins Oct. 16. The Infinity Ward-developed game launches Oct. 23 on Xbox Series X and S, PlayStation 5 and PC via Battle.net, Xbox on PC, Steam and Nintendo Switch 2. Watch the PC trailer below. IN-GAME EVENTS “Fortnite” is celebrating this spooky season with Fortnitemares presenting a cursed cast and new characters coming all month from” Five Nights at Freddy’s,” “Hazbin Hotel,” “A Nightmare on Elm Street,” “Beetlejuice,” “Obsession” and more. Players can drop into Freaky Fields or the new Nightmare Neighborhood POI, where Freddy Krueger is waiting. Defeat him to claim Freddy’s Nightmare claws, which let you teleport into range and slash opponents. Reveal enemies with the new Bonerattler SMG and take aim with returning weapons like the Wood Stake Shotgun and Pumpkin Launcher. They can also activate cursed cartridge overrides that grant invisibility while sprinting, boost damage at low health or conceal your squad as Halloween props. The Horde Rush LTM is back, and on Oct. 8 an updated Nitemare Island arrives in reload alongside the “Stranger Things” and Squid Grounds maps. articles.title: IDF Slams ‘NAZA,’ Saying It Presents a ‘Distorted, Misleading and Disingenuous Picture’
articles.full_text: Oct 2, 2026 7:24am PT IDF Slams ‘NAZA,’ Saying It Presents a ‘Distorted, Misleading and Disingenuous Picture’ By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest IDF Slams ‘NAZA,’ Saying It Presents a ‘Distorted, Misleading and Disingenuous Picture’ 1 hour ago ITV Boss, Sky’s Content Chief Set Out Vision for Acquisition, Try to Calm Nerves: ‘The Competition is Ferocious’ 3 days ago Graham Norton Shoots Down ‘Conspiracy Theory’ That Taylor Swift’s ‘Opalite’ Video Was Shot Before She Came on His Show 3 days ago See All Courtesy MK2 The Israeli Defense Forces has slammed the documentary “ NAZA ,” calling it “manipulative,” “misleading” and “based on substantial factual errors.” The film premiered at Venice Film Festival last month, where it received a 24.5-minute standing ovation. It has since screened at the San Sebastián and New York film festivals, and will open in U.S. theaters next week before streaming for free on The Guardian website in late November. The British newspaper are co-producers of the movie, which is directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor. Related Stories Netflix, Amazon and YouTube Form D.C. Lobbying Group Amid Backlash Over Cost of Sports on Streaming Prime 'Big Deal Days' 2026: What to Know About Amazon's October Prime Day Sale In its statement, the IDF said that it did not have a chance to view the documentary prior to its premiere and claimed the directors did not put forward the allegations in the film to the IDF before publishing. The IDF has now responded to the numerous claims in the film, which takes its title from the phrase “collateral damage” in Hebrew (“Nezek Agavi”). Popular on Variety Among other points, the IDF said that it operates under binding directives that “explicitly” distinguish between military operatives and uninvolved citizens; it has never planned or carried out a strike in Gaza in which 500 civilians were killed, as one anonymous contributor claims in the film; and it has never used AI to select targets to strike, saying these are only ever planned by “relevant professionals.” All 24 contributors in “NAZA” are anonymous, filmed against a nighttime skyline in Tel Aviv. In its statement, the IDF said “it is apparent that in various cases interviewees raise speculation and assumptions without a factual basis.” They added that the filmmakers also left out crucial context such as showing the full chain of command, which they said includes roles dedicated to “mitigating civilian harm,” and played down the Oct. 7 attacks on Israel, in which over 1,000 people were killed and over 250 hostages were taken. “The film ‘NAZA’ presents a distorted, misleading and disingenuous picture of the IDF’s target planning and striking process,” the statement reads. “The film’s narrative is based on substantial factual errors stemming from manipulative misrepresentations of reality.” Contacted by Variety for comment, a spokesperson for Guardian News & Media said on behalf of the filmmakers: “The IDF’s attempt to portray the 24 participants in ‘NAZA’ as junior-ranking officers involved only in the early stages of the targeting process is false. They include officers and soldiers who were involved in multiple stages of the targeting process in Gaza, including intelligence, operations and the final authorization process.” The Guardian added that “the process of assessing the credibility of the testimonies was rigorous. It included leaked classified documents, detailed verification of specific strikes and corroboration via a wider pool of confidential journalistic sources who did not appear on camera in the film. Over the past three years we have together interviewed more than 100 sources familiar with IDF systems used in the war in Gaza, including senior-ranking commanders directly involved in the authorization of strikes.” The statement concluded: “The Guardian stands fully behind the film, which builds on three years of detailed reporting by the Guardian and our partners. Several highly respected news organizations have subsequently confirmed the IDF’s use of AI-driven systems in the Gaza offensive and the loosening of safeguards to protect civilians, including the New York Times, Washington Post and Associated Press.” Taylor Swift Song ‘August’ Removed From Trump TikTok Video Taylor Swift Praises Phoebe Bridgers’ New Album ‘Lost Weekend,’ Calls It an ‘Absolute Triumph in Every Way’ Taylor Swift Surprises Emmys in ‘SVU’ Parody but Skips Show to Attend Chiefs Game With Tom Cruise Taylor Swift Sings Mashup of ‘All Too Well,’ ‘I Knew It, I Knew You’ and ‘August’ in Grammy Museum Video Todd Rundgren Slams Taylor Swift, Says She ‘Ruined Music’ and Is ‘the Apotheosis of Mediocrity’ Emmy Producers on Recruiting Taylor Swift, the Ideas She Brought to the Show and How This Year’s Telecast Wound Up Short Loading comments...
