articles.title: Music Industry Moves: Frank Briegmann Gets a Big Up at Universal Music; Warner Mexico Promotes Yusim Aladro to GM
articles.full_text: Oct 2, 2026 8:00am PT Music Industry Moves: Frank Briegmann Gets a Big Up at Universal Music; Warner Mexico Promotes Yusim Aladro to GM By Jem Aswad Plus Icon Jem Aswad Executive Editor, Music jemaswad Latest Venom Frontman Conrad ‘Cronos’ Lant Dies at 63 17 hours ago Grammy Asian Pop Category Will Go Forward, CEO Says: ‘We Understand This Conclusion Will Not Satisfy Everyone’ 23 hours ago Sia Sells 50% of Music Catalog to Pophouse in $180 Million Partnership Deal 1 day ago See All Universal Music Group has promoted Frank Briegmann to Chairman & CEO, Universal Music Europe, Australia, New Zealand, Canada & Deutsche Grammophon. He will continue to report to Lucian Grainge, Chairman & CEO of Universal Music Group. Briegmann will work closely with the leadership in each market, including Olivier Nusse who continues as CEO, Universal Music France; Sean Warner who continues as President & CEO, Universal Music Australia & New Zealand; and Julie Adam who continues as President & CEO, Universal Music Canada. Spain will continue to be led by Luis Fernández, President, Universal Music Spain, and Portugal will continue to be led by Ana Hernandez, Managing Director, Portugal, both reporting to Jesus Lopez. The United Kingdom will continue to be led by Dickon Stainer, Chairman & CEO, U.K., reporting to Grainge. Related Stories Alan Cumming Sheds His 'Traitors' Kilt for 'Tip Toe', a Searing Parable of Homophobic Backlash: TV Review Briegmann joined Universal Music in 2004 as CEO of its German business, becoming the youngest executive ever to lead a major music company in Germany. His responsibilities have since expanded across Central, Northern and Eastern Europe, alongside his global leadership of Deutsche Grammophon. Popular on Variety “Frank and I have worked together for more than 20 years, and he’s a fierce artist champion with a proven track record of building long-term careers, Grainge said. “He combines creative expertise with business acumen and the insights of data and technology. Just as importantly, he respects what makes every market different and knows how to give great local leaders the freedom and support to succeed. Frank’s promotion is all about the power of possibility; making it easier for artists, ideas, and opportunities to travel across borders.” + Warner Music Mexico has promoted Yusim Aladro to the role of General Manager. Aladro, who joined the company at the start of the year, reports to Tomas Rodriguez, President of Warner Music Mexico. According to the announcement, Aladro will spearhead the strategic direction and development of all domestic music within the country, and “drive seamless integration across A&R, creative marketing, and artists’ brand building to accelerate cross-border success for Mexican artists globally, while continuing to expand relationships within the artist, management, and independent label community.” She was previously Director of Marketing and has worked closely with Myke Towers, Elena Rose, Flvckka and Yng Lvcas. Previously, she held senior leadership positions at Rico o Muerto, Downtown Artist & Label Services, Altafonte, Auditorio Nacional México, and Alive Entertainment. “Yusim represents the modern, holistic music executive – combining a deep, intuitive understanding of artist development and creative strategy with sharp commercial acumen,” Rodriguez said. “Her leadership will not only accelerate the growth of our domestic roster but also inspire the next generation of women leaders across the Latin music industry.” + King, Holmes, Paterno & Soriano has promoted Erika Savage to partner. At the firm, Savage represents artists, songwriters, managers and independent music companies across recorded music, live performance, influencer marketing, endorsement agreements and other areas. Her clients have included Pink, Dr. Dre, Tyler, The Creator, Blink-182, Carole King, Sia and Melanie Martinez, as well as independent labels and music companies including Sub Pop, Ghetto Youths International, The Core, Nice Life Records and Victor Victor Worldwide. Before joining the firm, Erika served as SVP of Global Music Operations at United Talent Agency, overseeing operations for its global touring division including leading its Business Affairs team and handling strategic planning. Prior to UTA, Erika spent 19 years at Universal Music Group, including as SVP Strategic Development at Interscope Records, where she led Interscope’s non-record revenue business and developed artist strategies across music, brand partnerships, merchandise and touring. She also negotiated recording agreements and handled Business Affairs matters for a roster that included Lady Gaga, Lana Del Rey and Billie Eilish. Managing Partner Howard King commented: “We are delighted to acknowledge Erika’s hard work and strategic vision in helping the firm provide superb service to our clients.” + Plot Twist Records , the independent record label founded by veteran A&R Executive and media personality Carter Gregory, has formed a joint venture deal with 10K Projects and Atlantic Records . The first signings to the label include singer Alabama Barker and DJ/artist Nic Vans (Nic Vansteenberghe), who gained prominence as the runner-up contestant on the reality TV series “Love Island USA.” The joint venture follows Plot Twist’s independent launch, during which Gregory signed and released Kylie Jenner’s debut single, “Fourth Strike.” Most recently, Gregory served as a VP of A&R at Capitol Records, where he worked closely with such artists as Fletcher, Doechii, Adela, Queen Naija and others. He is also the host of the podcast “The Set List.” “Carter is not only an expert at identifying culturally impactful artists who are moving the needle, but he’s exceptionally talented in creating communities around the music he loves,” said Atlantic Music Group COO Zach Friedman. “We’re thrilled to be working closely with him on his expanding roster of artists at Plot Twist.” + Artist-songwriter-producer Taylor Hanson has signed with WME for worldwide representation in all areas. He was recently a contestant on Season 35 of “Dancing with the Stars” on ABC. The Oklahoma and Los Angeles-based musician is also working on his debut solo album, planned for release in 2027. Hanson rose to fame in 1997 when Hanson, the band he formed with his brothers Isaac and Zac, released their major label debut, “Middle of Nowhere,” featuring the global hit single “MMMBop.” Over the years the group has earned three Grammy nominations. Hanson was also part of the group Tinted Windows with Bun E Carlos (Cheap Trick), James Iha (Smashing Pumpkins) and the late Adam Schlesinger (Fountains of Wayne). + Warner Music Central Europe has announced the appointment of Nici Ochmann as its Head of Culture & Creator Marketing, effective immediately. In the newly created role, Ochmann will shape the company’s culture and creator marketing strategy in GSA by developing artist and creator-led partnerships and campaigns, authentic cross-industry collaborations, and digital-first cultural narratives; she will also build partnerships with domestic and international artists and creators who are in GSA. She is based in the company’s Berlin headquarters. Ochmann moves to WM Central Europe following a 10-year tenure at Adidas, where she most recently served as Global Culture Marketing Cluster Lead for GSA. Niels Walboomers, President of Warner Music Central Europe, says, “Nici brings an invaluable perspective from the lifestyle space, where its culture moves at lightning speed. Her ability to bridge brand narrative with creator dynamics makes her the perfect fit for our vision of the company and will play a vital role in ensuring our artists stay at the bleeding edge of fan connection.” SoundExchange has announced the appointment of Paul Shaver as Senior Vice President, Business Development. He will report to President and Chief Executive Officer Michael Huppe. Shaver joins SoundExchange from the Canadian Musical Reproduction Rights Agency, where he served as President of both CMRRA and SX Works. In his new role, Shaver will spearhead SoundExchange’s efforts to identify strategic growth opportunities, develop innovative partnerships, and expand the organization’s impact across the music ecosystem. He will also help shape SoundExchange’s approach to emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, as the organization evolves to meet the future needs of creators and rights owners. Prior to CMRRA, Shaver held senior leadership positions with Nielsen Entertainment, Universal Music Group, EMI/Capitol Music, and Virgin Records. + “Paul is a respected and forward-thinking executive with experience across many aspects of the music industry,” said Huppe. “He has a proven ability to anticipate change, build innovative solutions, and turn opportunity into growth. As technology reshapes how music is created, distributed, and monetized, Paul’s leadership will help SoundExchange expand its impact and remain at the forefront of the industry’s evolution.” Tuesday, Sept. 29 Universal Music Group has named Libby Bush to the newly created role of President, Global Brands and Commercial Partnerships, starting in November. According to the announcement, she will “lead a new global function that brings together UMG’s brands, media, and commercial partnership businesses, including Universal Music Group for Brands … Spanning digital platforms, physical products and live experiences, these collaborations will be rooted in artists’ originality and authentic connections with fans.” Based in Los Angeles, Bush will report to UMG’s Chief Operating Officer Boyd Muir. She joins from Creative Artists Agency, where she served as Global Head of Entertainment Partnerships and was a member of the Agency Board. Previously, Bush founded Tandem Entertainment, an entertainment partnerships agency acquired by CAA in 2020, and held roles at Marvel Entertainment, ABC Entertainment, the WNBA’s Los Angeles Sparks and the National Basketball Association. Muir said, “As the ways fans experience music evolve, the opportunities for our artists multiply. Bringing our brand, media, and commercial partnerships together under Libby’s leadership will help extend our artists’ reach and grow their revenues, while giving our partners new ways to build relationships with fans and collaborate with the world’s most influential voices. Libby brings exceptional creative and commercial expertise to the world’s leading music company. She’ll work with our talent, teams, and partners to create memorable experiences for fans, lasting value for brands, and new possibilities for artists.” + Avex Inc. has increased its ownership of Brandon Silverstein’s S10 Entertainment , acquiring 85% of the company from Silverstein and his partners. The transaction further integrates S10 into Avex Music Group. Silverstein continues as CEO of S10 and Avex Music Group, a board member and equity partner in Avex Music Group. Terms of the deal were not disclosed. The transaction follows Avex’s March 2025 acquisition of the S10 Music Publishing catalog, which includes shares of hits by Justin Bieber, Drake, Tate McRae, Kehlani, Doja Cat, Post Malone and Rihanna, among others. In the transaction Silverstein was represented by Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP. “S10 is an exceptional management company that is playing a key role in realizing our global ambitions,” said Katsumi Kuroiwa, CEO of Avex Inc. “Bringing S10 into Avex reflects our confidence in Brandon’s leadership and our commitment to growing Avex’s global music business. Together, we will bring the full breadth of Avex’s capabilities to artists and creators around the world.” + Warner Music Group has named Sonny Takhar as Chairman and CEO of Warner Music U.K. & Ireland, effective January 2027. Takhar will oversee creative direction, artist development, and strategic operations across WMG’s recorded music footprint in the U.K., the world’s third-largest music market, and Ireland. Takhar will report to Val Blavatnik, Managing Director of Warner Music North America, U.K. & Corporate Development. Takhar’s remit will also include operational oversight of WMG’s independent distribution arm, ADA, in the U.K. and Ireland, and he’ll work in close partnership with Elliot Grainge, CEO and Chairman of Atlantic Music Group and Chairman of ADA in the U.S., as well as Aaron Bay-Schuck, Chairman and CEO of Warner Records Group. A founding partner of Syco Entertainment, Takhar played a key role in the careers of One Direction, Labrinth, Leona Lewis, Little Mix, James Arthur and Fifth Harmony, alongside the launch of global TV franchises “The X Factor” and “Got Talent.” More recently, Takhar co-founded Los Angeles-based KYN Entertainment in a joint venture with Live Nation, and worked with Westlife and songwriter-producer Steve Mac. Blavatnik said, “Sonny is one of the most visionary executives in music and his track record of discovering, nurturing, and breaking global superstars speaks for itself. His instinct for talent, deep understanding of the wider music ecosystem and strategic global perspective make him the perfect leader to power Warner Music UK & Ireland forward.” + Amra , the global digital collection society, today announced that its Chief Executive Officer, Tomas Ericsson , will transition from his role as CEO after 13 years, effective January 1, 2027. He will assume the role of Chairman of the Board. Robin Davies , Amra’s Chief Operating Officer for the last four years, has been named Chief Executive Officer of the company beginning on January 1st. Ericsson launched Amra in partnership with Kobalt Music Group in 2013, ultimately licensing digital rights directly across more than 200 territories, 45 publishers and growing into nine figures gross by 2026. “We are so grateful for Tomas’ vision and leadership as he and his team have built amra into one of the industry’s most innovative and transformational organizations,” said Laurent Hubert, CEO of Kobalt. “We are also looking forward to Tomas continuing to contribute to the business as Chairman. amra will be in good hands with Tomas’ ongoing guidance and with Robin, who has been with amra and the Kobalt organization for a decade, at the helm.” + Danny Goldberg has promoted Jesse Bauer to the position of Senior Vice-President and Gabriel Barreto to Vice President of Gold Village Entertainment, the New York based artist management company that Goldberg launched in 2007. Bauer has been with the company since its inception; Barreto joined in 2021. Gold Village represents Steve Earle, the Waterboys, and others. + Music Services , a division of SESAC Music Group, has named Nick LaPointe Senior Director of Business Development, and Jay Sudarma Vice President of Marketing for Music Services and CCLI Group. LaPointe joins from FUGA AVS and previously held roles at AdRev and Warner Chappell Music; Sudarm’s new role comes alongside a promotion to Vice President of Marketing at CCLI Group, where he previously served as Director of Marketing. Both appointments are effective immediately. “We’re thrilled to welcome Nick to the team. Throughout his career, he has earned the trust of independent publishers and labels by helping them turn their rights into meaningful revenue,” said Rose Cook, Chief Operating Officer, Music Services. “During his tenure at CCLI, Jay has proven the value of a disciplined, data-driven approach to marketing, and this expanded role is a natural next step,” said Cook. “He will work across brands in the Music Services portfolio, including AudioSalad, Audiam, Music Services Inc., The Harry Fox Agency, HAAWK, and CCLI, bringing a unified voice to a growing collection of brands while preserving the qualities that make each one unique.” + ASCAP President and Chairman of the Board Paul Williams has announced that Jim Selby has been elected as a publisher member to the ASCAP Board of Directors. Jim Selby is President, Global Music Publishing at BMG, leading the company’s worldwide music publishing, and played a key role in its recent merger with Concord. Williams commented: “The ASCAP Board cares deeply about making decisions that are in the best interests of the membership as a whole. As a global publishing leader, Jim has the expertise to tackle the complex issues facing music creators and publishers in today’s market, from both the challenges and opportunities of AI to licensees who want to pay songwriters less. He will be an invaluable voice on the ASCAP Board in our mission to advocate for and protect our more than one million members.” + Universal Music Group has named Òscar Celma as Senior Vice President, Applied AI and Machine Learning, effective immediately. Celma will help lead the development and application of AI and machine learning across UMG’s global operations, supporting UMG’s labels, divisions and businesses. He will report to Hannah Poferl, UMG’s Chief Data Officer. In his previous role at Spotify, Celma helped lead the development of AI-powered personalized listening experiences including AI DJ, Jam and Daylist, as well as personalization and discovery. He also held roles at Conde Nast, Pandora/SiriusXM and BMAT Music Innovators. Poferl said, “Òscar brings a unique blend of quantitative and product experience, deep expertise in AI, and a love of music. He’s built teams that have delivered and knows how to turn data at scale into useful insights. With the breadth and depth of UMG’s data, there’s enormous potential for him to help our teams do more for our artists.” + Chrysalis Records , part of the Reservoir group of companies, and associated artist management & music publishing company Blue Raincoat Music announced that broadcaster-journalist Steve Lamacq has joined the company as Curator, New Music & Talent Development. The newly created consultancy role focused on helping both companies identify, champion and nurture the next generation of breakthrough artists. Working alongside Chrysalis’ and Blue Raincoat’s existing A&R, management and creative teams in a consultancy capacity, Lamacq, a veteran of the BBC and NME, will help discover, champion and develop emerging talent, drawing on more than four decades of experience at the forefront of alternative and independent music culture. Lamacq was appointed an MBE in 2025 for services to broadcasting and to music venues. Jeremy Lascelles, CEO of Chrysalis Records & Blue Raincoat Music said: “Steve has an extraordinary ability to spot great artists early. Time and again he’s identified talent long before the wider industry catches on. When I asked him if he fancied working alongside us in this capacity, I was over the proverbial moon when he agreed. It’s pretty much a dream scenario for us. Alongside his deep knowledge of music, he has built a level of trust with artists and audiences alike, that makes him uniquely qualified for this curating role. I’m thrilled with the association and think we’re going to have a lot of fun.” Taylor Swift’s ‘Patient Zero’ Music Video, Starring Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell, to Debut at VMAs Graham Norton Shoots Down ‘Conspiracy Theory’ That Taylor Swift’s ‘Opalite’ Video Was Shot Before She Came on His Show Country Songs Take All Five Slots in the Billboard Hot 100’s Top 5 for the First Time in Chart History Taylor Swift Premieres ‘Patient Zero’ Music Video at VMAs, Turning Her New ‘Showgirl: Encore’ Single Into a Dramatic Ghost Story Taylor Swift Surprises Emmys in ‘SVU’ Parody but Skips Show to Attend Chiefs Game With Tom Cruise Harry Styles Pokes Fun at Ex Taylor Swift’s Wedding During Madison Square Garden Show Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘Spring Awakening’ Revival Cast, Whitney Leavitt, Mason Alexander Park Among Variety’s 10 Broadway Stars to Watch for 2026
articles.full_text: Oct 2, 2026 8:00am PT ‘Spring Awakening’ Revival Cast, Whitney Leavitt, Mason Alexander Park Among Variety’s 10 Broadway Stars to Watch for 2026 By Haley Kluge , Rebecca Rubin Variety is proud to announce the 2026 edition of its annual 10 Broadway Stars to Watch. These actors, composers, librettists, and playwrights — working on shows including “Purple Rain,” “Warriors,” “Spring Awakening,” “10 Things I Hate About You” and “Wanted” — represent the future of theater. This year’s roster of standouts will be honored at our annual Business of Broadway Breakfast, hosted by Tom Felton, who is currently reprising his signature role, Draco Malfoy, in the play “Harry Potter and the Cursed Child.” At the Oct. 5 event, Variety will celebrate the upcoming season with exclusive conversations with Rachel Zegler, Diego Rodriguez and James Olivas for “Evita,” which opens in spring 2027; Aaron Sorkin, Bradley Whitford, Tom Blyth, Krysta Rodriguez and Michael Arden for “A Few Good Men,” which begins previews on Oct. 8; and Bartlett Sher, Adam Speers and the cast of “Dolly: A True Original Musical,” which launches in January 2027. Here are Variety ‘s 10 Broadway Stars to Watch for the 2026-27 season. Jethro Compton, ‘The Curious Case of Benjamin Button’ Compton likes wearing many hats. After writing the book and lyrics for “The Curious Case of Benjamin Button,” designing the set and directing the show on the West End, he’s bringing it all stateside. The musical — which retains only the core premise of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s short story and departs significantly from the David Fincher film — sets the tale in a Cornish fishing village, with a folk score performed by a cast of actor-musicians as Benjamin ages backwards. Compton’s urge to multitask came out of necessity. He started as a producer working with “exceptionally tight margins.” “I realized the only way I could make the budgets stack up was to hire myself to do as many roles as possible. It also turned out to be a wonderfully efficient way of working, as it drastically reduced the number of meetings I had to attend,” he says. His resourcefulness is clearly working — Compton has been developing the show for seven years, and its West End iteration brought home three Olivier Awards, including for best new musical. “For me, writing and directing are completely different skill sets that require very different ways of thinking. I don’t feel like I’m ever wearing both hats at the same time,” he says. “In the writing room, I’m a writer. In the rehearsal room, I’m the director.” He adds, “I love and loathe them in equal measure!” First West End show “Les Misérables” Most listened to cast album “Come From Away” Theater superstition you believe “It’s bad luck to say, “Good luck,’ on opening night.” Peter Duchan, ‘Purple Rain’ and ‘Practical Magic’ Years ago, Duchan was warned not to expect success as a librettist until he was in his 40s: “I’ve always understood this career as something of an endurance test.” At 43, he’s making his Broadway debut with “Purple Rain,” the stage version of the classic Prince album and film, about the rise of a tormented young musician known as the Kid. Duchan’s big break comes more than a decade after he emerged on the New York theater scene with 2012’s Off Broadway musical “Dogfight,” based on the 1991 movie starring River Phoenix. “We’re trying to honor what’s singular about Prince while crafting a fictional character separate from him,” Duchan says. An adept multitasker (and an expert at translating from screen to stage), Duchan is working on another major musical adaptation, “Practical Magic,” based on the 1998 fantasy comedy starring Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock as witchy sisters. “These are just the two you know about!” Duchan teases. “I spend all day, every day, thinking about musical-theater storytelling. If I haven’t clocked my 10,000 hours yet, I’ve gotta be pretty close.” First Broadway show “Les Misérables” at the Broadway Theatre Go-to Broadway karaoke song “The Feeling We Once Had” from “The Wiz” Show that needs a revival “We haven’t seen ‘The Most Happy Fella’ on Broadway in over 30 years.” Aneesa Folds, ‘Warriors’ It’s hard to typecast Folds. The actress, comedian, writer and improviser has built a career at the intersection of musical theater, hip-hop and comedy. As a high schooler, Folds posted on Tumblr that Freestyle Love Supreme was “everything I’ve ever wanted to do.” Years later, in 2019, she made her Broadway debut with the act. “Freestyle Love Supreme is the thing that taught me that you as yourself is enough,” she says. “You can just be who you are.” Since then, she’s created and performed her own work and starred as Hallie Parker in the “Parent Trap” spoof “Ginger Twinsies.” “I get to do such strange things, and I love it,” she says. “My last thing was playing an 11-year-old white girl.” Now she’s reuniting with frequent collaborator Lin-Manuel Miranda on “Warriors,” his concept album with Eisa Davis that’s headed to Broadway in spring 2027. The musical reimagines the cult film’s gang as women. And for Folds, a Queens native with “music in my blood,” it’s also a celebration of her hometown. “It’s every single genre in the world of New York,” she says. “For anyone seeing it, listening to it, you’re going to relate to something, no matter what.” She adds, “It’s not about fragile, delicate women. It’s about women fighting and standing up for themselves.” As for what’s next? “Theater is in a weird place right now. Let’s just fuck it up.” First Broadway show “The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee” Show that needs a revival “Seussical” Ethan Gruska and Carly Rae Jepsen, ’10 Things I Hate About You’ Image Credit: Courtesy Images More than a decade after Jepsen made her Broadway debut in the 2014 revival of “Rodgers + Hammerstein’s Cinderella,” she’s returning to the New York stage — this time as a songwriter. She and Gruska are composing the music for “10 Things I Hate About You,” a musical by Lena Dunham and Jessica Huang that’s based on the classic 1999 teen rom-com. Jepsen is best known as the Grammy-nominated singer of “Call Me Maybe” and “I Really Like You,” while Gruska is a producer who has worked with Phoebe Bridgers, Fiona Apple, and Bon Iver. They first collaborated on Jepsen’s 2023 album “The Loveliest Time,” and Gruska describes having “immediate chemistry.” For Jepsen, crafting tunes for Broadway requires a “different side of the brain” than writing pop songs. “I find it so challenging in the best way,” she says. “We get to play with humor and all these deep emotions, which is so satisfying.” Knowing how much people love the movie, the duo is striving to handle the material “with care but not trepidation.” With a year until the musical begins previews, Jepsen says, “I’m trying to not get too bogged down by other people’s expectations of the show. I know it’s beloved, but that doesn’t scare me — that excites me.” Adds Gruska: “Making sure we are telling that story, honoring the tone of the movie, and being free to push it forward and be ourselves has been a wonderful and rewarding challenge.” Most listened to cast album “Jesus Christ Superstar” (Jepsen) Go-to Broadway karaoke song “Maria” from “West Side Story” (Gruska); “On the Street Where You Live” from “My Fair Lady” (Jepsen) First Broadway show “Spamalot” (Gruska) Ryo Kamibayashi, Ashlyn Maddox, Tyler Jordan Wesley, Amalia Yoo, ‘Spring Awakening’ Twenty years after “Spring Awakening” launched the careers of Lea Michele and Jonathan Groff, a new generation is getting its turn. Thousands of performers responded to an open casting call before Kamibayashi, Maddox, Jordan Wesley and Yoo emerged as the leads of the Off Broadway revival. “It was like the Hunger Games of New York,” jokes Kamibayashi, who plays Moritz, the troubled schoolboy. “I skipped Jury Duty to go to my first appointment!” says Maddox, who plays the leading naïve Wendela. The foursome came to auditions with varying familiarity with the show and were encouraged to “approach it like it’s a new work,” says Yoo, who plays the free-spirited Ilse. “It hasn’t been done with people who look like us, people with our lived experiences.” For Wesley, who plays the rebellious lead Melchior, that opportunity is personal: “Having been a little Black boy from South Carolina seeing this industry and being like, ‘I want to carve out a piece of this for me’ … to be realizing that with this show is very cool.” None of the four has connected with their predecessors yet, though Wesley is looking forward to meeting Groff. “I know that he’s a Beyoncé lover. I also love Beyoncé, so I think we’ll hit it off there,” he says. And if history repeats itself? Kamibayashi jokes, “Hopefully we all get to book our version of ‘Glee’ after this.” Dream shows or roles on Broadway Bobby in “Company” or George in “Sunday in the Park With George” (Kamibayashi); “Carnival” (Maddox); Judas in “Jesus Christ Superstar” (Jordan Wesley); the Witch in “Into the Woods” or Mary Todd Lincoln in “Oh, Mary!” (Yoo) Liisi LaFontaine, ‘Wanted’ LaFontaine is one-half of the duo at the center of the new musical “Wanted” — a Western about biracial sisters who pass for white and rob their way through 1893 Texas. “Hot — sign me up!” LaFontaine jokes. But it was the “depth and truth” of the story that captivated her. After leading West End productions of “Dreamgirls” and “Moulin Rouge!,” LaFontaine is making her Broadway debut this season at the James Earl Jones Theatre. “I’ve been working towards this moment for the last decade,” she says. “I’m just kicking my feet.” LaFontaine has been developing the role of Martha since the show’s earliest iterations, alongside now co-star and “twin flame” Solea Pfeiffer. Playing the biracial sisters has allowed the pair to unpack questions about their own identities. “It feels like we get to represent ancestors we didn’t know we had,” LaFontaine says. Martha and her sister, Mary, are based on the real-life great-great-aunts of book writer and lyricist Angelica Chéri, giving LaFontaine a “direct line” to their history — and a particular responsibility in bringing Martha to the stage. “I feel an immense pressure to get it right, but I also feel so much freedom knowing people don’t know her yet and I’m the one chosen to introduce her to the world,” she says. “Creating a character is such a gift, but also a very different kind of responsibility.” First Broadway show “I saw my mom play Sarah in ‘Ragtime’ when I was 3 and scream-cried because I thought she got killed onstage.” Show that needs a revival “Aida” Whitney Leavitt, ‘Just in Time’ Leavitt became famous on reality television as the breakout star of “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” and later on “Dancing With the Stars,” but she secretly dreamed of performing on Broadway. Though she grew up as a competitive dancer, she abandoned her acting ambitions to become a stay-at-home mom. Still, she made her Broadway debut last year in “Chicago” as Roxie Hart, and her run broke the box office record for highest weekly sales in the show’s nearly 30-year history. “I walked into the Ambassador Theatre hoping I could do the role, and I left that experience wanting even more,” Leavitt says. She didn’t have to wait long for her next gig. In December, Leavitt is returning to the stage in the Bobby Darin musical “Just in Time” as singer Sandra Dee. “I wanted my next role to challenge me and feel completely different from ‘Chicago,’” says Leavitt. “I’ve experienced people forming opinions about me based on pieces of my life, and Sandra’s story made me think about how important it is to protect the parts of yourself that are yours.” Leavitt’s pivot from reality TV to theater is notable because she’s bringing new audiences to Broadway. “That’s one of my favorite parts of this experience,” she says. “If someone came because they knew me from TikTok, ‘Secret Lives’ or ‘Dancing With the Stars’ and left loving Broadway, that’s a win. Because once you see one, you’re going to want to see them all!” First Broadway show “Hairspray” Go-to Broadway karaoke song “If They Could See Me Now” from “Sweet Charity” Theater superstition you believe “Not wishing someone good luck before they go to stage; I don’t want to hear that!” Show that needs a revival “Guys and Dolls” Nathan Levy, ‘The Fantasticks’ Levy isn’t new to Broadway — he has four shows under his belt — but his fifth feels different. “Just now, with this show and with this role, I’m finally arriving,” he says. “It’s all starting to make sense.” This fall, Levy will originate Lewis in the Broadway debut of “The Fantasticks,” more than 65 years after the musical premiered Off Broadway. The new production reimagines the central romance as a queer love story, turning Luisa — a role traditionally played by a soprano — into Lewis. For Levy, that gender-bend allows him the freedom to explore the character separately from those who’ve come before him. “It’s essentially a new role, so I can just sort of approach it as that,” he says. “It could be super intimidating to go down the rabbit hole and see all the great women, all the great sopranos, that have come before me. But it’s nice and refreshing to know that we’re switching it up.” The change also gives the decades-old love story a new perspective. “It’s really refreshing to see a queer love story these days where the sexuality is not necessarily the struggle or the main conflict,” Levy says. “It just is.” First Broadway show “Newsies,” with “The Fantasticks” choreographer Christopher Gattelli Go-to karaoke song “Bohemian Rhapsody” or something from “Legally Blonde” Show that needs a revival “Bye Bye Birdie” Mason Alexander Park, ‘Much Ado About Nothing’ After lighting up the West End in productions of “Cabaret,” “Oh, Mary!” and “The Tempest,” Park, who’s nonbinary, is making their Broadway debut as Margaret in “Much Ado About Nothing.” “I think London has finally had enough of me,” Park cracks. Director Jamie Lloyd’s revival of Shakespeare’s comedy, starring Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell, drew raves on the West End. During that production, Park learned the importance of taking the work, but not themself, seriously. “We are so fortunate to get to make fools of ourselves amongst talented friends for a living, so might as well enjoy as much of it as possible,” they say. Having acted in two Shakespeare plays, Park is no longer intimidated by the material: “There’s so much room for interpretation and play, might as well take a big swing. The legacy of his work should liberate you rather than scare you.” If Park does get nervous about a project, they remember their favorite piece of advice: “Embrace your singularity. If they wanted someone else, they’d just call them to do it instead.” Most listened to cast album “Hedwig and the Angry Inch” Show they’re most excited to see this season “Evita” Dream show “Kiss of the Spider Woman” Zoe Sarnak and Michael Weiner, ‘Galileo’ Image Credit: Courtesy Image Sarnak and Weiner’s first writing session started like a jam. “She picked up her guitar. I go to the piano. We talk; we sing together, band style,” Weiner says. “It kind of evolves really organically from there, just going back and forth.” The first-time collaborators wrote the music and lyrics for “Galileo,” a musical about the father of modern science. The show marks Sarnak’s Broadway debut and Weiner’s first Broadway musical since 2013’s “First Date.” Their style of collaboration — a “yes, and” approach, as Sarnak describes it — has helped them create a score that gives each character a distinct musical identity. For Galileo, the answer was rock. “He felt like a rock star in his generation — one of those rebellious people who would challenge authority — which is what rock music is all about,” Weiner says. Sarnak has her own connection to the material. The daughter of a scientist, she double majored in molecular biology and music before pursuing songwriting. “I have always felt that math and science minds, they’re artists, they’re dreamers,” she says. “They see the world in this unexpected, outside-of-the-box, expansive way.” First Broadway show “A Chorus Line” at the Shubert Theatre (Weiner); “Guys and Dolls” or “Chicago” (Sarnak) Taylor Swift Announces New Single, ‘Patient Zero,’ Coming This Week There Is Precedent for Taylor Swift’s ‘Cleveland!’ Making the World Go Crazy: Paul McCartney’s ‘Silly Love Songs’ Era Emmys: A Breakdown of the Music Nominees From Lady Gaga’s ‘Dead Dance’ to Hans Zimmer’s Race for His First Win Travis Kelce Breaks Down Wedding to Taylor Swift and Says Adam Sandler Officiating Was ‘Absolutely Insane’: ‘He’s the F—ing Best Person on This Planet’ Country Songs Take All Five Slots in the Billboard Hot 100’s Top 5 for the First Time in Chart History Tom Cruise Says Taylor Swift Was ‘Schooling Me on Football’ at Chiefs Game, Calls Her a ‘Brilliant Musician and Director’ Loading comments...

articles.title: Disney Licenses Slew of Titles to Netflix, Including All Five ‘Ice Age’ Movies, ‘Percy Jackson and the Olympians,’ ‘Felicity,’ ‘Will Trent,’ ‘Elio’ and More (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Oct 2, 2026 8:02am PT Disney Licenses Slew of Titles to Netflix, Including All Five ‘Ice Age’ Movies, ‘Percy Jackson and the Olympians,’ ‘Felicity,’ ‘Will Trent,’ ‘Elio’ and More (EXCLUSIVE) By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest New Name of Paramount-Warner Bros. Unveiled: Skydance 2 hours ago Ynon Kreiz, as Co-CEO of Paramount, to Receive Pay Package Worth More Than $46.5 Million 19 hours ago Kylie Kelce Apologizes to Kate Middleton for ‘Offensive’ Gaffe in How She Referred to British Royal 21 hours ago See All Courtesy of Disney Sure, Disney and Netflix compete for streaming subscribers — but the Mouse House also sees the rival’s massive customer base of over 325 million as a way to monetize and promote its own content, and Netflix is happy to write the checks. Disney Entertainment and Netflix have entered into an expansive new content licensing agreement, which will bring an eclectic mix of library titles and current-season TV shows to Netflix for varying periods of times on a nonexclusive basis. Related Stories Emmys in Talks to Move to Amazon Prime Video Under New Licensing Arrangement, as the Broadcast Wheel Deal Ends (EXCLUSIVE) Prime 'Big Deal Days' 2026: What to Know About Amazon's October Prime Day Sale In some cases, part of Disney’s strategy is to drum up interest in upcoming releases. Disney+ original series “Percy Jackson and the Olympians” Seasons 1-2 will be available on Netflix globally beginning Oct. 4 as part of a three-month promotional window in advance of its Season 3 premiere on Disney+ on Nov. 20. Popular on Variety Similarly, all five of 20th Century Studios’ “Ice Age” films will be available on Netflix worldwide beginning Oct. 4 in a separate three-month promotional window ahead of the franchise’s sixth installment, “Ice Age: Boiling Point,” releasing in theaters on Feb. 5, 2027. The movies are “Ice Age” (2002), “Ice Age: The Meltdown” (2006), “Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs” (2009), “Ice Age: Continental Drift” (2012) and “Ice Age: Collision Course” (2016). Three current series from 20th Television also are coming to Netflix: Crime drama “Will Trent” Seasons 1-4 and sitcom “Shifting Gears” Seasons 1-2 will be available on Netflix globally, while action-drama “Tracker” Seasons 1-3 will be available on Netflix internationally outside the U.S. as part of a multiyear term. “Will Trent” (S1-4) will be on Netflix globally as of Nov. 3, ahead of the Season 5 premiere on ABC in early 2027. “Shifting Gears” (S1-2) is coming to Netflix beginning Dec. 1 in the U.S. and internationally in January, ahead of the Season 3 premiere on ABC on Jan. 7, 2027. “Tracker” (S1-3) will be available on Netflix internationally as of Feb. 26, 2027; Season 4 premieres on CBS on Oct. 4. The deal includes a selection of non-franchised Disney-branded films from Walt Disney Animation Studios and Pixar. Beginning in early 2027, Oscar-winner “Soul,” “Elio,” “Raya and the Last Dragon” and other movies will be will be available to stream on Netflix globally (with title availability and launch dates varying by region). In addition, a selection of library series from Disney Entertainment will be available on Netflix. Those include “Felicity” (available on Netflix in the U.S. Oct. 7, internationally at later dates), “Revenge” (global), “Army Wives” (global), “Fresh Off the Boat” (U.S. and select regions) and “This Is Us” (internationally outside the U.S.; it had been previously licensed to Netflix in 2024-25 in the U.S.). The new batch of Disney-owned TV shows and movies will join other licensed content from the media conglomerate on Netflix, including “Grey’s Anatomy,” “Arrested Development,” “Scandal” and “Black-ish.” From Disney’s perspective, the expanded licensing pact is a win-win: Disney is bringing the collection of titles to a broader audience to boost their visibility (while also generating millions in incremental revenue) and Netflix is adding more content offerings. And Disney is not deviating from its general strategy in which Disney-branded titles remain largely exclusive to its platforms and TV channels. All titles that are currently on Disney+ (including the “Ice Age” movies and “Percy Jackson”) and Hulu will continue to be available. Netflix, in addition to a broad lineup of licensed titles, also spends a bunch of money on originals. Those include animated hit films “KPop Demon Hunters” and “Swapped.” Its upcoming slate of originals includes “Steps” (Nov. 20), “Charlie vs. the Chocolate Factory” and Guillermo del Toro’s “The Buried Giant,” with sequels to “Leo” and “KPop Demon Hunters” in the works. articles.title: Amy Goodman Documentary ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ Acquired by Music Box in North America, Home Entertainment Release Set for Oct. 20 (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Oct 2, 2026 8:10am PT Amy Goodman Documentary ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ Acquired by Music Box in North America, Home Entertainment Release Set for Oct. 20 (EXCLUSIVE) By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest AGC Studios Launches AGC Digital, a Division Focused on Nurturing Creator-Led Intellectual Property 1 day ago Thessaloniki’s Agora Crossroads Co-production Forum to Feature 14 Projects From 15 Countries 1 day ago Woody Allen’s New Movie to Star Marton Csokas, Jemima Kirke and More as WestEnd Boards Sales 1 day ago See All Courtesy of Music Box Films Music Box Films has acquired North American rights for documentary “ Steal This Story, Please! ,” and will release the film on all major digital platforms on Oct 20. The film, initially self-distributed by the filmmakers, had a successful theatrical release across the U.S. in the spring, grossing close to $1 million. “Steal This Story, Please!,” which focuses on the work of trailblazing independent journalist Amy Goodman , is directed by Academy Award nominees Carl Deal and Tia Lessin. Popular on Variety Related Stories Alan Cumming Sheds His 'Traitors' Kilt for 'Tip Toe', a Searing Parable of Homophobic Backlash: TV Review Music Box will also release the film on DVD and Blu-ray with the physical media release date to be announced. It will have a live online screening on Oct. 13 at 8 p.m. ET, followed by a live Q&A talkback with Goodman, alongside Lessin and Deal (“Trouble the Water,” “Citizen Koch,” “The Janes”). Premiering at the 2025 Telluride Film Festival, “Steal This Story, Please!” went on to win audience awards at 11 festivals — including Mill Valley, Palm Springs, Santa Barbara and Woodstock. The film, which had theatrical booking support from Michael Tuckman’s mTuckman Media, opened on a single screen in New York at the IFC Center in April, grossed over $30,000 opening weekend and was held over for 12 weeks. Expanding nationally, the documentary screened in more than 50 markets and was one of the best performing non-fiction releases of this year. Music Box has acquired the film for theatrical and home entertainment rights, taking over theatrical bookings moving forward. In a statement, the distributor said that Goodman “has reported some of the most urgent and underreported stories of our time on her daily global newshour Democracy Now!. Drawing on an extraordinary archive, filmmakers Carl Deal and Tia Lessin take us behind the scenes with the warm, wisecracking granddaughter of an Orthodox rabbi — raised in a tradition of asking hard questions — as she navigates a media landscape reshaped by technology, corporate consolidation, and political assaults on the press.” It added, “Urgent, provocative and unexpectedly funny, ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ explores what’s at stake when journalism is threatened, and why the act of bearing witness has never mattered more.” Deal said, “We are thrilled that ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ will be part of the Music Box family of high-quality independent films, and that Amy’s story will get to home audiences far and wide at a moment when free expression is in the crosshairs of the President of the United States.” Lessin added, “Long before attacks on the press became a defining feature of our political life, Amy Goodman understood that democracy depends on independent, uncompromised journalism that doesn’t bow to power. We are excited to join forces with Music Box Films to build on the theatrical success of the film and ensure that it reaches home audiences in the same spirit of editorial freedom and direct engagement that has defined Amy’s work, as well as our own.” “ ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ had the highest-grossing week of any documentary in the history of the Music Box Theatre in Chicago,” said Music Box Films. “We are thrilled to continue our relationship with Amy, Carl and Tia, in expanding the audience reach of this powerful documentary.” “In a marketplace where industry leaders continually harp on about the limited theatrical prospects for documentaries – especially those of a political nature – the unabashed success of ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ proves that audiences are still wanting to be moved and entertained,” said Tuckman. “Grossing close to a million, the release is a testament to Carl and Tia’s belief that theaters are still the best place for documentaries to engage and inspire audiences.” “Steal This Story, Please!” is executive produced by Jane Fonda, Rosario Dawson, Tom Morello, Sheila Nevins, Julie Cohen, Tony Tabatznik, Bill Haney, Jonathan Logan and Steve Silberstein, produced by Deal and Lessin, with producers Karen Ranucci, Diana Cohn and Caren Spruch. The sale of the home entertainment rights was negotiated by Brian Andreotti on behalf of Music Box Films and Ben Schwartz and Joe Tufano at Submarine. articles.title: How Elizabeth Holmes Was Secretly Filmed for ‘You Can See Everything’ Doc: 7-Person Crew, 16-Hour Shoots and Cameras Covering the ‘Whole House’
articles.full_text: Oct 2, 2026 8:10am PT How Elizabeth Holmes Was Secretly Filmed for ‘You Can See Everything’ Doc: 7-Person Crew, 16-Hour Shoots and Cameras Covering the ‘Whole House’ By Jordan Moreau Plus Icon Jordan Moreau Latest Nathan Fielder Speaks Out on Living With Elizabeth Holmes While Filming ‘You Can See Everything’ Doc: ‘She Seems So Genuine’ but ‘I Know She’s a Liar’ 1 day ago Ex-‘American Idol’ Contestant Caleb Flynn Found Guilty of Murdering Wife 3 days ago Elizabeth Holmes Posts Cryptic Message From Prison Ahead of ‘You Can See Everything’ Release: ‘I Was Silenced for a Long Time’ 4 days ago See All Courtesy of A24 Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim shocked Hollywood and the world when they revealed they’d secretly been filming Elizabeth Holmes ahead of her 11-year prison sentence for their documentary, “ You Can See Everything .” The film had a surprise premiere at the Telluride Film Festival last month and had another early screening at the New York Film Festival on Wednesday, where the co-directors peeled the curtain back on how they pulled off the shoot. Holmes and her partner Billy Evans invited Fielder, Oppenheim and a small camera crew into their San Diego home 34 days before Holmes began her Theranos fraud prison sentence. Fielder, who makes his feature directorial debut with the film, is known for blending bizarre, real subjects with absurd, scripted comedy on his shows “Nathan for You” and “The Rehearsal.” But he had planned to stay behind the camera when he and Oppenheim embarked on “You Can See Everything.” Popular on Variety Related Stories Paranormal Comedy 'Don't F — k With Ghosts' Premieres On Demand, Launches Original YouTube Channel (EXCLUSIVE) Prime 'Big Deal Days' 2026: What to Know About Amazon's October Prime Day Sale “I was like, ‘I’m definitely not going to be in this when we started,’” Fielder said. “I was behind the camera with Lance, and it was strange. [Holmes and Evans] would keep talking to me or asking me questions, and I would answer from off-camera. But then eventually, the operators would start panning over to me because the conversations would be long.” “You became this accidental investigator of everyday moments,” Oppenheim added. “I feel like that also came about too because the way we were shooting it initially was with one camera and anamorphic lenses, and it was extremely cumbersome. It was the wrong approach for this. Every time we would miss a moment or try to change a lens, that would be when they would also be engaging Nathan off-camera. So eventually, probably about a day of getting it fully wrong, we decided essentially to completely change the way both of us work.” Fielder and Oppenheim both brought crew members from their past projects, including cinematographer David Bolen, who worked on Oppenheim’s recent film “Primetime” and his docs “Spermworld” and “Some Kind of Heaven.” “It basically made us work in this completely new way, which oddly and ironically, is as close to the tenets of documentary filming, which is just fly-on-the-wall, vérité filmmaking,” Oppenheim said. “So we had three cameras, two operators, one would be sometimes on Elizabeth or Billy, one would be on Nathan, and we basically pick zones of the house and have these extremely long zoom lenses. Then I would be hidden behind the wide camera. We were trying to do that in an effort to try and take all the pressure away from any moment. We would be shooting like 16 hours a day, so they wouldn’t really know what we were interested in necessarily.” “We didn’t always know either,” Fielder joked. “We started setting up the cameras where we had a wide lens that would cover the whole house, so if something happened, we wouldn’t miss it. The other two 25mm to 250mm lenses could be wide, but then also zoom, so we could basically capture everything.” Fielder revealed that the crew was comprised of just seven people, and only four of them would be inside Holmes’ house at any time. He also shouted out Bolen, who “found a way to make shots look beautiful in the day or the night.” “As long as there was a light, we could make it work,” Fielder said. “If we were live and then something interesting started happening, [Bolen] could pick up the camera and tripod, move to a new spot, re-lock the head in 10 seconds. It looks amazing, and it’s a testament to the team who put this together. It was down to this whole dance we had, and it was just amazing and one of the best experiences I think we’ve had making something because of that exploratory freedom and being able to let our curiosity drive us.” Oppenheim and Bolen collaborated on “Primetime,” starring Robert Pattinson as “To Catch a Predator” host Chris Hansen. The film was shot in a boxy 4:3 aspect ratio to mimic the retro, reality TV look of “To Catch a Predator” from the 2000s. Oppenheim used the same format on “You Can See Everything” to get close-up, reaction shots from Holmes, Evans and Fielder. “One thing we realized with the one camera that’s panning is that the moment you say something to someone, you want to see their face the moment they hear it,” Fielder said. “Especially in a movie like this, where you’re trying to evaluate if someone’s being honest or not, when you have to swing, you’re missing a few seconds.” Oppenheim added, “The aspect ratio of the movie came about because we’re confined largely in one space, and there was so much. Every time we put the camera somewhere, when we originally were in a larger aspect ratio, it felt like you were seeing so many details that were distracting you from the human face. The face is the ultimate landscape. articles.title: Ynon Kreiz, Newly Minted Co-CEO Of Paramount, To Get Pay Bump After WBD Merger Close, $31.5M…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes , Jill Goldsmith October 1, 2026 2:27pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc Ynon Kreiz, who will be co-CEO of the combined Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images Ynon Kreiz , who was tapped Wednesday as Co-CEO of the soon-to-merge Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, will collect a $31.5 million signing bonus and at least $35.1 million a year in total compensation by 2027. In an SEC filing Thursday, Paramount laid out terms of the former Mattel CEO’s 5-year contract and said its board of directors approved the appointment of Kreiz on Sunday. His exit from Mattel was announced Wednesday morning, with Paramount revealing his new post later in the day. After a lengthy legal challenge by 12 state attorneys general and the Writers Guild of America put it in limbo for two months, the $110 billion merger is slated to close on Tuesday. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Executives Ynon Kreiz Anointed Co-CEO Of New Paramount-WBD; David Ellison Says Mega-Studio Is “Transformational Moment For Our Industry” News Paramount-WBD Merger Is A Go As Judge Approves Legal Settlement, Last Hurdle To Close Kreiz will receive a signing bonus in the form of restricted stock units [RSUs] worth $31.5 million. Beyond the signing bonus, the filing lays out two sets of figures – one covering the brief pre-merger period and then another reflecting the time after the completion of the deal. The official first day of Kreiz’s employment contract is Monday, October 5, meaning he will have had time to put a few office supplies in desk drawers and visit the commissary before the elevated figures take effect. Kreiz, 61, will be paid an annual base salary of $3.5 million, rising to $5 million the day after the merger closes. His annual bonus targeted at $1.5 million will increase to $4.9 million. He will be eligible for 2.6 million shares of Class B stock along with another stock award of 1.25 million shares. Within 15 days after the merger close, he will be granted RSUs worth up to $5.1 million, prorated based on the part of the first year of employment following the merger close. Starting on October 5, 2027, the first anniversary of the start of the contract, Kreiz will be granted annual equity awards worth $20.1 million. While there are a number of variables, as is always the case with executive compensation, the upshot of the new figures is that Kreiz will be at the high end or above the range of his recent pay at Mattel. In 2023, he took home $18.9 million for running the toymaker, with the tally jumping to $37.8 million in 2024 and then declining to $15.1 million last year. The filing said Kreiz, who led Endemol Group, Maker Studios and Fox Kids Europe before joining David Ellison as Co-CEO, has “extensive leadership experience in the media and entertainment industry.” That background merited his appointment to the company’s board of directors along with the exec position, the board said. articles.title: International Insider: Merger Approved!; RTS London’s AI Buzz; Deadline @ Zurich
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max International Insider: Merger Approved!; RTS London’s AI Buzz; Deadline @ Zurich ‘Celebrity Traitors’ Returns With Biggest Ever Launch Ep Of Nearly 9 Million Viewers BBC Gives First Look At ‘The Last Detectives’ Crime Drama From Matthew Barry, Nicola Shindler View All October 2, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Paramount-Warner Bros. is set to close Getty Images Welcome, welcome Insiders. Max Goldbart here taking you through a week in which one of the biggest entertainment deals of this century was waved through. Read on. And sign up here . Merger Approved! Getty Images C-suite winners and losers: In the end it all happened quite quickly. Several weeks back it appeared that David Ellison might feel the full force of regulators in the UK and Europe, not to mention dozens of U.S. state AGs. Fast-forward to Wednesday and the $110B Paramount -WBD mega-merger was officially waved through and the new company will officially launch on Tuesday (October 6). Thoughts moved at lightning speed to the C-suite winners and losers, and we didn’t have to wait long for the departure of Cindy Holland, who it is heavily presumed will be replaced by HBO boss Casey Bloys as chief of streaming across both behemoths. In her email to staff, Holland hinted at Ellison “optimizing for HBO stability,” clearly a somewhat barbed nod to her successor. HBO was talking up its Spanish originals at Iberseries in Madrid this week and all eyes will now be on how much Bloys looks to expand the joint operation’s streaming strategy outside of the U.S., with internationals boss Sarah Aubrey expected to remain by his side. Nellie Andreeva’s deep dive can be found here . One name that wasn’t expected to pop up this week was Ynon Kreiz, the Israeli-born former Endemol Group boss who exited Mattel, and was then swiftly named co-CEO of Par-Warner, sharing top-dog duties with Ellison. Kreiz brings weighty international experience to the new entity, and was for a couple hours rumored to be taking up a big international job before being named co-chief. The long-serving Gerhard Zeiler still holds the international keys at Warner with Kevin MacLellan in an equivalent post at Par. Thoughts now turn to the outposts of both of these big beasts, where there is surely much rejigging and “optimizing” to come. Related Stories Executives Paramount-WBD Deal Architect Gerry Cardinale Says Most Of $6B In Expected Cost Savings Will Not Be Layoffs Executives David Ellison's "Coziness" With Donald Trump Is "Way Overstated", Per Paramount Backer Gerry Cardinale AI Chatter @ RTS London Watch on Deadline BBC Studios Generating headlines: Just a day before the merger completed, Reemah Sakaan, the boss of Paramount UK network 5, was facing tricky questions across the pond over political interference from her new overlords, but she batted them away with aplomb. This was at the RTS London Convention, where the great and good of the Brit TV industry gathered for a day jam-packed with news lines. With hundreds being laid off across the BBC and Channel 4, a new content chief set to be imminently announced at the latter, and the mergers at Sky-ITV and Banijay-All3Media taking hold, there was plenty to address. In the end, it was AI that once again generated headlines. Prime Video international boss Kelly Day laid down the gauntlet with a full-throated backing of AI first up, as she said the tech is “not a threat to creativity,” but is “creativity unleashed.” Not to be out-headlined, BBC DG Matt Brittin then raised eyebrows when he out-the-blue admitted he’d been sent a fully AI-generated episode of Doctor Who. “Pretty good,” was his verdict, leading BBC commissioners in the crowd to choke on their morning coffee. The reality is that the tech is here to stay and the peeps in charge clearly want to be realistic about its benefits… Creatives may take a little while to join them. Steven Knight, who is vehemently anti-AI, spoke a few hours after Brittin. However, all the crowd really wanted to know from the Peaky Blinders creator was the identity of the next 007, given that Knight is writing the Amazon MGM movie (Amazon was also sponsoring the RTS event). In the end, the crowd waited and waited, before all they got was a firm “no” to the question of whether writing the movie about the most famous spy on earth is giving him sleepless nights. Knight was neither shaken, nor stirred. All our RTS coverage can be found here . The Insider Interview: Academy Boss Bill Kramer @ Zurich Photo courtesy of Violeta Sofia Our Deadline Studio in Zurich was replete with big stars and industry names over the past week (for Martin Moszkowicz, Romain Bessi and more click here ), so it was difficult to boil the Insider Interview down to one. In the end we opted for a fascinating sit-down with Academy chief Bill Kramer, Mattel Studios’ Robbie Brenner and Sony Pictures Classics’ Michael Barker. The trio, unsurprisingly, wanted to chat about Obsession and Backrooms, the year’s big hits that look set to usher in a wave of YouTube creatives to mainstream film. For Kramer, their breakout success speaks to “the importance of fandom,” no matter where it comes from. >>> Watch the Interview Global Breakout Big Band Story, TF1 The French TV industry has its challenges at present, but Cat’s Eyes stands out. TF1’s series is about to launch Season 2 and is based on a cult 1980s Tokyo-set manga. The first season was a ratings hit airing on Hulu in the U.S. We checked out what the growing international buzz is all about. >>> Read The Breakout The Essentials Anthony Avellano for Deadline/Sarah Dunn/Getty/Stefan Kokovic/Getty 🌶️ Hot One : Nicolas Cage, Michael Sheen, Jordi Mollà, Emilio Sakraya and Adrian Topol are starring in C.L.A.Y. , a psychological cyber-thriller from Simon Afram. 🌶️ Another : Cast has been confirmed for Woody Allen’s next movie including Marton Csokas and Jemima Kirke. 🥇 Team unveiled: Banijay set out its new sales team under Cathy Payne, with Rachel Job nabbing a top job and a number of long-serving execs exiting. 📆 Premiere date: Indian rural horror Kaali Keti will be given a theatrical release on October 23. 🚪 Closing down: True Brit Entertainment, UK seller of The Death of Robin Hood, has filed for bankruptcy . 🏆 Awards latest: The European Film Academy has named Beki Probst, Marin Karmitz and Sandra den Hamer as the first recipients of its new Community Award. ⛺ Fest latest: Stewart was at Iberseries in Madrid, where co-pros , YA and the Banijay-All3 merger were in the spotlight. ⏱️ To the Tardis: Multiple BBC Studios labels will likely apply to be the next producer of Doctor Who . 🍿 Box office: KPop Demon Hunters 2 is targeting a “very broad theatrical release,” per Ted Sarandos. 🖼️ First look: At the third season of hit African drama series Shaka iLembe before its MIPCOM debut. International Insider was written by Max Goldbart and edited by Jesse Whittock. articles.title: U.S. Job Growth Slowed To 29,000 In September, With Slight Dip In Movie And Music Employment
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Fox News Tops September And Q3 Ratings; MS NOW Sees Gains, CNN Shows Uptick In Some Categories Warner Bros Fires Off Cease And Desist Over Fox Nation’s ‘The Vow,’ But Network Rejects Claim New Series Infringes On ‘The Bachelor’ Fox Business To Debut ‘Big Money In The Morning’ To Replace Maria Bartiromo’s Show View All October 2, 2026 5:46am Add us as a Google Preferred Source U.S. Department of Labor building in Washington, D.C. Robert Knopes/Education Images/Universal Images Group via Getty Images U.S. job growth slowed in September to 29,000, while unemployment ticked up to 4.2%. Overall, the employment situation was largely unchanged during the month, amid continued concerns over rising prices. Employment in movies and music dipped slightly, shedding about 200 jobs to 328,500. Employment among broadcasting and content providers fell by 3,000, to 328,100. Industry lobbyists have pointed to job losses in movie and TV production as they press for passage of a 20% federal incentive, with hopes that Congress will take up a bill during the lame duck session. Related Stories News Aaron Sorkin Clarifies He "Was Never Asked" To Omit Trump From 'The Social Reckoning' But Film Is "Not A Red-Blue Thing" News Fox News Tops September And Q3 Ratings; MS NOW Sees Gains, CNN Shows Uptick In Some Categories The figures from the Bureau of Labor Statistics are the final monthly release before the midterm elections on Nov. 3. Watch on Deadline The Bureau of Labor Statistics also revised previous months’ figures, as is typical. The figures for July were changed downward by 31,000, showing a loss of 10,000 jobs. August’s job numbers, which were surprisingly robust, were revised down by 29,000 jobs, to 133,000. The biggest gains were in health care, adding 17,000 jobs, while there was a slight growth in construction and manufacturing jobs. The average hourly earnings rose by 5 cents, or 0.1%, to $37.81. Over the past 12 months, average hourly earnings have risen by 3%. Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal, called the report “mediocre.” She wrote on X, “The biggest sore spot = wage growth of 3% in past year. articles.title: ‘Night Of The Living Dead’ Vertical Microdrama Readied For Horror-Focused App Room418
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Prime Video’s ‘Bloodaxe’ Adds Maddy Ambus, Steven Brand & Lasse Steen To Cast Disney+ & Indonesia’s Vidio Launch Subscription Bundle ‘Shaka iLembe’: First Look At Season 3 Of MIPCOM-Bound African Zulu King Drama View All October 2, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Dylen Postnikoff is a co-founder and CEO of Room418; the original 'Night of the Living Dead' Courtesy/Everett Collection EXCLUSIVE: A newly-established microdrama business geared towards horror is adapting genre classic Night of the Living Dead ahead of its full launch. L.A.-based Room418 is positioning itself as a studio and platform that puts “vertical-first originals at the center of a dedicated destination for horror fans, alongside curated programming in vertical, horizontal and mixed formats.” A slate of acquired shows will launch the vertical video app, with original productions following. Related Stories News Vertical Video Economy Worth $150B, Even Without China – Owl & Co Report News Vertical Video Studio LoveHit Launches With Adaptations Of Literary Classics Starring Microdrama Regulars & Eric Roberts Former Blink49 Studios, CBC and Shaftesbury exec Dylen Postnikoff is leading Room418 as co-founder and CEO. Postnikoff, a comms and marketing specialist who helped shape the international profiles of Schitt’s Creek and Anne With an E , has been working at Wild Cards maker Blink49 since June last year . With horror from emerging creators already one of the stories of the year in film and TV through the successes of Curry Barker’s Obsession and Kane Parsons’ Backrooms , Room418 is looking to tap into the zeitgeist. As such, it is planning on working with creatives who’ve found success on Wattpad and digital platforms. Watch on Deadline An invite-only beta version of the Room418 app will launch this fall ahead of a commercial launch, featuring a slate of licensed horror content. Ten original and adapted projects have been optioned and are in development as well. Notably on the development slate is a vertical reimagining of George A. Romero’s 1968 horror classic Night of the Living Dead . The film has been in the public domain since its original release due to an error by its original distributor. The news comes hours after Deadline revealed filming has wrapped on Twilight of the Dead , a horror pic considered the “final chapter” of the late Romero’s zombie saga. Also on the slate is a screen adaptation of Ben Sobieck’s When the Black-Eyed Children Knock , which was popular on Wattpad. Room418 and Slash Management are also co-producing an original project with digital horror creator Monse Gutierrez, whose social handle is @CVNELA. The company is also collaborating with L.A.-based REELi Studios on an original horror series inspired by Filipino folklore, with production planned in the Philippines. “What makes horror so interesting globally is that fear is universal, but the mythology is local,” said Postnikoff. “Every market has its own stories, folklore and voices, and horror audiences are unusually willing to cross borders to discover them. At the same time, mobile has changed where discovery actually happens. We’re building Room418 to connect a global genre audience with a new generation of creators and stories designed for the way people are watching now.” The Room418 team see horror as particularly well-suited to the growing microdrama market, with cliffhangers and fan culture making aligning the genre with vertical video’s quick-hit format. “Vertical changes more than the frame,” said Postnikoff. “It changes the rhythm of the storytelling, how quickly you establish a world, where you build tension and how you earn the next episode. What excites us is what that unlocks. “A microseries can be a complete entertainment experience in its own right, but it can also introduce a filmmaker, prove an audience for an idea and become the first expression of IP that grows into film, television and beyond.” Postnikoff has worked in entertainment and media for more than 15 years, leading on brand and franchise strategy for the likes of Murdoch Mysteries and Kim’s Convenience . She’s hoping to apply her expertize in studio positioning, corp comms and audience growth to Room418’s mission to create a horror-first destination for genre fans. Room418 is working with technology firm KINO Studios on the app’s product and technical infrastructure. Members of KINO’s founding team previously were executive producers on A24’s Undertone , which premiered at the Sundance Film Festival. Should Room418 originals be successful, the company is eyeing expansions into film, television, adaptations and experiences. The invite-only beta of the Room418 app will launch later this fall ahead of the company’s commercial rollout.
