articles.title: Paramount-WBD Will Now Be Called Skydance, David Ellison Reveals
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Paramount-WBD Deal Architect Gerry Cardinale Says Most Of $6B In Expected Cost Savings Will Not Be From Layoffs David Ellison’s “Coziness” With Donald Trump Is “Way Overstated”, Per Paramount Backer Gerry Cardinale Starz Goes Dark On Verizon FiOS Amid Carriage Dispute; Verizon Responds View All October 2, 2026 6:27am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc After the expected close of their merger, Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery will together be known as Skydance . CEO David Ellison revealed the new name Friday in a post on X . The $110 billion merger is projected to be finalized on Tuesday after a year-long pursuit by Ellison and a two-month delay caused by antitrust lawsuits by 12 states and the Writers Guild of America. Related Stories News Paramount-WBD Merger Is A Go As Judge Approves Legal Settlement, Last Hurdle To Close Executives Ynon Kreiz Anointed Co-CEO Of New Paramount-WBD; David Ellison Says Mega-Studio Is “Transformational Moment For Our Industry” “What once was the peak, is now just the beginning,” Ellison wrote. “Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren’t rewriting history – we’re equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for bold, quality storytelling.” The choice of the name, he said, stemmed from several objectives. One is to preserve the history of Paramount and Warner Bros. as individual entities under the Skydance umbrella. “We never wanted a new corporate identity to diminish, alter or overshadow either one. Instead, we wanted a name that would give the combined company an identity of its own while allowing Paramount and Warner Bros. – and all our extraordinary brands – to remain in the spotlight.” Watch on Deadline When Skydance acquired Paramount in August 2025, the company wanted to take advantage of Paramount’s familiar consumer brand while also emphasizing Skydance as the corporate parent. That meant the official name was “Paramount, a Skydance Corporation,” which was later streamlined to “Paramount Skydance Corporation.” Before the two large media companies combined, the new entity also faced the legal obstacle of an antitrust lawsuit by 12 state attorneys general and the Writers Guild of America, which labeled it an illegal monopoly. The settlement of the lawsuits, laid out in a 5-year consent decree, requires separation of the Paramount and WBD operations in several business areas. It also tries to guard against one of the major studios being dissolved, as has been the fear of merger opponents. Those precautions meant that a name appearing to favor one merger partner over the other would also be a potential problem. In the absence of any official guidance on the name, colloquial handles like “WarnaMount” or “ParaBros” became commonplace. One stark reality of the new identity is that Discovery Communications, which went public in 2008, two decades after the Discovery Channel lit up as a cable network, will now no longer have its name in lights. What once was the peak, is now just the beginning. Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren't rewriting history — we're equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for… pic.twitter.com/uInLRY3IrE — David Ellison (@ellisonskydance) October 2, 2026 Paramount-Warner Bros Will Be Called Skydance, David Ellison Reveals Par-WBD Film Shakeup: Greenstein & Goldberg Poised To Run; De Luca, Abdy Likely Out ‘Verity’ To Seduce $55M+ Global Bow As ‘Digger’ Impacts Theaters ‘Celebrity Traitors’ Returns To BBC With Biggest-Ever Launch Episode More from this Story Arc Paramount WB October 2, 2026 Josh Greenstein & Dana Goldberg Poised To Run Combined Paramount Warner Bros Film Unit, Setting Up Likely Michael De Luca & Pamela Abdy Exit October 1, 2026 Ynon Kreiz, Newly Minted Co-CEO Of Paramount, To Get Pay Bump After WBD Merger Close, $31.5M Signing Bonus View All Story Arc Read More About: 17 Comments

articles.title: Canal+ Calls VAT Hike “A Direct Attack” On Its Operations In France As Guilds Protest Move
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie CANEX Creations CEO Osahon Akpata Talks Mission To Shake Up Film Finance in Africa: “There Is A Huge Opportunity To Create IP That’s An Investable Class” Kelli Garner & Michael Stahl-David To Co-Star In Romantic Road Movie ‘You Always’ Dark Sky Films Takes U.S. Rights To Prize-Winning Emirati Horror ‘The Vile’ View All October 2, 2026 6:29am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Canal+ HQ in Boulogne Billancourt Getty Images Paris-based pay-TV giant Canal+ has hit back at the French government’s plan to double the VAT rate on TV subscriptions from 10% to 20% saying it could leave a potential €200M ($225M) hole in its finances. The planned hike was confirmed in a draft budget plan for 2027 presented by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on Thursday. The controversial package aimed at reining in France ’s public debt, with the government says is poised to hit a record 121.7% of domestic product (GDP) in 2027, proposes some €43B ($48B) worth of “recovery measures” which include increasing revenue from VAT. Related Stories News David Michel Buys Cottonwood Media Out Of Federation Studios News YouTube Says 'Obsession' & 'Backrooms' Point To Awards Future For Films Born On The Platform In a separate development, the budget plan also includes a proposal to cut to a tax deduction for YouTube , YouTube, TikTok, Facebook and Instagram linked to payments they make to France’s National Cinema Centre (CNC). Watch on Deadline These platforms were integrated in 2016 into France’s virtuous system of obligations, under which all entities distributing content in the territory are required to pay a percentage of their local revenue to the CNC, which is then put back into the local film and TV industry. Up until now, the obligation was based on around 35% of their advertising revenues thanks to 66% “abatement” but this has been halved. The measure is expected to raise around €60M ($60M) Canal+ reaction Canal+ called the decision to double the VAT rate for TV subscriptions “inconsistent” and “ill-advised”, noting that the government had only just last year confirmed that the 10% rate would stay in place. “If adopted, this measure would have a massive negative impact on the Group’s revenue and operating margin, potentially reaching €200 million annually, while the revenue gain for the State would amount to less than a quarter of that figure,” read a statement from the pay-TV giant. “Canal+ would be unable to absorb such a loss in France and would consequently be forced to adjust its operations in mainland France and the Overseas Territories. This would inevitably impact subscription prices, workforce levels, and financial contributions to the film and sports ecosystems—and the creative sector more broadly. The film and rugby communities have already rightly raised alarms regarding the risks this measure poses to the future of their respective industries.” Canal+, which floated on the London Stock Exchange in 2024 as part of a restructuring by Vivendi and has also expanded its footprint in Africa with the acquisition of the MultiChoice Group last year, said the VAT hike in France would lead it to double down on its international activities. “With operations now spanning nearly 70 countries, Canal+ regrets this direct attack on its business in its home market of France; it will draw the necessary conclusions and accelerate its international expansion strategy,” said the pay-TV. Industry reaction Rumors of the proposed VAT regime change for Canal+ had already sparked alarm bells with the French film and TV sectors earlier this week. Canal+ is one of the France’s major backers of local and European films and series. In July, it pledged more than $1 billion (€980 million ) for French and European cinema over five years in a fresh deal with the country’s main producer groups. It followed a previous accord in which Canal+ invested €480 million in French and European films from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2027. News of the tax hike for Canal+ also follows in the wake of news that the government was also planning a €47M ($53M) cut in public funds for state broadcaster France Télévisions in 2027 . Pre-empting the confirmation of the Canal+ VAT hike, France’s film and TV guilds put out a statement earlier this week. Bannered “Who wants the skin of French film and TV”, it declared that the Canal+ VAT hike combined with the France Télévisions cut flew in the face of promises made by President Emmanuel Macron at his Lumière Summit in September. “That summit…. had the stated aim of placing France at the heart of global creative production,” it read. “France Télévisions and Canal+ are two pillars of French film and audiovisual financing. “Through their investment obligations, pre-buys, and commitments under the media chronology rules, they enable hundreds of projects to get off the ground each year, ranging from debut features and auteur-driven works to genre films and international co-productions. Cutting their resources inevitably reduces their capacity to invest in creative work. Since funding obligations are tied to revenue, every euro taken away from these groups translates into fewer funded projects, fewer shoots, fewer jobs, and less diversity on screen. Targeting both groups in the same budget means striking at the very heart of the French model. articles.title: BRAVO Film Festival To Pause For 2026
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Erik Bright Joins PMK Entertainment As EVP Content & Strategic Communications ‘Clarissa’ Trailer: David Oyelowo, Sophie Okonedo, India Amarteifio & Ayo Edebiri Lead Starry Virginia Woolf Adaptation AGC Studios Launches Digital Division Focused On Creator-Led IP View All October 2, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source BRAVO Film Festival. Organizers behind the BRAVO Film Festival , the popular L.A.-based event focused on Brazilian cinema, have canceled the 2026 edition of the festival. Organizers said the event will not take place due to circumstances beyond their control. They added that preparation for next year’s edition will continue. “Our commitment to Brazilian cinema and to the filmmakers, partners, and audiences who have supported BRAVO has not changed,” Talize Sayegh, the festival’s founder and executive director, said in a statement. “We are grateful for that community and focused on returning next year with a festival worthy of it.” Related Stories News DramaBox Sets Brazilian Vertical Series From Cimarron & Trio Of Colombian Originals In Latin American Push News Prime Video Sets Launch Plans For Marília Mendonça Documentary 'Sentimento Louco' Founded in 2008, the BRAVO Film Festival often serves as a U.S. showcase for the year’s most exciting Brazilian talent. The festival traditionally screens Brazil ’s submission for the Best International Oscar as its opening title. In 2024, that was Walter Salles’ I’m Still Here, and 2025 was The Secret Agent , directed by Kleber Mendonça Filho and starring Wagner Moura. Watch on Deadline The organization has longstanding partnerships with American Cinematheque, the Brazilian Consulate in Los Angeles, Cinema do Brasil and Projeto Paradiso. “This pause gives us time to keep building what BRAVO stands for: a stronger bridge between Brazilian filmmakers and Hollywood,” Thiago Macêdo Correia, the festival’s creative director, said in a statement. “The work continues, and we are excited to return next year with the stories, talent, and energy that define Brazilian cinema.” The festival ran across November in Los Angeles. The 2025 edition opened at the Academy Museum. articles.title: Josh Greenstein & Dana Goldberg Poised To Run Combined Paramount Warner Bros Film Unit,  Setting Up Likely Michael De Luca & Pamela Abdy Exit
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony TIFF Midnight Madness Hit ‘River’ Gets Winter 2027 Date From Blumhouse Atomic Monster ‘Verity’ To Seduce $55M+ Worldwide Opening As Box Office Braces For ‘Digger’ Impact – Global Preview ‘Ebenezer’ Trailer: Johnny Depp Leads Ti West’s Dickens Remake View All October 2, 2026 7:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc L-R: Josh Greenstein, Dana Goldberg, Michael De Luca, and Pam Abdy Skydance/Courtesy The soon to be merged Paramount Warner Bros Motion Picture unit under the freshly labeled Skydance is bound to be run by current Paramount Motion Picture co-chairs, Josh Greenstein and Dana Goldberg , multiple sources say. Related Stories News Paramount-WBD Will Now Be Called Skydance, David Ellison Reveals Executives Paramount-WBD Deal Architect Gerry Cardinale Says Most Of $6B In Expected Cost Savings Will Not Be From Layoffs This comes after a sleepless night for Warner Bros’ Motion Picture Chairs Michael De Luca and Pam Abdy , who we hear, first learned that they weren’t making the jump to the new company from reports last night. It’s our understanding that Paramount co-CEO David Ellison never made a phone call to them about their future and whether or not there’s a job offer in hand. The news comes at a stinging time, as Warner Bros’ faces an epic flop in the $125M-$160M+ priced Tom Cruise starring, Alejandro Iñárritu social satire, Digger, which is poised to open to around $30M WW or less this weekend. De Luca and Abdy have been at Warner Bros since June 2022, when they jumped over from MGM following Amazon’s acquisition of that storied studio. The duo recently re-upped their contracts under WBD CEO David Zaslav through 2030. Key to their future at the new Paramount Warner Bros is whether or not Ellison continued to honor their current terms, which would have Warner Bros marketing and distribution departments report into them. From the sounds of it, those are tough terms for the numbers-crunching Ellison to honor. He’s a loyalist to his 16-year production colleague Goldberg, and longtime amigo Greenstein who have been steering the motion picture unit into financially reasonable shape following the old Paramount. Watch on Deadline Paramount will inherit a combined slate around 71 dated features through 2028, 56% of that generated by De Luca and Abdy’s Warner Bros. There’s still more to be dated by both studios in 2028. Paramount will also gain a film library that includes the $4.37 billion global grossing 2025 slate that De Luca and Abdy built as well as Oscar winners One Battle After Another, Sinners (until the rights of that film revert to its director Ryan Coogler) and Weapons. In addition, the new Paramount is looking at a potential $1 billion-grossing year-end holiday tentpole in Warner Bros/Legendary’s Dune: Part Three. There appears to be some talks as to exactly what De Luca and Abdy’s role will be in the new entity, however, the duo weren’t contracted to report into other motion picture chairs, rather the CEO. Reporting into Greenstein and Goldberg doesn’t sound like a likely scenario for the duo per sources. De Luca and Abdy could be offered a producing contract in the new Skydance. The executive chart for the new Paramount Warner Bros is expected to be announced in a matter of days. Ellison brought in former Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz as co-CEO. “Ellison will focus on the company’s long-term strategy, creative vision and direction, including its talent relationships, strategic partnerships, technology and capital allocation,” Paramount said. “Kreiz will focus on the company’s day-to-day management and integration of the combined businesses.” There was an optimistic buzz on Thursday that De Luca and Abdy would also have gate rights on the Melrose lot, and potentially report into Kreiz, but that’s not the likely scenario. Additionally in the new Paramount Warner Bros as of late, Casey Bloys was tapped as streaming head of the combined Paramount-WBD with Paramount’s current Chair of Direct-to-Consumer, Cindy Holland departing. Mark Thompson was told he’d stay on to oversee CNN going forward. While De Luca and Abdy had a great run at the box office last year, this year has been littered with myriad misfires including The Bride, Supergirl with no movie earning more than $100M stateside. The total domestic box office for Jan. 1-Oct. 1 is $448.4M. However, Paramount, too, hasn’t had a great box office year, their current domestic box office YTD right behind Warners with $429.8M, however, they had two $100M+ domestic titles in Scream 7 and Miramax’s Scary Movie. At the year-to-date North American box office, the newly combined Paramount Warner Bros would count $878.2M ranking behind Universal ($1.8B), Disney ($1.55B) and Sony ($1.28B). Under De Luca and Abdy, Warner Bros tallied 30 noms earlier this year, which tied the studio’s record from 2005. Warners took home 11 of those Oscars (six including Best Picture for One Battle After Another , four for Sinners, and supporting actress Amy Madigan’s win for Weapons ). The two had a reputation for protecting filmmakers’ vision, and were audacious in bankrolling auteur projects like Paul Thomas Anderson’s most expensive movie ever, the $140M One Battle After Another and Coogler’s $90M period vampire musical Sinners. One Battle After Another wound up being Anderson’s highest grossing movie ever at $213M+ at the global box office, though film finance sources questioned its profitability. Sinners was a great success with close to $372M WW. De Luca and Abdy presided over MGM starting in January 2020 until April 2022. There they built a slate which assisted in fueling the studio’s sale to Amazon for $8.45 billion for the 4,000 title library. During their run there, theatrical releases included No Time to Die, House of Gucci, Paul Thomas Anderson’s Licorice Pizza, not to mention they teed up Creed III, which became the highest-grossing in that franchise and the second-highest-grossing in the Rocky franchise. Paramount could not be reached for comment. The new class also includes Rashida Duvall (Alijah Kai), a first-gen criminal justice major; Shaquille Johnson (Cornell Young IV), a five-star athlete choosing legacy; Amir Rodale (Jordan Aaron Hall), a sharp psych major better at fixing everyone else’s problems than facing his own; Hazel Henry (Kennedi Reece), a church-raised small-town girl defining her own values; and Kojo Achebe (Chibuikem Uche), a Ghanaian-Nigerian fashion entrepreneur finding the courage to follow his vision. Bell as Ron And for us old-school fans, back for more, in addition to Guy and Hardison, the series saw the return of Darryl M. Bell as Ron Johnson, Cree Summer as Freddie Brooks, Charnele Brown as Dr. Kimberly Reese Boyer, Jenifer Lewis as Professor Davenport, Jada Pinkett Smith as Lena James, Dawnn Lewis as Jaleesa Vinson-Taylor, and Glynn Turman as Col. Bradford Taylor. Season 1 premiered on September 24 and debuted in the No. 4 spot on the Global Top 10 English TV list, earning 4.2M views and hitting the Top 10 in 15 countries, Netflix touts in a release. “It’s so validating to be bolstered by our amazing audience. We are beyond excited to return to Hillman and continue to tell meaningful and heartfelt stories that resonate across generations. I am thrilled for our brilliant cast and our hard-working crew,” Pride shared. Added executive producer and director Debbie Allen , “YAY! HALLELUJAH! The people and Netflix have spoken. A Different World brought something everybody needed: joy, romance, relevance, authenticity, and HEART! Thank you for getting us into the Top 10 worldwide! And now, gear up! We’re coming back at you with Season 2!!” In addition to Pride and Allen, the show’s executive producers include Tom Werner , Reggie Rock Bythewood , Gina Prince-Bythewood, and Mandy Summers. articles.title: Obscured Releasing Acquires NA Rights To ‘The Drug In Our Pocket’ Ahead Of Hamptons World Premiere
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Obscured Releasing Acquires NA Rights To ‘The Drug In Our Pocket’ Ahead Of Hamptons World Premiere Oscars: Pakistan Picks Mo Naqvi’s Doc Thriller ‘Hanging By A Wire’ As Best International Feature Entry ‘Musk’ Director Alex Gibney On World’s Richest Man: “He’s A Bullsh*tter” View All October 2, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'The Drug in Our Pocket' Obscured Releasing EXCLUSIVE: Obscured Releasing has acquired North American distribution rights to The Drug in Our Pocket , a documentary by Anne Sundberg about the pernicious effects on young people of constant smartphone use. The feature produced by Beth Kojima and Anne Sundberg holds its world premiere Saturday at the Hamptons International Film Festival in New York, and heads from there to the Heartland International Film Festival in Indianapolis and the Newport Beach Film Festival in Southern California. The Drug in Our Pocket is expected to get an Oscar-qualifying run this fall, followed by a limited theatrical release in early 2027. Related Stories Acquisitions Obscured Releasing Takes North America To Emily Robinson's SXSW Horror Pic 'Ugly Cry' News Sian Clifford Satirical Comedy 'Lady' Scores U.S. Deal “ The Drug in Our Pocket examines how smartphones, designed to connect us, have radically reshaped childhood, adolescence, and mental health,” notes a release. “Through intimate conversations with young people, parents, and leading experts, the film reveals a generation that is thoughtful, articulate, and increasingly aware of how digital environments shape their attention, emotions, and sense of self.” Watch on Deadline The documentary premieres as dozens of states have banned or restricted the use of cell phones in schools, recognizing the impact of the devices on student mental health. Similarly, several countries including Australia, France, Greece, Malaysia, and Brazil have moved to ban or restrict teen access to social media. From Instagram “With The Drug in Our Pocket , director Anne Sundberg brilliantly weaves psychological expert interviews, behind-the-scenes stories from tech whistleblowers, and deeply personal accounts of teenagers and parents exposing how big tech and our government have failed us,” said RJ Millard and Bill Guentzler of Obscured Releasing. “This is a necessary call to action highlighting the impact of social media and technology which offers us the steps we can take to reclaim our power, and attention.” Sundberg’s credits includes four films co-directed with Ricki Stern: The Trials of Darryl Hunt , Joan Rivers: A Piece of Work , The Devil Came on Horseback , and Reversing Roe . Director Anne Sundberg Courtesy of HamptonsFilm In a statement, Sundberg said, “RJ and Bill are brilliant at connecting films to audiences. They understood that for us, The Drug in Our Pocket isn’t just about documenting young people’s experiences growing up online. They share our vision that this film can start a larger movement asking us all to pay attention to our attention. We are thrilled to be working with them on this release.” The acquisition deal was negotiated by Anne Sundberg and Beth Kojima on behalf of the production and Bill Guentzler and RJ Millard on behalf of Obscured Releasing. The Drug in Our Pocket is directed by Anne Sundberg and produced by Beth Kojima and Anne Sundberg. Kojima, Sundberg, and John Wayland wrote the film. Wayland edited the documentary. Timo Elliston and Brian Jones composed the score. Executive producers include Regina K. Scully, Jenna Bush Hager, Crystal McCrary McGuire, Ashley Graham, Lizzie Tisch, and Jonathan Tisch. Obscured Releasing Obscured Releasing was launched by RJ Millard and Bill Guentzler in 2025 “to build film-first distribution strategies that prioritize collaboration in order to engage audiences through festival play, publicity and promotional campaigns, theatrical runs, and thoughtful VOD release windows.” Among its titles are Blue Film , starring Reed Birney and Kieron Moore; Siobhan McCarthy’s trans high school comedy She’s the He ; Christian Nilsson’s Westhampton , starring Finn Wittrock, RJ Mitte, Jake Weary, Amy Forsyth, and Tovah Feldshuh. Documentary releases include Stop The Insanity: Finding Susan Powter , and Endless Cookie . articles.title: Disney’s Worlds Collide Tour Hits All the Right Notes With ‘Descendants,’ ‘Zombies’ and ‘Camp Rock’ Stars
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke , Brianna Nordyke , Brooklyn Nordyke October 1, 2026 7:32am The Worlds Collide cast Courtesy Disney Concerts It’s safe to say there are a lot of tired — but really, really happy — kids in Los Angeles on Monday morning. Crypto.com Arena was filled on Monday night with adults and kids — from toddlers to teens — for a jam-packed, fast-paced, high-energy show courtesy of Disney . Eight cast members from three of the company’s hit movie franchises — Descendants , Zombies and Camp Rock — performed a three-hour show (with a 20-minute intermission) featuring all the big songs from those movies and then some, with the whole thing ending around 10 p.m. This reporter’s own kids didn’t get to bed until close to midnight — but they will tell you it was definitely worth staying up late for. Related Stories Business Disney+ Strikes Streaming Bundle and Content-Sharing Deal With Indonesia's Vidio Business Disney Entertainment TV Comms Chief Naomi Bulochnikov-Paul Departing The cheers were deafening inside the arena for the Worlds Collide tour, which features Malachi Barton ( Zombies 4, Camp Rock 3 ), Liamani Segura ( Descendants: Wicked Wonderland , Camp Rock 3 ), Dara Reneé ( Descendants: The Rise of Red ), Mekonnen Knife ( Zombies 4 ), Hudson Stone ( Camp Rock 3 ), Swayam Bhatia ( Zombies 4 ), Kiara Romero ( Descendants: Wicked Wonderland ) and Alexandro Byrd ( Descendants: Wicked Wonderland ). Among the set list were such songs as “It’s On,” “One Beat Away,” “Play My Music” and “We Rock” from the Camp Rock movies; “Like the Zombies Do,” “The Place to Be,” “Ain’t No Doubt About It” and “Someday” from the Zombies franchise; and “Perfect Princess,” “Chillin’ Like a Villain,” “Rotten to the Core” and “Ways to Be Wicked” from the Descendants soundtracks. Renée brought the house down with her powerful rendition of “Evil Like Me” from Descendants (sung by Kristin Chenoweth and Dove Cameron in the original), while Barton brought out his guitar for “Tomorrow” from Camp Rock 3, a song he said he’d begged to be allowed to perform. Stone, who also performed with his guitar, noted he’s the youngest on the tour, at 14 years old, but held his own with the rest of them. (The other performers range in age from 17-26.) Even with numerous costume changes, the show moved quickly. Between the different songs, at times various cast members would come out and address the audience directly, giving words of encouragement and inspiration. For example, Romero and Byrd talked about embracing your cultural heritage, while Romero, Segura and Bhatia spoke about the importance of friendship. Each of the actors got their time to address the crowd directly, and on big screens were shown images and videos of all the performers when they were younger. Many of them talked about their earlier ambitions to be professional singers, actors and/or dancers. A few of them, including Reneé, Barton, Segura and Stone, also got their chance in the spotlight to perform original solo songs, including “Never Waste a Heartbreak” (Reneé), “Stay for the Credits” (Barton), “Talk” (Stone) and “All the Things I’ve Learned So Far” (Segura). (In a nice touch, merchandise being sold in the lobby included not only shirts with all of the performers together but also tees featuring each person individually.) Among the younger fanbase, Barton and Segura have emerged as big stars, and the crowd went wild for their duet of Camp Rock ‘s iconic “This Is Me,” originally performed by Demi Lovato and Joe Jonas in the movie. In a surprise moment, Barton, who also stars alongside Bhatia in Disney’s upcoming series Coven Academy, brought out the stars of that show, which debuts Thursday. The show included elaborate choreography and big numbers and set pieces along with quieter moments, including a medley around a faux campfire. Barton and Segura again dueted on a Camp Rock song, “Wouldn’t Change a Thing,” during that portion, which also featured Romero singing “If Only” (from Descendants ), Reneé and Byrd singing “So This is Love” (from Cinderella and Descendants: The Rise of Red ) and the entire group singing the Camp Rock chant. The Worlds Collide cast Courtesy Disney Concerts So what did the younger attendees think about the show? Here are some reviews from two in the target demo: Brianna, age 14: “It was really engaging. They really wanted you to stand up and dance and be part of it, like when they taught us all a dance. The music was really good. I liked how they sang songs from even the [previous] movies that a lot of them weren’t in, like ‘If Only’ and ‘Someday,’ which was my favorite Obviously, those songs are really good. I also liked how they brought out their own stuff, like Hudson Stone sang ‘Talk’ and ‘Stay for the Credits,’ which are both really good singles that they made. “I liked how they showed videos of them when they were younger, so like I feel like it could have like inspired some kids to pursue what they want to do in their life. They also had a lot of messages about positivity. It was really nice because I feel like they were inspiring all the kids. I think it was a good length with an intermission.” Brooklyn, age 11: “What I liked about the Worlds Collide tour is that I loved all their outfits, how they spread positivity to children and just telling you to be yourself, and I loved how they showed younger pictures of [the performers], and I thought that was really fun. I loved how they mixed the songs. They are really good singers and I loved it overall. They were just telling kids to be their self, and I thought that was really positive, and I really liked how they did that. “I also thought the costumes were really good because they had a theme for everything, and they all had matching outfits, and I thought that was really cool. My favorite song, if I had to choose one, it would probably be ‘Wouldn’t Change a Thing’ from Camp Rock, because it’s a really good song. I also liked how they walked through the audience too. I really enjoyed it overall, and it was a really good show.” The Worlds Collide tour hit the Kia Forum in Inglewood on Wednesday and next travels to the Honda Center in Anaheim on Thursday before leaving Southern California for stops around the U.S. and Canada. It’ll go global starting in December with stops in Mexico, Great Britain, Germany, France and more. THR

articles.title: Bennington College, Alma Mater of Brett Easton Ellis and Donna Tartt, Launches Screenwriting MFA
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Mia Galuppo Plus Icon Mia Galuppo Senior Entertainment Reporter miagaluppo Follow Sign Up View All October 1, 2026 8:00am Bennington College Bennington College Bennington College has long been known for graduating literary talent, with notable alumni like Brett Easton Ellis, Donna Tartt and Kiran Desai. Now, the Vermont school is looking to break new screenwriting stars. Bennington is launching an MFA in screenwriting, planning for a two-year low-residency program that will see a small cohort of students participate in four ten-day residencies, two at Bennington in Vermont and two in Los Angeles, as well as eight ten-week online courses. “This is a unique screenwriting MFA, perfectly suited to our times,” said Theodore Braun, the director of the new Bennington program. “It blends the rigor of residential education with the flexibility of low residency, giving writers anywhere access to Bennington’s humanistic tradition of the liberal arts, elite screenwriter mentors, and the immersive professional energy of Los Angeles.” Related Stories Business Disney+ Strikes Streaming Bundle and Content-Sharing Deal With Indonesia's Vidio The Show Formerly Known as 'South Park' 'South America' Takes on the Literal Dicks of Big Tech Billionaires in New Episode Braun notes that the inaugural class will be “just six gifted, driven writers-students who are serious about building a body of work and launching a professional screenwriting career.” As for faculty, Bennington has lined up working writers that include The Holdovers writer David Hemingson and Bridgerton writer-producer Janet Lin, as well as Alexa Alemanni ( The Librarians ), Malia Scotch Marmo ( Hook ) and Aaron Rahsaan Thomas ( S.W.A.T. and Friday Night Lights ). Over the course of the program, students will produce feature scripts, spec television episodes, an original pilot and series bible, among other projects. The program will culminate in a capstone industry showcase in Los Angeles. Bennington has already graduated several well-known screenwriters, including Melissa Rosenberg, responsible for the Twilight adaptations, and Sofia Alvarez, who is behind the To All the Boys I’ve Loved Before films. “I think what Bennington excels at — its whole reason for being — is finding, nurturing, and empowering original voices,” offers Rosenberg. “That and the spirit of collaboration make it a wonderful place to launch this new MFA.” THR

articles.title: ‘Trailer Park Boys’ Actor Michael Smith Has Sexual Assault Charge Dismissed
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 1, 2026 8:03am Michael Smith as Bubbles (center) is flanked by fellow cast members John Paul Tremblay and Robb Wells. Netflix Logo text Mike Smith, the Nova Scotia actor best known for playing Bubbles on the Trailer Park Boys comedy , has had a sexual assault charge against him dismissed. A three-day sexual assault trial in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia began Thursday, but Judge Jill Hartlen called a halt to the case after crown prosecutors declined to present any evidence, according to the CBC News website on Thursday. “The court has dismissed the charge against Michael Smith, concluding the legal proceedings that began in October 2025 regarding an allegation dating to December 2017,” Trailer Park Boys Inc., a Nova Scotia-based company that produces the series and in which Smith is one of three directors, said in a statement obtained by The Hollywood Reporter. Related Stories TV Netflix's New Releases Coming in October 2026 TV 'East of Eden' Review: A Terrifying Florence Pugh Towers Over Zoe Kazan's Accomplished Netflix Adaptation of the John Steinbeck Classic The company also has as directors Trailer Park Boys co-stars John Paul Tremblay, who plays Julian, and Robert Wells, who plays Ricky. The company added: “Now that he (Smith) is cleared of this matter, Mike is resuming his responsibilities with Trailer Park Boys Incorporated.” Bubbles, Julian and Ricky and the rest of their Sunnyvale Trailer Park crew featured in the cult Canadian mockumentary about three petty criminals running scams from their Halifax business. The franchise included a TV series that streamed on Netflix and movies. Smith stepped away from Trailer Park Boys Inc. in Oct. 2025 when he was charged with one count of sexual assault stemming from an alleged incident in 2017, and pleaded not guilty. The CBC, Canada’s public broadcaster, on its online news site said an unnamed complainant against Smith in a statement said she was “unwilling to sacrifice my mental health” by testifying during the trail. The Trailer Park Boys was created in 2001 by Barry Dunn, Wells, Tremblay and Mike Clattenburg and originally launched on Canada’s Showcase channel. The series ended its Canadian TV run in 2008. Netflix picked up the Trailer Park Boys property in 2014. THR

articles.title: What Ratings Issues? NBCU Telemundo Chair Touts World Cup Success for Live TV
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 1, 2026 8:30am Luis Fernández Courtesy of NBCUniversal Telemundo Enterprises Luis Fernández , chairman of Spanish-language media powerhouse NBCUniversal Telemundo Enterprises and former Telemundo news chief, was one of the high-profile keynote speakers on Thursday afternoon at the sixth edition of Iberseries & Platino Industria in the Spanish capital, Madrid . In his appearance, he spent some time modestly taking a victory lap for Telemundo’s success with the soccer World Cup 2026, as well as touting the power of live and linear TV. Telemundo is part of entertainment company NBCUniversal, which is owned by Comcast but is scheduled to be spun off by the cable and telecom giant next year. “The FIFA football World Cup was the most-watched sports feature in Spanish [in the U.S.]. We never had those ratings,” Fernández told the Madrid event during his appearance entitled “Leadership, relevance and transformation of the Spanish-language audiovisual industry.” He particularly lauded the combined World Cup offerings across both streaming and linear services, emphasizing: “We were able to bring together Telemundo and Peacock, our streaming platform. Five out of the 10 most-watched programs on Peacock were events that happened during the World Cup.” Fernández also told the Iberseries crowd that based on how the World Cup was presented and consumed, his company’s advertising sales team signaled to him that they were expecting better Los Angeles Summer Olympics 2028 ad momentum than previously thought. The exec on Thursday further touted the importance of constant reinvention in the media and entertainment sector. “This industry has to reinvent every year, every month, every day,” he said. “And if you’re not adapting and reinventing yourself, you will be out of the system.” That means rethinking approaches and taking some risks. “If we fight, if we work, are bold and fearless, and also creative, we’ll be able” to succeed, he concluded. Luis Fernández at Iberseries 2026 As one example of the change he has brought to Telemundo, Fernández pointed to his early efforts to move beyond the image as a reality TV-centric broadcaster despite some initial skepticism within the company. “I was thinking of what we could do to improve the channel, to be more competitive, and to be more relevant,” he said. “We have reality TV, but we also have news, we have sports, we have fiction. So we had to get rid of that image that had formed.” How does the Telemundo chair feel about the outlook for linear TV versus streaming? “I think that streaming services are our rivals and our competitors, and I think that linear TV really has a lot of power in live shows,” Fernández offered. “The streaming services eventually will be able to be good at live TV, but right now, live TV is something where we have much more to offer.” Pointing to the World Cup again, he also shared: “I always hate when people say that linear or traditional TV is falling in viewership, ratings.” It will not surprise you that, in this context, Fernández also told Iberseries about his interest in continuing to offer up sports programming, including beyond soccer. “For me, that’s one of the key pillars of our strategy for the upcoming years,” he emphasized. “Sports licensing is one of the things that we’re investing in.” Asked about his view on AI, the exec replied: “It is an opportunity.” Without going into too much detail, he mentioned that the media space has always faced technological changes. Wednesday’s conference day saw creators of series that address far-right politics, the climate crisis and more discuss whether great dramas can change the world. And Mediawan executives shared insights on their strategy and focus, including such hits as F1: The Movie , Slow Horses and Call My Agent! On Tuesday, Amazon MGM Studios executives discussed the success of the Mercedes Ron young adult novel adaptations and Spanish zombie horror film Apocalypse Z , while Parrot Analytics shared data trends and estimates for the subscriber impact of Netflix’s Argentina hit series The Eternaut . And a YouTube top executive predicted at Iberseries that more Obsession – and Backrooms -style film hits from online creators. The sixth edition of the industry gathering wraps up on Friday. THR

articles.title: CNN Chief Mark Thompson May Stay On After Sale — Though Contract Talks Are Early
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 1, 2026 8:50am CNN chief Mark Thompson Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images CNN may have more stability than some had feared under the combined Paramount-Warner Bros. David Ellison has held discussions with CNN CEO Mark Thompson about keeping the veteran executive in charge of the cable news channel, a source familiar with the matter says. The contract talks, however, are said to be very early, and there is no assurance that they can come to terms on a new deal. No change in leadership is expected at deal close, with Thompson’s current contract to lead CNN running into next year. The Wall Street Journal , which first reported the news, said that Thompson wants assurances that he will have autonomy over the global news brand, including on editorial matters. CNN will have an “editorial independence board” once the deal closes , with a group of journalists establishing guiding principles for the news outlet, and resolving any disputes with corporate leadership. If Thompson and Ellison are able to come to terms on a new deal, it would come as a sigh of relief to many CNN talent, who have been fearful of a dramatic overhaul at the channel post-merger, especially given Bari Weiss’ aggressive changes at CBS News. That doesn’t mean CNN won’t undergo changes under the combined company, but it does mean that Thompson will be able to continue executing on the digital reboot that he is in the middle of overseeing. While CNN’s linear ratings have been challenged in recent years, it remains a profit center among the WBD cable channels, filings show. Those profits will be particularly important as the combined company seeks to pay down an estimated $80 billion debt load. That said, one observer says that the merger will almost certainly require some level of consolidation between CBS News and CNN, though the devil may be in the details as things move forward. THR

articles.title: ‘Rolling Loud: The Movie’ Review: Owen Wilson Plays a Very Bad Dad in a Tone-Deaf Would-Be Comedy
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Frank Scheck Plus Icon Frank Scheck View All October 1, 2026 9:00am 'Rolling Loud: The Movie' Ketchup Entertainment An underage teenager gets snuck into a hip-hop music festival headlined by Travis Scott and soon goes missing, his desperate father frantically attempting to find him before it’s too late. No, it’s not a harrowing drama based on the tragic 2021 real-life events at Scott’s Astroworld concert in Texas, where 10 concertgoers were killed in a fatal crowd crush. Instead, Rolling Loud: The Movie is…a comedy. Discuss among yourselves. Rolling Loud: The Movie The Bottom Line A bad idea, terribly executed. Release date : Friday, October 2 Cast : Owen Wilson, Matt Rife, Christine Ko, Christian Convery, Jolene, Henry Winkler, Travis Scott Director-screenwriter : Jeremy Garelick Rated R, 1 hour 35 minutes To say that this effort written and directed by Jeremy Garelick ( The Wedding Ringer , Murder Mystery 2 ) — who is modestly described in the film’s press notes as “reinventing Hollywood comedy with brain, heart, and guts” — comes across as tone-deaf is an understatement. Even if you ignore the disturbing parallels to past events, this story of a dad attempting to bond with his 13-year-old son by irresponsibly sneaking him into the popular hip-hop music festival of the title while lying to his wife and the festival’s security personnel just feels icky. Did I mention it’s a true story? Related Stories Movies 'Practical Magic 2' Summons $30M to End Spider-Man's Streak at No. 1 Movies 'Practical Magic 2' Whips Up $4.7M in Box Office Previews Yes, the filmmaker apparently did take his 13-year-old to the festival, filled with people walking around in various states of undress and many of them using drugs, against his wife’s wishes. And he did lose contact with his son, unable to reach him because of the lack of cell phone reception. Apparently, rather than feeling chastened, he thought: “What a great idea for a movie!” Of course, it still could have worked if the film actually proved funny. Instead, it’s a witless, moronic, slapstick-filled mediocrity that basically serves as a feature-length commercial for the popular music festival where parts of it were filmed (Live Nation is among the production companies). To that end, the film features not only Scott, playing a recliner-chair-loving version of himself (don’t ask), but also such real-life hip-hop stars as Sexyy Red, Ski Mask the Slump God, and Ty Dolla $ign, none of whom are likely to enlarge their fan base. Wilson plays hapless furniture salesman Hank — he works at “Raymond & Ferguson” — who tells his wife Melanie (Jolene) that he’s taking their son Zion (Christian Convery) to their lake house, but instead brings him to Rolling Loud. There he runs into his co-worker Terry (comedian Matt Rife , managing to make his character as annoying as his stand-up), whom he had just been ordered to fire by their boss ( Henry Winkler , squandering some of that good will from Barry ). Distracted by Terry, Hank doesn’t think much of it when Zion excuses himself to go to the bathroom. But he becomes increasingly anxious when his son fails to reappear, and that’s when the would-be comic complications ensue. They include an episode in which Hank retreats to a quiet room, only to discover that his lying conversation to his wife has been broadcast to a disapproving crowd outside; a physical altercation with security guards when he attempts to report his son missing; and accidentally throwing Linda (Christine Ko), a festival volunteer worker, off of a Ferris wheel, injuring a wheelchair-bound bystander in the process. And, of course, Hank also accidentally takes drugs and begins tripping. And the volunteer strips naked to distract the security guards, revealing a forest-level growth of pubic hair in the process. (The appealing Ko, who provides some genuine amusement in her role, deserved better). It’s all about as laborious as it sounds, with Wilson, utilizing his familiar style of motor-mouthed pathos and desperation, working very hard to infuse comic energy into the strained proceedings. By the time he gets onstage with Scott and then disastrously leaps into the mosh pit, all you’re thinking is that he needs to collaborate with Wes Anderson again, and as soon as possible. As for Scott, if he survived the fallout from Astroworld, he can survive this. Full credits Production: American High, Live Nation Production, Live Nation Studios, Rolling Loud Distributor: Ketchup Entertainment Cast: Owen Wilson, Matt Rife, Christine Ko, Christian Convery, Jolene, Henry Winkler, Travis Scott Director-screenwriter: Jeremy Garelick Producers: Stella Bulochnikov, Jolene, Jeremy Garelick, Will Phelps, Doug Banker Executive producers: Ryan D. Adams, Dan Kaplow, Michael Rapino, Matt Rife, Pasquale Rotella, Christina Shams, Matt Philip Whelan, Matt Zingler Director of photography: Bradford Lipson Production designer: Kathrin Eder Composer: Chanda Dancy Costume designer: Wlaa Elashkar Casting: Findley Davidson, Mary Vernieu Rated R, 1 hour 35 minutes THR

articles.title: Martin Grove, Longtime Columnist for The Hollywood Reporter, Dies at 83
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All October 1, 2026 9:12am Martin Grove Courtesy of Grove Family Martin Grove, who wrote more than 3,300 columns for The Hollywood Reporter over 25 years as one of his era’s most respected and influential film experts, has died. He was 83. Grove died Tuesday at Providence Cedars-Sinai Tarzana Medical Center of cancer-related natural causes, his daughter, Universal Pictures vp media Alyson Grove, told THR . He inspired her to work in the business, she said. Grove’s “Hollywood Report” column, which centered on box office analysis, marketing and distribution, appeared on the pages of THR from July 1985 through January 2000. His “Filmmaker Focus” column, which showcased the art of making movies, then served as an exclusive THR.com feature through December 2010. Related Stories TV Peppino Mazzullo, Voice of Topo Gigio, the Italian Puppet on 'The Ed Sullivan Show,' Dies at 100 Movies John Grover, Film Editor on Six James Bond Movies, Dies at 87 “My dad truly loved his time at THR ,” his daughter said. The amiable Grove also appeared as a movie expert on CNN’s ShowBiz Today from 1989-2001 and as a movie analyst for CNNfn’s The Biz from 1996-2004, and his entertainment business reports could be heard weekday afternoons on the all-news Los Angeles radio station KNX from 1999-2004. In 2001, Grove taped luncheon interviews at Wolfgang Puck’s Spago in Beverly Hills with the likes of Ron Howard, Ridley Scott, Steven Soderbergh, Wolfgang Petersen and Michael Bay for the AMC series Behind the Screen . And from 1990-2008, he produced, wrote and provided the voiceovers for 90-second sponsored movie previews distributed to airlines including American, United, Delta, Northwest and TWA. Born on March 30, 1943, in Perth Amboy, New Jersey, Martin Allan Grove received his bachelor’s degree from Rutgers University, where he majored in art history and journalism and worked for the campus radio station, WRSU. En route to earning his master’s degree in screenwriting from NYU’s School of the Arts by taking night classes, he spent his days at ABC, where he handled radio network publicity and then business publicity for ABC television. As management, he helped keep WABC, New York’s top-rated radio station, on the air during several extended talent and engineering walkouts in 1967 by filling in on the graveyard shift for such popular DJs as Bruce Morrow (Cousin Brucie) and Dan Ingram. “As the strikes went on,” he said, “WABC created new jingles promoting ‘The Strikebound Sound of 77 WABC,’ and I had my own ‘Marty Grove’ jingle to use on the shows I did.” Grove later directed publicity for the advertising firm Foote, Cone & Belding, headed corporate communications and investor relations for 20th Century Fox in New York and Los Angeles and led marketing for Warner Bros. Television in Burbank (at Fox, he did marketing for its Movietone News library of newsreels as well). Before studios routinely announced box office figures, Grove served from 1985-95 as an Entertainment Tonight consultant for a Monday feature that projected grosses, and he appeared frequently on ET as a film expert during this period. Grove interviewed celebrities and filmmakers for THR ’s televised coverage of the 1987 Cannes Film Festival and anchored the paper’s TV coverage of the NATO/ShoWest theater owners conventions in Las Vegas from 1987-91. Starting in 1988, he hosted half-hour talk show episodes about Hollywood and two-minute commentaries about movies for Movietime, the cable network that later became E! Entertainment; produced, wrote and hosted the series For Your Consideration about Oscar and Golden Globes contenders on Time Warner Cable in New York and L.A.; and was a film industry analyst for the Financial News Network. During his career, Grove showed up on the NBC Nightly News , the CBS Evening News , ABC World News Tonight , Today , 20/20 , CNBC’s Power Lunch and Fox News programs was quoted in The New York Times , Wall Street Journal , Time , Washington Post , Sunday Times of London , Rolling Stone and Agence-France Presse . Since 2008, he served as CEO and president of ZAMM.com, for which he wrote, produced and voiced hundreds of movie preview videos as part of a content partnership with Amazon. A member of the WGA West, Grove sold screenplay pitches to Paramount and Columbia that he wrote and developed but that were not produced. He also authored a novel set in the world of network television, 10 pseudonymous mystery novels and a half-dozen pop-culture paperbacks, including an authorized biography of John Travolta, an instant biography of Elvis Presley published within days of his 1977 death and profiles of The Beatles, The Osmonds, Henry Winkler and Paul McCartney. Along the way, he still examined the estimated box office numbers every Sunday and the actuals every Monday. In addition to his daughter, survivors include his wife of 55 years, Marjorie; son Geoffrey; daughter-in-law Hilary; granddaughter Reesa; and grandson Rogan. THR

articles.title: Pro ‘Fortnite’ Gamer Cody ‘Clix’ Conrod Launches New Holding Company Full Box to Align Owned Businesses, Collabs and Philanthropy (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 8:30am PT Pro ‘Fortnite’ Gamer Cody ‘Clix’ Conrod Launches New Holding Company Full Box to Align Owned Businesses, Collabs and Philanthropy (EXCLUSIVE) By Jennifer Maas Plus Icon Jennifer Maas TV Business Writer @jmaasaronson Latest Pro ‘Fortnite’ Gamer Cody ‘Clix’ Conrod Launches New Holding Company Full Box to Align Owned Businesses, Collabs and Philanthropy (EXCLUSIVE) 20 minutes ago Fugitive Films Co-Founder, Former MTV Scripted Boss Launch Romance-Focused Vertical Content Studio, Rommi (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Author Chloe Gong on ‘Eyes of Kings’ ending, ‘Deadlock’ debut and how she wants ‘These Violent Delights’ adapted for TV or film 5 days ago See All Full Box Professional “Fornite” player and star gamer Cody “ Clix ” Conrod has launched Full Box Inc., a creator-led holding company to encompasses his nine businesses, ventures and community initiatives A nod to the sport itself, the name “Full Box” comes directly from the massive Epic Games-developed online game, where the term describes surrounding an opponent with control, skill and competitive execution. Per Full Box, the name “reflects both the competitive mindset that has defined [Conrod’s] career and the company’s approach to building a complete business ecosystem around a creator.” Related Stories Melissa McCarthy on Getting Serious for 'JonBenét Ramsey,' the Psychiatrist on Set and Hollywood's 'Bulls---’ Excuse for Why Comedies Don't Work Anymore 'It's Time for My Voice': Jennifer Hudson on Reviving 'Dreamgirls,' Booking Tom Cruise for Her Talk Show and Writing Original Music Again Joining Conrod at Full Box is Darren Glover, who spent six years building the gaming division at VaynerSports and served as Conrod’s first agent. Glove is set as Full Box CEO while Conrod serves as founder and chief creative officer and continues to compete and stream at the highest level of “ Fortnite .” Popular on Variety Full Box is focusing its holdings around three pillars: Operating Companies, Full Box Ventures and Impact. Built around Conrod’s commitment to giving back to the community he grew up with, Full Box Inc.’s Impact arm houses the Dr3amin Access Fund, a career development initiative providing kids with gaming PCs, hardware and programming designed to create pathways into competitive gaming, content creation and game development. The Fund formalizes Conrod’s longstanding grassroots efforts, which delivered more than $250,000 in gaming equipment through Clixmas, his large-scale holiday event, in 2025. “When we’re talking about new talent in the space, little short story: A gaming computer that I gave away around two years ago to a kid that was on 60 FPS, playing on a console, had no earnings. I gave him a Clixmas computer, and now he’s literally here in Belgium competing for $10 million right next to me, and he made over $150,000,” Conrod told Variety during an interview out of the Fortnite Global Championship last month. “So that one kid, his name is Joshreyli , happened off of me giving away, I think at that time was like 40 computers. So as time gets on, and now that it’s an official thing where people could now give us money in the Dr3amin Access Fund, and we could give that back, how many more kids can we help elevate and give access to, where they could actually become that? So these next five years is really just continuing to build it.” To date, Full Box Inc.’s Operating Companies division is comprised of owned businesses including: ● Clix Gaming, a content and production company spanning live streaming, competitive gaming, brand partnerships, and interactive digital experiences across Fortnite and Roblox. ● Clix Creative: A creator-led game studio building experiences within the competitive Fortnite ecosystem, built around ranked play, personal progression and tournaments. ● Dr3amin Clothing, the apparel and lifestyle brand inspired by Conrod’s personal journey. Full Box Ventures currently supports: ● Reach Clipping: The fastest-growing clipping agency on Content Rewards, helping creators and brands scale short-form distribution through performance-based clipping campaigns. ● Real Sports App: A booming social sports platform combining live scores and play-by-play with community, conversation and gaming at its core. ● Rorra: A next-generation water filtration company focused on making cleaner water more accessible. ● TapCaps: A brand co-founded alongside fellow creator Lacy, blending gaming and mainstream culture through limited-edition blind-box collectibles that double as clickable fidget toys and functional keyboard keycaps. ● XSET: A gaming lifestyle brand and media network where Conrod serves as a competitive player and co-owner. Glover says the overall Full Box business is made up of multiple revenue streams which are all built around, but not beholden to, Conrod’s “Fortnite” presence. “‘Fortnite,’ Roblox, ‘Minecraft,’ and ‘Grand Theft Auto’ are the only games that you can earn within the game itself,” Glover says. “So our business model is vertically integrated, which is very unique in the gaming world, where there are lots of people that make content about video games and they monetize on the media of the content, which is great. That’s a super simple way, but that’s a really bumpy road to create a business around that. ‘Fortnite’ gives you the ability to make money by playing the game. You’re creating content about the game. We have a creator code; that’s people putting in an affiliate link in the store when they buy something. They’re supporting Clix by putting in code Clix, which is a whole different content model and a fun thing that Cody has created are these, ‘Use Code Clix’ commercials.” Glover adds: “So we have an affiliate link model from all the commerce that’s happening inside of the store. We have games and experiences that we’re building with Clix Creative that we monetize specifically based on engagement, very similar to a YouTube model… So we’re making revenue for the business by players playing our maps and experiences. So we we’ve got this like very cool model that we make content about the game and we make content within the game. So for us, it’s not about trying to predict where the game goes.” This includes not only an ongoing collaboration with “Fortnite” maker Epic Games, but also one of its major investors, Disney. “We have a really good relationship with Disney,” Glover says. “I just saw Josh [D’Amaro], the CEO, last Friday, and praised him for his belief in ‘Fortnite.’ So for us, it’s not about trying to predict where they go. It’s just us creating the infrastructure that’s going to support wherever they take it.” Abhishek Chaubey, Navdeep Singh to Present Shivam Shankar’s ‘Bhed, Bakri, Bhoot’ on Anurag Kashyap-Curated YouTube Channel (EXCLUSIVE) John Oliver Embarrasses Trump Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy Over ‘Godawful’ YouTube Reality Show and ‘Real World’ Past In Docuseries ‘Keinaan, Go Back to Somalia,’ Finnish-Somali YouTube Star Turns Racist Comments Into a Personal Statement Director and Producer James Wan on YouTube Filmmakers: ‘You Don’t Even Need to Be in the System Anymore to Get Something Made’ Google’s Sean Downey on the YouTube TIFF Takeover, Oscars Ad Integration and Creators vs. Influencers Netflix, Amazon and YouTube Form D.C. articles.title: ‘La Bola Negra’ Star Guitarricadelafuente to Receive Discovery Award at SCAD Savannah Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 8:30am PT ‘La Bola Negra’ Star Guitarricadelafuente to Receive Discovery Award at SCAD Savannah Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE) The musician makes his feature film acting debut in the epic drama, directed by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi. By Marc Malkin Plus Icon Marc Malkin Senior Editor, Culture and Events marcmalkin Latest ‘La Bola Negra’ Star Guitarricadelafuente to Receive Discovery Award at SCAD Savannah Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE) 42 minutes ago Bradley Whitford on Bringing Back ‘The West Wing’ as a ‘Limited Series’ 17 hours ago Queer Dating App Jack’d Launches Film Festival With Judges TS Madison, Miss Lawrence, Bobby Ashley, Mike Gauyo and Dyllón Burnside (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago See All Carla Oset/Netflix “ La Bola Negra ” star Guitarricadelafuente will be honored with the Discovery Award at this year’s SCAD Savannah Film Festival. The musician is being recognized for his breakout feature acting debut in the Oscar-buzzy drama. In the movie, directed by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis — Guitarricadelafuente stars as Sebastián, a soldier during the Spanish Civil War who falls in love with a wounded prisoner (Miguel Bernardeau) he is assigned to guard while he is in hospital. Related Stories 'It's Time for My Voice': Jennifer Hudson on Reviving 'Dreamgirls,' Booking Tom Cruise for Her Talk Show and Writing Original Music Again 'People Are Still Terrified of Me': Sharon Stone on Thriving for 46 Years in Hollywood and Why 'My Lane Was Never Going to Be Sex Psychos' Guitarricadelafuente, 29, will receive the award following a screening of “La Bola Negra” on Oct. 24. Popular on Variety Sebastian is one of three stories in the film about queer men spanning nearly a century of Spanish history. The ensemble also stars Milo Quife as Carlos, a young man who is rejected from a members-only social club in Granada in 1932 for being gay, and Carlos González as Albert, a queer historian in 2017 who uncovers his own family secrets following the death of his grandfather. Rounding out the cast are Lola Dueñas, Penélope Cruz, Glenn Close and Julio Torres. Guitarricadelafuente first gained attention in 2018 with “El Conticinio,” a song which he recorded on a PlayStation microphone. That same recording was later chosen for a 2025 Apple commercial directed by Spike Jonze and starring Pedro Pascal. Early hits “Guantanamera” and “Nana Triste” (with Natalia Lacunza) drew 59 million and 70 million streams, respectively. His debut album “La Cantera” was released in 2022 followed by “Spanish Leather” — with a cover shot by Wolfgang Tillmans — in 2025. Guitarricadelafuente’s original song, “La Nieve,” from “La Bola Negra” is now available to stream. “La Bola Negra” won the People’s Choice Award at the Toronto International Film Festival, the Audience Award at the San Sebastián Film Festival and the best director award at Cannes for Calvo and Ambrossi. Guitarricadelafuente joins previously announced honorees for this year’s SCAD festival, including Helen Mirren (Legend of Entertainment Award), Julianne Moore (Icon Award), and Patrice Vermette (Variety Creative Impact in Production Design Award). The festival runs at The Savannah College of Art and Design Oct. 24-31. “La Bola Negra” opens in limited release on Oct. 16 before expanding wider and premiering on Netflix on Dec. 2 YouTube Locks Down Coachella Rights Through 2030 as It Unveils New Microdrama-Inspired Experience for Shorts, AI-Powered Tools for Music and Studio, and More Netflix, Amazon and YouTube Form D.C. articles.title: Paramount, CNN Chief Mark Thompson in ‘Early Stages’ of Discussions to Keep Him in Post
articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 8:39am PT Paramount, CNN Chief Mark Thompson in ‘Early Stages’ of Discussions to Keep Him in Post By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest Paramount, CNN Chief Mark Thompson in ‘Early Stages’ of Discussions to Keep Him in Post 9 minutes ago Fox Business Taps ‘Big Money’ Roundtable to Replace Maria Bartiromo in Mornings 32 minutes ago Anvara Aims to Build Marketplace for Advertisers Looking for Events to Sponsor 1 hour ago See All Noam Galai Paramount Skydance and CNN chief Mark Thompson are in the “early stages” of discussions that could keep him as the leader of the news giant, according to a person familiar with the matter, a sign that the company is likely to keep CBS News and CNN apart initially as it navigates its purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery. CNN declined to make executives available for comment. Paramount could not be reached for immediate comment. Related Stories Paige DeSorbo on Leaving 'Summer House' Behind and Speaking Out About a Past Abusive Relationship: 'Domestic Violence' Can 'Truly Happen to Anyone' 'People Are Still Terrified of Me': Sharon Stone on Thriving for 46 Years in Hollywood and Why 'My Lane Was Never Going to Be Sex Psychos' Thompson’s fate remains unclear. He has called for CNN to operate without interference in its editorial mission. Paramount has agreed to set up a board to keep tabs on the independence of its news properties as part of its recent settlement with a set of state attorneys general who wanted to block its deal. Thompson’s current contract is believed to run out in 2027. Popular on Variety The Wall Street Journal previously reported on the talks between Paramount and the executive. The news could bring some relief to staffers at CNN, who have been worried about the fate of the news division under Paramount. Staffers have wondered about Paramount CEO David Ellison’s commitment to credible newsgathering given recent scrutiny of the executive he installed at CBS News, Bari Weiss. They are also concerned about the direction Paramount may see for CNN’s new streaming service. CNN’s progress with digital audiences has been slowed by a bevy of changes in the company’s corporate direction in recent years. Thompson last week expressed a desire to stay in the role. “I am enthusiastic about staying,” he told employees during a recentl town hall meeting, according to two people with knowledge of his remarks. Even so, he also confided he has no knowledge of how Paramount Skydance wanted to proceed once it completes its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. “How Paramount wants to run news” is not known to him at present, he said. During his tenure, Thompson has focused on getting CNN content in front of younger viewers and digital audiences. CNN has been testing new formats with its “CNN All Access” subscription service, and has seen up and coming personnel like Abby Phillip and Harry Enten gain some traction. Warner Bros. Discovery projected in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission earlier this year that CNN will generate $600 million in profit in 2026 on $1.8 billion in revenue. articles.title: Grammy Asian Pop Category Will Go Forward, CEO Says: ‘We Understand This Conclusion Will Not Satisfy Everyone’
articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 8:59am PT Grammy Asian Pop Category Will Go Forward, CEO Says: ‘We Understand This Conclusion Will Not Satisfy Everyone’ By Jem Aswad Plus Icon Jem Aswad Executive Editor, Music jemaswad Latest Sia Sells 50% of Music Catalog to Pophouse in $180 Million Partnership Deal 2 hours ago Billy Joel Gives Health Update After Brain Surgery: ‘I’m OK — It Sounds a Lot Worse Than It Actually Is’ 1 day ago LCD Soundsystem Announces 2026 NYC Residency — Including 100th Residency Show 1 day ago See All HYBE Grammy chief Harvey Mason Jr. has issued a statement in which he says the Awards’ controversial newest category, Asian Pop, will go forward for the 2027 ceremony. Mason had previously signaled that the Recording Academy was reconsidering the new category in the wake of decidedly split reactions after it was announced in June. BTS in particular objected to the category , implying that it effectively ghetto-izes a genre of music more than highlighting it and saying they will not submit their music for Grammy consideration in 2027. Related Stories Her Road to the Top: How NBCUniversal TV Studio Chief Pearlena Igbokwe Learned to Balance Business and Creative Instincts 'It's Time for My Voice': Jennifer Hudson on Reviving 'Dreamgirls,' Booking Tom Cruise for Her Talk Show and Writing Original Music Again “We hope our music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language,” the group said in a statement. Popular on Variety However, Mason is unequivocal about the award going forward, at least for 2027, based on conversations with multiple people in the community. “Over the past several weeks the Academy has been conducting listening sessions and have been in dialogue with leaders of the Asian music community,” Mason’s statement reads in full. “The journey has been rewarding and inspiring. Our organization is at its best when we engage deeply with music people and go the extra mile to understand their lived experiences. “In this case, we heard candid feedback from people in our community who don’t support the continuation of this category. We also heard from people who didn’t have accurate information about the category, and having space to clear up misperceptions has been especially valuable. But by far, the loudest feedback we heard was from people who were enthusiastic supporters of the category, fellow music creators expressing their encouragement for keeping it. “We understand this conclusion will not satisfy everyone, and that never feels good. But at the same time, we are confident it’s the right conclusion for the music community overall. As is the case with all our categories, we will continue to diligently engage with the music community and keep striving to honor this music — and all music — in the best possible way. We look forward to celebrating the Asian Pop Music Performance nominees at the 2027 Grammy Awards.” The Academy also noted that it has received a “robust” number of submissions for the category, signaling strong interest in its first year. The introduction of the award revived a familiar issue with the Grammys ’ genre-specific awards. While the intent may be to recognize music in a certain genre or language, many people within that community feel that it actually ends up being exclusionary, with voters relegating music or artists into those genre categories rather than more-mainstream ones; this has been a common complaint with regard to the Latin Grammys. While BTS has been nominated for Grammy Awards five times, in pop and other categories, the group has never won. “Golden,” from the smash film “KPop Demon Hunters” and performed by the fictional group Huntr/x (vocalists EJAE, Audrey Nuna, and Rei Ami), is widely considered the first KPop Grammy win, taking the award for best song written for visual media earlier this year, although it did not win for best song. articles.title: Middleburg Film Festival Sets ‘Being Heumann’ as Closing Night Film, Martin McDonagh, Seth Rogen and Rosalind Eleazar Lead Honorees
articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 9:00am PT Middleburg Film Festival Sets ‘Being Heumann’ as Closing Night Film, Martin McDonagh, Seth Rogen and Rosalind Eleazar Lead Honorees By Clayton Davis Plus Icon Clayton Davis Chief Awards Editor byClaytonDavis Latest Variety’s ‘Pixels and Pencils’ Animation Panel Returns to SCAD Savannah Film Festival With Directors of ‘Wildwood,’ ‘Ray Gunn’ and More 2 days ago Julianne Moore to Receive Icon Award at SCAD Savannah Film Festival With ‘The Debut’ Set as Centerpiece Selection 3 days ago Lance Oppenheim on ‘Primetime,’ ‘You Can See Everything’ and How Chris Hansen’s Reaction ‘Is Exactly What the Film Is About’ 6 days ago See All Apple Original Films “ Being Heumann ,” Oscar winner Siân Heder’s Apple Original Film, will close the 14th Middleburg Film Festival , which runs Oct. 15-18. The festival has also set Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s “La Bola Negra” as its Friday Spotlight and Tony Gilroy’s “ Behemoth !” as its Sunday Spotlight. As previously announced , the festival will open with Jesse Eisenberg’s “The Debut.” Martin McDonagh, Brad Bird, Seth Rogen , Rosalind Eleazar, Guitarricadelafuente and casting directors Adam Caldwell and Bernard Telsey will be honored at this year’s festival. Billie Jean King and Bill Pullman are among the special guests. Popular on Variety Related Stories Melissa McCarthy on Getting Serious for 'JonBenét Ramsey,' the Psychiatrist on Set and Hollywood's 'Bulls---’ Excuse for Why Comedies Don't Work Anymore Paige DeSorbo on Leaving 'Summer House' Behind and Speaking Out About a Past Abusive Relationship: 'Domestic Violence' Can 'Truly Happen to Anyone' Over the past decade, Middleburg has become a reliable fall stop for awards hopefuls. Being close to Washington, D.C., helps it draw national press and its small size gives filmmakers time for longer conversations with audiences. This year’s lineup continues that tradition. Caldwell and Telsey will receive the festival’s Special Achievement in Casting Award and join a post-screening Q&A. The recognition arrives as the Academy’s achievement in casting category enters its second year. Representing “La Bola Negra,” Guitarricadelafuente wrote and performs the film’s original song, “La Nieve.” He will receive the International Spotlight Award, participate in a post-screening discussion and join the festival’s Songwriters and Composers Panel. Gilroy will be on hand for a post-screening conversation following Searchlight Pictures’ “Behemoth!” where Pedro Pascal plays a gifted cellist and former child prodigy who returns to Los Angeles after two decades on the road to record film scores and confront his complicated family history. McDonagh will receive the Director Spotlight Award for “Wild Horse Nine,” also from Searchlight. Set just before the 1973 Chilean coup, the film stars John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell as longtime CIA agents sent from Santiago to Easter Island, where they confront their dark pasts and a conspiracy unfolding around them. Bird will receive the Spotlight Animation Award for Netflix’s “Ray Gunn,” a passion project more than 30 years in the making. Bird wrote and directed the sci-fi noir, which is set in Metropia, a city where humans and aliens live side by side. Rogen will receive the MFF Artistic Achievement Award at an “In Conversation with Seth Rogen” event covering several of his films at the festival. He stars in Olivia Wilde’s A24 film “The Invite” alongside Wilde, Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton, playing one of two married couples whose relationships are tested by a dinner party that grows more unpredictable as the night goes on. Rogen also produced Leah Nelson’s animated film “Tangles” with Lauren Miller Rogen, Evan Goldberg and others. Based on Sarah Leavitt’s graphic memoir, it follows a young artist who moves home to care for her mother after an Alzheimer’s diagnosis. Rogen will join Nelson and Miller Rogen for a post-screening conversation. Eleazar will receive the Breakthrough Actor Award for A24’s “Misty Green,” written and directed by Chris Rock. In her first leading film role, she plays Misty, a once-successful actress whose career has stalled. She is fighting to win back her place in Hollywood while dealing with financial trouble, broken relationships and her own self-destructive streak. The annual Songwriters and Composers Panel will feature Ari Balouzian (“Primetime,” “You Can See Everything”), Lesley Barber (“Gail”), Jesse Eisenberg (“The Debut”), Lukas Frank (“Behemoth!”), Guitarricadelafuente (“La Bola Negra”), Daniel Pemberton (“Ink,” “Project Hail Mary”), Christopher Spelman (“Paper Tiger”) and Diane Warren (“Maserati: The Brothers”). “Toy Story 5” production designer Bob Pauley will lead a masterclass on his more than three decades at Pixar. Pauley was part of the original “Toy Story” creative team, designed Buzz Lightyear for the 1995 film and has worked on all five installments. He will also lead a drawing demonstration focused on new characters from “Toy Story 5.” Tennis legend Billie Jean King will attend with Liz Garbus and Elizabeth Wolff’s documentary “Give Me the Ball!” The film uses rare archival footage and candid interviews to examine the victories, struggles and personal sacrifices behind her tennis career and her fight for equality in sports and beyond. King will sit down with festival founder and board chair Sheila Johnson for a one-on-one post-screening conversation on Sunday, Oct. 18. Finally, Pullman will attend with “Everybody Digs Bill Evans,” Grant Gee’s unconventional portrait of the jazz pianist. Set in 1961, the film follows Evans (Anders Danielsen Lie) after the sudden death of his bassist and close collaborator Scott LaFaro, when grief drives him to stop playing and retreat from New York to his family home. MFF advisory board members Albert Berger and Ron Yerxa executive produce. The full Middleburg Film Festival lineup and honorees are below. The full schedule and lineup are available at middleburgfilm.org . Olivia Wilde, Seth Rogen, Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton appear in The Invite by Olivia Wilde, an official selection of the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.
