articles.title: Theaters Re-Invest $2.7 Billion to Bring In Moviegoers With Heated Reclining Seats, Full-Service Bars, Immersive Sound and More
articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 9:00am PT Theaters Re-Invest $2.7 Billion to Bring In Moviegoers With Heated Reclining Seats, Full-Service Bars, Immersive Sound and More By Pat Saperstein Plus Icon Pat Saperstein Deputy Editor @Variety_PatS Latest Beyond Fest Organizers on Improved Ticketing, Fans ‘As Unhinged as We Are’ and Their 7 Titles Not to Miss 2 days ago ‘Lightworkers’ Doc: Tom Morello, Henry Winkler, Lee Grant and More on Why They Fight for Democracy: ‘Comfort Is a Danger Zone’ 6 days ago Hannah Einbinder Speaks Out After Being Arrested at Netanyahu Protest: ‘Let Us Not Mistake the Spectacle for the Story’ 7 days ago See All Courtesy CinemaUnited As the summer box office closes at an all-time high, theaters across North America are aiming to keep audiences engaged by spending $2.7 billion over the past two years on upgrades and innovations. The exhibition chains are investing big in amenities such as premium large formats and expanded food and beverage services, according to Cinema United , which unveiled its Cinema Investment report Thursday. In the past year alone, theaters spent $1.2 billion to create premium entertainment experiences. The eight largest domestic circuits spent $840 million in the past year after pledging $2.2 billion to modernize and upgrade theaters over a three-year period. Related Stories Melissa McCarthy on Getting Serious for 'JonBenét Ramsey,' the Psychiatrist on Set and Hollywood's 'Bulls---’ Excuse for Why Comedies Don't Work Anymore 'People Are Still Terrified of Me': Sharon Stone on Thriving for 46 Years in Hollywood and Why 'My Lane Was Never Going to Be Sex Psychos' The report spotlights extensive investment at several circuits, such as Florida’s Epic Theatres, which added Luma 4D E-Motion recliner seats, proprietary premium large-format projection with augmented audio, full bars and arcades. Utah’s Megaplex opened an entertainment complex featuring interactive, augmented-reality bowling at its Downtown Daybreak location. Popular on Variety Meanwhile, Cinemark offers 72% reclining seats, the highest concentration among major U.S. exhibitors, plus 650 D-Box motion seat-equipped auditoriums and private label PLF Cinemark XD. Classic Cinemas upgraded its 100-year-old LaGrange, Illinois multiplex with amenities including heated recliners and DTS:X immersive object-based sound. Cinema United represents more than 63,000 screens worldwide. The report also featured Major Cinema, a chain of cinemas in Thailand, which offers 23 kids cinemas that include ball pits at the front of the colorful auditorium furnished with sofas and large pillows. “From the world’s largest circuits to independent theaters on Main Streets across this great nation, theater owners have shown how much they believe in the future of the big screen, and 2026’s strong box office proves that commitment is paying off,” said Michael O’Leary, president and CEO of Cinema United. “When a theater reinvests in itself, everyone wins — moviegoers get a better experience, studios get a stronger platform, local businesses benefit, and contractors get the work that comes with it. Cinema United members are reaffirming that there is nothing like seeing a movie on a big screen. Every investment in a movie theater is an investment in the community it serves, which is why moviegoing will remain essential for generations to come.” Harkins theaters added 13 new Cinéxl PLF auditoriums and four Cinébar locations, plus Arizona’s first 4D E-Motion location at Phoenix’s Norterra. “The benefit to communities from movie theaters is unmatched by any other premier entertainment experience, and that is why they remain so valued in major cities and small towns worldwide,” said Mike Bowers, CEO of Harkins and chair of Cinema United. “These investments continue our industry’s long history of ensuring that every moviegoing experience is a premium one.” French President Emmanuel Macron Calls on YouTube to Finance Content and Warns of Growing Threat to Cultural Model (EXCLUSIVE) YouTube’s Pedro Pina Says Platform Can Fuel Britain’s Next TV ‘Golden Age,’ Unveils $4 Million Pledge: We’re ‘Not the Villain’ YouTube Locks Down Coachella Rights Through 2030 as It Unveils New Microdrama-Inspired Experience for Shorts, AI-Powered Tools for Music and Studio, and More YouTube Unveils Foundry’s Fall Class of 2026: Underscores, Zeina and 14 More Like Nastya Signs Content Development Deal With Disney Abhishek Chaubey, Navdeep Singh to Present Shivam Shankar’s ‘Bhed, Bakri, Bhoot’ on Anurag Kashyap-Curated YouTube Channel (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments...

articles.title: Amelia Dimoldenberg to Bring ‘Chicken Shop Date’ Final Season to Netflix and YouTube (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 9:00am PT Amelia Dimoldenberg to Bring ‘Chicken Shop Date’ Final Season to Netflix and YouTube (EXCLUSIVE) By Ethan Shanfeld Plus Icon Ethan Shanfeld @ethanshanfeld Latest Sets and the City: Why New York’s Film and TV Business Is Booming 22 hours ago ‘Barbershop’ TV Show Sets February Release on Amazon, Drops First Look at Jermaine Fowler 1 day ago ‘Digger’ Confronts Negative Buzz: New Ad Tells Moviegoers to ‘Decide for Yourself’ After Tom Cruise Movie Called ‘Unpleasant’ and ‘Baffling’ 2 days ago See All Photo by Laura Schaeffer “ Chicken Shop Date ” is coming to Netflix. The final season of Amelia Dimoldenberg ‘s popular interview series will air on the streamer on Oct. 2, at the same time it will go live on the host’s YouTube and social media channels. Netflix is also adding past episodes from the “Chicken Shop Date” library, including interviews with Andrew Garfield, Damson Idris, Central Cee, Sabrina Carpenter, Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman and Jack Harlow. Related Stories 'People Are Still Terrified of Me': Sharon Stone on Thriving for 46 Years in Hollywood and Why 'My Lane Was Never Going to Be Sex Psychos' Melissa McCarthy on Getting Serious for 'JonBenét Ramsey,' the Psychiatrist on Set and Hollywood's 'Bulls---’ Excuse for Why Comedies Don't Work Anymore Dimoldenberg launched “Chicken Shop Date” in 2014 and has since hosted 115 episodes of the series, a deadpan and flirty digital talk show driven by the host’s British comedic sensibilities and filmed in local chicken shops. While early episodes largely featured British rappers, Dimoldenberg eventually began to court A-list singers and movie stars like Jennifer Lawrence, Paul Mescal, Cynthia Erivo and even Paul McCartney. Popular on Variety “Chicken Shop Date” earned a 2022 Streamy Award win for best indie series, and Dimoldenberg was recognized on Time magazine’s inaugural Time100 Creators list in 2025. She also served as the Academy’s social media ambassador and red carpet correspondent at the Oscars for the past three years. Dimoldenberg directs “Chicken Shop Date” and produces under her Dimz Inc. banner. Diara Vassallo Ndiaye and Zoe Dimoldenberg also produce, and Ashleigh Kybert is the head of content and social. “From self-releasing our very first episode of Chicken Shop Date to partnering with Netflix, this journey has been all about connecting directly with people who love the show. I’m thrilled that our catalog is expanding its reach with Netflix, bringing our dates to a whole new world of fans without losing our original essence,” Dimoldenberg said. Netflix’s licensing of “Chicken Shop Date” is part of the streamer’s broader effort to get into business with creators. In an attempt to compete with YouTube, the company has licensed a bevy of popular video podcasts and has greenlit some of its own. It has picked up food and cooking content from Mythical Kitchen and Nick DiGiovanni as well as children’s programming like “Danny Go!” And Netflix has also inked partnerships with media brands — including Variety — to license editorial content on the platform. articles.title: UTA Streamlines Film, TV and Talent Leadership; Matt Rice Rises to President of Filmed Entertainment Unit
articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 9:02am PT UTA Streamlines Film, TV and Talent Leadership; Matt Rice Rises to President of Filmed Entertainment Unit By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest Don’t Lie, Don’t Cry and Use Common Sense: Adam Levy, Judge Judy’s Son, Joins the Family Business With ‘Adam’s Law’ 1 week ago How NBCUniversal Television Thrives on Collaborative Energy Between Studios and Platforms: ‘We Cheer Each Other On’ 1 week ago Her Road to the Top: How NBCUniversal TV Studio Chief Pearlena Igbokwe Learned to Balance Business and Creative Instincts 1 week ago See All Courtesy of UTA UTA has taken a dramatic step to streamline the leadership of its film and TV lit and talent departments to reflect the industry trends of blurring lines between disciplines. As part of the change, agency veteran Matt Rice has been promoted to president of the new UTA Filmed Entertainment unit. In the new structure, UTA’s Allan Haldeman, Blair Kohan, Jay Gassner and Julien Thuan have been elevated to managing partners of Filmed Entertainment. UTA has named new department heads to lead key segments: Amanda Hymson and Jordan Lonner will lead Motion Picture Literary; Lucinda Moorhead and Mickey Berman will run TV Literary while talent will be steered by Hanley Baxter and John Sacks alongside longstanding talent chief Mike Jelline. Related Stories 'It's Time for My Voice': Jennifer Hudson on Reviving 'Dreamgirls,' Booking Tom Cruise for Her Talk Show and Writing Original Music Again Melissa McCarthy on Getting Serious for 'JonBenét Ramsey,' the Psychiatrist on Set and Hollywood's 'Bulls---’ Excuse for Why Comedies Don't Work Anymore Another new wrinkle is the formation of a Filmed Entertainment board that includes agency stalwarts including Jelline, Berman, Moorhead, Jason Burns, Marissa Devins, Dan Erlij, Chris Hart, Jason Heyman, Keya Khayatian, Rich Klubeck, Billy Lazarus, Gregory McKnight, David Park, Theresa Peters, Shani Rosenzweig and Larry Salz. Popular on Variety UTA chief executive David Kramer outlined the reasoning for the changes in a memo sent to agency staffers on Thursday morning “UTA has never been a place that waits for change — we anticipate where the industry is going and build for what comes next,” Kramer said. “As the business evolves and film and television increasingly converge, this team positions us to lead that evolution, unlock new possibilities for our clients and bring the full power of UTA to everyone we represent.” Rice joined UTA in 2002 after getting his start at the Broder Kurland literary agency. He’s one of the town’s top representatives of writers, directors and showrunners, including such notables as Phil Lord & Chris Miller, Michael Schur, Alec Berg, Bill Hader, Seth Rogen & Evan Goldberg, Will Forte, Justin Halpern & Patrick Schumacker, R. Scott Gemmill, James Gunn, Dan Goor, Chris McKenna & Erik Sommers, Adam Reed, Sebastian Maniscalco and Matt Rife. “This move reflects what sets UTA apart — a bold, collaborative and forward-thinking approach. I’m excited to build upon the work of this exceptional group of leaders and continue to deliver best-in-class representation to our clients,” Rice said. UTA’s shakeup of its longstanding departmental lines reflects the shifting sands for the content business as well as the business of representing boldface name talent. The growth in audience and influence among the largest social media platforms has revved up the creator economy and birthed a new breed of digital media superstar. All of this has challenged the traditional operations of Hollywood’s largest talent and management firms. Here is Kramer’s full memo: UTA has never been a place that waits for change — we anticipate where the industry is going and build for what comes next. With that in mind, we are announcing a streamlined, future-focused leadership structure for our Filmed Entertainment group which reflects the evolving business of film and television and will enable us to maximize opportunities for clients. By bringing together partners across Motion Picture Literary, Television Literary and Talent, we will continue to deliver unrivaled seamless client representation, sharpen the agency’s competitive edge and increase efficiency and collaboration. I’m thrilled to announce that Matt Rice has been elevated to President of Filmed Entertainment. Matt is a phenomenal agent and partner who has helped spearhead a transformative expansion of UTA’s television division. In his expanded role, he will lead overall strategy and execution across all areas of Filmed Entertainment. To support Matt and drive leadership across the entirety of the Filmed Entertainment group, we have elevated Allan Haldeman, Blair Kohan, Jay Gassner and Julien Thuan to the role of Managing Partner of Filmed Entertainment. This newly established leadership group will be critical to driving growth, connecting opportunities across our business and delivering exceptional results for clients as film and TV increasingly converge. To further capture market momentum and maximize client opportunities we have also established a Filmed Entertainment board. These senior partnerswill leverage their collective expertise, experience and deep industry relationships to aggressively pursue client development and new initiatives. Board members will include Mickey Berman, Jason Burns, Marissa Devins, Dan Erlij, Chris Hart, Jason Heyman, Mike Jelline, Keya Khayatian, Rich Klubeck, Billy Lazarus, Gregory McKnight, Lucinda Moorhead, David Park, Theresa Peters, Shani Rosenzweig, and Larry Salz. All of our Filmed Entertainment Department Heads play an integral part in ensuring our teams operate at the highest level in service of our clients. As we move to this new chapter, we are excited to appoint several new Department Heads across Filmed Entertainment: Amanda Hymson andJordan Lonner (Motion Picture Literary); Lucinda Moorhead and Mickey Berman (TV Literary); Hanley Baxter and John Sacks (Talent, alongside incumbent department head Mike Jelline). These agents have distinguished themselves through exceptional client representation and will be responsible for furthering the growth of their respective businesses. We’ve had an extraordinary year, with UTA clients behind some of 2026’s biggest box office hits and most acclaimed television productions, earning top honors at the Academy Awards, Emmys, Golden Globes and Tonys. We are building from a position of immense strength, and this new leadership structure is designed to carry that momentum forward and position us for even greater success. Please join me in congratulating our new leadership for Filmed Entertainment. We have so much to be proud of and I can’t wait to see this team take us to new heights in the coming year. articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 9:03am PT Jackie Chan, Anil Kapoor Films Among 335 National Winners at Asian Academy Creative Awards By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Sabu’s ‘Arrested Memory’ Leads Golden Horse Awards Nominations, Shu Qi’s ‘Girl’ Close Behind 3 hours ago Ballet Star Tiler Peck to Make London West End Debut in Susan Stroman’s ‘Little Dancer’ (EXCLUSIVE) 8 hours ago Venice Golden Lion Winner Milcho Manchevski’s ‘Sister Brother Manhole Cover’ Heads to Tokyo for World Premiere, Trailer Unveiled (EXCLUSIVE) 9 hours ago See All Golden Network Asia Films fronted by Jackie Chan and Anil Kapoor are among the 335 national winners named by the Asian Academy Creative Awards . “The Shadow’s Edge” won Best Feature Film for Chinese Mainland, and “Subedaar” won it for India. The winners come from 18 nations and territories and span 39 categories. They now move on to the international round. Grand winners will be named at the gala awards final at Singapore’s Capitol Theatre in December. Related Stories Paige DeSorbo on Leaving 'Summer House' Behind and Speaking Out About a Past Abusive Relationship: 'Domestic Violence' Can 'Truly Happen to Anyone' 'People Are Still Terrified of Me': Sharon Stone on Thriving for 46 Years in Hollywood and Why 'My Lane Was Never Going to Be Sex Psychos' Mediacorp led the company count with 23 wins. Prime Video India and Astro Malaysia collected 19 each, and CNN took 15. Popular on Variety Chinese drama series “The Lead” won more categories than any other title, with six. They included Best Actress in a Leading Role for Liu Haocun. Best Drama Series, however, went to the bigger-budget “Legend of the Magnate.” Malaysia’s haul came with a note of loss. Horror feature “Malam Terlarang” (Forbidden Night) won four categories, among them Best Feature Film and Best Actress in a Supporting Role for Sofia Jane. Its Best Direction (Feature Film) win went to Norhanisham bin Muhammad, who died in May. Astro’s family crime drama “Good Boys Go to Heaven” added five Malaysian wins, taking both Best Actor and the drama series prize. In Japan, “Song of the Samurai” also won five categories but lost Best Drama Series to “Alice in Borderland.” Non took Best Actress for “Miss King.” China’s “Swords Into Plowshares” also collected four wins, as did Season 3 of India’s “The Family Man.” Bai Yu was named Best Actor in a Leading Role for Chinese Mainland. Taiwan broadcaster PTS also scored four wins with “Dogman.” The series took Best Drama Series as well as acting honors for Chang Hsiao Chuan and Tarcy Su. GMMTV’s “Enigma Black Stage” picked up four Thai wins. Scripted categories were hotly contested. Gemini Norawit Titicharoenrak was named Best Actor for “Ticket to Heaven,” while Mono’s Manatsanun Phanlerdwongsakul took Best Actress for “Sweet Dreams.” In the Philippines, Vice Ganda, one of the country’s biggest stars, had to get through an extra tie-breaker round before securing Best Actor for his performance in “Call Me Mother.” Nadine Lustre, who stars opposite him in that film, also advances, though her nod is for headlining Viu’s “Love, Siargao.” Animated feature “The Violinist” took Best Feature Film, Best Animation and Best Screenplay for Singapore. Its voice cast includes Tan Kheng Hua and Ayden Sng. Sng was separately named Best Actor in a Leading Role (Singapore) for the series “Double Helix.” Singaporean independent Refinery Media won three categories for lifestyle show “Man of the Hour.” CNN’s 15 wins came in the factual categories. One went to Kristie Lu Stout, a previous winner, for Best Factual Presenter (Thailand). She will go up against another past winner, Singapore’s Wei Du, who was recognized for CNA’s “Walk the Line: ICE Nation.” Awards chair Beverley McGarvey, president and streaming lead at Paramount ANZ, said the awards show every year how deep the region’s pool of talent and original ideas runs. “Our stories are becoming more confident, more distinctive and more influential, not only in their home markets but with audiences all around the world,” she said. McGarvey said that entry numbers were level with last year’s. She added that the size of the national winners field makes it the world’s biggest showcase of Asia-Pacific content. This year’s jurors came from 38 countries. The awards use a two-round system. A jury of senior industry figures from TV networks, streamers, production outfits, distributors, buyers and screen agencies first scores entries at the national level. It scores them again in the international round to choose the grand winners. articles.title: Kevin Feige Hails Theatrical Experience as ‘the Real Movie Magic’ at Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Tribute
articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 9:09am PT Kevin Feige Hails Theatrical Experience as ‘the Real Movie Magic’ at Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Tribute By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest Don’t Lie, Don’t Cry and Use Common Sense: Adam Levy, Judge Judy’s Son, Joins the Family Business With ‘Adam’s Law’ 1 week ago How NBCUniversal Television Thrives on Collaborative Energy Between Studios and Platforms: ‘We Cheer Each Other On’ 1 week ago Her Road to the Top: How NBCUniversal TV Studio Chief Pearlena Igbokwe Learned to Balance Business and Creative Instincts 1 week ago See All Ryan Miller / @captureimaging.com He’s a “great guy who’s incredibly humble” who has also produced 38 movies in 17 years that have delivered more than $35 billion at the box office. Twelve of those titles delivered more than $1 billion; three of them generated $2 billion apiece. Not to mention, Kevin Feige is the architect of the most meticulously crafted, interconnected cinematic universe in the history of motion pictures. Disney Entertainment chairman Alan Bergman reeled off those stunning stats (and admirable qualities) as he took part in Wednesday night’s tribute to Feige, president of Marvel Studios and chief creative officer of Marvel, who was honored with this year’s Pioneer of the Year laurel from the Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Foundation . Related Stories Melissa McCarthy on Getting Serious for 'JonBenét Ramsey,' the Psychiatrist on Set and Hollywood's 'Bulls---’ Excuse for Why Comedies Don't Work Anymore Her Road to the Top: How NBCUniversal TV Studio Chief Pearlena Igbokwe Learned to Balance Business and Creative Instincts “Guardians of the Galaxy” star Chris Pratt and writer-director Jon Favreau were on hand at the Beverly Hilton hotel to laud the Marvel leader. Composer Michael Giacchino was there via video because of illness. Others who paid tribute in prerecorded reels include Marvel’s Louis D’Esposito and MCU stars Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Hayley Atwell, Chris Hemsworth, Paul Bettany, Hailee Steinfeld, Pedro Pascal and Vanessa Kirby. Popular on Variety Feige was the star of the night but the conversation in the packed ballroom was dominated by the big news of the day, Paramount Skydance’s surprise news that Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz is leaving the toymaker to join the Melrose plant as co-CEO with David Ellison. “He believes in the movies, and even more than that he believes in the people who make the movies,” Pratt told the crowd at the Beverly Hilton. The event raised $1.9 million for the Will Rogers Pioneers Assistance Fund, which helps those in the film exhibition community who need assistance. Also in the crowd were Disney chief Josh D’Amaro, AMC Theatres leader Adam Aron and Eduardo Acuna of Regal Cinemas, producer Scott Stuber among others. Favreau echoed Pratt’s comments about Feige’s passion for all things related to cinema. “The man loves movies. He listens to movie soundtracks in his car,” the “Iron Man” director told the crowd. “He’s driving down PCH blasting the ‘Ferngully’ soundtrack.” Feige took a bit of gentle ribbing about his love of custom baseball caps and other characteristics that have become his signature. From video, Giacchino introduced a large tiki band that emerged on stage to perform Marvel movie tunes with a Polynesian flair. The executive and producer lived up to his advance billing for humility in his remarks at the end of the night. And he had some thoughtful observations about what it is that makes moviegoing so special. He even name-checked his childhood haunt, the Rialto Theater in Westfield, New Jersey. (“Sitting in the dark, eating Twizzlers. I was hooked,” he recalled.) “Underneath all the technology and the spectacle, the years of work from development to post. It’s still the same thing: a group of people making something with others, and then a group of people sitting in the dark and experiencing it with others. That is the full process of a movie,” Feige said. “The final crucial part of that collaboration is the audience. Movies are an invitation to experience a story together. When a film connects and the crowd is cheering, laughing and crying together, that shared emotion is the final step in the process. That’s the real movie magic, You might even say it’s not a real movie without it,” he said. articles.title: Hearst Renews CBS Weekend Series ‘The Visioneers With Zay Harding’ Through 2028
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Starz Goes Dark On Verizon FiOS Amid Carriage Dispute Ynon Kreiz Anointed Co-CEO Of New Paramount-WBD; David Ellison Says Mega-Studio Is “Transformational Moment For Our Industry” Ex-Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz In Line For High-Level Paramount Exec Post View All October 1, 2026 6:57am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Hearst Media Production Group has renewed CBS weekend educational series The Visioneers with Zay Harding for two more seasons, through 2028. The show was first announced by Hearst in March 2025. Season 3 of the 30-minute eco-adventure original, which is produced by the Hearst production division in partnership with the VoLo Foundation, will premiere on Saturday. Hosted by Harding, an international explorer, the show features scientists, engineers and everyday people who are creating sustainable environmental solutions. Related Stories Executives Hearst Corp. CEO Steven Swartz Expects "Strong Year" For TV Division, Hints At M&A At A+E Global, Local Stations News 'Lucky Dog: Down Under' Expands Pet Franchise In New CBS Weekend Block The series airs weekend mornings as part of the CBS WKND educational/informational programming block. Timeslots vary by market. Watch on Deadline Guests this season include actor Edward Norton; former NFL player and ocean-conservation advocate Kelvin Beachum; NASCAR driver Austin Green; and Luci Baines Johnson, daughter of Lady Bird Johnson. Episodes are set from the Great Barrier Reef to America’s ports, racetracks and wildflower fields. “Alongside our partners at VoLo Foundation, we’re proud to bring audiences two more seasons of The Visioneers,” HMPG President Bryan Curb said in a statement. “The show has struck a real chord with viewers, sharing stories that prove environmental stewardship can take many forms – and that building a more sustainable future can be an engaging, hands-on adventure.” Thais Lopez V., president of VoLo Foundation, said the series “shows that the solutions to our biggest challenges are already in the hands of people with the courage to imagine a better world and the determination to make it real.” HMPG’s slate includes more than 30 original series and hundreds of hours of content annually on broadcast networks, station groups, connected-TV and streaming platforms. Its library spans 85 series and 6,000 episodes, with content across 100 countries. articles.title: ‘Best Pancakes In The County’: IFC Picks Up Domestic Rights To Nicolas Cage, Justin Long & Shelley Hennig Action-Thriller; First Look Revealed
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas ‘Best Pancakes In The County’: IFC Picks Up Domestic Rights To Nicolas Cage, Justin Long & Shelley Hennig Action-Thriller; First Look Revealed Crime Pic ‘American Muscle’ Being Sold By Protagonist Picks Charlotte Kirk & Neil Marshall Thriller ‘Spiral Down’ Adds Costas Mandylor, Michael Pare, Alessandra Williams, More View All October 1, 2026 7:25am Add us as a Google Preferred Source (L-R) Nicolas Cage, Justin Long and Shelley Hennig Getty Images EXCLUSIVE : Independent Film Company has acquired U.S. rights to Best Pancakes In The County , the action-thriller written and directed by Ken Sanzel ( Kill Chain ) and starring Nicolas Cage ( Longleg s), Justin Long ( Weapons ) and Shelley Hennig ( Unfriended ). The deal was negotiated by Mark Ward, Chief Acquisitions Officer for Independent Film Company and Eduard Osipov at Beno Films on behalf of the filmmakers. Pic will be released in theaters and on digital platforms November 20, 2026. The synopsis reads: “Set over the course of one explosive night, Best Pancakes In The County transforms an unassuming small-town diner into the epicenter of a deadly standoff involving rogue federal agents, a fast-talking con man with a dangerous past and a waitress harboring secrets of her own. As loyalties blur and tensions erupt, survival depends on who can outthink — and outgun — everyone else.” Related Stories Trailers 'Madden' Trailer: Boom! Nicolas Cage Transforms In David O. Russell's Biopic Of NFL Icon Reviews 'River' Review: Joshua Giuliano Makes Directorial Debut With Tragic Family Drama Wrapped In Atmospheric Slasher -- Toronto Film Festival Cage stars as “The S.O.B., an eccentric and cunning criminal caught in the escalating confrontation”. Below is a first-look image. The film reunites Sanzel with Cage following their collaboration on the 2019 action thriller Kill Chain . Long plays Cookie and Hennig is Dolly. The ensemble cast also includes Lauren German ( Lucifer ), Ravi Patel ( Animal Control) , Brandon Mychal Smith ( Get On Up ), Kelly Greyson ( Sleeping Dogs ), Jaylen Moore ( Six ), and Michael Sirow ( Sleeping Dogs ). The movie was filmed in Arkansas and is produced by Eduard Osipov, Raja Collins, Eric Brenner, Niko Fomenko, Gary Preisler and R. Wesley Sierk III. Executive producers include John D. Straley, Audra Gricius, Jina Panebianco, Lance Kawas, Ahmed S. Boomrod, Eugene Pruss, and Nadine de Barros. The film is produced by Beno Films and backed by CaliWood Pictures, with Fortitude International handling international sales. “ Best Pancakes In The County is exactly the kind of eccentric and wildly entertaining ride that Nicolas Cage does better than anyone else,” said IFC Entertainment Group’s Chief Acquisition Officer, Mark Ward. “Ken has built a tense, funny and unpredictable thriller around a fantastic ensemble, and we can’t wait for audiences to experience the chaos this November.” “Working with Nic again was an opportunity to create a character who could be funny, dangerous and completely unpredictable from one moment to the next,” said writer-director Sanzel. “And then he took it to wilder and more unexpected places than I could have imagined. We wanted to take this seemingly ordinary diner, fill it with people with dueling and hidden agendas, juxtapose the threat of violence with the urgency of getting breakfast orders right, and keep turning up the pressure until everything explodes. IFC immediately understood the fast, fun tone of the film, and I’m excited to have them bringing it to audiences.” Watch on Deadline Nicolas Cage in Best Pancakes In The County Ted Sarandos On WB Pursuit, Netflix Engagement Growth Challenges & More Becerra & Hilton Tussle Over Blame For Losing Hollywood Jobs In Debate Sound Decision? The studio said the division will partner with digital creators to turn their ideas, content, and audiences into entertainment franchises. Jared Jacobs will lead the division as SVP, AGC Digital. He will report to Joel Zimmer, President, AGC. Unscripted Television on digital strategy, development, creator partnerships, and new IP. He also served as VP of Development at Night Studios, where he helped lead the company’s creator-led entertainment slate and developed projects with some of the world’s biggest digital talent, including MrBeast, Kai Cenat, Ryan Trahan, Sam & Colby, Moriah Elizabeth, and Zach King. Before that, Jacobs held roles at Blumhouse Television, Mark Wahlberg’s Unrealistic Ideas, Endeavor Content (now FIFTH SEASON), and WME. articles.title: Nicolas Cage, Michael Sheen, Jordi Mollà, Emilio Sakraya & Adrian Topol Leading Cyber-Thriller ‘C.L.A.Y.’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas ‘Best Pancakes In The County’: IFC Picks Up Domestic Rights To Nicolas Cage, Justin Long & Shelley Hennig Action-Thriller; First Look Revealed Crime Pic ‘American Muscle’ Being Sold By Protagonist Picks Charlotte Kirk & Neil Marshall Thriller ‘Spiral Down’ Adds Costas Mandylor, Michael Pare, Alessandra Williams, More View All October 1, 2026 8:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Nicolas Cage, Michael Sheen, Jordi Mollà, Emilio Sakraya and Adrian Topol.jpg Anthony Avellano for Deadline/Sarah Dunn/Getty/Stefan Kokovic/Getty EXCLUSIVE : Nicolas Cage (Longlegs) , Michael Sheen (Masters of Sex ), Jordi Mollà (Mobland ), Emilio Sakraya (One Piece: The Battle Of Alabasta) , and Adrian Topol ( Snowflake) are starring in C.L.A.Y. , a psychological cyber-thriller written, directed and produced by Simon Afram. The film marks Afram’s directorial debut and reunites some of the key cast behind upcoming WWII espionage feature Fortitude , which Afram wrote and produced for director Simon West. Additional casting on his directorial debut is still coming together. C.L.A.Y. “follows a brilliant but socially invisible computer prodigy who finds purpose and belonging when he is drawn into C.L.A.Y. (Clowns Laughing At You), an underground hacker collective whose daring exploits turn digital provocation into real-world consequences. As the group’s notoriety grows, their actions attract the attention of intelligence agencies, criminal syndicates, and rival hackers.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories News 'Best Pancakes In The County': IFC Picks Up Domestic Rights To Nicolas Cage, Justin Long & Shelley Hennig Action-Thriller; First Look Revealed Trailers 'Madden' Trailer: Boom! Nicolas Cage Transforms In David O. Russell's Biopic Of NFL Icon The film is due to shoot on location in London, starting November 2026. Production company of record is Clay Pictures Ltd. Pic is produced alongside Edward Kahl (Queen of Manhattan) , Reza Roohi ( Fortitude ) , and Adrian Topol (Faking Bullshit) , with executive producers Bianca Goodloe (Mission: Impossible II), David Scaramanga (Fortitude) , and Daniel Haido (Fortitude). Casting is by Rich Mento (Warm Bodies) . Bianca Goodloe Esq. at Goodloe Law is legal counsel for the production. “ C.L.A.Y. is about identity, belonging and the extraordinary power the digital world can have over our real lives. At its heart, it’s a deeply human story about people searching for purpose in a world where almost anything is possible behind a screen. I wanted to create a film that pulls you in, remains unpredictable, and stays with you long after the film ends,” said writer-director Afram. Cage is represented by WME, Stride Management, and GGSS&C LLP. Sheen is represented by CAA, Link Entertainment, and Schreck Rose. Mollà is represented by IAG and Creative Partners Group. Sakraya is represented by Independent Talent Group, Done Deal Entertainment, and Artist International Group. Topol is represented by Fischer & Partner Agency Germany. articles.title: UTA Sets New Leadership Structure For Filmed Entertainment Division Under President Matt Rice
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Joachim Rønning Sets Horror Film ‘System’ With Spooky Pictures & Image Nation Studios Neon Counters A24’s SCP Foundation Movie With “Open-Source” Project To Release Under Creative Commons License 20th Century Studios Acquires Horror Package ‘Every House Is Haunted’ From Netflix; ‘Don’t Move’s Adam Schindler & Brian Netto Directing View All October 1, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Matt Rice, newly appointed President of UTA's Filmed Entertainment division Sonali Ohrie UTA on Thursday announced a comprehensive reorganization of its Filmed Entertainment Division, elevating Matt Rice to serve as its President. A longtime partner at the agency who most recently served as head of its TV department, Rice is known for his work with top writer, producer, director, talent and comedy clients like Phil Lord & Chris Miller, Mike Schur, Alec Berg, Bill Hader, Seth Rogen & Evan Goldberg, among others. “Matt is a phenomenal agent and partner who has helped spearhead a transformative expansion of UTA’s television division. In his expanded role, he will lead overall strategy and execution across all areas of Filmed Entertainment,” said CEO David Kramer in an internal memo to staff this morning. Related Stories Agencies UTA Signs 'Brian' Filmmaker Will Ropp Agencies UTA Signs 'Club Kid' Star Reggie Absolom In addition to Rice’s role, UTA has announced the promotion of Allan Haldeman, Blair Kohan, Jay Gassner and Julien Thuan to Managing Partners of Filmed Entertainment. Amanda Hymson and Jordan Lonner are now heads of Motion Picture Literary, with Lucinda Moorhead and Mickey Berman heading up TV Lit, and Hanley Baxter and John Sacks joining the incumbent Mike Jelline to head up the Talent department. Watch on Deadline Additionally, UTA today announced the formation of a Filmed Entertainment board, consisting of senior partners who, per Kramer, “will leverage their collective expertise, experience and deep industry relationships to aggressively pursue client development and new initiatives.” Board members include Mickey Berman, Jason Burns, Marissa Devins, Dan Erlij, Chris Hart, Jason Heyman, Mike Jelline, Keya Khayatian, Rich Klubeck, Billy Lazarus, Gregory McKnight, Lucinda Moorhead, David Park, Theresa Peters, Shani Rosenzweig, and Larry Salz. Kramer emphasized, in his memo to staff, that the reorg is intended to “increase efficiency and collaboration,” thereby maximizing client opportunities and sharpening “the agency’s competitive edge” amidst a rapidly evolving entertainment landscape. Kramer said that “UTA has never been a place that waits for change,” calling the new leadership structure “streamlined” and “future-focused.” He went on to say, “We’ve had an extraordinary year, with UTA clients behind some of 2026’s biggest box office hits and most acclaimed television productions, earning top honors at the Academy Awards, Emmys, Golden Globes and Tonys. We are building from a position of immense strength, and this new leadership structure is designed to carry that momentum forward and position us for even greater success.” Kramer’s assessment echos comments he made about the agency’s “record-breaking year,” “strength” and “momentum” in an Aug. 26 memo, in which he hit back at a Variety article about recent UTA client departures, which alleged internal anxiety, accusing the author of unprofessional bias. ( Variety ‘s parent company, Penske Media Corporation, also owns Deadline .) Read the full memo below: UTA has never been a place that waits for change — we anticipate where the industry is going and build for what comes next. With that in mind, we are announcing a streamlined, future-focused leadership structure for our Filmed Entertainment group which reflects the evolving business of film and television and will enable us to maximize opportunities for clients. By bringing together partners across Motion Picture Literary, Television Literary and Talent, we will continue to deliver unrivaled seamless client representation, sharpen the agency’s competitive edge and increase efficiency and collaboration. I’m thrilled to announce that Matt Rice has been elevated to President of Filmed Entertainment . Matt is a phenomenal agent and partner who has helped spearhead a transformative expansion of UTA’s television division. In his expanded role, he will lead overall strategy and execution across all areas of Filmed Entertainment. To support Matt and drive leadership across the entirety of the Filmed Entertainment group, we have elevated Allan Haldeman, Blair Kohan, Jay Gassner and Julien Thuan to the role of Managing Partner of Filmed Entertainment. This newly established leadership group will be critical to driving growth, connecting opportunities across our business and delivering exceptional results for clients as film and TV increasingly converge. To further capture market momentum and maximize client opportunities we have also established a Filmed Entertainment board. These senior partnerswill leverage their collective expertise, experience and deep industry relationships to aggressively pursue client development and new initiatives. Board members will include Mickey Berman, Jason Burns, Marissa Devins, Dan Erlij, Chris Hart, Jason Heyman, Mike Jelline, Keya Khayatian, Rich Klubeck, Billy Lazarus, Gregory McKnight, Lucinda Moorhead, David Park, Theresa Peters, Shani Rosenzweig, and Larry Salz. All of our Filmed Entertainment Department Heads play an integral part in ensuring our teams operate at the highest level in service of our clients. As we move to this new chapter, we are excited to appoint several new Department Heads across Filmed Entertainment: Amanda Hymson and Jordan Lonner (Motion Picture Literary); Lucinda Moorhead and Mickey Berman (TV Literary); Hanley Baxter and John Sacks (Talent, alongside incumbent department head Mike Jelline ). These agents have distinguished themselves through exceptional client representation and will be responsible for furthering the growth of their respective businesses. We’ve had an extraordinary year, with UTA clients behind some of 2026’s biggest box office hits and most acclaimed television productions, earning top honors at the Academy Awards, Emmys, Golden Globes and Tonys. We are building from a position of immense strength, and this new leadership structure is designed to carry that momentum forward and position us for even greater success . Please join me in congratulating our new leadership for Filmed Entertainment. We have so much to be proud of and I can’t wait to see this team take us to new heights in the coming year. articles.title: ‘The Grid Unplugged’ Clip: Devastating Doc Explores Failing Power Grids That Sparked California Wildfires — Watch
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘South Park’: Trump’s Animated Penis Flies Away In Deepfake Clip Roasting “Billionaire Of Weenietown” Amid Data Center Infestation ‘Heated Rivalry’ Producers Launch Book’s Irina Foundation In Real Life Macklemore Announces Free Palestine Tour “Sold Out Immediately,” Lineup Coming Soon View All October 1, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EXCLUSIVE: As parts of California continue to rebuild following wildfires in recent years, The Grid Unplugged explores a systemic failure at the root of the problem. Making its world premiere at the Hamptons International Film Festival, Deadline has an exclusive clip from the Rick Cutter -helmed documentary written by Adam Samuel Goldman, which asks what happens when the world’s power grids can’t keep up with growing demand. Featuring interviews with leading energy experts, innovators and policymakers about how to modernize our infrastructure, the timely documentary uses California’s devastating wildfires to discuss a larger story around the growing strain on aging power grids and why it isn’t discussed with more urgency. While also spotlighting alarming risks, the doc offers potential solutions to another looming crisis. articles.title: David Ellison Wants CEO Mark Thompson To Remain At CNN After Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Deal Closes
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson , Jill Goldsmith October 1, 2026 9:03am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Mark Thompson Photo by John Lamparski/Getty Images for Advertising Week New York Paramount CEO David Ellison wants Mark Thompson to remain at CNN after the Warner Bros. Discovery deal closes, a move that would settle at least some of the speculation over the future of the network under its incoming new owners. Talks between Ellison and Thompson are said to be in their early stages, according to sources familiar with the matter. The Wall Street Journal first reported on Ellison’s plans to retain Thompson, who was tapped to lead the network in 2023. Since then, he has sought to integrate the linear and digital operations while launching CNN’s All Access subscription and streaming service. Related Stories News CNN Again Removed As TV Pooler Set To Travel With Donald Trump News Warner Bros. Discovery Strikes Mega Content Deal With UK's ITV For TLC & Quest Shows Like 'Mock The Week', 'Dr. Pimple Popper', 'Salvage Hunters' Under Thompson, CNN also has continued to aggressively report on the Trump administration, while embarking on a lawsuit against the president after he banned the network and two other outlets from the White House grounds. The network also has defended its reporters in the face of attacks by the president, including its chief White House correspondent, Kaitlan Collins. Watch on Deadline The Journal also reported that Bari Weiss, the editor in chief of CBS News, was not expected to have a role in CNN. There has been speculation among current and former staffers at the network that Weiss could be given additional responsibilities after the deal close, as CBS News and CNN will now be sister networks. According to a financial filing earlier this year, CNN was expected to generate $1.8 billion in revenue for the 2026 fiscal year, and $600 million in profit. The network was estimated to reach $2.2 billion in revenue in 2030, with $700 million in profit.
